lines: The sky had been on the brink of breaking down ever since we arrived at the airport, but in a moment's obstinance, it allowed the cold wind to freeze its tears into ice.
The deafening roar of jet engines slowly fades away as it grows ever more distant.
And now, as if to drown out their noise, the scattering powder snow descending from the heavens grows ever more dense.
I look up at the sky overhead, searching for the source of the pure white snow.
No, that's just an excuse. In truth, it's my attempt to look away from the reality before my eyes.
…More specifically, it's an attempt to completely avert my gaze from the airplane that's taking off at this very moment.
It fell on the day we made our promise to always be together. The three of us.
It fell when three became one, as two broke away.
Falling on the day when two, separated, become a pair of ones.
As if to cover up all the pain and sadness, the snow always seems to pile up at our lives' crossroads.
"She" is gone now. And only "she and I" remain.
"Come on, let's go back… There's nothing left here anymore, you know?"
Contrary to my response, my legs refuse to move an inch.
"Can we at least go back inside the airport? Even if only for some hot coffee?"
Fixing my gaze toward the sky, I can't bring myself to turn around for the person calling out to me.
I can't even bring myself to apologize for being so callous to her.
I've already committed the most despicable act of betrayal against her, after all. It wouldn't be right not to see my despicable actions to their very end.
"Are you determined not to listen to anything I ask?"
That's why I don't want her to direct her tender words at someone like me.
"If you're saying that you won't move from here…"
"I'll do this. I'll keep doing it for as long as it takes… to make sure that you don't freeze."
Against my back, I feel a gentle and warm sensation.
Two arms wrap around my chest in a tight and powerful embrace.
"If you don't want this… if you think this means betraying her, and if it's just causing you to suffer more…"
…And then, a burden crushes my heart.
The warmth spreading across my back makes me freeze in place.
The more genuine she is toward me, the more I feel like I'm being crushed under the weight of my sins.

For even now, she has remained this kind to me… enduring everything, pushing herself to the limit, and still forgiving everything I've done… Holding back all of her own unease deep down inside, just for my sake…
"…I'll get the wrong idea, you know?"
"I'll end up making the worst possible assumptionーthat, overwhelmed by sadness, you'll come to accept me, you know that?"
Even at this very moment… I can't deny the truth that "she" is the only thing on my mind right now.
Even on the day when I lose that which is most precious to me, sure enough, these white flakes have appeared before me once again.
The snow will cover up all of it.
It will cover up the pain, the sadness… and the truth that I do not want to face.
A white world abundant only in beauty expands before our eyes, leaving us there in its wake.
But at the end of the day… snow is all that it is.
Once it melts, all of the hidden truths and forgotten emotions it had been hiding will once again be brought into daylight for all to see.
Dark and filthy, like mud trampled on over and over.
"Lemme go! Besides, why am I the only one who's required to stay anyway?"
"It's not just you! Look, we've still got three people here!"
"No, you have two left. Though you had six people here just ten minutes ago, it's a wrap. All gone. The club fell apart in mere moments."
"Who's going to play the drums, then!? We've got no one else. Are you abandoning us too?"
"Then what about our bassist? The keyboard player? And what about that singer, who happened to be the first to leave?"
"L-Look, I'll think of something! It only took a month to gather those members anyway…"
"The school festival is next month. So tell me… how exactly do you plan on making it?"
"Mmmh… Maybe ask the guys who are already good at this? You know, the music students?"
"As if they'd be willing to mess around with amateurs like us."
"They only gather a few people in their circle and play obnoxiously difficult songs every year. They'd be inviting us to a dream world in all the wrong ways."
"Those guys were always about classical stuff. It's such a waste at a festival, it just puts everyone to sleep."
"They don't know what it means to have fun, always acting like every year is some kind of competition."
"They're not seeing the big picture. It's not like we're going for the fine arts or something, y'know?"
"Yeah, we're really in one hell of a mess here…"
"Well, now that this discussion is over, I'll be excusing myself."
"Ahh!? When did you manage to derail the conversation!?"
"Hang in there, Iizuka. I'll be praying for your success. And I'll be sure to put a white flag on your grave!"
"Hold it right there, Fujishiro! You traitor! Come back here! Come back here right now!"
"I'll haunt you! I'll curse you! I'm gonna get back at you one day!"
"They don't even realize that they'd be the stars of the school festival. That's why they're just giving up."
"What the hell is your school life for anyway? You can only do this while you're still young, you know?"
"Don't direct that aura of despair toward me! This isn't over yet!"
The conflict between the two of them seems to have died down, and thus only the two of us remained.
Perhaps it's better to say the two of them were so caught up in the heat of it all that they completely forgot I was even here.
…I guess it was inevitable for things to turn out like this, though, to an extent.
"Hey, Haruki, what are we going to do? Looks like it's just you and me now…"
"No, it's just you. Even though six people were here just ten minutes ago."
"You traitor! Who's gonna play the guitar if you leave!?"
Only two guitarists remain. Right now, we seem more like a folk music club.
"Haah… Why would things end up like this? The festival is happening next month!"
"It's because you decided things on your own without taking my advice into consideration."
"Well, Haruki, you lecture people way too much."
"For the record, Takeya. I did warn you from the very beginning, didn't I? You shouldn't have brought that girl here."
"Speak of the devil, here it comes again…"
That's right. A single underclassman started all of this.
"I never said that a female singer was a bad idea. But you should have seen this coming from a mile away."
She was the runner-up in the underground Miss Houjou High contest during the school festival last year, and is one of the favorites this year.
"I know that, but… she said that she really wanted to try no matter what."
She apparently has plans to enter showbiz, and that seemed to be one of the reasons why she entered this year's contest with some extraordinary enthusiasm.
"The burning passion deep inside of her was just dying to burst out, as if to say she wouldn't allow anyone to get in her way…"
Simply put, it looked like she wanted to promote herself by going on stage during this year's festival…
"Well, I got a bit of an advance payment from her, you see…"
Consequently, our light music club was subject to her influence.

Every year, someone is nominated to be club president in order to gather volunteers in the three months leading up to the school festival. This year, it happened to be none other than my dearest friend, Iizuka Takeya.
"Rare as it may be, you've been had, Takeya. And this is the result."
And this one girl, who was abruptly brought in, caused friction among all the club members.
"…I guess you can't judge a woman by her looks."
To put it simply, she's the ultimate circle crusher.
"You did the same thing yourself, didn't you?"
She did everything in her power to persuade and manipulate members who were not satisfied with her.
"You can tell I'm that kind of person from a single glance, so I'd say I'm justified."
How do I know just how far she had gone? Well, simply put, I was also one of her targets.
"Hey, there's nothing you're going to get out of convincing me, you know?"
…Yeah, the word "persuade" is definitely an understatement.
I dare not say in what way, however.
"Without a doubt… this is quite a mess."
"We've already signed up to perform at the festival, and the program has to be submitted shortly… We have to pull ourselves together somehow."
"Indeed. This is a truly serious situation."
"I can't think of anyone who'd help us make it happen… You know anyone?"
"…Of course not. But bowing my head and begging the music students isn't really an option either…"
"Would they condescend to us and pick us apart bit by bit before actually refusing, or would they toss us aside with a single word, I wonder?"
"You're in… quite the predicament, aren't you? Between a rock and a hard place."
"You're not worried at all! You're treating it like it's someone else's problem!"
"I can tell by the song you're playing right now! Actually, you're doing that on purpose, aren't you!?"
"Oh no, not at all! My body's just moving on its own…"
"Oh, forget it! I was stupid to think I could rely on you to do all the work!"
"Wait, that was your intention all along…?"
"I'll find them for sure! An expert bassist, a genius drummer, a brilliant keyboardist, and a beautiful singer!"
"So you really haven't learned anything from this, have you!?"
"See ya! I won't let you join us even if you come crying and begging later!"
…And just like that, I find myself alone in Music Room 1, which we can only use twice a week.
Only a month and a half left… Since we can only practice here another ten times, the situation really has devolved into a pure blank slate.
Truth be told, I was only pretending to be indifferent in front of that irresponsible, carefree club president…
With that being said, in one way or another, I expected something like this would happen. Even though I was hoping it wouldn't.
The singer may have been someone akin to a calculating scientist who balanced the friendships among us guys on a scale…
But even so, if I had her popularity, good looks, and silver tongue, I could probably achieve my goals rather easily as well.
On an October evening in late fall, with the school festival happening soon next month…
I, Kitahara Haruki, of Houjou High School's Class 3-E, could only let out a deep sigh, out of anyone else's sight.
"Yeah, I'm changing my vote for the second-year Yanagihara from 'very high' to 'high.'"
Being an executive committee member for the school festival's Miss Houjou High in all but name, one needs the resolve to use even a drawback like this to their advantage in the information war.
"You were the one saying that Ogiso's winning streak might be broken the third time around though. What's with this turn of events?"
"Polls are living things. Predictions I made yesterday may be absolutely useless today. We have to deal with the fact that information changes on a daily basis."
"So there are no worthy challengers this year either, then…?"
"Come on, weren't you listening? The predictions I make today may be useless tomorrow."
"Well, still… personally, I have no objections to Ogiso having such a large lead."
Houjou High School's festival takes place on the same day as Houjou University's festival, right next to our campus.

The university's festival gets swarmed every year not only by local visitors but also by those from outside the prefecture. As such, it's a given that our own festival is pitifully small in comparison, since our high school is merely affiliated with and shares the university's name.

Nevertheless, we manage to drag over spillover visitors from the neighboring university through whatever means necessary, from luring them in to having them think we're some rest stop. This makes the turnout every year fairly decent.

Among other things, there are some cunningly placed signboards within the university, and in a sense, the enthusiasm surrounding the Miss Houjou High contest is greater than anything on the university campus. For us, anyway.
The actual Miss Houjou University event steals the stage on the last day of the university's festival each year, and has transformed into an event that even attracts the press.

However, merely being affiliated with the university, we are not allowed to have the kind of autonomy which they hold. We had to consider public criticism, the decisions made by staff, and the fact that the school directors never formally approved the holding of our beauty pageant.
Except, the High School's students had reached that rebellious age. Pretending to concede, they shifted their efforts underground.
And so, those upperclassmen that smoldered underground… they, the organizers of the school festival executive committee, opened up Miss Houjou High behind the scenes.
Since it's an anti-social tradition, it's no wonder it's been passed on for generations now, that's just plain common sense in this world.
It lacks stage events and a swimsuit competition.
An underground beauty pageant where regular attendees of the school festival are encouraged to vote for their favorite girl… based on pamphlets with photos that are distributed on the day.
Given that it was hardly anything spectacular, the students' regulations and the campus' tacit consent had clued in that it was a failure in the making.
On top of that, the champion that was crowned when I enrolled has still not been dethroned.
"Morning. Day after day, you're exactly five minutes late."
"Have you ever considered that if only you arrived five minutes earlier, you wouldn't have to hear those unpleasant personal lectures of his?"
"Well, just keep that in the back of your mind. Now then, let's work hard today, shall we?"
In the late autumn The neighboring student does Not a single thing
"Okay, now turn this way and smile～"
"Naturally, having won consecutively for the last two years, we understand you have high hopes for winning again this year. Are you feeling enthusiastic going into this?"
"'I'll work hard without forgetting my original goal,' then… Do you have any rivals this time? Anyone you're wary of?"
"Next is… sorry, could you turn that way? I'd like to get a profile shot too."
"'Anyone participating is my rival,' then… Right, and to finish up, could you give us a short self-introduction, please?"
"Ah, your introduction alone will be uploaded to the website, so I'd like you to speak directly into this."
"We'll only be uploading it onto the Houjou school network anyway, and right now the security's being set up, so this won't leak out. Of course, if you don't want to, just a text comment will do."
"Actually, he's on the committee. I'm just a helper…"
"I'm Hayasaka, from Class E. Nice to meet you."
"Ah, is that so? Umm, well, you see…"
"Ah, there you are. Haruki, did you get permission for the Rugby Team's stand?"
"I already sent a letter yesterday. Explaining all the details to the club president."
"All right, thanks. Sorry for bugging you all the time."
"…Uh, sorry for getting distracted. So… where were we again?"
"Listen, I'm pretty sure saying this right now, seems really inexcusable…"
"This year, I'm going to have to withdraw from the contest…"
"…Do you mean that… you've never really liked events like this from the very beginning?"
"B-But you entered both last year and the year before…"
"My friends simply wrote my name down. I was really reluctant to do this from the start."
"Even if you say so, you've won two years in a row since enrolling. What's this all about now…?"
"I found you, Kitahara-kun! How's the pamphlet proofreading going?"
"It'll be finished tonight. You can make the request to the printing shop this coming Monday."
"Thank you, I'm in your debt! Be sure to bring it tomorrow morning."
"Once I've worked out the details… Sorry, I got distracted again."
"The entry requirements state that people can enter 'personally, or by proxy,' but only with consent, of course. If you don't like it, Ogiso, we can revoke your entry."
"Whether you're from the executive committee or the student council, you can't force people to participate. In the end, the school festival is really just a festival, remember?"
"I'm just a helper, so I've tried my best not to butt in."
"Well, you're butting in right now, full-force. In fact, you're doing everything by yourself."
"That's because I couldn't stand watching you guys act like this. There's less than two months until the festival, how can you guys be so carefree?"
"…Anyway, let's get back on topic. Forcing people to participate is off limits. Any objections?"
"Besides, I'm sure Ogiso's got her own share of worries. She'd be troubled if she became too famous."
"Oh, Kitahara! Sorry about this, but could you make sure this gets to Nishiyama? He's sick at home today…"
"Aah, I'll give it to him on my way home. I just need to drop it off, right?"
"So then, what happens if he stays home tomorrow? Fine, I'll be sure to pick it up as well."
"Really? Can I leave it to you? I'm really grateful. I'll be counting on you, then!"
"Anyway, we'll revoke your entry. I assume you're fine with that, Chikashi?"
"I apologize for my lack of courtesy. See you."
"All right, on to the next one. Let's finish up as much as we can today."
"Let's see… The next one is Yanagihara from Class 2-C."
"…How about we call it a day?"
"What happened to that pointless sense of responsibility of yours just now, huh?"
"…I'm renouncing my withdrawal. I'm Ogiso Setsuna from Class 3-A. Let's do our best together this year too."
"You know what… I do have some responsibility; in my case, as someone who was chosen."
"I am, but… it's no big deal…
"And what's your reason for going out of your way to tell that to Haruki, rather than me?"
"So in the end, was all that just on a whim?"
"I… seriously respect you, man. The way you can persuade someone just by turning your back to them."
"Good work… Oh, it's just you, Takeya. Where are the other members?"
"Thank you for not holding back the sarcasm, oh great friend of mine."
Music Room 1, which we can only use twice a week.

This person loitering around without preparing for anything right nowーthe president of the Light Music Club, a student from the same grade who's been in the class next to mine for the past two yearsーis an inseparable friend of mine.
"No dice. Absolutely nothing. The good ones are all more or less participating elsewhere."
It's been two days since our club essentially fell apart.
Speaking from experience, one should never rely on Takeya to try to mend friendships destroyed over a woman. However, there he was, running around trying to find new members…
"Finding an expert bassist, genius drummer, brilliant keyboardist, and a genuinely beautiful female singer… may be nothing more than a pipe dream…"
"So why aren't you just looking for people who are somewhat experienced with the bass, drums, keyboard, and a somewhat cute singer?"
Though, for reasons beyond my control, it seems it was pointless after all.
"What we're talking about right now isn't the dream of a magnificent future. It's about the reality of how we need to perform in a month."
"…What kind of pronunciation was that just now?"
"It's only been two days since this problem came up! It's absurd to give up so soon…"
"It's been two days, and there's about a month and maybe ten days left till the main performance."
"The only conclusion I'm drawing is that it was hopeless from the start. Maybe I've just been discouraged by these long past two days."
"But Takeya… you've been so fired up about making the most of these three years…"
That was also his reason for dragging me into the club as a backup member, even though I had no experience playing the guitar at all until third year.
"Indeed I was… I even came up with signs for when we're on stage."
"Like, I'd put up my thumb like this, and it would be a sign to Keiko meaning, 'I'm playing just for you.'"
"Clapping would be the sign to Reina. Walking up to the front while waving would be the sign to Yuu. And finally, playing with the guitar facing up, the sign to Nozomi…"
"It would have all made such a great compilation…"
"What exactly are you trying to compile here!?"
Backstage after the performance would have been terrifying…
"I've told you this before, Takeya… so I'll spell it out clearly for you today."
"You've spelled it out many, many times for me already, so just stop bothering me already."
"To begin with, the one you really love is…"
"Stop! Even if you are my best friend, I won't hear any further than that."
"Besides, it'll only burden you further, Haruki."
"I don't really mind… I'm only participating in what I want to do."
"Sure, you're like that now. But as soon as the people around you run into problems, you're off taking charge of everything."
"That's also… something I do of my own volition."
I'm amazed that I can't even find the words to deny that.

"You're not only helping us, you're also doing things for the festival committee, the executive committee, being the admin of the school web page, being the class representative, even on the library committee… besides the fact that you're just lending a hand."
"I'm starting to feel horrible here, so please leave it at that."
Tonight's schedule runs through my head from him simply listing all of my positions… I'll be lucky if I even get two hours of sleep tonight.
"You know… I may seem like I'm rather self-centered and only care for myself, but I still make sure to watch out for my best friend too."
"I suppose I do agree with the first half of what you said…"
But with that said, I don't plan on completely denying the latter half either.
It's true that he was being run ragged by girls at about the same frequency as the other two primal urges.
But, in his case, he didn't seem to hold any grudges, and he even had the thoughtfulness to introduce me to his exes.
…Though I'm not sure it's appropriate to call that being thoughtful, at any rate, there's no doubt that he looked out for me.
And besides, up until last year, he wasn't like the people that had come and gone…
"I don't know. It just happened to match up."
Takeya pokes his head outside the window, leaning his ear toward the neighboring classroom.
Toward the piano that's playing in sync with my guitar.
The first time I noticed was about two months ago.
I wasn't part of the actual group that was set to perform during the festival. I wouldn't join in when the club was practicing, and when they'd leave, I'd end up practicing a lot on my own.
That piano accompanied me many times, until I finally got into shape. And when it was pleased with my form, it accompanied my music.
It was a mysterious sound that would pull pranks on me, guide me, and even show me my weaknesses simply through hearing it.
"He doesn't always play the piano. Sometimes it's the bass, or the drums…"
Though last week, he caught me off guard by suddenly playing the saxophone.
"Are they doing band practice in there as well?"
"Who knows? I've never heard 'them' play together. Seems like he's alone."
Which is precisely why he intervenes when I'm alone. Seems like he has a lot of spare time.
That was also par for the course.
No matter what instrument or song, he's never missed a note.
…Perhaps he's had a lot of practice. He certainly does seem to have a lot of spare time.
"…Hey, Takeya. That gives me an idea."
"…I haven't even said anything yet though?"
"Music Room 2 is the music students' territory. They're not gonna get involved in our nonsense."
The answer he had prepared was far too comprehensive.
"I swear, the music students are like feudal lords. They only have a single class for each grade, yet they have the other two music rooms all to themselves."
Houjou High School has three music rooms. Music Room 1 and 2 are here in the main building. There's an annex opposite of us connected by two sections where there's an extra-large third music room.
However, all the clubs have to share the cramped Music Room 1. Unlike the other two, which are reserved only for the music students' classes, the eighth class of each grade.
It goes without saying that it's a haven for people who have hopes of getting into a music career. We also have to think of the school's interests as well, so there's nothing we can really do.
But there is no way us regular students would be satisfied with this state of affairs. Hence, the regular and music students have traditionally been at odds with each other.
"Since the girls were all like spoiled princesses, I'd figured they'd be easy to trick… but before long they would start droning on about lessons, or competitions, or whatever."
Though I suppose that's not the only serious grievance in his particular case.
"Well, that aside, my chances were pretty slim to begin with. Especially since I'm in third year already, things have gotten pretty tough."
"And it's always about that Matsukawa guy. Him getting third place in the spring national competition was a pretty big deal apparently."
"Then, you think Matsukawa-kun's the one next door?"
"You didn't check to see if it was him? You two seem to always be at it."
"It's locked tight. Not even a crevice in the door, and the curtains are always drawn shut."
"…That's pretty shy. Maybe he's doing secret special training?"
I'd be lying if I said I wasn't curious. Even more so with him trying to hide behind the Iron Curtain like he is.
To an amateur such as myself, his piano playing is perfect. And although not as perfect, his bass, drums, and saxophone all hold up well.
If he really is doing this all by himself, he's impossibly multi-talented. Maybe not a prodigy of an artist, but certainly an amazing performer.
Though I can't really tell, since we've never actually met. Houjou High's music students are not to be underestimated either…
"I already knew, but you're really not getting any better."
"That's because you just won't shut up!"
This guy can't be my best friend, no way.

Having finished that heated session feeling satisfied with myself, and after lecturing Kazuji for not being sick in even the slightest at his home in Nishiyama, the red of the autumn evening sky had faded away before I could realize it.
Past Minami-Suetsugu Station, the entertainment district for the students; the second closest station to school, Suetsugu-chou Station, shows an unchanging scenery.
The florist turns off the brilliant lights within her store, emphasizing its solitary atmosphere in front of the station.
A girl with braids diligently stocks the shelves of a supermarket's storefront.
An elderly person with a cane leisurely walks up and down the street, clearly without a real destination in mind…
…And I run into someone unusual there.
Although there wouldn't be anything unusual about running into her at school.
"What're you doing around here? The station here goes opposite from where you live, doesn't it?"
Takeya introduced me to her during our first year as a girl he'd been "inseparable from since middle school."
"And what about you, going the same way I am?"
"The prep school's this way, you see…"

She used to be the girls' basketball club's captain, although she's retired right now. A noteworthy figure in terms of physical ability and leadership, all the while possessing a talent for meddling perhaps even greater than mine.
"I see… Speaking of which, I heard you're having trouble getting a recommendation for university. Despite already clearing two-thirds of your requirements, no less."
"Shaddup. I don't want a coward who's constantly studying saying that to me."
"What's cowardly about following my primary responsibility as a student?"
…Despite that, she's become an important friend of mine. Although, since I exceed her in both grades and grace, I'm not terribly conscious of the fact that she's of the opposite sex.
"…Oh yeah, Ogiso's in the same class as you are, right?"
"What's this? You're interested in Setsuna? Could it be that you're finally interested in girls, just like any other average guy?"
And yes, this tactlessness is also one of her traits.
"I've always been average. In fact, I don't think there's any other male student closer to 'average' than I am."
Usually I'd justify myself by saying, "I only look quiet because of who you keep comparing me to," but due to various circumstances, I decided to hold it in.
"I see, spring has finally come for you too, Haruki… If you could just direct your devotion in that direction, you'd definitely be able to become way more popular than Takeya."
"Except, that's not how it is, you know…"
"…Still, aren't you setting the bar rather high? It'd be better if you started with a girl that Takeya could introduce to you."
"In how many ways are you trying to insult me with that single comment?"
This lack of delicacy of hers is quite troublesome…
"But this is Setsuna we're talking about! The girl who won Miss Houjou twice in a row! The one rumored to win for a third time now!"
"For a rumor, that sounds awfully likely to happen…"
Besides, if anyone else won, it'd be the first time anyone would've done so since our enrollment.
"And she's way up there, you know? I don't think she's someone a beginner like you could handle."
"You seem to know quite a bit. Is she dating someone?"
"Don't even speak of dating, she hardly hangs out with anyone. She doesn't even come when she's invited to go shopping or to karaoke after school."
"Not really. I just met her yesterday. That's all."
Io senses that "this conversation is over" by my refusal to divulge further.
"Ah, by the way, I heard things are going pretty bad with your club for the school festival performance?"
…Or so I thought. A miscalculation on my part, it seems.
"Takeya's carefree attitude has gotten him into some bad luck there. He should've learned his lesson already."
"Is Takeya really all that carefree? In his own way, he's…"
"I've been hanging out with him for a very long time, you know. I can already tell what that idiot's doing anyway. I bet it's trouble with a girl again, isn't it?"
"Don't you think that his personality became all twisted like this because he's been hanging out with you for so long?"
…Is what I want to say, but considering the fact that I might have to stick around this girl for another four years, I decide to keep my mouth shut.
"Next is… Umm, Hayasaka-kun, if you would please."
Confirming that Chikashi is safe, my eyes once again return to the bundle of papers in front of me.
10:00, Drama Club - The Demon of Uzukiyama 11:00, Wind Instrument Club - Game Music Medley.
"They can't even fit in fifteen minutes of intermission? What about ten…?"
I pointlessly groan at the stage program for the school festival.
Tomorrow morning is the final deadline for submitting the program of the stage events. In other words, today's pretty much the last day for all entries to be collected.
Changes or additions can still happen after today, but then there won't be any advance notice. They'll just get announced on the school web page.
"Switching from stage drama to musical performance takes fifteen minutes. Then from one musical performance to another, it should be ten… How's that?"
Which is why I need to fit in as much as possible right now.
Even though I'm not part of the school festival executive committee, nor am I in charge of the program. And in truth, I don't really have any power…
I don't really feel it's irrational or pointless, but even with my burning sense of responsibility and nosy tendencies, it seems that this too, is far beyond my capabilities.
From the eyes of a school festival committee assistant, this is the moment where everything goes back to square one.
And as a member of the Light Music Club, I can't help but give a light sigh.
Takeya had me register as soon as the stage event started taking applications…
That's how we managed to secure the stage when it's at its liveliest, not to mention easiest to advertise.
I thought doing so would be to our advantage at the time, but now I'm not so sure…

"Sorry! I never told you, did I? He was feeling ill so he headed home early today."
"Uh, umm… he's got the stomach flu, so I don't think he'll be back for another two or three days. Yeah, when he comes back, I'll introduce you two."
"It's your fault for putting on a show, right? You should have just told her the truth that we don't actually have a pianist."
"And then tell her we don't have a bassist, or a drummer, or anyone at all!?"
"Don't misplace your anger. This isn't like you, Haruki."
"Well… there's the old saying, 'A man in love has the strength of a million horses.'"
"You just keep talking. Your sarcasm won't work on me now."
"But, if you keep fooling people like that, you're not gonna be able to back out at some point."
"When that happened, I had to do so many things just to preserve my image…"
What I'm doing right now is exactly what Ogiso has been doing for the past two years.
In order to get others interested in me, I'm leaving misunderstandings as they are, and slowly driving myself into a corner.
…Even so, telling Ogiso the truth now would completely destroy her motivation.
Because when she spontaneously started singing like that, it wasn't just because of my crappy guitar playing.
It's because the fluent piano was there to match my clumsy melody.
"H…Hey… are you really gonna bow your head before the music students? I don't like this."
"You don't have to come, Takeya… But right now, begging that 'Matsukawa-kun' is the only option we have."
The fluent pianist that would always improvise, no matter which melody I played.
Our Light Music Club, which currently only has guitarists, was in desperate need of such abilities.
I take a deep sigh in the empty classroom.
My body and mind are both at their limits…
"I'm never going to bother with those music guys again. Why are they all so prideful anyway?"
Despite the enthusiasm I had for the music students, in the end, it was exactly as Takeya had predicted.
"Still, what's up with that…? Then who's using Music Room 2…?"
…No, the result is much worse than the prediction.
I found Matsukawa-kun in an instant. He was skinny, tall, and wore glasses with a rather strong index. He seemed like a very nervous guy.
…And after talking with him for a little bit, my first impression of his crowd was right on the mark.
When he heard my request, Matsukawa wouldn't stop mocking the foolishness of the Light Music Club.
Declaring that we are disorganized, reckless and disgusting, and that being the amateurs we are, we should just give up since it won't end well anyway.
Still, despite his terrible personality, what kept me talking to him and stopping Takeya from pouncing on him was his enchanting piano playing.
But then, at the end… that bastard said something unforgivable.
"Anyway, I've never even used Music Room 2. There's no one in this class that uses it. There's no way anyone would approach that detestable place!"
…This time, it was Takeya who was trying to stop me from pouncing on him.
"If that's how it is, then just say so to begin with… We'd have left in an instant with that…"
Then I wouldn't have had to take all those insults.
And with that, we're back to square one with finding the owner of Music Room 2.
The only thing we've learned so far is the fact that no one from the music program uses the second room.
The truth is, even though we asked people other than Matsukawa, they all said, "We've never used Music Room 2."
After all, Class H has the spacious Music Room 3. It looks like they'd have no real reason to go out of their way to use a music room on the other side of the building.
The music students seem to think Music Room 2 is exclusively used by regular students, while regular students assume the opposite.
Furthermore, the attitude they had when I asked them about Music Room 2 was quite suspicious.
It seemed like they didn't want to touch the subject. They'd give unpleasant looks, and would try not to get involved.
Even if it's true that no one from the music program uses the room, somehow it feels like they know something.
Perhaps their attitude is the key to solving this mystery…?
No one should even be using that music room. A piano that echoes… and nobody knows anything…
One of the school's… seven mysteries.
"The owner of Music Room 2." Could he possibly have passed away long ago…?
"Ah, n-no, wait, sorry. It's my fault for getting spooked for no reason…"
"Wait, wait, wait! I said I was sorry! I'm sorry, okay?"
What am I doing? Throwing away the lifetime opportunity of getting to talk with my neighbor, who speaks maybe once a month?
…Speaking of which, a few days ago she did come to speak to me, but I seem to remember completely ignoring her.
"U-Umm, how come you're staying this late? Are you in a club?"
"You're not playing that crappy guitar today?"
"…We can only use the music room twice a week. We're a miserable little club, after all."
"Are you gonna be fine going to the school festival like that?"
"…We're doing fine. We've even found a singer."
"Listen and shudder! It turns out she's…"
"I'm not listening, so I won't be shuddering."
We haven't held a conversation this long in months, so why isn't it going anywhere?
…I guess this being the first time in months we've properly communicated is the very reason for that.
"Don't you have any members besides the guitarists and the singer?"
We haven't held a conversation this long in months, so why is it drowning me in such sorrow?
Come on, Chikashi, that was uncalled for.
Her seat may be right behind you, but there are things you shouldn't tell others.
"A man on the verge of tears isn't cute at all."
"It's fine… It's all good! We still have one last secret weapon!"
Though it feels like it just slipped through my fingers a moment ago.
"Oh? Well, good for you. So, who is it?"
"You know, you ignored me every time I came to talk to you, so don't go out of your way to talk to me when I'm down…"
"If you're just gonna make fun of me, go home. I just want some time alone."
"That's right. Okay, goodbye then. Good work. Shoo, shoo!"
It felt like her usual cold gaze had a freezing surge today…
Despite the force of the impact, the classroom door somehow retained its shape.
Once that shudder ceased, the silence I desired in this classroom finally came.
"What am I, an elementary school brat…?"
Once again, my annoyance has only increased.
"My first screw-up in a long time…"
It seems I can't communicate with my neighbor properly. Even though I can talk to Ogiso surprisingly well.
We ended up in the same class when I entered third year. I'm ashamed to say it, but I hadn't even known she was around before then.
I could never get used to her blunt attitude, and she could never stomach my nosy attitude, so we were in conflict since the very beginning.
But now, when I thought our relationship was finally making progress for the better…
…At least she didn't get physical with me, though she did seem pretty fed up.
She's one of the few girls I know that I've always wanted to get along with.
Now that I think of it, maybe I'm the type of person who pays a lot of attention to girls' appearances.
When I awakened, I realized I had fallen asleep.
It seems my body and mind were exhausted from having two consecutive events spinning round my head.
Stretching out hard and trying to regain my senses, I slowly glance over the classroom.
In doing so, I notice the significantly darker shade of red engulfing the empty room.
Looking at the time, it seems like it's just past five. In the end, I'd also slept through my usual practice time.
Insulted for no reason, going back to square one, and then getting into an argument.
In the end, I never found out who the owner of Music Room 2 is. On top of that, the piano has been silent since that time when the three of us were in harmony.
What if… he never returns to Music Room 2…?
The piano has been silent since that time when the three of us were in harmony…?
It… was playing just now, right?
And it stopped playing just now, right?
With how dazed I was, I'd completely ignored the melody that was playing just after I woke up.
It was such a professional performance that I probably ignored it, like one would ignore the sound of music playing on a busy city street.
…Although I came up with a bunch of excuses, it doesn't make up for the fact that I'd made a fatal mistake…
I hadn't noticed at all the moment I opened the door…
The truth is, today was the first time Music Room 2 was left unlocked.
The chilly breeze flowing in from the open window.
The rattling of the curtains, spurred on by the force of that breeze.
The magnificent grand piano sitting there, enshrined, right in the middle of the classroom.
But as expected… there's no one here.
The partner that was out of my league, who always accompanied my guitar.
Just a moment ago, as usual, he was playing with a sound that was casual, profound, elegant, and stubborn.
I got insulted by Matsukawa from the music program for no real reason.
The search for the owner of Music Room 2 going back to square one.
Then… getting in a pointless argument with the neighboring student.
And wasting my chance at almost catching the owner of Music Room 2, through my own blunder.
But, at the end of that blunder, right at the end of it all, I'd grabbed that fine thread.
"I'll catch you next time. I'll make sure of it."
After many days of complete silence, the piano in Music Room 2 has played its melody.
And thus, I've been granted another chance.
He wasn't one of the seven mysteries of the school, the ghost of a pianist.
He was just a complacent human being who was wary and securely locked the door during practice time. Yet he forgot to lock the door and window when heading home.
It's been a day since I just barely missed the owner of Music Room 2.
As I predicted, he started practicing again yesterday.
"I'm… going in. I'm counting on you should anything happen to me."
"Hey, Haruki… before you go over there, you want to check out how you look right now, just once more?"
"…Don't remind me. I'd just mustered the courage for this, too…"
Thanks to Takeya uttering that one comment, my eyes fell upon the unsightly appearance around my waist.
The way the tug-of-war rope I'd snatched from the gym storage room was tied to my torso was quite conspicuous.
One end of the rope was anchored to a pillar in the classroom. Perfect.
…Though when I first checked its length, it exceeded the building's height by a decent amount, so it wouldn't work very well as a lifeline…
"If he won't open the door, then you could just wait for him to come out. Why go through the window?"
"If I used such an obvious approach, I don't think that person would accept my request…"
After all, thinking about it, this person doesn't even want people to see him when he's practicing. From that, I'm almost certain he's someone hard to please.
…At the very least, it's clear that he's an oddball who's willing to play with me, there's no doubt about that.
I have dim prospects for directly approaching such a person. I must make as much of an impact as possible to catch his interest, or this isn't going to work out.
"Besides, people say 'fool around while you're still young,' right?"
"No they don't. You're Japanese, so speak proper Japanese."
"All right, I'm going this time. Watch the rope for me."
"Be careful… getting hurt for something like this would be really stupid."
With Takeya's warm encouragement from behind, I take a step outside the window frame.
Two meters between here and Music Room 2's window.
For starters, I should move along the rain gutter between classrooms, and then jump to new footing at the other classroom.

I've checked that both distance and strength are fine plenty of times. If I have the reflexes of an average man, I should have some leeway. If I don't, then my lifeline should keep me in check, at least.
…Still, that became nothing more than wishful thinking once I actually looked down from the third floor.
This is… higher than I thought…
The wall's hard. And rough, at that…
Even if I have a lifeline, should I lose my grip, my body would smash into the wall…
Bringing back my fighting spirit to forget the fear in my heart, I close my eyes and grab the rain gutter.
…Then, after realizing it's too reckless to do this with no sight, my eyes spring wide open.
Hold onto the rain gutter… and move my feet along…
It looks like my first step was a success.
As soon as I put my entire body weight on the rain gutter, I hear a disturbing, creaking sound. I do my best to ignore it, control my breath, and reach for the window of the next classroom.
Since the window happens to be open like always, my left hand is somehow able to grab hold of the window frame.
My left hand latches onto the window frame, and even my left foot gets in.
All that's left is to kick hard with my right leg from the rain gutter, and slip into the room just like that.
Just you wait… owner of Music Room 2.
Making sure of my final destination, I peep into the window, the grand piano in the middle of the classroom clearly visible.
Though there was no one there yesterday, and although it's really obvious to say this, he's there sitting now, playing wholeheartedly with his fingers on the piano.
No… there's nothing obvious about it, actually.
I can only see "him" from behind.
Glossy black hair dances across the student's back.
"His" build is smaller than I had expected.
It isn't just the fingers, it's as if the entire body is vividly putting itself into playing the piano.
Sensitive, with a small face, and most importantly, the paleness of the face from the side.
However, wiping away all those minor details, what absolutely enthralls me is that strong melody ringing in my ears.
I had decided that it was a guy at some point, but now I realize that I had no basis in doing so.
Not to mention… not to mention, this girl is…
"Hey, you there! What are you doing!?"
Just as I was about to take a step forward to check "her" face…
My actions, which may or may not be a violation of the school rules, are found out by the school staff.
"Aaaaaahhh!? Someone, hurry up and bring a mat over!"
And… the best-case scenario I had in mind for this mission is being proven impossible at this very moment.
My lifeline hadn't been of use yet.
The moment my feet slipped, my arms desperately reached out and managed to grab the bottom of the window frame.
So all that was left was to pull myself up, elevate my body as much as I could, and magnificently jump into the classroom…
I'm sure I could do that… if I was grabbing onto an iron rod.
My fingers are currently hanging onto the window frame, so I can't focus the power in my arms.
And most importantly… right now, I am completely baffled.
I can't hear anything. Not even Takeya calling out to me, or the riot below me.
Because… just on the verge of falling, I've found out who "she" is…
"You were the one… playing the piano!?"
The owner of Music Room 2… is none other than my neighboring student.
"Kitahara… what are you doing, you idiot…?"
The neighboring student in my class.
"Touma… hey… sorry to bother you, but I need you to wake up for a bit."
"Ahh!? Excuse me, sorry… you're Touma Kazusa, right?"
"You haven't attended school since the opening ceremony, right? Have you been sick?"
"I do realize that we weren't doing much in classes while you were absent, but there were a lot of notices and forms handed out…"
"Here are the textbooks for all your subjects, your student ID card, and all the forms in the order in which you should be turning them in."
"Oh, also… in case you need it, I got you a form to get the student ticket discount. You come to school by train from Iwazu-chou, right?"
"And this is the one thing you mustn't forgetーthe parent-teacher meeting printout. It's starting next week, so be sure to pass this on to your guardian."
"I was planning on bringing all this directly to your house, but I had a lot of things to do… Sorry about that."
"Do you have any questions regarding anything up to now? I'll try to answer what I can."
"…Next, I'll explain how to fill out these documents. We'll start with the form for buying the school jersey."
"I get that a lot, but this is important. If I'm annoying you, then do your best to memorize it all the first time so I don't have to repeat it."
"Ah… that's right. We haven't met before. I'm Kitahara Haruki. For what it's worth, I'm the class representative for Class E for the first half of the year."
"Well, your face had 'Who the hell are you?' written all over it, you see."
"…Hold on, are you still feeling sick after all? Do you want to go to the nurse's office? I can take you there."
"Hm? No, I haven't actually touched you yet."
"…I understand. We can do this later. Oh, that's right! If you'd like, I could take these to your house after school…"
At the time, I'm pretty sure I retorted in my mind with, "Pretty sure I haven't touched you at all."
But to begin with, she… the way Touma Kazusa kept using the phrase, "Don't touch me" wasn't in its literal sense.
I must have realized soon enough that it was akin to a "keep out" warning… that she was telling me not to get involved with her all along.
I was so consumed by boredom… or rather by self-admonition, so much that I'd unconsciously escaped to the past.
Well, the memories I escaped to weren't really all that beautiful either.
"Tell me, why'd you do something like that? You know full well how badly hurt you could have gotten if you'd fallen from there, right?"
"Ah, umm, that was… I'm sorry, I wasn't thinking straight at all."
"Well, even if you insist that's the case…"
It's been a day since that mess.
Despite the fact that I was scolded right on the spot, it'd become so much of a problem that the homeroom teacher also lectured me the next morning.

"This isn't like you, Kitahara. Normally you'd be the one preventing others from acting out like this. Did you think that since you're not the class representative anymore that you can just toss out your responsibilities?"
"No, that's not what I… I'm sorry."
"I bet Touma was the one who provoked him anyway. There's no way Kitahara would do something so ridiculous all on his own."
"W-What? Umm, I'm not sure I understand what you mean. Why are you making it sound like it's Touma's fault now?"
In fact, I don't even understand why Touma was dragged in here to be scolded as well.
"I thought that'd be the end of it when you left the music program on your own, but you're still nothing but trouble even among the regulars. Touma, do you even plan on graduating?"
The music program…? And she left on her own…?
"Besides, I was against letting Touma use Music Room 2 exclusively."
"Her parent may be a famous pianist, and said parent might have made a sizable donation to the school, but all that special treatment's starting to get to her head."
"Suwa-sensei, that's enough… I'll be sure to reprimand Touma myself."
For some reason, the conversation is moving away from my misdemeanor.
With all these unexpected and unreasonable accusations being thrown around all over the place, I don't even know when to cut in anymore…
"…Hey, why are you reprimanding Touma? And why is she being blamed alongside me? I'll have you know, she saved my life."
Since I can't stop the conversation from going off-topic, all I can do is bring up that cheap sense of justice of mine for now.
…As expected, of all their reactions, hers was the coldest.
"I've warned you many times, Kitahara. A serious, hardworking guy like you shouldn't get involved with Touma. You don't want to waste your university recommendation, do you?"
"I'm the one you should be angry with. This has nothing to do with Touma, does it?"
"Is she really not involved? Are you sure Touma isn't just getting you to say that?"
I used up all my energy before classes even started… I'm confident I'll be sleeping through first period.
Still though, the attitude those teachers had… What was that? Just thinking about it makes me sick.
Ahh, I know it's not my problem but… No, the fact that it has turned into her problem is the issue here.
"Unbelievable… Why do I have to put up with this…?"
"You should have said that earlier, not now!"
It's too late to regret it now.
"It's pointless to tell the teachers anything. Adults won't understand a thing."
"What's up with that hackneyed rebellious attitude? You're sounding like a delinquent from the Showa Period…"
I have so many things I want to ask her, but…
"…It must have been terrible for you. I'm sorry, it's all my fault."
"I'm 100% sure that your idiocy is to blame for this, Kitahara."
Judging by her expression, I get the feeling Touma isn't all too opposed to the idea of just forgetting about what happened.

"Still, you know, I guess that's the result of my everyday general attitude. If you gained the trust of the teachers, Touma, they might end up needlessly covering for you like they did for me, you know?"
"I refuse to live a calm, boring life like yours… all while sucking up to those above me."
"My life goal, you see, is to live longer than average people."
"You really are a dull guy. The stereotypical class representative, no doubt about it."
"Well, I was the class rep for the first term…"
"You know, I've been wanting to tell you this for a while now…"
Touma's thin, white finger points straight at me to condemn my words…
And then, seeing someone running down the hallway toward us, she unnaturally brings her finger down.
"I heard it all from Iizuka-kun… Are you okay? Your fingers aren't hurt or anything, right?"
"Hmm… I can't tell just by looking at them. Your fingers weren't injured, right? You almost fell from the window, didn't you?"
She nonchalantly lifts up my hands, then spreads them out and carefully investigates them in worry.
I'm glad that she's worried about my injury, but the way Ogiso's fingers are caressing the palm of my hand right now is… it's, how do I say this, quite, um…
"I'm fine, I'm fine, I'm fine already! I'm not hurt anywhere. Anyway, that's not what you should be worried about!"

I instinctively raise my hands above my head so Ogiso can't reach them, relinquishing myself of the blissful sensation of her hands. With that, any chance of explaining myself in a cool-headed manner is out the window.
"Ah, okay… Well, what was the punishment?"
She crosses the fingers she used to embrace my hands earlier over her chest, staring at me with a cute gesture.
"Yeah… They said they'd decide later. Well, I don't think it'll be anything like a suspension, disciplinary action, or suspension of club activities."
"I see… That's a relief. There's only a month left until the school festival, right?"
…And I guess her occasional glance to her right is also a form of affectionate gesturing?
True enough, it doesn't seem like any severe punishment will be levied on me.
"Yeah… What a relief. Since you went through the trouble of joining us, Ogiso, it'd be terrible if we couldn't perform at the school festival."
"Revocation of the Light Music Club's privilege to use the music room."
The very possibility of such a "light punishment" as suggested by Suwa at the end would have been fatal to us right now.
"You're right, it would be really frustrating if we couldn't perform over some silly accident, now that I've finally decided to join."
"Ah…! Umm, that's not what I meant! I wasn't trying to blame you or…"
"Well, anyway, sorry for making you worry. For now, let's leave it at that."
"Alright. Yup, I was really worried. So be sure to reflect deeply on this."
"Just kidding, a few minutes should be enough, hehe!"
Back then, I hadn't noticed it at all.
How perfect Ogiso's timing had been… How Touma's expression had changed ever so slightly…
"Ah, that's right, Ogiso, let me introduce you to her."
After half a year of knowing her, I'm happy that I can casually put my hand on her shoulder, and have her casually punch me with clenched fists in response.
She's no longer saying, "Don't touch me" to me.
So this is Touma when she's not holding back.
Hearing her play unrestrained by my clumsy guitar does sound incredibly cool, but… personally, it just makes me sad.
"Touma Kazusa. Class 3-E, number 32 on the class roster. Part of the go-home club. Address is 6-2-12, Iwazu-chou. Telephone number…"
"You can find all that in the class registry."
Actually, I've memorized the whole thing. Just one of the duties of a class representative.
"But you don't know this, do you? Her class last year was 2-H. The year before that, it was 1-H…"
"She may be our classmate, but that doesn't mean you should go prying into her past."
"You were perfectly content digging through all her other personal info, though."
The last class for each year. In other words, the music program's class.
"Well, in that case, it's no wonder I'd never seen her until last year."
Classes A through G are in the main building. A new building was added for the music program three years ago. Class H stays there, so they never interact with us.
"That wasn't the only reason, it seems…"
"She'd been absent for almost half of second year, and barely passed."
"Could it be, she had problems with her health last year?"
"According to rumors, and from my own experience, the problem appears to have been her personality."
"She still has a bad personality even now, but she's properly coming to school. Although she is late most of the time."
"…Wait a sec. Something you just said bothers me. What do you mean, 'From my own experience'?"
"The first time I saw her was in your classroom, and three days later I tried to ask her out, but she just kicked me out of nowhere!"
"Wait, wait, wait! What were you thinking, acting without a single word of permission from me!?"
"Well… she's the prettiest girl in your class by far, isn't she? She's the only one I'd ask out, you see."
"You won't be satisfied until you have a girl from every class? Do you plan to get 24 girlfriends across all years and classes?"
His immoral line of thought… no, rather, his sharp sense and ability to identify the very finest leaves me in awe…
"No way, I'd definitely pass on the music students. So that makes 21 in total…"
"You don't deserve the company of other guys."
All the girls he's been trying to introduce me to were without a doubt from that 21…
"It's a thing of the past, let's just forget about it. Besides, it's not like she's your girlfriend or anything, right?"
Why am I… at a loss…?
"…Even if she isn't, somehow you're getting along with her."
"W-Well, on the surface, her personality seems bad, but deep inside… I mean, if you get to know her, she's not a bad friend… besides, she sits next to me."
"While we're on the topic… it seems that up until last year, she'd never even talked with any of the other music students."
"Touma Kazusa, you see… was a model student ever since she enrolled in the music program."
From this point on, Takeya starts giving me some incredibly detailed info on her, so detailed and accurate, in fact, that I can't help but believe him.
The only problem is that most of the information he knows is centered around her gender.
During first year, she participated and won in the national competition.
Matsukawa finally placed third at the same contest this year, but she'd already dominated in it two years ago. Touma was in a different league from the very beginning.
At first, the music teachers had all praised Touma. When compared to Touma, her classmates all appeared to be inexperienced amateurs.
Even so, if only she had acted like a normal model student, her classmates would've respected her without fear and would've aspired to be like her without avoiding her.
It would seem that there's something else that, even now, continues to antagonize the relationships she has with others…
"She's Touma's mother, right? I think I remember seeing her name in the guardian register…"
"I figured you'd say that, but it creeps me out that you remember that much."
The truth is, I only know the name of several specific parents. Luckily, he does not pursue the matter further.
"Do you remember, Haruki… there was a whiskey commercial or something years ago, with a lady in a red dress playing the piano."
"Umm… Was that during elementary school? I think they had a series of commercials, with one top artist appearing for each one…."
"Yeah, yeah, that! Anyway, the pianist was the first one in that series."
"Aaah, yeah, there was something like that! I'm sure my mother bought the CD, even though she isn't a fan of classical music at all."
It's true that I remember seeing it credited to Touma Youko on screen. I'm about 80% certain of it.
"She was performing in Japan at the time, it seems she's in Europe now."
Despite being a classical pianist being a small occupation in Japan, her CDs were very popular.
On top of that, it's selling incredibly well, even in the countries where classical music was born.
"Apparently, she donated a substantial amount to our school. The piano in Music Room 2 comes from the Toumas as well."
Her mother happens to be an extremely famous celebrity, even on her own turf.
And if she's also made such a large donation to the school, no wonder the staff would give Touma special treatment..
Yes, for example… preferential treatment, like one music room out of the three being put aside specifically for her use.

"Touma Kazusa had been the gold standard of a student since the music program was established… The teachers were partial to her, and she had status, money, and fame. She was most certainly a student who was given the highest graces…"
"With all of that put together, everyone in her class hated her, and Touma showed no signs of wanting to meet them halfway either."
She was snarling at both the teachers and her classmates equally for looking at her through tinted glasses.
"By second year, she was barely talking to any of her classmates."
"What's with that… What was the class representative doing!?"
"Normal class representatives don't act like you, being so irritatingly nosy, mediating between people, and dealing with every single thing."
Isn't it the representative's job to grit their teeth while taking all the jobs others wouldn't want to do?
…Even if it means that other people may end up hating them.
"Well, with all that, she really couldn't stay there much longer. And then she transferred to the regular program, which brings us to now."
"Well, what'll you do? Will you still try to recruit her into the club?"
With so many emotions swirling around in my mind, I can't immediately provide him with an ideal, logical response like I always would.
"She's going to be a difficult one, that girl. She might refuse, despite getting along with you."
All I can say is that I feel frustrated, and it feels like my rationality is being overshadowed by my emotions. And I'm terrible when it comes to emotional reasoning.
"After all, she even brushed someone like me off. For any other man to be capable of opening up her heart would be…"
Because her piano once matched up with me…
"I'll do whatever it takes to make her one of us."
Because I was enchanted by that sound…
"She's that good, isn't in any clubs, and is in the regular program… There's no reason not to invite her, right?"
On top of that, it's because… she's the one who played that beautiful melody…
"How do you plan on telling Ogiso? You're still lying to her about the pianist, right?"
"I'll explain it properly to her. And I'll apologize too. But… I'll make sure she understands that we absolutely need Touma."
"I won't give up. Because I absolutely need the two of them. They're both invaluable."
"I never thought I'd be hearing that from you."
I may very well be doing something despicable right now.
I'd be lying to someone who'd joined me because they trusted me, and I'd be causing a lot of trouble for a friend who'd saved me.
But I can't stop now. I don't want to stop either.
There's only one month left until the school festival.
There isn't any time left to think this over, have any regrets, or lose my way now.
"Well, anyway, there's just one thing I should warn you about."
"I don't mind you recruiting Touma, but don't do it out of some odd sympathy for her. She'll only be offended if you go out of your way for her."
"Also, don't go off lecturing like you always do. I know you mean well, but there are also times when you should really take a step back."
"No need to tell me twice. I understand myself the best."
"Someone like her would no doubt find your pushy, stubborn attitude annoying. Be really careful, okay?"
"I'm telling you… I won't do annoying things like that. I've been getting along with her for half a year, you know? There's nothing to worry about."
"Don't use that word all of a sudden."
The next day, after hearing about Touma's experience these past two years from Takeya…
Right after school, Touma headed straight for Music Room 2, and just as she opened the door…
"What about your practice? You've only got a month left."
"I was thinking of avoiding that music room until they decide on my punishment."
She found a certain annoying former class representative sitting there, fully prepared to play the part of her eager audience.
"Do you honestly believe you'll make it acting so carefree like this?"
"It'll be fine. In a few days, we'll get someone amazing to join us."
"I see, so you're glad about that too. Then let's get straight to…"
"Though, if I was in this amazing person's shoes, I wouldn't get on your pathetic excuse for a boat, even if I was stranded in the middle of the Pacific Ocean."
Compared to what I've heard from her since the beginning of spring this year… her vocabulary has since expanded beyond expressions like, "Shut up", "Get lost", or "Don't touch me"…
"Even if I remain silent, a certain idiot who can't take a hint will just keep talking anyway."
"Though, even if I tell you that, I have a feeling you won't leave."
"You sure know me well. As expected of a friend."
Personally, I think it's nice that she now follows up with expressions other than, "Shut up", "Get lost", or "Don't touch me."
…Though I would like it even better if we could just start a conversation without having to go through all that trouble.
Is she aware that I'm looking her way…?
Regardless of whether she is, I can only sigh in admiration of Touma's finger movements.
I mean, I can't even keep up with how fast she's moving.
Not only do her fingers move along the keys at incredible speed, but they also easily move from one side of the keyboard to the other. Something that should be hard for her slender hands to do.
Being the amateur I am, I can hear nothing off-key. I can't clearly hear every note, but I can't tell her apart from a professional… Well, I guess that's what makes me an amateur.
It's possible that Touma can no longer feel my presence here.
The look on her face right now is one she normally wouldn't show anyone.
Without me realizing it, she started making use of that "privilege of ignoring me," which she'd earned a month after we met.
"Good morning. Rare to see you arrive before class starts."
"You don't have to look so obviously annoyed."
"Good morning! Good morning, Touma! The bell will ring soon, so please, wake up already!"
"Look, I'm sorry for waking you up, but the career interest survey is due at lunch today."
"I'll be collecting them for the teacher. I figured you probably threw out the form, so here's a new one. I already filled in what I know, like your name."
"I won't look at what you write. It'll go straight in the envelope, and I won't take a peek whatsoever. So, well, um, please fill it out before lunch."
"No, don't just roll it up. Fill it in properly."
"If you want, you can just write 'university,' 'find employment,' or just 'I haven't decided yet.' The teacher said that you should at least write your current thoughts, or lack thereof."
"Besides, if you're so interested in bothering me, why don't you go collect everyone else's forms…?"
"I picked everyone else's forms up yesterday. Yours is the last one."
"…There were about three people absent yesterday, weren't there?"
"I gave them a phone call and picked the forms up at their houses. They filled them out, even though they were sick."
"That's a cruel thing to say. Our classmates are all serious, you know."
"Who do you think I'm talking about…?"
"Besides, the school is affiliated with a university, so you can write down, 'Enrolling in Houjou University.' They couldn't care less if you just wrote that down."
"There's just no way I'm going there."
"So you don't want to lie…? You're more sincere than I thought. I'm impressed."
"…Don't jump to your own conclusions and see me in a better light. It's annoying."
"If you don't want people to reevaluate their opinion of you, just going along with the flow would work out better, you know."
"Look, that way people wouldn't be so impressed when you give a rare display of good conduct and evaluate you more normally, right?"
"I have no intention of letting anyone evaluate me."
"I don't recommend filling out the form during class. If you can, try to get it done before the first bell…"
"Well, this decision could have an effect on the rest of your life, so you can think about it for a little longer. I'll leave it up to you, then."
"Is there something you're not sure how to fill out?"
"I'll do as you ask, so you can at least listen to one of my requests."
"Ahh, of course! If there's anything bothering you, I'm sure I can help…"
"If I ignore you from now on, don't worry about it. I'm just extremely annoyed and disgusted."
"Whoa, don't throw it at me. You should turn it over first…"
"I don't really care if you look at it. I just wrote, 'Enrolling in Houjou University,' like you said."
"Are we done here? I'm going back to sleep, then."
"I get it… From now on, I won't mind if you ignore me or anything."
"So please don't hold it against me if I keep on rambling anyway, Touma."
"Good morning, Touma. Great weather we're having today, huh?"
"Just wait a second, Kitahara. That's not how the promise…"
"I'll do as you ask, so isn't it only fair that you listen to one of my requests?"
"This isn't 'just one thing'! How shameless can you be!?"
"Touma… don't tell me you've just noticed that now."
Touma was willing to allow me to say things like "good morning" or "goodbye."
…Though, of course, she never really replied.
"Like I said, I understand everything now. I know all about how you've spent the past two years."
"I think it's unacceptable that you'd be excluded from your class over stuff like your mother being famous or the teachers favoring you."
"Still, you know… although this may sound quite painful, I think you should try to get along with everyone."
"How should I say this, conveying your feelings doesn't only include the positive stuff. Negative feelings like hate or unwillingness are also part of it."
"You might hate smiling at first. But even if you force yourself to smile, your smile will reach those around you. And if others smile back, then you'll also come to enjoy it."
"I think living that way is a lot better in comparison. No, I guess I'm not sure if people our age would understand such a line of thought."
"Ah, so, this introduction was a bit long, but what I wanted to talk about was…"
"Get out. Don't come here ever again."
"Wait, I was about to get to…"
Even if I called from the other side of the door, Touma wouldn't unlock the door to the second room again.
What did I do to make her so mad? I wasn't doing anything out of the ordinary…
"…Anyway, I'm sorry. I lied to you a little, Ogiso."
Ogiso looks at the sky through her fake glasses, as if she has no interest in what I just said.
"That pianist from before wasn't actually a member of the club… she just happened to be in the classroom next to us, and played with us from time to time."
"But you guys were in such perfect sync. I heard it from the rooftop every now and then, it seemed as if you guys were having so much fun…"
"That's only because she matched her pace to mine… No matter how badly I messed up, she would help the song take shape…"
Ogiso still doesn't show any interest, toying with her braids.
"Well, you know… at me for lying that we had a keyboardist. There really isn't anyone else other than you and us guitarists."
"That was just me getting the wrong idea. There's no reason for you to apologize, Kitahara-kun."
"Is there something else still bothering you?"
"If it's fine, then it's fine, right?"
Even though she says that, what's this strange oppressive feeling I'm getting?
During the short time I've known Ogiso, I have never seen her angry, but…
If something like that were to really happen, I'm quite sure that this is exactly how she'd act… Or is it just my imagination that I feel this way when looking at her right now?
"Ah, and, well… sorry about your job."
"Kitahara-kun, you've been doing nothing but apologizing for a while now."
"Still, I should be apologizing for what happened. I mean, I was the one who forcibly dragged you into this."
As it turns out, today was Ogiso's last day on her job.
"It's fine, I never felt pressured to do this."
Going with the excuse that she was focused on the school festival, she left her part-time job that was perfect for a student like her.
"I did enjoy this job, you know? I got to meet so many people, learn so many things… and most of all, I earned a decent amount of pocket money, too."
Even so, I waited at the exit as Ogiso was held up by the manager and part-time lady. They were all talking, weeping, and giving farewell gifts.
…It seems that even at her part-time job, her usual personality was well-liked.
"But in the coming month, I'll get to experience a completely different form of joy, so I don't regret it, you know?"
"Y-Y-Yeah… right. Umm, yeah… we've gotta do our best."
Before I knew it, Ogiso's expression had changed into a genuine smile, one different from earlier.
Her expression is, well… Let's just say she looks deviously cunning, such that it's more than enough to soften up whoever's looking at her, even through those fake glasses.
"We should start practicing as soon as possible…"
Right now, I don't have the time to be enjoying that alluring smile of hers.
"…Her name was Touma-san, right? Our potential keyboardist."
"Yeah… Though she vehemently refused my offer just a little while ago."
I actually hadn't even gotten to inviting her in the first place.
"Do you have to recruit her no matter what? Can't you find anyone else?"
"There's only a month left… We don't have time to take a step back and look for more candidates."
"Besides, you prefer Touma too, right? You were interested in singing with us because of her piano, right?"
"Well… at first it was like that, yes…"
On that rooftop, where we had our second meeting..
If it were my guitar alone, there's no way Ogiso would have wanted to sing along.
"Back then, I didn't know there were such peculiar conditions attached…"
Putting aside my performance, that miracle of a session on that day was only made possible by both Touma's piano and Ogiso's singing.
"…Sorry, I wasn't listening. What did you say?"
I feel like I heard some kind of grumbling.
"Still, what'll you do? Touma-san's quite difficult, isn't she?"
"Yeah. If I can't convince her to join in two to three days, we won't be able to make it at all."
Once this week passes, it'll already be November. There'll only be three weeks before the school festival.
Even though we already fall into the category of impromptu groups, if we can't start practicing soon, then we'll end up being a makeshift one.
"First, we need to get her to listen to us… Do you have anything in mind?"
…I do. Actually, only one thing comes to mind.
Touma hasn't yet refused to become part of the Light Music Club, nor has she gotten angry over being invited.
…After all, our negotiations haven't even started.
As for why she got mad, I still don't have a clue, but it most likely had something to do with my attitude.
In other words, there's still a chance for things to move along if someone else does the talking.
But the one negotiating would have to meet two conditions. They'd have to be related to the Light Music Club, and they'd have to be able to talk easily with Touma.
There are three people who fulfill the first condition. And within that, the only one who fulfills the second condition…
"Um, Ogiso. I actually have a request I'd like to make…"
Of course, I currently don't fall in the second category.
And if Touma remembers her first meeting with Takeya… well, I guess they were just never meant for each other.
In other words, with all these facts put together, it's quite obvious who it is I have to ask.
She's a girl, and she can easily start a conversation. Most of all, the only person able to oppose that rebellious Touma is someone who is the complete opposite of her…
"…I'm going to try talking with her again."
But that'd be too convenient… There's no way I can ask Ogiso to do that after she just joined.
Even I am not so shameless that I'd let someone else get completely tangled up in the mess I've made.
"Well, anyway… I was wondering if I could make use of you just a little."
…However, I am shameless enough to tangle her up just a little bit.
"Ehhhh!? N-No way, I can't do that…!"
"Please! The only way I can persuade Touma is to have her understand your circumstances!"
"T-That doesn't mean… I can't just talk to her about myself after we've only met once. She'll probably just respond with 'So what?'…"
"We'll be doing this together, so isn't it only natural for you two to know about each other?"
"How does that follow what you're asking…? They're totally unrelated…"
The only thing now that can stand up to "Touma's two years" is "Ogiso's two years."
Though their pasts may be completely different, I'm sure both of them have experienced things like perseverance, frustration, and having to work hard.
"B-Besides, that was supposed to be just between you and me, Kitahara-kun…"
"I really apologize for that, I truly do!"
I quickly bow down, begging Ogiso, though in truth, it's to hide the fact that my face is about to flare up.
"But Touma is a really good person. She won't tell anyone else!"
Yes, Touma is a good person… She would never do anything as horrible as what I'm doing right now.
"…Is Touma-san really so necessary that you have to go this far?"
"I'd like to hear your personal opinion, Kitahara-kun…"
"We'll be doing this together, so isn't it only natural for us two to know about each other?"
"Or… is it something only between Touma-san and you, Kitahara-kun…?"
"She was the first person to ever take my guitar playing seriously."
"Do you mean how she accompanied you, despite never meeting you?"
"…No, this goes further back. It was during summer."
"What are you doing here? Aren't you part of the go-home club? It's the middle of summer vacation."
"I can tell that you're rather crappy at playing the guitar…"
"Aren't you also part of the go-home club, Touma? What are you doing at school in the middle of summer?"
"You sure are childish, lashing back at someone the instant they strike a nerve…"
"I only started this year. It's a given that I'm somewhat terrible at this right now, isn't it?"
"I mean… you're just holding down chords, right? I can't understand how you could possibly miss."
"That's what everyone says when they've never played it themselves…"
"You know, Touma… you should change your tendency of laughing at those who are doing their best."
"In my opinion, anyone who is willing to break a sweat over something is an admirable person. That is, I admire anyone who puts effort in, whether it be physical or mental."
"Anyway, what's up today? If you want me to give you supplementary lessons, then wait a little bit until I'm done and I can…"
"…I'm sorry. Please don't make me feel any more pathetic than I already am."
"I'm devastated… I've lost all hope in my own talent…"
"This isn't about talent, it's about practice. Like you said, the difference is in how much sweat we've broken over it."
"To learn this, even a little amount of practice should be enough if you do it seriously. You act all high and mighty, but you don't try hard enough."
"No way… I may not be good, but I've been practicing for two hours every day…"
