"This kind of instrument normally takes ten hours of practice a day."
"No, I'd be a pro if I practiced that much."
"That was amazing, though… Do you play the guitar too, Touma?"
"Nope. I've just been messing around with it for the past few days."
"Don't be going off negating everything you said just now…"
"Now, once again from the top. I can give you a few pointers to start you off."
"Why'd you come to school during the summer holidays…?"
"You say I should hurry and play, and then you say I should play slowly…"
"A class representative with excellent grades such as yourself should be able to figure out the basic difference in nuance."
"This is the first time you've spoken to me on your own, isn't it?"
"In the end, that day was the only time I'd ever talked with her that much."
"She actually has a pretty bad personality. She teaches me like a Spartan, and she doesn't hold back the criticism and insults."
"But I couldn't defy her. In fact, I never even thought about talking back to her. After all, she plays way better than me."
"Also, in just a single day, and despite all the badmouthing, she taught me how to play the guitar in detail."
"That's right, why hadn't I noticed until now? She can play well without much practice at all…"
I should have figured the owner of Music Room 2 was someone who could play anything better than the average person, like the bass or the drums.
She was someone always deeply engaged in music. One who could easily let slip phrases like "practice ten hours a day."
The only one I knew who was so dedicated to it, apart from the music program students.
"I see… So that's how it is…"
"Kitahara-kun, whenever you're talking to girls, you seem to end up talking about other girls."
I did feel like the conversation was starting to get derailed, but Setsuna's statement went beyond that.
She won't drop the topic for some reason. Even though all I did was follow Ogiso's wishes, telling her what she wanted to know…
"Well, normally I don't talk to girls about this sort of thing. Io's about the only one I talk to anyway…"
Even so, why do I feel this inexplicable guilt creeping up my spine, along with this cold sweat and nervosity?
"Umm… Was what I said really that strange?"
"Then don't pause for so long, please…!"
The sweat pouring from my body is frozen in an instant by the chilly winds of fall. I might even catch a cold from this.
"Let's go, Kitahara-kun. It has gotten quite late."
Jeez, I shouldn't be doing things I'm not used to…
I really, really shouldn't be doing things I'm not used to…
"Well, I was rather quick to refuse a while ago, but…"
However, while I'm wrapped in regret, the tide of battle suddenly changes due to one single utterance from Ogiso.
"You can tell Touma-san about my circumstances."
"Yup… If that's what would help her have a more positive outlook on life."
What's with this turn of events…? No, perhaps she finally understands what I have in mind.
"I-I see… Thank you, Ogiso. I really owe you one!"
"In return… I want you to get Touma-san to meet me. I really want to get to know her after all you told me."
"Yeah, I promise. I'll drag her out if that's what it takes!"
I'm glad… I'm really glad. This time, this time for sure…
"…And then, she ended up singing 30 songs in a row, and it was past midnight before I knew it."
"Oh man, the rumors are very much wrong. She's hardworking, and rather plain, with a good personality. I never knew she was such a playful, interesting girl."
"Anyway, I'd just like to have you listen to her sing just once… I'm sure that would change your mind."
"Well, when I say she's good at singing… she is good, but as in, she's good at singing karaoke, you know?"
"Still, that isn't really the main point here. I truly felt it when I first heard her singing on the rooftop… Well, what was that cliche phrase again? 'Picture perfect'?"
"Anyway, I'm sure our stage performance will be the talk of the school regardless if we succeed or fail miserably. After all, Ogiso Setsuna is going to be singing."
"But I don't want to fail… I want people to talk about how great we were. After all, I don't want Ogiso to lose face after she joined us out of kindness."
"…Is that all you wanted to say?"
"Well, I'm getting to the main point here. So anyway, Touma, if you'd like, would you…"
"I seem to remember telling you to never come in here again. Why are you here?"
"No, you keep saying this and that, but you still allowed me to ente… Uwaaah!?"
Well, it pains me to admit it, but for now I have to give up the negotiations in Music Room 2.
I told Ogiso on the way home that I had failed in persuading Touma yet again, and was taken aback a bit by the words she said right then and there.
"I knew it'd turn out that way…"
"Touma-san, right? Umm, we met a while ago…"
"Ah, you remembered my name. Thank you."
"Are you on your way home? I'd like to chat with you a bit."
"Yup, with you, Touma-san. Is that okay?"
"Eh? Ah, umm… I'm off to go buy sheet music though…"
"Then let's go together. When we're done, maybe we can go and have some tea?"
"That's an okay, then? Let's get going. If we don't hurry, the book store will close up."
"Ah, I see. That's right. Heheh, oh my, I'm jumping to conclusions."
"Eh…? You're eating this now? Won't you be too full for dinner?"
"But isn't there dinner waiting at home?"
"Still, the nutritional balance is poor if you're only taking these. You should at least get a salad to go with it."
"…Are these the only kind of people he hangs out with…?"
"Because, didn't you get hit on like five times just walking in front of the station?"
"On top of that, you drove everyone away real quick. I guess beautiful people are really persuasive when they're angry."
"I wasn't the one getting hit on."
"Not at all, I'm sure you were their target, Touma-san."
"You should be more aware of how people perceive you. You'll come off as rude if you're too humble…"
"Come on, I'd only get hit on around two or three times if I were walking on my own."
"Aah, I'm getting kind of hungry too. I wonder if it'd be fine if I had an apple pie before dinner?"
"Alright, onto the main topic. You see, I joined the Light Music Club."
"Having said that, we're just a one-shot group that'll be disbanding as soon as this year's school festival's stage performance is over."
"It's the first time in my life that I'll be singing in front of so many people, so I'm feeling a bit tense."
"I can't just do that… Everyone's doing their best."
"'Doing their best'? There's only one guy working his butt off. The group has practically been disbanded already…"
"But the information you have is a bit outdated now. There's one more person doing their best."
"So you see, Touma-san… we'd like to have at least one more person giving it their all…"
"Did that idiot rope you into this?"
"Nope. Kitahara-kun never asked me at all. He's the type that ends up burdening himself with everything even though he knows it'd be better to rely on others."
"Maybe you actually know about that already, Touma-san?"
"Anyway, Kitahara-kun said that we can't do anything unless you join the group."
"He said your skills are essential to pulling off this year's festival performance."
"And… he said he wanted to do this with you, no matter what."
"I'm not lying. Kitahara-kun most definitely said that, you know?"
"I don't want to do it. I'm not interested at all."
"You've been irritating me for a while now… Do you always put on this innocent charade?"
"I wonder? Well, I certainly haven't talked about something like this at school."
"It's rare to see someone go this far, doing favors for that idiot… You have bad taste."
"Hey, Touma-san… don't you think we could be really good friends?"
"Not at all. And what makes you think we would?"
"I have no idea what you're talking about."
"If possible, I'd like you to explain to me exactly how your thought process brought you to that conclusion, in detail."
"You knew that the guitarist in the classroom next door was Kitahara-kun, that's why you played along with him, right?"
"Normally it'd be stranger not to notice. Well, I suppose I get it. Kitahara-kun is 'that idiot,' after all, just like you said."
"Also, Kitahara-kun seriously thinks you hate him… Because you hurl so much abuse at him, unlike with other people."
"Even though you ignore everyone else, you're always getting angry at him… But that's just what Kitahara-kun believes."
"You've really bought into that idiot, huh."
"…I wonder? Maybe I have. What do you think?"
"Hey, do you have time? If you'd like, let's go to a karaoke…"
"I refuse. I couldn't stand someone singing forever by themselves."
"The truth is… I asked him to tell you that."
"Because I figured you'd get angry, Touma-san."
"I mean, I got really angry too. He kept on speaking so highly about you."
"Yup, for now I'm satisfied. See you again, Touma-san."
"I just can't deal with people like her…"
"Why are you more surprised about that…? Don't you think you're being a little rude to her?"
I found myself absolutely terrified at Ogiso's bombshell announcement that she had "talked to Touma-san yesterday."
"Ah, well, umm… There hasn't been anyone around me that had that good of a first impression of her…"
"That's… because they don't know all that much about her, I think."
I was terrified because she realized that I wanted her to talk to Touma, even though I never actually told her to.
"T…Thank you… Ogiso. No, really. Umm, from the bottom of my heart, I apologize."
"Please, you're exaggerating. I also wanted to talk with Touma-san… for more reasons than one."
In the end, she took immediate action. Part of the reason was probably for my sake.
"Though we sure got to talk about a lot of things. It was so much fun!"
"And all of her reactions were so interesting, I thought she seemed rather cute!"
"…I don't think her impression of me is good though. Ahaha…"
"…I'm sorry, but the person I was telling you about was Touma Kazusa, my classmate…"
"I know that already. You introduced me to her, Kitahara-kun."
"…Are we really thinking of the same person?"
"She completely matches your description of her, you know?"
Fun to talk to…? Interesting…? Cute…?
"Did I… really praise her that much?"
Well, certainly, if Ogiso has that kind of impression of her, it's perfect…
If I was passionately using words like that earlier, then that might change things a little…
Indeed, I feel like as she looks up at me, Ogiso's eyes are somewhat lacking in kindness.
"I… don't think I went that far…"
"I said that although her personality is bad, the fact that she can't follow through with her cruelty due to her kind nature was interesting…"
Damn, I just dug my own grave…
"I never said 'cute,' right? That's the truth, right?"
"Those are some pretty pathetic excuses you have."
"I apologize if I've ruined your mood."
"Though I'm not quite satisfied with the reason…"
"Everything is my fault. Please forgive me!"
"…I can feel my own personality getting twisted the more I talk to you, Kitahara-kun."
"Even Touma-san feels that way, and maybe that's why she isn't honest."
"Well, she was bitter to begin with. Though it's much better now…"
"If you put it like that, does it mean there's nothing I can say about her!?"
"Jeez, what am I going to do with you…"
"What am I supposed to do then?"
Setsuna, who went out of her way for me without me even asking…
"Then… perhaps I should make you do something for me."
I didn't ask her to do anything, yet it seems like she has built up a lot of incomprehensible stress.
"Don't screw with me! Why would I have to!?"
"Well, you see, members should deepen their friendship…"
The third day in a row at Music Room 2.
Having already been forcibly kicked out two days in a row, I knocked on the door in utter fear, only to be met with a tired-looking Touma who opened the door right away.
"I never said anything about joining. And that invitation is just her idea, isn't it?"
Her bored expression changed in an instant when I asked, "Would you like the three of us to hang out tomorrow?".
"I want the three of us to talk things out. Up until now, we've always been talking past each other, and we've never been able to talk properly about the club."
"I don't plan on 'properly' listening, so there is no point in talking about it."
"Come on Touma, it's Sunday tomorrow, can't I convince you to come somehow?"
"Listen to me 'properly' when I'm talking to you!"
She's not as blunt as usual. If I had to say, she seems rather bewildered. This might be the first time I've seen Touma like this.
"Perhaps you're taking piano lessons? Are you really practicing ten hours a day?"
"If you are seriously practicing the piano, then perhaps pushing you to mess around with us is a bit…"
"I told you, I'm not doing that!"
"Hey, Kitahara… why do you always say things that get on my nerves?"
She could've just said, "Yes, I'm practicing" as a lie, and I'd have no choice but to give up.
She has a hard time following through with both her coldness and curtness.
She always leaves an opening for me like this, which is why I never once considered that I should stop.
"…Sorry, am I being a bother again?"
"If you've figured it out yourself, get lost. And don't come back here ever again."
That makes the third time she's said, "Don't come here ever again."
She could have just locked the door, yet she never rejects me directly…
"…In that case, Ogiso told me to convey a message from her in the event you should refuse me."
Like I said, if she leaves so many obvious openings…
"Her exact words were, 'If you don't come, I'll tell Kitahara-kun about that.'"
"H-Hey… I'm not sure it's okay for me to ask this, but what exactly is 'that'?"
"H-Hey, Touma. Did something happen between you and Ogiso…?"
She has never reacted like this before, and I bet she will never react like this again… Actually, I'm not so sure about the latter half.
I don't ever recall Touma yielding as easily as this.
Ogiso… What in the world did you…?
"You're late. What took you so long? Who do you think you are, walking so nonchalantly when you're making people wait?"
I arrived just on time, and Touma promptly began to mercilessly throw abuses at me.
"I thought that arriving five minutes early at the meeting spot was an unspoken rule."
"You seem to know your etiquette well, despite your dirty mouth."
"That's completely irrelevant, not to mention rude!"
Touma never compromises when it comes to her own internal logic… No wonder we always argue.
"Sorry～! I got held up a bit!"
"I made it within five minutes but… Touma, don't you have anything to say to her?"
"Don't kick my legs, especially not with those pointed ends…!"
Her attitude suddenly changes when the topic shifts to Ogiso… But seriously, why?
"…Putting that aside… All right, where will we be going now?"
We're in front of Suetsugu-chou Station, one station away from school and nearest to Ogiso's house.
It's a great deal more peaceful than Minami-Suetsugu, which is where our school lies. Ogiso was the one who suggested we meet here.
"I don't care where, let's just get this over with quickly. The result will be the same, anyway."
Although she gave in to Ogiso's unknown threat and devoted her precious Sunday afternoon to this, she seems grumpily determined to not sign off on her soul.
"Regardless, you two can decide where to go. I'll play along with you guys a little for the time being."
"…Sorry, I was just messing with Touma since she said she doesn't care where…"
"How low can you go, you sorry excuse for a human being…?"
"Umm, aren't you two being kind of mean to someone? Me for example?"
Besides, if we do go there, things will probably get out of control, and we won't get anything discussed. Not to mention, it would be tremendously awkward.
"Well, umm… For now, let's find a family restaurant or something…"
"Oh, that's fine, I've actually already decided where we'll be going beforehand. Let's go, you two."
"Could've just said so from the start then.."
"Why not say that directly to Ogiso, instead of whispering so only I can hear it?"
"Because I don't know how she'd counterattack…"
"I seriously have to know. What happened between you two when you first met?"
"We'll be going in here first. Kitahara-kun, if you don't mind, could you carry the basket?"
During my quiet exchange with Touma, Ogiso had already reached her destination.
Actually, this place happens to be…
"Manager! Long time no see… Though I guess it's only been three days."
This is the very same place I came to pick up Ogiso…
"Ah, that's not it. I'm just a customer today. I hope you will give us a lot of freebies."
"Hey, do you guys want to have anything specific for dinner?"
"Hey, Mooom? Where's the potato starch again?"
"Jeez, I keep telling you over and over that I don't know where 'there' is."
"It's in the cupboard. Look in the third drawer."
"Umm… Ah, here it is, found it!"
"Besides, the only reason you don't know something so simple is because you don't normally cook."
"I do cook～! Jeez, don't embarrass me when we have guests over!"
"They're on the second floor, so they can't hear us, can they?"
"Actually… when you open the door like this, you can hear just about everything from downstairs."
"Hey, oh no, it's boiling over! I'm sorry, Mom, but could you take care of mixing the starch with water?"
"Now what? When I said I was going to help earlier, you just got mad and refused me."
"But Mom, you always end up leaving too much to instinct. And you lecture me on every little thing too."
"I've got years of experience on my side. It's always delicious whenever I make it, right?"
"But then it'll end up being your flavor, Mom. It has to be my flavor today."
"It's not really your flavor, Setsuna, but that of the cooking book, isn't it?"
"Just be quiet already and do as I say, Mom!"
"Jeez, this girl… You should know better than to yell in front of guests…."
"They won't hear me. They're in my room, after all."
"Ah, here's some castella cake from the Fukuma shop. Looks like dinner won't be ready for a while if they're gonna be… Oh…"
"Leaving it open would have been more fun. See? My sister's completely different from when she's at school, isn't she?"
"No, I don't think my conscience would have been able to last any longer."
Carrying her groceries from the supermarket, Ogiso led us to the gates of a detached house that was a fifteen-minute walk from the station.
And as expected, the doorplate read "Ogiso"…
"Takahiro-kun, was it? What grade are you in?"
"Third year, middle school. I'm three years behind my sister."
Thus, she brought us straight to the second floor, and left us in her bedroom.
Unable to bear the awkwardness any longer, Touma was just about to say, "I'm leaving" when this young man appeared like a savior, bringing tea..
"Which means you're taking entrance exams. Are you going to be enrolling at our school?"
"Grades-wise, I could make it, but it might be impossible financially. Dad's all burned out just from enrolling her there."

In total, the lot is about 200 square meters large, and the house takes up about half of it. Its first floor has a living room, a study, and a master bedroom, while the second floor has the children's rooms; a stereotypical "detached home."
Though the family has to be quite well-off to even be able to afford a house around here.
"On top of that, if she continues her studies in Houjou University… I don't know if we'd be able to afford my entrance tuition."
Though, compared to some other students in our school, this really is just an "average" family.
It's just a guess, but I bet this place is nothing compared to the home of the classmate sitting before me.
"Ah, Takahiro-kun, don't be scared. She's just really shy, you see."
"Ah, well… I am scared, but only a little bit."
"Loosen up a little, would you? He's acting more maturely than you are."
"W-We…Well I, look… who could have predicted this turn of events…?"
"Still though, I think this is the first time my sister has brought friends home since she enrolled in Houjou."
I suppose it's due to her misunderstood reputation of being the school's number one lady.
"She had plenty of friends come over during middle school. She'd throw her birthday parties inviting all the girls from her class… Twenty of them in this tiny house, can you imagine?"
Despite being so sociable and ordinary, Ogiso had to start worrying about maintaining her image due to that trivial rumor.
Whether she's an ordinary girl or an unattainable flower, it doesn't change the fact that Ogiso is overflowing with charm.
"And now she's bringing friends home again, six months before graduation. I wonder what brought about this change."
"Well, about that… there's something that the three of us absolutely have to discuss today."
"Yeah, Ogiso and I have to convince Touma here no matter what."
"She doesn't seem to understand our feelings at all… No matter how many times we tried, she wouldn't accept."
"Umm, so basically, you mean… you're trying to untangle this complicated relationship between the three of you?"
"Ah, I guess you could put it that way. Touma here's pretty stubborn, as you can see."
"What, am I wrong? Feel free to voice any objections you have."
Yeah, we won't settle for a compromise today.
We're down to the wire, where the slightest thing will tick off Touma, and either she'll become our ally, or she'll never talk to us again.
"That's not what I mean… He'll definitely get the wrong idea from what you just said…"
"Sorry to keep you waiting! Wha… Takahiro? What are you doing here?"
Ogiso frowns a bit as she looks at the three of us in the room, carrying a large, steamy tray.
"I told you not to bother us, didn't I? Your sister and her friends have something really important to talk about. Come on, get out! Right now!"
She sternly raises her eyebrows, looking like a typical sister scolding her younger brother. I've never seen something like this before.
"Ah, well, umm… Your guests seemed a bit neglected, and I had some time to kill, and you left them here without even bringing them tea, and…"
And in the next moment, she slowly lowers her eyebrows, and her expression changes into one of a forgiving big sister.
"Hmm… Maybe I went too far. Dinner is ready downstairs, so go eat. I was the one who made it today, so I can't really guarantee the taste."
What is this…? It feels like I've seen something I shouldn't have.
"I'm not sure when you got yourself into this mess, but…"
"U-Umm, well, uh… Good luck. I hope you manage to settle everything peacefully."
"Sorry, things were a bit of a mess down there. That's why preparing this took a bit longer than expected."
"That's fine, or rather… Ogiso, this is…"
"Let's eat first. The heat will at least help mask the flavor."
Yellowtail teriyaki, chop suey, and Hamburger steak. The main dishes are a magnificent blend of Japanese, Chinese, and Western cuisine.
On top of that, rice and shijimi soup too. No matter the dish, she took into consideration how the colors and appearance would match up when plating them. A perfect example of a "family dinner."
With how great it looks, it's guaranteed that the flavor will at least be average.
"Because Kitahara-kun said that he wanted to talk over dinner."
I'd meant some place quieter where we could talk, like at a family restaurant or a cafe.
"It's cheaper to be eating dinner at home. And besides…"
"It's bad for Touma-san's health if she always eats out, so I thought I might kill two birds with one stone."
I thought I warned her many times that Touma is particularly hot-tempered…
"Well then, Touma-san, help yourself. You won't be able to fight on an empty stomach."
Should I say Ogiso is fearless, or that Touma is just defenseless against her…?
"You can have as much as you'd like. There's enough for seconds too, so don't be afraid to ask."
I really can't understand the dynamic between these two.
For some reason, we were completely silent for the entire duration of the dinner.
I'm not sure what Touma was so stubborn about. Since she was so focused on eating up everything she grabbed, there was not much we could really discuss…
And once Touma had eaten it all, Ogiso asked her with a smile if she wanted seconds.
After several seconds of tension, Touma silently handed her rice bowl to the smiling Ogiso.
And this, perhaps heart-warming scene, repeated itself at least twice.
During this time, I had only managed to ask for seconds once.
"Well, how did you guys like dinner? I think it turned out okay, but…"
"Really? I'm so glad! I only make food about once a month, so I didn't really feel all that confident, you see…"
I have to say it tasted pretty good.

The taste was essentially by the book; it was neither too sweet nor too spicy, and the bitterness, sourness and just about everything else was done just right, such that it wouldn't be embarrassing to serve such fare anywhere.
I don't mean anything bad when I say it was by the book either.
It's because she followed the instructions in the book carefully that she was able to make something like this in practice. She'll only get better from now on.
Given that she's already produced such results with only normal effort, I have no doubt that I can expect greater things from her from here on out.
"Ahh, no, there's no need, thank you."
Though Touma tried to stand up, it's obvious that her movements have been dulled since she took on Ogiso's challenge and ate three whole bowls of rice.
"Come on Touma, can't you join us? We only have this little request that you help us with all sorts of things for the school festival."
"How can you call it 'a little request' and then ask for me to help with 'all sorts of things'?"
"I think that people who complain about every little detail will end up losing the trust of others."
"What a coincidence. I happen to agree with you, Kitahara."
For some reason, Touma is looking at me as if objecting to something.
"Come on, Touma-san, can't you help us with this?"
"…You can keep trying to appeal to my emotions like that, but I won't budge."
"Whatever you may try, be it sincerity, devotion, or goodwill… I'm not someone so weak-willed to fall prey to something so cheap."
"After all… I've never been a considerate person at all to begin with."
"Kitahara-kun, I'm sorry, but… I'm not sure I understand what Touma-san is saying. Could you explain it to me?"
"Basically, Touma's saying that she sees your hospitality as some form of sincerity, devotion, or goodwill."
"Ahh, if that's what it is, then we can split the cost. Umm, I think it would be something like 1000 yen per person…"
I get the reason why Touma can't deal with Ogiso, as well as the reason why Ogiso seems completely oblivious of that fact.
"So you see, Touma, Ogiso doesn't really think of today as anything particularly special."
"Why…? Bringing others to your house, having them taste your cooking… what for?"
"Maybe… you don't understand because your personalities are so different?"
Unlike Touma, Ogiso was simply raised that way.
…Although I'm sure she'd make even less of an effort to understand if I told her that, so I kept those words to myself.
In other words, their relationship was predestined to be turbulent because of this.
"Listen, Touma-san. I didn't treat you to all this because I had an ulterior motive. I just felt that we could talk more easily on a full stomach…"
Isn't that what it means to have an ulterior motive?
"…Do you expect me to believe that you have pure intentions, when you've already put me through so much torment?"
…I feel a bit ashamed for anticipating that very retort.
"Torment…? I was just teasing you a little!"
"Wrongly jumping to conclusions about other people's feelings, and embarrassing them until their face burns with shame. You call that 'just teasing'!?"
"Come on, Touma… what in the world did Ogiso do to you?"
"Ahh… that's probably because, Kitahara-kun, Touma-san is in…"
"Fine then, we'll leave the emotional arguments out of this! Let's be rational!"
Seeing this exchange between them makes it even harder for me to ignore factors other than "how they were raised"…
"For starters, the plan you guys have is just impossible…"
The moment Touma's words were about to flare up…
Ogiso puts out the flames with cold water, even though she was the one waiting for this topic to be brought up.
"I'm sorry, but… be quiet for a moment…"
Commanding us, she moves as if sliding across the floor, and as she reaches the door, she puts her hand on the knob.
"Hey, Takahiro. This doesn't seem as bad as you claimed it was."
"That's just for now. I'm telling you, it's going to get real ugly."
"Their relationship doesn't seem that bad to me. Sure, that girl didn't talk too much, but both of them seemed quite polite."
"I'm sure of it. I heard it from them. The reason why she came to our house is to make those two break up."
"Why would they talk about it here? And what does it have to do with Setsuna?"
"That's exactly why it's gonna get ugly. Basically, the reason why the two of them are fighting is…"
"That's right… Nee-chan stole her boyfriend, and things are about to go ballistic."
"That's… quite a mess. And how does that boy feel about this?"
"Well… it seems that he's all over Nee-chan right now. But his ex-girlfriend just won't let him go, so he seems to be in a tough spot."
"But isn't that Setsuna's fault? She put herself between a couple who were dating, right?"
"There wasn't the slightest hint that she was dating anyone… Yet now suddenly she's having an immoral affair… You're good, Nee-chan!"
"There's nothing 'good' about it at all! Betraying her friend in such a cruel way… I don't recall raising such an immoral daughter."
"Could you do something about it, Mom? As an adult, maybe something before they get into a scuffle…"
"I'm the one who wants to do something about you two!"
"I was wondering what those whispers I was hearing were… Takahiro! Just what kind of a person do you take your sister for!?"
"W-Well… see, I was worried about you, Nee-chan…"
"And Mom, it's always the same with you! You're still believing Takahiro's gibberish nonsense!"
"W-Well, you know… recently young people have been getting into those… what did they call them? You know, those friends-with-benefits relationships or something…"
"Jeez, Mom! Daytime dramas, variety shows and weekly women's magazines are all off-limits from now on!"
"I-I'm so sorry! I never meant for you to bear witness to this side of my family. I humbly apologize for my mom and brother's rudeness!"
"T-That's okay, we don't mind… right, Touma?"
"I'm really sorry, Touma-san! My family is a bit overprotective, or rather, they're not really thoughtful…"
"W-Well… you guys get along and that's what's important, right?"
It didn't take much to convince Setsuna's family that we were part of the light music club, here to discuss our plans for the school festival.
…Though I'm not sure why they accepted it so easily. In any case, we're in a rush to resolve all our issues now, so I'll just leave it at that.
"…Well, since they let me have a part-time job, I can't really go up against them."
Though she calls it not wanting to go up against them, it's probably more that she can't stay angry at them.
When Takahiro-kun and Setsuna's mother learned about our activities, they had a sudden change of heart. Satisfied, they said they'd definitely come to the festival.
Besides, Ogiso didn't tell them not to come or that she wouldn't like them to. In a way, she'd forgiven her family much sooner than we did.
"Were you offended? They really didn't mean anything bad. I'll apologize in their stead, okay?"
"I said I'm not angry. You aren't either, right, Touma?"
How should I put it, this anticlimax has… left both Touma and me dumbfounded at how ridiculously well this family gets along.
"That's how it is, so we'll leave it at that. By the way, is it okay if we eat the cake your mother brought?"
"Ah, sure. Mom actually baked this one herself. She always bakes a cake at noon on her days off…"
Also, although I do feel sorry for Touma…
I definitely don't think of this as an unpleasant situation. In fact, it's the exact opposite.
It's that kind of embarrassing, nostalgic feeling you get from seeing a ten year old home video…
It makes me feel truly happy, if just a little.
"To begin with, the plan you guys have is just impossible to pull off. You're not going to make it in time for the festival, no matter who joins you."
"It won't be that way if you join us, Touma…"
I gulp down my cake and sip my black tea.
I also make sure no one is eavesdropping from the hallway.
It's almost 7 PM, and our negotiations have finally begun.
"In that case, Kitahara… what exactly would you have me do?"
"Well, the piano, obviously… In terms of band composition, you'd be the keyboardist, I guess. Anyway, I just want you to perform with us, Touma."
"We're… well, Kitahara-kun in particular is a huge fan of your piano, Touma-san."
"Please don't say that about me right in front of her…"
"At least deny it before getting embarrassed. You disgust me."
A flaw in my personality is that I'm not used to hiding my embarrassment and lying.
"And who will be the bassist? And what about the drums? Sure, it depends on the songs you pick, but you know that just adding a pianist won't be enough, right?"
"We can think of solutions to those problems as we go…"
"Even though you have only three weeks left? How many days will this 'as we go' take? All of tomorrow?"
"Well, if only you'd joined us sooner, Touma."
Come on, she could've just let that one slide…
"There's no time for that. With merely two weeks of practice, what kind of results do you expect to achieve? If you perform like that, we'll just end up a complete and utter joke."
"Get it? This whole ideal plan you're talking about is already nothing more than a dream."
"Is… Is it wrong for me to dream…?"
I know it is, but still…
If someone shuts me down so bluntly, I can't help but hold it against them. I find myself wanting to sulk just like my friend here usually does.
"This isn't like you. I could never imagine such words coming out of the ever-realistic Kitahara's mouth."
"Preparing in advance, avoiding risks, keeping things stable. That's what defines you, isn't it?"
Though her sulky attitude is a completely different matter, given her family's history.
"You avoid competition, you make sure no one's left behind and that everyone makes it to the end together. You don't oppose anyone, always smiling quietly."
Her words are merciless… but it's true, that's the kind of person I've always striven to be.
"…You sure seem to know a lot, Touma-san."
"We're not talking about me right now. Don't try to break my train of thought."
"Well, excuse me then… for acting so out of character."
But the person I want to be right now… it goes against the whole image I've built up until now.
"I didn't say it's something to be sorry about. I just said it's strange."
"But… what's wrong with a single month's leeway? A single month for me to act out of character, and embarrass myself."
"You might regret it. You might lose the whole 'serious, hardworking, honors student, class representative Kitahara Haruki' image you've had until now."
"I've already considered that. The two and a half years I've spent building up my image isn't that fragile."
"…That puts you in utter contrast with my two and a half years."
"Sorry to tell you, but that goes without saying. I did my best to get on the teachers' good side, while you did your worst to get on their bad side."
"So don't think you have me all figured out. Even I can be pretty unpredictable every once in a while."
"And I'm saying that's not like you…"
"For once, I don't care if you start hating me for it, but I'll still make sure you join us whether you like it or not! …If possible."
"…Wait a second, now. I've never said a word about hating you…"
"Setsuna. I need to speak with you. Please open up."
How many times has it been already that we've been interrupted just when the discussion is about to reach its climax?
The time has finally come. The time for our plans to be turned completely upside down by an unrelenting force.
"W-Wait, stop! Why are you bringing that up in front of my friends…?"
"That'd be because you lied, wouldn't it? You never told me anything about singing at the school festival."
"I didn't lie. It's just… I haven't found the right time to tell you guys."
"You should consult your father and mother before doing something like that. We promised to do that long ago, didn't we?"
"T-That's… well yeah, we did a long time ago… But I'll be a university student next year!"
"Just let it go, Dad. It's not like she has caused a problem or is quitting school. This is nothing compared to those things."
"The festival only happens once a year, so what's wrong with letting loose a little?"
"No… we heard about it just earlier. She's going to form a band with the other two. Her female friend is really cool."
"She's quite beautiful, I'm sure she'd be wonderful on stage… She should go and sing instead of Setsuna."
"Oh, come on… Singing is the only thing I can do…"
But there are no such positive comments about me.
"Is this why you quit your part-time job? Were your late night visits to karaoke bars just an excuse for you to rehearse?"
"Sure, I did leave my job, but the karaoke thing is just a hobby of mine… And I've never actually practiced even once."
"Seriously? But the show is this month! That's really pushing it!"
"…Maybe you shouldn't go? I don't want my daughter to make a complete fool of herself in front of all the students…"
"We'll make it work! Kitahara-kun and Touma-san are both really good, so it'll be fine!"
"In any case, please explain this from start to finish. After that, we'll all decide whether you can participate."
"I'm sorry, but please have them go home. We have something very important to discuss as a family."
"If you can't do it yourself, I'll apologize to them… It's been three years since you had friends come over, so I want to greet them properly too."
Naturally, it's already pitch black outside when we leave the entryway. I can't help but shudder as the cold night wind stabs at my skin.
I'm sure it'll take at least fifteen minutes to reach the station from the residential area. The light of the moon, the stars, and street lamps softly illuminate our way.
"That's fine. I don't really feel sorry about it."
Touma was five minutes behind me. Finally leaving the entryway of the Ogiso household, she now stands beside me.
I start walking, and she shows no sign of hostility, disgust, or embarrassment as she walks beside me.
And as we advance, she shows no hostility, disgust, or embarrassment as she talks to me.
I really am… a little embarrassed.
"But that's just me telling her. You'll have to tell her that yourself tomorrow."
Despite saying we aren't bothered, the two of us hung our heads for a while as we made our way to the station. We couldn't find any more words to say.
Ogiso's father came upstairs to her room, and politely apologized to us.
Despite my own apologies, the explanation that I was the one who forcibly invited Ogiso, as well as the fact that she quit her job because of me, he simply took it all as "his daughter's problem."
He just said that the family had something to discuss today, and he apologetically sent us home, bowing his head.
It seems that Touma also feels the same uneasiness that I do.
An entire family council to discuss whether she should perform at the school festival…
Even though he's such a strict father, he never said anything like, "Everyone be silent" or "I won't allow this."
He only pointed out the parts that Ogiso couldn't come up with excuses for, and he listened to her opinions in earnest.
Normally I'd force a comment right afterward, but I just can't do it now.
"Her family interfering that much… and she even thinks it's completely natural…"
Because… I feel like I've come across something incredibly remarkable.
To think that a family straight out of a soap opera still exists in reality, even now…
"Count me out… I can't imagine myself being in a situation like that."
Which is why it had such a noticeable effect on Touma.
"I won't accept it… I'll lose if I do…"
Shivering as if she were cold, Touma looks up at the night sky overhead. A commonplace, and not too beautiful night sky.
She had stopped walking by my side at some point, and although I look back at the road behind, I'm unable to see that brilliant face.
"But you know… I had stuff like that happen at home too, years ago."
With how weakly she said that, I can't tell what she's feeling at all… Is she angry? Is she smiling or crying? Was there any emotion to it at all?
"My curfew was at six, and whenever I was late, my mother would walk around restlessly in front of the house, and my father would lecture me really strictly."
Which is why I'm not sure whether she's listening to my silly story, or if she's shut me out completely. Perhaps it's something else entirely.
"When I secretly drank plum wine at my friend's place, I was busted the moment I came back home because my face was flushed red. He called my friend's home, and lectured me as well as my friend."
Even so, I continue my story, because I experienced that kind of drama at home in the past as well.
"Though they didn't care nearly as much about me once I entered middle school."
"…It's more the fact that my father left, really. Well, he pays plenty of child support, so I don't really have any right to complain."
It's not something to boast about… And in front of Touma of all people, it really isn't something to boast about.
My father's from Okayama. His family there is quite famous, owns a mansion, and runs a thriving family-owned enterprise.
As the eldest son, my father was next in line to become the owner. He had good grades, got into a good high school, then got into a good university…
It would have been smooth sailing except for one thing: he married my mother, and she gave birth to me… From the family's perspective, it was a blunder.
Regarding what actually happened, I've heard much about it from my mother's grumbling, but I never really cared.
After hearing the two argue without any regard for each other's feelings, I lost any desire to take sides.
And thus, all that remained was the Kitahara household, which received monetary aid from a certain wealthy family in Okayama, and a mother and son who had grown indifferent toward each other.
"…I see you're still a half-assed idiot as usual, Kitahara."
"…I figured you were the only one who wouldn't be taken aback, Touma."
All three times I've talked about my family circumstances with my friendsーTakeya includedーtheir reactions were not very pleasant, so I've started avoiding talking about it with others.
"Well, I never knew my father's name or what he looked like. I haven't lived with my mother in years. The credit card she left me doesn't even have a limit."
Her family issues far surpass mine. And compared to Ogiso, her family is from a different genre of soap opera.
"…You're as easy to understand as ever, Touma."
"…I thought you'd be somewhat taken aback, Kitahara."
"Well, I'm half-assed, as you say. I suppose that's why I can relate to both your family and Ogiso's family, Touma."
"And what would you understand… Well, I suppose you would."
"After all, if I were to look up your mother, I'd get over 100,000 results."
All sorts of old gossip can be read from the top of the search results related to her as well as from her encyclopedia pages.
"My family circumstances aren't that complex. They're really perfectly normal. In some people's eyes, they're no big deal at all."
She had married and divorced twice. Despite that, she had given birth when she was single.
"But that's exactly why… it's fine for me to be frustrated, right? It's fine for me to be pointlessly angry at her, right?"
"And that's exactly why I'm not good with her. Not one bit. I'm sure we'll never see eye to eye until the day we die."
Again, Touma looks up at the sky, talking with a very weak and frail voice. Still, she's a lot more talkative now than she was before.
But I still can't tell if she's angry… if she's smiling, crying… or even feeling anything at all.
"She'll either become my worst enemy… or the greatest friend of my life."
However, after looking up at the sky, she turns toward me…
"I promised Ogiso just before I left."
She shows me an expression that suggests regret for her previous abusive language. A somewhat uncomfortable, girlishly embarrassed expression.
"I told her, 'If you can persuade your parents, I'll join the Light Music Club.'"
This expression that she has kept hidden from me these past six months shines brighter than any gem in the night sky.
…Setting aside my earlier lackluster description of the night sky as "commonplace, and not too beautiful", that is.
"You don't want me to? Then I could take that back."
"But, but, but… I was already thinking of my next plan, too! I secretly swore to myself I'd definitely persuade you tomorrow!"
I thought that among all my failed attempts at persuading her, today would be the biggest failure.
The discussion over the club was crushed by an unexpected reality check, and I was sure that the friendly banter of the Ogiso household only made Touma angrier.
"You're bold, Kitahara. Did you plan to convince me with your tepid attitude…? You're getting ahead of yourself."
…Did Setsuna incur something other than her anger?
"Though I must say we're nearing the time limit here. From now on, we'll have to make use of every day."
"Didn't you think our plan was impossible…?"
"It sure is. If not for me."
It might be my turn to look away now…
The moon and stars in the sky aren't commonplace, or lacking in beauty at all.
"You guys are completely different from me, you see… I thought that it'd be impossible for us to understand each other…"
No matter how many times I anger her, and no matter how many times Ogiso makes her uncomfortable.
"But if that's the case… there might not be any harm in us being together."
In the end, Touma never betrays my firmly held notion that she's a good person deep down. A side of her that only I know.
"The amount of gratitude you have for me today won't ever be enough."
"Thank you, thank you… I mean it, thank you so much!"
It's Sunday, with only two weeks and a few days before the performance.
But at last, the Light Music Club, which was very close to being disbanded, has now managed to regain its form at the bare minimum and is finally pushing toward its final school festival.
"To sum it up, she'll be joining the Light Music Club starting today…"
"…This is Touma Kazusa. Please give her a warm welcome, everyone."
With a magnificent applause from Ogiso alone, my introduction of the newest member of the Light Music Club to the other members ends.
She seems to change on a whim. She was so talkative last night, but today she showed up unhappy, and then suddenlyーthe next momentーshe was even worse.
"And this is Iizuka Takeya. He's our current club president, and a guitarist."
Oh yeah, didn't he get kicked for trying to flirt with Touma or something?
"And this is… well, Ogiso Setsuna, but you already know her well. She's our singer…"
For personal reasons, I completely ignore Takeya's issues and quickly continue on with the discussion.
"Nice to meet you, Touma-san. Also, you can call me Setsuna, it's fine."
"I don't want you calling me Kazusa."
For her first words here, Touma sets up a clear line of defense against the super-friendly Ogiso.
"A-Aha… In any case, let's all do our best for the school festival, okay?"
When Ogiso called me last night… it was almost 1 AM.
From what I gathered, she'd been arguing with her father up until then. Her usually high-pitched voice had become deeper, and her breathing had a husky, almost seductive quality…
Still, her actual tone of voice sounded far too excited…
Meaning that Ogiso would return to the club, and Touma would also join.
After that, because she was probably too ecstatic, we spent about two hours talking…
She said, "I'm going to call Touma-san's place right now!" and I scolded her, reminding her that it was 3 AM.
"Ah, by the way, Kitahara-kun. You can also call me…"
In truth, I recall hearing those devilish words whispered to me countless times over the phone last night.
But right now, I'm not confident I can keep myself under control if I call her by her first name.
See? It all went out of control.
"W-Well then… let's begin the meeting now."
For some reason, the president has lost the will to fight. So as presumptuous as it may be, I take control of the situation.
On top of that, our dear president lost his usual self-confidence and carefree attitude, and took a seat in the corner of the classroom, shuddering.
It sure was loud when Touma sent that chair flying.
"Umm, well, what should we do? We've gathered everyone for now…"
"Were you listening to me at all last night? What even gave you the idea to say such nonsense?"
"N-No, I was listening, I was. Yeah, yeah, we need a bassist and drummer, right?"
Her sudden protest surprises me, but I'm so glad she cut me off before I could say something as stupid as, "Let's try playing together," like I was about to.
"Certainly, we could form a normal band with four people, but it's a different story with a singer who can only sing, two guitarists, and a keyboardist."
"L-Like I said… one step at a time…"
"Besides, you're far too hasty with this 'gathering all members' deal, when we haven't even decided on a song…"
"Ah, there's a song I'd like to do…"
Probably because she can't stand watching me fall into this unavoidable dilemma, Ogiso timidly raises her hand.
"…Well, is it okay to say it now? You two seem to be talking about something important."
"Not at all! Like Touma said, we can't move on without deciding on anything. Isn't that right, Touma?"
"…Yeah, it's good, it's all good. Well, what song did you want?"
Yeah, it's all good. She can scold me later…
"You mean us? Should we be aware of the song you want to sing, Ogiso?"
"Then, I'll give you hints. If you don't get it right after the third one,
"Eh? No, wait a minute! Is this song of yours that important…?"
Of course, I'm fully aware I only said that because I'm just a sore loser.
But it's really surprising to me that even Touma would remember something like that so vividly.
"Are you guys even aware that I'm here? Harukii!"
"It's still quite a nostalgic song… How long has it been?"
"Don't call it nostalgic. It's an eternal classic."
"Not having a drummer and bassist will hold us back…"
"And the season for this song is coming again… Though the school festival is a bit early for it."
"Well, the soonest we'll be seeing white snow gently piling up upon the streets is next month and thereafter."
"There's a sax in the interlude too…"
"Of course I do. I did say it's nostalgic, but I didn't say I'm not familiar with it… But you can count me in the Ogata Rina camp."
"So how will we make this work? What will we have to throw away, and what will we get?"
"I'm just giving credit to an artist who's got talent. That's all. What, do you guys hate Ogata Rina or something?"
"I bought her most recent album. The limited edition first print, no less."
"Four people… Vocal, guitar, guitar, keyboard. A bit one-sided. We should at least have a drummer…"
"Oh, nice. I missed the first print, so I've still yet to get it."
"Ah, I'll lend it to you. Want me to bring it tomorrow?"
"Really? Thanks. Then, to return the favor, I'll…"
"…How do you guys get along so well? One of you is Miss Houjou and the other is a stubborn representative…"
"Please don't put it that way. You've just reminded me of all the things I've missed out on in life."
"Do you still regret it? About being Miss Houjou, I mean."
"Yup, I suppose. I'd almost graduated without having met a certain stubborn representative…"
"…Hey, Haruki. Can I say that I'm dreaming right now? And it feels like a terrible nightmare, at that."
"…Hey, could you guys shut up for a moment?"
"…Hopeless chatter that has absolutely nothing to do with you, Touma."
It feels terrible to have Ogiso laughing at me when this concerns her just as much.
"Sorry about all that idle talk. Well, let's cut to the chase!"
"What is it, Touma? Did you come up with an amazing idea that could revive us from our… President?"
She neither joined our gossip nor snapped at us, she was only thinking of something in her mind. And the first one to be addressed was…
An unexpected question, directed at an unexpected person.
"I'm asking if you can use a synthesizer."
"Ah, no, I know what you mean, but…"
"Come on, Touma… don't scare him so much…"
I'm a man who's had his fair share of cowering when her beautiful face starts looking threatening.
"We don't have time. So hurry up and answer… if you would be so kind?"
That politeness of hers feels really forced and thoughtless…
"Well, to an extent. But if it's programming…"
"Touma, if you need someone for that, I could…"
"Okay, President. You don't need to come to practice from now on. Actually, don't even come to school; just focus on programming all by yourself as per my instructions."
That unexpected question directed at an unexpected person becomes an imposing command, and soon the Light Music Club's founder is out of the picture.
"I'll send the equipment that you'll need to your house. You can go home now. Good work today."
On top of that, the one who kicked him out is none other than our newest member… Although there was a lot of fanfare in getting her to join.
"With our current numbers, someone has to take on that role. We absolutely don't have enough people in the sound department."
"Using synthesizers is good. We have no choice since we lack the members. But you can let me deal with…"
"You have to learn to play at an acceptable level first, Kitahara. We'll talk after that."
The sound of her piano is so gentle and always helps me along, so why is she so merciless in person?
"Anyway, drums first. I'd like to at least finish one song before the week is done. Can you do it? Well, do it even if you can't."
"C-Come on, Touma… If you need someone for programming, I can do it… I was in charge of that in the past."
It's more appropriate to say that I was responsible for everything outside of performing the instruments.

Since our schedules were different, I couldn't spend much time practicing with everyone, so I was left to make the backing part of the songs, which is why most of my time was spent tinkering with the synth rather than practicing the guitar.
"Look, isn't it better if you let Takeya play the guitar, and I go do the programming instead?"
"See? We'd have the right people in the right places. We should try to keep our chances of pulling this off as high…"
"But that's assuming you can explain that reality right now to Ogiso."
"Hmm? What do you mean? What'll happen if Kitahara-kun switches with Iizuka-kun?"
"How about you tell her that you won't be by her side on the stage at the festival?"
Farewell, Iizuka Takeya. I won't ever forget about you.
"Now then, we have two weeks until the festival day. We'll make it one way or another, and I'll hit you if you even think about giving up."
"…Amazing. I understand now why you wanted her to join so much, Kitahara-kun…"
I never expected her to suddenly take control of everything, though…
"We'll think about the remaining songs as we go. Right now, let's focus on getting one song finished this week."
When I said we should plan things "as we go," she got mad at me…
"Well, we don't have time, so let's try doing it together… Ogiso."
"Yup! Also, you can call me Setsuna."
And she'd definitely get pissed off and scowl at me if I said, "Let's try doing it together"…
"You can sing the melody to the song, right? Want to do voice training?"
"Sorry, I've never actually been in the school chorus or anything, so I don't really know how that works. My voice just comes out whenever I sing normally."
"Well, I guess it can't be helped then. I suppose we'll have to go off the cuff… okay, Ogiso?"
"Ah, wait a minute. I'm not ready yet…"
I hastily reach for the guitar in my case so as to not be left behind by the two who are already prepared…
"…What are you talking about, Kitahara? Why would we need to wait for you?"
…I was going to, at least, but the merciless words Touma spills on me freeze me in place.
"I mean, we're playing together, aren't we?"
"At your current level, you'll just be a bother."
"I'd like to see how good Ogiso is for today. I don't have time to babysit anyone else."
The session we had between the two rooms and the rooftop… the day we first met…
"Go practice by yourself in Music Room 1. You can use the next room as well, right?
Even though she just joined today, she's already kicked out the president and is now excluding the only remaining senior member from band practice.
Did she persistently refuse to join in order to hide just how much of a tyrant she is…?
"If you don't like it, you could just stop complaining and show us something real. Then I'll be happy to oblige, Mister Vice President."
Farewell, Kitahara Haruki. I won't ever forget about me…
We got scolded and chased out of school by the security guard, by which time the dark, late fall night had already engulfed the sky.
After parting with Ogisoーwho commutes on footーat the station, the silence that lasted almost a station's journey between Touma and me is broken again.
"How was Ogiso's singing? From what I can tell, it seems like she's really on the right track."
"…Yeah. For an amateur, she's one of the better ones. I could even say that regular people might be fooled into thinking she's a pro."
Actually, even when it was the three of us, Ogiso was the only one keeping the conversation alive. So in reality, it might have been several hours since we talked.
"I know, right! Just as I expected. She sure is the queen of solo karaokes!"
"…Doesn't that mean there's no one under her rule?"
Though that may have just been Ogiso trying to smooth things over between the two of us after Touma had excluded me.
"W-Well, let's put that aside for now. I assume that we can have high hopes for our singer now?"
"I already knew that part would be fine. The problem instead lies with just about everything else."
Still, I won't let myself brood over it. This is a path we must go down if we're to shine on the festival stage.
"So we'll start with the bass, then. Well, I could try it again tomorrow."
"Oh? So in just one day, you've already reached a point where you can afford to worry about others?"
…Believe me, I'm not brooding at all right now.
She really shouldn't be so sarcastic if she's only going to regret it moments later.
I suppose that's just how Touma is, and I don't particularly mind that imbalance in her personality.
"I live in an apartment, so I can't play properly like I do at school, but I could practice with headphones."
"So I have to work on my skills even at home?"
"Of course. You're at a level where it's doubtful if you'll succeed even with 24 hours of practice every day…"
Well, I do mind the fact that she doesn't learn from her mistakes. I don't hate that part of her, but I do mind.
"At the very least, you should go over what you've practiced today. You can only sleep after you manage to play those parts perfectly."
"All right, all right, already. I'll practice after I eat dinner and study…"
"Eh? Ah, well… I mean, we have exams right after the festival ends…"
"All right, all right, already! Damn it, people who never prepare for tests have it so easy."
I get the feeling that her enthusiasm toward the performance has done a full reversal.
How do I say this… maybe Touma's just that fussy when it comes to music, or maybe she really has nothing but music…
"Besides, I'm sure you already have a recommendation for Houjou University, right? Why would you need to study now?"
"One normally studies the month before tests, right? Doesn't matter if it's periodic exams, placement exams, or end-of-term exams."
Well, following that line of reasoning does oblige one to study the whole year long… like I do.
"All right. I'm sorry. Don't look at me with such contempt, okay?"
"Yeah, I promise. I won't think about anything else but the guitar until the school festival. But in return, I want you to promise me something."
"That you'll definitely come up with something later."
"That everything will be fine as long as I put all my effort into my own part."
It's quite a shameful declaration, if I may say so myself…
Though it's shameful to make Touma, who just joined today, handle everything…
At the end of the day, though, that avoidant attitude of hers can actually come across as really reliable.
When I first heard her play that one summer day… that's when I first learned to rely on her.
And today, finally, we've regained that teacher-student relationship, so there's no more need to worry now.
…To someone else, my proclamation would most likely sound unbelievably pathetic, and I doubt that's just my imagination.
"Iwazu-chou, Iwazu-chou. Please mind the door when exiting."
The third station from school, nearest to Touma's house.
Touma walks off without lingering, yet she turns around and looks straight at me once again.
"The truth is, Kitahara, I'd like you to play with us as soon as possible too."
And, sure enough, this is how she ends the conversation.
Witnessing her worry about me makes me feel so glad I made her part of the team.
"Still, Ogiso takes priority first, right? As long as the vocals go well, who really cares about how the guitar plays?"
"…Well, that's one way to put it."
"The doors are closing. Please be careful."
"So really, I'm not mad about today. Although, I'd love it if you could include me as soon as possible too."
"Damn it… I almost did it without a single miss!"
"Okay, let's take a five minute break."
"Well, you're the one who did most of the work. Is your throat feeling okay?"
"Yup, don't worry. I'm always singing for around three hours straight."
"Hey, I made some honey lemonade. Do you want some?"
"…Ah, it's Kitahara-kun's guitar. Hang in there!"
"Just a little longer. You don't mind if the window's open for a bit during our break, do you?"
"Don't you think we should call Kitahara-kun over soon?"
"Not at all. He's still got a ways to go."
"But you know, it sounds like he's not making mistakes anymore."
"Even if he is, his tempo is all over the place. He suddenly slows down at the difficult parts."
"We don't have much time left, though. We won't make it for the performance if we don't practice together soon."
"Everything's going just according to my plan. We'll have everyone practice together on the weekend."
"You overestimate Kitahara too much, Ogiso. He's not that capable…"
"Overestimation is 'too much' by definition, isn't it?"
"…You shouldn't let yourself be corrupted so much by Kitahara, Ogiso. You'll end up with a rotten personality with nothing but fault-finding on your mind."
"…Hey, Touma-san? Aren't you also actually holding back quite a bit?"
"Not at all. Besides, why would I even…"
"You're playing along with Kitahara-kun's guitar though, right?"
It's 8 PM once again. It's been three days since we started practice.
The security guard frowned saying, "Touma-san's daughter again?". It was the third day we'd used the Touma family's influence, that had to be our limit.
"Then say that first… I'm a bit tired too."
After the three of us walked down the dark streets together, and after the two of us got on the train, we engaged in our usual unenergetic conversation.
"This is the usual for me… about four hours."
Putting aside studies and a bunch of things, I was able to free up a lot of time to spend on practicing the guitar.
The guitar head laid on top of me when I woke up on the floor last night.
"Hey, how long have you been awake, Touma…?"
How long has she been awake? She just spaced out for a few seconds.
"I know I have to practice, but what do you do when you get home?"
"Well, there are finals right after the festival…"
In and of itself, I was quite happy that she could tell this kind of joke, but I'd like her to at least figure out the timing better.
"I'm fine. It's not like you could do anything about it even if I explained it, Kitahara."
"Could it be… that I put a large burden on you without knowing?"
"If you have time to feel guilty, use it to practice instead! Are you practicing at least ten hours a day?"
She didn't deny it… So I really am burdening Touma that much…
"I know you mentioned it before too, but does it really have to be ten hours a day?"
"Since I was three, it was like that during Christmas, New Year's, my birthday, and even when I promised to go out with friends…"
"And normally, I'd begin preparing three months before competitions. During that time, it ended up taking about sixteen hours a day."
"You really like picking out the small things, Kitahara… I did have at least a day like that every three years."
It'd be so miserable if she lived like that for a thousand days without a single day like that.
…Though I really don't want to think about what happened during the other 999 days.
"It's really paradise right now. There are days when I don't have to play at all…"
"Well, can you play properly now? Can you play without missing a note until the end, in perfect rhythm, and while accompanying other people?"
Though it was an obvious topic to change to, her attitude shows that she's regretting what she just mentioned.
"I think I might be able to pull it off now, but I can't really tell without actually trying it first."
I've gained enough experience throughout my life to know when to play along when someone wants to change the subject.
"So you can accompany us now, huh?"
"That's not what I said. I said I'd have to try it first."
"That's exactly what I was hoping for. Then, how about tomorrow after school…?"
"I'll be finishing up with Ogiso tomorrow. I still don't have time to keep an eye on you, as always."
"…So in other words, we're postponing it until the weekend?"
That's a shame. I was so close to getting acknowledged by Touma.
Even if it was just a way for her to get away from the previous topic…
In the end, it seems like we took a step forward with our preparations for the performance, but we're still short on time.
"Iwazu-chou, Iwazu-chou. Please mind the door when exiting."
The usual station. And her usual stride.
And the usual conversation we have, exchanged between the train and the platform.
"The doors are closing. Please be careful."
This isn't the usual station I get off at.
The instant the train doors started closing, Touma grabbed me by my necktie…
Well, this is three stations from school. The station closest to her home.
I thought that I wouldn't be capable of making such an impossible assumption, but…
It looks like it's not all that impossible.
"What's wrong? After all this time, you're going to get cold feet now?"
As for where I am right now, I'm at Touma's house.
But that's not the issue right now… I mean, normally it would be, but…
"I knew you'd say that. That's why I never wanted to invite anyone over."

My first impression of the Touma household as I first passed through the gates was that it had an extravagant exteriorーsuch that it was intimidating to even a certain bastard son of the wealthy Okayama familyーbut that was only the beginning.
Before I had time to be taken aback by the unbelievably large living room or the wide, well-maintained garden just outside, I was suddenly taken to the basement.
And when Touma turned on the lights, I saw a white room around 40 square meters large.
But what caught my eye the most was a microphone dangling from the ceiling of a small room, closed off by glass windows.
"That's just one of its functions, isn't it!? Why is all this in a residential house!?"
The room beyond the glass window was filled with even more amazing equipment, something you'd find in a school broadcast room, and its purpose here was obvious.
Actually, Takeya and his group often went to a nearby rental studio, but this is on a completely different level altogether…
"Originally, this was a studio built into the household for a certain world-famous artist. My mother only bought it, along with all this equipment."
"You know this artist's true identity, don't you?"
Then again, Touma's mother is also a "world-famous artist."
"I haven't used anything but the piano in a while, so I had someone come in and do maintenance yesterday. In any case, it seems everything still works fine."
"If it frustrates you, then try being abandoned by your parents."
"Don't joke about something like that so lightly, it's painful."
"Then don't poke your nose in so casually."
"I'll apologize if you put it that way. I'll apologize and make the whole mood super awkward."
"…Let's just practice for now, okay? Practice. Like you asked, I will accompany you for as long as you want, Kitahara."
Regarding how far I can push my luck, and where I should pull back… It's still very much like a tightrope trial.
In fact, perhaps I've been pushing my luck all day today, and it's simply that she has grown more tolerant to it.
Even so, I feel like our conversations have started to become more and more in sync, just like I've always wished for since spring.
"Aa-ah, now it's all over the place."
"Then, do you want to use a metronome on the next run?"
She's always watching me, always pointing out my mistakes, yet never making a single mistake herself…
"Look. Up until now I've adjusted my tempo to match yours, but we can't have it that way anymore, okay?"
I've fully realized… with the way I play, it's just not possible for me to keep up with Touma's tempo.
"Besides the vocals, the rhythm for the synth isn't going to change, so you have to keep up by yourself."
How much unreasonable trouble did she put herself through to accompany me up until now?
"Aa-ah, this is just no good! I knew it already, but you've just got no talent, Kitahara."
She puts me down like she enjoys it, and in response I…
"One more time from the beginning, please!"
"Yeah, yeah. As many times as you'd like."
I've decided that I'd hang on desperately, haven't I?
"Hey, come on, this time you're too fast!"
After all, all of this just feels great.
To have Touma do her best to find all of my mistakes.
To have Touma laugh at how terrible my playing is.
To have Touma fully utilize her usually limited vocabulary just for the sake of disparaging me.
…To have Touma looking only at me. To have her always smiling at me…
"One more time! Damn it… I always keep screwing up at the same spot!"
"I guess you really can't get out of a rut if you get stuck once. Well, let's leave it at that today…"
"I'll definitely finish it in one go! Sheer effort has always gotten me out of tough situations!"
"Ah, but you know, the last train's…"
"Then… as requested, let's do it once more, from the top."
When I come to, I see a brightly lit white room.
I've been hugging the guitar I was playing like a body pillow.
Pulling off the blanket covering my body, I quickly become aware of the implications of "coming to" in the first place.
"Fuaaah… I have to head back home… Touma?"
My back is stiff and aching all over from sleeping on the floor. I put the guitar in its case, and finally take a look around.
There's no one by the piano anymore. I'm the only one in the room.
I struggle with my body, sluggish from having fallen asleep in a bad position, and open the basement door.
Perhaps the last train's already gone. If that's so, the taxi fare will be pretty horrible for a student like me.
While irrationally cursing at the needle on the watch, which is pointing at the wrong spot, I get a breath of fresh air on ground level after having been underground for several hours…
And I encounter something that I shouldn't have seen no matter what.
"Wait, stop, Touma! I realize that this is a very bad situation, but could I just please ask you a couple of questions?"
"O-Okay… You see, I've been completely confused since waking up. I'd like you to at least understand my situation here…"
I timidly turn away, and the wonderful spe… no wait, the "shocking" spectacle hides itself behind a door.
"Jeez, what's up with this…? Why do I have to deal with this, just for showering at my own home…"
Ah, the sound of rustling clothes…
"Uh, umm… My first question is… What time is it?"
No, I must suppress my worldly desires for the time being…
"Well, it's broken. For some reason, it says it's 7:50."
"Your brain is what's broken, not the watch."
Thus she answered my second question as well… That being, "Why is it so bright outside?".
"I'm heading off to school soon. I'll probably get there on time if I leave now."
"Eh? You're kidding! I haven't changed clothes! I haven't taken a bath either, I haven't even washed my face!"
"Not your problem…!? What do I do? If I lose my recommendation because of unfounded rumors like me staying over without permission, loitering around late at night, or going to clubs…"
"Guys shouldn't worry over such trivial things! Besides, you did stay over without permission."
It's true that I'm staying over without permission. It's true that this is the first time I've visited the home of a girl who lives by herself.
It's also true that… this is Touma Kazusa's home.
Takeya would probably commend me if he found out, and then criticize me when I tell him that nothing happened.
"If you're worried about that, then you can head back home, take a shower and get a change of clothes."
"Well, I can't be late. I've never been late since I enrolled."
"There's just no pleasing you… I just don't care anymore. Do whatever you want."
She opens the living room door again, and the Touma I'm used to seeing every day emerges.
But even with her usual school uniform, the vivid image of what lies underneath is still fresh in my…
I can't bear to face her…
"I'm gonna head out now. I'll give you the key, so give it back when you get to school."
"Ah, wait, don't leave me! I don't remember the way back to the station!"
"Then hurry it up already. Soon we'll have to run to make it."
"A-All right. I'll go grab my stuff right now."
I'm saved again, by the fact that Touma is a good person deep down.
I do want to point out to her that she could have just woken me up before the last train left, but let's not do that.
"Umm… I'm sorry. For catching you in a rather… immodest state."
"…! Don't remind me of something I just managed to forget!"
"I was practicing last night, and it was morning before I knew it…"
As I rubbed my sleepy eyes and left my seat to freshen up my face, I found Ogiso standing in front of our classroom, waving and waiting for me nonchalantly.
I quickly turned and noticed that the seat beside mine was empty. I truly admire her sixth sense for danger, especially at times like this.
"I didn't manage to take a bath either… so I'd stay away if I were you."
It's not as if I hate eating lunch together with Ogiso. Rather, it makes me feel really happy.
"You're right, your hair is such a mess!"
As Ogiso rustles through my hair, I feel an indescribably intimidating air.
…Specifically, it's not coming from Ogiso, but rather from all the male students around us.
"Yup, yup, you really are working hard, Kitahara-kun. I'll give this cream croquette to you as a reward."
"At least let me finish my sentence…"
And the moment Ogiso took a side dish from her bento box and placed it onto my plate… the glares directed toward it grew even more intense.
Our surroundings can't keep up with the incredibly sociable attitude that Ogiso had never shown before.
"Right, right, by the way, there are already rumors going around about the Light Music Club."
"The rumors are only about you, Ogiso, and it's not just because the school festival is near."
"You've changed recently, Ogiso. In a lot of ways, at that."
"I suppose. It feels like there's a load off my shoulders now, I'm doing what I want to do."
Yeah, Ogiso has been quite defenseless recently.
The "wall" that she had built up where she'd treat everyone as a friend had now crumbled away, since she's clearly favoring a… certain someone.
"Thanks to that, one could say that your standing in Miss Houjou is becoming less and less certain too."
Specifically, it means that because of her actions, she was no longer guaranteed to be the top favorite in the school rankings.
However, the problem is that Ogiso is still very attractive. That's why it's so difficult for anyone to estimate the chances of her winning.
"You mean my three-win streak is at risk?
…That doesn't sound too bad either. Like, 'I'm gonna return to being a normal girl!', you know?"
"…So the stage performance next week will be your retirement concert?"
There's a misunderstanding circulating among everyone suggesting that Ogiso Setsuna has finally got herself a boyfriend.
But that's just a false assumption. After all, Ogiso treats Touma and me with the exact same attitude.
In other words, she's treating me the way she is simply because we're friends, and not because she's seeing me as someone of the opposite sex.
"Well then… that was a nice meal. Let's go back to class and get some sleep…"
…Though that's something only Touma and I know.
"All right. Are you fine with a hot black?"
"Cafe au lait. With a lot of sugar."
"Now that you mention it, Kitahara-kun does look sleepy too. The two of you are working hard, huh?"
"…So he didn't tell you. Well, not like he could."
"That's because I told him to forget about sleeping until he could play properly."
"You sure are strict with Kitahara-kun. Tough love from a teacher to her pupil?"
"…It's just that I can't stand people who are crap with musical instruments. Even though the instruments all yearn to be used to make beautiful sounds."
"Well, Kitahara-kun's already gone home because you keep being so strict with him every day."
"He can do as he pleases. I have no complaints as long as he gets better at playing."
"Hey, Touma-san. At this rate, how long will it be before we can perform together?"
"Eh, really? Wow, that's so soon! I see… Sounds like it'll be fun!"
"Keep your hopes up… You'll definitely be surprised."
"For all the ill you speak about him, you sure have a lot of trust in him."
"The doors are closing. Please be careful."
20:15, at Iwazu-chou Station. Touma got off the train at exactly the same time she did last night.
Well, it's as we agreed while we were on the train this morning, so there's nothing really surprising about it.
"This time I've come fully prepared. I also took a bath, and brought a spare uniform."
"You sure are eager to stay over again, aren't you?"
Today, I returned home as soon as classes ended, and within the span of two hours I got changed, took a bath, took a nap, did my own practice, and returned here.
Because I realized last night that my "master" is exceptional at teaching…
"I'll return on the last train this time. This is all just a precaution in case that doesn't work out. It's normal to prepare for everything, right?"
"…It's annoying how convincing it sounds when you're the one saying it."
Even the master herself is obviously irritated, but since she's always like that, I'm not worried in the slightest.
"I'll be fine today! I'll clear it perfectly and head home as soon as I can."
Touma puts on a disinterested face, gallantly leaving me behind like she always does.
So I hurry to catch up with her, not losing sight of her elegant black hair.
"Oh, by the way, is there a convenience store along the way?"
"Actually, I was hoping to get a travel set."
"…Are you planning on ever going home?"
And today, I'm once again looking forward to hearing the beautiful sound that spreads from her fingertips.
"In just two days… you sure have made yourself comfortable."
"I've been sleeping on the floor for two days straight, so my body hurts like hell."
It's 7:15. The alarm I set on my watch just in case came in handy.
Even so, sleeping for only two hours is quite tough. In the end, we practiced until almost five in the morning. It's scary how easily we lose sense of time while in the basement.
"Are you going to take a bath? If you don't mind, let me wash my face and I'll be right out."
