"I didn't peek on purpose yesterday either. It was just a happy coincidence."
"I see, I feel sorry for you… for what's about to happen to you now."
"I'm joking, I'm just joking… Ahh, this feels great!"
"I told you to not make yourself at home."
The cold water splashing against my face makes my body go stiff.
It's Friday. One more day and it'll be the weekend. I'll be able to practice as much as I want from dawn till dusk.
…I need to maintain my stamina, though.
"Whew, I'm awake… Ah, that's right, Touma, want me to make breakfast?"
"That's why you fall asleep in class all the time. If you don't nourish yourself well in the morning, your body won't wake up."
"You're one to talk with how you've been this week, Kitahara."
"Well, putting that aside, how about I do it as an apology for yesterday?"
"…If you can do it, go right ahead. Just use whatever's in my fridge."
"Are you underestimating me? Toast and eggs sunny-side up are my specialty."
And that's about all I'm capable of making. For a male student, I'm as average as they come.
"I see a lack of trust in your expression… Just you watch!"

I'll show her that I'm capable of more than just barging into people's homes, begging them for lessons, never letting them sleep, falling asleep before they do, and even stealing a glance at them when they're changing clothes.
…What kind of despicable bastard am I?
After five minutes of noise, Music Room 2 is enveloped in silence.
Ogiso looks at me dumbfounded, and Touma breathes a heavy sigh as she looks at the ceiling.
With hope and anxiety… and a tiny bit of confidence, I look at Touma.
And with the "OK" that I had been eagerly awaiting from Touma, I feel like exploding with happiness…
"We did it! We did it, Kitahara-kun!"
…Or I would have, had the shockwave beside me not extinguished me.
"See Touma-san, it's like I said! Kitahara-kun can do anything if he puts his mind to it!"
From the bottom of my heart, I feel so happy that we've completely blown past all my predictions… Come to think of it, just how little faith did I have in us, anyway?
"He worked hard all by himself, and he managed to produce just the result we were hoping for! Amazing!"
"Definitely. It seems like we've really underestimated Kitahara."
Touma completely takes over the conversation, noticing that I have absolutely no idea how to explain myself.
"With this, we've got one song done… There's still a lot ahead of us, but let's call it a day."
I look at my watch… It's a little past 5 o'clock. Even though daytime is shorter in this season, evening hasn't settled in yet.
In the past week, our "acting president" never ended the Light Music Club's practice sessions this early.
"To make up for it, we'll meet up tomorrow at 10 AM. We need to match up with the synthesizer, and we have to decide on the next song."
"We can meet up, sure… but where? Is it okay to use this place on Saturday?"
"I know where we'll be practicing. We'll meet at Iwazu-chou Station's north entrance. Kitahara, go ahead and call the president too."
I see… It's finally time to let Ogiso witness "Studio Touma" as well.
"Our first rehearsal will be this Saturday and Sunday, so you'll all be staying over this weekend."
"Staying over? Wow, really!? Amazing, we're gonna be staying over!"
And… it's finally time to open up "Hotel Touma" to Ogiso as well, I guess.
"I mean, if we don't get everyone pulling all-nighters, it just won't feel like the school festival's really coming up. Don't you think so?"

"Back in middle school, we weren't allowed to stay overnight in school either, not even right before the festival. So if we did stay, we'd turn off the lights and hide when the teachers went by patrolling."
Though in middle school, I was in the position of patrolling and forcing people who stayed all night in school without permission to go home.
"I haven't been able to do that much since enrolling here…
It's probably because everyone around you was really conscious about not wanting you being involved in any unrefined physical labor.
…Though considering all that, I wonder just how much she will let loose now, having been held back for the past two years.
"…And now, it's your turn, Kitahara. You have an important role to fulfill now."
"Yes. We ended practice early just for this. So let's get going."
"Like I said, our cell phones will constantly be on, and you will be able to contact us at any time. That means you'll be able to call not just Setsuna-san, but the two of us as well."
"And if no one happens to pick up?"
"I have a memo prepared. If no one among the three of us answers within five calls, Setsuna-san's curfew will be set to 6 PM from then on."
"6 PM… That's a bit tight, isn't it?"
"…Putting my daughter aside, what do the other girl's parents say to all this?"
"…Let me be honest about that. Touma-san's family lives abroad, and she has no guardian present currently at her household."
"There's a helper who comes to clean the premises twice a week, but the truth is, no one lives there other than Touma-san."
"Living on her own! So cool, I wanna move out of the house soon too!"
"What are you talking about? A lone girl studying and living by herself… It's not as easy as you think it is, Takahiro."
"…I'm aware you might object after this conversation. Even so, everyone agreed to bring up all these details so we could get your permission without hiding anything."
"Why not let her, Dear? Setsuna's friends are doing their best for her…"
"Ma'am, it's not a matter of us doing our best. It's just a matter of whether or not we can get permission for her to stay over."
"It's exactly as he says. You shouldn't be getting the wrong idea."
"There are plenty of bedrooms available, and they'll be separated by gender, of course. Even so, all I can do from here is ask that you trust me."
"Kitahara-kun, was it? How do I say this… you think quite like an adult."
"Sure is. I can't even believe he's in the same grade as my sister."
"No, I'm not saying it's a bad thing. If anything, I'm actually impressed by how reliable you seem to be."
"I've lived with only my mother, so perhaps it's only natural that I've become like this."
"Oh, is that so? What about your father?"
"No, it's fine… They divorced when I was in sixth grade of elementary school."

"Even so, my life as a student hasn't been affected by it at all. We receive child support every month, and I'll even be able to further my studies at a university, so I'm grateful to my father even now."
"It's just that… since I'm the only man in the family, it's a habit of mine to try and act tough no matter the case… In the past, people have remarked that I never really acted like a child."
"Well, that must have been difficult for you. Our Setsuna and Takahiro have both been spoiled a lot, so they just selfishly do as they please."
Start off with a strong emphasis on reason, then make an appeal to human sympathy leaving no room for any remaining opposition.
And so, the overall positive response I'm getting here means progress for the stay-over tomorrow. Things should be fine from here on out so long as I don't mess up any further.
But besides that, I should just get one thing out of the way…
"Is it really okay for Kitahara-kun to be having a meeting with my family alone…?"
"The burden on your throat would be too great if you tried to persuade them yourself, Ogiso. This will surely go late into the night."
Also, you can just call me Setsuna."
"We can't hold a candle to Kitahara when it comes to sophistry, that's the only thing he's good at… Don't worry and just leave it to him."
"We might as well put him to use for once given that he's already dragged me into all this."
"…What? Is there something you want to say?"
"Isn't putting three sugar sticks in a bit too much…?"
"What are you, a high-class lady!? …Well, I suppose you do qualify as one…"
I had predicted that the Light Music Club members would say things like that as a reaction to seeing Touma's house.
They're not the problem, though. Rather, it's more so the fact that I have to force myself to react the exact same way they are, given that I've already experienced this.
"Come on in. You can leave all your stuff other than the musical instruments here."
"Please excuse me. Ah, put your shoes in the rack here."
Moreover, I'll have to act more surprised than I was a few moments ago. …My acting really isn't the best, though.
"It's a bit cold right now, so bear with it until the heating kicks in."
"What the hell, what the hell is this!? Why is this sort of thing in a normal house!?"
"I'm really surprised. Ah, watch out for the cord there."
"Amazing… Is this your piano room, Touma-san?"
"This was set up by the previous owner, I've just been using it as-is."
"So the previous owner was a studio musician? Still though, he had to be bourgeois…"
"Seems like it, but I don't know the details. Well then, let's start setting up."
"All right. Takeya, come and help here."
While glancing at Takeya who is still recovering from the shock, and Ogiso who is looking around with glittering eyes, I flip the switch of a device that I'm actually familiar with…
"…Oh, wait. Where should I plug this in?"
Whoops, I'm supposed to pretend I'm not used to this.
Just as I had carefully planned, our stay started off with everyone being taken aback by the Touma household's extravagance.
We're all sweating after having played just one song, even though the heater hasn't warmed up the room yet.
But I guess that's what they call concentrating and giving it your very best.
Ogiso looked at me dumbfounded yesterday, but today she smiles brightly at me.
"I guess the drums won't be an issue. If we just adjust the bass a little bit…"
As expected, Touma is already devoting her attention to the synth data that Takeya programmed.
And Takeya is so stunned it's almost rude… What an impolite guy.
"Haruki… when did you even? I mean, it's like you can finally play properly!"
"I'm in a good mood right now, so I'll let that slander of yours slide. Don't let it happen again, though."
"You've improved so much that I just realized how half-hearted you were before. I was wrong about you."
"At least listen to what I said literally seconds ago…"
"All right, the synth looks good. Okay. I'll do some fine-tuning myself later. Thanks, President."
"Now then, we've gotta think about the next song."
"Uwaah, already on to a new song!"
"H-Hey, Haruki? Did, did she just… thank me…?"
"After giving it some more thought, one song isn't enough for our repertoire. We should have two more songs if possible, or at the very least one more."
"We still have a week left. At our current pace, one more song seems about right."
"Of course she's thanking you. You really did well, seriously. My bad, Takeya, really."
"Well, I don't really care for your gratitude."
"The other bands probably have about three songs prepared… but I suppose that can't be helped. We've only had two weeks to properly prepare, after all."
"We'd be putting the cart before the horse if we added too many songs and the quality of the individual songs suffered as a result."
"But it's her we're talking about! Touma Kazusa! I can't believe she'd say that after hearing the rumors about her in school!"
"Who cares about her reputation or what rumors there are? The truth is, Touma's a really kind person deep down. Man, it's so frustrating that no one understands this…"
"Don't whisper praises behind people's backs. I can hear you loud and clear."
"Geh, you heard!? Sorry, were you offended? I apologize."
"Jeez, I can't let my guard down for even a second…"
"Let's discuss the second song, then. Any requests?"
"Well, as the president, I'd like to…"
"Eeeekk!? I'm sorry! I'm sorry I interrupted you, please continue as you like!"
"A lot better than a certain masochist who takes pleasure in being told off."
"Well, sure, let's hear your opinion then, President. Anything on your mind?"
"What do you mean? Aren't you the president of this club to begin with?"
Not that anyone could tell with how things are playing out right now…
Is it atonement for dragging him off the stage? Touma is being kind of nice to Takeya today.
But she's only being "kind of" nice… It's quite sad.
"…I guess I'd like to hear something from Ogata Rina. You know, since our first song is from Morikawa Yuki, right?"
"Takeya… your choices always safely follow some sort of bandwagon…"
"…And quite a wonderful one, at that."
"Yeah, a big yes from me! I can sing any of her debut songs.
…I don't think I can work with her recent English versions, though."
"…Truth is, I also prefer Ogata Rina."
"Heh, is that so? I guess great minds think al…"
"Okay, all right, President. You've done a good job. Take a break in the corner now."
"Never in my life have I ever been pushed to the sidelines this much…"
"We'll go with one of Rina's songs, then. Any song in particular you would like to cover?"
"Should we go with a song from one of her recent albums? I brought this one since I planned to return it to Ogiso…"
"Ah, excuse me. Could I give my own personal opinion again?"
"Whatever motivates the singer takes top priority."
"…These three really get along well when they're together."
"Then, you see, here's the first hint. If the first song was White Album…"
"It went on sale during the same year… Kitahara-kun is correct!
Oh my… why was it so easy to figure out?"
Ogata Rina's signature song. It was released the same year as White Album, eclipsing it and winning her the top prize at the music festival.
It was the song that caused her sudden rise to stardom, and until now, it and its various versions such as live or "best of" versions have been included in countless albums.
An artist with a career as long as Ogata Rina's generally has a very wide fan base, and there would often be minor differences in how different generations receive a song.
However, regardless of this song being in the style of her early young-idol era, it has the support of fans from almost all age groups.
"It's fine. Yeah. I'm sure that everyone's heard this song before, and it's pretty easy to enjoy."
"Really? That's great. I can sing it regardless of which arrangement of the song we go with."
However… Touma and Takeya didn't react as excitedly as we did for some reason.
"Me? Why? It's a cool song, isn't it?"
Or rather, they seem somewhat worried…?
"Well, sure, yeah, it's a cool song. But that's…"
"Heh, ha, hahaha…! Y-You're… really okay with this, right, Kitahara?"
…And then, it's as if her funny bone got tickled.
"Eh? Eh? I-Is there something strange about it?"
"Haha, there isn't, there really isn't… Yup, when it comes to the vocals, anyway… Haha… heh… haha!"
"What, you're creeping me out… Anyway, we're set, right? Sound of Destiny it is, then?"
"Yup, it's a done deal. I won't let you back out now. Ahaha… heheh… ahahahaha…!"
What caused Touma to act so out of character…
…Was something I would become aware of five minutes later.
I completely and utterly forgot… what exactly makes this song so "cool."
"Are you really going to do this, Haruki? This solo…"
This song… has a really complex guitar solo at the very end.
"How long are you going to keep that up!?"
"Good luck, Kitahara. You can do it for sure. Aha, ahahaha…"
Her sadistic tendencies are further fueled by my teary eyes… It doesn't seem like her laughter will end anytime soon.
Playing on the monitor in the room is Ogata Rina's Budokan Live DVD, now several years old.
Putting aside that the hall went wild over the first encore song being Sound of Destiny…
Once the vocal section had finished, the camera immediately switched from Rina to the guitarist in the accompanying band, focusing on his fingers.
It's like nothing but the guitar matters… No, more like the guitar is leading the last part of the song and holding it together.
"To say the least, it's impossible for me. No way I could move my fingers like that."
"But it'd be amazing if you could. Wow, it's so cool…"
"Well, sure, it would be cool if I could play it…"
In this world, one should be aware of and come to terms with one's own limits.
An amateur like me who only started playing the guitar this year to tackle this so ambitiously… Who do they think I am, Icarus?
The wax wings on my back would melt away from my own greasy sweat before I could even challenge such a difficult song.
"Hey, let's do it! I wanna see you play this, Kitahara-kun!"
In contrast to my pessimistic outlook, it seems Ogiso is all fired up about this.
"It doesn't matter if you screw up a little. It's just a festival, so everyone'll laugh and let it slide."
"That's right, they'll laugh at me before letting it slide!"
I'll let myself be laughed at too, okay?"
"Uhh, it's up to the audience to decide who they laugh at, you know…"
"Nope. It's already been decided! Touma-san even said we can't change it now. We're doing this song! Period!"
I wonder if people at school would be terrified seeing this obstinate side of Ogiso.
…After all, there's a shining example of that happening in front of my very eyes right now.
If things have come to this, there's nothing I can say to change things.
That's because the only person who can snap her back to reality also happens to be the most knowledgeable in music, someone who's relentless, and doesn't give in to others…
"It's fine, right Touma-san? Kitahara-kun can definitely do this!"
Touma makes fun of me so much, but… I know that she doesn't really mean it, and I know that she wouldn't allow something this ridiculous to happen.
There's no way she would allow this, knowing it would turn out a complete failure…
"Yeah, it'll be fine. Kitahara can do it."
"Right! I knew you'd say that, Touma-san!"
The raven that was laughing is not laughing anymore…
"W-Wait, Touma! What happened to your pride? I thought you had a stance of never compromising when it comes to music…"
"And of course, I won't. You'll definitely have to learn this."
"I'm telling you it's impossible! You should know my capabilities the best, right?"
"I told you when we chose this song, didn't I? 'You can do it, I'm sure.'"
"I hate jokes. You should know my personality the best, right?"
For Touma to be making this elaborate a prank…
I'd be laughing my ass off if not for the current situation. How is this happening…
"Anyway, let's start right away. Individual practice first. Ogiso?"
"Yup! Do your best, everyone. We only have a week until the main event."
Yes, only one week until the main event.
Without a doubt, we've lost all sense of rational judgement, deluded into thinking we could take on the world after just mastering a single song.
…No matter how you look at it, it's just impossible.
"I've done all I can here. Since we've decided on the song, I can do the work at my place."
"Even if you're going home, you could at least eat dinner with the rest of us."
"Like I said, I've done all I can here. I mean that I can't even work here, so I have to hurry back home."
Takeya's expression is strangely calm and serene, despite him being treated terribly by Touma and being sent home basically crying.
"It's not like I was treated terribly and am being sent home crying, all right?"
For my thoughts to have reached him like that…
"I'm looking forward to the school festival. I can't imagine how the performance will be like that day."
"I'm the one who can't imagine it at all…"
"Somehow, I just somehow feel like it'll all turn out perfectly fine."
"I can't imagine your train of thought either…"
After that, I did attempt the solo numerous times, but I still couldn't get past three seconds…
"Well, there's bound to be a lot of tough things coming, and I'm sure there'll be troubles you'd never experienced before, but grit your teeth and keep yourself together, all right?"
"I know. This is the first and last time I can act like an idiot as a student. I'll savor it in all its glory."
Even though I was busy with class rep work and always headed straight home to study in the past, I won't forget to have fun this time.
During these past two and a half years in school, I've had such a pathetically clean and proper life that it hurts.
I won't let anyone stop me from having a blast just once on the day of the festival.
"Indeed, it'll be your first and last heavenly experience. For your lifetime, anyway."
"Should you really be going that far? Is my life only going to go downhill from this point?"
"But it's true… You have such a crazy chance of success with either of your two options. It's unbelievable…"
"…If you don't want me to hear, just keep quiet, don't talk to yourself under your breath."
Takeya ends our conversation, feeling that it could only turn into a squabble at this point.
In the end, he leaves me with a smile that was unlike him, as if he were saying, "There's nothing I can teach you anymore."
And then, his expression changes as if he remembered something.
"By the way, what are you gonna do with that thing? I still have it on me."
He brought up a topic I'd almost forgotten.
"There's still time, though. If we start now…"
"We've only got a week left. Even if it were finished, when would we practice?"
"…Yeah. Sorry I couldn't keep my promise."
"I lost the moment I let it pass as just a spoken promise, anyway."
"…Thank you… for easing my guilt at the very end! I'll see you next time, then. Later, man!"
"Yeah… Next time, then. See you on Monday."
"Even after being hurt, And getting hurt by others…♪"
The valiant progress I'd been making thus far… came down to me hitting a wall at the solo's five-second mark.
"Just call it a day with this. Go take a bath when Ogiso comes out."
"I'm fine. It'd be bad if I went in after Ogiso or before you…"
"You could just change the water before you go in."
"That's not what this is about. Also, think about global warming, you bourgeois."
She's probably just trying to be considerate, but it's hard to imagine she even thinks of me as a guy with the way she's treating me now.
Well, that's just what I think given that she's cool with letting us stay over, but somehow it's hurt my pride as a man just a little bit…
Even so, it'd be foolish of me to give up this advantage for such a reason alone.
"…Move your fingers like this. Wanna give it one more shot?"
"Come on, don't tear apart my pride in just 30 seconds…"
And while most people would have trouble climbing over that wall, she just flies over it.
"I've been fooling around with guitars for about two years myself, so there's nothing strange about me being able to play at least this much."
I admire her, and envy her a little bit.
"But you're good at studying, Kitahara. I'm not proud of it, but I don't even know if I'll be able to graduate."
"But you're better when it comes to all the cool stuff."
"What's cool depends on one's viewpoint, doesn't it?"
"That's right. There are things that I think are cool. So if you ask me, those would be the piano, the guitar, and Touma."
"…Give me the guitar for a sec."
I sense that things could become rather awkward, so I take the guitar from Touma once again.
"…Though I do regret what I just said a little bit, all of it is unfortunately true."
…However, I do feel that pointlessly following up on my own statement is symbolic of how uncool I am.
Even if I try my best to fake it and change the subject, I can barely last even five seconds.
Maybe it's because I'm tired and sleepy, but I am more vexed than usual, ashamed, and…
"It's all right. You can do it, Kitahara."
"I'll make sure you can play… I'll turn you into the cool man you spoke of."
Yet somehow, this awkwardness and embarrassment feels pleasant.
"In return, don't think about sleeping until the festival's over."
"Be sure to come here every day next week too. And skip classes if you have to. Can you do that?"

I want to think it's a lie. I want to think it's a joke…
Because if it isn't, everything that I just did in front of Setsuna would be…
Class is only about to start, but I already feel the strength fading from my body. This week's off to such a great start…
"In truth, I started listening a bit before the "See you after school" part."
Just as I thought all power had left me, I tense up completely, my stomach twisting and turning.
Seriously, what a way to start the week…
"T-That was… well, I don't plan on making excuses. Umm, it's been like that since I got home last night…"
"She was sulking so much yesterday. I was worried that she was going to start crying… She probably held it in until she had some time alone with you."
I'm all tensed up and nervous about it…
"I suppose it's all well and good. The princess seems to be in good spirits. I feel like the tribute you offered her is a bit too shabby, though."
"I'm just a simple commoner, after all…"
But she doesn't show the reaction that I was somewhat hoping for.
"Now then, let's get studying. The end-of-term finals are coming up soon… I get the feeling there's something else right before that, though."
From the beginning until the end, Touma had an astonishingly kind smile that was nothing like her, watching over Setsuna… and me.
"The princess would also like you to pay the same tribute…"
"I must refuse, sir knight. For I am but a wandering musician. I wish not to be tied to any single country."
Which is why I end up feeling really relieved…
But there's still a strange feeling lingering in my chest; a prickling sensation, like a single thorn that hasn't been pulled out.
"Kitahara, here's the list of necessary materials. Motoyama said to send it to you for a review."
"Hey, Kitahara-kun, I've got a question about the basketball club's supplies. Do you have time after school today?"
"Hey, Haruki. About the popularity odds that came in today…"
"I told you all already… I can't afford to help anyone right now. I'm sorry, but try someone else."
"I know, I know. You just have to give it a quick glimpse… If you can really stop at that, that is."
"Come if you have the time… Everyone is waiting."
"You're the one who turned Miss Houjou High into a free-for-all. Take some responsibility, at least."
"Don't just focus on hitting my weak spots. You guys really are getting better at begging. Not to mention…"
"Okay, I know you're all excited because the festival's coming up, but the materials we're covering today will be in the exam. It's not my fault if you don't listen!"
"We're in the middle of class right now."
Since the festival's right at the end of this week, the atmosphere in the classroom has completely changed.
Only a small part of the class is actually paying attention to lectures. Everyone else is either texting, making plans for the festival with people around them, or just generally being too excited.
"What's the big deal? This is the last year we'll get to act like this."
"Even though you plan to fool around for another four years starting next year…"
"I'm telling you, it's just this week, jeez."
"And I'm telling you to at least pay attention during class."
Saying that, Chikashi pointed right behind himself.
And indeed, I saw the figure of a student focusing and taking notes as if her life hinged on it, much like how I just described one should.
Our resident sleeper… is, for once, not actually sleeping in class…
No, far from it, in fact.
"It's gotten so lively since the start of this week. Students from all classes are staying so late after school."
"That's just because they didn't prepare ahead of time and are panicking now."
"Ahaha… That definitely sounds like something you'd say, Haruki-kun. Are preparations for the contest all good?"
"Of course. My successor has been in charge of everything since last week… I hope."
"Huh? So you left the executive committee…? Is it because you got so tied up with the club?"
If anything, the real problem stems from suspicions regarding my close relationship with a certain candidate. But I wouldn't tell Setsuna that, even at gunpoint.
It's a good thing I left last week. If I'd stayed until this week, they probably would have kicked up a big fuss about it.
…Though right now I can't really exclude the possibility that they still might.
"Hey, speaking of which, what's Class E doing?"
"Your generic haunted house. What about Class A?"
"We came up with some weird name like 'Taisho Romance Cafe' or something…"
"…That one sure feels like it's trying too hard to be specific, doesn't it?"
"For some reason, the guys are doing their best sewing the uniforms. They're a lot more skilled with their fingers than I thought."
"I have a feeling they're just doing it to fulfill a messed up desire of theirs…"
"I'll be working at the cafe on Friday morning. Be sure to come and visit, okay?"
"All right. I'll come if I can."
I will. Absolutely. No matter what.
"Then, the three of us can go around the festival together starting in the afternoon. Oh, how about we go to your class's haunted house?"
"Eh? Uh, umm, well that's a little…"
"Oh, are you on duty from the afternoon?"
"No, Touma and I are both free all of Friday. But…"
Our haunted house is limited to couples only…
"I'd just like to get better at playing before then."
Yeah, that was a great follow-up… but not being able to go around the festival with Setsuna is a double-edged sword in itself.
The games begin this Friday. And the showdown is on Saturday.
Putting aside whether desperately struggling will get anything done, it's all we can do within the span of five days.
Fifteen minutes on foot from school.
The two of us walked down a path that has recently become familiar to me, and arrived in front of the "Ogiso" nameplate.
"Well, a guy who wouldn't walk a girl home even when she's all by herself in the dark would be despicable, after all."
"J-Jeez, stop! I was just really out of it then."
This is my new path home starting from today.

Motivated by a desire to make things up to her, a slight worry and a self-righteous sense of responsibility, I offered to walk her home. I approached the situation fearlessly and like I had nothing to lose.
To make it easier for her to accept my offer during school lunch, I added conditions like, "if it's past 6 o'clock" and "at least until the school festival is over."

At first, a smile broke out on Setsuna's face for a moment. Afterward, however, she looked troubled due to her reservations and refused by shaking her hands and lowering her head, before finally nodding deeply.
"I told you not to worry about it. I'm seeing you home because I want to."
"I don't think there's anyone who would mind seeing you home among us third-year guys, though…"
"I'm not interested in the opinion of an unspecified majority, though."
"I'm worried about you, Setsuna, so please let me walk you home every day… Does that work?"
"Well then, stay warm and get some sleep. It wouldn't be funny if our singer caught a cold now."
"Ah, yup. I know. I've been gargling my throat the moment I get home every day."
…Seriously, she's so adorable and ordinary about everything.
"You're going to Touma-san's place, right? …I mean, right now."
The moment I was about to smile, I felt like something suddenly pierced straight through me…
And then, I felt the blood draining from my face…
"…? Ah, wait… Don't get me wrong! J-Jeez! Why'd you turn so pale?"
"Eh? Ah… Did I get the wrong idea?"
Like what? In what way? To what extent?
"D-Don't respond in such a weird way… You're making me look like an overbearing girl who's desperately trying to keep her lover from leaving her for another woman!"
I have to admit… those words really hurt. I don't even understand them, but they hurt.
…In particular, it's mainly my heart that's hurting right now.
"Like I said, that's not it. I just wanted to ask you to take some apples.
My relatives from Aomori sent some over yesterday. They're really sweet."
"Look, Touma-san's living alone, so she probably doesn't get enough vitamins. Actually, I'm certain she doesn't."
"I suppose you're right there… She's a product of fast food, convenience store bentos, sugar, glucose, and syrup."
If we try to apply such a fact to what we usually see before us, however, it's really an eternal mystery as to how exactly she maintains that figure of hers…
"Wait here for just a bit, Haruki-kun. I'll be right back!"
I'm so embarrassed in so many ways that I feel like I could melt any second now…
"Iwazu-chou, Iwazu-chou. Please mind the door when exiting."
Since I'd spent fifteen minutes on each part of the round trip, I ended up coming to the Iwazu-chou Station platform about thirty minutes late.
There are just as many people flooding out of the train here as ever, each of them going their separate ways.
Following this scenery that has recently become familiar to me with my gaze, I start climbing the stairway leading to the north ticket gate…
This is a residential area where most people are getting off during night time, yet there's one person sitting on a bench waiting… and not for the train.
"The doors are closing. Please be careful."
"Studying. The exams are pretty close now."
"Look, you don't have to tell such an obvious lie…"
With that, Touma shuts the notebook that she had been enthusiastically writing in, and gets up as if nothing had happened.
And thus the question that I wanted to ask but was afraid to ended up being sealed away, as expected.
With the same, slightly wry smile from this morning, I walk by her side as always, but a little farther away than usual.
No matter how often I glance at her face from the side, she keeps looking straight ahead, and like always… no, this time it's a little colder than usual.
"Here… Ogiso wanted us to split these."
It seems that even the act of passing her an apple has had a new rule imposed upon it.
"Hey, is that seriously supposed to be your dinner? Start eating properly already."
"Listen up. I know you're all excited because the school festival is close by, but the result of today's test will directly affect your final grade."
"Jeez, who in their right mind gives a pop quiz this time of the year…? What a sadist."
"That's why I kept telling you to at least pay attention to class…"
…Though I made a big deal of others to do it, even I can't help but hold my head seeing this reading comprehension quiz's long sentences.
Well, that said, I'm pretty sure I can still answer all of the questions.
Tuesday. Three days until the school festival. And four days until our decisive battle arrives.
The classroom's gotten a few more ornaments and decorations, too. In the restlessness of the entire school populace, the only one who remained the same is our guidance counselor.

A commotion broke out in the class for a bit as he abruptly announced a pop quiz. However, after realizing that any objection or opposition wouldn't change the situation, the class could only concede in silence.
"Ten minutes left. The trick to these long passages, you see, is to read the question first…"
Well, he's certainly enthusiastic about education, and his teaching style isn't bad at all. I'm not of the opinion that a teacher who's loved among their students is necessarily a good one, either.
It's just that, well… if he could just be more tactful about what's going on around him, he'd make it a bit easier for me to defend him as well.
With these thoughts in mind, I write down "4" in the space of the eighth, final question, and then check if my name and class are filled out.
"What the hell are you doing, Touma!?"
A sudden, loud shout right beside me nearly makes me drop my pencil.
…Truth be told, it wasn't the volume alone that startled me, but also the name that he yelled.
"You're supposed to be reading right now! What exactly is this!?"
Never mind this test, Touma hadn't spoken a word in class this whole week, only scribbling away enthusiastically with her pencil. For some reason, she has ended up becoming a target nevertheless.
"Not to mention we're in the middle of a test. Why are you always, always pulling these stunts!?"
"You don't feel sorry at all, do you? Where's your exam sheet?"
"Look at this! You haven't even written anything besides your name! You weren't planning to do anything from the very beginning, were you?"
"I couldn't understand it at all. I'm sorry."
Usually, she'd get annoyed by this point from talking back and being dismissive of him, but today, she's being unusually humble.

The way she's saying "I'm sorry" is completely different too. Even if it's only natural to accuse her of not doing it in good faith, she's honestly bowing her head, without even looking to the side or scowling.
"…W-Well, umm. If you don't understand the questions, it's multiple-choice, so you could just fill it in at random. But doing something else is just outrageous."
"Take your seat, and continue with your test."
Even Suwa seems to be baffled by Touma's commendable response.
Disappointed and slightly embarrassed, he turns the other way, and starts walking back to his podium.
Seeing this exchange makes me breathe a sigh of relief, and Touma's developing cooperativeness makes me somewhat happy.
"Could you… please return that? It's important…"
Perhaps something changed inside her from sticking with me, or with Setsuna.
"I'm confiscating this. If you must have it back, come to the faculty room after school."
The thorns surrounding her from all around have shrunk, and bit by bit, the snow has melted ever so slightly.
"The rest of you, focus! We're still in the middle of a test here!"
It would be wonderful if everyone could get to know the real Touma like this…
But those convenient thoughts of mine…
"What do you mean, confiscated!? After school!? You think you have the right to take that away from me!? Don't screw with me!"
…Are shattered in a matter of seconds, lost without a trace.
I try to hold Touma back as she snaps, but she dodges me with ease, as if she had eyes on her back.
…Thus, I end up spectacularly crashing into Chikashi's desk, given that my reflexes are average at best.
She does a feint on Suwa and easily snatches the notebook back, leaving both him and the whole class bewildered by the sudden turn of events.
For a moment, Touma holds it to her chest as if it were a treasure…
She immediately calms down and checks the notebook that's back in her hands. Then, as if having completely lost interest in her surroundings, she nonchalantly leaves the classroom.
All that's left is a commotion that would otherwise be unimaginable during a test…
About a third of our classmates' voices that I can overhear echoing in agreement with Touma, with the rest condemning her…
"I have absolutely no idea what goes on in her head…"
As well as Suwa-sensei's dumbfounded murmuring.
"I'm sorry! I'll come to apologize later. I'll write an apology letter, too. So umm… In any case, I'm really sorry!"
"Umm… In any case, I truly apologize! Please excuse me!"
Even though I've failed already, I desperately try to convince myself that I'm not too late to cover up for Touma's outburst.
It's the middle of third period.
Music Room 2 is never used for lectures, so Touma's making good use of it as her hideout even though classes are still ongoing.
…Well, looking at the situation from this perspective, I can't say that I have absolutely no sympathy for Suwa's case.
But even so, in the end, I followed Touma like always.
Seated with the chair turned backward, I rest my elbows on its back and my chin on my elbows, listening to Touma's furious melody.
"Let's go apologize to him together after school. I'll think of what to put in the apology letters later, but you'll have to write your copy yourself."
And while I'm at it, I lecture her.
"And who asked you to do that?"
"Well, I asked myself. It would be fatal if you were to be suspended right now."
"Don't mind it, it's just plain scribbling."
I'd like to ask, "Why go through that for just some scribbling…?"
But there's hesitation in my heart that I can't put into words, along with an inerasable sense of trust. In the end, I choose to stay silent and just remain by her side.
"What ever happened to never skipping class and always being on time?"
"That's not something for you to worry about, Touma."
"You might be held back a year, you know?"
"That's especially not something for you to worry about either, Touma."
As she usually does, Touma responds with an exasperated sigh.
By now, her furrowed eyebrows and her tense shoulders have slightly relaxed, and her fingertips have mostly calmed down too.
Although that might just be because she changed the melody.
"You must be bored listening to this, aren't you?"
"Not at all. I'm a fan of your piano playing, Touma."
Still, it couldn't have been the song alone that caused the tone of her voice to become gentler as well.
I want to believe that I helped out too, even if just a bit.
"The only side of my piano playing that you know about… is the pop music that I only play to mess around with you."
"If that's the case, then I'd love to listen to you playing some classical music in earnest, and not just messing around."
"It'll sound pretty boring to an amateur…"
"That's fine. It's a performance from the master, after all."
With a sarcastic smile, Touma's fingers jump about as if dancing.
Waves of sound with a variety of different emotions flow out, and slowly start enveloping me.
"Nice job falling asleep after bugging me so much with wanting to listen…"
"And right in front of me, no less. How can you even fall asleep with such a loud noise so close?"
"Ah, well… how should I put it? Hearing you playing the piano really relaxes me, Touma."
Waves of sound with a variety of different emotions enveloped me as they flowed out…
There was something about it that felt so amazing. Yeah, no way that was boring at all.
…Is what I want to believe, but I can't really be sure.
"Even though I did my best and said such embarrassing things!?"
"Look, just go back to the classroom. And don't come back until after school."
"So this is that woman's house, huh…"
"I texted Setsuna a while ago, and she said she just had to come…"
"I'm Ogiso Setsuna, from Class 3-A. I got out with a lie along the lines of, 'I have a headache, so I'm going to the infirmary'… Ehehe…"
"Is that something a school idol should be doing…?"
"And is this something the eternal class representative should be doing…? Here's your guitar."
"Yup. Hayasaka-kun told me where the locker is."
"What are you guys doing…? Didn't fourth period just begin?"
For a moment, Touma spaced out as she watched the exchange between Setsuna and me, before the school bell snapped her out of it.
But that short window of opportunity was all we needed to hook the guitar up to the amp, turn the microphone on, and completely set up for practice.
"Listen, Touma. I don't think what you did was right whatsoever."
"But, you know, we're all in the same club. We're in it together, whether it be fun things, bad things, bothersome things… or even anger toward society, okay?"
"There are times when a man must rebel against his teachers, even if it looks bad on his report card."
"…You should come up with something a little more generic and cool, you know."
"Not to mention… Setsuna would be sulking again if I had kept quiet about something as fun as this."
"Well of course I would! We promised not to keep any more secrets, after all!"
Thus, rather than running after Touma alone, I decided to bring Setsuna along here with me.
Even if it's an "activity unbecoming of students" such as this one, the three of us have to act out together.
"…You two are going to be held back a year because you keep hanging around me, you know?"
"What are you saying? You've got it backward. You're the one that's going to graduate because you keep hanging around us."
"After the school festival is over, we'll tutor you personally, all right? I'm confident that I'm better at English than Haruki-kun is, at least."
"At any rate, our graduations and recommendations are pretty much guaranteed, so we'll be sticking with you through each and every supplementary exam you've got."
"There's no one here quite as stupid as you are, Touma."
"Well, when it comes to grades, right?"
"Are you trying to cover for her?"
Touma's response is as blunt, exasperated, and slightly cold as ever.
"With that out of the way, since we've all gathered here, let's practice until lunchtime… But let's try to be quiet about it, since classes are still running."
"Oh, that sounds great. Lunch is gonna be all the more delicious if I sing now!"
But under that cynicism, and through her calm, wry smile, I sense the slightest bit of kindness blooming in her heart.
And so, for a short spell, and in obvious violation of school regulations…
…The three of us enjoy our rebellion without a cause to the fullest.
And naturally, all three of us got scolded afterward.
"I made it in time… Hahah… I guess I really am a genius, huh…?"
"Ah, morning, Kitahara. You should get going or you'll be late."
"7:15. You stayed up past 6 AM this time."
I only slept for about an hour…? Well, that would explain why I hallucinated hearing Kazusa sounding strangely happy.
"You might be able to make it in time even if you take a shower right now."
"I'm good… I'll hurry to school and sleep until classes start. Just like you, Touma."
"Actually, you should be the one taking a shower. And you should be hurrying too, or you'll be late."
Normally, she'd be done with showering by the time I wake up, but she's still wearing her plain clothes today.
"Ah, well, the thing is… I'm skipping today."
"This week has been pretty busy, you know… I thought I should get some sleep today, at least."
"…I've been wondering since yesterday, what exactly have you been doing, Touma?"
Even though she usually sleeps off most classes to recover her energy, this week she's been staying awake writing something in a notebook, even during her precious sleep time.
She didn't even let up after school or at our practice sessions in the evenings. Even during break periods, she was muttering to herself, and just like she said, she's had no time to sleep at all.
"I'm fine… Things are looking pretty good today."
"You'll be late if you don't hurry."
"I'm going to be sleeping until noon. I'll take a hot shower when I wake up, eat plenty for lunch, and get some more sleep until our evening practice."
"Yeah, so… sorry, but I'm going to have to miss out on afternoon practice. Apologize to Ogiso for me."
"…All right. I'll let the school know too."
Truth be told, I would normally take the logical approach here, but Touma's physical condition takes priority.
Right now, I need to put aside the fact that I have no idea why Touma's pushed herself so hard lately.
"Okay, I'll be using your bathroom then."
Today, I'll be taking a nap until the first class starts, maybe even sleep a few classes off, and practice with Setsuna after school.
After that, I'll head home to take a bath, change, and come back here to practice until morning.
With such a strict regimen, I'll perfect that difficult song within the remaining 72 hours. Nevermind if I can or can't do it, I just have to.
"Fuwaaahhh… Well then, I should also… Huh?"
"I'm just imagining it, right? I mean… I have to finish by tonight…"
It's the first time I really took a break during classes since I enrolled.
As for the duo practice with Setsuna, it turned into me practicing on my own while talking to her.
I headed home, took a bath, and had dinner.
…It's been a while since my mother came home so early, but in the end, we didn't really talk much. She didn't even bother to ask where I was going on my way out.
And so after all that, I've arrived at the Touma residence, which is completely dark for some reason.
The front door was left unlocked, probably since when I left this morning.
…Could she have slept through the whole day?
I don't hear any response at all, even when calling out to the living room.
Just how tired is she…? Why'd she need to push herself that far…?
Compared to me, she's a genius who only needs a few hours to perfect any song…
And so I enter the Touma household in search of its owner, harboring some curiosity, concern, and envy.
It took me less than ten seconds to realize that something was wrong.
"I can't say for certain, but it's possible. Her temperature is particularly high, and her consciousness appears to be hazy."
And so I realized that what came to pass was the worst possible scenario.
"I've given her medicine, but if she doesn't get better, please bring her to the hospital."
Having said that, it could have been even worse had I not noticed. I'm glad that I'm so persistent in coming in every day.
…Right, as if. The reason this happened in the first place is because I came here every day and wouldn't let Touma get any sleep.
"Well, it's no good to worry too much about it either. If she rests for at least three days, her temperature should drop."
It'll be Sunday after three days. Even if she does recover by then…
Well… It wouldn't be like Touma to let me notice, I guess.
Thanks to the injection from earlier, her pained breathing has calmed down now.
Still, even though I got her into a futon, wiped away her sweat, had her drink some water, and called over a doctor, she hasn't answered no matter how many times I've tried calling her.
Taking the ice bag which had become lukewarm from being on her forehead, I change its contents with fresh ice from the freezer.
With a faint hint of redness on her usually porcelain-white face, along with drops of sweat on her skin, Touma looks somewhat alluring.
With those inappropriate thoughts in mind, I find myself feeling guilty, and coming up with excuses and apologies to her for some reason.
What beats me up the most inside is the notebook that lies beside Touma right now as she's sleeping in the living room.

The notebook that she's barely let go of in the past week, even in the middle of class or on her way to school. The same notebook which a teacher tried to confiscate, making her snap. Her behavior baffled me completely.
Be it the fact that Touma forced herself to work so hard because of this, or the fact that I failed to notice it at all…
Realizing the truth now, the only thing I can do is assume responsibility.
It may seem ridiculous, but the weight of her feelings is expressed in the musical notes in this notebook.
"Yeah… Three cups of water. Soy sauce, sake, salt, soup mix… Yeah. Yeah."
"Ingredients… well, there's almost nothing here… Eh? Even canned food would be fine?"
"You know, it's nice that you want to make it yourself and all, but wouldn't it be better to just grab an instant pack from a convenience store? You haven't made it before at all, right, Haruki-kun?"
"A guy's cooking for her with all his sincerity and devotion, so I'm sure it'll make her happy… To tell you the truth, even I want to try it too, like, right now."
"No, I'm sure you'd only be disappointed. If nothing else, I'm absolutely confident about that."
"I'm scared of letting her out of my sight. I need to make something with whatever is already in the house… She still hasn't woken up."
"Ah, umm… let's see. Tuna, salmon, grilled chicken… Oh, I see canned peaches. I can use this as a dessert."
"That's about it. There's nothing else besides the pasta sauce… Huh, what? With this?"
"I see… How about a risotto then? But meat sauce might be too heavy for a sick person."
"Ah, there's vongole… Eh? Yeah, white ones. Vongole in bianco."
"I put the rice in the cooker a while ago… It's fine, I can handle it."
"Eh? What do you mean, you're coming over?"
"If you can't do it, then I should come over, right? Oh yeah, I could bring some ingredients from my fri…"
"Why? I'll be right there if I take a taxi. Even Dad wouldn't mind if I told him it was to nurse Touma-san…"
"I shouldn't be saying this, but I'm really good when it comes to this sort of thing, you know?"
"Right now, we need to make sure your throat stays healthy, Setsuna."
"Our stage performance is already the talk of the school now… Why do you think that is?"
"It wouldn't be Touma's keyboard, and especially not my guitar. Even our songs are just old pop tracks, we don't have anything original."
"That's my answer to you asking why. Got it, Miss Secret-weapon-singer?"
"Yeah, thanks. I'm mixing it into the rice right now. Yeah, smells great."
"The question is if Touma will even want to eat this, though… No, doesn't look like she's awake yet."
"Now, turn the fire off after one more minute, then put the eggs in… It's fine, it's going well. Thanks a lot, Setsuna."
"Huh? Next time? Y-Yeah… Sure, I'll make you some anytime, if you're actually willing to eat this stuff."
"Uh, umm, let's see… Well, after the school festival…"
"Wha…? Monday? The holiday? F-First thing in the morning at your place!?"
"W-Well, that's uh… Of course, I'm okay with it. But you have to help, okay?"
"Look, don't get so excited… Okay, I got it. It's a promise."
"Okay, I'm hanging up… Good night, Setsuna."
"Touma! You're finally awake, that's a relief… I just made some rice porridge, so if you could take a spoon…"
"Why are you acting like you own the place? Go back home if you aren't here to practice, you idiot."
"Terrible. I don't even know where to start with this. You seriously expect someone to eat this crap?"
"Obviously your fever's messed up your sense of taste!"
From the look on her face and how much she's sweating, I don't think she's recovered yet, but her sharp tongue seems to be back in top form…
"You weren't feeling well this morning, right? That's why you stayed home, right?"
"You're misunderstanding. I had things to do today, so I stayed home…"
"You said you were sleepy this morning, remember?"
"…Sleeping just so happened to be one of those things."
"But you didn't really get any sleep, did you? When did you faint?"
"Don't dodge the question. And if you don't have an appetite, you don't need to eat any more."
"I'm not saying I'm not hungry. It just really tastes bad, that's it."
"Yeah, fine, fine. I don't really care what it is, so let me just clean it up."
"Don't interrupt someone while they're eating. I absolutely need this to recover by tomorrow."
Isn't it hot, holding the pot like that?
"You can't afford to waste even one day. Are you aware of what exactly it is you've gotten yourself into…?"
"If you've got the time to make something as useless as this, you should be practicing instead…"
"…None of what I said just now even reached you, did it?"
"Pretty much. I'm not sure if you were saying that in a delirious state, or if it was due to the medicine's side effects…"
"I can't practice properly if I do."
"But then you'll have less of a chance of catching my cold. Go home, take some medicine, and go to sleep."
"If it means you'd get better, Touma, I don't mind catching your cold."
If I couldn't play, it would be my embarrassment alone, but if Touma couldn't play, our group would completely fall apart.
Of course, the same holds true for Setsuna's vocals.
But without Touma's keyboard, there'd be no performance to begin with.
"That's just an urban legend. It's nonsense. You actually believe that superstition despite being the pragmatic honors student that you are?"
"Also, the last train's already left anyway."
"…Then go practice over there. Don't be here the entire time."
"When you're done eating, Touma, take your medicine, get a change of clothes, and go to sleep."
"Don't try to rush if it tastes bad. You'll choke over it."
"Take it slow and easy. I don't want you to push yourself right now."
Bit by bit, Touma sips down that failure of a rice porridge I concocted.
Her breath is still very warm, and occasionally unsteady. I can't imagine her getting better soon considering that.
But the fact that she has a healthy appetite means there's still hope.
And then, the words Touma utters give me even more hope.
"Of course you won't. Neither will I, Setsuna, or even Takeya. No one plans on giving up."
Whether it be making memories, triumphing over the music students, or promoting the beauty contest…
Whatever nostalgic, sophisticated or convenient motive we had, no one has any idea what it was right now.
We've completely lost sight of our goal along the way, and are now just running along with the momentum, going completely off track.
"So eat up, take your medicine, get changed, and go to sleep. Don't let that determination go to waste, okay?"
But going off track in itself is fun, enjoyable, and kind of scary… It's become so absurd.
"…Don't you dare peek while I'm changing."
"I knew you would say that, so I won't let it get to me one bit!"
"As always, Shibata-san will be coming to take care of food and other daily necessities. You shouldn't feel inconvenienced in any way."
"Also, continue to take your lessons from Sakurai-sensei. It's no issue if you decide to choose someone else, though. Pick a teacher that will motivate you to learn."
"And… there shouldn't be any problems in regards to your enrollment. You'll be contacted later with details about your entrance exam."
"There's no point in bringing you with me as you are now."
"Come on, jeez… Horrible way to wake up…"
"Aah, damn it! I almost had it!"
Making a mistake in the very last measure is about as frustrating as making a mistake on the last question of an exam.
Well, there's no point crying over spilled milk.
I started practicing at four in the morning, I've been practicing for five hours now. Despite that, I still haven't managed to play the whole song without making a mistake.
I'm definitely getting better at playing. After all, in this last performance, I only made…
"Eeeh… So you think making only five mistakes counts as 'getting better' at it?"
"Not to mention, even an amateur could tell exactly where you messed up. We're in trouble if you're satisfied with this."
"Hey, I'm the one in trouble right now! You shouldn't get up yet, Touma!"
The patient whom I diligently cared for ended up pouring cold water on my moment of self-satisfaction.
"I'm fine. My fever has gone down now too."
"Don't make such obvious lies, I'm begging you."
Her face is still red, her eyes are teary, and her forehead is glistening with sweat.
Leaning against the wall, she looks like she can barely stand. She must have used up all of her strength to get down here.
"Sorry, I'm going to touch you for a bit."
Even though I only touched her forehead, she still lashes out at me, as expected.
"…Feels like your temperature is still over 38°C. I said you should be in bed, didn't I?"
"Come on, let's head back to the living room, Touma. Can you walk?"
"Give me a break. There's no way I'm going back there."
"I can't afford to leave you alone given how crappy your playing is! There's only two days left, remember?"
"I'm practicing with all I've got. Have some more faith in me…"
"But I promised… I'd make sure you can play it…"
Be it from the high fever, the medicine, or maybe even both, she's even more stubborn than usual.
I assume she's not doing it intentionally this time, just following her instinct.
"Even so, you have to sleep, Touma. Otherwise I won't play."
Saying this, I can't help but grin for some reason.
"Kitahara… don't you want our performance to be successful?"
"You told me to stay away from you so I don't catch your cold, didn't you?"
Oh, you did. You sure did.
"…Fine then, I can't win against your stubbornness, Kitahara. I'll take my medicine and rest… right here."
She doesn't even understand what I'm telling her. No, she's doing this on purpose.
"How do you plan to fall asleep? I'll be playing non-stop from now on, you know?"
"I won't be able to hear a thing once I black out."
"Anyway, I refuse to sleep anywhere but here. This is as far as I'll compromise with you."
"Don't tell me you expect me to carry it."
"I said I'd stay here for your sake, Kitahara, so… why should I…"
"Yes, you are. How unbecoming… Are you even a man?"
"I am not angry! Not even a bit, I'm not angry at all."
Even though she's so angry herself, how come she's worrying about whether I am angry or not?
Really, what should I do with her…?
"All right, let go of my sleeve already. You're stretching it."
"…!? I'm not holding your sleeve. I have no idea what you're talking about."
Why is she holding her hands up and apologizing so exaggeratedly as if she were a heel wrestler trying to gloss over the fact that they just played dirty?
"Take your medicine, and check your temperature regularly. Lie down quietly, and speak up if you don't feel well… Understood?"
"Now then, you should have breakfast. Can you eat porridge?"
"Yes, I can. I will eat it no matter how awful it tastes, if it helps me get better."
She's pushed through with her demands up until now, but right now she's smiling with upturned eyes, as if she's genuinely relieved. I can't understand her at all…
Maybe she's just scared of being alone?
…No, there's no way. She's been living alone for three years now, after all.
"All right, I'll bring the futon down and make you some porridge. There should be some left over from last night…"
"I'll be back in ten minutes, just wait here!"
"Your call cannot be connected at the moment because the number you have dialed is outside the service area or the cell phone may be switched off."
"Oh, no… Was the call last night too long?"
"I guess he's still at Touma's place…"
"As soon as I feel like it."
"Why do you keep staring at me like that?"
Even though she promised me that she would sleep as soon as she took her medicine, she's been staring at my hands ever since.
Could it be because of my poor skill, or because I'm being too loud? Maybe it's a whole different reason entirely?
"Listening to my crappy guitar won't make you get better."
I told her to sleep, but Touma's excuse was that she's teaching me.
But in the end, she's achieving neither; she's simply watching me play the guitar while being half-asleep.
"Let me listen to your guitar, Kitahara."
Though I'm only able to feel her gaze, I feel a lot more nervous than usual.
"Setsuna? We're heading to the AV room next, you know?"
"Ah, sorry. I'll be with you in a moment."
"You'll be fine… right, Touma-san? You'll definitely get better, won't you?"
"Stop it already, just rest. Even if you tried to get up, I could force you to lie down easily with the way you are now."
Even though her weakness shows through occasionally, Touma's attitude toward me has remained quite bitter. And her condition is still somewhat unstable.
"What do you want for dinner? Think you can eat something other than soup yet?"
"I think so. I'm actually kind of hungry. I think I'd be okay with anything that's not spicy."
She's lying down, taking medicine and eating properly. She's really putting in the effort to get better now and has the right attitude going about it, but…
Even so, her fever hasn't gone down yet. I don't know when she'll recover. Will it be tomorrow, the day after, or even Monday?
We're done for if she's only going to get better by the latter two days, though I suppose we were already done for for quite some time…
"After that… I want to have some doughnuts. A French cruller with whipped cream."
"As soon as you get better. Just eat some pudding for tonight."
"Then I want a big serving. Have some syrup to go with it, too."
"…You leave nothing to chance when it comes to dessert, do you?"
The dress rehearsal must have started by now.
I asked Takeya to do it last night as we'd be disqualified if no one participated.
I guess Touma and I will have to perform without proper rehearsal on the stage.
"Well, I'll forward your demands to your helper. She was excited about being able to cook for you after a long time."
"Now that you mention it, she's always been meddlesome… Not as much as a certain somebody, though."
It's high time I made up my mind.
Which should I prioritize, her condition or her determination to not give up?
"I see. She hasn't fully recovered yet…"
"Yeah… I called her house, and the helper picked up and told me so. She also said she works at her house on Mondays and Thursdays, two days a week."
"Living leisurely alone in a mansion with a helper… I expected no less from Touma Youko's daughter."
"But… I don't think she really enjoys living alone. It feels to me like Touma-san is actually lonely."
"I'll definitely move out and live alone when I enter university, even if it ends up being even farther from the university than my parents' place."
"You can't really bring a girl over unless you live alone, huh? Last year, just as things were getting good in your room, your grandpa collapsed, right?"
"Please send my regards to the person you got that information from… Tell him, 'Go to hell, Haruki!'"
"But your grandpa's life was saved because you were there, right? Isn't that great?"
"…This doesn't feel like a prank or a joke, either…"
"Nothing, I'm just wondering if we can make it. Our performance is the day after tomorrow."
"I'm sure we can. Touma-san will make it."
"Even if Touma gets better, Haruki's been slacking off for two whole days. Will he really be able to play?"
"I'm sure it'll be fine! It's Haruki-kun, after all!"
"…Yeah, you don't even try to hide it at all. On the other hand, he's desperately trying to keep it secret."
"Let's do our best the day after tomorrow… Well, I'll just be in charge of the synthesizer backstage, though."
"You really are a lifesaver. Thank you for all you've done so far, Iizuka-kun. Also, we'll be counting on you the day after tomorrow."
"…Please stop it with the heartwarming comments already. You're only fueling my contempt for Haruki right now."
"Right, it's our turn. Let's go, Setsuna-chan."
"Hey, Ogiso's rehearsal is about to begin! Gather everybody!"
"Ogiso-san's really gonna sing… Wow, for real, this is great!"
"Wait, don't start yet! I have to grab my digital camera from my clubroom!"
"You dumbass, we're short on time here! We can't wait because of such an idiotic reason!"
"There's not all that much to see, either… Not today, anyway."
"We'll have to play for a much bigger audience during the real thing. Don't tell me you're overwhelmed by this many already."
"C'mon, let's confirm where you'll be standing on stage."
"Oh, yeah, Setsuna-chan, could you come with me for a bit when the rehearsal is over?"
"Hold on, don't be afraid, I won't do anything bad…! No, what I meant is we need to coordinate your on-stage costume."
"There's even a stage costume…? We don't have to go so far."
"I was under great pressure because, you know, you two are both really gorgeous."
"Well, they're just rentals. I scoured a bunch of shops for good costumes… with Yanagihara Tomo."
"I'm okay… I'm fine, definitely… If we're all on stage together, I'll do all I can…"
"If you're done setting up, please start!"
"We don't have the guitar or piano here, so try doing it with the synthesizer for now."
"The rehearsal. Try singing the first few lines, at least."
"Is the microphone ready? Can we start now?"
"…Do I have to? Right here, right now?"
"Heeey! Sorry, everyone, but some of our members couldn't make it today! So please bear with there being no performance! We're just here to fit the protocol!"
"Takeya, don't hold out on us, dude! I helped prepare this rehearsal just to see her, you hear!?"
"Well, it's not a problem for us, actually. If anything, it just saves us time, but… will you guys really be fine without rehearsal?"
"We'll be fine, we can make it no matter what! …I hope."
"You'll think of something, right? I'm counting on you… Haruki."
I stop myself from saying, "Don't get too excited, you'll make your fever come back," realizing that motivating her is more important now.
Recalling the proverb "sickness and health start with the mind," I direct my prayers to the people in the past who lived by those principles.
"When you get better, you should thank Shibata-san. She's really worried about you."
"…Understood, I'll do it the next time she comes."
Touma said Shibata-san is a temporary worker who comes to her house just to do the cleaning, but that's far from the truth.
Both her appearance and character fit the description of a typical, overly helpful neighborhood lady. She even cooked for us, even though it's not in her contract and we didn't ask her to.
"In the original contract, she was supposed to cook and look after you every day, right?"
Being the chatty neighborhood lady that she is, she explained the Touma family's circumstances to me while we were doing the laundry.
…Touma might have pushed her away because of this personality.
"Furthermore, Shibata-san told me that you fired your piano teacher, family doctor, rice dealer, sake dealer and insurance man, cutting your ties with everyone…"
I mean, Shibata-san is so meddlesome that she even gets along with me so easily.
"Why did you do that? Does it have to do with you quitting the music program?"
"…You don't plan to be persistent like you usually are?"
"For today, your recovery takes top priority."
"Warm up and sleep tight. I'll change your ice bag later."
"If you feel sick, let me know right away. If I'm asleep, just give me a kick to wake me up, understood?"
"And if my guitar gets annoying, just tell me so, and I'll mute it."
"I… I thought about giving up on the piano."
"I thought about abandoning my place as her daughter."
I've known about the fable named 'The North Wind and the Sun' since childhood.
But until now, I couldn't grasp the true meaning of the story.
The separation between Touma Youko and Touma Kazusa appeared to have gone smoothly on the surface.
The mother's move abroad was quite natural considering her ability and career, and the daughter was proud of her mother who was active worldwide.

And so the mother had paid the utmost attention not to inconvenience her daughter. Providing her with food, clothing, housing, money, and education to such an extent that a common person might think of her as overprotective.
…The mother didn't take her daughter with her, having denied the possibility of them living together from the very beginning.
"She abandoned me because I wasn't talented enough… it seems."
"She said it clearly, after all. There was no point in bringing me along."
Stories like these with discord in mutual feelings usually happen due to someone's misunderstanding.
"I know it's lame, but until then, Touma Youko had been my goal, my teacher, my rival… she's everything to me."
But I gave up on the idea of making a safe and pathetic comment like, "I can't say for sure unless I hear from both sides."
"So when I found that I meant nothing to her, I… How should I put it…? Everything felt so stupid and pointless."
I mean… even if it was a misunderstanding or her imagination, the fact of the matter is that she was shocked and has to cope with it.
"The truth is… I don't know whether I was really unhappy then… or whether what she did was actually wrong, either."
Her mother is responsible for making her sad.
She is responsible for her becoming a delinquent. She is her mother, after all.
"I just… couldn't stand feeling so helpless. That's all."
"You are a terrific pianist and you play beautifully, but under all that, you're just an ordinary person!"
No, there's no way I could say something as embarrassing as that…
"Nothing much, just that… I was deceived by all the fancy international stuff, but it's just a plain parent-child squabble, after all."
"Putting it like that makes it sound like you're denying everything that's happened so far."
"Well, isn't that only natural? I've only known you for about six months, since spring, but you've been causing no end of trouble to everyone around us."
"Then that just makes you a proper scumbag, doesn't it? You've been troubling someone as miserable as I am, after all."
"If you troubled someone, you can make up for it by helping someone else. That's how the world works."
"Don't try to end this conversation with such a superficial wrap-up. It doesn't change the fact that you're a scumbag."
"You're just as bad, Touma. Shifting responsibility to someone else is something only a delinquent would do."
"Talking with you makes me realize how ridiculous life is."

People fret over problems related to home, family and friends… and they compare their problems to others to console themselves, get heavily depressed over them, or struggle to overcome them only to end up in a worse situation.
Everybody thinks that such problems bother only them, and sometimes they see them as life-or-death situations. But if they could look at their problems objectively, they'd realize it's no big deal.
"That's why, Touma… Let's enjoy ourselves on Saturday."
A rather forced way of changing the topic…
Touma looks half-speechless and half-exhausted… but she doesn't show the slightest hint of loneliness. I'm just happy to see her like this.
"Rather than just your mother, let's get everyone fired up! Let's amaze them all!"
"Well, they'll be amazed for sure… they'll think we're amateurs and find our composition absurd."
"Anyone who has dedicated themselves to playing an instrument would look down upon it as a silly street performance by versatile, but unskilled clowns."
"Really? Well, that's a shame… Too bad, since our audience will be nothing but amateurs this time."
"They're amused most by things that are just plain amusing. They're the simplest but the toughest opponents at the same time."
We'll be on the stage of a festival, not one of a concert or a competition.

They won't pay for our performance. They might come for something else. Worst case scenario, they might come just because they're told to fill the hall, and might have no interest in music in the first place.
What can attract such people? The real deal? Or an amateurish band's honest performance?
There's no way I could play real music, anyway.
"…I'll show you what I can do. I think I'll enjoy playing for the first time in a while."
"I knew you'd say that with the way you are now, Touma. So rest up and get better quickly."
"Then, if your fever does go down the next time you wake up…"
"Please send my regards to the person you got those lyrics from… Tell him, 'Go to hell, Takeya!'"
"…I don't want to boast, but it is a great song. I think I am a genius after all."
"Seems like the medicine is kicking in, huh?"
"I'll be making a lot of noise now, but just try to ignore me and get some sleep, all right?"
"I can't hear sounds that are out of tune anyway, so there shouldn't be any problems."
"Your call cannot be connected at the moment because the number you have dialed is outside the service area or the cell phone may be switched off."
"Oh, there you are, Setsuna! Come on, you've gotta come in and change now!"
"Ah… But there's still a whole hour until we open up the…"
"No, there's 'only' an hour. This kind of stuff never goes according to schedule, so we have to be prepared ahead of time!"
"Look, there's like ten people already lined up in front of our shop. They must know that your shift is today. Jeez, they should go and help out their own classes…"
"Oh, it's nothing. I just couldn't sleep well last night."
"…No matter what the reason is, I don't feel reassured."
"A-Anyway, I'm fine… I'll be fine today, at least."
"I heard about your club from Takeya. But there's no point worrying about it now. Just relax!"
"Well, you're the ex-captain of the basketball team, and really brave, so it may not seem like a big deal to you, but…"
"No way! I can't sing in public. No way I could raise my voice in such a place."
"Even Io can't deal with it… If that's the case, how could I…?"
"Even so, you can't run away from it, can you? You agreed to it, after all. Then again, if the other members don't show up, you don't have to worry about it."
"That's right. I said I'd do it! I have to make our performance successful no matter what. I can't cause trouble for Haruki-kun or Touma-san…"
"Considering the members, you don't need to worry about that. I'm sure Haruki's the one causing all the trouble!"
"Why aren't they coming…? Why aren't they answering my calls…? Our performance is tomorrow…"
"…So it comes down to this, huh. Unbelievable. Takeya's joke might actually come true."
"Nope! Time's up! Setsuna, you are a retro maid today. You agreed to do this as well, so do your best!"
"…Actually, I refused it countless times so that I could focus on our performance tomorrow…"
"If you don't make an appearance in our shop, we'll have a riot on our hands. Come on, just leave your stuff in the locker, and let's get going!"
Smile and practice saying, 'With pleasure!' and 'Welcome home, master!'."
"I'm pretty sure you've got that all wrong…"
I think I've mentioned it before, but…
Houjou High School's festival takes place on the same day as Houjou University's festival, right next to our campus.

The university's festival gets swarmed every year not only by local visitors but also by those from outside the prefecture. As such, it's a given that our own festival is pitifully small in comparison, since our high school is merely affiliated with and shares the university's name.

Nevertheless, we manage to drag over spillover visitors from the neighboring university through whatever means necessary, from luring them in to having them think we're some rest stop. This makes the turnout every year fairly decent.
Today is the first day of the annual super-popular Houjou University festival and our somewhat-popular Houjou High festival.
The joyous eve of our reckless challenge.
"Haruki! Why'd you turn your cell phone off yesterday!?"
After noticing that this morning, I felt dizzy because of my carelessness.
So that's why I didn't get any periodic updates from Setsuna, the ones she'd started giving me since last week.
"Do you have any idea what a mess it was? Without you two, we couldn't rehearse at all!"
"That's exactly why I left it all in your hands, President."
"Well, sure, I had them pass the protocol for our performance… but I couldn't ease Setsuna-chan's anxiety no matter what I tried…"
"She was deathly pale. Could barely even walk on stage, too."
Always in the spotlight… Forced to enter the Miss Houjou contest every year… Not to mention, she can sing perfectly on her own. To think that Setsuna…
Hold on, none of these facts suggest that she can handle being on the big stage…
"She got scared, realizing that the place where she will have to sing tomorrow is not a karaoke booth, the music room, or Touma's house."
"Yeah, by the way, you're already exposed by now, so you can just call her Setsuna."
"Well, what's our next move, Haruki? Think we can perform tomorrow despite Setsuna-chan's condition?"
"And what about Touma's condition? Not to mention… have you even learned how to play?"
"Right now… I don't have the time to worry about such trivial things."
"Trivial… Actually, those are pretty critical factors that'll decide whether we go through with it or quit at the last moment, you know?"
"That's not like you, President. When did you turn into such a timid man?"
"Around the time when you took over my position as lead guitarist."
"By the way, Haruki, where are you headed? We've already passed by Class E."
"My class? Why would I need to go there?"
"…What exactly do you think a school festival is?"
Finally reaching my destination, I find something unexpected waiting for me there.
A long line of people is crowding the entrance of the classroom. And the gender ratio of the line looks quite skewed, too…
"That's Class A's Taisho Romance Cafe, you see."
"I can see why something like this would be popular, but don't you think it's weird that there's that many people here?"
There's enough people to fill up a classroom three times over.
At this rate, the people at the back of the line will have to wait for around an hour…
"I guess it's to be expected. There's a rumor going around that Setsuna-chan's shift here is only today, so I bet everyone rushed over to see her."
"All these people are here… just to see Setsuna?"
"I'm pretty sure I told you this before. You underestimate her way too much."
"That goes for tomorrow, too. When you guys get on stage, I'm sure the gym will be full. She naturally attracts attention from the whole school, you know."
Because I've seen her naive, frank, selfish, and mischievous sides, and even had her snap at me. To me, she's just a regular girl-next-door…
"That's why you have to decide carefully whether we'll perform tomorrow or not. You're the only one who can protect her now, after all…"
