No matter how much Takeya worries about us, or how much sincere advice he gives me…
"All right, everyone, break it up! You can't line up here yet! Get back to your posts!"
I don't have time to worry about that now. There's something much more important for me to do, after all.
"What are you all doing here? Why aren't you helping out your own class? What the hell do you think the school festival is!?"
"Wait, that's what I just said to yo…"
"Hey, you're bothering Class A! If you don't leave now, we'll forbid you from entering here later! Get away from the entrance, right now!"
"Finally! Hey, let's get supplies into the classroom while we can. At last, we can prepare for our shop properly."
"Get a move on, everyone! We've only got fifteen minutes before opening!"
"Setsuna, you help out too. Look, we haven't even laid out the tablecloths yet."
"Um, do I look silly at all wearing this costume?"
"…To tell you the truth, the costume does look kinda silly, but…
that's the whole idea of our shop, so I think it's fine."
"But that's not the problem here! Just tell me if I look good in this outfit or…"
"Well, you should just ask the person you really want to hear it from, then… Just turn around a little!"
Even though I haven't seen her for only two days, Setsuna looks like a different person.
…I guess it's because of the costume.
"Kitahara, I need to ask you for a favor. Could you send some of the executive committee members to help us? You're the chairman, right? Once our shop opens, people will just crowd up again…"
"No, I'm not on the executive committee. I'm here on personal business."
I can see myself laughing it off if I were mistaken for a committee member, but mistaken for the chairman is just too much…
"I heard from Takeya about yesterday. I'm sorry that I couldn't make it to the rehearsal…"
"No, it's not your fault. I should be apologizing since I couldn't do anything to help…"
"I didn't notice my battery died. And you called me over and over…"
Actually, it took me about ten minutes to listen to all of her messages…
"Yeah… Um, sorry, I probably overdid it. But I was just worried about Touma-san and… well, um, you know…"
"Ahem! Everyone eavesdropping, get back to work right now! We're almost out of time before we have to open!"
"Give it a rest, Io. No one's listening to you."
"Touma is fine, she'll come tomorrow. I checked her temperature this morning, it was 36.7°C."
"…! That's a relief! I'm really glad, Haruki-kun!"
"It's been such a hard week, but your efforts have gotten us through it, Haruki-kun!"
"No, it's still too early to think like that. Let's not until tomorrow's performance is over."
"I expected no less prudence from you, Haruki-kun! I'm really relieved to see that you are your usual self… I'm so glad…"
"Come on, you guys, go continue this in the corner or something… You're bothering our preparations."
"Give it up, Io… They aren't listening either."
It's not that I have a problem with my surroundings, I just don't know how to breach the topic…
"I will do my best, definitely! I won't have any trouble with you two by my side!"
"That's the thing… I need to ask you a favor regarding that…"
If we keep talking here, we'll just bother Class A even more.
…But at the same time, what I'm about to do will cause an even bigger problem.
So I have to get it over with as quickly as possible to give them time to recover.
"I sincerely apologize for what I'm about to do, Class A. But…"
…Save the criticism for next week. I can't even begin to imagine how harsh it will be.
"Sorry! I don't think you'll ever forgive me, but I'll be taking Setsuna!"
A maneuver executed at the speed of light.
Taking her hand and squeezing through the arranged tables, I push my way through where the crowd is the thinnest.
"Make way, coming through! Hey, don't be running there!"
Just like that, the two of us got out into the hallway.
"Wh-What are you doing? What's going on!?"
"All we can do to overcome your anxiety is practice, right? We've still got about 30 hours left!"
It's a spur-of-the-moment excuse, but admittedly, the fact that we are running out of time is true.
"I'll apologize to everyone in Class A as much as it takes! This is all my fault, it's got nothing to do with you!"
"No, that's not the point! Do I have to go outside… looking like this!?"
No one's coming after us. The kidnapping of Class A's princess went without a hitch!
"No, wait, hold on! I can't believe this happened! What the hell is going on here…? And we have to open up, like, right now!"
"What will you do? Cover for him? He is a member of your club, after all…"
"…Is what I have to say as a student of Class A."
"Why don't I have my guitar here!? I feel like I could play like Paul Simon right now!"
"…Sorry, I'm only familiar with sports, so I don't know how to follow up on that one."
I assumed that she was confident on stage just because she is capable of easily attracting a lot of people's attention.
"I knew it was just a rehearsal. But standing on stage, illuminated by the spotlight, I felt my throat dry up and I couldn't make my voice come out at all."
But she had never stood on stage willingly before.
"I was sweating all over, my legs were shaking, I couldn't hear a thing… and…"
Even though she never acted of her own accord, good results always came to her spontaneously.
"I wanted to run away, but my feet wouldn't move an inch. I'm scared to think what would happen if I got on stage in this condition at the school festival…"
"I'm really sorry. I should have called you, at least…"
Even so, she chose to get on stage by herself this time. She might have done so because of a certain someone's selfish desire…
"Even that situation was less embarrassing than the one I'm in now!"
"Don't make such a fuss, Setsuna… Everyone's looking at us."
"They're not looking at us because I'm shouting, you know!"
"I know, but you're still attracting more attention if you do, don't you think?"
"Aaah, jeez! I admit the way you're being so calm is reliable, but it's also so frustrating, Haruki-kun!"
Since it's past 10 AM, there are a lot less commuters and students on the train. On the other hand, there are a bunch of housewives on shopping trips and the like…
…As expected, Setsuna's kimono-style maid costume made her quite the inviting target.
"Aaah, this is so embarrassing… I could just die. During the rehearsal, my mind just went blank and I couldn't think of anything, but now I can feel every single person's discerning gaze…"
"You were about to work in that outfit, weren't you? What's the difference?"
"There is a certain time, place and occasion that I can deal with wearing this costume, and it's definitely not a train on a weekday!"
I'm guessing the Taisho Romance Cafe is that specific place.
…Actually, I can figure out that much just from its name.
"Fine already, I'll apologize to you as much as you want once we get off the train. So just calm down now, and prepare your voice. We'll be practicing soon enough."
"…Your instructions are so specific. I wonder when you'll find the time to apologize."
"I will! If you so insist, I'll apologize right now!"
"You could've at least let me change my clothes…"
"If I'd done that, your colleagues from Class A would have just snatched you right back. And I bet they'd have beaten me up too… They'd have smashed my fingers or something."
"That kind of joke might earn you points in a shoujo manga, but I won't yield to you!"
Although I do wonder what manga she's thinking of, honestly, the only thing that comes to mind with a situation like this is a soap opera…
"If it's that embarrassing for you, feel free to hide with my profile."
"You don't have to tell me… I'll put you on the spot too…"
Setsuna's hands are clutching my chest, and her body's sidled close to mine.
From how strongly she's holding on to me, I can feel how desperate she is to hide with my profile… or rather, to just disappear altogether.
"Like this, you'll be the center of attention together with me, Haruki-kun… Hehe, hehehe…"
Hold on, she's definitely desperate about something, but could I be getting the wrong idea?
The train isn't that crowded, but all the seats are occupied…
Being stuck in such a tight space, I can't help but feel conscious of all the looks the other people in the train are giving us.
…And the moment Setsuna hid behind my chest, all their gazes focused on me.
I wonder how many boys wanted her to speak to them like this today…
"You're usually very gentle, but you do get very forceful sometimes, don't you?"
"I wonder why, then? Why are you being so childish and unreasonable today?"
"Say, what's on your mind right now? Or should I say… who is on your mind?"
"…I know full well… You are in love with the young lady."
"But that's fine. After all, my feelings only go one way… My unrequited, fruitless, and ephemeral feelings."
"But, every now and then, just like this… I'd like you to…"
"Iwazu-chou, Iwazu-chou. Please mind the door when exiting."
"Aa-ah, that's a shame. I was just getting to the good part!
Come on, then, let's get off, Haruki-kun."
"Oh, you planned for this, didn't you!? You were expecting the timing to be just perfect, weren't you!?"
"My throat dried up, I was sweating like crazy, and barely standing! I thought my heart would stop for a moment!"
"Yep, yep, that's it! That's exactly how I felt yesterday!"
What happened to that soft voice of hers from just a moment ago…?
Pointing and laughing at me, the charming waitress seems to be back to her usual self.
"I… I just can't think of any way to beat you."
"You think you could beat Touma-san, then?"
By this point, she has accepted the role of a waitress, and is no longer worried about the sharp stares of those around us. She really is a strong girl, despite her looks.
"Mister student, mister student? Tell me, what do you think about that?"
"Come on already! We're gonna be practicing non-stop for the next 24 hours!"
After this, I'm sure that I'll have even more trouble looking her in the eyes…
She takes all my requests no matter how ridiculous they are, overcomes all difficulties on her own, and remains our greatest asset.
"Touma-san! I'm so glad you recovered! And I'm so sorry that I couldn't help you…"
Setsuna, seeing Touma after two days, is getting so excited that I think she might… Oh, there, she just hugged her.
"Are you really fine? Is your strength back? I'll make something that'll restore all your stamina tonight!"
"…For starters, explain something to me. What's up with that outfit?"
The modern-era Touma doesn't seem to be familiar with Taisho-era waitresses.
"This is… well, you see, Haruki-kun forced me to…"
"Don't just skip over the whole story and summarize it in one ambiguous line!"
"I see… So the cafe opened on schedule. That's great."

"It is not at all! The guys who waited in line were all excited to see you, then made a fuss with the executive committee! Should I also remind you about the person who's supposed to act as your substitute now?"
"…I'd really like to see it. Io the waitress!"
"Give me a break… All those arrangements I made to make sure I wouldn't have to serve customers have gone down the drain!"
But I had no idea you did something like that. That's pretty unfair, since you wouldn't let me quit no matter what."
"Setsuna, you're Class A's main attraction! Not having you here today was out of the question…"
"But the same goes for you, doesn't it? The number of customers didn't decrease, did it?"
"Sure it did! …The line outside is only about half as long."
"…Meaning you're very busy right now! Sorry for bothering you, and thanks for calling."
"No worries, I'm just glad to hear you're fine, Setsuna. Right, I should get back to work."
"I am really sorry. Once our performance is over tomorrow, I'll personally apologize to all of you."
"There's no need for you to do that, Setsuna. Just send Haruki over to beg for our forgiveness… Takeya will be next on that list."
"No, I did this of my own accord. I chose by myself to betray you all…"
"That's why I won't let Haruki-kun apologize. This is our class's problem, so we shouldn't bring outsiders into this, right?"
"You kidnapped the bride… Kitahara, you can't ever enter Class A again, you know that?"
"You don't have to tell me that… I couldn't get my cell phone to work, so I went to see her personally."
"It's a pretty reckless thing to do nonetheless… Ogiso must have been happy."
"Stop jumping to conclusions as if you'd witnessed it. She was actually incredibly mad."
"Even though you two rushed into my house holding hands?"
"That's your proof, see. Proof that I dragged her here against her will."
"Still, truth be told, I messed up. If only I'd noticed my cell phone's battery was dead last night…"
"…So let's just both do our best. I'll leave the singing to you, and you leave the humiliation to me."
"Ahaha… I'm honestly relieved I decided to avoid it."
"I'll have you make it up to me someday. Later, then."
"Ah! Wait, Io! Could you forward another message to everyone for me?"
"Tell them, 'If you have time tomorrow, please be sure to come watch our performance!', okay?"
"It's a new song. The third song, our last number."
"I'm afraid we only have 24 hours left to practice this song, since I got sick."
"No, it's not all your fault. I couldn't play the solo of Sound of Destiny until this morning, either."
Setsuna looks at the handwritten lyrics, the music score, Touma's face, and my face alternately, blinking in surprise.
Her reaction is quite understandable. I mean, no one would expect a new song at this point.
"The synth part is already finished, the guitar part is simple enough… In addition, I composed this song with your vocal range in mind."
"My vocal range… you mean this song is… original?"
"Yeah, to cut a long story short."
"W-Wait, I can't keep up with all of this…"
"Touma composed thisーour third song. I didn't think we'd make it, in all honesty, and I already gave up halfway…"
"I couldn't care less about this song, but you know, Kitahara insisted on playing it no matter what…"
For someone who "couldn't care less," she was pretty fired up about it. Composing this song even in the middle of a test and pushing herself so hard she got sick.
When a teacher tried to take the notebook away, she got so mad and yelled, "What right do you have to take it away!?". Is that really how someone who doesn't care acts, huh?
"Well, Setsuna, we will be playi… Oh?"
"What's wrong? Is there something bothering you?"
Oh, this is bad. Her being-left-out paranoia is about to make a grand comeback. That's why she suddenly went silent…
I have to be careful now, or we'll run into a world of trouble again…
"That's right. We kept this a secret from you on purpose."
What the hell are you thinking…?
"Kitahara told me not to tell you about this because he wanted to surprise you."
I thought Touma was about to pour gasoline on the fire, but it was actually water…
"The lyrics seem to be written 'with Ogiso's image in mind,' you know?"
And she passes me the hose abruptly.
"Hey, what are you… no, actually, I wrote the original lyrics way before."
"Still, you know… after you joined our club as the singer, Setsuna, I modified the lyrics to match your image…"
"That means Kitahara wrote the lyrics for you, and I composed for you. This is the song we created only for you, Ogiso."
"Touma, you just said something incredibly embarrassing…"
"I'm only saying this because you obviously can't explain it to her properly. Take some responsibility and explain it."
She's right. I have to explain this embarrassing story.
I started making it for an embarrassing reason, and I gave up because I was embarrassed, and yet, it has finally seen the light of day.
"I wanted to try writing lyrics, even just one song was fine. That was the reason why I joined this club in the first place."
That's why I have to come clean about it right now.
"There were two guitarists in the club at the time, so I never imagined I'd be playing on my own during the school festival."
I have to tell her, the girl who turned my cheap lyrics into a great song out of genuine, unnecessary kindness.
"But I wanted to achieve something… I wanted my three years of high school to end with one big, stupid bang. After all, I've had such a gray life up until now you could almost say it's ideal…"
I have to tell her, to the person who will embrace my song and sing it with a voice which I could only dream about.
"I was good at writing, you know… Well, until then, I only wrote essays, mathematical proofs, chemical formulas, chronological tables, English translations, things like that."
At first, I thought about composing the song by myself, after learning to play the guitar from Takeya.
But I realized the limits of my musical talent and ability… After hearing the delinquent girl beside me playing the guitar much better than me, I gave up on composing soon enough.
Next, I tried devoting myself to writing lyrics, but my lyrical sense was… well, let's just say that I found out it was not where I belonged.

Even so, I managed to finish writing the lyrics by using the words that I learned from midnight radio shows around ten years prior. At the time, I hadn't fully understood the meaning of those words, though.
"…Anyway, read it over once, and tell me if there's anything that needs correcting. Touma didn't change even one line, so I feel a bit insecure."
"…Even my hands couldn't fix that mess."
"What do you think? Is it impossible to master this song in only one day, after all?"
"Sorry, but could you please be quiet for a moment?"
Staring at the music score, she mumbles something.
"Practice has already started, so could you play it for me once, Touma-san? I can't read sheet music…"
She raises her face, and puts on an expression so serious that I feel like she can't hear me at all.
"We don't have much time left, Haruki-kun. There's only one day left! …Let's work hard together and complete our song, okay?"
And so began our last 24 hours.
Houjou University's festival takes place on the same day as Houjou High School's festival, right next to our… I'll omit the rest; it's getting pretty repetitive.
Today marks the second day of the highly popular Houjou University festival and the somewhat popular Houjou High festival. With it being a Saturday, it's a day off for many people.
And it's also the day of our actual make-or-break performance.
"Come on, why aren't you complimenting the both of them with words like 'beautiful', or 'wonderful', or 'freakin' awesome!'?"
"No, I think you should hold back on that last one…"
Paying no heed to their banter, I find myself frozen like a cliche manga protagonist who accidentally entered a room while girls were changing inside.
After all… I'm so captivated by the sight of these two right now that all of Takeya's flattering compliments seem like ridiculous understatements.
"What's the meaning of this, you damn perverted president…? When did I ever agree to wear a costume like this?"
"We decided on the costumes on the day of the rehearsal. So unfortunately, since you didn't come, you forfeited your vote."
"There were a few other candidates I had in mind, but I think this black one suits Touma-san the best."
"So this was your decision, Ogiso!? This color… this design… and just look at how revealing it is!"
"I don't think Setsuna had any bad intentions… Besides, that costume is a perfect contrast to hers."
Black and white… Cool and cute…
If you ask me, these costumes are perfect choices. Considering their respective images, they aren't anything out of the ordinary and totally feel just right.
"All the costumes that Iizuka-kun brought were pretty similar to begin with.
…What should we do? Wanna swap costumes with me?"
"That one would be even worse… I think I'll just wear my school uniform."
"Hey, whoa, don't take your clothes off in front of the guys!"
"I mean, Kitahara's going out in his uniform, isn't he? It's not fair!"
"But, y'know… it'd just be a waste of money to get him a costume. It's only natural to invest in the ones who can draw people's attention, right?"
"I won't be drawing any attention either!"
"I imagine you'll draw in a lot of the underclassmen who know nothing about you."
"It'll only last for about ten minutes anyway. Let's just bite the bullet and get embarrassed together, okay?"
"You may feel embarrassed, but I'm sure those watching you will love it!"
"Ah, by the way, the executive committee will be recording those ten minutes to be preserved for all eternity on the school's website."
"Ki-Kitahara… how long are you planning on keeping that mouth of yours shut? Say something already!"
"No, I… I'm honestly not sure whether I should say what's on my mind or not…"
"Well, how about that. You actually do want to hear Haruki-kun's impression, don't you, Touma-san?"
"No, the things you and I want are quite different, Ogiso."
"I feel like… I won't be able to stop showering the both of you with extremely passionate praise if I start… Could you two bear with me?"
"Do we look good? Say, these costumes look good on us, don't they?"
"Oh, this is dangerous… Awesome… So awesome… You two look so freakin' awesome! Those costumes look so good on you I can hardly resist!"
"Ahahahaha… Hold on, Haruki-kun, you sound like a totally different person right now!"
"Ah, I'm so sorry. But… this really is just too incredible."
"Well, due to obvious reasons, Haruki will toootally ruin the visual impact while you guys are on stage…"
"Still, Takeya, you'd ruin it all the same if you put yourself between these two. It's a pretty big problem either way…"
"Um, well, I mean… Setsuna and… Touma, you're both… how should I say this… perfect?"
"But you're glad to hear that, aren't you? Just be honest like me, Touma-san."
"This is why I keep saying I just can't deal with you, Ogiso…"
Our debut is only two hours away.

I am incredibly nervous, but even more than that… I feel so excited about finally being able to move my fingers and body more skillfully than I ever have. I feel like I won't make a single mistake while playing today.
Then again, it'll be exactly the sort of situation in which I'm most likely to make a fatal mistake…
No, it's no use worrying about it now.
"Yo, Haruki. Listen, I wanted to talk to you a bit about the Miss Houjou High contest…"
"I am no longer a member of the official nor the unofficial school festival executive committee, you know."
"Well, what you're doing now is like when a former member of an election administration commission becomes the private secretary for the candidate."
Both executive committees had a lot to say behind my backーnot for quitting in itselfーbut for the reason why I quit.
"The contest is drawing a lot more attention this year. I had a thousand ballot slips printed out, but it's been only two days and we've already run out!"
"The school administration won't let it slide if you keep that up. Be careful not to let the contest's scale get too big."
The reason being is Miss Houjou High differs from Miss Houjou University in that it's unofficial. The school administration doesn't approve of it, but it at least still tolerates the event.
If even the slightest issue occurs, the contest can be canceled on very short notice. That's why the unofficial executive committee has to manage it with the utmost care.
…At least, that's what the committee's previous chairman has informed me of so very eloquently.
"What are you saying, man? Whose fault do you think it is that the contest's scale grew so big this year in the first place…?"
"I'll have you know that everything was handled with a lot more caution while I was still on the committee."
"Well, you quitting the committee and the reason why you did it is what made this year's contest such a big deal."
"Just call her Setsuna. Takeya's already told me everything."
"Plus, the two-time winner of Miss Houjou High is finally going on stage this year, you know? Both of those things have really been making waves."
"Have you noticed that there are a lot more university students visiting our festival this year? Even though they have their own festival… It's weird, isn't it?"
I thought it was just my imagination, but there really are a lot more people who look like university students than usual, even since morning…
They usually come to our festival in the evening, and even then, they only take a short look.
"The high school and the university are on the same server, so I guess they can see our festival's web page."
And vice versa, we can see their web page too. From there, we often gather information to loaf around at their university festival, neglecting our own.
I mean, they have celebrities and scholars coming to their festival as guests. Not to mention almost every event that they hold is on a much larger scale than ours.
Speaking of which, I think I heard something about Ogata Eiji coming to some panel discussion or another as a guest this year…
"Well, I found something interesting on the university's forum. A thread regarding Ogiso's stage appearance… The discussion was pretty lively."
"University students must have a lot of free time…"
"She's gonna be a freshman there next year, so it's no surprise that she's getting all the attention."
"This reflects on the contest too. People are no longer wondering if Ogiso can win the third time in a row, but instead by how much of a lead she will win."
Meaning that she's not only our school's idol anymore, but Houjou University's as well…
At times, I find it hard to link her image as a school idol to who she really isーa girl who feels happy just because I call her "Setsuna."
"I can't afford to embarrass myself, no matter what. For both my sake and Setsuna's."
"Are you deliberately pushing the topic in that direction?"
"There's still more than an hour until it starts. What do you wanna do?"
"The other performances have started already, right? How about going to the gymnasium?"
"I don't really care for high schoolers' performances, though."
"But we came here to watch a high school girl sing, y'know?"
"Hey, Kitahara! Sorry, could you come take a look at something? The battery in our stand is acting weird."
"I don't care. I'm not on the committee."
That's the third group of university students who are here to see our… no, who are here to see Setsuna.
Chikashi wasn't exaggerating. There are definitely a lot more university students around than usual.
Shouldn't it be more meaningful to go to the university festival over the affiliate high school's…?
"Come on, hurry up or there won't be any seats left!"
"Why should I be in the audience…!? This isn't how it should have turned out!"
"You're still going on about that… You brought it upon yourself, you know?"
"Besides, I know that you tried to get on stage just to get more attention, but are you even any good at singing?"
"No way she can sing well either…! I'm sure I'll enjoy laughing at her from the audience!"
"It's so unfair! It was my plan originally! Then that damn Ogiso Setsuna showed up and ripped me off!"
"Maybe she's even more eager to attract attention than you are, Tomo. That might explain why she's won the contest twice in a row, too."
Yeah, I'm pretty sure I just saw someone familiar, but my mind was in denial over it.
"Kitahara-senpai! Sorry, we really need your help! Our cook cut her finger!"
"I keep telling you all, I'm not on the committee! The executive committee members are on standby in that tent over there, so go and ask them for help."
Never mind the university students, a lot of our schoolmates are coming to see her as well.
It's not just guys, either; a lot of girls are also gathering at the gymnasium, just in time to see our performance.
…I have no idea what's going to happen.
"Wow, it's so crowded. This is nothing like a usual high school festival."
"It's so cool… I think I wanna go to this school now, too."
"What are you saying? Takahiro, you wouldn't make it here with your grades, you know."
"But, you know… if I went to a private school just like Nee-chan did, it would be hard to pay my tuition, that's why…"
"If you could enroll here, I'd let you, even if it meant it would be hard on us. Just remember that there are plenty of good public schools too…"
"Aa-ah, there it is, over there! That building must be the gymnasium! Nee-chan's performance is starting at 3 o'clock, right?"
…There goes my opportunity to greet them. I didn't think they'd really come.
University students, our schoolmates, and even family members…
The amount of attention Setsuna is attracting shows no sign of slowing down.
"Like I said, I'm not on the commit…!?"
"Could you tell me where the gymnasium is? This is my first time here."
"R-Right this way! Please, I'll take you there."
That was close… I almost lashed out at a guest…
"Only two groups left before us, huh…"
"…Hey, doesn't it seem like the audience has been getting bigger and bigger?"
"Yeah, it looks like there are no seats left. A lot of people are standing. And we're just a light music club that reformed a month ago… This is no joke…"
"Are all these people here to see Setsuna?"
"Well, at the very least, I'm sure nobody came to watch Haruki play the guitar… Looks like there are a few who are here to watch Touma, though."
"Then again, they seem to hate her so much. Maybe they're just here hoping to make fun of her?"
"The more they stand out, the more enemies they'll have… The same goes for Setsuna-chan. If she messes up, they'll turn vicious in a heartbeat."
Well, I suppose Haruki is the only one standing by you among all the male students, after all."
"You're one to talk, Miss Spartan Captain… Come on, we should go and meet up with them already."
"I hope Setsuna doesn't choke up again… Don't say anything stupid that could put pressure on her, okay?"
"Yo! We're up next, huh? There's a bunch of people standing in the audience just here to see you guys, you know?"
"What did I just tell you a moment ago, dumbass!? Read the mood for once, come on…"
"Let me see… Wow, it's true! Haruki-kun, Haruki-kun, there are so many people!"
As Setsuna walks up the stage discreetly, she peeks at the audience through the gap between the curtains, and describes what she sees.
"Just like I said earlier, see? Word has spread even throughout the university."
In saying that, I only came back here a few minutes ago, so I'm fully aware of the disaster that's waiting for us in the audience, in a way.
"…Also, your mother and brother are here. You should be able to find them if you look through the audience."
Just as I'd expected, most of our audience are "amateurs." They don't usually go to concerts or have much of an interest in music, they're just here to see Setsuna.
"…Having those two watching is just the worst. I'm sure they're gonna chew me out about my singing when I get home. Even though they're completely out of tune themselves when they sing karaoke."
"Wow, you go to karaoke with your family too?"
"…Yeah, but usually they sing one song per person while I end up singing five in a row, so lately they don't really want to go with me."
"You obviously brought that upon yourself. Why can't you seem to have any modesty when it comes to singing?"
"I can't help myself! I can sing better than them anyway, so there shouldn't be any problem if I sing more, right?"
"See? Who can't read the mood now?"
"You two must be so excited due to lack of sleep. After all, we haven't gotten a wink of sleep since yesterday."
"You didn't get any sleep either, Touma. How come you're so calm?"
That said, it's not like I've ever seen her excited even once in the whole half a year I've known her.
"I've been playing the piano at competitions since I was five years old, at least three times a year. And there were… about two times I didn't place first, maybe?"
"…No, I wasn't asking you to boast."
It is something she deserves to boast about, though. I guess she really is a genius.
"Then, I'd like to ask the veteran Touma-san to give us some advice!"
Returning from the side of the stage with the same cheer she had a moment ago, Setsuna approaches Touma with a request.
Whether she's euphoric or restless, there's no sign of that pale, shivering, and frail girl from yesterday.
Even if she makes a careless slip-up now, I'm sure she won't get nervous over it. I can see her strong determination shining through her eyes.
And even under the dazzling spotlight of the stage, Touma's detached yet fearless expression shows no sign of breaking for even a second.
They're both such reliable partners… If someone's gonna screw up here, it's gonna be me for sure.

"There's no way this will end well with our lack of practice. The responsibility is all on the president, who broke up the club right before the festival, and Kitahara who insisted on reforming the club on such short notice."
She didn't say 'if we fail,' but rather asserted that I've failed already…
"These two underestimate music. Besides, Kitahara even proposed that we should add one more song a single day before our actual performance. I seriously doubt his sanity at this point."
Even though she composed the song…? Even though she programmed the backing track on her own as well…?
…What is she doing? Shouldn't she be trying to encourage us right now? There's not even ten minutes left before it's our turn, right?
"Then… I guess I'm insane too? Despite all that's happened, I believe that Haruki-kun did the right thing."
"…There you have it. I guess we've all gone insane by now. So we might just make it, right?"
"Let's enjoy ourselves, alright? And let's amaze everyone with our performance, okay?"
"If either of you two run into trouble, just listen to my melody. I'll lead you, alright?"
"For the last song, let's just enjoy ourselves, without worrying about the audience. Because it's our song and our song alone."
"That works for me… How about you, Kitahara?"
The previous band has finally finished its performance.
In less than ten minutes, we will climb up on this stage and perform in front of this huge audience.
There's no way out anymore. There's no time for us to do one last rehearsal either.
I'm sorry for pulling in such a huge audience, okay?"
"Whenever you act all arrogant like that, it just leaves me speechless… Come on, let's go, Kitahara!"
"Yeah! Don't make fun of me if I mess up the solo, you two!"
Even so, we've done all we can.

In the limited time we had, we've practiced, pulled all-nighters, made an original song, fought amongst each other and reconciled. One of them caught a cold and I took care of her, while the other got stage fright and overcame her fear. And at last, we find ourselves here today.
I don't know if it would be right to call it friendship or something entirely different, but the three of us definitely have a strong bond now… Or so I believe.
So let's make those two weeks of preparation pay off in the next ten minutes!
"What's wrong with those two… trusting Haruki so much. Have they lost their minds?"
"It's a relationship you couldn't get even if you spent your whole life trying to. You can't look at girls in any way but a romantic one, after all."
"But… if the three of them are this close right now… it's only going to get worse for them from now on."
We're welcomed by a storm of applause far too excessive for our unproven, impromptu band.
And through the gap of the rising curtain, we are met with numerous curious gazes from the audience.
At the center of the stage…
…Stands the highlight of our groupーour singer, who I'm sure is drawing the attention of more than 99% of those present here right now.
As Setsuna begins to sing, a wave of cheering arises, conveying the audience's astonishment to us.
…They had no idea that Setsuna is the solo-karaoke queen. They've never heard her sing, after all.
Most of them probably thought we chose her because of her popularity, and she half-heartedly accepted because she wanted even more attention.
And I'm sure that less than ten people know how many times she's sung this song and how much effort she's put in to polish it in these two weeks.
She's no match for a pro, and there are a lot of amateur singers who can sing better than her.
But her singing far exceeds what an ordinary high school girl can do. I bet that's why they're so astonished right nowーbecause that's all they thought she was.
As for me, on the audience's right side, I concentrate on playing my part while letting Setsuna handle the audience's extraordinary reaction.
There's no need to worry about her now. She's gleaming with confidence, completely different from how scared she was at the rehearsal.
I don't need to think about how to play… Just let my fingers move spontaneously, step by step…
Amazing… My fingers are moving perfectly in spite of myself.
Compared to how terrible I was two weeks ago, this is amazing.
And on stage right, the audience's left side, Touma is playing the keyboard completely unfazed.
Unlike a piano, an electronic synthesizer doesn't require delicate adjustment of force to play. That's why she can keep watching over us the entire time.
"If either of you two run into trouble, just listen to my melody. I'll lead you, all right?"
I'm sure she has every intention of keeping true to those words, and I think it wouldn't be particularly difficult for her to do so either.
Now that the initial excitement has died down, the audience seems to be ready to listen to our performance.
This is originally a quiet song, so I knew we couldn't keep the audience excited from the beginning until the end of the song.
And the fact they're quiet means that they're earnestly listening to Setsuna's singing as well.
From here on, it's only a matter of time before they won't just be focusing on the singing, but will also pay attention to Touma and I performing.
Touma's performance is as perfect as it's ever been.
Even though she's not looked at her fingers even once, she's completely on-key and her tempo is flawless.
She's also stopped worrying about Setsuna, so she's free to focus on my finger movements.
…I really am the most unreliable member of this band of ours, huh?
Still, even with how unreliable I am… I think I'm doing pretty well so far.
It's like something inside of me has awoken; my finger movement and coordination are top-notch. I basically haven't made any mistakes so far.
In any case, my mind's drifting off to focus on the solo in our second song, but my intuition is still handling this perfectly in spite of myself.
That said… This is me I'm talking about. And it wouldn't be me if I didn't have some sort of contingency in mind.
…That very concern has found its way even into my next plan.
I give a suggestive wink to Touma, who's been looking at my fingers all along.
It's a plan that I came up with on a whim, and one which Touma frowned upon as a ridiculous street performance.
"I'm telling you, they're gonna love it!"
"…Don't blame me if something goes wrong."
Even after another few encouraging winks from me, Touma looks at me with doubt and a bit of ridicule, but her gaze remains as cool as ever.
"I'll do it if that's what it takes to shut you up."
In the end, she candidly sticks out her tongue at me…
She leaves her keyboard and makes her way to the center of the stage.
Despite playing the saxophone, which is not her specialty, she's still composed enough to wink back at me.
"See, I told you! They loved it!"
"I can't believe Touma of all people is pulling such a stunt…"
"This is an affront to music. After being called a genius and prodigy, and being pampered to no end, she lowers herself to this? Disappointing."
"…Were you expecting something from her? I thought you hated her the most."
"I can't bear to look at this charade anymore. That's not my rival anymore, that's just a clown showing off a stupid skit."
"I don't think Touma ever thought of you as a rival, though. I don't recall you ever beating her in any competition."
"But, you know, this time… it's their win again, isn't it?"
"How do you feel about all of this?"
"Hang on a second… what's going on here?"
"I can't believe they got the audience so fired up. The singer and the guitarist are both such obvious amateurs."
"We started practicing months ago. I can't accept losing to a group like this!"
"Chiaki… No matter what anyone says, you're the star here today, okay?"
"Don't talk to me right now. I'm basking in the afterglow."
"As I thought, the audience is much bigger in the afternoon. It would've been nice if we had gotten to go last…"
"Hey, hey, forget about that for now. Look, isn't that person cute?"
"You're telling others not to talk to you, but now you want to talk…"
"Isn't it cheating to have Ogiso as the singer?"
"None of the boys are even listening to the song. They're just here to gawk at Ogiso-san."
"No, not the singer, the guitarist. The way he looks uncertain about which girl he wants to impress."
As the final wave of applause hits us, we make eye contact to commend each other on a great performance.
…With the exception of a certain someone, who'd given a nonchalant response instead.
"I'm keeping it together, somehow… Keep watching over me, okay?"
Then, as the applause grows quiet, we prepare ourselves to face our new, incoming trial.
"I won't let you die in vain!"
"I'd rather you help me before I die here…"
We've come here unpreparedーwe didn't even decide whether we'd do it or not previously.
Judging from the audience's reaction, though, I'm sure they're hoping to hear Setsuna's unaltered voice…
"Umm… Hello, everyone. We're the Light Music Club!"
Two days ago, Setsuna couldn't speak a word even without an audience, but now she's addressing so many people.
"We hereby welcome you to the Houjou High School Festival! Are you all enjoying yourselves?"
"Umm… We didn't plan to have a speech like this, so I'd just like to apologize in advance if it's a bit awkward."
"…To be honest, I was really surprised to see so many of you here to see us. If we knew this would happen, we would have come up with a name for our group."
"Ah, and as for the song we just performed… well, I suppose I should introduce it to anyone who might be unfamiliar with it."
"It's called White Album and it's around ten years old now, I think… It was Morikawa Yuki-san's debut song."
"The song is kind of old, but it caught on at the time, and has been a sort of a winter classic since. I'm sure there are a lot of you here who know it, right?"
"It's beautiful, but with it being such a tranquil song, I was worried if everyone wouldn't get into it… But it looks like I was wrong, what a relief!"

"To tell you the truth, when we first thought of using this song, it took a lot of courage to decide on it because it's a pretty old song… If we'd messed up, everyone would have been quiet after our performance."
"But all the members of the club liked the song, and more importantly, since I love it so much and wanted to sing it no matter what, we decided on it!"
"…Well, that's about it for the song's introduction… Next, I would like to introduce our members."
"First up is… right, let's start with me. I'm Ogiso Setsuna from Class 3-A. I'm the singer!"
"Standing here and singing in front of everyone… I've never been this nervous in my entire life."
"…But I think I'm performing even better than usual thanks to the support from all your amazing cheering. Thank you all very much!"
"…Oh, by the way… there's a certain poll that happens to end tomorrow, and I'd really appreciate it if you supported me there as well!"
You're actually more than good enough for this, Setsuna…
"Un… Unforgivable! What's with that woman!? Trying to appeal to them using this situation? I'll never forgive you… Ogiso Setsuna!"
"Um, next up is Kitahara Haruki-kun from Class 3-E, our guitarist!"

"In the past, Kitahara-kun was the head of the festival committee and he was also a class representative. He's been involved with a lot of things at school, so I'm sure he's had many opportunities to help you all out with all sorts of things."
"What the… That can't be Haruki, right? How is he playing so well?"
"If I had to say… it's probably because he had an excellent mentor, right?"
"Kgh, what does she have that I don't?"
"To start with, her gender, or maybe being Haruki's type…"
"And just as he's done for many of you, he was the one driving us on and supporting us through his two-faced nature. He's someone that we could always depend on."
As always, she pays no heed to the time or place when it comes to these things… or rather, isn't she taking it a bit too far this time?
"…He's got a really tough solo part in the next song, so if he screws up, please feel free to laugh at him."
So Setsuna's the type to really get carried away with things like this…
"And last, but not least… Touma Kazusa-san from Class 3-E!"
"When it comes to Touma-san… I'm sure that everyone here is surprised to see her, right?"
"All right. Let's get started with the next song!"
"…You really plan to go through with it, huh?"
"When she joined our group, we were amazed by just how skilled she was. I can't even tell you how many times she's helped us already!"
"There's no way we can pull out after coming this far!"
"…Then I need you to absolutely follow my lead, got it?"
"She's in charge of playing the keyboard, the saxophone…"
"And for Sound of Destiny, I was told to delete the bass programming and do the keyboard instead…"
"Oh, Haruki was the one who came up with that. Touma didn't really want to do it, apparently."
"But the fact that she went along with it so easily is what makes it so detestable."
"That's the one thing I must admit, yeah."
"If only her personality was more ordinary, I think she would take away half of your popularity… among the underclass girls, that is."
White Album was a success in itself.
And the crowd is really getting into Sound of Destiny too. We had a feeling this would happen since it's more popular than the first song.
At first, they only concentrated on Setsuna, but it's pretty obvious that the crowd's focus is starting to shift.
From keyboard to saxophone, and now, on bass.
The audience's full attention is now on the clown dressed in black on top of the stage, who couldn't care less what anyone thinks of her.
With her genuine, polished skills and looks that rival even Setsuna's.
While she was looking at me during the first song, I could feel that she was just teasing me a bit, but she's slowly losing her composure now.
Her dignified behavior is gradually becoming more and more stiff.
She looks just like… a parent who's holding a video camera, watching her child's performance in open class.
Don't underestimate me! I show Touma my confidence by sticking my tongue out at her, much like the way she did it to me.
But it's not really reassuring. Looks like my master really can't trust her disciple, or she just thinks it'd be cuter if I made a fool of myself.
No matter what happens, it's almost time…
Since we're short on people, we're using pre-recorded segmentsーa rather underhanded method. As a whole, our performance is pretty shallow.
Even so… I absolutely cannot let myself fail here.
It was my selfishness that dragged the two of them into this. I cannot afford to let them down at the end!
Hey, can the two of you not just look at me simultaneously like that!
"Hm? Setsuna looks kind of strange, don't you think?"
"Don't miss, don't miss, don't miss… Come on, almost there…"
"It's Haruki's solo, so what's up with everyone else being more nervous than him…?"
Overwhelmed by the roaring applause, I let out a deep sigh of relief.
There's still the last song to go, but I've passed the biggest hurdle.
The bassist is in awe too… Even though she was basically just winging it herself.
And the singer is overcome with emotions, looking at me with tears in her eyes. Come on, you should be responding to the audience's cheers, not looking at me!
"Hey, Takahiro. We've heard this song somewhere too, haven't we?"
"You're so noisy, Mom. Be quiet for a bit!"
"What are you saying? Everyone around us is a lot more noisy…"
"All right, then. You can buy one for yourself if you get a part-time job."
I don't think a lot of people noticed it…
But our performance in the second song turned out worse than even some of our practice sessions.
…Especially just before my solo part. It wasn't me, either, but Touma's bass and Setsuna's vocals.
With the way both of their gazes were wandering, and how there were a few hiccups in the singing, it would probably sound pretty bad to anyone listening closely.
Looking at the overall result, I was the only one who gave my best performance… I never could have imagined an outcome like this.
I wonder what invited the delighted expressions they have on their faces now. And I wonder how they can seem to gloss over the whole thing without any regrets.
…Was it really that surprising for me to pull it off? So much that they're not even worrying about their own mistakes?
These two… I wonder just how little faith they had in me.
I wonder just how worried they were about me.
…Well, this is no time for me to get all sentimental too.
"This next song… will be our last one."
After letting out everything, I feel something touching my cheek, bringing me out of my daze.
I turn to look, and see a small fist in front of me. Behind it, I see Touma's face, looking at me with a teasing smile.
"This song is… I'm pretty sure that most of you here are unfamiliar with it…"
"It's not saying much, but you really outdid yourself, huh, Kitahara?"
I can't tell whether that smile is supposed to convey consideration, praise, or a tease, but it's definitely a genuine smile straight from her heart.
"…Oh, what am I saying, I'm sure none of you will recognize it. This is an original song that we just finished yesterday."
But as expected, that smile only lasts but a moment.
Leaving me scrambling for a proper response, she goes back to her keyboard that she'd left alone for around five minutes.
"We've only had a single day to practice it, so I don't know if it'll go well, but…"
Though their ends were pointed upward in a smile just a moment ago, her lips are now sealed and straight as an arrow again, and the dignified Touma Kazusa is ready to continue.
That cold expression tells me everything I need to know.
"I'll sing and enjoy it from the bottom of my heart and up until the very end. Please lend me your ears, everyone."
"Here we go, it's the last spurt."
"What we did there amounted to an after-meal exercise for me."
"And I'm exhausted both physically and mentally."
Just like before, I sit down backward on a chair, leaning my arms and chin against it as Touma tosses gentle words of abuse my way.
"It was scheduled to end at 3:30 from the beginning, anyway."
"I actually have a lot of complaints. Only the beginning was really any good."
"Even so, it was a huge success. We were a big hit, right?"
"We won't ever be able to make it up to the divine Muse of Music."
The curtains rolled down with overwhelming cheers from the audience…
Still in a quiet daze, we quickly tidied up the stage and prepared to climb off it.
As if hiding our embarrassment, we gave the audience one last awkward bow and left the stage. All that, just some half an hour ago.
It was such a great success… but I can hardly believe just how successful we were.
"Io took her. She apparently needs to make up for her absence from yesterday at the cafe."
"Wasn't the theme of the cafe Taisho Romance?"
"Her stage outfit is more popular right now, isn't it?"
I'd bet everyone would want to hear her say, "Welcome" just for them, right after her dazzling performance on the stage.
In just an hour, that super-limited-offer of the cafe will close. I don't even want to imagine the queue there.
"She's still in that outfit, so being stared at by the guys at such a close distance must be torture."
"Then again, Touma… you're being looked at by a guy from really up close right now too."
Despite her cynical remarks, she should have had plenty of time to change.
But Touma is still wearing that same outfit, like a lingering aftertaste of our performance.
"…Of course I'm cold. It's almost the end of fall, after all."
"Hey, I bet you've actually taken a liking to that outfit. Isn't that right?"
"You're so annoying… Why do you have to split hairs over everything, Kitahara? Even back when we first met, you were…"
"I was, and that's exactly why I've been able to stay with you, Touma. I haven't done anything wrong."
Touma's murmuring softly fades into the noise from outside the window…
"…You fell asleep while listening to me playing the piano again."
As I snap out of it, I realize that my chin isn't in its proper resting place, and that I'd dozed off.
"Eh, ummm, like I said… your piano playing is so amazing, Touma, that it emits alpha waves, and…"
That reminds me… I've only gotten about an hour of sleep in these past three days. It's impressive that I've held out for this long.
"…If you do that while I'm in a competition, I'll hit you."
"Does that mean you'll be keeping an eye on my seat in the audience from the stage the whole time?"
"I'm just joking, of course… but are you serious about entering competitions again?"
Up until recently, when talking about the piano, Touma had always used past tense, so that sounded differently, even in the roundabout way she put it.
Perhaps… She's finally ready to give up on the idea of giving up on the piano.
In that case, it's really her own business… but I'm just so happy about it that I don't even want to consider it her business alone.
Even though I don't know just how good she truly is, I'm happy for her simply because I'm a zealous fan of her piano playing.
"Hey, a competition would be great for you, of course, but what I'd really like is for the three of us to do something like this again if we find the time."
"You still haven't learned your lesson after barely pulling off this tightrope trial…? Besides, isn't it time for you to be thinking about your future?"
"That's what I mean. I want us to get together again after graduating… maybe for the university festival, or something like that next time."
"Touma, what will you do about university? Will you be going to a music university after all? Somewhere in the capital, maybe?"
"I still have my graduation to worry about before that, you know."
"Even after we graduate… I hope we can keep seeing each other."
…Did I manage to say it naturally?
"I want us to keep being together, always."
Even though I'm expressing it in the most natural way possible, what I'm saying is really unnatural.
"You're going to Houjou University together with Ogiso, right?"
"Setsuna's the same. She wants to be together with you too, Touma."
Touma gives me an ambiguous answer that's in stark contrast to her usual sarcastic and confident tone of rejection.
"Was being with us… not fun for you?"
And so the words that came out of my mouth were… akin to sleep-talking.
"Touma, Setsuna, and me… When the three of us were together, you didn't feel happy?"
I'm so sleep-deprived it's ridiculous… That's why I can write this off as just sleep-talking.
"I've been so happy and having so much fun every single day…"
Because I know full well I'd never say something as embarrassing as this if my brain were working properly.
"After all, I must seem like the luckiest guy alive from the other guys' point of view. I've used up a lifetime's worth of luck, so I'm sure it'll all come back to bite me sooner or later."
No, stop it. Just fall asleep already…
"That's not really the point, you know, but… at the same time, it has very much been happening."
"There's this unattainable flower I've always adored, who took the initiative and came down to meet me at my own level…"
I'll just say a lot more stupid things… It'll all slip out, one after the other…
"And the person I always admired and wanted to become friends with ended up being my true friend. She's become someone I can talk to with mutual honesty…"
"So she's a 'flower,' and I'm just a 'person,' huh…?"
"…There's no way I wouldn't like it. There's no way it wouldn't be fun. There's no way I wasn't happy."
"You can't figure that much out without asking? Not even that much…?"
"If that's the case, show it through your expression… There's no way I could figure out that poker face of yours…"
"What's wrong, Touma? Why are you… shivering?"
"I see… Winter's right around the corner, huh…"
"Good work, Setsuna! Here, have a drink."
"Okay, here's to the Light Music Club's and Class 3-A's success today!"
"Sorry for making you do this unscheduled, even though you're already so tired."
"Nah, it's fine. I was the one who ran away yesterday, after all. I'm glad I could make up for it."
"Thanks to you, I heard our sales increased by around 30%. The class rep was so happy I saw him crying a little while ago."
"Ah, ahaha… I'm just glad I could help."
"Your popularity is godlike now, Setsuna. That stage appearance did wonders."
"It was really fun. And it's all thanks to Haruki-kun and Touma-san."
"…Yeah, you really looked like you were having fun. Despite being dragged into it forcefully by Haruki."
"Yup… I'm really glad to have met the two of them. It feels like I've made my best memories with them."
"Since it turned out like this, maybe I should have introduced you to Haruki sooner?"
"Oh, right… you already knew Haruki-kun from before, Io?"
"He's a pretty good guy, but our interests never really overlapped. We never really hung out all that much either."
"Then… do you know if he's ever had a girlfriend?"
"There's no way he did. It's a mystery as to why he took up the guitar, too."
"I see… Is that so… So Haruki-kun and I are the same, huh…?"
"…Well then, thanks for the drink. I'd better go get changed now."
"Yeah, Haruki-kun said he'd be waiting there. Touma-san might be there too."
"Yeah, thanks for everything today. See you tomorrow."
"Errr, well… This may not be the right time to say this, but…"
"What's wrong? Why are you suddenly being so roundabout with your words?"
"Well, this is… it's kind of hard for someone like me to give this kind of advice, you see…"
"You know, if… if you're really serious about him, I think you'd better hurry up."
"By that, well… I mean, there's no deep meaning behind it, but…"
"Um, was that too unclear? I can explain, when I say 'him,' I mean…"
"You don't have to say it. It's fine."
"What I mean is, I know exactly what you're trying to tell me, Io. Who you mean by 'him', why I should hurry… and of course, what my own feelings are."
"I'd be fine if we stayed like this. I can't be happier with our current relationship."
"We had so much fun on stage today, so… I want us to keep having fun, just like that, for a little while longer…"
"That's why… I don't want to change. I don't want anyone to change."
"…There's really no deep meaning behind that, okay?"
"You… really like to sleep while I'm playing the piano. Don't you think you're being rude?"
"You look so happy… Were you that delighted to be on stage?"
"Well… I was happy, for what it's worth."
"You're such a boring guy, you know."
"Serious to a fault, always quibbling and bound by rules… So big-headed and sucking up to the teachers… Getting good grades while you're at it and tooting your own horn over it."
"I swear, with how terribly boring you are…"
"It just makes me want to tease you, you know…"
"I'm… I'm sorry… Sorry, Kitahara… I really did it."
"This is… all your fault, you know?"
"…No, that's not it. I'm sorry, I'm just terrible…"
"I can't help myself, okay? …I'm not strong enough to hold myself back like you are."
Once again, I find that my chin isn't in its proper resting place…
And I also realize that the color of my surroundings has completely changed.
The darkness enveloping the music room, coupled with my blurry vision, makes it so I can barely see anything.
Along with the setting of the sun, the bustling sounds of my classmates have calmed down little by little.
Shaking my head, I try to recall the moment before I lost consciousness.
I'm sure I was here with Touma, listening to her criticize our performance, and talking about the future, as well as the coming season…
I feel like there were some boundaries I crossed in our conversation that I shouldn't have, but having just woken up, I can't remember what it was for the life of me.
Right then… Right, I must have told her about…
Just like that, while I was completely spaced out, thinking about what I'd said…
…All of a sudden, I feel a soft, yet captivating voice brush against my face.
"Good morning, Haruki-kun. And good work today."
…It wasn't a metaphorical statement, either. Her breath really touched my face. That's how close she is to me.
She kneels in front of me to match her height with my gaze, intently watching me without even blinking through the dim lighting.
"That ended a long time ago. It's almost six already, you know?"
"…It's that late already? I sure slept a lot, huh."
"You sure did. I've been here for more than half an hour now."
"You could have just woken me up…"
"You really didn't need to be so considerate of me. After all, you must be tired too…"
"If I'd done that, I wouldn't have been able to take my time looking at your sleeping face, Haruki-kun. It'd be such a waste."
"Come on! Tell me you're just teasing me!"
What's more, she hasn't stopped gazing at me ever since I woke up either.
"Huaah… Ow, ow, ow, ow! Aah, my body aches all over…"
Standing up from the chair, I stretch my body.
Of course, it's all just to hide my embarrassment.
"You did a great job today. No, not just today, you've been giving it your all this entire week."
"The same goes for you, Setsuna… Wait, what?"
At that moment, I finally notice the warm coat draped over my shoulders.
It seems to be quite light, and I can see the red fabric even in this darkness. And no matter how I look at it, this really doesn't look like something a guy would wear.
"My mom brought it here for me. It's a change of clothes since I didn't go home yesterday."
"…I have a lot I need to apologize for."
I'm sorry for making you take care of me. I'm sorry for being the reason you needed a change of clothes to begin with…
…I'm sorry that you're obviously freezing in that stage outfit of yours given the time of day.
"Here, you can have it back. …I'm really sorry. This sort of thing really should be the guy's job, after all…"
"It's fine. Haruki-kun, you've already more than fulfilled your role as a guy, you know?"
As I return the coat, Setsuna turns her back to me and drops her guard.
Not having to ask the reason why, I gently put the coat over her shoulders.
"You gave me courage. On that grand stage, facing so many people… you gave me the courage to enjoy myself and sing there."
I was the one who was being encouraged, really.
All throughout that hopeless situation, which would have had no real consequences even if we'd chosen to give up…. And even as I continued pushing forward through it, driven only by my selfishness…

She had been the first to support me, and she'd put everything into dragging the second person to support me into our circle. Through it all, she always assumed the role of being the bright ray of sunshine among us.
…And those episodes of sulking and her moments of imperfection only served to fuel my sense of responsibility even more.
"The thought of having to sing in front of other people is really scary, but once you cross that line, nothing can really stop you."
With her back still turned to me, Setsuna recalls the whole experience while gazing up at the dark ceiling.
"Yes, even now I remember it vividly. Singing while illuminated by the bright spotlight…"
As if she could still see the spotlight shining upon her, she extends her hand through the darkness, shielding herself from its dazzling light.
"…Come to think of it, I didn't even wave to them!"
"Don't worry about something so trivial. I bet no one paid it any mind."
The girls were absolutely beautiful and captivating on that stage, after all.
There can be no doubt about itーand I'm saying that as someone who's had the exclusive, fortunate luxury of seeing it all as close as one can get.
"Aaah… I can still hear the cheering… I guess I won't be able to forget it for a while. If I close my eyes, it's like I'm still in that dream."
"Then how about we do it again? Me aside, I'm sure Touma and you could attract an even bigger crowd, Setsuna…"
I can see Touma just refusing the idea flat out, though…
"From now on… stay with me always, okay?"
"…As long as you want me to, Setsuna."
And just the same, Setsuna holds back from taking a stance on the idea as well.
Well, I suppose it's to be expected, since we've gone through just as much, if not more hardship for all the joy we've experienced.
"You'll be going to Houjou University, right? The liberal arts, right? Which department are you aiming for?"
"Eh? No, right now I'm thinking along the lines of public policy…"
"No, I'm pretty bad at English. Relatively, anyway."
"Well, I'm bad at politics and economics too. I know that for a fact."
"We don't need to forcibly enroll ourselves into the same department, right? If we enroll in the same university, we can meet every day, just like we do now."
"Sure, being able to meet every day is important, but the amount of hours we can see each other every day is just as important, isn't it?"
"There are a lot of core courses that we'd have to attend together in the first place. Why are you in such a rush to make a decision all of a sudden?"
"Rather than worrying about something so far ahead, we should focus on our promise first. Even after we start university, I want the three of us to do something together again. You, Touma and me…"
"Even after we've entered university… even once we're in our second year, and then our third year, and even if we're in different departments…"
She's different from the way she was rallying a full crowd just a few hours ago.
"And even if I happen to repeat a year, and become your underclassman, Haruki-kun…"
"If you just continue on the way you have so far, there's no way you would have to repeat a year…"
She's also different from the way she was singing full of confidence in the Touma household studio just a few days ago.
"Calm down. I'll turn on the light…"
If I had to say, I'd compare it to yesterday morning.
Setsuna now resembles the way she was when I took her away during my Class 3-A visit: hesitant and looking ever so little…
And much like she did back then… Setsuna grabs my hand that's reaching for the switch.
"Please, don't… I'll wake up from this dream if you do…"
They're connected. My right hand and Setsuna's left…
Intertwining each and every one of our fingers one by one, her soft hand wraps around mine.
"Today, I just want to keep on dreaming."
She looks like the Setsuna I saw yesterday, but she seems to be hiding something different deep down inside…
She takes my other, freely hanging hand as well.
"Of basking in the spotlight, taking in such fervent cheering, singing my favorite songs and enjoying myself from the bottom of my heart…"
They're connected now, too. My left hand, and Setsuna's right…
"And then… of everyone else loving it too."
Through the darkness… I can feel Setsuna's warm breath on me, and I can see a bit of light reflecting in her sparkling eyes.
"Of the person I love praising me… so I'd get carried away and ask for a reward…"
And now… I'm hearing hypothetical words that could sound incredibly ambiguous and misleading to the right person, hinting at a profession of love.
"Of that same person showing me just a bit of a wry smile, and then gently taking my spoiled self into his arms…"
"…Still, this is… a bit different from what I had in mind."
The coat that I'd put on her earlier delicately slips from Setsuna's shoulders.
And all because she moved, bringing our connected hands to her chest while resting her forehead on my chest.
"I have to admit that being the one to make the first move like this wasn't part of the plan at all."
Though it was brushing against my face up until a moment ago, the warm sensation of her breath is now caressing my chest.
"I was really hoping to be on the receiving end… so it might have come as a bit of a surprise. But since I'd been waiting for so long, I'd be happy anyway."
And though I can no longer see her sparkling eyes, it's the smell of Setsuna's hair that's now stimulating all of my senses.
"…Because it all felt like… such a beautifully convenient dream for me, you see."
It's not just her forehead, but her cheeks and ears are also buried into my chest… I imagine she can hear my heartbeat.
"But I guess I can't help myself… I just couldn't get over my crush, so it's all my own fault, right?"
Setsuna looks up at me once again.
But what's changed now is that slight difference in our height…
Her eyes and lips have risen to be level with mine.
The light from Setsuna's eyes disappears yet again, now hidden underneath her eyelids.
Was it not meant to be?
Can we not remain the way we are forever? Can the three of us not stay together?
If I'm the one who has to make the decision… If the whole burden of it must fall on my heart alone…
I'll decide it myself. I'll make my move. And I'll take on everything that comes after…
Even if I've only made it up to my late teens, I've always taken things into my own hands. That's how I've always lived my life up until now, and that's why I…
I willingly join my own lips with Setsuna's.
And Setsuna… has no real reason to resist.
Setsuna's lips are actually clinging to mine now.
They're so warm, soft, and smooth…
"So this is the sensation of a girl's lips" is what most guys would say in this kind of situation, but that's a far cry from what I'm experiencing.
It's an incredible sensation, where the slightest touch is more than enough to completely steal my heart away.
Breaths unconsciously spill from my mouth, and I can feel Setsuna's breath against my face as a result.
Just as I expected, warm, soft, and smooth breaths pour out from her equally warm, soft, and smooth lips.
An electric, numbing sensation assails my entire body.
As if every fiber of my being were tensed up in this moment, and all of my nerves were fixated on a single point.
And so we continue kissing each other lightly and awkwardly, yet passionately and intensely, feeling like countless seconds, or even years have passed by as we do so…
As my grip loosens on her, Setsuna's lips finally separate from mine.
…And then, I force myself onto Setsuna once more.
"Mmm… Mm, m… Mm, haa. Ah… Ahaha…"
Nevertheless, Setsuna lets out a smile in response to my forceful approach, with her lips still wet.
While I, on the other hand… I feel as if I could die in peace over the unimaginably pleasant sensation.
As November approached its end, it happened on a particular Saturdayーthe second day of the Houjou High School Festival.
It would be the day when the three of us had the most fun we'd ever had, and where we were also at our closest and our happiest.
The very last day the three of us could truly be together.
"Well, you didn't come to the school festival, so…"
It's right about the time when one should be feeling a sense of loneliness in the air following the Houjou High School Festival's closing ceremony ending without a hitch.
"…You barged in here just because of that?"
Having taken a train ride that spanned three stations, I arrived at a certain person's house and pressed the doorphone.
"I was worried, all right? You were out cold from your high fever up until just two days ago, after all."
"That was three days ago. I had mostly recovered by Thursday. A class representative like you really shouldn't make so many mistakes when it comes to trivialities."

"…Then allow me to fill you in on those trivialities. Starting from Thursday morning at 10 AM, measured in two-hour intervals, your temperature readings were the following, Touma: 38.8°C, 38.5°C, 38.5°C, 38.3°C…"
"…Well, I'm not a class rep, so there's no need for me to remember those."
"Anyway, aren't you going to let me in?"
"This is the home of a young girl living by herself, you know. Don't you have any common sense?"
"I've been inside every day for the past week, haven't I? Not to mention I even slept over too…"
"Don't say things like that while you're outside! What if weird rumors start spreading throughout the neighborhood!?"
Never mind the fact that the voice coming from the intercom is actually louder than mine…
"…And here I went through the trouble of coming to visit this late. At least have some common courtesy and treat me to some tea, would you?"
"No one would treat a sudden, uninvited guest to tea! When you put it like that, you make it sound like Japanese culture is all twisted."
Why has she been acting so distant since yesterday?
It should be impossible for her to know what's changed about me… yet.
"'Did something happen,' you ask… You mean to say that nothing happened with you, right?"
"You're the same as ever, right, Kitahara? You don't have any strange misunderstandings, no wrong impressions, and you're still as plain as you've ever been… is what I'm asking."
Honestly, I have no idea what Touma's trying to ask me.
I guess she's hoping that I've stayed the same as I've always been. That I haven't changed even after that special day…
"I'll make you some tea, but after that… just go home, okay?"
I have no idea how she interpreted my reply, but for now, I'm just glad she's finally opened the proverbial Heavenly Rock Cave.
"That's the sixth spoonful of sugar, you know?"
I'm pretty sure it used to be five spoonfuls before. Not that much of a change, in any case.
Hold on, this is too thin…
I don't mean to sound clever, but frankly, this is just plain steaming hot black water…
"Why are you here… Why did you come over to my place so soon after yesterday?"
"I told you before, I was worried your cold might have returned."
"Well, now you know for sure, right? I'm perfectly healthy, so hurry up and go home."
"I need to talk to you about something."
"…! You said that you'd only have tea, didn't you? That's cheating!"
"Well, I did say that, but… come on, let's just stop this pointless argument."
It's different from the way we'd trade mutual insults while still being able to slowly but surely grasp the other's intentions regardless, up until last night.
Is it… because I've changed…? But there's just no way, right?
I'm doing everything I can not to be self-conscious about it, after all.
Even if things turn awkward between us later because of this, that really shouldn't be the case right now.
"Well, wait… Before you start talking, I just need to ask you one thing…"
Perhaps, and in a number of ways, she regrets and feels cornered by how open she was with me before.
"I'm pretty sure this is not the case, but… you're not the type to tell lies and tease others on purpose in order to gauge their reaction, right?"
"…Why aren't you answering? Are you really that kind of guy after all, Kitahara? Then… the real reason why you're here today must be…"
"Ah, no… I hope I never become that kind of person."
It's true that I'm hesitating on giving an answer, but it's not because it was right on the mark.
"Always being sincere to others, without telling lies and hiding any secrets is my ideal… Are you okay with that answer?"
It's just that I couldn't figure out what Touma's intentions are or what she's trying to ask, so I was trying to think up a generic enough response.
"Touma, you… said you needed to ask me 'one thing'…"
"That's your fault for not giving me the kind of answer I wanted!"
"My answer was perfectly fine, wasn't it!? It's your question that was flawed!"
"…Even so, please answer another question for me."
It seems like this time, both of us have realized that this argument is pointless.
"Your reason for… coming here today, Kitahara… Is there something that you want to tell me? Or perhaps… you have something you want to ask me?"
"…It's about me. I want you to hear me out, Touma."
This is my own decision. That means I'm not here because I want to hear Touma's opinion.
Rather, nothing will change if I hear her opinion. I can't let my current feelings be swayed by anything other than my own will right now.
"Fine then. Feel free to say whatever you want to. I'll listen to it if I feel like it."
"That attitude of yours isn't making things easier for me…"
I don't know what Touma was afraid I was going to ask her, but it looks like she's not worried about it anymore; she's visibly completely relaxed.
…Even though I'm still so nervous. Contrary to my words, I've been tense for a while now.
…Well, I perfected my poker-face a long time ago, so there's no need to worry.
"By the way, how was the school festival today? It's the last day, right?"
Not to mention, even after telling me to say whatever I want, she starts up the conversation again…
"I swung by the classroom in the morning, then from afternoon, I just kind of strolled around campus. I even participated in the evening festival."
"I swear, I'm amazed you can even enjoy that infantile festival."
"Is that what someone who was totally fired up yesterday should be saying?"
"…There was an announcement for Miss Houjou at the festival's closing ceremony."
"I bet Ogiso won by a landslide anyway, right? Ever since we enrolled, she's been uncontested."
Chikashi brought up the topic of how much of a lead Setsuna would have over the other contestants. She completely dominated the ranking, just as he predicted.
Out of all the valid votes, 683 in total, 402 went to her. With a majority of over 60%, Setsuna won spectacularly for the third time in a row, uncontested.
…After hearing the announcement, Setsuna smiled wryly, unable to hold it in.
"The most interesting thing about this year's election were definitely the invalid votes."
"Oh? Since her victory was already assured, a bunch of people decided to just mess around with it, huh?"
"The votes were for… 'The keyboardist girl from day two', 'The third-year saxophonist girl', 'The girl that was in Ogiso Setsuna's band'…"
"…'The girl who played a bunch of instruments', 'The bassist with straight, long hair', 'The girl who played White Album in a black outfit'…"
"There were a total of 59 of those invalid votes. If they had been valid, it would have been enough for fifth place."
Chikashi told me after the official announcement.

Since there were no actual check marks on the voting slips, everyone came up with a unique way to vote. It caused some trouble for the people who had to count the votes, but it was great fun at the same time.
"…That has nothing to do with me!"
"With this, your greatness will be well-known within the school. My ambitions have been fulfilled."
"I said I don't care about it at all. You can celebrate it yourself…"
Not caring if Touma wants me to or not…
"Yeah… Let me do just that. Here, cheers."
As I say that, I lift my cup and finish off the tasteless, cooled-down, and now-barely-drinkable liquid as if it were a fine wine.
Touma… doesn't join me, of course.
"If you've recovered, you should have come, Touma. Setsuna and I called you a bunch of times, you know?"
"I'd prefer not to be in the middle of such an awkward atmosphere."
As I put my cup down, as if timing it intentionally, she takes her own cup and tilts it.
"And if I'd joined in, I would have just been a bother."
And she continues to tilt her cup, waiting for the thick sugar on the bottom to come together…
"I mean, you were with Ogiso, right?"
"Yeah… We went to check out the university festival together in the afternoon."
I can't read Touma's expression, hidden behind the cup.
"You ate takoyaki… and candy apples together, right?"
"Well… we had crepes and ramen, too…"
I can only see her shoulders shuddering every now and then.
"Did you dance with her… by the bonfire?"
That's how I know that she's carefully listening to me.
"Then, after parting with a kiss, you came here, did you?"
And right now, as I nod to reply to the person right in front of me…
Touma came into my view before I knew it.
That took so long… The lead-up took too long to get through.
"And Setsuna… I still can't believe it, but she gave me the okay."
Even though it was awfully hard to say, and even though I'm still feeling awfully unpleasant.
