Not to mention it's annoying to have you pointing out things I'm well aware of.
"It doesn't bother me. I'm actually thinking that it's good that I didn't place."
As Setsuna rubs her eyes, Touma reaches across the table and starts sincerely and gently stroking her hair.
…The fact that it looks terribly similar to what I usually do with Setsuna likely means that anyone would want to do that to her once.
"How come? Even though you tried so hard… you weren't rewarded…"
"…You don't sound like it's not bothering you in the least, though."
"No, I'm not talking about not placing. What I mean is, I… it doesn't feel right for me to be this relieved."
"Never knowing when to let things go, always brooding on the past… and having such a grim personality that just won't let me move on…"
"…Let's forget I said anything just now."
"I really have no idea what you're talking about."
What confuses me the most is Touma putting her head down and self-deprecatingly talking about herself like this, something I've never seen her do before.
Then, still acting so unlike her usual self, Touma looks up at me and gives me a look of sincere relief with a shy smile.
"Well, whatever. There's always next time. I can just try again, so I'm not all that disappointed."
"I've realized that I have talent in piano. After all, making the finals after messing around for two years must be proof that I'm a genius."
"It doesn't come close to your talent in bragging about yourself, though."
"It was fun, after all… Impressing someone with my music."
"I wouldn't be surprised if it started snowing."
We held an impromptu consolation party together in a family restaurant until it was late at night.
When we finally decided to call it a day and came out, we were met by a dark sky and chilly winds.
"All right, I'm heading this way. Kitahara, take care of Setsuna… Please keep her safe from those evil hands of yours, okay?"
In this cold air, chilly enough to freeze both body and soul, Touma was entirely like her regular self.
"Will you be coming to school again from tomorrow on?"
"I guess I will… since I don't have a good reason to skip anymore."
As she says that, she brings both of her hands to her lips and lets out a white puff of breath through them.
"That's great… That means the three of us will be together again starting tomorrow."
Through her demeanor and speech, along with the lonely atmosphere she's brought about recently, Touma looks like she's drawing a line…
"Yeah, thanks. Let's get along until graduation, Kazusa."
"…There, you heard her. I hope we'll get along until graduation, Kitahara."
"Don't ignore me like you did last month. It was pretty hard on me too, okay?"
Even the ambiguity in her behavior, where I can't tell if she's being serious or merely teasing me, feels pleasant in comparison.
This new side of her is enough to throw me off balance once more.
Is she cutting us off again? Was I wrong in thinking that she had opened up to begin with?
I can't read that girl. I've known that all along… but she's too much for me to handle.
"Hey, it's me. Yeah, it's over. Now? I had dinner and now I'm on my way home."
"And about the results… Yeah, turns out the two-year gap was too much, after all."
"It was not good at all. Just like you said. I still have a long way to go."
"Well, nothing we can do now. It's all my fault. I'm not sure if it's too late to start now, but I'll work hard for another year, and then next year I'll… Huh?"
"W-Wait… hold on… I… I failed, you know? I didn't live up to your expectations, right?"
"So what do you… what do you mean?"
"'A prodigy at the age of ten, talented at fifteen, and a normal person after twenty.' Or so they say, anyway…"
"You're much rougher than you used to be before. It's like you've gone back to being a diamond in the rough."
"Are you suggesting that… I've gone sloppy?"
"If you want to put it like that, then sure… But you're still better than me when I was young. That's something I don't like admitting, even if you're my daughter."
"I'm saying that you haven't gotten any better, but your potential has increased dramatically."
"What are you trying to say, exactly?"
"Do you happen to know of an old guy by the name Martin Flugel? He's something of a veteran in our field."
"I've heard he's been saying some nonsense like he won't accept more than two students a year anymore. He's getting on in years, I guess."
"Well, he's over 70 now, isn't he? It's amazing that he's still an active professional in itself."
"He has an audition starting next week. Wanna go?"
"What do you mean, 'go'…? You're not saying…"
"Of course, it will be in Vienna. I don't think that guy could survive a plane ride at his age."
"Since you haven't been overseas recently, I can accompany you to start you off, so what do you say?"
"Will you give up after all? I don't mind if you want to play around in Japan for another year."
"Well, think it over. Keep in mind though, the flight is booked for the day after tomorrow, so you've only got a day to spare."
"If you find it difficult to decide now, it might be better to turn it down this time. This will change your whole life, after all."
"Anyway, I'm going to head on home today, so let's talk about this more later. I'll see you…"
"Alright, that's it for homeroom. It seems that the flu is going around, so don't forget to take preventive measures, everyone!"
"Nothing, I just wanted to ask you to go out with us right now if you're free. We're going to celebrate the current executive committee members stepping down."
"Ah, sorry. I have something to do today."
"…It's Ogiso, isn't it. Sorry, that was actually really tactless of me, wasn't it?"
"No, when I said something to do, I didn't mean it that way…"
I actually can't think of a rebuttal since he pretty much has a grasp on the situation already.
"Still, if that's the case, Haruki, then wasn't what you did earlier even more tactless?"
"What do you mean… what I did earlier?"
"I'm talking about the person who sits next to you."
"I thought you were ignoring her since New Year's, but you've been constantly throwing glances at her seat ever since she stopped coming to class."
"If you know she's not coming, then stop looking that way hundreds of times over. And stop sighing whenever you do, as well. You were the one who said that happiness slips away if we don't grasp it."
"That's all I wanted to say. See you."
That was an utterly unremarkable scene of a Wednesday after school.

Ever since February arrived, students have been conspicuously missing classes due to their university entrance exams and job interviews. With it being the flu season on top of that, the amount of people in class has been reduced to around half of what it usually is…
Since I was only worrying about a single person among more than twenty absentees, it's only natural that a certain classmate of mine would react like that.
"…There, you heard her. I hope we'll get along until graduation, Kitahara."
"Don't ignore me like you did last month. It was pretty hard on me too, okay?"
"After saying something like that… What are you expecting me to do?"
You're the one who told me not to ignore you three days ago, right? You're the one who said we should get along until graduation, right?
Then why aren't you showing up?
How much longer are you going to keep confusing me until you're satisfied, Touma…?
"Yeah, she said she went to see a new teacher who will be teaching her starting in April."
"She said that he's a very famous and strict teacher, and that he only takes in two students a year. That's why his exams take several days, apparently."
"She said she didn't know, either. It could be done this week or it could last the entirety of February."
"She has already started moving toward her next goal. Kazusa… she's really looking ahead…"
Touma's reason for not attending school becomes instantly clear.
"Yeah, yesterday. I had left a message on her answering machine telling her to call me back."
If that's the case, then why hasn't she responded even once to my numerous calls since Monday?
Why haven't I received even a single reply from her regardless of how many texts I've sent her asking, "Are you alive?" since Monday?
It's hardly been any time at all since she told me "Don't ignore me," but now she's the one ignoring me…
"A little. Could she have forgotten about your birthday already?"
"At the competition, she promised that she would definitely attend the party. Did she mention that at all?"
"It's fine. This is an important time for Kazusa, is it not?"
That's right. It is an important time.
Even I understand that this is an important exam for Touma, one that could not only affect this one year, but also determine the course of her entire life.
…And yet for something seemingly so important to her, she didn't even bother to let me know, now, did she?
Is this the extent of what I mean to her?
"For now, let's support Kazusa as she tackles her new challenge. I can hold my birthday party any time, and it's not like it's set in stone that she's not coming…"
"Your birthday… how about we celebrate it with just the two of us?"
"The 14th is a weekday, so let's move it up a little and say, make a reservation at a restaurant this Saturday?"
"Of course, we can go to karaoke as well. I'll hang out with you for however long you want."
"We can have a party with the three of us again some other time. But I want to celebrate it with just the two of us for now."
For now, I want to cherish this person in front of my eyes… I want to cherish Ogiso Setsuna.
After all, it's only natural for one to cherish the person that's the most important to them.
"I'm not saying… I'm against it… but…"
"Ah, um… sorry. I guess I made quite the unreasonable request."
"Um… forgive me for making such a hasty and forceful proposal, but could you at least take it into consideration?"
"Aren't you just saying the same thing, but in a more polite manner…?"
As I thought, I couldn't keep that uncharacteristic burst of forcefulness and proactiveness up for very long.
However, just this one time, I have no intention of backing down.
"This is the first special occasion since we've met, so… I want to spend that time together with you, Setsuna."
After all… if I don't settle this soon, I don't think I'll be able to stay sincere to Setsuna.
So if I could meet with Setsuna alone this weekend…
"Let me… think about it for a while."
I am going to confess to Setsuna. I am going to tell her everything honestly.
I'm going to tell her that my heart is losing its direction. That I'm feeling captivated by Touma, even if only slightly.
That I am deeply attracted to Setsuna despite that. That I want my heart to truly find its proper direction.
That Setsuna… is the one I want.
"I think it'd be best… if we all celebrated it together, okay?"
It turns out my overwhelmingly passionate offer didn't even last through the same night before being rejected.
"How about Saturday at 5 o'clock, my place? My family, Kazusa, Haruki-kun… I'd really like to celebrate it with everyone."
"I'll send Kazusa a text as well… Although I'm not sure if she will come or not."
"Haruki-kun, I bet you were thinking about taking me to an expensive place or something, right? It's too early for us to be doing something like that."
It might sound like she's concerned about the cost, but I can't help but think she's hinting at something else.
"And I'm sorry, okay? I know I'm being selfish again."
I'm not sure if Setsuna understands that I'm at the end of my rope, but she seems to want to maintain our current distance either way.
"Why are you apologizing, Setsuna? If anything, I am the one who should."
"No, I'm sorry. I'm really happy about your offer, but…"
The relationship between the two of us. The relationship between the three of us. She merely wants to cherish both.
It's as if she is gently whispering, "There's no need to rush things."
"If you keep apologizing, I'll get down on my knees and apologize, okay?"
"Saturday it is, then… I'll be looking forward to it."
"Okay, I'll make a lot of delicious food and wait for you guys. So I'll get my hopes up just a little for your present, okay?"
"I'll put all the money I was originally going to pay for the dinner toward it, so I'd say you can get your hopes up quite a bit."
"Hey, come on! Don't waste your money like that!"
"It's not a waste, if you ask me."
"Oh jeez… If you keep saying that, I'm really going to get my hopes up, okay?"
If she's so sure she wants it this way, I have no choice but to go along with it.
Even if doing so might leave my heart with just the slightest bit of unrest.
"Don't rush… Listen to yourself and just don't rush this."
"It's me. Mom told me to borrow your travel bag."
"I put it out there, so take it. I also put a scarf inside it."
"Got it. I can take all of this, right?"
"I'll be expecting souvenirs. White chocolate, ramen, king crabs…"
"Don't be so selfish. You decided on your own to drop out of this trip."
"Not to mention you're the one who said you wanted to see the winter festival to begin with. I wanted to go to Okinawa."
"Although it's for both of our graduations, I'm the one who's celebrating her birthday, so it's only natural that my opinion would be favored, right?"
"That's right, and this is supposed to be a present for you, Nee-chan. So what are you thinking, dropping out yourself?"
"…Come on, I've been apologizing about that over and over, haven't I?"
"Since you said that you were going to gather your classmates to have a party for the first time in three years, we gave up… Still, dad felt really down, y'know?"
"…I'll be a good daughter when you guys come back. You can help me out with that too, Takahiro."
"Oh, hey, is that girl coming to the party too? You know, the keyboardist?"
"Kazusa? Well, I did invite her, but…"
"…Maybe I should skip out on Hokkaido as well."
"Don't be silly and get out with the things you need already. I need to go take a bath soon."
"Are you really inviting all your classmates? Could it be that you actually only invited one person?"
"It's just a coincidence that they're going on a trip without me… and that there's nobody else in the house but me, okay?"
"If you don't show up… I don't know what will happen between us, okay?"
"Because… I don't think I'd be against it at all."
"Here, please go ahead and check the engraving."
"Very well, I'll go ahead and wrap it. Please wait a moment."
As soon as the salesperson leaves, I start to feel hot and feel beads of sweat forming on my brow.
Maybe it's because the heater is set too high, or maybe it's due to the fact that I'm still not used to this type of shop… Or perhaps I've finally fallen prey to the flu.
It's because the thing she just made me check is a silver ring with "Setsuna" engraved on the inside.
…I feel like I've really done it now. It's an embarrassingly overbearing birthday present that I am absolutely not allowed to hesitate with for even a moment.
"I'll take this one, please," I said. "Please engrave a name on it," I said. I want to point and laugh at myself for saying that two days ago.
I'm sure Setsuna will accept it with a smile and feel happy about it.
At the moment, I'm feeling overconfident about that one thing.
Exposing myself to the cold wind, I realize that the cold sweat earlier really was from the heating inside.
…Talking about cold sweat might make one think otherwise, but I don't think I'd be wrong in saying that today might be the coldest day of the year.
Picking up the present didn't take as much time as I had anticipated… Then again, I left my house undeniably early to begin with, leaving more than two hours left until the meeting time.
Since I don't have the audacity to go window shopping in this busy commercial district on Valentine's Day by myself, I start heading over to the station.
…While thinking about possibly having to keep Setsuna's family company until the preparations for the party are done.
"For the bra… Would front hook or back hook be easier to undo?"
"…I guess it's still way too early."
Even after checking my watch over and over, there's still more than two hours left.
Suetsugu-chou is only three stations away. Even if I slowly walk from there, there would still be more than an hour and a half left.
"The next station is Iwazu-chou, Iwazu-chou. The exit is on the left side."
My feelings sway a little, and I know that it's because of the name of the station I'm passing by now.
"For now, let's support Kazusa as she tackles her new challenge. I can hold my birthday party any time, and it's not like it's set in stone that she's not coming…"
A certain bad-tempered friend of mine lives in this neighborhood, the one who let me down after making me get my hopes up.
"Iwazu-chou, Iwazu-chou. Please mind the door when exiting."
"I'll send Kazusa a text as well… Although I'm not sure if she will come or not."
I wonder if she's seen Setsuna's text? Would she consider giving a little bit of her time for this? Above all, would she even be home right now?
…Would she be weighing the exam against her friendship right now?
"I'd really like to celebrate it with everyone."
"The doors are closing. Please be careful."
I don't want Setsuna to be lonely. I want her to genuinely smile.
Because Setsuna wants the three of us to stay together.
"I won't let her skip out on this."
There's enough time for me to go to that idiot's house, get into a big fight with her, and drag her out of there.
"It's about time to prepare the fruits and whipped cream… There's still more to cook too, I wonder if I'll make it in time?"
"Could 24 cm be a bit too much? There's no way we can finish this…"
"Well, it's fine. We can eat it tomorrow, no problem."
…And so I ended up here on the spur of the moment.
If I think about it rationally, the best decision would probably be not to bother Touma while her exam is in progress, just like Setsuna said.
She might be taking a nap right about now, completely exhausted after doing some intense training in the basement.
Or maybe her teacher is not even allowing her to go home, and is subjecting her to strict lessons every day.
The more I think about it, the more I realize how stubborn I am and how justified Touma's actions are.
It's merely revealing that in using, "For Setsuna's sake" as an excuse, I am trying to justify my frustration because, "She didn't contact me."
Realizing this as I continue to press the button on the intercom, I start to feel like I'm the dumbest person alive on the planet right now.
Above all, I should have confirmed with Setsuna first before trying to barge in uninvited like this…
As I keep backing myself into a corner, I hear an unfamiliar voice.
"Um… this is the Touma residence, right?"
The gender is right, sure, but it's not Touma's voice. The helper, Shibata-san, whom I met last time, didn't have a voice this deep either…
"…Would you leave if I told you it's not?"
"I've checked the nameplate! This is definitely the Touma residence!"
…But her personality… seems to be fairly similar to Touma's.
"Uh, excuse me. I'm… my name is Kitahara. Is Tou… I mean, i-is Kazusa-san in?"
…Why am I getting so nervous over just saying her name?
"Um, I'm a classmate of hers. And who am…"
"Sorry, but could you face toward the camera?"
She completely interrupts my question, "And who am I speaking to?".
She seems like a self-centered person. Yup, she's quite similar to Touma…
Similar to… Touma… Wait, so in other words, she's…
"I knew I'd seen you somewhere before… You're Guitar-kun!"
And now… an unbelievable turn of events is unfolding before me.
The person who showed me inside was neither Touma nor the helper.
Wait, there's something wrong with the way I said that. She's not Touma, but she is a Touma.
What I'm trying to say is…
"You're a pretty plain one after all."
"I'm… sorry for failing to meet your expectations."
"Huh? Ahaha, I didn't mean anything bad by that, okay? I was just thinking that you look like an earnest, normal boy. Someone who lives in a different world from my daughter."
"Is that so…? You didn't mean anything bad, huh…"
The person before me is no doubt Touma Youko. The person I'd seen in some commercial ten years ago.
"Anyway, go ahead and drink up. The tea will get cold if you don't."
"Ah, of course. Thank you fo… Pffp!?"
"But it's hot right now. Be careful."
She's undoubtedly of the Touma bloodline.
This tea might as well be water with way too much sugar thrown in, and that's proof enough.
"…No matter how much you look, I'm gonna stay plain, okay?"
"That's not to say you don't have any unique features. As proof of that, I could remember you after seeing your face."
"…Speaking of which, how do you know me? Did you happen to see the recording of our school festival or something?"
"…Looks like you don't remember me. Maybe my own face isn't all that memorable."
"Thanks for the help back then. It was my first time visiting Houjou High… Even though it's a place my daughter has been attending for three years."
"Like I said, I'm not on the commit…!?"
"Could you tell me where the gymnasium is? This is my first time here."
"R-Right this way! I'll take you there."
"I was really surprised. The kind committee member who had just showed me the way was playing the guitar right next to my daughter!"
I do have complaints about being mistaken for a committee member when that was the first time she had ever met me, but that's not the main issue right now.
"Shibata-san contacted me, you see… She said that Kazusa was going to play in the school festival."
Touma Youko came to Houjou High's school festival. …To watch her own daughter's performance.
What's more, she came back all the way from Europe.
"I was sure she'd be playing the piano, so I was really surprised. About how it was a band, and how she was playing the saxophone, the bass, all of it."
"That was… because of my unreasonable requests."
"Even then, heh… it was interesting. The singer had a nice voice, too… The song repertoire wasn't really to my taste, though."
I'll take her lack of comments about the guitar as an act of pity.
"There was nothing particularly outstanding about her performance in itself… Though more importantly, it was quite the treat to see."
"Seeing Kazusa enjoying her performance so much…
Hmm, I wonder? When was the last time I'd seen it?"
I had jumped to a very wrong conclusion…
I thought that if I ever happened to meet this person, I wouldn't be able to help but say something rude to her.
I'd ask her why she abandoned Touma and left her here in Japan…

I'd confront her about how Touma's actually a good person who easily gets lonely despite her tendencies, and how she'd made her daughter so sad and twisted that she almost drove her to give up on the piano she loved so much.
I'd imagined myself rationally pointing out her faults as a parent and denying her an escape for her selfish behavior…
Yet… the person in front of me right now…
Doesn't give me the impression of the person Touma only referred to as "that person" at all.
"Why did you come to our house?"
"As I said earlier, I have some business with Touma…"
"Why did you come to meet Kazusa now?"
"That's… because we have a party scheduled today."
Is there a meaning behind her emphasizing "now"?
"…She'll be coming back today. I think it'll be around 6 o'clock?"
It's an hour late, but that shouldn't be a problem. It looks like we can celebrate Setsuna's birthday together, after all.
That's a relief… We'll be able to see Setsuna's smiling face.
"She was over there until yesterday. The exam was a little difficult."
"I've heard about it as well, that it was to learn from a famous piano instructor… So, is it over now?"
"It looks like she got held up a bit. She told me over the phone last night that she would be coming back soon."
"Yes, although it was quite a struggle. I had to come back by myself first due to circumstances."
"Of course! How could I not be happy?"
"…Is that so. I guess that's about as far as that goes, huh."
She's certainly relieved about the fact that her daughter passed the exam.

It's hard to sense even a bit of her supposed eccentric personality that the media and her daughter gave me the impression of her having. When I think about it, it makes perfect sense that she's acting like a nice, normal lady right now since she's happy about the good news.
"Well, you said that you're taking her to a party, right? When is it starting?"
"She won't make it then. I'm sorry, but you'll have to tell the others she can't be there."
"Ah, but being an hour or so late won't be a problem…"
"Her arrival time at the airport is at 6 o'clock,
and it will take quite a while for her to get here, no?"
"…Where is she supposed to be arriving?"
"Could it be that… you really haven't heard anything from her?"
Why is she looking at me with such a complicated glint in her eyes…?
"Where are you now? Are you alright?"
"I'm on my way… I'll be a little late. Go ahead and start without me."
Seeing as I usually get to my appointments 30 minutes beforehand, I'm basically calling her an hour late.
"…Could it be that you're not feeling well? You sound like you're in pain."
"Maybe… Somehow, I don't… feel so well…"
…The moment I utter those words, an increasingly intense wave of nausea washes over me.
Because I'm doing the one thing that I have detested the most until now.
"A cold? Did you catch the flu? You should be in bed, then!"
"It's fine… I don't have a fever, at least. I can make it."
I'm lying to her at this very moment.
"No, don't push yourself. We can reschedule the party anytime…"
"I'll be late, but… I'll definitely be there. Even if it's after the party has ended, I'll at least show up."
I might not be showing up alone, though. Considering the time now, we'll be at least two hours late.
…Hiding such a crucial piece of information immediately gives me a splitting headache.
"We can do it another day, okay…? Just with the two of us, like you wanted."
"My actual birthday isn't until a bit later, though, is it?"
"I have to see you today. If it's not today, I…"
My heart might drift away to somewhere else.
"…It's nothing. I just feel a little lonely, that's all."
"Sorry. For being late, and being so selfish on top of that."
"But please don't overdo it. If I happen to see you looking really ill, I'm just going to make you sleep instead of letting you join the party, okay?"
"I'll definitely be there… Please start the party with everyone else and apologize for me."
"I got it. I'll deliver the message."
"Ah, and by the way… is Touma there, by any chance?"
"No, she hasn't even contacted me. She must be busy, after all."
My entire body is drenched in cold sweat from how unbearably disgusting I feel.
I added a lie on top of another lie to cover up what I'm about to do.
I've crossed the line and am doing the worst thing I possibly could…
And to the most precious person in my life, of all people.
"Thank you for using our service. We are approaching the terminus, Narita Airport Terminal 1. The exit doors are to the right. We will be arriving on time. Please be careful when exiting."
My only saving grace… is that Setsuna is not by herself right now.
That even if I'm not there, her family will help dampen her loneliness.
"'Start the party with everyone else,'… huh?"
"If I do that, I'll get fat… Haruki-kun."
It was fairly easy to find the arrival gate.
The arrival time, the airline company, the departure airport… Touma Youko told me everything.
"I'm here to take you to Setsuna's birthday party."
Although I know what Touma is really asking, I deliberately only tell her what I want to say.
"I'll carry your bags. Come on, let's go."
Without even trying to argue with me, Touma lowers her head and awkwardly mutters to herself.
By the time Touma spoke again, it had already been a while since we'd gotten on the train.
All the while, Touma kept throwing uncertain glances my way, as if something was making her feel awkward.
"She was a lot nicer and more normal than I had thought she'd be. It was quite a relief, but also a bit anticlimactic."
When she said, "I'm pretty nervous since it's the first time I'm talking to my daughter's boyfriend," I thought she was teasing me for a moment.
"I've also only recently realized that my mom's that sort of a person, myself."
On the day of the school festival, Touma's mother returned to Japan just to hear her daughter's performance.
Not for a competition or a concert, but for a mere sideshow like that.
"She has aged too, after all. She doesn't have the power to turn everyone around her against herself anymore."
"Is that so? I think that she still looks freakishly young."
Even though she didn't tell me in detail about what happened between her and her daughter…
It looks like they've resolved their misunderstandings and reformed their bond somewhat.
"It's silly that I'd been hating my mom despite who she really is. The truth is, I've realized that I was just a daughter who made some very wrong assumptions."
…Although I never managed to understand what she meant by those enigmatic words, "Maybe it's thanks to you, Guitar-kun?".
"So…? What did you hear from my mom?"
"I heard that your new teacher has been decided…"
"Aah, that? It was really difficult, yeah."
Something that the both of us have been meaning to confirm, but were unable to due to our fear.
"He made me play the same piece over and over, and if he didn't like even a single part, he made me repeat it all from the top."
"If he wanted to flunk me, he could have done so quickly, but he just kept telling me to come back again the next day over and over. Ultimately, it took a whole week for him to come to a decision."
"I see… that must have been really hard on you. Well done."
"Aah～ I don't feel like doing anything today. I'll go home, take a hot shower and then head straight to bed."
"…Unfortunately, I can't let you do that, Touma."
"Because you're coming along to Setsuna's birthday party with me."
"Listen, I just said I'm tired. Besides, Setsuna only needs you there…"
"Once you get there, you will tell her straight. That you're going to be living with your mother… That you'll be moving to Europe next month."
However, I have no choice but to confirm it.
Touma falls silent… wordlessly confirming my statement.
Apparently, it was originally Touma Youko's proposal.
With Touma's graduation and her mother's change in her base of activity…
Both of them would be living in Austria together.

For that reason, her mother has been looking for a new house in Austria, and making new arrangements for Touma's training. With the aim of reintroducing the strict and rigorous education for her daughter that she'd once given up on.
I pointed out sincerely to Touma Youko… that doing all this after three years of neglect is too sudden.
However, she admitted the fact that she'd abandoned Touma, and also acknowledged Touma's current talent.
"I'm taking a taxi home. Let's part ways here."
"No, you're not. We have to go see Setsuna together."
"I told you that I'm tired, didn't I?"
"Call her, then. Tell her yourself, Touma."
But above all, what came as the biggest shock was that Touma agreed to her mother's proposal willingly.
Even though her mother gave her the right to refuse, she never used that right.
"There's nothing we can do about you going to Europe… No, if anything, I think it's a good decision for your career and your family."
"Yeah… I'll finally get to live with my mom."
"Right, I think that's… a good thing."
She should be genuinely happy to say that, but when she mutters it and strides at a pace that makes it seem as if she's running away from me, I frankly find myself unable to accept it.
"But you'll be breaking our promise, so you have to explain it to Setsuna. I won't allow you to leave without saying a word."
"Eventually is not good enough. Tell her now!"
Perhaps realizing that I won't stop no matter how fast she walks or even runs, Touma gradually slows down.
"Give me a break already. Telling her right now takes a lot of determination."
When she finally looks back at me, as if having given up…
Touma shows an expression that I had never seen before… Maybe it's wrong to describe it as such, but it's a very subservient smile.
"Kitahara, you know Setsuna well, don't you? You know that this is sure to make her cry, right?"
"Of course it is. You're breaking our promise, after all. The promise that the three of us would stay together forever."
My irritation only grows as she continues to smile in that way.
"No, that's wrong. We made a promise that couldn't be kept to begin with…"
"In that case… don't put the blame on me like this."
"I'm not blaming you. I'm just asking you to be honest with her. I'm just… telling you not to lie… that's all."
"I will, I will tell her… I'm just asking you to wait for today."
Who is the lowly liar here, spewing words that apply far more to himself?

"I never expected to be found out right after returning. I was going to spend about a week trying to come up with some exc… No, I mean, I was going to take some time to find the right words to say, and then do it."
I really can't believe this. Am I out of my mind right now?
"I was hoping that you two could hear me out calmly. If I said it now, we would probably end up arguing. So please, give me some time to sort this out."
"Setsuna hasn't realized it yet, right? Then it's fine, isn't it?"
Is Touma out of her mind right now…?
"So, please, Kitahara. I'm begging you. Let's not tell her today, okay? Not me, and not you either."
Why is she acting so subservient and undignified, and making excuses left and right with that faint smile…
"Be by her side… for her birthday party. Just let me… distance myself for a while."
This… This is… not Touma Kazusa.
"Well then… I'll be going home now."
Touma leans toward the road and raises her hand.
A taxi notices her immediately, stops in front of us, and opens its door.
Lastly, with a face on the verge of tears, she looks my way and apologizes.
But while that apology seems to be directed at me, she's only really concerned about Setsuna.
As Touma tries to get in, I…
I grab her raised right hand and forcefully pull her back to the sidewalk.
"I'm sorry. She's had a bit too much to drink… Please just go on ahead."
Overtly displeased, the taxi driver clicks his tongue and quickly drives off.
I stand there bowing my head and keeping my eyes on the taxi until it fades out of sight.
Naturally, Touma now stands next to me, with her right wrist still in hand. And her expression has changed drastically.
From a tearful smile to perplexed anger.
"That's what I should be asking you…"
But that expression of anger is proof that I've finally cut off all of her escape routes.
And so, in the next moment, as I raise my head, I glare directly at Touma's face.
"Why…? Why are you trying to leave me!?"
And… if there are things one should and should not say according to common sense, the thing I just said definitely belongs in the latter category.
At last, I've come face to face with my true feelings.
"Why didn't you consult me even once about this!? Why, why…!? Touma!"
I didn't lash out at her over the fact that she lied to Setsuna, but the fact that she tried to leave me.
"Is that all I mean to you? Is that all I've ever meant to you!?"
Not only is she trying to leave me, but in acting so utterly uncharacteristically of herself, Touma is thoroughly crushing even my memories of her, and I couldn't forgive that.
Touma's confusion and anger quickly subsides.
The more and more heated I become, the more blank and cold her own face becomes in contrast. It feels like everything that's led to this point could be frozen and reduced to nothing.
I can feel myself becoming increasingly pale as well.
All the powerful emotions I just poured out are losing their momentum and are leading to a letdown.
"Ah, what a mess. Now I've done it. It's all over"… These cold thoughts of mine are transforming into cold sweat and crawling down my back.
Hearing those words, I sense the metallic taste of blood spreading throughout my mouth.
"That's all you mean to me, and that's why I didn't tell you anything."
I have gone so numb already that I can't even feel the pain that should come after.
"About going overseas, about us going our separate ways, and about how I felt… I didn't tell you anything… That's all you mean to me."
"What friends? How could I ever be friends with someone I can't even tell all the things I want to?"
My eyes that were glaring at Touma until just now are now focused on a point on the road.
Ridiculed and crushed by Touma's sneering words, my aimless feelings have now truly lost any place to go to and are about to flow out through my eyes.
"Ahh, this is getting ridiculous… Why do I have to stand here and smile while looking like I'm making excuses?"
"And the whole, 'Why are you trying to leave me'…? How can you say something like that with a straight face? Kitahara, who the hell do you think you are?"
My stupid misunderstanding is going to make stains around my feet.
After being ripped to shreds by someone who's not even a friend, but a mere acquaintance.
That's not something I want to hear from my best friend's boyfriend!"
"Weren't you the one who left me first!? Weren't you the one who went to a place beyond my reach first!?"
As I raise my eyes once again…
I see the things I almost shed, now flowing down without end.
Unbelievably enough, from Touma's own eyes.
"Always keeping me at arm's length, but never letting me reach you. Wasn't that torture your idea!?"
I truly believe that no one in this world would be able to joke around with words and a bearing like that.
"So why… why am I the one taking all the blame…?"
The words spilling out from her trembling lips and the emotions engulfing her distorted face align perfectly as Touma screams them out.
"Every day, every single day… watching you, and having my heart shredded to pieces… And now that's somehow all my fault…? You're awful…"
As usual, my mouth denies Touma's words.
"But Touma… I thought you didn't think anything of me… I thought that… I alone was just running around in circles, thinking myself pathetic for being unable to give up…"
If I don't deny it… all the decisions I have made up until now will have been for nothing.
"That's why I… told myself to at least become sincere. To never lie to you or Setsuna."
Like how I have always had Touma on my mind. How it only took one moment for me to become attracted to Setsuna.
"When Setsuna confessed to me, I wanted to ask if she was joking… But then I had to think about it very seriously."
Like how I fell for Setsuna's singing voice. Like how I entrusted my body to Touma's performances.
"If someone were to ask me whether I like or hate Setsuna… Well, isn't it a given? Of course I like her…"
Like how if I were asked the question of who I liked more, the true answer was already so clear…
"Setsuna seemed so ridiculously happy when I told her that, and that's when I finally realized that she was serious."
But then, how rather than continuing to dwell on my delusions, I believed that I should treasure the words and emotions of someone who gave me her heart.
"Even so, I simply didn't want to lie to you, Touma. That's why you were the first one I told about it."
Like how I believed that my feelings would never reach that certain someone who never told me anything.
"You're saying that telling me first was you being sincere…? What part of that was being sincere?"
"But Touma… you said that you give us your blessing."
"Forcing the knowledge of something that will clearly hurt them on someone… You call that being sincere?"
"I never knew I was hurting you. Because you were just your usual self…"
"That's just the ignorance of a loser who has no idea how to handle women!"
"That's right, I'm just a plain, boring loser! Someone like you would never even take a second look at me…"
"Don't you dare tell me what to feel when you don't know the first thing about women! What's wrong with me falling in love with a loser!?"
"Then why didn't you say something!? How the hell was I supposed to know!?"
"How could I have!? Setsuna already said it first… I would have definitely hurt Setsuna if I did…"
See… you're just like me, aren't you?
In order to be sincere to Setsuna, you couldn't be sincere to me, right?
…Even after finding out each other's misunderstandings, the crack between us is already too wide to mend.
Coinciding with our moment of silence, snow begins to fall.
As if to cover up this sorrowful encounter, the white, untarnished snow falls from above the city.
"Kitahara, it looks like we've finally become friends just now, you and I."
Touma wipes around her eyes in one swipe and once again forces out a subservient smile.
"I've told you everything that I wanted to. Now you know everything about me."
"Though, our friendship ended the moment it started."
One step, two stepsーTouma backs away, once again trying to escape toward the road.
"Don't chase after me… Don't chase after me this time. Don't ever show yourself in front of me again."
"Even though I'm telling you this right now, I'm actually deeply regretting it inside, you know?"
One step, two stepsーI close the distance between us. I corner Touma.
"W-Wait, Kitahara. I told you not to…"
Focused on me, Touma hits the guard rail behind her and can't back away any further.
"Ah, s-stop… Stop it. You can't… do this…"
Finally, I've caught Touma inside my arms.
As I grab her shoulders and come face to face with her, her swollen red eyes and wet cheeks make her look like a completely different person.
Her beauty remains the same even in her miserable state, and that unwavering fact carves itself into my heart…
There was only one girl on my mind in the whole world.
Touma's lips, as if reflecting her own tastes, have a very sweet aroma to them.
With a supernatural charm, they strip me of all reason and immerse me in a state of ecstasy.
While savoring the dreamlike sensation of her lips, I invade deeper through a slight gap between them.
There's something in there, even hotter and softer than her lips, though with a slightly rougher surface as well.
As I wrap around the tip of her tongue with my own, Touma's entire body starts to tremble.
This brings me even more delight, and as I proceed even deeper inside with the intent of entwining with everything in her mouth…
I feel the sharp pain of her furious rejection on both my chest and cheek.
She pushed me away with all her strength, and then slapped my cheek with full force.
With the clear intent of rejection.
As if telling me that it's too late.
As if to say that she won't ever give me a second thought anymore.
As if saying that I'm as good as nothing to her now…
"Why are you so used to it!?"
If only she'd just said any of those things to me…
"How many times have you kissed Setsuna already!?"
But the words that Touma uttered…
"Just how far will you leave me behind until you're satisfied!?"
…Were those of unbelievable repressed sadness and jealousy from the depths of her heart.
Finally, without looking back, Touma turns and runs away from me at full speed.
The gradually intensifying snow hides her silhouette.
If I ran, I might be able to chase her down. I might be able to catch Touma again.
But the falling snow… and Touma's last words…
…Shackle both of my legs, weighing them down with inescapable, heavy chains.
"37.8°C… Looks like you've made it through the critical part."
"Critical…? You don't need to exaggerate it…"
"What are you saying!? Don't underestimate a cold!
Just this morning, your fever was almost 40°C, you know?"
"Figures. You seemed to have been fading in and out of consciousness from such a high fever."
It doesn't seem as though she was exaggerating even in the slightest.
Monday was a national holiday. Meaning it's been two days since then.
But it feels like it was just yesterday to me.
As nighttime came, snow started falling intensely, and showed no signs of stopping even after midnight.
Amidst that snow, I stood in place… I couldn't move after parting with her.
I couldn't even go and meet Setsuna even though she was waiting. I just stood there motionless… I guess.
"I'll put the rest of the porridge in the refrigerator, okay? It's the one I told you about before, the canned one."
The next thing I remember, I was shivering in my bed. My face was a tearful mess and my throat was dry.
"When you're hungry just 'ding it'… No, I mean, heat it up in the microwave and eat it.
Ahaha, looks like I picked up my mom's way of talking."
When I next came to my senses, I saw Setsuna in front of me with a relieved expression and felt a cold towel on my face.
"Hmm? What is it? Want some water?"
"First off, I'm sorry that I didn't come to your party."
You shouldn't have even tried to leave your home in that condition, you know?"
The sheer convenience of my currently miserable state happens to fit the bill for a valid excuse for missing Setsuna's birthday party.
"Well, I would like you to be more aware of how poorly you're treating your own body, Haruki-kun."
"I'm just kidding. You must be really sick if you're taking that seriously."
But in a situation like this, not saying it is essentially the same as lying to her.
"Second of all, I'm sorry that you had to come all the way here."
"When Kazusa fell sick, I couldn't even visit her. This is payback for that!"
I'm glad that you're relying on me."
"You should stop apologizing already… There's a limit to how timid you can be, you know?"
At first, when I saw Setsuna, I thought that she had gotten worried because she couldn't get in touch with me, so she decided to come here.
When I checked my phone's call history, I realized that… I was the one who called her first.
Maybe I just called because I wanted to apologize for not coming to the party.
Maybe I just wanted to leave her a happy birthday message.
Right now, I can't really remember why I called her.
Nevertheless, the fact remains that I called her. I told her that I'd collapsed.
…I reached out to the girl whose feelings I'd betrayed one-sidedly just a few hours prior.
"Try not to think too much, you should just get some sleep right now."
I'm not even capable of admitting that I've betrayed her, and yet I'm longing for nothing more than her kindness again.
I'm the worst of the worst.
"I think it's about time for me to head back. It's about time for my family to come back home too."
"…Y-Yeah. Err, they went to the shopping mall together this morning. Right, they're shopping, eating, and watching movies…"
"Is that so? Sorry, again. I'm sure you wanted to join them too, right, Setsuna?"
"D-Don't worry about it. It's a bit embarrassing to always be going out with my family anyway."
There's no way Setsuna… or any other member of the Ogiso family would want to distance themselves like that.
Setsuna went out of her way because of me. For a traitor like me…
There's a small box wrapped in paper…
I want you to have it…
I don't have the right to say something like that right now.
"Get some sleep, okay? I think you'd better spend tomorrow resting too. I'll come by again after school."
Her hands are cold from her efforts to take care of me, but that's exactly what makes them comfortingly warm… and makes me want to cry.
Setsuna closes her eyes in front of me. Her breath brushes against my lips.
But I can no longer accept such beautiful, genuine feelings from her.
Setsuna's lips are soft and warm…
"I hope that'll help you get well soon."
That's why… the moment she leaves…
The tears that I held in finally begin to overflow.
The truth is, I don't have the right to cry at all, but my tears just won't stop.
Regardless of whether it's done out of kindness or cruelty…
Regardless of whether it's for the sake of oneself or someone else…
A lie is still a lie.
And liars are simply the worst.
"My fever had already gone down yesterday in the first place. There won't be any more important classes either, so I just brought the essentials."
In the end, I finally return to the world today after two days of being sick.
"Oh, so you've recovered. I'm glad, it's such a relief."
"Thank you for visiting me every day. You really helped me out."
My mother actually came home every night, but besides exchanging a few words with me as usual, she didn't even bother coming to check up on me.
That's why Setsuna nursed me and prepared all my meals up until yesterday, though my laundry inevitably piled up.
"Don't worry about it. I enjoyed doing it too… It's my privilege as your girlfriend, right?"
It really helped me, and made me so happy.
But my heart was hurting the whole time.
"Let's go to school, then. Since you came all this way to pick me up, Haruki-kun, I don't want us to be late."
"Ah, wait a minute. Before that, here…"
"…Jeez, now you're bringing it up. I've been waiting like, 'Is he gonna do it yet, is he gonna?' all along, you know?"
I've actually had a paper-wrapped basket hanging from my hand for the occasion of my return.
"The store salesperson recommended it, so if you have any praise or complaints, you can take them there."
Unwrapping the paper, she discovers a potted flower.
"This is… a butterfly orchid, isn't it? It must have been expensive, right?"
"You promised not to ask about the price."
"Thank you… I'm really happy with it."
"And I'm sorry for giving it a bit late."
"You're not late, though, you know? Not at all."
It's not the day of the party. It is actually Setsuna's birthday today.
After finally being able to get out of bed yesterday, I bought this present in a flower shop in front of the station.
"Thank you so much… I'll take good care of it."
"Yeah. I chose it because I knew you'd be able to."
I put all of my heart in it.
But I decided not to put any truly significant meaning in it.
I hid the ring that I had bought before in the deepest corner of my desk drawer.
And I sealed it away in the deepest corner of my heart.
"Then, this is a humble response from me… No, I'm actually only saying that to hide my embarrassment.
Then, just like I expected, Setsuna opens her bag, and hands me a small, red paper package.
"Ah, here, I'll let you check inside my bag while I'm at it.
There aren't any others meant for anyone else, see? That's the only one."
"Ah, well, I did end up giving one to my dad and Takahiro, but…
Well, you can overlook that, right?"
Setsuna laughs mischievously while jokingly sticking out her tongue.
"I thought you said you liked winter?"
"I never said I like winter. I said I like snow."
"Won't you feel cold when it snows, though?"
"Well, I won't feel cold in the slightest as long as it snows. I'd be fine even in the snow-capped mountains or in Hokkaido!"
"…I really can't understand what you're saying sometimes, Setsuna."
"Aa-ah, I hope we get snow again. A whole blanket of white, just like last weekend… Ack."
"No, it's actually my fault. You don't need to apologize, Setsuna."
"I was worried about it, hoping I could help you forget about it… I'm so clumsy."
Setsuna's kindness stings me in a way that's different from the chill of the wind.
It's a reserved kindness, one that's the complete opposite of how I meddle in others' business like I usually do.
"Say, Setsuna, why do you like the snow so much?"
But I can't face that kindness head on.
"Normally, people have some deep reason for it, right? Some scenery that you saw in the past, a fond memory… or maybe your name?"
"Aah, now that you mention it, I do have the character for snow (雪) in my name Setsuna (雪菜), huh. I never gave it much thought."
"Now that I mention it… Don't you think your parents would be really upset if they heard you?"
"Is it strange to say that I just like it? Do you hate it, Haruki-kun? The snow, I mean."
"I don't exactly hate it, but I do think it's all sorts of trouble."
I would've smiled and answered with, "No, I actually like it too" if I were my usual self, though.
"Trains arrive late, people tend to slip accidentally. And yet the school never even gives us days off."
It seems that I'm bothered by something I can't really put my finger on today, and I suppose that's why I'm getting worked up over otherwise trivial matters.
"Besides that… cars can crash into it too."
"Ahahaha, yeah, that really happened to us, huh?"
"I was prepared for an accident back then. But even still, it wasn't a good feeling."
"But it was so beautiful, right? The blanketed scenery we saw through the inn's windows, and the snow that came down in the open air bath."
"I'd really like to go again… Just like that, the three of us together."
I see… Now I understand why I'm disturbed by Setsuna's words.
I'm afraid of it because it's beautiful.
That I'm afraid something unbelievable might happen again.
I clench my fist tightly in my pocket.
I've given her the present. I've received her Valentine's chocolates.
I know deep down that I'm not supposed to say what I'm about to say on a day like this.
But that would just mean prolonging my sins.
Truth be told, I should have said this on that snowy day in particular… No, it's something that I shouldn't have done in the first place.
"I have something I need to tell…"
It's about Touma. About Touma's future.
All of it… I should have told her all of that on my own accord, but…
"I apologize for not telling you anything until now. I'm sorry, Setsuna, Kitahara."
The first meeting of the Light Music Club after entering the new year.
Today's agenda… concerns our keyboardist-saxophonist-bassist-acting club president, Touma Kazusa's future after graduation.
"Anyway, it's all decided already. After graduating, I'll be moving to Vienna."
Because of the all too sudden declaration of our parting, Setsuna is at a loss for words, as expected.
And because I already knew all too much about this shocking revelation, I couldn't even raise my head.
"To further hone my piano skills at the very place its art was born, in addition to living with my mother… Is that a good enough reason?"
"But since you'll be breaking the promise, you'll have to explain it to Setsuna. I won't allow you to leave without saying anything."
Touma really did keep her promise with me.
Just like this, she's telling Setsuna personally, and having to accept her surprise and grief.
"Yeah, Touma Youko. A pianist nearing the end of her career, and my former teacher. A non-intervening failure of a mother figure."
Then again… the way she's going about it is sly.
She made her confession and brought up "living with my family" fully aware that Setsuna couldn't possibly oppose such a reason.
"She abandoned me for three years, but with a few sweet words, she regained my trust. Looks like I have a bit of a mother complex after all, huh."
After ignoring me all day, she threw me a message written on a torn piece of paper during the last class today.
"Don't you dare tell Setsuna about that."
I glared at her for quite some time after reading it, but she just nonchalantly looked out the window like she used to before.
"She came back near the end of last year, and we talked about a lot of things. About what happened three years ago, and about our current situation."
Following that, Touma went on to talk for a long time, enough to make me wonder if she was really the Touma Kazusa I've known for all this time.
Until three years ago, without even realizing it herself, she had only been playing the piano for her mother.
She didn't seem to care at all about the "amateurish impressions" of her own feelings, or the responses of the audiences watching her perform in competitions.
All she aspired to was to be graded well by her motherーand the teacher her mother brought. Nothing else beyond increasing their approval interested her in the slightest.
"That said, I never felt unsatisfied or uneasy. I could grasp most of the music as long as I practiced, after all, so I never felt that I should quit or that it was just too difficult."
She'd inevitably succumbed to a trap all geniuses are vulnerable to, as the child of a genius herself.

Touma Youko had solidified her position of fameーbe it as an artist or as an entertainer. As such, her fear for her daughter's future caused her to distance herself from her daughter for quite some time.
As if to say it wasn't really her cup of tea.
"A cruel mother, right? A strict teacher, right? It's no wonder I lost my way."
"B-But why now? Why is she trying to take you away now, Kazusa?"
"She watched our performance during the school festival… and regained her interest in me."
I know it is, because… I met with Touma Youko personally and heard it first hand.
"I was just playing around on the stage… I still can't understand how a proper artist thinks."
We weren't up there for anybody else but ourselves, but even then, in a completely different sense, we succeededーin somehow managing to catch Touma Youko's interest.
That's why she gave her daughter another chance, advising Touma to participate in the competition.
Depending on the result of the competition, and how Touma performed, she would decide whether or not to take her daughter to Europe with her.
"But… but… Kazusa, do you really want to do it? Do you really want to leave and study abroad?"
Even though there's clearly no way we can stop her…
Even though Touma has already reached the point of no return, judging by her determination and the whole situation…
Setsuna still refuses to give up without a fight…
"Or maybe… don't tell me, Kazusa, are you still…"
"Yes, I want to study abroad. I've made my decision."
But the words she wanted to say are easily countered.
There's no way for me to know what Setsuna tried to say…
"And my mother… when I think about it, I don't really hate her that much."
But I have a feeling Touma knows, and she doesn't want her to say it.
"That's why I believe that taking my own path is the right thing to do."
To that end, Touma looks straight at Setsuna, asserting her determination through a relieved expression.
"I'll repair the relationship with my mother. This time, I'll be a good girl, just like Setsuna."
As if trying to erase the weak Touma of the past from my memories, she looks straight at us.
Standing before us, Touma appears unnaturally and perfectly strong.
It's that same sensation that gnawed at me when I'd covered up my lies with even more lies.
"So… let's meet again someday. All three of us, okay?"
This is what Setsuna truly wants. And it's also what I used to want.
Right now, you don't even believe your own words, do you? You're just forcing yourself to believe, aren't you?
"This means we won't be able to stay together forever… But to me, Setsuna and Kitahara, you two are my most precious and irreplaceable friends."
You're trying to shut me up by calling me your friend, aren't you?
"I want you and Kitahara to always stay like this."
Stop lying already, you stupid idiot…!
"Please… keep a place for me to return to."
"It's almost time for graduation, isn't it?"
On our way home, after parting with Touma.
After being silent and dejected for the longest time as we were walking hand-in-hand, Setsuna finally speaks.
Even though she seems to be just stating the obvious, the emotions behind her words are different than usual.
"Until now, I've been underestimating the upcoming graduation…"
"It'll just be an event to celebrate graduation, there'll be no real farewell in it… That's what I always thought."
Around half of our classmates will be enrolling at Houjou University, after all.
As for the three of us, two of us would have gone to the same university, while the remaining one would also be nearby. We would always remain together.
That would brush away any loneliness threatening Setsunaーafter all, she'd believed that she'd be spending the same unchanging days with the same familiar faces come April.
"But it really is a special day after all… Just like in middle school, it's hard, bitter, and makes me want to cry. It's just like that, all over again…"
Setsuna's right hand grips my hand firmly.
"All we can do is… respect the decision she's made."
I can't respond to Setsuna's grip.
There's no need to feel lonely… I'll always be by your side… I can't bring myself to say those words.
"It's sad that she decided without telling us, but there's no way simply talking to us would have changed her mind… This is the most important decision in her life, after all."
Instead, I try to put on a relieved expression, just like Touma's. With confidence in my eyes, I look straight at Setsuna.
"Even if we told her not to go or that we won't forgive her, it won't make a difference now. It'll just make us all feel bad. You don't want that to happen either, right, Setsuna?"
Ahh, I understand now… There's a trick to it.
Without changing my expression or letting the muscles of my face move, I can open my eyes wide and dry them off.
"That's why I'll… see her off with a smile, just like she wants us to."
Even I can appear unnaturally and perfectly strong. That's right.
"Well, what will you do, Setsuna? Will you just cry bitterly and make Touma cry too? If that's your plan, then don't expect me to help you."
"Putting it that way makes it sound really mean… Haruki-kun."
She just selfishly shouldered what was supposed to be mine to bear.
My sins are far heavier than hers, yet I've pushed all the excuse-making on her.
"Sorry. But you have to decide before graduation day."
"Yeah… Sorry. I'm sorry for saying what I did now, too."
But for now, I won't cry.
…Because it'd just wet my eyes that have finally dried.
Finally, we've arrived. It feels like the walk took longer than usual.
Just like usual, Setsuna looks straight at me.
But her voice is anything but the usual, sweet one I'm used to.
"No, it's nothing. I don't really need to ask it."
I suppose it'd be better to say that her words are so vague it sounds like she's monologuing.
"Well then… good bye. See you tomorrow."
If it were like usual… with sweet whispers, Setsuna would give herself to me.
While feeling our touch and scent, we would join our lips, entangle our tongues, feel each other's breath, exchange long kisses…
If only that painful thing hadn't happened…
But Setsuna's own anguish is saving me right now.
She's sparing me from a conflict of emotions that will include pain, euphoria, guilt, and love.
She's allowing me to keep my current feelings unnoticed by her.
There's only two more weeks until graduation…
I wonder how we'll feel by the time we have to part ways.
I wonder who will be by my side when that time comes.
…I wonder if there even will be someone by my side.
"You knew Kazusa would be studying abroad…"
"That's why you looked so worn out all this time…"
"Long time, huh. Since you were here last time, too."
"…Well, I was prohibited from coming here, after all."
He's right, I haven't been to Music Room 1 in so long.
Before the three of us formed our group, and moved to the room next door…
This is where I originally practiced, back with the former Light Music Club…
"I haven't heard your guitar for a long time, either. You haven't played since the school festival, right?"
Although all the other members were actually more skilled than me, they'd just practice for a little bit and then call it a day pretty early.
I was the only one who remained as I fruitlessly persisted in my struggle. Until one day, I got reliable accompaniment to back me up…
"I thought you had surpassed me for sure back then, but I guess you're back to being crappy just like that, huh?"
I swear… I can't believe I call this guy my best friend.
"More than half of us are simply moving up a grade. Nothing much will change even if we go to university."
If I just ignore what little will change, I'm sure I won't feel so lonely.
"Well, recently I've only gone for girls who aren't too clingy, so this'll be goodbye to about 80% of them.
…Really makes you feel lonely, doesn't it?"
"…That's just a self-fulfilling prophecy. Actually, you shouldn't even choose your girlfriends like that."
And so, intentionally or otherwise, Takeya continues to make empty conversation, keeping my mind off things.
"You should limit yourself when you enter university, you know? You'll only end up putting holes in your heart from all the loneliness."
I know there's a good reason why he's like this, but at least I can preach at him without fear of repercussion.
He's easy to talk to, and he lets me talk my heart out with him. In a sense, he's a truly precious friend.
"…For this half year, Haruki, you've also enjoyed three years' worth of sour-sweet events, haven't you? …Along with very strong bitterness."
"You're playing old songs again, Haruki. …If I'm not mistaken, that song is about not forgetting someone you parted with, right?"
"I just love this song, that's all there is to it."
"I've told you before, haven't I? In your case, whatever song you're playing is an expression of your feelings."
Easy to talk to, lets me talk my heart out. In a sense, a terrible friend to deal with…
"What's so good about that terrifying girl? Nothing about her is a good match for you, you know?"
"That girl decided to leave you herself. That should tell you just how little you mean to her, right?"
"I really have no idea what you're talking about. Cut it out with the misunderstandings, dude."

If I were my usual self, I'd say, "I can't figure out who you're talking about if you're only using pronouns. Tell me, in simple terms, exactly who you're talking about." I would go out of my way just to choose words he can't stand.

"That's why you have to get back on your feet. Don't you dare let go of what you have right now."
This guy… hardly even knows the whole story…
He's only been able to get some information from rumors, observe our behavior, and make nothing but wild guesses.
…So how could you have reached the core of the problem so fast?
"Well, it's true that you're not fit to be with Setsuna-chan either. The only one fit for her is yours truly!"
"How can you say something like that so nonchalantly? Setsuna…"

…But who exactly is that supposed to be, then?
"You get that, Haruki? There's a future for you and Setsuna-chan, you know?"
"Starting from spring, in the same university, on the same campus… This time you'll have thousands of guys as your foes. You better be ready, got it?"

"Haruki, you're different from me. …Don't you ever become like me and disappoint me, got it?"
Do you know that there's not even the slightest inkling of one in my heart… Takeya?
"Hey, do you know why I joined the Light Music Club?"
"Haruki dragged you into it, right? Takeya said something like that."
"I was standing here one day, overlooking the schoolyard… and heard White Album being played…"

"Well, if they've made it that far, that means our friendship wouldn't be easily broken, right?"
"…But I guess that's arrogant of me."
"…Thank you. That's why I'm really glad to have you as a friend, Io."
"That said, Setsuna, you still haven't told me why you've been so down lately."
"…It's nothing interesting. It really is just a pointless, little memory."
"I did it again. Why did it turn out like this…?"
"It wasn't supposed to be like this, not like this."
"It's not your fault, Setsuna. There's no way her going to study abroad is any of your fault."
"You're really scary, Io. Maybe I shouldn't say any more…"
"It's all Haruki's fault. He completely ignored your feelings and acted rashly, Setsuna…"
"I was actually the one who made the first move."
"On the night of the school festival, after I parted with you, Io… Soon after getting to the music room…"
"But why? I mean, Setsuna, back then you were…"
"N-No, even so. That has nothing to do with what's going on now, right?"
"Then why did you say it was Haruki-kun's fault, Io?"
"That doesn't matter. It can't possibly be your fault, Setsuna."
"You're not answering my question, you know?"
"The fact that you and Haruki are dating and the fact that that girl's leaving to study abroad have nothing to do with each other, Setsuna!"
"There's no way she would decide her future just because of that. It's just like she said, it's all for the piano and her mother!"
"Kazusa… has been really good at hiding it. But I already know what it is she's hiding."
"I'm telling you, Setsuna, you're just imagining things."
"Even if I am… I'm still sad about it nonetheless."
"Running away after being rejected by a boy in this day and age would just be too embarrassing, you know… Way too serious, don't you think? There's just no way."
"It wasn't supposed to… turn out like this…"
There's only a week left until graduation…
Since the day Touma told us about going abroad to study, she stopped coming to school again.
She never picked up her phone either. There wasn't even a dial tone.
…I'm sure that's because she's blocked my number.
After fulfilling the one promise she made with me, she disappeared from my side once again.
"We will now proceed with the presentation of the graduation certificates."
…There's no longer any time left until graduation.
With her reply, I feel an instant change in the atmosphere from the guys around me.
Students seated beside me chatting amongst each other. Students pointing their phone cameras toward the stage even though it's prohibited. …Students openly directing their hostile gazes at me.
And in between all that, I…
I simply maintain my gaze upon Setsunaーand Setsuna aloneーas she walks down from the stage after bowing to the principal.
"Ahh!? Excuse me, sorry… you're Touma Kazusa, right?"
"Ah… that's right. We haven't met before. I'm Kitahara Haruki. For the time being, I'm the class representative for Class E for the first half of the year."
Several hundreds of students will climb up and walk off immediately afterward, as if on a perfectly orderly assembly line.
Yet right there… for what it's worth, is supposedly the proof of our three years here, compressed into a mark of ink on a piece of fine paper.
"I hereby bestow the graduation certificate to Kitahara Haruki from Class 3-E, with the same honors."
This may be the first and the last time many of the students will actually have any sort of contact with the principal.
As I entertain such mundane thoughts, the next name is called, and the assembly line is set in motion again.
"This is the first time you've spoken to me on your own, isn't it?"
The name of a specific female student who came out of nowhere to attend class for a day two weeks ago, before going back to being absent.
Even though she's still not here today at the graduation ceremony, she has indeed auspiciously graduated.
"If that's the case, then I'd love to listen to you playing some classical music in earnest, and not just messing around."

"Ah, well… how should I put it? Hearing you playing the piano really relaxes me, Touma."
From the principal's oration to the guest speeches, the ceremony moves along without delay, and now… the semifinal event, the farewell address from the students, has ended.
All the speeches were appropriate for a metropolitan graduation event, covering key points and briefly summarizing them, progressing at exemplary speed.
And I too, of course… have absolutely no intention of breaking this tradition.
"Next, a speech from the representative of the graduating students, Class 3-E, Kitahara Haruki."
I earned this spot on the main stage after two and a half years of a dull life.
The mark of an honors student that I hadn't lost despite falling out in the final half of the year.
This will be my final task. My last shining moment on the stage.
If this were a movie, a TV series, or a teenage novel…

"I'd like to express my sincere gratitude to the principal, our guests, teachers, as well as parents and guardians for being present for all of us here today."
Unfortunately, I'm not the kind of person to do something like that.

T-These guys, even right up until the very end…

Regardless of whether I'm "still" going on about it, there hasn't even been any progress since then.
