I've just been absentmindedly going to school, greeting Setsuna in the morning, sighing while staring at the empty seat next to me, leaving school with Setsuna, and taking her home without even kissing her before we part ways.
This cowardly charade has been going on for the past week.
"Takeya, it's fine, isn't it? Time will solve it. By the time April comes around…"
"If time alone were enough to set this guy straight, I wouldn't be worrying like this."

Starting this spring, my new life will begin… The changes might be drastic at first, but after that, I have a feeling nothing much will change. A year that will simply slightly alter my course of life will begin.
As time moves on and leaves my feelings behind, I have to start a new life.
Chikashi points with his eyes toward the entrance of the building.
From Chikashi's attitude and Takeya's intimidating glare, I quickly realize why.
Setsuna is standing there with Io, carrying a plastic tube, just like me.
Noticing me, Io taps Setsuna's shoulder and joins the two guys that I was with until just now.
The only ones who remain are Setsuna and me, and…
The chilly wind tries its best to blow away the awkward mood, but its efforts prove useless when I can't even look Setsuna directly in the eye.
I… no, anyone would know that the right thing to do here is to follow the natural course, as led on by circumstances.

Setsuna is bound by the pain of losing a friend, and I, who have also lost… a friend… should be the one to heal her. It would be the best course of action, and would only result in our bond growing deeper.
It'd be the decision that won't hurt anyone. The decision that will make everyone happy.
…No, that doesn't sound quite right. The decision that will hurt the least amount of people, and that will make the most people happy.
As I was trying to find the determination to make such a decision, Setsuna completely turned the situation on its head.
"There was a letter inside my desk… It wasn't there this morning."
"I just realized it… Kazusa came to the graduation ceremony. She was here until just now!"
While we were spending our time in the gym, holding back our tears as well as our yawns during the understandably emotional, yet inevitably boring ceremony…
"What should we do… She's not picking up her phone. Are we really never going to see her again?"
Touma was here… She was here, and I could reach her if I just ran a little…
"I have something that I have to tell Kazusa. Other than saying goodbye, it's something very important…"
I can hear Takeya's voice from behind.
"You idiot, stop, come back!"… I can hear him implying all of those things as he calls after me.
However, my legs are no longer capable of listening to reason.
I exit the school gate, looking at the surrounding paths left and right.
But there is no sight of a girl with black hair that reaches down to her waist.
And because of that… my mind completely cuts itself off from my sense of reason.
I collapse on my bed, completely exhausted.

How many hours has it been since I dashed out of the school? The sun had been high up above and gradually sank in the west. I kept on running nonstop until it had completely hidden itself beneath the horizon.
I ran around the school, in front of the station, downtown. And between each instance of looking for her somewhere else, I stopped by Touma's house.
But no matter how much I tried, I could not find her, and no matter how many times I rang her doorbell, there was no answer.
I was suddenly made to realize that the neighborhood that we were confined to was actually much larger than I'd ever thought it was.
It also made me realize that the reason Touma stayed by my side all along was because she did so of her own volition.
A part of my heart that wants me to sink into my bed from the tormenting exhaustion is at odds with another piece of my heart that insists I must go out again to find her.
Already taken completely past its limits, my body finds itself in complete agreement with the part of me that wants to sink into bed, but my heart still struggles against it.
After all, something inside me is still burning.
The feelings I couldn't convey, my heart that couldn't reach her. Now that she has realized it at last, I'm still faced with the painful truth.
And even then, I continue to betray someone precious to me, using my shameless, lingering attachment to someone else as the strength I need to keep running.
I flip my phone open and press its buttons.
With the intent of conveying my current situation, and my feelings to the person I left behind in the schoolyard…
They might end up coming out as nothing more than half-baked words that won't even amount to a clear answer.
But I can't delay my answer any longer. I really have to tell her this time…
Just as I'd found the determination not to hide my feelings any longer…
The name that shows up on my phone's screen is…
The most precious name to me in the entire worldーTouma Kazusa.
"Where are you right now? Where in the world are you?"
"Mm… Well, somewhere far away, I guess you could say?"
Hearing her voice is all it takes to bring me to the brink of tears even as I lie down on my bed.
I force myself to speak in an unpleasant tone in a desperate attempt to suppress my sniffling.
"I've been looking for you… I heard that you were at school, that you left a letter… Setsuna told me. So I… went to your house, in front of the station… everywhere!"
"I heard your speech, you know… You sure did a great job spewing out unappealing, insincere and convenient words one after another back there. It was actually impressive."
"Why didn't you come to the graduation ceremony…? Why didn't you show up so we could meet you…?"
But no matter how I look at it, the words coming out of my mouth are conveying the same irrepressible feelings that came out the day I cruelly and persistently pushed all the blame on Touma.
"How could I meet the two of you now…? I've done so many terrible things to Setsuna."
"So you're trying to end it all with a single letter?"
I was the one who did all those terrible things…
And yet, I was the only one who was promised that I could stay with Setsuna, and continue to always be with her.
"You don't have to worry… I didn't write anything that would get you in trouble."
That means… you didn't write anything remotely close to the truth…
Aren't you just telling me the sad fact that you're entirely incapable of speaking sincerely to your own friend?
"Hey, don't cry, Kitahara. That's such an undignified way for a man to act."
"Shut up… I was never dignified to begin with."
"You should at least send me off with a smile. This will be… our last conversation, after all, so…"
"No… Don't say it'll be our last!"
"Stop whining… You're acting like a child."
"I want to see you… I want to see you, Touma… Where are you…?"
"No, I'm not telling you. I've already decided that I won't ever meet you again."
Touma's words pierce my heart like frigid icicles.
Even though she is holding back and acting so tenderly…
The pain, bitterness, and sorrow drive me to the brink of helplessness nevertheless.
Wanting to ease the pain, if even only a little, I ultimately shut off the path that was supposed to lead me to my new life in spring.
I'm sorry, Setsuna… I can't return to you anymore.
Touma's voice is still tender as always… though all the same, her words are still cold.
"So I… really hate you… and myself."
Then, her voice trembles ever so slightly from exasperation mixed with grief.
"It's too late. There's nothing you can do now, no matter what you say."
"So I can't even say it if it's late? Do I have no choice but to hide my feelings?"
"That's right… Don't make things any more painful for me than they already are."
And she's giving me no mercy.
"Do you think… I'm secretly against the idea of moving over there?"
"That's right. I really do want to go."
"I want to get better at the piano, and I want to live with my mom."
Touma's words go in through my right ear and exit straight out of my left ear.
"There isn't only one truth. My desire to move over there… and my wish to stay here… they're both real."
I just got a clue that I can't afford to ignore.
"It's snowing… It's been snowing a lot this year…"
"Hey, Kitahara… Whenever I see the snow, I will always remember."
"I'll remember how I played White Album with the two of you."
"How much fun I had messing around with you two in the snow in the mountains."
"How on that snowy street… you took me into your embrace…"
"Whenever I look up into the snowy sky, I'll remember."
"Even if I'm looking at a sky so far away from here, on the other side of the world… I'll absolutely… definitely… remember all that…"
The park right in front of my apartment, by the stairs…
My beloved coward, hiding under a light pole.
I heard the sound of an ambulance siren from Touma's line.
And at just about the same time and volume, I heard the same sound in my room.
That was when I realizedーTouma was actually very close by.

Unlike last time, nothing's obstructing her nowーregardless, I easily close the distance separating me from her.
She looks as if she's given up on something…
As if she's gotten over somethingーTouma's refreshed expression is one that I haven't seen her make in a while.
They're not unnaturally dry like that last timeーrather, her tears are now pooling in her eyes as best as she can hold them back.

I behold a resigned expression, and with it, a union of true strength, beauty and cuteness all at once.
This is itーthis is the face of the Touma that I love more than anything in the world.

"I loved you so much, so when you were taken by Setsuna, it was so painful for me…"
I take another step, and then another.
The distance between Touma and me slowly but surely closes.
"There, I said it… Setsuna, I'm so sorry. But this is fine, right…? Because he can only hear my voice… Because I'll never meet him again…"
The two of us are connected through something other than radio waves.
"It's your fault for reminding me of the joy in playing music."
"It's your fault for teaching me how painful it is to fall in love with someone."

No, Kazusa desperately extends her left arm and wraps it around my neck.
After exchanging them over the phone with our voices alone… we affirm our feelings through the sensation of our united lips.
Kazusa's not trying to run away anymore.
She gently… no… passionately leans herself against me.
Using all her strength, she insists that she remain within my embrace.
There's no need for words anymore.
Without even checking if there was anyone else in the house, we unabashedly went up to my room, still holding hands, and fell on the bed.
My mother hasn't returned yet, but even if she had, we would've done the same.
And then, deciding not to waste even a single moment of what little time we have left, I skip the light kisses and our tongues become deeply entwined.

Before I could even say anything…
Kazusa's tongue touches a part of mine, and it stings a little.

"Let's head to the cafeteria. I suppose I could spare you a Lunch Set A."
"That's what I'm talking about! Haruki, I love you～!"
"…Even if you're joking, don't say stuff like that so nonchalantly."
Winter is… just around the corner.
The annual university festival held around the latter half of November has also come to an end, and the campus is completely clear of any traces of the festival.
"How many times do I need to tell you this, Izumi?"
"Ah, Haruki, there you are. Hey, about that fee we had to pay for the seminar when that instructor came and taught us…"
"I already confirmed the price with him and made sure he got the money. Here's your bankbook. And this is the receipt."
"Sorry about causing you trouble all the time… Oh, there's still some money left, lucky me!"
"Um… where were we, again? Ah, that's right, yes. How many times do I need to tell you, Izumi…"
"Mmhm, I'll listen to you no matter how many times I need to."
"Don't sleep in the lab just because you got drunk and missed the last train. Consider yourself lucky I got there first…"
"Don't the seniors do that too, though? I mean, that's the reason why they put the sleeping bag in that lab to begin with."
"That's a special privilege for those in the fourth year and above. It's a forbidden zone for us newcomers in the third year."
Our day-to-day university livesーnothing but an ephemeral dream to some, the mere passing of fall break to othersーhave returned.
"If you want to sleep in the lab, go ask the professor for a research topic first. You've never even shown up to a seminar, have you?"
"The last time I went to ask for a topic… he told me that you're the one in charge of me, Haruki, so I should ask you first."
Although I'm honored that I've gained your trust in only a few months, please don't give up on your teaching duties toward her all the same…
"You were the only woman in the lab that late at night in the first place… at least try to be a little conscious of your own safety…"
"Aah～ I get it, I get it. I completely understand, Mr. Police Officer. I'll be more careful next time."
"I can understand that you're more relaxed now that the university festival is over, but don't forget some self-discipline even after you've had your fun…"
"Aah～ I get it, I get it. I completely understand, O Mighty God. I'll be more careful in my next life."
"…If you really think that way, then at least show me some respect."
Izumi Chiaki is stuffing herself with fried mackerel right in front of me without a care in the world.
She's not the type to dress stylishly or work on her messy hair, but given how she isn't even putting on makeup, she's got a pretty attractive face.
I'm admittedly rather thankful for her existence as merely a simple seminar colleagueーa woman that doesn't really feel like one.
"Kitahara-kun, Kitahara-kun. About the seminar training camp next year requested by the professor…"
"I'm looking around Niigata for now. I'm negotiating with three hotels that have tennis courts near them."
"…You've already made so much progress, I see. Oh, and about the inspection…"
"Leave that part to the graduate students. It should be done by the beginning of next year."
"Thank you, that's perfect! …Ah, sorry for bothering you, Izumi-san."
"Uhh… Ah, that's right, we were in the middle of a conversation, weren't we?"
"Do you have any plans for later today? …That's all I wanted to ask."
"After fourth period, I'll be heading to prep school for my part-time job. After that, I'll be working at the publisher's office until midnight."
"…A workaholic as usual, huh. Do you even have a personal life?"
"I am the very definition of a working student."
"How do I say this… it feels like you're forcing yourself to work unnecessarily hard on purpose, Haruki."
"And that's exactly why people take advantage of you so easily. You're losing out on life."
So the living proof of the fact before me keenly points out…
"As the saying goes, 'Struggling during one's youth is worth paying for.'"
"…If you're going to put it that way, I suppose I'll sell you some. I'll make you a deal at 220 yen for now!"
"That's not the price of a struggle, but the price of a mixed tempura udon bowl…"
"…Oh, fine, I'll give up on the mixed tempura. I'll settle for the croquette-udon for the low price of 200 yen!"
I wasn't expecting you to put it into practice so soon.
"Okay, that's all for today. Your mock exams will be starting next week, so work hard, everyone."
My first job of the day ended without any trouble.

Despite the fact that this tiny facility can't compare with other famous prep schools in terms of sizeーmuch less in terms of the quality of the teaching staffーquite a number of students have gathered here, aiming to get into a university.
Well, I guess that's why a part-timer like myself managed to get this teaching job, one that I appreciate greatly.
It's why I managed to maintain my role as a modern Japanese and English grammar tutor here for a year and a halfーdue to the lack of qualified people for the job.
I've finally gotten the hang of teaching as well, somewhat. I have a grasp of the students' attention, too.
Somehow, just as I was getting a little too immersed in some sentimental thoughts, a soft voice calls out to me in the classroom, which I'd expected to be empty by now.
"Umm… Do you have a moment right now?"
Yada Mihoko. A third-year student from Houjou High. An underclassman of mine, in other words.
"By the way, I hear you've already acquired your recommendation? Congratulations."
"Thank you very much. It's all thanks to you, Sensei."
"It's all because you did your best, Yada."
"No, it's really all thanks to you, Sensei. Since you've always stayed after class to tutor me…"
As a student who's been sitting in the very front during lectures and often stays after class to diligently ask questions, her name was the first I'd memorized among my students.
"Well, in your case, Yada, your grades were good to begin with, and you're a hard worker on top of that, so I had no real reason to worry about you."
With her excellent grades and ideal learning mindset, I have no idea why she ended up coming to prep school when all she needs is just a recommendation from her homeroom teacher, however.
"So what is it? If it's the usual questions… Well, since you've already decided what you want to specialize in, I suppose it's not that."
"N-No, it's just that. I'd just like to ask some questions… as usual."
At any rate, to think that she'd be such a hard worker…
Even for my standards… well, not to sound pretentious, but even I would've taken it easy on studying during a period like this.
"Of course not. Have I ever turned down any questions after class?"
…Perhaps it's better to say it was a period where I couldn't think of anything.
"…No, never. No matter how late it got, you always tutored me wholeheartedly."
"N-No, it's no big deal. You don't have to praise me like that… Well, let's take a seat first."
However, just as I was abruptly caught by these thoughts in my head…
Her normally downcast eyes stare intently at me.
"…Is it true that you're quitting this month?"
Although I haven't told anyone other than the principal and the other teachers, the truth is, I only have three classes left to teach here.
"I'm about to graduate into my fourth year, so I won't have much time for this, what with seminars and job-hunting and whatnot."
"You'll be quitting all of your part-time jobs?"
"Nope, only this one. I'm planning on only working at night from now on."
"I… see. You'll be that busy, huh…"
"It's better to say that I'm just going back to focusing on my main duty as a student."

I won't allow my priorities to become disoriented, resulting in the cliched case of becoming burnt out at work and being unable to graduate. Whether it's because of common sense, for my life, or for my own dignity.
"Well, starting next year we'll be going to the same university. Let's meet up some time on campus, okay?"
As if she couldn't accept what I just said, she unnaturally suppresses her expression and continues asking me questions.
"Sensei, do you still remember when you first taught here last year?"
"You said that you wanted to introduce yourself given it was your first time teaching back then and had a Q&A session after that. When someone asked, 'Do you have a girlfriend?' you froze up."
"Having a good memory is a valuable asset, but I think it's more important to be selective of what you should remember."
"Sensei, after a long pause, you mumbled that you didn't…"
"No, what I'm trying to say is…"
"Is that… still the case right now?"
"Sensei, you… no matter how late it gets, you'll stay to answer my questions, right?"
"If you need more time, I'll wait. So please, take your time to consider…"
"Yeah… nothing's changed. Not a single thing since then…"
"P-Please hear me out! I, uh, I, Sensei… Sensei, I, I lo…"
My voice was simply calm, yet clear… Unbelievably calm, in fact.
"It's just a misunderstanding on your part. Please forget about it."
"Please don't ask me something like this again. …Now then, goodbye."
As usual, nothing's really changed. I'm still my everyday, usual self.
"Hey, part-timer, how's the progress on the questionnaire I requested earlier?"
"I've already compiled it into an Excel file and I'll send it to you now. I've prepared it so that you can calculate different sections separately."
"Here's the rough draft from the contractor. Take care of the editing, okay? Do it by today!"
"Hey～ hey～ Kitahara-kun. We're going to be changing the current Tokyo's Curry Ranking Series into the Seafood Edition this time."
"I need to gather reviews from the internet like before, right? Let me see… I can finish it by tomorrow."
"Sorry, I need this in a two-page layout. You can refer to the previous issues for the format.
…Oh crap, this is bad, I'm so late!"
"…It's fine if you have to go, but I may have to ask for some help if I don't understand something, so keep your cell phone on, okay?"
"Sorry, text me if you need to!"
Kaiousha Building, third floor. Editing department of the Kaiou Graph magazine.
Today's second job, progressing as planned.
"…What's up with Kizaki? He sure was in a hurry…"
Kaioushaーa massive magazine publisher with over twenty different departments.
"I heard something about his girlfriend threatening to break up with him, and that today was his last chance."
Even though I start work here at 6 PM, I can easily spend seven to eight hours here, a fact that both myself and the company appreciated.
"…Sure, but is that good enough of a reason to leave everything to the part-timer? Final proofreading is due the beginning of next week."

At any rate, by showing up three to four times a week,

I gain the reward of earning enough money to pay my rent with some to spare and a workload that's more than enough to kill someone.
"I'll contact him if I really can't do it. And if I run into any trouble, I'll ask you for some help, Hamada-san."
Both aforementioned benefits are essential to me, so it's an important part-time job for me that I don't intend to resign from any time soon.
"I've got plenty of my own work to worry about! I have three different projects planned this month alone! If you need help, ask Matsuoka or Suzuki…"
"Then again, is there anyone who isn't busy around here?"
"Someone who isn't busy… How about the managing editor?"
"…I understand. I guess I'll discuss this with Managing Editor Tanaka. Excuse me, Tanaka-san!"
"W-Whoa, wait, wait, hang on! We were just messing with you!"
"You were kidding, huh? Well, if I were to drop Kizaki-san's article, who should I have to settle it in my place?"
"Jeez, come on, Kitahara. Don't take it so seriously when it's obvious someone's pulling a prank… Hold on, you're doing this on purpose, aren't you?"
"If I could make this article a success just by laughing, I wouldn't mind laughing my ass off…"
"Kitahara-kun, you're so good at working you make it look like a joke, but it's impossible to laugh when you actually try to tell a joke."
"The problem lies with how his superior is training him, as I thought…"
"Heh…? You dare speak so shamelessly even after misusing my gopher?"
"Ooooh… I thought you had gone overseas for the week?"
From the looks of it, it seems that everyone was so busy messing with me that they were ambushed from behind.
"Ah, she contacted me an hour ago saying she'd reached Narita Airport. But I didn't think she'd show up today…"
"You should have told us something this important earlier, Kitahara!"
With her hands on her hips, her tall, dignified appearance and terrifying presence is enough to make not only part-timers but also official employees shudder in fear.
"Ah～ Mari-san. It's not like we're ordering him around, okay? Kitahara-kun's the one who asked if anyone had any work for him…"
"Yes, that's right! There's not a single person who's idle enough to mess around here, right? 'If they're idling, use them, even if they're the President' does happen to be our motto…"
She's not all that much older than the others around me, though. A "young employee," in her own words.
Just like that, her intimidating gaze falls upon me.
"…I already finished the work that you assigned me two days ago, Mari-san."
Of Kaiousha's Kaiou Graph editing department.
"I'm the one who assigns work to you, remember? How many times do I have to tell you not to accept other people's assignments?"
"Well, I have my own livelihood to worry about too."
"That's the first time I've ever heard a part-time student say something like that…"
"How many times do I have to tell you? If you keep overexerting yourself and working yourself to the bone like this…"
"Never mind that, how was your trip? You went to London, right?"
"I can't just go to Europe and settle with visiting just one country, right? I went to eight countries in five days."
"A movie preview and an interview with Director Hagen, a car exhibition in Italy, and an anime fair in France. Along with writing journal entries about tourist destinations while I was traveling…"
"…Aren't those completely unrelated to our department?"
"Can't help it, can I? It's to save on expenses. I negotiated with each department and had the expenses split. The articles I write are the best anyway."
"Don't you think that there's an underlying reason why Kitahara-kun goes around asking other staff members for work?"
This was the first time I'd met such a frightening workaholic in my entire career.
"I'm sorry. For going off on my own accord."
"It's fine. Just be more careful next time."
As always, Mari-san has a short fuse, but she doesn't stay angry for too long.
After chugging down a can of cold black coffee, she's back to her usual self.
"…If you have that much time to spare, I'll start tripling your usual workload, so make due with what you have for now."
"Just kidding. I brought back a lot of work with me, so help me out. I've got interviews in four different languages. I'll even throw in a raise."
"I can't work with anything other than English or French. I might take twice as much time with it. …Wouldn't you be better off asking someone else…?"

"Even though you accept as many assignments as you possibly can, you divide your work into things you can and can't do… In terms of doing odd jobs, you're already on the level of a third-year employee."
"…Isn't the number of odd jobs supposed to decline the longer you work for a company?"
"However, it seems I have to warn you one more time. Kitahara, don't you think you're working too hard for a part-timer?"
"I think that's because I'm working under you, Mari-san…"
I can't believe I'm hearing this from someone who increased my workload threefold just a minute ago.
"I heard this from a friend in the HR department, but… you said you wanted to work under someone who gives the most unreasonable tasks during your interview, right?"
"…I thought I'd get the hang of the job faster if I did that."
"Kitahara… just how much of a masochist are you?"
In that case, I guess the fact that they made me your subordinate makes you a huge sadist.
"I requested it so that I could pack in as much experience as possible. I… want to become a publisher."
"Is that really all there is to it?"
"Of course. In the end, this is still just a part-time job for me."
"To me, it just seems like you're purposely trying to make yourself suffer as much as possible."
"…Have I hit the nail on the head?"
"Don't you think that you're straining yourself even more than I am, though?"
"I've got plenty of experience under my belt, so I can push myself hard because I know exactly where my breaking point is."
"It's just that I tend to make the people around me worry since my breaking point is pretty high."
"And you have no qualms about boasting, I see…"
I don't enjoy her trying to analyze me at all. Truth be told, I'd like her to stop. But it's certainly true that she has way more experience in life than I do.
As I throw away my can into the recycle bin in resignation, I attempt to sneakily run back into the editing department…
"Oh, and don't you dare take any work home."
"Ahh, I guess I'm busted. Just as I was casually thinking about doing that."
Even as I'm about to leave, Mari-san seems to be a lot more nitpicky than usual today.
"No need to worry about things like information leaks or compliance. Since you're a part-timer, just listen to your employer."
"Besides, even if you took your work home, it's not like you'd get a pay raise. You're still just a part-timer, you know?"
"Rather than that, I'm trying to be more reliable. Maybe I'll get more important assignments next time."
"Like I said, you're still just a part-timer…"
"Even when I do go home, the only other thing I have to do is study."
"Don't say such lonely things even though you're a university student. You can meet lots of people at clubs or mixers, can't you?"
"There's a lot of people like me at Houjou University, you know? Boring people with no particular interests, that is."
…Did that come across as too gloomy? Even the usually firm Mari-san looks a bit taken aback.
"W-Well then, work hard. Actually, no, try not to work too hard."
"Ah, I almost forgot. Here, a present to cheer you up."
She hands me a souvenir doll keychain that you could probably find in a souvenir shop anywhere around the world.
It wouldn't make the recipient particularly happy or disappointed. It's just a plain, handcrafted gift.
"Don't worry, I'm just trying to harass you a bit."
"Isn't harassment something you do to make a person worry?"
Well, as long as I overlook the fact that the person who made this has incredibly poor taste.
"Well, you don't have to take it if you think it's harassment, you know?"
I'm sure that when she found this thing, she was imagining how speechless its recipient would be while cracking a grin.
…Yeah, just like the expression she has on her face right now.
"As if. I'll gratefully accept it… But I won't treasure it too much."
If I remember correctly, I know a person who likes these kinds of weird things.
"Whatever, it'd be weirder if you actually decided to carry it around."
…Really, why did she even buy this kind of thing in the first place?
"Well then, please excuse me for today. I was told not to work too hard just a little while ago."
"Then put that document back. I just told you not to take anything home."
After burning through all my energy, I collapsed on my bed as soon as I got home. …Just as I planned.
Staring at the familiar ceiling I've been staring at for the past three years since I moved in, the white light indifferently greeted my return as usual.
No one can bother me in here. It's like my own personal castle.
It's an apartment that can even separate me from my mother, who might as well have been the air to begin with. A clean apartment that I've always longed for.
Just a ten minute walk from Minami-Suetsugu Station. And only a half-hour train ride from my old house.
The rent's 80,000 yen. Even though I work such long hours every day, more than half of what I earn is spent on this place.
Hearing that, most people I know would be surprised and wonder why I'm not living with my parents.
But the way I see it, now that I'm finally capable of living independently, it's actually harder to find a valid reason to live with them.
There are people who would say that living alone in an apartment is too luxurious for a university student, even if it's just a studio apartment.
But since I'm able to live in a place that I rent with my own hard-earned money, I couldn't care less about what other people think.
I'm still relying on my parents to pay for my tuition, but I plan on repaying them in full after I get a real job.
After all that's taken care of, I'll be able to truly call myself "Merely an independent man named Kitahara Haruki."
"Let's go out for a drink this Saturday. Meet at Onjuku Station by 6 o'clock. Come even if you're dying!"
Even now, Takeya texts me around three times a week.
Although he tries to call once in a while, I have classes in the morning and work from afternoon till midnight, so our schedules simply don't match.
But the fact that he still contacts me frequently like this makes him a great friend of mine, even if I take into account the fact that he's still a massive playboy.
"Sorry, I've got plans to die at my job again this Saturday. Thanks for the invite, though. Bye."
I rarely accept any invitations to hang out with him these days.
Just as I desired, I can't keep my eyes open any longer.
Fatigue soon envelops my entire body, but it feels so pleasant.
The reason why I can no longer move isn't because of physical fatigue, but rather, because my brain is too tired to even think.
I'll take a shower as soon as I wake up, and then start reviewing for classes during breakfast.
If I'm lucky enough to have spare time, I'll continue on the work I smuggled back last night.
Right when I'm about to enter work mode, I always have to leave for my first class.
Hopefully, tomorrow will be as busy as today… because these busy days are the most enjoyable to me. As I pray for that in my heart, I drift off into sleep slowly but hastily.
Seeking to slip into a deep sleep in which I won't even dream.
"Eeh～ are you sure? You're really gonna give me something this cute?"
I already knew she'd like it, but to think she'd like it this much…
"The quality of the shrunken head isn't bad at all. And the wrinkles, and the subtle softness of this thing, it's awesome!"
"On second thought, give it back so I can throw it away."
I've always thought she was kind of weird, but I never expected her to prove me right to such an extent.
"Should I attach it to my bag? Or maybe my house keys…"
"Do whatever you want with it, just don't tell anyone you got it from me, got it?"
"Why? Don't want people to get the wrong idea and think we're in a relationship?"
"Actually, I couldn't care less about that part…"
I would just really hate it if people thought I'm the type of person who buys these stupid things.
"Oh yeah, let me treat you to lunch. Consider it me returning the favor for this little thing, as well as for yesterday."
"Can you not show me such a bad omen? It's bad enough that it's almost the season for the first snowfall."
"…You say that, but you know that I'm treating you to pasta at an outdoor cafe, right? With dessert and coffee included, no less!"
"Do you really want it to snow that badly?"
You could get three lunch set As with that kind of money…
"Well, snow sounds good to me! It's white, cold, and beautiful～! What's the matter, Haruki, you don't like it?"
I almost let something weird like, "I don't dislike it, but it's painful for me" slip out.
"Let's get going, then. You don't mind walking a little, right?"
The outdoor cafe is in the opposite direction from our laboratory in Building 3. It's located on the edge of Building 6, at the southern side of the university campus.
It's a place I haven't set foot in ever since I became a third-year student.
"Hurry, hurry. There won't be any seats left if we don't hurry, you know?"
Well, "I'm sure it'll be fine…" Or so I told myself for no apparent reason, anyway.
"Wow, it sure has gotten colder, huh?"
"Every year after the university festival, it sure starts feeling like winter. Maybe I should wear an overcoat starting next week."
"Hey, hey, never mind that. What's happening with the mixer with the medical students this weekend?"
"The plan was to go for a bit of karaoke at Que Sera around 6 o'clock and then head to Florence at 8 o'clock, but…"
"Due to a little bit of a problem we've run into, we're still not sure if we're having the meetup at all…"
"Eh, what do you mean? Didn't you say that they were completely on board with it, Yumi?"
"The thing is… The one who made them very excited is…"
"…Aaah, so that's it. The problem is that their real target is saying she's not going."
"Huh? Ah, sorry… I've already got plans with some friends that day…"
"Could you just try coming to karaoke, at least?"
"Yeah, you disappearing halfway through is actually exactly what we're hoping fo… Er, I mean, there shouldn't be any issue if you do!"
"You don't have to be so shameless about it…"
"I'm very sorry. I really can't go. Because…"
"Ah, come to think of it, the project we were assigned before the university festival… When's it due again?"
"Obviously, it was due before the university festival started, Princess No-Show."
"Ahh, darn it, this was a golden opportunity too…"
"Not even the medical students in our university interest her, huh… Do we have no choice but to bring out the real lawyers and doctors?"
"N-No, that's not the issue here, is it? I've never seen her show up to these kinds of events to begin with."
"Izumi… You haven't shown up at the seminar for over two weeks already, have you?"
"Since you're always eager to help… I don't suppose you'd be willing to do my assignment too…?"
"No. Impossible. Never. I only help people when they're willing to work hard themselves."
"Well, in your case, the more you try to avoid people, the more famous you seem to get."
"Stop increasing the number of men you've shot down already. All you need to do is find a boyfriend like anyone else would, and stuff like this wouldn't… Actually, it might still keep happening…"
"Hm? What's wrong? Are you feeling alright?"
"I was working my butt off at the time! I can't even put into words how much blood and sweat I poured into it…!"
"Really, Izumi, you are so honest. I see you in a different light now… You can't even come up with a decent lie anymore."
"Come on, don't just stand there. Let's go, Setsuna!"

The outdoor cafe is in the opposite direction from our Literature Department in Building 3. It's located on the edge of Building 6, which houses the Political Science and Economics Department at the southern side of the university campus.
In my three years of studying here, this is a place I've never set foot in since changing departments.
"I'm sure it'll be fine," I thought… Yeah, right. How could I make such a careless mistake?
This is no place for us "Literature" students. It's the "Public Policy" students' territory.
And I shouldn't have anything to do with this place…
"Let's hurry, Izumi. There'll be no seats left if we don't."
"What is it? Are you really feeling sick? Need to go to the infirmary?"
A chill crawls up my back.
Then again, I guess winter is right around the corner.
For the third time since I came to Houjou University…
The season of White Album arrives once again.
"I-I see. You want to be a publisher. That's why…"
"Eh? Ah, I don't think so, I think literature will suit you well. After all, Haruki-kun, you're very good at writing."
"Is that so… You've already thought it through. I'm no match for you after all."
"Me? No, not yet. Even though there's only two years left, I still can't think of anything for my future yet."
"I see, I see… You're planning to transfer to the Literature Department."
"Well, of course. Even if we're in different buildings, we're still on the same campus. If we want to meet up, we can see each other every day."
"H-Hey… can I still… keep calling you from now on?"
"O-Oh… well, if you're that busy, you don't have to force yourself. You're working hard every day, huh, Haruki-kun. How many part-time jobs are you working now?"
"I see… it must be hard on you. Please take care of yourself, okay?"
"Eh, oh, um… I don't mean anything specific by that, um… I'm just… wondering."
I didn't wake up because of the dream. I simply woke up.
It's just that it's barely been 30 minutes since I went to sleep. And somehow, I'm sweating so much it's enough to make me feel sick.
As I turn on the lights, my eyes, initially flinching from their radiance, slowly adapt to the brightness.
I shake my head slowly, wanting reality to settle into my brain, yet that familiar memory keeps forcibly recurring in my mind.
…I must return to the present as soon as possible.
After forcing off the wet T-shirt that had stuck to my skin, I rush into the bathroom and immediately turn on the shower tap.
Caring for neither the initial splash of cold water nor the subsequent, brief sensation of hot water before the shower reaches its set temperature, I thoroughly soak myself, starting from my head.
Each time I receive those intense sensations through my skin, I pray that they wake up my body while numbing the thoughts emerging in my mind.
Those thoughts being recollections from three years ago, thoughts I'd tightly locked within a drawer of my memory.
My encounter with Setsuna. My encounter with Setsuna's singing.
And my encounter with the true self of a certain girl named Ogiso Setsuna after peeling away her disguise, all three years ago.
We performed on stage together, did foolish things together and laughed together. The irreplaceable past that the three of us share, dating back three years ago.
Although there were a couple of twists and turns, we managed to understand each other in the end, as our words, passions, and lips drew closer to each otherーall of that happened three years ago.
Her bashful and mischievous smile from three years ago has disappeared, and a tearful smile, born from her three years of enduring, giving up and pushing herself to the edge, is painted in its place.
She's becoming more and more beautifulーalmost infuriatingly so.
Setsuna, who was already pretty, sweet, and charming during high school, has now become even more of an astounding beauty.
Even more so than three years ago. Even more so than one year ago. And even more so than just earlier this year.
While she's almost never revealed her true self since then, she remains a stunning person to those around her.
Everyone was captivated by Setsuna. Her gorgeous figure was etched into everyone's minds.
And yet Setsuna never even had eyes for any other man.
She continued to force herself to smile for me. I felt as if she could see straight through my heart with her lonesome smile.
Even so, her smile never faded. She remained by my side the entire time.
She desperately tried to stay by my side.
By my side, by the side of the one who destroyed everything and wounded Setsuna more deeply than anyone ever possibly could.
…Not once did she leave my side.
No matter how hard I try, my heart can't come back to the present.
I hadn't seen Setsuna in a month.
In the past week, I've steadily tried to exert my brain completely, working myself to exhaustion so that I wouldn't have time to think about it.
And yet in the end, all it took was another glimpse of Setsuna's miserable smile for all of my efforts to go to waste, and I've been pulled back into the past.
When will you start hating me?
How deeply must you hurt yourself until you'll stop forgiving me?
"Yo, long time no see. I see you still have those dead fish eyes after pulling an all-nighter again today."
"I just gave you a light tap. You like to exaggerate everything, as always…"
"What you wanted to say was 'your eyes are as rotten as a dead fish's after pulling an all-nighter,' right? Don't omit stuff like that. It's not proper use of Japanese, you know?"
"…And you're as nitpicky as ever, too. I just don't get you."
Even amidst our university lives, if there exists only a single person who would greet me with his fists before his voice, it would be Takeya.

Most people who've done this to me in the past have subsequently changed their attitude toward me after being fed up with my unending lectures, though that's simply a matter of how long we've known one another.
Being one of my very few friends from high school, I'm grateful to have him as my friend, even if he can be difficult to deal with at times.
"Going home already? You're early today. Don't you have to stop by the seminar?"
"Not today. They're hosting a joint party in the seminar today."
"…That's the one thing people would usually make sure to show up to, you know?"
"I don't have the money, time, or interest for it."
"Since it's the Literature Department's seminar, shouldn't you have a harem in there? How in the world could you choose not to go?"
"…I have no idea what you're talking about."
A friend that I'm grateful for, a friend that's just a little bit too much to handle, and a friend that knows me like the back of his hand…
We were together in the Public Policy Department up until our second year, and we ended up fighting when he discovered that I changed departments.
"Well, whatever. Wanna go have a drink together, Haruki? We should spend some quality time together, just between us two men."
"You don't have to force yourself. You're the type of guy who would drown in alcohol if you didn't have a girl to hit on while drinking."
"Why am I still friends with you after all these years?"

Nine-tenths of his daily conversation consists of pick-up lines, complaints or narcissistic bragging, but when this joker decides to talk seriously with me, his words seem to hit my heart where it hurts every time, almost fatally so.
And yet his lack of patience doesn't win him any fights in the end.
"In any case, I still have a part-time job today. Didn't I tell you that in my text?"
…No, perhaps this guy simply can't bear witness to the way I act any longer.
"At least try to value hanging out man-to-man once in a while. You can spare me one day, can't you?"
"…Assuming it's truly going to be us 'hanging out man-to-man.'"
It appears he's finally remembered the one time he attempted to use the same trick on me before.
…Which causes the tearful smile of a certain someone to suddenly resurface in my head once more, something that immediately returns my clouded mind to its senses.
"…Maybe next time. I'll be the one to contact you then."
Even now, I still think of Takeya as an irreplaceable friend.
Seeing him worry about me like this brings grateful tears to my eyes.
"Haruki… Hey, listen to me. How long are you gonna…"
Still, I don't want to see him every day like in the old days.
If I were to do that, I'd only drag everyone around me into playing a charade that would make everyone miserable again.
"You should lay off those high school girls already. You're a third-year university student, for crying out loud."
"…I appreciate your honest concern, but I don't see why you're bringing this up now."
As Takeya turns to look where I'm pointing my chin at, he seems to finally catch on to what I'm implying is about to happen.
The nostalgic uniform of our high school and the girl wearing it, who appears to be waiting for someone.
Well, she only appeared to be waiting for someone until just now. The moment she noticed Takeya's face, her expression changed as if to say she's found her target.
"Aa-ah, man. She seems really mad, right? Didn't I tell you to keep it under three women at a time?"
Given her change of expression, what happens next should be some sort of deja vu.
After this, she'll either be crying and clinging onto Takeya or angrily yelling at him… Come to think of it, there was that one time where he was immediately slapped across the cheek.

Oh well, I'm used to such scenarios, nevertheless. I should be capable of turning my head and pretending not to hear anything, all the while ignoring any nauseating content of their lover's quarrel that my ears happen to pick up.

And when Takeya sees the girl off after changing her crying face to a smile after no time at all, the time for me lecturing him with something starting with, "It's about time you…" would ensue after gently patting his shoulder.
"No, wait a minute. I don't plan on either confirming or denying your accusations, but let me just say that I have absolutely no idea who that girl is."
This instance should be no exception; the girl's already walking straight toward us.
"That's even worse. You shouldn't ever forget the face of a girl who you brought to tears."
Her face is obviously filled with rage, but it's because of that expression that I feel somewhat reassured. …It's a better response than having to see a girl cry, anyway.
"How could I possibly remember every single one? And unlike you, I didn't stick with only one girl and then made her cry like there's no tomorrow."
"Ugh… Hey, there's a line, and you know it!"
"We need to talk. Please come with me for a moment."
"A better response than having to see a girl cry" is something that only applies to cases where I in particular am not the culprit.
I realize now that I have no memory of any situation in which an unknown girl abruptly appeared and glared at me with such hostility up until this point.
"Well, what happened? You couldn't bring Haruki here after all?"
"Let's see, two glasses of draft beer, a Caesar salad, a mixed pizza with diced steak…"
"Also, I'll have fried tofu in a meat stew and dried squid with salted mackerel. That'll be all for now. …There was nothing I could do. A lot happened."
"You really think you can get away just like that? Do you have any idea how much hard work I put into it this time…"
"With the exact same trick you attempted the last time, you know? He's on high alert this time because of that."
"Really, Haruki… How long does he plan to let this drag on!?"
"And that's not all… The worst possible competitor interrupted at the worst possible time, too…"
"You'll know exactly what I mean if you meet her. …I guess they say that there's always at least three people that are completely alike in the world."
"Hold on, Takeya, could you please explain this more simply…"
"Oh, there she is! Over here, this way!"
"…Good evening. Am I interrupting something after all?"
"'It may be a bit early to ask, but do you have anything in mind for your next work?'"
"Um… 'We were hoping to do a musical, but Kevin wouldn't agree to it' …Hm?"
"…'Something along the lines of a musical would be nice. I'm sure Kevin (The producer, Mr. Kevin Crowney) would be mad and vehemently disapprove, though (laughs)'…"
"…Oh? Didn't you say that you might not be able to come today?"
After hearing a greeting from behind me, I glance at the clock to see that it's almost 8 PM right now.
…It seems that as many as two hours have passed while I was single-mindedly delving into the work I have with me.
"Saying that I might not be able to come also means I might be able to come…"
Did your girlfriend cancel your date or something?"
"Yes. That's right, it's just like that. I'm useless…"
"…Don't put on that happy face and nod in agreement. Do you even realize how depressing you sound?"
"…Don't put on that whiny face, either. Was I right?"
"…Please refrain from talking to me too much. I have to finish all this work by the end of the day."
Even I'm aware of the fact that my excuse sounds unnatural…
But within twenty hours, my weakness was exposed to me twice, and both times I was told, "Everyone has moments like that."
"That's the work I assigned you. If I remember correctly, that's not due until all the way next week, on Monday?"
"You'll already have new work waiting for me by then, won't you, Mari-san? That's just how you work."
"Well, you have a point. Perfect, we just decided to work on a new project in our meeting earlier."
She can just about write a magazine on her own, even though she hasn't been working for a full five years with this company.

"Well, you can go the extra mile if you're telling me you won't push yourself over the edge. But I won't forgive you if it ends up affecting the quality of your report. We're trying to make money with the material you're writing, you know?"
After leaving a few words of concern and an unrelated message, Mari-san heads back to her desk with a massive amount of unfinished work.
After this, I'm sure she won't talk to me for the next few hours. No doubt, she's even more of a workaholic than I am.
"'Finally, please give a message to fellow Japanese fans.'"
And that's why I love this place.
All the people around me are "experienced adults," so I can continue to be myself in peace…
If they don't know anything, I can easily keep my distance.
Don't seek the truth from someone you're not familiar with.
Do you believe that you can apply your morals to another person's life?
Maybe that person is simply trying to speak the truth, too?
I know you'll retort by saying "I'm not messing around," but I know you are, so stop messing around…
You ask me how I know? You ask me why I judge other people by my own standards?
You don't even understand that, right…? That's exactly why I said you don't understand anything.
"Oh, so your girlfriend's name is Koharu-chan, Kitahara? Seems like you two got into quite a fight, huh?"
"I was just in the middle of mentally praising you, please don't ruin it…"
Aren't you just like I was three years ago?
"I'm her classmate. Ever since we enrolled."
The girl, who had bluntly introduced herself as Sugiura Koharu, subsequently mentioned the name of Yada Mihoko.
Just from hearing that name, I immediately understood the reason this girl had come looking for me.
And while I'm at it, I can feel my sense of guilt slowly welling up.
"Hang on. A girl from high school confessed to you…? Haruki, do you even understand the situation you're in!?"
"That's why I rejected her… Isn't that obvious?"
"…And why would it be obvious, exactly?"
"You're a third-year university student, so you don't want to waste your time on a girl much younger than you, is that it?"
"That's exactly what you meant when you told me…"
Lecturing people isn't only for their sake…
"She's been absent from school the past two days."
"When I visited her, she couldn't stop crying because she was coldly rejected by the Kitahara-sensei whom she respected so much…"
"It's just a misunderstanding on your part. Please forget about it."
I had only said that reflexively. Looking back on it right now, I felt it was a natural response.
Even so, for me to have put it so inappropriately toward someone, and to a younger girl of all people…
After reconsidering what I had done, I finally realized the sin I had committed.
"I'll send her a text and apologize to her."
I'm sure she didn't have any bad intentions. She was only trying to clearly get her message across to me.
I had said such cold words to a girl like it was nothing, and that was truly unforgivable.
"But still, I can't accept her confession. I'm sorry."
It was a necessary evil I had to endure to prevent myself from committing an even greater sin.
That's why I had no choice but to bear the lesser of the two evils.
"As a student, Yada-san is an ideal girl. She never forgets to ask how I'm doing when she attends my class, greets me politely, and she also stays late to ask me questions…"
"Wow, she made it really obvious, huh? You should have noticed sooner…"
"That's why I couldn't help but feel happy about it, but it's possible that I got too close to her. If that's the case, I apologize for my actions."
That single sentence managed to quell the heavy mood that otherwise couldn't have been brushed off by our usual comic relief character.
In an instant, the girl who had been glaring at me the entire time changed her cold expression to something softer and gentler…
"Kitahara-san, you're more reasonable than I thought you'd be. I can see that you already understand Mihoko's situation… I'm relieved."
At that moment, it was like a gust of warm wind blew through the building.
"Come to think of it, though, you're pretty brave, Koharu-chan. You actually yelled at a university student you've never even seen before."
"It doesn't really have anything to do with bravery. I just wanted to do what's right."
It's hard to explain why, but that doesn't feel like a proper response…
"…Sounds like something I'd hear from a certain good friend of mine."
I don't quite understand what she means by that either…
"Also, being called 'Koharu-chan' by someone I just met is a little…"
It's probably the sight of this girl's gentle expression that led me to think that.
Both her dignified expression from before and her current gentle expression suit Takeya's tastes, which is to say any normal person's tastes…
"So I suppose that's all? I still have to go for my part-time job."
…But what difference does it make if I think about these things?
"Oh, you have to go, Haruki? Then here, cover the bill…"
"Eh? Given that you just ditched me, you've left me with no choice but to get more acquainted with Koharu-chan."
"I don't recall ever agreeing to the second half of that comment…"
"…You heard her. Come on, let's go, Takeya."
"Well, too bad, then. See you again, Koharu-chan. Ah, here's my mail address. Let's meet again next time, just the two of us."
"Um, Kitahara-san. About what we just talked about…"
After figuring out how to deal with Takeya, Sugiura Koharu looked straight at me once again.
"Yeah, I'll be sure to contact Yada-san. See you, then."
"Please talk it over with her properly, okay?"
As expected, the soft expression she had for a while tensed up once again…
"I understand. I'll apologize for my cold attitude."
"Don't just apologize, okay? Please talk to her properly."
"Just apologizing won't solve anything. Please tell her the reason why you rejected her."
Then, as she started speaking with the tense expression from earlier, the mood shifted back again…
"Mihoko is serious about her feelings toward you, so please give her a serious reply."
"You have a reason, don't you? You can't accept Mihoko's feelings no matter what because of that reason, right?"
"If that's the case, please tell her that reason. And then, please convince Mihoko with it."
Just like that, she returned to her relentless self.
In a way, I could also see an unrelenting justice brimming in her eyes.
"If she continues to be this depressed, I'm worried she might not be able to fall in love again."
"Okay, we got it. So all we need to do is to help that girl accept it, right? We'll take care of it. I'm partially to blame as well, after all."
I imagine it's because my expression instantly changed.
Takeya, who had only been joking around, now stood between the two of us seriously, trying his best to defuse this situation.
"Just covering up the truth won't do. Please don't lie, just tell her the truth. If you already have a girlfriend, just tell her that."
"Um, that's… H-He'll work it all out for sure!"
"Mihoko is really serious about it. So if you have to reject her, please be sincere with her… Please."
Sugiura Koharu bowed her head deeply.
She's serious, inflexible and leaves no chance for her opponent to escape. At the same time, she's consistently and entirely honest with herself.
The truth is, it felt so familiar because it sounded like I was listening to myself. I'm incredibly familiar with this line of reasoning, as well.
"L-Let's go, Haruki. We'll contact you later. See y…"
"Why should I tell something like that to a total stranger?"
I reacted in the worst conceivable way.
"…!? Ha-Haruki… It's fine. Just let me handle this, okay?"
"Even if I properly talk it over with her, even if I tell her everything, would she accept it? How can you be so sure she will?"
I vented the unsightly emotions buried deep inside to a girl who's three years younger than me.
"T-That's… The problem doesn't lie with the other person then; the problem is inside your heart!"
"You kept saying it was for her sake over and over again, but now the problem is inside my heart as soon as it's convenient for you?"
"I told you to stop it, Haruki… No matter what the reason is, you can't be arguing here!"
"Why should I reveal the part of me that even I want to look away from to someone who fell in love with me on her own for no good reason!?"
My dark emotions erupt like lava and envelop my surroundings with cloudy, pitch-black ash.
"H-How can… you say it like that? Is that all Mihoko's feelings mean to you?"
"Exactly. That's the kind of person I am. Why couldn't she understand? Why couldn't she hate me…?"
Through a small gap in the dark cloud, one could see the burning magma that was about to erupt.
"Even so, she's fallen in love with you regardless of who you are. It can't be helped!"
"'It can't be helped' doesn't cut it! Don't fall in love with someone like me!"
At the very next moment, I began to regret my foolish words and actions.
"Sorry, I really don't have any more time."
I left that place as if I was trying to escape.
"Haruki! Hey, wait! …Sorry, I'll pay you back next time. I'll get in touch with you later, bye!"
…Wanting to chase after someone but being held back by the bill must be incredibly awkward.
"Don't fall in love with someone like me, huh…"
"…It's nothing. Maybe I've had a bit too much to drink?"
"What's the matter, Takeya? You don't look so good. The two girls here should be a lot better than the ones you see at your average mixer."
"I have to admit that's true, but on the other hand, I've never been to a mixer as dead as this one…"
"No matter what you say, Setsuna is here only for viewing. Please keep your hands off her～!"
"I'm fully combat ready here, and I have no problem putting my defensive capabilities to use if necessary."
"Don't you dare. The table of men over there has been eyeing Setsuna for a while. If you leave now, they'll come over for sure, right?"
"Wouldn't that be ideal for you, Miss Combat-Ready?"
"Oh, you're terrible, Takeya! Just get out of here!"
"Ahaha… You two are getting along well as usual."

"Oh, does it really look that way?"

"Not at all."
"Ah, excuse me. Another gin and tonic, please."
"Oi, Io, why can't you react more like a normal woman would? Like, do something that could make a really desirable guy fall for you, you know?"
"Well, it's because you're not cute at all…"
"'Oi, Io' is a palindrome! I got teased with that a lot back in the day…"
"Come on, Setsuna, talk some sense into her. This pathetic sports-junkie hasn't ever had a single boyfriend even though she's a third-year in university."
"Compared to a guy who's been dumped more than a thousand times in the past three years, I wonder which is more pathetic."
"Ahaha… Hahaha… Really, honestly… some things never change."
"S-Sorry… It's just that I really had so much fun…"
"I'm so thankful to have the both of you with me, Io and Takeya-kun, it makes me want to thank God."
"Instead of thanking God, you could just thank us instead, you know."
"You can always count on us to go out for some drinks or hang out. No matter when, we'll be here for you, Setsuna."
"Yeah, thank you. Really, thank you so much."
"I just… It's all because I have my family and friends like the two of you… that I can live on as Ogiso Setsuna."
"I hope we'll keep getting along in the future. Let's keep being friends."
"No, you don't need to make a promise."
"Because if we make a promise, I'll become dependent on it."
"I swear I won't ever end our friendship. And until you want me to, I won't leave you."
"Because I would come to keep believing in that promise, and end up being hurt countless times."
"Well, what should we do after this? Tomorrow is a holiday too…"
"Wanna look for a quiet place to drink again? Maybe go bowling? Or maybe, enjoy a live performance from Setsuna-chan after all this time…"
"Ah, sorry, I have to go home soon. My dad will start worrying about me."
"…I see that 10 PM curfew of yours still hasn't changed."
"…Some things never change, even in the Ogiso family."
"I'm very sorry. You guys came to cheer me up, but all I did was ruin everything…"
"We wouldn't have invited you if we weren't prepared for that kind of stuff."
"…Thank you, Io. I really appreciate it."
"That's why I'll give you a call again some other time. Don't you dare reject it!"
"…Let's take you home. The three of us should be heading back now."
"No, that's fine. I don't want to bother you two any longer."
"He was planning to come, but he couldn't because of his job. He felt really bad about it… He's still worrying about you, Setsuna-chan."
"No, I'll be embarrassed if you thank me like this. After all, I was told to relay that message, yet I forgot about it until now."
"Well, he's busy running all over the place."
"Really? Is he tired? Did he look like he's eating properly? Did he say he's getting enough sleep?"
"Ahaha… You sound like you're his mother, Setsuna-chan."
"He's just really busy right now! He has to focus on himself for the time being."
"So that's why… even though you might not see him very often, please, don't hate Haruki, okay?"
"How could I… ever come to hate him…?"
"Uh, y-yeah… Of course. Well, good night!"
"After all… I'm the one who's been making Haruki-kun suffer all this time."
"What are you trying to accomplish by telling such a transparent lie?"
"I don't want to hear that from the one who organized such a transparent event and failed to accomplish anything in the end."
"It's all your fault for not being able to drag Haruki here."
"You butt into others' problems too much. You're just like how Haruki used to be."
"But still… it's been three years, right? Why does it have to drag on like this? It's about time they got back together."
"It's been three years. Why are they still thinking about each other? It's about time they broke up."
"…That's the right way to solve this. It's just that it's not something either of us want."
"…The two of us are nice people, huh?"
"Doesn't mean much if we're the ones saying it."
"So what should we do next? It's a holiday tomorrow…"
"Of course, you don't have to accompany me. Anyway, see you next year."
"I seriously hope you can figure out the reason why I'm being such a nice guy…"
"'Itayama Kazuhisa. Serie B, plays for Ricci. 17 years old. Moved to Italy alone after dropping out of Fujiyama-Kita High School…'"
"Phew… I'm going to go grab a midnight snack. Want anything, Kitahara?"
"I'm good. I'll be leaving after I'm done with this."
"That's good, it's better if you go home early. Good work today… But I'll take that back if you're still here when I come back."
Although she said, "It's better if you go home early," if she's getting a midnight snack now, when exactly does she herself plan to go home?
But I don't have the right to say that because I missed the last train. Now I have to spend 40 minutes walking back home.
I guess I'm lucky, though. I'll probably be so tired I won't even dream today. Or maybe I'll sleep right through the holiday tomorrow.
I'd been considering changing departments for a long time.
I realized that I didn't have much of an interest in public policy when I was still taking the basic courses.
In addition, I was planning to work at places where I would have to write a lot, and it made me think.
When I finally made up my mind, I tried to use the positive benefits to convince my friends.
…Of course, that's not all there was to it. Some of my friends already know the real reason.
I left my home to rent an apartment close to the university. In order to make enough money to get by, I worked numerous part-time jobs.
I participated in lectures that had nothing to do with my specialization. I'm also very active in the newspaper club, going to their seminars and working with their social media.
In any case, I tried my best to cut down my free time… to run away from Setsuna.
"'Hirasaka Miyuki. A patissier working at Sherry Hotel, located in Paris. 23 years old. She won a contest sponsored by a confectionery company when she was just 19 years old…'"
After all, Setsuna holds no resentment toward me for what I've done to her.
Even though I betrayed her in an unequivocally cruel way, she went on smiling for me as if nothing ever happened.
She's not forcibly closing our distance whenever I try to run away, though she's not distancing herself from me on her own accord either, only looking at me with that same gentle gaze every time.

A scene that excites and fills my chest with butterflies whenever I lay eyes on it, overflowing me with a desire to touch such a beautiful girl both in body and in soul as I clumsily approach her, unable to help myself.
But the moment I inch closer to touching the depths of such recollections of memories, I would remind myself how cruel I'd been to her and run away before her very eyes.
It's a cruel loop that's repeated for the umpteenth time, and it shows me not only exactly how tired I am, but how tired Setsuna is, as well…
I resent the man I am for taking away what Setsuna could have been. And I can't forgive the very same man who had stolen the voice of the songstress who I had once admired.
That's why I can only give up on Setsuna. To become a person she hates and detests.
I wish that Ogiso Setsuna would return to her true self dating back to our high school daysーsomeone who didn't belong to just a single person, but to everyone.
Instead of being chained down by a person such as myself, I wish she could fly freely like she used to.
If one day, these wishes of mine come true…
That's when I'll finally be able to recover from this deep slump I've been stuck in for the longest time, or so I hope.
Dreaming about it is too painful, so I try to escape into reality, but before I realize it, I'm unconsciously thinking about it again.
I completely forgot about the article I was supposed to be editing… Even though the draft is due tomorrow morning.
Mari-san went on an overseas business trip to gather materials to write this special issue of Kaiou Graph.

If I remember correctly, this article's title is 'Japanese Youths Active Around The World.' An article that reports on young Japanese people who are not well-known within Japan, yet are famous abroad…
Right before I closed the report, I scrolled all the way to the bottom…
Among the professional soccer player and famous patissier, among all the famous names, at the very end, one name stood out to me.
"Touma Kazusa. Trustee International Piano Competition, second place."
"I wish she could fly freely, just like she used to…"
"I see… So he ended up giving you a call. Isn't that great, Mihoko?"
"Eh… ah, um, I see. That's… um, uh… I suppose that might be the case."
"But listen, I've been thinking… Isn't this for the best? Like, the stuff he said came across as a bit weird, so…"
"Th-That's… No, I'd never actually met him before… but with all you've told me about him, Mihoko…"
"Ah… Sorry, I'm sorry. I shouldn't have badmouthed him even though I don't know anything about him. Yeah, that's right, I won't understand unless I actually talk to him."
"B-But… hasn't he already quit that job? How exactly do you plan to meet him and talk things through?"
"You want to just walk into his university? Are you really up to the task, Mihoko?"
"…Right? That's why I think it's better to just give up on him already…"
"I get it. I get it, okay? So don't cry anymore, please."
"That's right, you have to talk to him face to face one more time. You have to get some closure for your own feelings."
"Hang in there, Mihoko. I'll do everything I can to help you out."
"Yeah, yeah… Well, I think you should come back to school soon. Everyone really misses you."
"What's up? Was that Yada? She's not coming today either?"
"Ah… Good morning, Sayuri, Ako. I see the two of you barely made it in time again today."
"What, are you still trying to cover for her? It's not like there's anything wrong now, is there? She's almost guaranteed to get a recommendation anyway, so she can afford to skip classes."
"It's not just that. She's had a lot going on lately."
"She's being a bit too selfish, isn't she? It feels like she's completely dependent on you because you always care for others too much, Koharu."
"Hey, are we really taking Yada with us? To our graduation trip, I mean."
"Of course we are. Why are you even bringing that up at this point?"
"Wasn't she arguing with people a bit too much during our school trip? It kind of ruined the mood at the inn."
"She can get really extreme with projecting sometimes as well, you know. It's like her surroundings have to turn gloomy too the moment she feels down herself."
"She only tends to argue because she's being honest to us about her feelings. Aren't you two just being harsh on her because you guys care deeply about her too?"
"Leaving her aside, I wish you'd worry about my lack of funds more. I probably won't be able to make it unless I start working part-time soon."
"I can lend you some money if you don't have enough. You won't have to rush to repay me either…"
"Quit it with the bourgeois talk. Come on, homeroom is starting. Let's head back to the classroom."
"That was only for the first half of the year…"
"Yo～! Good morning, Sugiura! You'll be late if you don't hurry!"
"You're the one who's late! And being the class rep doesn't give you the right to run down the hallway, Ogiso!"
"And that's our class rep for the latter half of the year, huh…"
"It's been quite a while since daybreak, after all."
"Nnng… Haaaaah. Speaking of which, what time is it?"
Feeling suspicious, I decided to pop into the Ogishima Laboratory before classes started, and found the source of my suspicions wrapped up in a sleeping bag again.
Still, I'll consider it an improvement that she asked for the time rather than the day after waking up, unlike last week…
"Oh, come on… the morning classes haven't even started yet, right? Just let me lie down for a bit longer. I'm still hungover from all the drinking I did last night…"
Scratch thatーit would be all too pathetic if I were to be satisfied with such a tiny level of improvement.
"There are so many faults here that I don't know where to start, but I'll tell you one thing… If you're not even going to write your paper, then stop staying on campus overnight."
Too pathetic for my future self, anyway.
Izumi slowly crawls out of the sleeping bag and gets up, then fixes her hair while letting out a huge yawn.
"Hurry and get up already. Clean everything up and get out before the upperclassmen get here."
"You're getting a great look at a girl sleeping, so a little hint of bashfulness from you wouldn't hurt, would it?"
"If you really want me to act like that toward you, shouldn't you at least try to put some more appeal into your expressions, gestures, and speech?"
"What? Are you saying you're into girls that are girly through and through, Haruki?"
"…That has nothing to do with this."
"Ah, you're trying to get away from the topic you yourself started!
Though I have a feeling that I'll get retorted tenfold if I were to continue, so I'll stop there."
"Don't block my counterattack by dropping the subject while still getting gratification for yourself. That's foul play."
"Heheh, well, what brings you to see an unappealing woman like me so early in the morning, Haruki?"
"The fact that you're only ever on campus in the morning…"
It annoys me to give Izumi the impression that I've come just to see her, but given that it's the truth this one time, I'm incapable of coming up with an excuse.
"…Hmm? Have you finally gotten serious about me? Was all that stuff about putting more appeal into my actions earlier just an attempt to hide your true feelings?"
"I asked the professor to extend the deadline on that paper you forgot to submit before the winter break. You have to complete it no matter what this time."
She really shouldn't be putting all her thoughts on her face. She's so easy to read.
"It seems that I'm now in charge of tutoring you, Izumi. And I have every intention of carrying out my newly appointed role to the letter, so I hope you'll accommodate me."
"…Was the professor actually serious about that?"
Perhaps it's better to say that a lot of what initially came out as merely a joke from him ended up coming true after all.
After all, from the look of her current attendance rate, assignment submission rate and exam results, Izumi isn't too far from being expelled.
When I happened to drop by and express my worry for her, the professor must have thought of me as her last hope.
"Wait a minute, Haaaruki… Why did you go and make such a promise without asking me?"
And, as expected, Izumi is venting her anger at me in response to the unreasonable task she will have to carry out.
"It's totally possible to get away with not submitting papers and assignments without getting noticed!"
…And through her excessively unreasonable comments, as well.
"Well, you should know that they'll definitely notice. They check every student's paper carefully."
"…Well, since it's come to this, you'll help me out. Right, Haruki?"
"Well, maybe a little. Since the professor asked me to…"
"Great, let's split the workload then! Haruki, you will be in charge of choosing the topic, gathering information and writing the paper, and I'll deal with everything else…"
"That's everything already! Do you seriously plan on not doing anything!?"
"I'll watch you work. I'll stay by your side. Ah, only during the morning or at night when I'm free though."
"That's what I'm supposed to say, isn't it…?"
Even then, from the available times she's given me… How many hours a day is she even awake?
"Then again, the only times I see you on campus is when you're sleeping or eating, anyway."
"That's because… I'm only here when I can't fight against my basic human desires, you see."
"What exactly are you doing when you aren't at the university…?"
Let's not think about any other desires of hers aside from sleeping and eating.
"Obviously, I'm out having fun, right? Spending time on things that interest me, maybe? Or perhaps I'm out making a noisy ruckus?"

"There's no context behind any of those things. And you just answered my question with more questions. That's not how you're supposed to talk! To think you call yourself a Japanese literature student…"
"Languages change over time, and so does their usage. Those who pick apart every single tiny detail and force outdated rules are the weird ones if you ask me."
"Fine, whatever you say. The deadline for your paper is this month, so if you don't want to ruin your Christmas and New Year vacation, get to work."
"Hehe… ran away from that one, didn't you?"
"I just told you, whatever you say."
Her impeccable talent for splitting hairs makes even someone like me not want to argue with her…
"In any case, I expect you to free your schedule up for Wednesday evenings after the seminar. Got it?"
"…Are you telling me that I have to come to the seminar?"
"Given that I'm in charge of you now, isn't that obvious?"
"A-And I have to stay in the lab, all alone with you at night, Haruki? …Isn't that dangerous?"
"Don't you worry. The upperclassmen are here at night as well."
"Eeh～? But I can't concentrate if there are too many people around."
"Stop being so self-centered… You really need to start taking your life more seriously."
"Those are some pretty big words for a newcomer."
"If I wasn't like this, a certain someone here would keep using me to do their work for them."
"Fine, then. I'll make an exception and let you take care of me. You should feel lucky that I'm such an understanding friend, Haruki."
If it wasn't me dealing with her, I imagine she'd be violated by now.
Hang on, was Izumi always like this, though?
"So you changed your department? What? So would that make you a first-year here?"
"I see… Hey, if that's the case, we've gotta throw a welcome party! Don't worry about it. We're fellow classmates starting today, right?"
"…So come on, go on and buy us some beer, would you, new guy?"
I sure had some rotten luck to have coincidentally sat next to this woman when I went into the first lecture hall of my specialized course.

I guess it's rare to see someone transferring from Public Policy to Literature, but within a single day, I was dragged to a canned beer welcoming party, an after-party at the cafeteria, and an after-after-party at the bar.
…Wasting all of my hard-earned money from my part-time jobs.
Then again, thanks to these splurges of hers, I was able to remember the faces of everyone within my year in a mere week…
And I ended up being the person everyone relied on when they needed help, much like how I was back in high school.
"Wooah, you have really neat handwriting. Hey, can I borrow your notes for a bit, Kitahara?"
"Eeh, what? You want to attend the Ogishima seminar, Haruki? I heard that there are a bunch of assignments there. Why not go somewhere else?"
"…Oh, well. But make sure you help me out and watch over me so I don't fail the course, okay?"
An attractive-looking face along with a well-proportioned body. And a slightly listless voice that pleasantly tickles one's ears.
