It was the first time I ever met a woman whom I felt no sense of femininity from, despite her appearing very much like one.
1. I'm not very good at dealing with her.
2. It feels nice being with her somehow.
"…People get mad at me a lot because of it. They say my thoughts are plainly visible on my face."
Acquainting with her is an experience that I've never had until now, given that she's the first person that I've ever known that I don't consider to be either a friend or a romantic partner.
"You know, Haruki… you should really treasure the people that are close to you. Once you lose them, it'll be too late."
"…You're the last person in the world I want to be hearing that from."
She doesn't think much before she speaks, but she rarely misses the mark with her words. I'm always torn between calmly retorting or emotionally snapping at her.
And that's one of the reasons why I'm not good at dealing with her.
I can't even tell if she's seen through me completely or if she hasn't seen anything at all.
She always wears such an aloof, air-headed expression, but in contrast, her words can really hit me where it hurts whenever I'm careless.

And even when she's dealing me these emotional blows, she knows how to properly keep her distance like a friend should. She never crosses any lines that she shouldn't, and she never establishes any massive rifts either.
If her actions are spontaneous and natural, she must have a gift for dealing with others. And if these are calculated facades… she must have a gift for tricking others.
…Though I might simply be overthinking it.
"…What are you smiling about? Does being together with me really make you that happy?"
Yeah, it does make me happy.
But if I said that, people would probably give me funny looks, and Izumi would likely accept me with open arms too. All pain and no gain, so there's no way I'd say that.
Even so, just being friends with her does feel nice.
I'm grateful to have someone whose business I can butt into without fear of reservation like this.
"It's just that being able to give you a little boost in motivation isn't something that I wouldn't be happy about, I feel."
"…You sure said that in a roundabout way, Haruki."
Maybe I really am trying to run away.
Since I can't face "girls" straight on anymore, maybe I'm just placing someone who's only "technically a female human being" by my side to help me retain my balance as a guy.
…Regardless, just the fact that I'm able to have such rude thoughts about her already makes this friend of mine, Izumi Chiaki, irreplaceable.
"After all, you're the first person who called out to me after I transferred here, Izumi. I'm grateful for that."
She gets too close at times, but she never goes too far. She knows where to draw the line when dealing with others.
And the gratitude she receives from others all conveniently goes in one ear and out the other.
These shortcomings of hers let me forget the burdens I carry, and provide me with a sort of comfort.
This is the exact kind of feeling I seek from the opposite sex right now. This is why… I can stay as just friends with this girl.
"Then I guess I'll be seeing you on Wednesdays. I'll be taking over your evenings!"
"As well as your body, your brain, and of course, the spare key to your apartment!"
"Don't worry about how I'll get there. I still remember your address."
I sure had some rotten luck to have coincidentally sat next to this woman in my first lecture.

I guess she must have found a public policy student transferring to the Literature Department to be interesting, considering she dragged me to a canned beer welcoming party, an after-party at the cafeteria, and an after-after-party at the bar.
And even after she was dead drunk, she barged into my apartment without a moment's hesitation. Thus began the after-after-after party.
…I recall that being quite a pain to clean up afterward.
"That I won't do anything. Or at the very least, I won't make the first move."
"Well, have you decided on your topic?"
Today's seminars are over, and the lab turned into a playground for the fourth-years and graduates.
Just as we were finally able to use the facility for its intended purpose, we could only hurry home and leave the university behind us.
…Something's wrong. There's definitely something wrong here.
"I was thinking about writing something on the folktales of the Hokuriku region."
"…That's a rather niche topic. Have you done any research on it before?"
"I took quite a detailed look at it once before entering university. I should be able to manage if I just copy the stuff I had from back then."
"Huh… You were quite the hard worker before, then?"
But right now, maintaining this failure of a student's motivation is my highest priority.
Letting her use my room, bringing a girl to my apartment, spending several hours alone with just the two of us.
If this were someone else… No, something like this would have made even my heart dance a few years ago. But now, I see this as nothing more than an obligation.
"Did you grow up around there, Izumi? In Toyama? Or Ishikawa?"
"I was born and raised in Tokyo… Heh, why do you ask?"
Should I joke about how her motivation always seems to be in the wrong place, or respect her ability to calmly do these things I've never even thought of?
"Would non-locals normally do research on that area during high school? That's got nothing to do with entrance exams."
As I pose my rather simple question, she stares at me as if trying to steal a peek into my heart again.
"You know, Haruki, maybe you really are a serious and hard-working person, but you've never actually involved yourself in anything pointless before, have you?"
It doesn't quite feel like I'm being made fun of, but I can't help but feel a little hurt when her sighs seem full of pity.

"Besides, you were probably thinking of taking care of dinner with a couple of convenience store bento boxes or takeout, right? And here I was thinking we were finally about to share a meal together."
"…Wait, hold on a second. You're making me take care of dinner, too?"
"See what I mean? That wasteless, effort-conserving, impersonal lifestyle of yours…"
"Forget about fruitless labor and all that, I don't remember signing up to wait on you hand and foot."
"I'm at a loss for words. And you still call yourself a man? Ah～ I really wish you wouldn't disappoint me like that, Haruki."
"I certainly don't recall going through the pain of giving birth to you, so why must I put up with you mooching off me like thi… Ah."
Just as Izumi's almost artistic ability to divert the topic in ridiculous directions was starting to make my heart feel at ease…
I spot a girl in a familiar uniform who seems to be waiting for someone near the front gate.
She ambushed me in exactly the same manner last week and sent my emotions spinning promptly after…
"Who's that girl…? Is she your girlfriend, Haruki?"
"Hold on, what do you think you're saying? That's Houjou High's uniform, you know?"
"…At least try to properly interpret my words when I'm talking to you."
Izumi, who keenly noticed that the girl's eyes gazed at me, throws all kinds of weird questions my way in an attempt to make me slip up.
…This is just an act, right? She can't seriously believe that I would go after someone outside of my age group like that, right?
"Then what's the problem? Is getting seen by her a bad thing, somehow?"
"The truth is… I got into a little mess with one of her friends. She got pretty upset over it."
"That friend would most likely be a classmate of hers, right? So you were messing around with high school girls after all…"
"Hang on! You know full well that there's an obvious difference between 'got into a mess' and 'messing around with,' yet you still misunderstood me on purpose, didn't you!?"
While I'm trying to clear up the situation, that girl's… Sugiura Koharu's gaze doesn't even budge an inch. However, she doesn't seem to be approaching me like the last time.
"Feelings that couldn't be conveyed, words that were never said, and an adult who just wouldn't understand… Well, how's it going, you pervert! Pedophile! Criminal!"
Which is probably because I have someone beside me who looks somewhat pretty from a distance, and whose true nature can't be judged from her looks alone.
Even so, she's wearing the same unchanged look as she did the last time. I doubt she'll just let us go if we try to leave through the front gate…
"Izumi… Go kill some time at a convenience store, or something."
"I'll go have a word with her. It won't take long."
And then try to lighten up my heavy, sinking feelings as I take a dignified step toward her…
"Now, now, just hold on a second!"
Suddenly, I feel strong pressure on my neck from my collar and black out for a second.
"Heey, Haruki… How about I take care of this for you?"
"What the hell was that!? Were you trying to kill me just now!?"
Yeah, right. She'd probably just laugh off a line like that, so I might as well save my breath.

"Regardless of my reasons, it's better to say that this is undoubtedly my responsibility. If I let someone else who has nothing to do with it step in for me, I can't even imagine what that girl will say to me."
"But she's not exactly involved either, is she?"
"So if I step in, we'll just be two fellow people that aren't supposed to be involved in all this. She'll be in no position to complain, right?"
I'm sure that bringing up a sound argument like that will only end up fanning the flames of her antagonism…
After all, I'm sure it would annoy me if I were in her position.

"Besides, I think it'd probably be easier for me to talk with her since we're both girls. I bet you acted way too stuck up when you talked to her the first time and ended up pissing her off even more, right?"
"…Are you saying that you saw us last week?"
"See? I assume you're leaving it to me from here?"
It seems that Izumi's not wasting any time on snappy one-liners and is getting straight to the point.
…To put it simply, it appears she's serious about wanting to go have a talk with her.
"Haruki, you must be bad at talking to girls other than me, right? Just leave it to me. Consider this full compensation for a night's stay and a meal, all right?"
"…I don't remember agreeing to let you eat and sleep at my place, though."
"Well then, hurry along and go to the supermarket to shop for tonight's dinner. I'll make sure to peacefully settle the issue in the meantime."
There's no way it'd go that smoothly.
Leaving it to someone like you would only make matters worse.
Even then, won't that just make it seem like I'm running away?
"I've only spoken to her once, but she's really serious, inflexible, and uncompromising. I don't think it'll be easy to appease her."
I hold back any real words of refusal in my mind and only offer her some advice that would help her to ease the ordeal.
"No worries, no worries! I'm more than used to dealing with those inflexible types of people."
That said, I imagine that Izumi's already caught on to the fact that I want to take a step back and walk away from this.
For someone who already knows me so well despite having been acquainted with me for only half a year, I admittedly really treasure her friendship.
…Putting aside that last and slightly ambiguous bit that she murmured, anyway.
"Could I speak to you for a little? Um, regarding Haruki-kun…"
"I'm really sorry. We've only just met and yet I've dragged you all the way out here."
"You were actually looking for Haruki-kun, weren't you?"
"Is it about your friend? Haruki-kun said he caused some trouble for her."
"I forced it out of him. He really didn't want to tell me anything at first, you see."
"E-Excuse me, but is he… no, I mean, is Kitahara-senpai… you know…?"
"What is it with that guy… He was lying after all! If he had a girlfriend, he should've just said so from the beginning!"
"I'm sorry… I need to apologize to both of you."
"Eh? Eh, ah, wait! Please, you don't need to do that."
"Everything's my fault. So if possible, please forgive Haruki-kun."
"Oh, no… I have no reason to demand an apology from you…"
"You may not have a reason, but I do. Although the person I really should be apologizing to is your friend, I suppose."
"You see, he… The reason why he takes such a cold attitude toward girls is surely because of me…"
"…What do you mean? After all, aren't you and Kitahara-senpai…"
"Dating? No, I suppose it's more appropriate to say that we were dating? …At least, I guess that's how he sees it."
"You noticed the past tense there, right? That's exactly what I meant."
"Yeah, we can still meet each other. And we can still talk to one another. But now there's a gap between us that neither of us can cross."
"It's all my fault. I forced my feelings on him and never considered his circumstances. I took advantage of his kindness and selfishly believed that our hearts were connected."
"As a result, I put him through a lot of pain."
"He's changed since then. He's lost the ability to smile from the bottom of his heart. No matter who it is, he can only deal with them through a mask."
"But the one part of him that never changed is his passion for helping other people. He is still as reliable as ever, and a lot of people crowd around him as a result."
"That's why most people couldn't see the changes he went through. Only those who were deeply involved with him could."
"But that's exactly why I came to understand… He's become unusually afraid of reciprocation."
"The fact that his actions may elicit such gratitude from others, or possibly even emotions greater than that… is extremely painful for him."
"Nevertheless, he can't help being a good person. That's how he's lived his life until now, and it's probably too late for him to change that."
"This is the dilemma he's struggling with. Despite still holding on to his kind and caring attitude, he can't bear accepting others' gratitude."
"That… sounds so weak. That's just messed up."
"Well, he said the complete opposite about you. He said that you're far too strong."
"That's all I wanted to say. So, do you understand now? That all of this is my fault."
"Why would you tell me all this? This isn't something that you would normally want to share with someone you've only just met, right?"
"Since I've involved myself in the situation between you two, I think it's only fair for me to fully explain our situation so that we can speak on equal footing."
"Not at all… I'm in the wrong. It's all my fault, after all."
"I've caused some painful memories for both you and your friend, haven't I…?"
"Eh? Oh no, I don't really mind. I'm just a messenger, that's all…"
"Even so, I'm sorry. I just… I just… I just wish I could've held on to him forever, and yet…"
"Aah… oh no… I didn't mean to get all…"
"I… I'm sorry… For making you see something so undignified…"
"No… I should be thanking you for telling me all that even though it was so painful for you to reveal it."
"No, I should be the one saying that. Because after this, you still need to go through this difficult conversation with your friend."
"Sorry for the wait! Let's get going, Haruki."
"…How did it go? She got mad, didn't she?"
It's been half an hour since we parted at the gate.
Izumi appeared before me, smiling as if nothing had happened, and took a peek inside my shopping bag despite my visibly restless expression.
"No, she was a good girl. She wasn't one bit unreasonable."
Even her tone's no different from usual, one that's clearly different from the tone I had following the stress and fatigue I'd felt after talking to that girl.
"She seems to have accepted the reasons behind your actions, so I wonder if she'll stop looking for you again."
"H-How in the world did you manage to convince her?"
"Nothing special, really. I just had a normal conversation with her, you know?"
I thought I also had a normal conversation with her back then, though…
Was the fact that they're both girls really the key after all, just as Izumi had said?
Or perhaps it was easier to talk to a cool-headed third party over a guy who can't help letting his emotions get to him?
Or perhaps casual people like Izumi happen to be the best at dealing with someone as uncompromising as that girl?
"Now then, we're a little behind schedule so let's hurry and get dinner started! So, what kind of treat am I in for tonight?"
There's a lot that's left unexplained, but Izumi does look proud of a job well done, that's for sure.
"Well, I was thinking about curry. It's simple enough that I can make it just fine."
Not to mention she's also lifted off a huge burden that's been weighing on my heart.
"Wow, awesome! Leave it to a good friend of mine to immediately know just what my favorite food is!"
"It's not like I can imagine anything you don't like, anyway."
She's never been a picky eater at the cafeteria either… A fact that's even more apparent whenever I'm the one paying.
"Then let's get going. Your apartment's around Nishiguchi, right, Haruki?"
"I'm sorry about all that. I didn't mean to drag you into my mess."
"It's fine, really. You left it to me because you trusted me, right, Haruki?"
That's how it ended up, that's for sure…
But now that I think about it, the description of "an odd person who willingly tries to get involved with others' issues like a weirdo"…
…Appears to be valid for all parties involved today.
"Forget about that, let's just hurry home, yeah? I'll help out with the curry too! I'll help rush you to finish it, help to taste test it, and help you to eat it all up, that is!"
"…I'd appreciate it more if you would do something that actually counts as helping out instead."
Despite everything, the steps I'm taking today feel much lighter than last week's as I begin my short walk back to my apartment.
And Izumi's walking by my side as if it's the most natural thing in the world.
"Get it now, little kitty? Us adults have plenty of ways to take care of a problem…"
"Wow, just as tidy as I thought it would be."
"Then help me preserve that image! …Specifically, don't make a mess!"
In the end, step by step, I brought Izumi up to my place.
On top of that, I'm now slaving away at these potatoes, carrots, and onions, and putting them in a pot to cook for this surprise guest of mine.
"The whole place is so thoroughly cleaned up, too. There's no way I'll be able to find any long strands of hair or stuff like that, huh?"
"I'm begging you, please, stop acting exactly like I imagined you would."
…Come to think of it, when was the last time I had a girl over?
To begin with, the only women who've ever been in here are Io, this woman in front of me, and… that makes three in total.
"Your photo albums～! Let me see your photo albums! I wonder where they could be…?"
"I've already hidden all those embarrassing things at my old place."
Needless to say, my mother, who lives a mere ten minutes away, isn't included in the aforementioned three.
"Worry not. Once dinner's over, you'll be having a lot less fu… Hey, don't just lie down! If you're bored, come help me out!"
"But, you know, isn't it pretty awkward to use someone else's kitchen?"
"I'd appreciate it if you could feel the same way about using someone else's bed."
"Ah, I have no problems with that. A different pillow or whatever doesn't bother me at all."
Considering how comfortable she looked sleeping on the cold floor of the lab, a pillow alone shouldn't make much of a difference…
"This has been on my mind for a long time now, Izumi…"
"You have no living skills whatsoever, do you?"
"Sounds about right. I wonder if someone would just take care of me after I graduate."
My favorite signature moveーlecturingーwhich I haven't used in quite a while, is completely ineffective against Izumi, who seems to live out her days freely and without care.
"Hey, hey, Haruki, why don't you become my patron? Think of the future prospects you'll have!"
"These future prospects you're suggesting do at least include your graduation, right?"
"Don't just suddenly ditch a conversation that you started."
Is this happy-go-lucky woman really going to be alright?
At this rate, I can't see her changing her easy-going lifestyle even after graduation.
…Well, before all that, we should focus on whether or not she'll actually graduate.
"Hey, Izumi. If, against all odds, you actually do manage to graduate from university…"
"Hey, listen to me when I'm talking to you!"
"Hey, hey, play a little for me later. I want to see how you look playing the guitar."
"You've already forgotten the reason you're here, haven't you?"
"Come on, just a little! I got it. I'll put in my best effort into writing the paper. In exchange, play a little for me when I'm done? Think of it as a reward."
"…I've given up on playing the guitar."
"Hardly… It's not like I was ever any good at it, so I'm not really all that attached to it."
That's right. Not attached at all.
I might have practiced very hard. I might have been very dedicated.
Because it's not fun. Because it doesn't make me happy. Because I don't want to remember…
But the word that escaped my mouth had nothing to do with that insignificant fact.
"Ah, Todokanai Koi? It's been playing on the school radio every day since last week, remember?"
My finger is stained in a deep crimson, yet I feel no pain.
"I first heard it during winter when I was a first-year student. I fell in love with it immediately!"
Because there's another fierce pain spreading throughout my chest.
"The vocals and the melody are both great, but I especially like the lyrics. It's not a work of art or anything, but it's really touching, you know?"
"I can sing the whole song, you know?"
I rinse my finger with some cold water, washing away the blood.
And after licking my wound, the taste of blood slowly spreads in my mouth.
"Hey, didn't you graduate from Houjou High, Haruki?"
Was my blood always this bitter…?
"Then you might have actually heard this song live before, right? Apparently, it was only played once around three years ago, during Houjou High's festival…"
"Yeah. I was always studying… Never was into stuff like that anyway."
"Ah, hold on, Nee-chan. I didn't get to read this week's Big Spiritual yet."
"Another detour? But mom and dad are probably there already."
"Oh, come on, I won't take too long. I'm only following two series here, it won't take more than five minutes!"
"Why don't you read something too, Nee-chan? This month's Lilian is out, too."
"I haven't read manga since I got into university."
"Seriously, you totally forgot how to have fun after enrolling. I don't know if you're just super busy or whatever, but you look so depressed every day…"
"Must be nice to enjoy your youth while it lasts, Takahiro… considering that you didn't get the recommendation?"
"Not to mention that insensitivity of yours! If you keep that up, Kitahara-senpai's gonna dump you for sure!"
"…We're doing just fine. Don't say something like that when you're not involved."
"Forget it. I don't have a brother named Takahiro anyway!"
"Ah, wait… I'm sorry. But you know, he hasn't come over or anything after you guys started uni…"
"…We're past that phase already. We can't be ourselves with that many people around, so we've only been meeting up at his place…"
"That's quite the vivid imagery you just gave your little brother."
"…Aren't mom and dad waiting for us?"
"Aa-ah… What're we gonna do… Let's at least not fight like this when we're having dinner with the whole family, okay?"
"Didn't you say some pretty mean things too, Nee-chan? So we're even!"
"Okay, I get it, okay! I'm sorry I forgot the family rule of 'the eldest daughter of the Ogiso family comes first no matter what,' alright?"
"Ah, well, I was just cracking a joke there…"
I reflexively grab my cell phone and peek at the display…
…And see a name that I haven't seen in a while.
My cell phone's been ringing for a while. Of course I know that.
But forget about my hands, I can't even move a single muscle in my body. All I can hear is my pounding heart, like ringing in my ears.
My forehead, back, and armpits are all scorching hot. Countless beads of cold sweat burst forth in an attempt to cool them.
As I finally regain control of my fingers, I move them only a few millimeters and once again do an awful thing to "her."
"…Sorry about that. I forgot to turn off my cell phone even though we're studying."
"I feel kind of bad if you're saying you did that because of me…"

Still, the awfulness of my action is clear enough that even this person so close to dozing off right in front of me has noticed it, and she's gone out of her way to imply just how deplorable I'm being.
"Are you trying to hide something from me, by any chance? Have you become a playboy to such an extent?"
"Come on, don't look so depressed! You're making me want to comfort you!"
"The voice message has been received. Thank you for choosing our services."
"Ah, yeah, thanks. How much was it?"
"I see. Okay, then… this… should just about cover it."
"What's wrong? Don't you want the money back?"
"How could a magazine this thin cost 3000 yen? It was actually a tenth of that, just 300! Don't just blindly hand over money like that…"
"You okay, Nee-chan? You've been acting a little weird for a while now."
"Was the article really that great? Which one is it? Can I take a look?"
"No, no, you can't look. The first person I have to show this to is…"
"Ah… sorry for yelling at you like that. But… you see…"
"Haah… Forget about it. Let's just go. The two of them are probably getting tired of waiting for us."
"…You're right. We're already ten minutes late."
"Just for today… please don't run away."
"You have one new message. First message. December 1st, 7:59 PM."
"Um, good evening, this is Setsuna. Sorry for calling you when you're so busy."
"But I really need to talk to you today about something. Um, so… Haruki-kun, have you seen this week's Kaiou Graph?"
"If you haven't, definitely go check it out. And… if it would be okay with you, please contact me afterward."
"Any time today would be fine. I'll be up all night. Early morning would be fine too."
"So, um… if, if you find the time… And if it's okay with you, um…"
By the time I looked at my cell phone again, it was already 3 AM.

I'd taken Izumi to the station, stopped by a convenience store, came back to my apartment, studied a little for tomorrow, took a shower, and as I finally slumped onto my bed, I realized it was already this late.
…No, I was actually fully aware of that. I had more than enough time to listen to a simple voicemail and give her a reply the entire time.
Speaking of which, before we parted ways at the station, Izumi told me to properly give "the person from earlier" a callback, to which I responded with silence…
There's no way Setsuna would know that I've figured out what she wanted to talk about just from hearing the magazine's name.
Neither would she know that I work part-time at Kaiousha, nor that I helped out with this week's issue…
We no longer share these little things in our lives that any friend or lover should know about with each other.
That's why I've put this message from Setsuna, one that I hadn't received in a whileーa very long whileーon repeat.
Her voice, vibrant as ever, seeps into my body and sends me into a daze that's both ecstatic and painful.
But in a corner of my mind, I'm fully aware that things can't go on like this.
That's why I have to respond to her request.
"Hahh! H-Haruki-kun? It is you, right, Haruki-kun?"
Joy, unease, relief, and regret strike me in unison the moment I hear her voice.
"Aha, ha… You really called… You let me hear your voice…"
Waves of similar emotions pour over from the other side of the phone, further amplifying our complicated feelings.
"…It's been a while. Have you… been doing all right?"
It really has been quite a while… since I last heard Setsuna saying "Haruki-kun."
"Yeah, I'm fine, I'm fine… But the seminars have been pretty intense lately, so I've been kind of busy, ahaha…"
"Yeah, me too… Not just with seminars, but I've had to juggle my part-time jobs as well. That's why I had to contact you this late… Sorry."
It's like an intoxicating melody that tingles the depths of my nose before sending a jolt through the depths of my heart whenever I hear it.
"No, I understand. You're working a lot harder than I am, Haruki-kun. I know that, really."
"That's why just getting in touch is good enough. I should be apologizing, too. It was brazen to ask you to call me all of a sudden…"
…And I don't just mean the moment of ecstasy, but the symptoms of withdrawal that come afterward as well.
"Ah, so, I should cut to the chase. It's about the issue of Kaiou Graph that was published today…"
"Yeah, I read it. Touma sure hasn't changed, huh?"
"I know, right? I knew it was Kazusa the moment I saw the photo. She had already become amazing before we knew it!"
"Second place at an international competition, huh? And in Europe, at that."
"I did a little research on the internet and found out that a whole bunch of world-class pianists placed in that competition before. …Kazusa's mom even got first place once."
"Which means her mom's probably rubbing it in her face right about now. And they'll start a huge argument over it."
"Ahaha… that does sound like something Touma Youko would do. She seems to treat Kazusa completely like a rival."
"Yeah… It'd be best if that were the case. Then Touma would have two of her dreams fulfilled at once."
"To stand on her own two feet with her piano, and to make up with her mom… She's really doing her best out there."
"But… that one other dream of hers is…"
"…Hey, how about a toast? To celebrate Kazusa's success, I mean."
"Do you have any alcohol in your fridge, Haruki-kun? If not, something like tea or juice will do!"
"I'll go get some right now! You should go get some ready too, Haruki-kun."
"Haah, haah, haah… A-Are you ready, Haruki-kun…?"
"My fridge is right in my room. More importantly, take a second to catch your breath, Setsuna."
"Y-Yeah… Sorry. Give me a second. Haa, haa, haaa…"
From the other side, I can hear Setsuna's frantic, joyous, and excited breathing.
How far back would I need to delve into my memories to remember the last time she's sounded this lively, I wonder…?
"Fuu, haa… Fuuuu… Okay, I'm calm now. All set here, Haruki-kun!"
As the sound of the carbonated fizz reverberates through my room, I catch the sound of a cork popping through the receiver.
"It was a year-end gift. Dad's more of a shochu fan, so I'm sure it'll be fine."
The image of Setsuna sticking out her tongue in a cute manner on the other side fills my mind without a hint of awkwardness.
"Well then, please take the lead for our toast."
No, there actually still was an ever so slight hint of awkwardness.
After all, my image of Setsuna has always been of someone a little childish, with mischievous eyes and constantly changing expressions, each as brilliant as the sun.
"It's your fault for suddenly bringing it up, Setsuna! Oh, enough already, cheers!"
As I lightly tap my cell phone with my beer can, I hear the sharp sound of glass ringing from the other side.
The beer feels cold and stimulating as I down it in one gulp…
Sliding down my throat, it fills my entire chest with warmth before finally reaching my stomach.
Now, I hear the sound of applause through the receiver.
A sincere cheer for her close friend's success. A sincere act of sharing her joy with another one of her close friends.
This genuine symphony from the bottom of her heart, devoid of any mixed feelings, is one that seems ever so distant to me…
"I'm happy, I'm so happy. Aha, ahaha, ahahaha… Oh no, I think I'm crying a little."
The truth is, I already knew all about it. I've known all along for five days now.
"Ah… This tastes great. I feel like drinking some more."
"Hey, slow down a little, would you? Did you get any better at handling alcohol since entering university, Setsuna?"
And yet I didn't tell anyone about it at all… Not even Setsuna.

It had nothing to do with company confidentiality either, especially since it's news that had already been published on the internet. Even though there wasn't a single reason that should have kept me from telling anyone…
On the contrary, I… I couldn't even find myself genuinely celebrating Kazusa's success like Setsuna's doing right now.
"Gulp, gulp… Mmm～ I'm totally fine. I got plenty of practice from the drinking parties with my friends from the seminars."
"I always just drink oolong tea, so everyone's starting to look down on me."
"So you never got any practice, after all…"
"Who cares, right, Haruki-kun? …This is the happiest I've been since university started."
Even though Kazusa has had two of her wishes granted already.
Even though she's been doing her best out there in a place beyond my reach, with more success than I ever could have imagined.
Even so, I can't bring myself to feel genuinely happy for her.
The reason can't be clearer to me, but it's something I can never speak of.
"The Kazusa that I love… The Kazusa that you love, Haruki-kun…"
"We're not allowed to apologize for anything to each other today, okay? Let's promise, until we hang up."
That each time she showers me with kindness, each time she forgives me…
"No matter what happens, I'll always love Kazusa."
It reminds me of how narrow-minded I am for continuing to run away, and just how weak I am for trying only to distance myself.
"Even if she comes to hate me or even loathe me, I just can't bring myself to think otherwise. …I might just be a big nuisance to Kazusa though."
I've been reminded so many times this way of the fact that I have no right to stay by Setsuna's side.
"No matter what happens, I'll always… love her."
There's Setsuna, the girl who was heartlessly betrayed three years agoーthe girl who remains boundlessly kind to me.
And then there's me, the very person who heartlessly betrayed her three years agoーthe man who continues to brush away all her kindness.
Though we're well aware that the distance between us is steadily increasing, which neither of us wants, we're incapable of changing how we treat one another.
"So if it's a day as happy as today, it's fine if I just keep on talking to you like this, right, Haruki-kun?"
Stop being such a good girl. Stop being so kind to me.
Don't corner me any further than thisーI beg you.
"Yeah… We talked for quite a while, didn't we?"
"A whole two hours… Will you be okay tomorrow? You have classes, right?"
"I normally go to sleep around this time anyway. You're the one I'm worried about."
"Ah, tomorrow's classes start in the afternoon for me anyway."
"Ah, but, you know, we had a lot of these long phone calls way back then too, didn't we? Waking up after those was quite tough back then… Ah."
"I kind of let the happiness go to my head, plus I'm a little drunk. I didn't mean to say something like…"
"Didn't we agree to not apologize? What are you doing breaking your own promise?"
"So don't sweat it. I'm not bothered by those kinds of things today. Conversely, I won't be apologizing for anything either."
"Good night, Setsuna. I'm glad we talked tonight, I had fun… If nothing else, that alone is the truth."
"I read Kaiou Graph. Touma's amazing, isn't she?"
Setsuna wants to talk to me about Kazusa's brilliant success overseas.
"I already thought she was beyond our grasp before, but I never thought she'd be where she is now."
But I can't bear to listen to Setsuna talk about a topic that will only end up reopening both of our old wounds the more we share in our joy from it.
"Well, considering her talent, it only seems natural. It'd be great if she could use this opportunity to achieve even more amazing things."
So I'll at least send her a text.
This way, regardless of whether the message is completely banal or whether it has emotions passionately poured into it, only the most literal meaning of its words will reach the recipient.
Nothing beyond the raw words, such as the tone of my voice or the emotions as I speak, will make it through.
And I'll also be able to take in Setsuna's words without having to feel the emotions behind them.
"Thanks for letting me know about the great news, Setsuna. Good night, then."
Immediately after sending my one-way text, I turn off the lights and pull my blanket over my head.
I'm running away from Setsuna's plea to hear my voice; I'm running away from Kazusa's efforts and hard work.
I'm twisting the memories I have back from high school, running away from the truth of what things have become now.
I haven't been able to take even a single step forward ever since I enrolled in university. As a result, I've also caused Setsuna to come to a standstill.
Once we graduate, once we go out into the world, once our surroundings change, once our relationships change…
Will I one day, from the bottom of my heart… be able to forgive myself?
"It's great, isn't it? Kazusa has finally had her dream realized."
"…Or maybe, Kazusa never thought of that as her dream?"
"I still think about it sometimes. It makes me wonder if this is what Kazusa really wanted, or something like that…"
"…But I guess it's not fair for me to be saying that, is it?"
"That's why the only thing I can do now is pray for her."
"I hope that Kazusa's truly happy about winning her prize. I hope that she's truly wishing for success as a pianist."
"Thank you for your text. I was really happy to read it. Good night."
"As I've said, it's about the Kaiou Graph we're releasing this week. You'll help out, won't you, Kitahara?"
A small article that was meant to only stay between us… Something that's really only meant to be discussed within our little circle…
"The woman on this page became quite the topic. The bimonthly musical magazine department has decided to write a feature on her."
"Yeah, I can definitely see why. She sure does stand out."
"What a beauty… That silky smooth long black hair over that gorgeous black dress. Not to mention she's barely twenty～"
"And that's not all. There's serious talent behind those looks too. It's been a while since someone shook up the classical music world like this."
Before I knew it, the topic had already extended slightly beyond our circle due to it being quite newsworthy for its targeted audience.
"The chief editor over at Ensemble seems to be on good terms with this woman's mother… with Touma Youko, and even got permission for an interview pretty easily."
"Touma Youko, huh? Hey, I'm pretty sure I saw her on TV when I was a kid."
"She was the pianist that represented Japan for a time back then, after all. She's mostly only active in Europe nowadays, though, so she's not as famous here as she used to be."
"But her fame on an international level has skyrocketed. She's already become one of the few Japanese people whose tickets will sell out in any country."
The lady who invited me into her home three years ago, served me what was practically sugared water, and chatted so vibrantly about the school festival with me…
Even within such typical conversation, the praise that she gets really is something else.
"And now her daughter's winning awards at international competitions. What's more, she's certainly got the visuals! There's no way this wouldn't catch people's attention."
How can they sing Kazusa's praises like this while knowing nothing about her other than what's written in this article?
She's just a student studying abroad who just happened to produce some results, and who just happens to be the daughter of someone pretty famous…
And she just… happens to be somewhat of a nice woman.
"Normally their team would be outsourcing this to an editing company, but since we decided on this so suddenly, not to mention the fact I came up with the original idea…"
"So in short, you went and grabbed work from another department again."
"We really shouldn't be criticizing Kitahara-kun, then! After all, his superior is such a pro at working across multiple departments."
"I already got the green light from both chief editors. There's also more than enough time until the bimonthly's deadline."
"The future looks pretty bleak… to me, but getting through stuff like this seems to be her specialty."
How did it end up like this…?
"Therefore, Kitahara… I'll have you finish what you started and leave you in charge of the article."
Mari-san's words strike me hard from two opposite directions.
"Leave me in charge of the article" means I'll need to take care of both the information gathering and the article writing myself… Or at least, that's what I think.
That's way different from my usual responsibilities of making copies, buying things, getting food, picking up manuscripts, fixing layouts, quality checking, and talking to the printing company…

…Though the latter half of that is already slightly beyond the responsibilities of a part-timer. There's a big difference between my work and that of an actual employee, where you're expected to "create something."
I never thought a part-time student like myself would ever be given a chance like this…
If I take on this assignment, I'll need to thoroughly research the interviewee.
That means I'll have to look into her history, talk to her acquaintances, and trace her footsteps.
Can I really do something like that? Can I really dig up my memories of her again?
"…I think this might be a little too tough for me. It's probably best to leave it to someone more experienced."
Hearing my response, Mari-san seems to be at a loss.
This does seem like a fitting reaction for someone as hypocritical as she is, though, given that she usually stuffs work down my throat while saying that I work too much at the same time.
"Do you think you're not skilled enough to take it on? If that's the case, I'd say you're underestimating yourself."
"…Not at all, it's you that's overestimating me."
Her confidence in me is only painful for me right now.
And knowing that the issue has nothing to do with what Mari-san's worried about only makes it worse.
"But haven't you been meaning to write something for a while? Didn't you say you wanted to get into publishing and gain some experience?"

And not just with words eitherーI did everything I could to get a chance at it. I'd said, "Please entrust me with more challenging tasks!", and "Please work me to the bone until I can't think anymore!" and whatnot.
But all of that work was meant to help me forget. It'd be pretty ironic if I took on a job that forced me to recall what I've been trying to forget…
"Then what's the point of me taking this job away from them by force…? Ah."
"Just what are you trying to do?"
"Just how much faith do you have in Kitahara-kun, Mari-san…? You've never done so much for the regular employees here. Take Macchan, for example."
"Why are you bringing me into this!?"
She's advising me not to take any extra work, but she's also making the effort to find more work opportunities for me…
"I see… I guess I got a little ahead of myself. Looks like I caused you trouble instead, Kitahara."
That said, well, how should I put this? It certainly seems like something a person with such charming contradictions as her would do.
"Now then, what should I do…? I wasn't really counting on anyone other than Kitahara…"
"I-I'll do it, Mari-san! I can't just take what Suzuki said sitting down!"
"Hamada's in charge of you, right, Matsuoka? If he'd be willing to lend you to me, I might consider it…"
"Not a chance in hell. If you have time to be daydreaming like that, hurry up and finish those tape transcriptions. The ones I gave to Kitahara are already done, you know?"
"Seriously!? Didn't we just get those yesterday…?"
"When I got to the office this morning and saw Kitahara-kun, he said he was just about to head to university."
"You've been totally surpassed by a part-timer… Be it in terms of your work ethic, results, or reliability."
"Hey, I don't want to be compared with Kitahara like that. He's a third-year student, you know? I'm only in my second year."
"I guess if you count a second-year grad student as a 'second-year'…"
"Don't you have any pride as a member of society…?"
"Hold on, Kitahara… What's this about you leaving in the morning? You didn't tell me about this."
"Sorry, Mari-san. I'd like to take back what I said."
"Forget about that for now! Just how long did you stay here last night… Eh?"
"Please let me handle it. Touma Kazusa's feature article."
In that case, there's… no way I can back down here.
Because if there's still someone who's willing to put their faith in me, then I'd hate to betray that trust.
"I'll do it. Please leave it to me."
Even so, I suppose I have no choice but to move forward after all.
Even if the means I'm using to achieve my goal would actually end up hindering said goal, it's a signpost that's bringing me closer to my future.
"In that case, let's head over to their chief editor right now. Come with me, Kitahara."
"Hey, hold on a second, Mari-san! I want to do something like that too! All I do around here is run errands for Hamada-san, anyway."
"He's simply a better errand boy than you. Whenever I sent Kitahara out to buy something, he never took over an hour, you know?"
"Eh? Ah, well… That coffee you asked for was actually only available in Chiba and Saitama…"
"Is that so? So I was just hallucinating all those times I saw you reading in some convenience store, huh? After all, you were making an expedition to Chiba."
"Those little things can add up over time and really hit you where it hurts, huh…?"
"Well, that's one thing… But I have another reason to give this job to Kitahara."
"So that actually was one of the reasons…"
"I suppose you're aware of what I'm implying, Kitahara, but…"
Mari-san wouldn't give me such an amazing opportunity just because I'm a little better than some of the others.
She knows that letting me handle it has certain advantages… Basically, she's already done her research, and that's why she picked me specifically.
"That's why you'll begin with the school she attended back when she was in Japan. You know what to do after, right, Kitahara?"
"Yes, I understand. I've built up a lot of trust with the teachers in the past, so I believe there won't be any problems getting their permission."
The interviewee in question is… Touma Kazusa.

She came in second at the Trustee International Piano Competition. She's the daughter of the world-class pianist Touma Youko, and she's been living together with her mother in Vienna for the past three years.
And before studying abroad, she got her education at…
"If you couldn't even catch on to that, then it's more than obvious that you're not the right person for this job."
"Well… we didn't really talk much back then. She was at the top of the music program, after all."
The little lie at the very end… is the only armor left still protecting the depths of my heart.
Without a doubt, that's the time displayed on my cell phone.

Having been scolded by Mari-san for working too late and having pushed myself to finish examining the massive pile of stuff she'd passed me, I found the whole affair really contradictory, and by the time I got home, it was already 6 o'clock.
It's the sole detestable day of the week for me, given that I have a lot of free time that I don't know what to do with.
That's why I worked until I almost passed out last night, barely managing to fall into a sleep so deep I couldn't even dream, and yet…
What happened to trample upon my day off where I didn't need to think about anything was a call from the city, but I didn't recognize the number.
"Ahh… this is Kitahara-kun, right…? I take it that you've been well…?"
"…I should be the one asking that. Are you okay?"
What wakes me up is the voice of an elderly man who sounds like he's in even worse shape than me.
"Wow, I really can't thank you enough, Kitahara-san. Things were looking pretty bad. The part-timers from last month all resigned, and now even the branch manager…"
"Broke his hip, I heard? Well, he is at that age after all…"
"Exactly. We're not even sure if he'll recover by the end of the year. I thought it was hopeless…"
A family restaurant around a ten-minute walk away from the station.
While I'm at it, given that it's a ten-minute walk from Houjou University as well, about three-tenths of the customers here consist of our university or the high school's students.
…If only that was the whole story.
"Don't use those puppy eyes on me. I agreed to help only for today."
"Ehhhhh!? No way! If that's the case, how are we supposed to stay open starting tomorrow?"
"Don't just leave everything to some guy that resigned half a year ago… You've already been the kitchen manager for two years now, right?"
Sitting in the branch manager's seat with distress written all over his face is the kitchen manager, Satou.
"I can't really deny that, but… Your resignation was really tough on the rest of us. We were still in pretty bad shape even after getting three more people."

The branch manager aside, he's the one with the most experience here, not to mention he's two years older than me. Despite all that, though, this slightly cowardly acting manager still speaks so politely to me.
"I left it all in the manual, didn't I? The way I see it, four people would be enough to run this place."
Although, I don't remember if I started speaking casually with him before or after he switched to being so polite…
"Well, having someone strict around really is the key to success. Everyone loosened up too much after you left, Kitahara-san."
I wouldn't go so far as to call him useless, but leaving him to manage the store by himself does worry me quite a bit.
"Then just be strict with them. Aren't you a full-fledged employee? You want to live up to that role, don't you?"
"I can't just talk to them like that… The branch manager doesn't even say anything most of the time."
…And that sense of worry happens to intensify particularly when we have conversations like this.
I was working here from the start of my second year until the spring of the third, so about a year in total.
Since I got really comfortable with the job before that, I didn't feel tired no matter how hard I pushed myself. That's why I came here, where it always seemed busy no matter what time of day it was.
But in the end, some complicated stuff happened, and I quit about half a year ago.
"Ah, Honda, good to see you. I'm just here today to…"
"Oh no, I'm so sorry for being five minutes late! I'll get ready immediately!"
I'm pretty sure he's also a second-year who started working around a year ago…
There was one instance where he was late for his shift and I attempted a single, "gentle" conversation with him, but…
"That guy never shows me that kind of respect."
"I don't care! I promised the branch manager that I'd help out only for today!"
"Well, I did hear that from the branch manager myself, too."
"…Then don't try to scare me like that."
"Well～ after I heard you were coming back, I couldn't help but get my hopes up, Kitahara-san. I thought that perhaps the terrible state this place is in would make you unable to walk away…"
"…I have to start job-hunting soon, you know?"
"I totally understand. We actually have a new recruit coming in today. I was hoping you could give her some training."
"Ah, so that's what's going on… You guys really have no one to spare, huh?"
"We can just barely handle Sundays with the five of us, so we don't really have the time to take care of a newcomer…"
"Good morning! Wow, it's really you, Kitahara-san! Welcome back!"
"Oh, you're a lifesaver! When I heard the branch manager collapsed, I thought we'd be finished for sure!"
"Oh no, I'm just going to be supervising the training for today, that's all."
"No worries, no worries. I already know how big of a revolution we're about to go through. Ah, but go easy on the new girl, okay? We really can't afford to lose anyone today."
"I see Nakagawa-san is still here. …I'm starting to see a little more hope for this place."
"All of the female part-timers here listen only to her…"
She's a vocational school student a year younger than me who started three months before I left.

This might be a little disrespectful to Satou, but I do remember her as the most useful staff member here apart from the manager, and the one who best understood my reign of terror while I was still working here.
And what I liked most about her was how she saw me as nothing more than just a coworker, and how straight forward she was with me when we talked…
"Oh, it hadn't even been a week after you left that she ended up leaving too."
"She was popular with many of the customers, so her leaving dealt us a pretty heavy blow. To think she'd just stop coming without even saying anything…"
Sorry… Satou. That's definitely due to all that "complicated stuff."
"Now then, there's only about an hour until we open. The new girl's been here for about an hour, so I'll introduce you two."
"Oh? That's pretty early for the first day. She's got great work ethics."
"I was responsible for her interview, see. She takes everything incredibly seriously. Threw about 30 minutes worth of questions at me afterward."
"Honestly, I almost thought she was your sister or something, Kitahara-san."
"…Um, how exactly did you reach that conclusion?"
"She's a third-year at Houjou High, so… even if she's not your sister, she does happen to be your underclassman, Kitahara-san."
"…Most of the part-timers here are related to our schools in one way or another anyway."
"I think her last name was Sugi… Sugi… Sugimura? No, that sounds a little off…"
A family restaurant located around a ten-minute walk away from the station.
While I'm at it, given that it's a ten-minute walk from Houjou University as well, about three-tenths of the customers here consist of our university or the high school's students.
Also, since it's a ten-minute walk from the university, about half of the part-timers here consist of our university or the high school's students…
"Hold it, Satou! What's the meaning of this!?"
"Ignoring the fact that I have no clue what's going on here either for a second, why are you both taking it out on me…?"
What a stroke of horrible luck…
"Sorry for the wait! Here is your cheeseburger combo and mixed pizza. …The tray is still hot, so please be careful."
"The tomato spaghetti and carbonara are ready!"
"Let me confirm your order: a clubhouse sandwich, one beef curry, and two drinks, correct? The drink bar is that way."
"Thank you very much. Your total comes to 2580 yen. …Your change comes to 2420 yen."
"Resupply the drink bar and the iced coffee. And the ice cubes too!"
"For example, if you needed a half-done omurice, you'd press this button. If you needed two…"
As the fierce battles both here and in the kitchen take their course, we reach the second half of the lunch rush.
"Then after you confirm the order, press this button… And finally, this button to send it over."
I remain at a corner of the hall with my new part-timerーwell, Houjou High's third-year student Sugiura Koharuーso as to not get in anyone's way.
"With this, the order will be sent to the kitchen, and you can then take the next customer's order afterward."
And so, training her in utilizing the data terminal to input taken orders is progressing smoothly at present…
…Or at least that's what I would like to say.
She's probably listening. She's also visibly irritated.

Is she willing to listen to the instructions of a man who'd broken down in the worst way possible during her first meeting with him, and who also happened to run away from their second encounter while entrusting someone else to deal with her?
…I have no doubt that this girl absolutely despises me right now, even as I enumerate these steps to her.
"Now then, practice time. Mixed fried foods combo, a Caesar salad, honey toast, a mango parfait, a coffee float, and two drinks…"
But with that said, the one who wanted to work here is none other than herself, and it just so happens that I'm the one in charge of her training…
Letting your own preferences affect your work performance would be nothing but trouble for the employer… is what I'd like to say.
Not only was she listening, she also picked it up extremely quickly.
To think she can use it this easily after only a single demonstration… If you consider her talent alone, she has the potential to be the store's finest.
She takes her training seriously, gives it her best efforts, and understands everything perfectly. Someone every pupil should aspire to be like.
But the irritated look on this pupil's face is a little troubling for me as a mentor…
"All right, let's move on to the next…"
"I'm more than prepared for the real deal. Further training would be a waste of time."
And so, the first words out of her mouth after about an hour seem to fundamentally reject our weird mentor-pupil relationship.
"You were just here to supervise my training, correct? In that case, thanks for your hard work. You're dismissed."
That, and I can only describe the attitude she's taking when it comes to cooperating with me as having very obvious dark clouds hanging over her head.
"Well, now… If you don't lighten up that expression of yours a little, greeting the customers might be a little…"
"You've also greeted guests before in the past, haven't you, Senpai?"
"Y-Yeah. I basically took on whatever position was short on people."
I forcibly hold back my urge to start lecturing her.
Even then, the attitude she's taking with me is unmistakably a consequence of the attitude I've taken with her in the past.
"…Are you sure you're gonna be okay?"
That said, I can't deny that the issue of her amiability around others might just resolve itself whenever I'm not right in front of her, just as she's implying.
Still, that alone isn't enough to conclude that she's ready for the job…
The lunch rush is just starting to ease up. Our floor manager, who is relieved that she can take a breather now, is fanning herself with a spare tray as she walks our way.
"I'm not the manager. I'm not even the kitchen manager."
…I'd tell her to watch her sluggish attitude a little, but now's not the time for that.
"Let's have her work at the hall for a bit. Let's see… let's do 30 minutes."
Just as expected, the two of them stare at me with dissatisfied expressions. The reasons behind them, however, are completely different.
"Please hold on a second. What do you mean, only 30 minutes?"
"…Can we really send her out? Won't she bother the others?"
Their responses are also, of course, completely opposite from one another.
"I do think we need to cut something down to size… A certain someone's ego, in particular."
"I even asked you to go easy on the new girl…"
Furthermore, both of their well-honed instincts seem to be able to sense that I'm clearly provoking a certain someone.
"That was pretty harsh… What, did she really annoy you so much?"
"Don't worry. This won't be enough to bring her down. I guarantee it."
I speak from plenty of experience…
"S…Stop looking down on me like that, please!"
"Okay, okay. Alright, Koharu-chan, why don't you give it a little go and we'll see if you can handle it, shall we?"
"Sorry about this. I'll take over once her training's done. …I might mess up more because it's been a while since I last did this, though."
"Haah… Why don't we call it a day here? The evening shift is about to arrive, right?"
"Yeah, I can let you go now. See? You're not rusty at all, Kitahara-san. Come on, just come back!"
"No, I absolutely can't. My knees have been on the brink of giving out for quite some time now."
"That's got less to do with your hiatus than it does with your age… Uh, good work today!"
Having received the… "warm" words of gratitude from both of the authorities, I unsteadily walk back behind the counter.
It's not that I feel that my stamina as a whole has gone down, but a job where I'm standing all day really hurts my leg muscles since I haven't been using them a lot lately.
Well, leaving that aside for now…
For the time being, I stand beside Sugiura Koharu, whose pride has been put to rest as planned, and whose expression finally befits a Japanese person.
"In any case, I'd like you to stay here a little longer and observe the others and how they work a little more."
The instant she stepped into the hall, the steady workflow that everyone was trying so hard to maintain simply collapsed.

"How to show customers to a table, and which one it should be, how to move around appropriately when you're not being called for, and conversely, what to prioritize when you have multiple things to do…"
Each and every one of her actions ended up hindering the other staff in some way, disrupted the pace of our customers, and ended up causing her to make mistakes herself.
"There are quite a few other things I want you to know too, but… well, you can pick up on the details as you go."
She later mixed up the orders, made even more mistakes, and caused further inconveniences for the customers.
"You're a smart girl, so… you'll probably get it in just another day or so. You'll be able to go work in the hall normally after that."
I called for a retreat just twenty minutes in. She's a clever girl, so she immediately realized the extent of her abilities, took a step back, and accepted my assistance.
That act alone really made me feel that she's actually not your ordinary worker.
"Well, with another two or three tries, you'd be a great asset. I'd say you were a great find for the store."
Well, I can only hope that she actually does something about her friendliness, though.
She still hasn't responded to anything I've said.
Still holding an irritated expression, never even facing me.
Even so, she's clearly acting differently than she was earlier in the day when she refused to look at me; she's paying close attention whenever I give her specific instructions.
"Are your shifts only on the weekends?"
"Until the winter break, yes. Once the break starts, I'll be coming every day."
That's why if I ask her a proper question, she'll give me a proper, albeit indifferent answer.
"Your next shift is the following Saturday, then? Would it be fine if I didn't come?"
"That's not really something I get to decide, anyway."
It's not like I can really give a statement saying her training's over right now.
But then, what should I do?
I initially agreed to working today and today only. If I keep sticking by her, it'll affect my studies and my job at the publishing company.
But even so, I should at least look at the scheduled shifts before leaving her by herself…
Stuck in this awkward, uneasy atmosphere…
The two of us quietly observe the store's activities for a while.
In the end, it wasn't until two hours later that I could get my hands on the evening shift schedule.
After all that happened, she mostly kept quiet, bade Nakagawa-san farewell, hurriedly changed out of her uniform, and gave everyone a deep bow.
"Well… good work today. Do your best next time too."
Not sure what to do after seeing her so depressed for the first time, I do my best to give a few words of encouragement, and…
A fist from the floor manager…
…And a knee from the kitchen manager.
"You made this mess, now clean it up!"
I should normally be staring back at these irrational words written across their faces…
I can feel a sharp sting in her words. Nevertheless, these two continue to stare daggers at me.
"Will you take responsibility if she doesn't come back next week?"
"I'll go with her, fine… I just have to cheer her up, right…?"
Must your expressions scream so loudly at me?
After all, I'm just someone the manager dragged in as a trainee supervisor for one day…
During times like these, silence speaks louder than words. They've long since mastered this strategy of mine…
About 30 seconds after I dashed out the door, I spotted her small figure.
There was no difference in her speed before and after I found her. As if to clearly express that she was neither waiting for nor running away from me.
"I should see you off after all. At least until the station."
I don't hear a "No, thank you" this time.
Just like when we were still working, if I'm not looking for a direct answer, she's content with just saving her breath.
…Which also means she's realized that I'll be following her regardless of what she says.
Therefore, the atmosphere right now is not one of rejection, but closer to that of resignation.
"I haven't done anything that would tire me out."
The proof being, when I do ask her a question like this, she'll hide her emotions as much as possible and tell me exactly what I need to know, but nothing more.
The two of us walk side by side through the streets at night.
The streets from Goodies to the station are bustling with people. To be honest, there isn't really a good reason for me to accompany her.
Even so, the reason those two forced me to chase her was due to problems with my own attitude, too, not just hers.
"Why are you trying to work at this time of the year?"
"…Because I'm going on a graduation trip."
I tried to strike up a conversation with her, but it seems like she interpreted it as me simply looking for an answer from her as well.
"A graduation trip, huh… Are you going with your classmates?"
"There's four of us in total. Ako and Sayuri and… Mihoko as well."
Her emphasis on the last name she mentioned didn't appear to be done with the intention of hitting a nerve.
The proof being her lowered voice when saying her name and the slightly downcast expression on her face right now.
"I… I see! If you're already planning your graduation trip, that means you've already got a recommendation, right?"
The same regular program in high school. The same department in university.
She really is the epitome of a junior of mine…
"S-So you're working to pay for your trip, huh? Your parents can't pay for you?"
"We're an average, middle-class family. …The other girls' parents seem to be paying for them, though."
"Going to a private high school was really tough on my parents too. It's all because I said I wanted to go to Houjou High no matter what…"
"Even so, asking them to give me a small increase in my allowance just so I can go enjoy myself… I really can't bring myself to ask them that, even if I don't require a big sum."
She's from a normal family, a rare case among students from Houjou High. She's a working student precisely because she's in a school for the privileged.
I did think that her personality, to an irritating extent, was too similar to a certain someone's, but to think that her family situation would be so similar to a certain someone else's as well…
Our chatter-filled walk continued for another ten minutes, and eventually brought us to Minami-Suetsugu Station.
"I, um… I might have been a little more strict than I should have today, but…"
"No, I should apologize too… I'm sorry for acting so arrogantly back there."
But those ten minutes of chatter definitely weren't wasted.
"In the end, I had a bit of a… bad impression of you, Senpai…"
"Well, that's to be expected. I took such a terrible attitude with you after all."
As our chatter continues, the overly negative impressions we had of each other slowly start to fade.
"Even so, that doesn't justify the attitude I had during work. I'm really sorry."
We've accepted each other's mistakes, and are slowly building up the courage to strengthen our relationship.
"There's nothing to forgive, but… I forgive you."
The instant I said "I forgive you"… I could actually feel something from her smile for the very first time.
As if to mock the "There's nothing to forgive you for, so I won't forgive you" situation that's been tearing at me for three years, my reconciliation with this girl came in a mere instant.
It was that simple… In a mere instant…
If I can be like this with someone else, then what in the world is going on between me and "her" right now…?
Now that we accept and respect each other, it's only natural that our mutual habit of minding other people's business starts to rear its head.
Besides, right around then, while I was listening to her, I was tending to the wounds in my heart for the first time in a long while.
"Please don't cause your girlfriend any more grief. I'll do something about Mihoko myself."
Although what she said coincided perfectly with the thoughts going through my mind.
I couldn't even think straight enough to identify who she meant by "girlfriend."
"Why do you always have to dig up topics that are already settled!?"
"You're three years older than me, aren't you? You're not even mature enough to just calmly take my advice!?"
"That's because you keep poking your head into places I don't want you in!"
"That's because you haven't been telling us the truth! You hid the fact that you had a girlfriend from Mihoko!"
"It's all because you're so indecisive that things have gotten so complicated!"
"Don't just draw your own conclusions then take it all out on me! This is a huge misunderstanding!"
"Again with the playing dumb! Are you intending to make not just Mihoko, but your girlfriend cry as well!?"
The argument between the impatient university student and the overly nosy high school student became so heated that they drowned out the noise of the busy street around them.
And with a, "Like hell I'll ever talk to you again!" from both parties, the two went their separate ways.
…Even though they'll probably see each other again soon enough.
The final look she gave me didn't contain any anger, hatred, or exhaustion.
"How could you just let her go like that…?"
It doesn't seem like she's forgiven me at all, but that's precisely why there was still a fierce look left in her eyes.
"After everything that happened… I can't believe she managed to hold back her tears."
"Will she even come back next week…? I suppose I should prepare for the worst…"
"It's fine… She'll come back for sure. She's a really strong girl after all."
She's serious, with a strong sense of responsibility and a hatred for defeat. …And even tougher to break than me.
Someone who's so similar to how I was three years ago wouldn't run away after something this insignificant.
That's why all we need to do is sit tight and wait.
I also have a feeling… or rather, I'm 100% sure that our paths will cross again…
"Kitahara-san's 'no problem' isn't too reassuring. He never goes easy when it comes to girls, after all. That's why Tanicchi…"
"Eh? What? What do you mean by that?"
After finishing the fourth and final lecture today, I've since walked for about… ten minutes.
Words like, "It's been three years", or "It really takes me back" seem too mundane for this scenery.
It's just that I find the ages and the uniforms of the students rushing home in the opposite direction to be somewhat nostalgic…
Well, I guess the very fact that I'm contemplating on how I've grown older makes me sound like a middle-aged man.
Peeking at my watch, I see that it's 3:40. I'm a bit early, but…
The instant I turned toward the buildings…
Whether it be by probability, expectation, or more than anything, by fate…
A certain someone who I was sure I'd be meeting here eventually was standing right in front of me with a surprised expression, just as I expected.
"Are you here to see me, by any chance?"
"I was just wondering if you were looking to apologize, is all. For saying mean things to me, for abandoning your position as my trainer, or maybe for showing up at my workplace in the first place."
"I don't think I'm in the wrong for any of the things you've just mentioned, though, not even in the slightest…"
"No, that has nothing to do with this."
"So you do have one after all! You were lying when you said you didn't have one!"
"I only said 'That has nothing to do with this.' I never said anything about having one, not even once."
And, as always, we get along like the same poles of two magnets coming together.
"Mihoko did come to school for a day a while back, but she stopped coming again recently, you know? …All because she found out you were lying to her."
"Don't spread slander like that around. While I'll admit the attitude I took with her wasn't the best, I can at least guarantee I haven't lied to her."
"I don't have a girlfriend. I don't even date girls in the first place… I don't have the right to."
"The right to…? I have no idea what you're talking about. All I'm hearing from you are desperate excuses for why you're distancing yourself from Mihoko."
"If you can't understand it, then don't disregard everything I said so easily."
"If you want me to understand, shouldn't you be explaining it in a way that's understandable? Isn't that what you call being sincere?"
"Don't bring up sincerity so lightly… Just who am I supposed to be sincere to here?"
"To Mihoko, of course. And, if you could also put it in a way that can satisfy me as well, then we probably wouldn't have had this argument in the first place."
"Isn't it your own fault that you're angry…?"
"That's all because you keep popping up in front of me and provoking me over and over and over again, Senpai!"
"And those were all coincidences. I've never actually wanted to meet you on my own volition."
I suppose I understand her frustration to a certain extent, though…
"So, what business do you have with me today? Did you just coincidentally get hired as our substitute teacher or something?"
"Substitute teaching comes next year… I do want to get a teaching permit, though."
"Oh, that's good. I'll have graduated by then, so I guess I won't be seeing you in class."
"On the other hand, we'll be walking around the same campus from then on."
Do I really get this irritating when I talk to someone…?
"…Game, set and match. I'll see you around."
"Eh? Wait… Hold on a second! I'm not finished yet…"
"I have an appointment in the faculty room at 4 o'clock. I can't be late now, can I?"
"Isn't it past 4 o'clock already? It's common sense to be there five minutes before an appoi…"
Finally having gotten her permission, I turn around and hurry to the buildings…
"I said wait! Weren't you here to apologize to me, Senpai!?"
"I don't believe I said I had any business with you in the first place."
"Then why did you even come here! Don't tell me you were just using me to kill time!?"
…Feeling a slight sense of superiority having outwitted her, while also holding in a considerable amount of dissatisfaction.
She really thinks I'm the one at fault for last week's incident, huh…
"Hah… Hah… Haah… W…What's his problem!? Coming over and getting me more and more wound up then just running away…"
"What!? I'll have you know I'm in a terrible mood right now!"
"Ah, I do think that was his last name, yes. But I totally don't have even a single bit of interest in that whatsoever!"
"Not a chance! How about you, do you guys know each other?"
"Is that right? Please send my condolences to…? Ogiso, is your sister's last name Izumi?"
"…I don't think my family has any complex issues like that, no…"
"Really, now! You got a job at a publishing company, Kitahara? I never thought you'd be interviewing me one day."
"Oh no, it's only a part-time job, for now. I'll be graduating next year."
A reunion with my slightly fussy guidance counselor…
"Oh, I see. But it does take me back. You were at the top of your grade and gave a speech during the entrance ceremony after being accepted here, right? I remember it like it was yesterday."
Doing nothing but fondly reminiscing about the past, he does test my patience a bit.
"You made the graduation ceremony's speech too, didn't you, Kitahara? You held on to your place as the top of the class for all three…"
"Suwa-sensei. I didn't exactly come here to reminisce about the past…"
And besides, I fell out of the top ten during the last set of finals, but he's probably forgotten unpleasant memories like that.
"Ooh, that's right, that's right. Last week's Kaiou Graph sparked a huge conversation here in the faculty room too."
The truth is, the response to my interview request as "Kitahara from Kaiou Graph" was awfully fast.
Even for the prestigious music program of Houjou High, which has produced many successful alumni, this award could still be considered an extraordinary accomplishment.
"Making a name for herself in Europe, huh? Quite a big deal, really."
"Touma's really doing her best out there, isn't she…?"
In a faraway place that I know nothing of…
Is she gritting her teeth as she works her heart out? Or is she humming a tune without a care in the world?
Has she gotten used to living abroad? Does she ever miss Japan?
Or perhaps she's already forgotten how to converse in Japanese already? Has she completely thrown away all of her memories of this country?
…Has she already forgotten all about me?
"She sure has made our school proud. Truly worthy of being called the finest student to ever enroll in the music program."
Having had my thoughts trail off to the distant unknown for a little while, I'm now incapable of following the active conversation I'm having with the man before me.
"She might have Touma Youko's blood in her veins, but the excellent education she received must have played a part as well."
"Still, helping Touma-san spread her wings and fly into the world was none other than the Houjou High School Music Program's age-old tradition, along with its spectacular guidance."
Well… addressing alumni with honorifics is normal… right?
"Oh yeah, do you know about the piano in Music Room 2? She treasured it during her days here, and it was in fact a donation from her mother."
"Yes, I know about that, of course…"
"We've had strong connections with Touma Youko for many years. After all, sending Touma Youko herself into the world was also none other than…"
"'She was quite the troublemaker' would probably be a better hit with the readers."
"Hahahah, you've got me there, Kitahara. Yeah, just like you said, she really was something else."
I interrupt Suwa-sensei's over-embellished praise because…
Somehow, I feel like… his words are a complete denial of the memories that I'm incapable of erasing for good.
"Well, geniuses are often a little tough to deal with. Still, I suppose the old days have become quite nostalgic now, huh?"
"It's only been three years, but it feels like it's been forever."
The pride of the music program? A prodigy born from a blessed background?
The Touma I know isn't some high and mighty noble, fit to always bask in the brilliance of the sun.
She was someone who was even labeled as the model underachiever, having enrolled in the music program only to barely even graduate after transferring to the regular program.
She couldn't make a single friend in her first year and made enemies of her entire class during the next. And as for her final year… A lot happened.
She was often late, absent without reason, and slept in class. Neither her classmates nor her teachers wanted anything to do with her, the biggest offender of which is standing before me right now.
Even so, because of the aloof, unconcerned way she presented herself as well as her elegant looks, no one could actually discover just how lonely she was deep down.
"Oh, speaking of which, Kitahara. I'm sure you'll cover that particular topic, right?"
"You know, the High School Festival's live performance… Weren't you in it too, Kitahara?"
"Ah, ahh, that thing…? Was I, now? It wasn't really a big deal…"
Once again, I can't keep up with how he switches from one topic to the next.
"Wasn't it a huge success? Rumors of that still flood the halls whenever the festival comes around."
But this time, even if I try to dodge it little by little, it's still too sensitive of a topic for me to have been prepared for.
"I believe the student council still has a recording of it on DVD. I'll have them give you a copy later."
"Thank you for your concern, but… there's no need for that, I think…"
"Really? I thought it was pretty interesting, though. To think that the prodigal pianist once played the trumpet and guitar at some school festival."
"The sax and the bass, you mean…"
I suppose it's in the school's best interests for me to write about something like that.
After all, that was the only school event she ever took part in.
"Um, let's see… He's a university student, around twenty years old, has a gloomy expression, likes to correct others, speaks rudely, and has an even ruder personality…"
