"…You started straying from physical characteristics about halfway through."
"…His height's a little short of 180cm. He's on the thin side, with no real defining characteristics…"
"Not at all! He's not attractive in the least! …Okay, maybe just a little."
"I can't just stand here and mock my friend's taste in men, okay?"
"Well, I haven't seen him… I haven't run into anyone for a while anyway."
"Then you should've just said that to begin with!"
"Haah… Haah… Haah… W-Where did that guy run off to?"
"Since when did a third woman come into the picture…?"
"How is he going to take responsibility if Mihoko ends up not being able to graduate!?"
The cold winter air pours in from the open window.
With the heaters long since shut off, it didn't take long before Music Room 2 was filled with winter's chill.
On the other side of the window, I can see the sports clubs that have just finished practice as well as the scarlet sunset transitioning into a light indigo.
And if I look straight down… the rigid pavement that would leave more than just a bruise had I fallen onto it.
"Kitahara… what are you doing, you idiot…?"
That's right… I remember hanging from this very ledge…
Looking back at it now, I can't believe how stupid doing all that was… although, I'm quite sure I thought it was pretty stupid back then as well.
But even so, the only thing that was on my mind back then was to find the owner of Music Room 2.
She was always here, playing the piano that's right before me now, without anyone bothering her.
As if to make fun of my arduous battles in Music Room 1 right beside her, she effortlessly matched her playing to my guitar to guide me.
"Though, even if I tell you that, I have a feeling you won't leave."
No matter how many times I overwrite these memories with new ones…
No matter how many times I repeat the words "I've already forgotten," as if to cast a spell upon myself…
The source of her hatred toward her mother, but also the one thing that bound the two together…
Once again brings out memories from three years ago to the present.
Without even sparing a glance in my direction… joyfully, yet somewhat sullenly…
…Effortlessly and flawlessly, you played the piano…
"…The song that we met by? Touma-san is correct!"
And right by my other side, there was Princess Snow White, who broke into song under the grace of her piano.
Those days brought me to the greatest heights of happiness and to the deepest depths of sorrow.
"…There's no way I wouldn't like it. There's no way it wouldn't be fun. There's no way it wouldn't be enjoyable."
"Don't tell me you can't even figure that much out without asking…"
"Even after we've entered university… even once we're in our second year, and then our third year, and even if we're in different departments…"
What interrupted me before I could sink into my melancholic thoughts was…
"You lied to me again, didn't you! Just how many people are you going out with…?"
Wearing the same uniform as the girls in my memories, yet with none of the nostalgia attached.
"Sorry. I'm just an outsider, yet I'm running around the school as I please."
"Eh? Ah, yes. The school is about to close, so we need to lock up…"
"Yeah, I know. I was a student here until three years ago, after all."
I'm sure that I'm embarrassed over being caught messing around…
But I also think that there's more to my expression, one that suggests that I'm also relieved over being found.
"Remembering to lock up is pretty impressive. Most people forget all about it."
"The upperclassmen, in particular… They get more and more careless about stuff like this."
"Yeah, not to mention these special classrooms. It really takes an effort to get the guys that don't want to go home to leave."
"…What are you doing in Music Room 2? It's not really used by anyone anymore."
"I borrowed the key from Suwa-sensei. I'll have to return it later."
"Then I'll take it to him for you."
I could feel that the cold air of the room had affected her from the tiny bit of contact I had with her hand just now.
"Did you know? The piano here was donated by the famous pianist, Touma Youko."
Now that I think of it… whether my feelings for this girlーSugiura Koharuーare of passion or indifference is something I haven't really thought about until now.
"Yeah, it's been making rounds around the school. Touma Youko's daughter is one of our alumni, and they say she took first place in a European competition."
With how I am right now, it wouldn't be unfair for someone to call me cold or heartless.
"It's about time I head home, then. It's gotten pretty dark, so if you'd like, I can take you to the station…"
"I have some other matters to attend to. …It's fine, I'm always doing things around this hour."
My responses come out more naturally than they had the week before, my words unconcerned with formality.
And for that reason, her refusal of my courtesy sounds unnaturally natural, and our conversation ended there as she no longer had any more cards to play.
"Oh, yeah… I might show up at your workplace again."
"If the job calls for it, then I have no right to complain."
The halls are already pitch black.
But right now, I don't really dislike this darkness all that much.
Perhaps reliving such memories in the very place they were formed will mitigate the pain that always comes with remembering them, if only slightly.
"Why did he look so sad and yet so happy at the same time…?"
"…This is a lot better than I thought it'd be."
"I can't have you looking down on me all the time, now, can I?"
It's been a week since our last study session.
During said week, Izumi managed to compile what she referred to as "an old pile of research files she dug up from her place," with her level of progression far exceeding my expectations.
I never could have imagined a product like this coming from someone who never even shows up to seminars, much less someone who's a month late on submitting her paper.
"The interpretations you came up with for these Oni folktales are pretty interesting. You even start empathizing with the Oni by the end of it."
It initially looked like a generic story about a samurai going to slay a mountain-dwelling Oni that's been attacking humans, but some unexpected developments pop up about halfway through.
As it so happens, the samurai is saved by the female Oni, the two fall in love, but she is branded a traitor and executed by her own older sister…

"This doesn't have the common theme of 'good triumphs over evil' you often see in these stories, plus it's also fairly romantic. …Is this really a local folktale that's spread around where you're from?"
"The most popular alternative theory says that the Oni is actually from a clan of hunters in space, and that a spaceship or her spirit itself is still on that mountain somewhere."
…The very fact that you're calling it an alternative theory suggests that it's not the most popular theory. Though I guess that's a trivial problem.
"…Well, you didn't not do your research… maybe. But, no, I can't jump to conclusions yet…"
"Really, Haruki? You really can't accept me if I'm not some lazy and hedonistic grasshopper or something?"

More importantly, there's the fact that this carefree woman in front of me was capable of putting together something like this three years ago, and it makes saying things like, "time is a cruel mistress" come to mind…
No, I really am sorry, Izumi. I apologize again from the bottom of my heart, so please forgive me.
"Well, Houjou accepted me because I used to be quite the hard worker. I'm not sure if it was the right decision on their part, though."
"You said you lived somewhere in the metropolis, right? Which school did you go to?"
"…Just some public school. Nothing out of the ordinary. If you weren't at least in the top ten, there was no way you could come here, to Houjou."
…Which means she was actually one of the top students in her class.
"I've asked you this before, but why were you conducting this far-out research before you even hit university?"
"Well, basically… I'm someone who's willing to put an enormous amount of effort into whatever I'm interested in… A geek, I suppose?"
"If only you could apply that mentality to your schoolwork…"
"I'll make some, so don't just fall over like that…"
The moment I stood up for a good stretch, Izumi just dropped her upper body onto the bed.
Just when my impression of her was finally improving, too… You really can't keep a good impression of this woman for too long.
"Aah, my legs are so numb… I can't handle sitting on my knees. Haruki… let's go buy a new table and some chairs. Wanna go have a look tomorrow?"
"Don't make such crazy demands of a working student who lives alone with no allowance. You were sitting with your legs spread to the side rather on your knees anyway, Izumi."
"For someone living in such a comfy place this close to the station, you're quite the cheapskate, aren't you?"
"Being so close to the station means my rent is a nightmare. You think I have the budget to be picking up unnecessary furniture?"
"Come on, can't you be a bit more considerate? You're terrible at this hospitality thing, Haruki."
"Also, don't just establish yourself as a resident of this household like that. You're only allowed here until your paper's done at most."
"And you're awful at this friendship thing, too! You're totally some kind of massive sadist, Haruki!"
This woman just told me not one minute ago that her legs were numb, and yet she's making a huge fuss while noisily kicking her feet around on my bed right now.
"Don't throw a tantrum like that at someone else's home. It's unsightly."
Especially not… with that outfit on.
I passed her the instant coffee I just made, and she started gulping it straight down.
…There are a lot of women around me who like their coffee black.
"That day you came over last week… There was a girl from the high school waiting at the front gate, remember?"
"Ah, you mean that girl you only planned a steamy one-night stand with, but who kept pestering you about entering a serious relationship after you had devoured her youthful body?"
"…We're probably thinking of the same person, but I'd appreciate it if you could do something about that preposterous misunderstanding of yours."
"You… told her that we were dating, didn't you?"
"…Didn't you say you didn't want to see her again?"
There was a brief pause at the very beginning, but Izumi doesn't seem to be fazed at all.
Well, it's not like I've ever seen her lose her composure in the half a year or so I've known her.
"We just happened to bump into each other somewhere else. And it seems she was carrying a huge misunderstanding about me with her."
"Well, did you manage to clear it up? The misunderstanding, I mean."
"I had no choice but to clear it up, obviously, the moment I found out you were lying."
"I even used what I thought would leave the least amount of loose ends, too."
On the other hand, it also means this woman lies without batting an eye.
Well, to speak of whether she's shown any signs of a conscience within the time I've known her, spanning more than half a year… I'll just stop here.
"Aa-ah, all my hard work has gone to waste. And all because you're just way too serious all the time, Haruki."
More importantly, she's looking at me with a dumbfounded expression, as if I'd failed to properly read the mood…
"Why did you tell her that… nonsense?"
I really have to take an admonishing tone with her.
Even though I know full well that she probably said all of that for my sake…
"After all, Haruki, you want to get away from women, right?"
"You really can't allow yourself to get too serious. Your aversion toward women goes beyond mere hatred, is it instinctual?"
"She did it all for my sake" is probably an understatement at this point.
"And that's why you're allowing meーsomeone who others see as a woman while you alone do notーto stay by your side, Haruki."
"So I figured I should live up to your expectations. That's why I simply put up that barrier for you just so you wouldn't get into any more direct contact with other women, you know, Haruki?"
Before I knew it, she's come to understand me.
"It's not like I'm upset or even shocked that you don't treat me like a woman, you know. I don't exactly hate our relationship as it is now, anyway."
She's already seen through the almost disrespectful sense of comfort I have when I'm with her.
"Actually, you could even say that I really like our current relationship."
And yet, she's willing to seal up her pride as a woman and any other such feminine emotions for me.
"So don't hesitate to come to me if you need to, Haruki. In exchange, I'll be counting on you for my paper, dinner, and a place to crash."
It's definitely not the simple exchange of services she makes it out to be. She's simply going along with "my ulterior motives."
I can't recall ever revealing this much about myself…
Why does this person know so much about me? Just how much does she actually know?
"If you… If you already knew this much, then why…"
"…Why did you choose to dress in such a revealing fashion today of all days!? I've been able to see them since a while ago, you know!?"
"Eeeh, is something wrong? Don't tell me you're getting all excited because you saw the bare legs and panties of someone you don't even think of as a girl? Ahaha, ahahaha～!"
If you know full well how I feel, then why are you still messing with me like this?
"Don't show your legs to a guy in his house, especially if he's not even your boyfriend! Don't cross your legs like that! How shameless…"
As soon as she got here today, she turned on the heater and raised the temperature by 5°C.
And, ignoring the baffled look in my eyes, she proceeded to take off her coat and sweater and started relaxing like she was in her own home.
…In just a camisole and miniskirt, she's dressed a little more casually than she really should be in front of a man.
"But the way you've been trying to look away from me is just so cute, Haruki. I was just about to flaunt my legs more than I'd intended to!"
Let's not forget two certain objects barely covered by her camisole that are ever so slightly bouncing to the rhythm of her laughter.
"At least put on a sweater or something. I seriously can't even look at you like this."
Does she even have a bra on under that? …I'm a little scared of the answer, so I won't ask.
"You're making such a big deal out of it, but it's just stuff I wear around the house. I can feel comfortable dressing like this precisely because we're friends."
"That's just you trying to trick me. I think you should look up the phrase, 'a hedge between keeps friendship green.'"
"You really mind it this much? Even though I'm not a woman to you? Haruki, are you bi or something?"
"I don't even know where to start with you…"
"(Pictured left) At the Houjou High School entrance ceremony."
"April, 20xx. Accepted into her mother, Youko's alma mater, Houjou High School."
"Her extraordinary ability was made clear the moment she entered, participating in a national competition while only in her first year."

"With overwhelming support from the judges in the final round, she took first place. From then on, the name of the 'most astounding prodigy since the school's founding' quickly spread throughout the nation."
I imagine that she'd either scratch her head in irritation or just straight up tear it apart if she saw this.
Still, with the info I gathered from my trip to the high school, I can't really write anything that doesn't reek of stealth marketing.
"I guess I should rein it in a little."
Before the interview, I did think I would need to apply a fair amount of editing afterward, but I didn't expect that it would be heading in this direction.
No matter who I asked, everyone from the faculty had nothing but praise for her, to the point where I'm almost starting to question my own memories.
It's like their memories of how they treated her and the humiliation they put her through were all cleanly washed away from their hearts.
I'd go as far as to consider them bullies… no, it's not like she was always on the receiving end either.
"But now that I think about it… this'll probably turn out boring."
Everyone holds nothing but admiration and praise for Touma, hailing her as an unbelievable prodigy, an unmatched model student, and an elegant and refined lady.
It's as if Touma had shed her mortal body and ascended into an overpowering, heroic being.
The facts might be twisted, but the material gathered from the interview remains the same.
If this Kazusa that's so fondly remembered by everyone was the real Touma Kazusa…
Could I, too, transform my feelings into more beautiful memories, I wonder?
Healthier ones, like the positive ones I used to have… It'd be great if that were the case, but I can't even bring myself to imagine something like that.
"Hey, Izumi. Isn't the last train about to leave?"
It's been some time since I last called out to Izumi, who's been quietly revising her paper beside me.

Usually her complaints start flying after a mere five minutes, dragging us back into the battle of lazed chatter versus tireless lecturing. However, it's now been 30 minutes since either of us even said anything.
I've never seen Izumi so focused. I guess my passionate efforts finally rubbed off on this lazy girl…
Well, it's not like I'm supposed to be this enthusiastic when it comes to helping her with her paper, though.
"Hey, did you hear me, Izumi… Geh!"
It seems that I was the only one among the two of us that was actually focused earlier.
The body of her paper is nearly complete, but was it inappropriate of me to have left her alone and remained mostly uninvolved?
"If you don't go soon, the train's going to leave. Wake up already."
Seeing how she wouldn't wake up no matter how many times I shook her shoulders, I move on to packing up her documents and whatnot to get her ready to leave.
It wasn't until now that I noticed her bag was much bigger than last week.
Much too big for regular school purposes, with more than enough space to pack a change of clothes for a night…
"So don't hesitate to come to me if you need to, Haruki. In exchange, I'll be counting on you for my paper, dinner, and a place to crash."
1. I should let her sleep on the bed.
2. I need to force her up.
I fell right into her trap.
Was gulping down an extra serving of dinnerーcurry againーtreating me to snacks, asking me to share a beer with her, and taking in my lectures all a planned set-up for this?
…Probably not. That's just how she always is.
Who am I kidding? At this point, analyzing her actions over the past few hours and getting upset over the current situation would just be a waste of time.
"I'm going to lift you up, okay? Forgive me."
Since I turned off the heater to save some electricity, all I can do is find a place for her to relax and keep warm.
Well, in my apartment, my bed is about the only place that would qualify…
As I drag her out from under the table by her underarms and grab the back of her knees to lift her up…
I experience the feel of her bodyーwhich I could only guess up until nowーfor the very first time.
This is bad, she's really soft. Far beyond what I had imagined.
And it's not just the softness of flesh. How should I put it? Her body as a whole brings about a feeling of flexibility.
If I were to associate her with a puppet, one could say she has a lot of movable parts. In actual human terms, she could pass off as a gymnast. Her body feels more tender than the average woman's…
As my thoughts slowly edge away from normalcy, the few seconds of what would seem like heaven to other men but like hell to me, finally end.
Completely oblivious to what I just did to her, Izumi continues her sleepy breaths.
Coming to a guy's house, changing her clothes, having dinner, and sleeping…
Well, if she did all this based on the assumption that I didn't think of her as a woman, then you can't really say she hasn't thought things through.
"You should really be a little more self-aware, Izumi…"
What will you do if I suddenly get some sort of weird urge?
…Wait, knowing her, she'd probably just brush it off with an "Aa-ah… Whaatever～" or something. That sort of passive acceptance might actually be scarier.
Seeing how just shaking one of her shoulders isn't waking her up, I grab both of her shoulders and start forcibly shaking her.
And as a result, her head ends up crashing down onto the table.
Thanks to that, she's now menacingly glaring at me, with a faint sparkle in the corner of her eye that I'm not sure is a result of her fatigue or simply pain.
But now's not the time to be caught up in these trivial details.
"Hey, this doesn't look good. You're running out of time before the last train leaves…"
"…The last train left like 30 minutes ago…"
It seems like I was more caught up in my article than I thought.
"Yeah, I'll go sleep in the bathtub. And I'll just take a blanket with me."
"Well, you're the one at fault here, Haruki, but it's not like I'm angry at you or anything."
"…If we continue this conversation, I might end up being the one getting angry at you, so how about we drop it here?"
As per a democratic vote just now, the "it's Haruki's fault for forgetting the train schedule and not waking Izumi up in time" party won, with a grand total of one vote.
As for the other voter, he didn't see much point in continuing this stupid argument and gave up his voting privileges.
"Won't it be really cramped in the bathtub? I don't mind you sleeping here."
"The bed" and "anywhere else" are a billion connotations apart.
…Was saying that with the blanket half open while lightly tapping the bed just another one of her jokes?
"Ahahaha… No need to be like that, Haruki. Poking fun at each other is what friends do, isn't it?"
That's what she calls "poking fun" at me, huh…
She's only pretending to understand me, isn't she? Just so she can mess with me like this…
If I really started looking at Izumi as a woman, she'd probably just get a big laugh out of it or something.
Having snuggled into this space too cramped for even a single person, the mounting fatigue slowly but surely blurs out my vision.
"Ah… I'm sorry for calling you so late at night."
"Uwaaaah～ Sorry, I'm still a little drowsy."
"U-Um, well… This number is, um, I mean…"
"Ah, wrong number? …Just be careful from now on, okay?"
"N-No, that's not it… There's no way I could mix up this number."
"Then who are you? Jeez, stop beating around the bush."
"…No, it's fine. I'm sorry for calling this late at night."
"3 o'clock… The same time as last week…"
"N-No, nothing at all. I'm sorry for waking you up. Well then, goodbye."
"Open uuup! Let me take a shower!"
An unfamiliar ceiling. An unfamiliar voice. And an unfamiliar sleeping position.
Being rushed by a seemingly desperate but somehow carefree voice, I slowly lift my body up…
The hand I was using for support slipped, and it took a short while before a dull pain began to throb in the back of my head.
"Whoa, that was a loud noise… Are you awake, Haruki?"
"Rather than 'are you awake?' shouldn't you have asked 'are you okay?' instead? Even if it's only out of courtesy…"
My hospitality to Izumi, who's only a friend, didn't end at just dinner. I also seem to have offered her some other form of accommodation.
"You didn't have to lock the door. What, you really couldn't trust my self-restraint?"
Even though it was more likely that I didn't trust myself, it's not like locking the door from the inside would do anything to stop that anyway.
"But, for real, you seriously slept like this last night? Doesn't your body hurt or something?"
I only actually fell asleep around the time the sun started popping its head above the horizon.
That aside, the fact that the back of my head's hurting this bad also means I can't really feel the pain anywhere else in my body.
"Yeah, around 8 o'clock. If you hurry, you just might make it to that first period class you love so much."
Not just the first period; I love all of my classes.
I guess I'm still half asleep since I could only manage to answer her in my head.
"I'll be borrowing your shower. Oh, and I want two slices of toast and my egg fried on both sides. I'm more of a sauce fan, so don't go putting salt and pepper on it, okay?"
"…Don't just assume I'll make you breakfast."
Do I even have any eggs left…?
"Stop wasting time and come out already. Well, I won't stop you if you say you want to join me or anything…"
"Well, I'd stop… Don't just start stripping!"
Even after telling her that wearing nothing but a camisole was enough to drive me crazy, she still…
I actually saw it for a split second.
"…You're never staying here again. If you miss the train again next week, you'll be sleeping outside. I'll have that sleeping bag you love so much ready for you."
…The change of clothes she brought are the long sleeved shirt and pants that she always wears. Stuff that isn't nearly as revealing.
"Aah, I just remembered, Haruki. I might need to apologize to you about something, maybe."
"If said something is supposed to be a given, don't talk about it as if it's still merely a possibility."
There are so many things wrong there that I don't even know what I should get mad at her for first.
"You left your cell phone in the room, right, Haruki? Someone called last night, so I answered it."
"If you consider something as trivial as that worth apologizing for, then why don't you be a bit more considerate about all the other troubles you caused…"
"It was a girl. After hearing my voice, she sounded pretty shaken up."
"I checked the caller ID this morning and it was… Ogiso… Yukina? I think that was her name."
That "Yuki"(雪) is actually read as "Setsu"(雪) for "Setsuna"(雪菜).
"She called at 3 o'clock, so it might have been some kind of emergency."
Three in the morning, so three hours past Wednesday.
Which means it's the same time as last week…
"It might be better if you gave her a call about it. Maybe she's caught up in some weird misunderstanding."
"Really? If you want, I could just call her back…"
The possibility never crossed my mind.
Our little exchange the previous week had been a joyful, irreplaceable moment for the both of us, one that we'd managed to share together for the first time after so long.
At the very least, that's how I felt about it. Setsuna probably felt the same… I think.
Our words reached each other and managed to shorten the distance between us.
So if I were to be given another chance to contact her, I'm certain that I'd unhesitatingly press the accept button if she were to call.
If we could just casually continue with that two, three more times, then maybe we could find our way back to the path we strayed away from three years ago.
We might have reached the first point, but our second destination happened to disappear out of the blue.
That's why this single point that will never be a line will never be the thing that connects us.
"We'll end it here for today. Bring the attendance sheet up to the front, please."
Our third lecture of the day is over, and the sun has already made its way over to the west.
There are no more classes left for the day, so we should head on over to the seminars…
"Hey Izumi. Regarding your paper, you should talk to Professor Ogishima about your progre…"
Now that I think about it… Other than signing the attendance sheet, this woman beside me spent the whole class lying on her desk.
Be it during the third period just now or the first two periods in the morning, all she did was sleep.
Even I, who slept in the hard and uncomfortable bathtub, managed to properly wake up, and yet the woman who slept on my bed is still half-stuck in dreamland.
"Wake up! You slept through all three periods!"
Just thinking about what happened last night almost makes me want to outwardly express how furious I am.
"Owowow… Jeez… What are you doing, Haruki…?"
…Well, I actually did express it though, if only a little.
"The lecture's over already. Just how much do you intend to speed up your growth?"
"What? So you peeked at me in the bath after all?"
"I was only talking about your height. There was no sexual meaning to that whatsoever."
"Fwaaa… Umm, what period was that just now? What time is it?"
"It's already this late? I sure have been studying for a while～"
"Your response certainly doesn't betray my expectations. It's about time for the seminar."
"Ah, sure, go ahead. I'll be heading back to bed."
"You're coming with me, of course. You finally managed to make some progress on the paper, so we should go tell the professor…"
"Just take care of it for me, Haruki. Besides, he'd trust what you tell him much more than any progress report I gave him."
"Have you never thought to rebuild this broken trust between you two at all?"
"Who cares what you do in university as long as you're not expelled? Alright then, good night."
"Hey, wake up already, Izumi! At this rate you're really not going to graduate! Do you really understa…"
A familiar figure with a familiar voice approaches me from the opposite direction of where waves of people are rushing out the door.
"Took me forever to find you. What are you doing hiding all the way here in the northern part of the campus?"
"Well, I'm obviously here because Building 3 is my home ground."
Building 3 in the north is the main building for the Literature Department, and this guy's Public Policy Department, Building 6, is all the way in the south.
"Ran away to the Literature Department right under our noses, you did. I can't even find anyone to borrow any cash from anymore."
That's why there's only a very slim chance that we would just happen to run into each other unless one of us deliberately wanted to.
"All right, how much do you need? Nothing in the five digits please. Also, you have to pay me back by the end of the year…"
"I didn't come here to beg you for money, man. I could get at least seven girls to treat me to dinner any day of the week."
"…How have you even managed to stay friends with Io for all these years?"
At first it was just his attempt to make her jealous and gain a reaction, but they ended up unable to break away from those old facades, no matter how many years it's been.
That's not to say Io's without fault, seeing how she won't give him a proper reaction.
"More importantly, I'm here to talk about you, not me… What in the world did you say to her?"
I hate the fact that I can tell who Takeya's talking about just from his expression and the way he's purposefully being unspecific.
"You know that's not true. How long do you think I've known you guys?"
"I really didn't say anything. We haven't even contacted each other in over a week. …At least I haven't."
It's Thursday already. It's been over 168 hours since then.
"So you're saying it's the opposite? Are you ignoring her again?"
What happened was a complete accident. I shouldn't need to get questioned by Takeya like this because of that.
"Why are you doing this, Haruki…? How long do you plan to keep this up?"
"I just told you, I didn't do anything."
…I don't want him to cover for me either.
"You'll never find anyone better than her… She'd take the Miss Houjou title in an instant if she tried. Not to mention how family-oriented and loyal she is… She's so perfect it's almost scary."
"Exactly. She's way out of my league. We shouldn't have gotten involved with each other in the first place."
"…Well, it's not like you've ever admitted you were just joking before."
Takeya and I… Takeya, Io, and I… Just how many times have we had this exact same conversation before?
"But Setsuna-chan wouldn't admit it either. She'd never admit to hating you or never wanting to see you again."
The three of us, the things I've done to Setsuna, and the awful way I handled things afterward.
"So if someone were to ask me to choose between you and Setsuna-chan, Haruki, I'd undoubtedly take her side."
Despite knowing how terrible I am and knowing that I'm the sole person at fault, these guys are still desperately trying to patch things up between us.
"Io said the same thing too. So, Haruki, you can whine and fuss all you want, but we've already got the majority vote here."
They're telling me I still have a way of making it up to her. And in the end, not only I, but she'll be saved as well.
"Try and talk to her properly again. It's killing us to see the two of you like this."
They're still stubbornly holding on to such a convenient, fairytale-like conclusion.
…All the while putting their own relationship on the shelf.
"You need to talk to her soon, no matter what, okay? If you need it, I could even set something up for you two…"
"Sorry. It's about time I head over to the seminar."
Takeya's concern really makes me happy. And Io's as well, seeing how she's probably the one pulling all the strings.
But I'm no longer someone who can just accept something so precious.
"Let's go drinking again one of these days. I'll call you. …It's pretty nice for us guys to hang out every once in a while."
Because he… no, neither of them really know. Neither of them know the true severity of what I've done.
That's rightーthey have no idea at all. They don't know the Setsuna from back then.
Setsuna's true self, who appeared at the final moment and at the very end of everything, whose wounds I find myself impossible to believe will manage to heal someday.
"Hey, wait up! I'm not done talking!"
"Then spit it out. Stop beating around the bush."
"This Saturday, she's going to a party with the guys from the Medical Department. The party organizers just let the word out."
"What's wrong with going to a party? Why do you look so worried? You didn't get an invitation, is that it?"
"It's true that the only guys allowed are those in the Medical Department, but… that's not what I'm trying to tell you."
"Isn't it just some kind of mixer? Did you get all riled up just for this? Even if it's about Setsuna…"
"From what I hear, that party is going to be pretty crazy…"
"Well, those guys are in our Medical Department, after all. They're not people we can compete against."
"Certainly… even the girls have tough times getting their hands on tickets. Setsuna-chan was personally invited by the party manager, though."
"Not much we can do about it, then. If you're so upset about it, go be a doctor or something. I'm bad with blood, so I'll pass."
"That's not what I meant when I said the party is going to be crazy… They might be using drugs or something on the girls. Knock-out pills or those aphrodisiacs…"
"…Isn't that just an urban legend? Made up by all the guys jealous of the Medical Department?"
"Well, looking at it now, the chance is about 50%… or maybe a little lower?"
"What a waste of time. I won't say anything to those guys from the Medical Department, so don't go spreading it around, okay?"
"Why would I be worried about these petty rumors?"
"The Italian restaurant on the fifth floor of Hishijima Building, Onjuku, 7 PM. Located at the 23rd exit furthest in the back, near the east entrance…"
By the time Takeya got to me, Izumi had already swiftly made her way out of the lecture hall.
And she apparently waited out here quietly until our conversation was finished.
"Ah, that sounds like something I'd say."
Another sequence of footsteps that are only slightly slower than my own follows me as I head to the seminar room.
And I thought she was fully intent on going home just a minute ago.
"I really think… you should give her a call."
Not an old friend like Takeya and Io, but more than just a regular friend in the same department. I'm just a little bit grateful for this sort of distance between us.
She's the only one who would casually step in and ask about something like this, and would know to not cross any boundaries she shouldn't…
"Could you lend me 9900 yen? I'll pay you back on New Year's."
"Too objective, unambitious, uninspired, and dull. There's no passion either. All you did was just list the comments you'd received as they are."
She's talking about the first draft of my first solo assignment that I've finally submitted.
"What horrible article is this? I only get more disgusted the more I read it. Is running errands the only thing you're good at? Can't you handle something that takes some actual thinking?"
Even if one were to describe her current actions as "teaching someone strictly to improve them," her sudden criticism is actually unbelievably harsh.
"No, this isn't even a matter of your skill. This is just completely off the mark. You have no idea on the message you want to convey to the reader, now, do you?"
Well, it's not like I'd believe those comforting words anyway. If I were to be asked why, I could only say that Mari-san's expression gave it all away.
"Yeah, yeah. Kitahara's just a part-timer. And this is his first solo article…"

"Who in their right mind would go and write a puff piece like this for their first article without explicitly being asked to? And for all the puffery it does, it's barely even flattering. This is absolutely worthless!"
If she were only upset because the article's worth less than the paper it's printed on, she probably wouldn't be having such an obviously irritated expression on her face right now.
"Kitahara… what in the world is wrong with you? I didn't think you could even come up with something as unreadable as this."
I'd also mention how she's talking more like a man right now…
"What do you think was the reason I chose you to handle this article?"
"Because I used to go to the same school as Touma Kazusa."
"Exactly. I had high hopes for the connections and background information you had. Details that outsiders had no access to."
"And what the heck is this? Don't you think even a child could pick up comments like these? At this rate, I'd say even Matsuoka could do much better than you!"
"You hear that, Matsuoka? Good for you. Mari-san has finally recognized your abilities, see?"
"I can't say I can really take that as a compliment after all…"
"Gulp, gulp… Fuuaah… That cooled me down a little."
"No, are you sure you didn't just get tenser?"
After finishing the drink on her desk in a single swig, Mari-san tries her best to look calm and composed.
"You know… if you can't connect with people, there's no way you can handle this job."
She's also trying her best to correct her tone.
"I know you're a little gloomy, not too great with jokes, and a little inflexible, but I don't think you're unable to communicate with others."
"Even if that's true, maybe it'd be best if you could put it a little nicer to your subordinate here…"
All of what she'd said is quite fitting of someone like me, and I think of each and every word she'd just said as a truth that I have no intention of denying.
Even up until now, I managed to interact with others. There were even times I was so deeply involved that people found me annoying.
…This excludes a certain special someone with some special qualities, though.
"Can't you dig out a little more of her actual personality? If you ask around enough, you're bound to find somebody, right? Like her past teachers, friends, boyfriends…"
"…She was always alone, all by herself."
It's more appropriate to say that she was the one who was actually unable to communicate with others.
That's why there's no one at school who knows about her true self.
And it's because of the fact that they know nothing about her that they're showering her with all this exaggeratingly flowery praise this time…
"'Touma Kazusa was always by herself.' Why didn't you write that down?"
"You clearly have a good grasp of her character already, don't you? So why are you holding back?"
I wrote those comments down as they were precisely because they didn't know enough to say anything other than those insincere compliments.
That said, I'm exactly the same as everyone else on the surface. I acted as if I knew nothing, and I didn't go out of my way to want to know anything.
It's only natural that something like that wouldn't sit well with Mari-san.
"Were you just being considerate of your schoolmate? Did you think writing something negative right after her triumph overseas would be detrimental to her?"
I just didn't know how to write it.
I was completely incapable of thinking about her. Rather, I didn't want to think about her.
"Those worries should only come after you've managed to put together something interesting. You're ten years too early for that."
I decided to tackle it myself to throw away my doubts and hesitations, only to keep running away from it all and end up with this worthless mess.
To think I let my awful self that hurt the one I love get in the way of what I wanted to do…
"At any rate, this article is headed for the shredder. Now then, what will you do?"
"I'll be discarding all my work so far, including the information from the interviews."
"No, I'll be starting over. I'll be changing the content significantly. I might also bring some subjectivity into it."
"That's what I was hoping to see from the start. You must have been misunderstanding my intentions thus far, Kitahara."
"Also, it might not make it past editing."
"I don't mind if you manage to come up with something that crazy. I'll tear it up with a huge grin on my face if it comes to that."
"If I'm not mistaken, the deadline is next weekend, isn't it?"
"That's the absolute final deadline. Have it ready the next time you come to work."
The next time would be Tuesday… In other words, I'll need to have it rewritten by Monday, huh.
"Well then, I'm off to a meeting. You can go home now if you'd like. Good work today."
Having laid out instructions that seemed too strict for a student but expected for an employee, Mari-san makes her way out the editing department's doors.
"Well, how should I put it? Don't worry about it too much."
"That's right, yeah, you're still a part-timer after all, Kitahara-kun. You were given such a tall hurdle to begin with."
Afterward, the department's members gathered around and started cheering me up.
"It's fine. Mari-san's criticisms were all legitimate. …That goes regardless of whether I mind it or not."
…It's probably thanks to these caring colleagues that Mari-san can be strict to her subordinates without worrying too much.
"Hey, Kitahara, wanna go grab a drink? I got my share of sermons from the managing editor today too, so why don't we go drown our frustrations together?"
"Nobody gave you permission to leave. You'll have those edits I asked for ready by tonight, yes?"
"…Umm, how about we meet up at the station around 1 AM? I'll probably have double the steam to blow by then, so let's drink until the sun comes up."
"…No, I'll be heading home. I want to hurry and start rewriting."
Or maybe it's because of these caring colleagues that Mari-san has no choice but to be so strict to her subordinates.
"Just don't stress out about it too much. If you get stuck, I can offer some advice."
"Thank you very much. Now then, if you'll excuse me."
"Must be nice to be able to leave already…"
There's only three days until my next deadline.
Since I'll be working at Goodies tomorrow, I actually only have two days…
Before those two days are up, I'll have to prepare an article packed with much more content than a week's worth of interview comments.
…The problem isn't with the time I have nor the available content. I have more than enough of both.
There's just one thingーam I actually capable of putting my thoughts onto paper?
Will I be able to bring myself to show others what I alone know about her true self…?
"Well, to address our morning shift, we'll begin with six people: Nakagawa-san, Iiyama-san, and Mizuhara-san will work in the hall while Honda-kun, Shimoda-kun, and myself will handle the kitchen."
"However, Kitahara-san will step in and help out whenever someone goes for their break, so I believe things will run smoother than usual."
This is my second day of working here again at Goodies since half a year ago.
"And as for our trainee, Sugiura-san, she'll be slowly integrating into the hall team starting today. Let's help her out as much as we can."
"I might still make a few mistakes here and there for the time being, but I'll work hard to improve myself so I won't slow everyone down. Let's do our best to work well together today."
And at the same time, it's also the second day that this girl who's bowing deeply before us right nowーSugiura Koharuーwill be working here.
She's definitely not some weakling who'd be discouraged by what happened last time, though I more or less expected as much.
"Well then, you're all dismissed. Everyone, begin preparations for the restaurant opening."
After our morning meetingーwhich acting manager Satou handled better than expectedーeveryone heads off to their stations.
That leaves me stuck here exchanging awkward gazes with Sugiura-san, who's essentially on standby until she's given a particular task, while I haven't been given a particular position either.
No, I'm actually the only one between us who doesn't appear to be very happy right now.
On the other hand, she's been intently staring at me for a while, without even moving so much as a muscle…
Well, I suppose she's probably waiting for me to give her instructions or something, but she doesn't need to look so scary, now, does she…?
"I want to join the team in the hall as soon as the restaurant opens."
Just as I was no longer able to stand another moment of our current atmosphere, she breaks the silence between us without any hesitation.
"It's still early before noon, so there won't be as many customers for now I think. I don't think I'll be a burden to the others for the time being."
"But in the event that I do end up affecting the flow of our workplace, please step in and assist me, Senpai. You're in charge of training me, so that's part of your job, right?"
Rather than say she's finally broken the silence, she's already gone as far as to start spouting out things non-stop since a short moment ago.
"I'll probably end up breaking the usual pace at around 11 AM, so I'll learn by observing how you all work from then on instead. Please step in and help the others out until 1 PM, Senpai."
"Starting from 1 o'clock, we can begin my training. I'll be asking as many questions as I can in order to improve myself as effectively as possible."
"I would like to go back to helping out again at around 3 PM, so please decide if I'm up for the task based on my performance in the morning."
"That will be how we'll proceed for now, right? Do you have any questions?"
"I believe everything you just said, right down to the 'Do you have any questions?' part, were supposed to be my lines, were they not…?"
And when I say "my lines," I'm not just referring to the position of the one saying them, but the spoken content as well…
After all, the schedule that I'd planned for her is exactly identical to what she had just proposed.
"So there's nothing else, then? In that case, we should go open up shop. Let's do our best today too."
"No, that's also supposed to be my…"
Is this her way of taking revenge on me, or is she just trying to cover up her embarrassment? Or perhaps this is simply the way she is…?
At any rate, Sugiura Koharu's second day at work begins with her forcefully pushing her opinions on me despite being well aware of her place.
…Quite the bossy one, now, isn't she?
"Thank you very much. Your total comes to 3280 yen…?"
"…I'm very sorry. Please wait a moment."
"The cash register made a warning noise and stopped functioning. I think I might have made a mistake."
"I see, let me take over for a bit."
"Please let me have a better look while you're working on that so I can understand it better. This is part of my training, too."
"You need to do this when you reset it. That will let you go back to when you first started with the receipt…"
"Um, you've never shown me this technique before, though."
"This technique's a bit of a cheat, so… I'm actually not sure if I should be teaching you stuff like this."
"You don't need to make such unnecessary considerations. I'll decide for myself whether the knowledge you're giving me is useful or not."
"There's no need to be so reluctant when it comes to teaching me what you know. It's okay to just force it all onto me."
"Look, the customer's still waiting. Please hurry… Can't you at least handle this degree of multitasking?"
"Hey, what's up with her? She seems really obedient today. Did all that stuff last week have that much of an impact on her?"
Why do I have to be subjected to her holier-than-thou way of asking me to teach her things…?
"Let me repeat your order. An egg-topped hamburger steak, combo A with rice, and a pudding parfait after the meal, correct?"
"Can I clean this side up? …Please excuse me."
"Would you like a refill on your ice water? …How about you, dear guest?"
"She seems to be doing just fine."
It's only her second day and there's already no need for me to step in anymore…
"At this rate, we might even be able to take her 'In Training' name tag off tomorrow."
"If that's the case, it'll be a new record."
Be it her knack for learning, passion, or even her perseverance, while I'm at it, she's definitely top class compared to the other part-timers I've seen work here.

Given the pace she's working at, I'd even go so far as to say she could be entrusted with taking on a managerial position during the short winter break, despite the fact that she's only working part-time…
"Man, we really struck gold with this one. There seem to be a lot of smart students from that high school, but all the same, there are also a lot of half-hearted ones, too…"
"Are you sure it's not our acting manager's lack of charisma that's the problem here?"
"That's exactly why it was the right decision to entrust you with her training, Kitahara-san. I'm very much indebted to you."
"…I really didn't do anything. She's made it here on her own two feet."
Amidst our light conversation, Satou's response begins to bother me mildly.
And here I was fully expecting him to play the straight man there.
"You can let her go now, right? She can thrive on her own now, right?"
"Huh? Well, we are short on staff. And I suppose I don't really have to play around with her anymore…"
"That means it's fine if you go help out in the kitchen now, right, Kitahara-san?"
I was careless for a moment, but I finally manage to sniff out what this fiendish acting manager is scheming right before my very eyes now.
"There's a mixer going on today. And, well, there's not enough people on the evening shift, so… I was wondering if you could fill in for me, Kitahara-san?"
"N-No, wait a minute. We've decided that I'd only be responsible for training, no…?"
"They say it's going to be one hell of a party! A friend of mine working at a bank told me that some of the new girls at his place are planning on going…"
"I think it's best if you don't get your hopes up, though…"
"I won't be angry no matter what you say to me today! So please! Let me be a man tonight!"
"Like I said, I don't think things will work out too well with them…"
"You won't? Even if I'm begging you this much, you still won't help me out?"
"…I suppose you have something you absolutely can't put off planned for tonight? If that's the case, I'll give up…"
"The Italian restaurant on the fifth floor of Hishijima Building, Onjuku, 7 PM."
Looking at the clock, it's only 5 PM right now. I still have more than enough time if I plan to do it…
"…Well, it's not like I have another job to get to…"
What would be the reason behind me doing something like that? And how would I even go about doing it?
…I don't even understand what I'm trying to picture right now.
"Aaah, no fair! And I was supposed to have approached Kitahara-san!"
"I promised to go drinking with some friends today, too. Hey, Kitahara-san, forget about the kitchen, could you help me out in the hall?"
What do you knowーa few moments of hesitation on my end and another noisy voice comes my way.
"Both of you having to leave early on the same day… Don't tell me you two are secretly dating."
"No, no, just no! Satou-san and meーimpossible!"
"As much as that's the irrefutable truth, you didn't have to go so far in denying it…"
"If you were the one who invited me, Kitahara-san, I probably would have thought about it. But your guard's so tight that it's probably unlikely to happen."
"No… I don't think going out drinking with me would be much fun at all, anyway."
"Still, you'd only be rated higher if one were to evaluate you as a man they'd entrust the rest of their life to. You're in Houjou, an incredibly hard worker, and you're also picky."
"And I'm just some random part-timer at best…"
"Is 'picky' supposed to be a compliment? People have really only used it to call me annoying up until now."
"That's because you seem like the type of guy who, after getting married and despite always correcting your wife on the tiniest little details, would just do all the housework yourself anyway."
"Then, unable to balance both work and family, you'd overwork yourself and fall into depression."
"What are you all doing, chatting on the job? Please focus on the tasks at hand!"
"All right, does everyone have a glass yet?"
"It's just a toast, a toast, okay?"
"Then let's get on with the toast. Um, Merry Christmas?"
"Ah, whatever! Who cares if it's Christmas or New Year's! Cheers!"
"Nice to meet you, Ogiso-san. I'm Shouda from M2."
"Ah, yes, nice to meet you too."
"The name's Takeuchi. My family runs a general hospital down in Yokohama."
"Anyway, drink up! Ah, I'll go grab some food for you, what would you like?"
"Eh? Oh no, I couldn't bother you with that. I'll just go myself and…"
"Don't worry about it. Hey, you're from around here, right, Ogiso-san?"
"…All I've been doing is drinking these days."
"Welcome! Table for four, correct? Will any of you be smoking? …This way to the no-smoking section, then, please."
While usually crowded with students from Houjou, this place becomes a hot spot for family outings during weekend evenings.
Even though it's a bit of a walk from the station and there are never really customers that have to wait for their turn, the restaurant's still 80% full most of the time.
"The Napolitan and deluxe pizza for Table 8 is done!"
Honda and I are the only two people in the kitchen.
We also got in touch with the other evening shift worker, whose reassuring message of "Just got up" let us breathe a sigh of relief.
"Yes, I'll be right there! Please wait a second!"
The hall's being taken care of by three female employees.

Nevertheless, we're down to about two and a half people's worth in terms of capabilities. It's now a Saturday night where the restaurant is a little off from its original functioning minimum of five people.
Which also means that our pace isn't as smooth as it usually is, if only slightly.
…If I were to leave my post right now, I can't even imagine the disaster that the others would end up with.
…It'll be about 30 minutes until the late evening shift employee arrives. Heading straight to Onjuku after that will take another 30 for me.
…It'd be 9 PM after an hour. It'd still be pretty early in the evening. I'll definitely make it in time.
It's all because he made that stupid prophetic announcement that, despite having nothing to back it up, is still more than capable of making me worry…
There's no way they'll be using drugs or anything, right? It's just a party for university students.
I think there might have been a similar party at one of the local universities nearby that was involved in a crime like that…
"That's what I ought to be saying!"
Before I knew it, my pupil, beneath me in both stature and age, came staring me down with a vicious glare in her eyes.
"Your hands have been moving on their own for quite some time now, you know?"
"It's precisely because there doesn't seem to be a problem that it feels eerie. Please don't work with knives while staring at the ceiling."
"…The sliced steak for Counter 12 is done."
And before I even realized it, too.
"You looked like you were spacing out for a while now. You really do have some important things you need to attend to, don't you?"
Her gaze remains overbearing, almost accusatory, even, as if to lay bare her suspicion of me lying to her.
…She couldn't possibly have any idea of what's happening on my end, though.
Just where exactly does her baseless confidence of "I understand what you're going through" come from, then?
…If I asked my past self that, would I have answered with a smug look on my face?
"You should start getting ready to head home. If it gets too late…"
Remarks that I could only describe as quite insincere spill from my mouth, perhaps due to me folding to the pressure of her troublesome gaze.
"Even when both managers aren't here? Even when we're clearly short on people right now?"
"And I do believe that my capabilities are getting to the point that I won't become a burden anymore, right?"
…But the one Takeya referred to as "a female Haruki" promptly dismissed everything that just came out of the real Haruki's mouth.
"I have their permission, of course. They have the utmost trust in me, since I've never once let them down before."
"I'll be working evening shifts when winter break comes around anyway. Staying out this late isn't a problem at all."
"But forget about me, you should focus on what's troubling you. If there's something wrong, then you should probably…"
"Sorry. I'll focus from now on. Go on, this is for Counter 12."
"I'll be fine. I don't think anything is going to happen, so…"
"Hey, Ogiso-chan, let's go skiing next week. I think it's already started snowing over in Inayama."
"Ah, but I've never tried skiing or snowboarding."
"I'll teach you, I'll teach you. If you don't want to stay the night, then we can come back on the same day. My car can handle eight people, so we can all…"
"You haven't even had a chance to see the snow yet this year, right? Do you dislike snow? It's even in your name."
"You won't change your mind? It doesn't have to be skiing, really. Want to just go have fun somewhere?"
"Don't you have anywhere you want to go to, Ogiso-chan? Anywhere's fine, we can even go swimming if you'd like."
"Yeah, hey, this guy's got a cottage over in Hawaii. We all went there last year on New Year's…"
"The snow and hot springs would be nice… maybe."
"Taking in the sights of snow slowly piling up on the other side of the window, looking up as the snowflakes gently fall upon you in an open air bath…"
"I guess I'm a little behind the times. My interests don't quite match up with everyone's."
"N-Not at all! Hot springs are nice once in a while, right?"
"Yeah, yeah, it gives off that classy, tasteful feel, right? Might be pretty cool."
"Ah, then let's just go with Inayama. They have hot springs there, and the snow's already piled up."
"Then we'll scrap the skiing. Bathing in the hot springs, drinking, watching the snow with everyone, and just leisurely passing the time will be our main goals."
"Then let's reserve our accommodation. One night? Two nights?"
"Mixed bathing. Find one with mixed bathing."
"Hot springs… I'm never going there again. And snow… I hate it."
"Ah… S-Sorry. What am I even saying?"
"L-Let me go get some air. I think I might be a little drunk."
"It sure is rare seeing you at an event like this. You usually act all high and mighty, but you're suddenly okay if people from the Medical Department are involved, huh?"
"…Did you forget who I am? Well, I guess that's to be expected. After all, it's not like you've ever realized that I even exist."
"I'm sorry… Are we in the same department? What year are you in?"
"My name's Yanagihara Tomo. One year under you. …Does that ring any bells now?"
"I'm sorry. As I thought, I can't…"
"…! Did you forget all about what happened back in high school? You even got incredibly popular over what happened with the Light Music Club."
"Is this what they mean when they say that people who like picking on others never remember the faces of their victims?"
"Ah… Could it be that you're Takeya-kun's…"
"Come to think of it, you haven't been up to much lately, have you? What happened to your overwhelming influence and dominance from back in the day?"
"I don't think I'm much different from how I used to be, though."
"You haven't been competing in the Miss Houjou contest recently either."
"That's because… it wasn't an event I wanted to participate in anyway."
"It would've been great if you had thought the same back in high school too."
"Well, since you weren't participating, I managed to win the title this year. Miss Houjou, that is."
"Oh, is that right? Congratulations. You're pretty amazing, Yanagihara-san."
"…Are you being sarcastic? Are you trying to make fun of me, since I never once won against you back in high school?"
"…You really have changed, Ogiso-san. Was that rumor true after all?"
"Ogiso Setsuna, dumped by her boyfriend during her graduation ceremony, and has been reduced to a shell of her former self ever since."
"Oh dear, looks like I struck a nerve. I didn't really mean to do that, though."
"Well, I don't really care either way. I've no interest in you now that you're like this. Now, if you'll excuse me."
"Aa-ah… Why won't those medical department guys shut up about how rich they are? What a boring party. Maybe I should just go home…"
"Oh? My bad! I didn't think there'd be somebody on the other side of the door."
"Oops, I was in a hurry, so… looks like we were both a little unlucky, huh…"
"Aah, you're fine, you're fine. No bleeding either, good for you!"
"Anyway, take care. I don't have another moment to spare over here."
"It's fine if you just think of it as karma, you know?"
"Aaah, I can't believe this, there's sauce all over my dress! I wonder if this'll stain…"
"Oh, you finally look more like a proper Japanese person now. It suits you pretty well."
"Sorry, regarding Table 4's order… they wanted to change their previous order of the mixed fries set to the chicken saute… Is that okay?"
"…Is that a no? I'll go tell them if so."
"No, I haven't started frying yet, so it's alright."
"Then answer the question clearly, please. It's hard to tell what you mean when you're quiet like that."
"I'll take care of the order change. You can go home now."
We were already here before the restaurant's opening at 10 AM, which means more than twelve hours have passed already.
That means the amount of hours we've been actually working is well into overtime territory by now, even excluding our breaks.
"We should be closing in no more than two hours."
"A part-timer shouldn't be working from opening to closing on her second day."
"But you said that we don't have enough workers around, Senpai…"
"That was only true until an hour ago."
I can't believe the sheer magnitude of her unnecessary sense of responsibility…
I can definitely see some of her classmates preferring to keep their distance.
"The amount of customers coming in has died down quite a bit, as expected, so it'll be fine leaving the rest to the evening shift."
Looking at the hall, it seems like only four-tenths of the seats are filled.
Students usually make up the bulk of this restaurant's customers, after all, so it's usually not too busy on a Saturday night like this.
"At any rate, good work today. To be honest, I didn't expect you to get the hang of it as quickly as you did."
The fact that she already worked so hard on merely her second day is… Well, in some ways, it was an expected outcome.
"I'll be staying here until closing time. I have to clean up the place, after all."
"But you've been working just as long as I have, right? You didn't seem to have taken any breaks either."
"…Satou also asked me to lock up afterward."
"Why do you keep insisting on having such an unnecessarily great sense of responsibility?"
Forget it. I'll refrain from arguing back.
After all, she's probably kept her fair share of "You're one to talk" or other similar remarks to herself, too.
"At any rate, take care on your way home, okay? Try to stick to the main roads…"
Did me not arguing back come off as that much of a surprise? She seems to be glaring at me rather sternly.
…I think it's better to say that I don't know what she's feeling right nowーall I know is that she's glaring at me.
"Although I wouldn't mind if some of that excessive sense of responsibility urged you to walk me to the station, you know?"
It's winter right now. The time is just a little past 11 PM.
Last week, I offered to walk her home when it was only 7 PM. I can't believe what I just did.
I guess she was right when she said I was lacking focus.
"Good work today… It's fine, it's my fault for coming in late. I'll take care of tidying up by myself…"
As I turn toward the kitchen, a dependable but frail voice answers me.
If you have any complaints, please direct them to the acting manager.
"Hey, who's coming to the karaoke after-party?"
"Who's staying behind to drink some more?"
"The taxi's here. Get in, get in!"
"You're coming to karaoke, right? We're heading there now, let's go together."
"Your friends all said they were coming too. Don't worry, I'll give you a ride home after."
"Then come with us! How about we go find some quiet place and drink some more?"
"The hell's your problem, Ibata? Don't just jump in out of nowhere, dude."
"You're the one who tried to run off first!"
"Then you come to karaoke with us too."
"But Ogiso-san just said she doesn't want to. Let's just go drinking."
"I need to head home soon, or else…"
"Don't be like that, Ogiso-chan. We finally got a chance to get to know each other better."
"Yeah, yeah! We've barely even had a chance to chat yet."
"There's a place that serves Dom Perignon around here. The atmosphere's nice, I'm sure you'll like it. That's fine with you too, right, Yano?"
"It'll be fine. Let's just get going. This way, this way."
"Hey, the taxi over there! Come here! Come on, get in, Ogiso-san."
"Oooh, there you are! I finally found you, Setsuna!"
"Jeez～ you really had me on your heels. And here I thought I told you not to go outside and just wait for me."
"You're… that girl from the bathroom earlier…"
"Eh, what? Come on, Ogiso-chan, hurry up and get in…"
"Sorry, not happening. Setsuna's about to go drinking with me!"
"Huh? What's going on? The hell are you talking about?"
"There's really nothing going on. We just planned to go together from the start, you know?"
"Hold on, hold on, just cut it with the jokes, would you? She's been with us the entire time…"
"Now, come on, how about you come with us, too? I'll call another taxi over."
"Well, I'm fine with it… but did you get the okay from Mizuno-kun? He's the one who planned our little event with her."
"Yep. Special orders from the organizer. We had it all planned from the start."
"That's how it is, so… come on, Setsuna, let's get going, shall we?"
"H-Hold on. I'm still not quite following…"
"I'll explain once we get away from these guys."
"…Okay, I understand. Well then, everyone, thank you for today."
"My bad, sorry I kept you waiting."
Even after her twelve hour shift, Sugiura Koharu is still her energetic but irritable self.
After throwing a shout and a glare my way, she starts silently heading toward the station.
She walks off without looking back whatsoever, perhaps due to her trust in my "excessive sense of responsibility."
And I, of course, with said "excessive sense of responsibility," act on it and match her quickening pace.
Only a few people still remain on the streets near Minami-Suetsugu Station when it's so close to midnight. The rather desolate atmosphere certainly adds to the chill on this cold winter night.
"Are you really planning to take it on? The evening shift job, I mean."

It might be fine for a guy or an adult to go through a road like this during this time of night and this particular season, but it really isn't a place a young girl such as herself should be walking through.
"Of course I will. I'm planning to work for quite some time, after all."
…But, as expected, she rejects all of my worries with a single sentence.
"Why do you need to push yourself so hard?"
"Because I want to reach my goal in earnings during the winter break. Including my savings, I'll need to get around 200000 yen…"
"200,000… Are you guys planning to go to Europe or something?"
"You seem to be knowledgeable about this. It'll be an eight-day trip across Spain, Italy, and France."
"…I'm glad I got the right answer, but don't you think that's way too extravagant for a graduation trip?"
"My thoughts exactly, but… when I suggested "Why don't we just go to Atami?" to the girls I planned the outing with, I was rejected immediately."
"I suppose you could have at least compromised with Hokkaido or Okinawa…"
"My friends all come from rich families… I actually have the slightest feeling that I chose the wrong school."
"I know what you mean. I graduated from there three years ago myself, after all."
"What was your family situation like back then?"
"Compared to the people around me, I'd say it was… average."
After all, a person close to me was the daughter of a world-class pianist, whereas I'm only from an insignificant branch of a prestigious family from Okayama.
"While we're at it, you mentioned you were working several part-time jobs yourself, didn't you? …You're also working pretty hard, Senpai."
Seeing you taking my words at face value stabs at my conscience a little…
"Anyway, that's just how it is. The lone daughter of a middle class family being surrounded by classmates like that has no other choice but to work her hardest behind the others' backs."
If I remember correctly, there were also people around me working hard while hiding it from everyone else…
But that might have just been a special case.
"I still think you should forgo the evening shifts. Going home alone this late at night is just too dangerous."
The peaceful atmosphere we've maintained up to this point is shattered in an instant thanks to my purposefully dense comment, returning us to the gloominess befitting of the season.
"So in other words… you won't be walking me home from now on? Is that what you're saying?"
And, of course, it naturally follows that this girlーwhose relationship with me is already rather delicate to begin withーwould take offense to what I just said.
"I never asked you to take me home in the first place. You don't need to feel responsible for that, so I'd like to ask that you stop meddling so much."
"It's not because I can't be bothered to…"
"Then why were you being sympathetic just earlier? You treated me kindly once only to now say that…"
"There's going to be situations where I can't take you home, right? Like if I stop coming to work…"
"…Are you quitting? The part-time job, I mean."
From her reaction, I can tell that that particular situation never once crossed her mind.
"I was only helping out in the first place. I only agreed to stay until I turned you into a full-fledged member of the team."
"Basically, I don't really know how things will turn out from here on, so try to stick only to the morning…"
"I don't need someone who's not even a fellow colleague at work to be worrying about me. …I'll be going now."
"You won't be taking me home anymore, right? Then we can just part ways here. Goodbye!"
"I'm taking you home right now, aren't I!? Don't interpret things the wrong way and start throwing a tantrum!"
"If you don't want to be treated like a kid, then stop running!"
On our way home, under the freezing sky.
Sugiura Koharu has been irritated the entire time… and right now, her mood just took yet another turn for the worse.
"Well, here's to us surviving through that absolute bore of a party. Cheers!"
"I thought you were just putting on an act to get me out of there. I didn't think we'd actually be drinking…"
"It was totally an act. And to prove that, there's nobody named Mizuno here, right? It's just the two of us."
"Are you acquainted with the party organizer?"
"No, I only talked with him a little during the party. He looked the most influential among the bunch, so I took a mental note of his name."
"I-Is that so… You pulled that off despite only knowing that much? You sure have guts."
"It's no big deal, really. I'm more than used to that by now."
"By the way… have I met you somewhere before?"
"…You're probably imagining it. This is the first time we've met."
"I'm Nagase Shouko. Economics Department, third year. Nice to meet you, Ogiso Setsuna-san."
"Ah, yes, nice to meet you too, Nagase-san. But if it's our first time meeting, why do you know my name…?"

"Everyone was talking about you before the party started, you know? 'Ogiso Setsuna is coming' and 'trade seats with me' and whatnot. …The guys sitting around you were all winners of their respective rock paper scissors tournaments."
"You're pretty famous, Ogiso-san. You seemed much more popular with the guys than that Miss Houjou girl."
"Everyone was talking about how astonishing it was to see you coming to an event like this."
"My friends were all pushing me to go, and after so many invites, it was kind of hard to keep rejecting them. And also…"
"…No, I just couldn't say no anymore, that's all. That was pretty silly of me."
"You know, I broke up with some guy recently, too. Thought I might have been able to find some new romance at the party, so I gave it a shot."
"Just like that little Miss Houjou said, nobody could stop bragging about themselves. Parents being on some board of directors, owning however many Ferraris or whatever."
"By any chance, did you actually know she was on the other side of the door back then…?"
"So just when I thought I'd go get a drink, I found myself a fellow party-goer who also looked bored out of her mind."
"So you invited me just because of that?"
"You're asking that when I'm already sitting here drinking?"
"Excuse me, another one of these, please!"
"Hardly, but I suddenly got the urge for another glass."
"Are you sure you're okay? Did you have a little too much? Do you feel really tired, or feel oddly relaxed at all?"
"No, not really. Maybe just a little bit drunk, that's all."
"So it was just an urban legend…"
"Oh, yeah. I should tell my parents that I'll be home late."
"Ah, we have a princess here. Just what I expected from a Houjou High graduate."
"No, it's fine. …I'm not really that kind of person anyway."
"Then, once again… to our little encounter."
"Now then, I'll be taking my leave."
"…What is it? If we don't hurry, we'll miss the next train."
"…Hah… Haah… Are you… in a sports club?"
In the end, I only managed to catch up to her after we got to the station's entrance, which is where we were supposed to part ways.
"I played tennis until summer came around."
The difference in the rates of our breathing is not a result of our difference in age, but rather just the difference between a sports club member and a former recreational club member.
"Take a second to catch your breath. I can at least wait for that long."
Well, whatever the reason is, it doesn't change the fact that I've been outclassed.
"What stop are you getting off at?"
By the time I caught my breath, the next train had already passed us by.
"I see, then I'll take you all the way home."
"The Minegaya neighborhood is a pretty quiet place, so…"
"I go to school from there every day, so I know that."
"What time do you think it is right now?"
"If it comes to that, I'll just call a taxi."
"We haven't finished talking anyway, right? Come on, let's go."
Even so, I can tell that she still has some things to say to me from the fact that she let that train go.
I think it's about time I settled the differences between us…
After all, we've been stuck in this endless loop of arguing, making up, and then arguing again for about half a month now.
If I don't put an end to this, it might start weighing her down emotionally.
"Instead of worrying about me, shouldn't you prioritize the stuff that's actually on your mind a little more?"
…But naturally putting an end to everything as soon as she sees me trying to settle things, as if she was waiting for that exact moment, might just be a part of who she is.
"There isn't really anything on my mind…"
"You're checking your watch again. That's the eighth time today, and that's only counting the ones I saw."
"I was just checking when the next train would be here."
"You really do have something you need to do, don't you? Something really important."
"That… has nothing to do with anything right now."
"See, that's what I was talking about."
"That attitude of yours. Trying as hard as you can to get involved in others' affairs, and yet not wanting anyone to get close to you."
"Whenever someone tries to get involved, you put a stop to everything, as if you were waiting for that exact moment. It's not just with Mihoko, but me as well."
"You keep forcing your ideals onto others, and yet you yourself don't stick to them at all… It's almost irritating how different of a person you become."
Her real personality isn't as superficial as that.
"That's why I don't know what you're even thinking about. I just don't understand."
"What would you even do if you could understand me…"
"Are you saying that despite trying so hard yourself to understand others? Despite always wanting to take care of others?"
Worrying about complete strangers, and even going so far as to help out someone you hate. An obnoxious meddler.
"Your friend once said something like this before, right? That we're very similar to each other."
"Then if that's the case… shouldn't I be able to understand just what it is that you want to do?"
"Like I said, we're not alike at all."
Firmly holding on to your own beliefs, not letting anyone or anything sway you from them. A sense of absolute justice, blind to the opinions of others.
"You want to talk it out with me? That's fine. But when you do, I'd like 'the both of us' to speak the truth."
"Why do you… always try to force your opinions on me?"
"Because I want to know more about you. I don't want to know someone I can't understand."
"That's so stupid… What's the point in doing something like that?"
"Would you be able to rely on someone who just gives up like that? Would you be able to stand taking advice from someone like that?"
"You're so strange, Senpai. You're meddlesome, strict, and I guess somewhat kind, but sometimes I also feel that you're distant, cowardly, and cold."
"Well, I feel bothered when you act like that around me."
"Why would it bother you? It shouldn't concern you at all!"
"Because I can't get it off my mind. Because I'm very interested in you, Senpai!"
With an irritated glare, the girl before me emits a strong air of hostility…
I wonder if she fully understands all the ways one could interpret what she just said.
Be it her determination to get the truth out of me or my uncertain desire to stop her from prying, both dispersed with the arrival of my phone call.
"Ah, Kitahara-san? It's… been a while. This is Ogiso speaking. Thanks for always taking care of my sister."
"So I just gave it to him straight. I told him that I'd overlook him hiding the other girl from me all this time, but I wanted a clear answer on who he'd pick between us."
"…R-Really. You told him exactly how you felt, huh?"
"And then he was all like, 'I love you too, but she's the only one for me!' seriously!"
"So I asked him what I was to him, and all I got was 'a very close second place'…"
"Can you believe that!? Who cares if the horse was off by a millimeter or an entire mile? It doesn't change the fact that my bet's a bust!"
"Anyway, it just made me think how stupid all of it was. I dumped that guy right then and there."
"Am I? I don't really think I'm all that strong. It hasn't even been a month yet and I'm already telling this stuff to other people. To someone I just met, no less."
"I just remembered that this is actually our first time meeting. It doesn't feel like that at all, though."
"I get that a lot. People say I'm too outspoken. It might have been a reason for the breakup in the first place."
"But it's not like I'd just tell anyone. You'd never tell anyone else, right, Setsuna?"
"Now, then! It's your turn now, Setsuna."
