"Seeing how many men have been lured by your devilish charms, your love life must really be something else, right? I'd probably melt just from hearing how heated it must be. I'm so looking forward to it～"
"C-Come on, let's not talk about that. I already said I'm really not that kind of a person."
"What are you even saying? You stole all the guys' attention for yourself back at that party, didn't you? Don't play dumb with me."
"That's not it. I'm really not like that… Oh… Whatever! I don't care anymore."
"The way you pout like that is also really cute, too! If I were a guy there's no way I'd let you go."
"…That's not what I was aiming for, okay?"
"Come on, there has to be something, right? Some kind of crazy scandal or whatever."
"Oh, you're single right now? Well, I don't mind if you tell me some stuff from the past. Like, from back when you were in high school?"
"Then let's just talk hypothetically! What kind of a guy would you entrust your lovely heart and soul to, Setsuna?"

"Exactly! It'll all be completely hypothetical. Regardless of how probable what you're saying is, it's absolutely not going to be taken as fact by meーnothing but supposition and imaginary conversation."
"Barkeep! Another one for both of us!"
"If we're only talking hypothetically, then… Someone that likes looking out for others would be nice."
"Minegaya, Minegaya. Please mind the door on your way out."
"The doors are closing. Please be careful."
"I could say the same… Weren't you planning to take me all the way home?"
"Sorry, I shouldn't have tried to be sarcastic."
"No… I should apologize. I did say I'd take you all the way home."
Takahiro-kun sounded almost apologetic during the phone call. He also… didn't seem worried at all about his sister's whereabouts.
He merely listened to his parents, who were worried after not being able to reach her cell phone despite it being an hour past her curfew, and contacted "the first person that came to mind."
"But I already told you, didn't I? You really don't need to come searching with me…"
"She's my classmate's sister. I'm worried about her too."
If you talked to her for just a few minutes, even if you didn't want to, you'd easily see that her words are neither lies nor exaggerations. Her concern is undoubtedly genuine.
"I didn't think you'd be in the same class as Takahiro-kun…"
"I'm the class representative for the first term, and he's in charge of the second term. We talk once in a while because of that."
"Topics of our discussions include… A graduate that randomly popped up at school pretending to be making an interview actually being his sister's boyfriend, among other things."
So that's why she reacted a little when I said "Takahiro-kun? Setsuna? Yeah, she's with me right now." over the phone.
"Even though it's just to stop them from worrying, was it really a good idea to lie to them like that?"
The reason being that the person beside me as I was talking on the phone wasn't her classmate's sister, but herself.
"Do you know where she went off to? And do you know why she ran away?"
"Ran away? You're exaggerating things a little. She just went out a little longer than usual. Besides, a 10 o'clock curfew for a university student is…"
"Want to try repeating that after you take a look at your reflection in the window?"
"Here, use my handkerchief. At the very least, you should wipe the sweat off your forehead. …It's the middle of winter, you know?"
"The heater's on way too high in this train, don't you think…?"
My eyes get a little fuzzy after a couple of drops slip in…
"I don't have someone I could call that."
"I was wondering what kind of answer you'd give me, so I asked it like that on purpose."
"Then I'll change my question. Ogiso's older sister… Setsuna-san, was it? What kind of person is she?"
"What's the point in asking something like that?"
"I'm going to be looking for her too, aren't I? If I don't even know what she looks like, how am I supposed to find her?"
"That's why I said you should just go home…"
"Then I'll call the Ogiso residence as soon as I get off the train."
"I'll tell them that I'm the one who's actually with you. And that you're not actually with their daughter."
"And also, I'll tell them that after the phone call just now, you started getting extremely anxious."
Getting driven into a corner by a girl three years younger than me only makes me feel all the more hopeless.
There's nothing inherently wrong with what she's saying either, making my search for a rebuttal a fruitless effort.
"Don't make her family worry any more than they already do. They're really, really nice people."
"…I know. Ogiso might get carried away easily at times, but he's a good guy deep down, and everyone in class trusts him too."
"And besides, I might just be worried over nothing. Actually, I'd say that's the most likely scenario."
"But there's still that one in a million chance, isn't there? I know you're not the type that would easily shrug off something like this. …That's also why you couldn't focus at work, right?"
"I don't mind if you drop the honorifics. You're my senior both at school and at work, anyway."
Maybe the irritated tone in my voice as I said her name put her off or something, but after "Sugiura" makes her comment, she puts on her usual glare.
"It's fine if you don't want to tell me why you're doing it, but please let me join you in searching for Ogiso-san."
"You sure love to mind others' business, don't you, Sugiura?"
"You're in no position to say that to me."
"Eh? So should I keep the honorific after all?"
"Not that! I meant the 'minding others' business' part!"
My little trap must have caught Sugiura by surprise. Her glare remains unchanged, but her face becomes flushed.
"If you're still relaxed enough to poke fun at others, then I guess you're fine. After all, remaining calm is good for your efficiency."
With that, our little bickering comes to an end, allowing us to cooperate on the task at handーefficiently, as she just described it.
"We're arriving at Sasakubo Station, Sasakubo Station. The exit is on the left side of the train."
I'll have to put on my usual study mode within the next five minutes.
This is my true battle stance. Doing anything and everything in my power to achieve the best possible results.
"Someone who likes to look out for other people…? Someone like that sounds rather convenient, although not exactly manly either, no?"
"How do I put this… He's someone who looks out for anyone? Someone who tries his best and puts everything he has into anything? …And someone who only loses out as a result."
"The truth is, I love being spoiled…"
"The way you talk does give off that feeling from time to time, yeah."
"That's why I'm attracted to guys I can rely on. I'd fall in love with someone like that and try to get him to spoil me even more."
"I'd like someone who'd do everything in his power to grant my selfish little wishes. I'd really like that person."
"Even if he might be a little annoying, and even if he might complain about stuff all the time, he'd never abandon me, no matter what."
"He'd be equally nice to everyone else, but save a special sweeter side just for me. Wouldn't that just be the best?"
"That's quite a modest selfish side you got there, huh?"
"As a result, when he'd hurt someone, he'd hurt himself more in the process. He'd blame himself for everything and end up hurting himself more and more…"
"Of course. Do you even need to ask?"
"You know, I… I loved him when he would look over to her with those gentle, affectionate eyes."
"He was serious, unwilling to compromise, and he firmly believed that he was a level-headed person…"
"But when he was with her, he'd get all flustered at the smallest things, or get nervous, or sometimes even excited. All of his little reactions just felt so interesting to look at…"
"Those little details of him seemed so lovely. …That's how I felt."
"I… I wouldn't have minded if he fell in love with someone else."
"If he still held some fondness for me, nevertheless… If I could just have been with them in their own world."
"Compared to seeing him crushed with regret, broken down into so many pieces… That way would have been so, so much better."
"I would have been fine with it. After all… I knew everything that was going on, and I still fell in love with him regardless."
"I see… You really are a woman, Setsuna."
"Do you not get what I mean, Shouko-san?"
"I guess. To take a page from a certain person's book, I'm really nothing like a woman at all."
"I can't believe it… I wonder how it came to this. I wonder how I ended up just wanting to tell you everything, Shouko-san."
"I never told this to anyone other than a few people… I never told this to anyone who wasn't a really, really close friend."
"Umm… I'm not too sure. There were at least 30 people in here, after all."
"Please take a closer look. It's the girl in the middle of this picture."
"Ah… I think she was here? Yes, that looks like her. She's really cute, right? There was quite a crowd around her, if I remember correctly."
…Which means Setsuna definitely made her way out of that party earlier.
"…!? Could you let me see that for a second?"
Which also means… with only the clues we have, the situation's only appearing to get worse.
"You have the party organizer's phone number, right? I'd like to contact him, so could you please give it to me?"
"Eh? Wait, but… do you know him?"
"If you're friends, then shouldn't you know his…"
"I lost my cell phone last week. I'm using a new one right now, so my list of contacts is pretty much empty."
"There's a chance that some illegal drugs were brought to the party today. The police might come to perform a search later."
"Before it gets to that point, I need to get in touch with the organizer. …Or maybe I should call the police over first?"
"Ah, all right. Let me go get the list of reservations."
My overly bold improvisation somehow managed to win the trust of the kind manager.
Yes, this is in no way extortion, just a fair exchange of information between two trusted parties. …Probably.
"…I knew it! Senpai, how do you explain this!?"
"…The girl in the middle is Ogiso Setsuna. She's Takahiro-kun's older sister."
"Isn't the girl on the right Touma Kazusa!?"
"…That has nothing to do with the situation right now. Don't get distracted by unnecessary information. If you get distracted and lose track of Setsuna, I'll get mad at you."
Having seen yet another part of my past involving someone else, Sugiura seems to have fallen into a bit of a daze.
"But enough about that, I need you to do something. Go buy a cell phone charger at the nearest convenience store. A U-mobile model. Disposable chargers are fine too."
But I don't need to hide it anymore.
"If your battery ran out, I could just lend you my…"
"The next couple of calls are going to be really, really important. I'll explain it to you later if you want. Just go get it!"
I've been laid back with her at work, but if we keep working at Goodies together, she'll end up seeing this side of me anyway.
…My "reign of terror," as both Satou and the manager so coin it.
"Sorry to keep you waiting. Umm, Mizuno-sama, correct?"
"…But the list here says Mizuno Haruhiko-sama."
"…He even used his brother's name. Is he in on it too?"
"Sorry for the trouble, manager. We'll try to keep the mess to a minimum on our end, so I'd appreciate it if you could keep quiet about this as well."
"If the police arrive, tell them exactly what happened. Everything will be fine if you can just buy us a little bit of time!"
In my heart, I'm truly prostrating myself before him in gratitude.
For prioritizing what I requested and not giving me any more trouble.
"Well, Haruki? How are things on your end?"
"I got in touch with eleven of them. Two groups of four people at the bars were clean. Two others are already home."
One of whom started yelling at me for no real reason, but after I got her name, the whole ordeal felt like a trip down memory lane…
"And… the last five were in a hotel."
"Two of them were there on their own volition, so I let them go. But the other three…"
"…Setsuna wasn't among them, of course. It's just that one of the girls got too drunk and looked pretty messed up in more ways than one."
"Oh, okay… Still, two guys? That's messed up! …It'd be pretty impressive if it were the other way around, though."
Sugiura Koharu let her sense of justice take hold of her and offered to take the girl to the station.
Of course, she also didn't forget to give the two students from the Medical Department a scathing scolding… It seems she really has no fear.
…Well, it might have been a result of my fierce exchange with the organizer over the phone setting off some kind of switch in her.
"So, how are things on your end, Takeya?"
"I got in touch with twenty-one of them. Eight are at a karaoke place, ten of them are at some after-party, and three went home right after."
According to the list I gotーcoercivelyーfrom the organizer, there were 33 people including Setsuna.
The guys were all from the Medical Department. The girls, according to Takeya, were all strictly picked from the other departments. The best of the best.
"Setsuna-chan wasn't at any of those places though. Assuming what they said can be trusted, that is."
"Probably. I have some past connections with a few of the girls, after all. …Hearing Chika was there was quite a shock, though."

And, also according to Takeya, even amongst that group, there was still nobody who could compare to Setsuna. There was even some sort of competition between the guys to try and get a better chance with her.
Really, this girl they call Ogiso Setsuna…
Just exactly how foolish can she be despite being blessed with such strong feminine charm…?
"Another thing, Haruki. Something one of the guys at the after-party said caught my attention."
"He said he saw a girl who seemed to be one of Setsuna-chan's friends call out to her, and the two of them went off somewhere on their own."
"…A girl that seemed to be a friend of hers?"
"I thought for sure it'd be someone else from the party, but now that we already confirmed everyone's whereabouts…"
"So she met a friend of hers by chance, and just went drinking with her…?"
"Probably. Or rather, almost certainly the case."
She didn't tell anyone from her family where she was going, broke her curfew, and even turned off her cell phone…
Slipped away from that crazy high-class party, ran into a friend, and is now drinking with her all the way past midnight…
"What is she trying to do… Getting everyone all worked up like this…"
"At least it's some good news! My little rumor ended up being just a rumor… Sorry about that, actually. I didn't really think it through when I told you."
"There's no way it's your fault, Takeya… I'm the one at fault here, really."
"Sorry, Takeya… For laughing off what you told me back then and making you work so hard after what happened."
"Your instructions were as clear as always, so I didn't really mind. Also… you should thank Io later, too. I got a good chunk of the guys' contact info from her."
"Shouldn't it be the other way around, man…?"
"This is a pretty delicate topic for me, so just drop it, okay? She was invited to begin with, you know…?"
Another little incident went down between these two, I see…
"Anyway… sorry about keeping you up this late. I'll just go around randomly looking for a bit more and head home afterward…"
"This is a good chance… If you find Setsuna, have a proper talk with her."
"You're being a bit more true to yourself now, aren't you? You're getting angry over what Setsuna-chan did, just like the old days, aren't you? …This is your chance."
"Whatever you're mad about, just let it out. How worried you got over all this, how many painful thoughts were on your mind… Let her know all of it."
"How could I… The one who's really in pain is…"
"It'll cheer Setsuna-chan up for sure! Don't you want to see her smile? Then just do what I said."
"Anyway, that's all the advice I have for you. See ya! Sweet dreams."
Takeya didn't wait for my response and abruptly hung up.
Actually, it's probably because he didn't want to hear me still wallowing in my indecisiveness any more…
The streets of Onjuku are as wide as they've ever been.
Now that I'm out of clues, trying to find Setsuna on these still bustling streets seems all but impossible.
Precisely because she knows how unlikely it is, she left me a tiny sliver of a chance to hang on to.
Not just for today, but tomorrow, the day after, before the year ends, or even next year…
She left me a chance for us to move forward again. A chance for Setsuna and me to talk again.
Is it because I always have my head down in deep thought like this?
No wonder I never notice this pupil of mine even when she's standing right in front of me.
"I somehow managed to get her on the train. …I can't say for sure whether or not she'll be able to get off on her own, though."
Just as expected, whenever the two of us come together, we end up sticking our noses into anybody and everybody's business.
The medical department guys will probably be staring daggers at me starting tomorrow…
"What should we do now? Want to go take a look at places you think she might have gone?"
"No… We don't need to do that anymore."
"Why not? We still don't know where she is, right? Aren't you worried?"
"I'm not worried anymore after the call I just got."
I summarize the important bits of Takeya's phone call just now for her.
The worst case scenario has more or less become an impossibility.
The girl she's with right now seems to be a close friend of hers.
It seems like it's about time to think of how to scold this girl who, without telling her parents, just wandered off drinking somewhere for no good reason.
"Really…? Thank goodness! Ah, what am I saying? We haven't even actually found her yet, so 'Thank goodness' isn't really appropriate."
"…No, it should be fine now. Sorry for dragging you along with me on this rather fruitless adventure."
"Just getting rid of that one in a million chance is fruitful enough for me, Senpai!"
Amidst our mindless chatter, I finally get to see an expression of hers that, although I'd never seen before, is exactly as I imagined it to be.
"If you wore this expression all the time, you'd look pretty cute."
…To think she almost made me blurt out something so corny. She certainly does have the charm to make a guy fall for her.
So this is what she's like on the inside… It's like I'm surrounded by nothing but amazing people.
"That reminds me… You looked a little scary back there, Senpai."
"Sorry. I got pretty frantic back there, so… I probably said some mean things to you as well, Sugiura."
"No, no, what was scary was actually the opposite…"
"You were pretty frantic back there for sure, but you also got more and more calm as time went on, like you were focusing every last bit of your energy on the task."
"After we got off the train, it was like a switch flipped in your head. You immediately started looking like someone really reliable…"
"You're just imagining things. I'm always like that, aren't I?"
"You're probably right. Maybe I only felt like that because… these busy streets at night are a little scary, after all."
That's probably because these past three years in university raised my skill in this field a little more.
Because I don't ever want to repeat the mistake of letting my indecisiveness lead me to make the worst possible choice.
But up until now, all I've done is run away from making decisions, so I never got a chance to really experience a situation like this.
"So… what should we do now? Just go home, or maybe give the Ogiso family a call? Or should we go check places that she might…"
And with the clock past midnight and Sugiura still looking as energetic as ever and seemingly in a good mood for whatever reason, I…
"Let me take you to the station. We're close to missing the last train of the day."
"…You're right. I'll take you up on that offer."
It's almost 00:30. I certainly wasn't joking when I said, "We're close to missing the last train."
Not to mention that, apart from places like Onjuku, you'd hardly see another soul on the streets this late at night.
However, that little, "You're right" she said just now clearly wasn't referring to the train schedule.
And also, she'll "Take me up on my offer"…?
Compared to her "No, thanks" or simply ignoring me outright, it's an unbelievable improvement considering only a few hours have passed…
"But I won't let you try to, 'Take me all the way home' like before, okay? You wouldn't be able to get home yourself if you did that."
"Don't worry, I'll take a taxi home from the station. It's only a short distance, but it's already this late, so I doubt the driver will turn me down."
"Let's go, Senpai. I think the last train on Saturdays leaves at ten to 1. We'll probably make it just fine, but we should hurry just to be on the safe side."
Well past midnight on these restless streets, Sugiura makes her way to the station with a light spring in her step.
She started working early in the morning, ran all the way from the restaurant to the station, and did a sizable amount of walking here in Onjuku as well. What a craz… What an energetic girl.
"What are you dragging your feet for? You were the one who tried to hurry me back home, weren't you? Could you at least keep up with my pace, please?"
She really is energetic… and a very fussy junior of mine.
The rather arbitrary decision I made after almost giving up ironically led me to the answer.
She's standing there before the entrance, staring up at the ceiling absent-mindedly.
"You should really head home. I'm really sorry about what happened today."
No matter how you look at it, a high school student really shouldn't be out and about at this hour.
"I'll… go searching for a little bit longer, then head home myself."
I'd also like to add… daughters from families as strict as the Ogiso family really shouldn't be running around at this hour either.
"Sorry I won't be able to take you home. Oh yeah, why don't you take a taxi home after you get off the train? Here's some money for the fare…"
"I don't need it. …Ah, but I'll still be taking a taxi. I won't try to be stubborn and walk home by myself."
"…I'm more worried about you, Senpai. Today's Saturday, so the last train of the night will leave soon, you know? How are you going to get home?"
"I'll be fine. If I really need to, I can just take a taxi from here. And as a last resort, I can just spend the night at an internet cafe."
"Didn't you already say there was nothing to be worried about?"
"There's nothing to be worried about, but I still feel like I should find her just to give her a piece of my mind."

"It's not just me, she made Takahiro-kun and her parents worry about her so much. She also caused plenty of trouble for my friends, and you too, Sugiura. …I'll have a word with her in your place, so could you forgive her?"
"Is that it? Is that really your reason for not caring to catch the last train home?"
"It's not a big deal… Tomorrow's Sunday, anyway."
"…You want to see her, don't you? Right this instant."
"Don't you want to see her smile?"
"…You're back to your usual self, I see."
Why does everyone… Why do they all act like they've got me figured out…?
Just as I was in a panic over my desperate attempt to step on the brakes seemingly having no effect, with a thousand voices shouting "I can't do this anymore" inside my head…
"We just barely managed to make up with each other, so it'd be a waste to ruin it over something so silly."
She takes the initiative and distances herself.
It seems as though she's finally picked up on the fact that I can't really help myself anymore.
"If only you could think that way all the time."
"That'll depend on what your attitude toward things is like in the future."
And yet, unable to make the same mental progress as her, I can only repeat my tired acts of sarcasm to Sugiura like I did before.
As Sugiura's figure slowly drifts further and further away, I start to ponder the numerous changes our relationship went through in the last few hours.
We were arguing like always, then in an instant, it felt like I was the one taking charge… But in the next moment, it felt like both our biological and mental ages were reversed…
Was it because she found a "foothold" for herself in my world after knowing about Setsuna and a little bit about Kazusa as well?
No, it's probably not just that. She's likely already surpassed me when it comes to building and maintaining relationships with others.
After all… I haven't made any progress in that field these last three years.
But now's not the time to let what seems to be regret take hold of me.
I have to find the girl who went out drinking without bothering to tell her parents, even if only with someone she knows and by a coincidental meeting.
Should I yell at her? Should I apologize? Or should I…
I don't have the slightest idea on how I should approach her.
But something in me is telling me I need to find her. …Of course, this is only out of wishful thinking, without any real rhyme or reason.
"…What's wrong, Sugiura? Did you miss the last train?"
"Ah, Senpai… No, there's still ten minutes until the last train leaves, but…"
"Are you short on money or something? Where are you right now? The east gate?"
"Yes! The east gate! Please come as soon as possible!"
"You don't need to panic that much. It's only a five minute walk to…"
"I found Ogiso's older sister! She's over here, outside the entrance!"
"The last train of the day to Washiou will be leaving shortly. Please take care not to miss the train."
"Well, there goes the last train, huh?"
I found Setsuna by the ticket dispensers with more than five minutes left before the last train would leave.
At that point, we could've taken our time walking toward the platform after passing the ticket gate and still have plenty of time to spare.
Setsuna didn't seem to want to move from that spot, however, and I couldn't bring myself to rush her given her reaction.
"What should we do now? Want to go stay somewhere? Just the two of us."
"After we've rested a bit, we're going home. By taxi. Your family's waiting for you, aren't they?"
Even so, when I asked her if she wanted to go find somewhere to sit together, she followed me without a moment of hesitation.
Which means the reason behind her not wanting to move back then was most likely not the result of having drunk too much.
"Takahiro-kun gave me a call earlier. I hear that you didn't let anyone at home know you'd be coming home late tonight?"
"We happened to bump into each other on these busy streets" seems to be too fateful of an explanation for her to accept.
That's why, even after I'd explained myself, her gaze apathetically fell to the ground with an expression on her face that suggested she'd expected something like this.
"Aa-ah, how annoying can they be? I wish both mom and dad would just give me a break already!"
Don't say things you don't mean!
"They said they couldn't reach your cell phone. That's why everyone was worried…"
"Ah, my battery was dead the whole time. I guess I'm pretty careless, aren't I?"
Even so, there should have been plenty of ways to get in touch with them. Like borrowing your friend's phone, or buying a charger…
There's no way you wouldn't be able to figure that out, right, Setsuna?
"Then… I guess you didn't have a choice. Looks like you just weren't very lucky today."

"Everybody there was super rich, one guy was like some heir to a hospital or something, and another guy had all these foreign cars… It's like they're all children of prestigious families from Okayama or something!"
"That sounds about right. They're all from our university… not to mention from the Medical Department, after all."
"Everyone was so nice, too. We had a blast talking about going skiing once the season starts!"
Aren't those just regular old pick-up lines? Did you really show those guys that smile of yours?
"Really…? That sounds nice. You like the snow so much, after all."
"I heard you met up with a friend after the party?"
"…I know a guy from the Medical Department. He was at the party too."
"Who was it? Aoyama-san? Itou-san? Kishiyama-san? Hibino-san?"
"…Well, whatever. I got to know her… Nagase-san, I mean, at the party. It was actually the first time we met."
"The first time the two of you met…?"
"She's really outspoken and a little unpredictable, but still really reliable."
"…From that description alone, it doesn't sound like she's very feminine at all."
"But she was quite the beauty, you know? And a really good person at heart, too. We had so much fun talking we lost track of time."
"Really, today was just the best…! I had so much fun and so many nice things happened. If only every day could be like this."
What do you mean, today was the best…? It's pretty much been the worst for me.
Do you have any idea how much trouble I went through because of your whimsical little stunt? You're getting way out of line!
"Have you sobered up a little? We should think about heading home now."
"By the way… I told your family that you spent the whole day with me today."
"Make sure to memorize what I'm about to tell you. Starting from noon, we took a trip by train all the way to Hakone to visit an open-air art gallery."

"We stayed at the gallery until closing time and then had dinner at a nearby restaurant. It wasn't until we got to the station planning to go home that we realized that the train schedule today was the weekend one."

"There were still trains running, but only a few, and finding transfers was also really tough. We realized then that we wouldn't be able to make it back by 10 o'clock like we had planned. And then, at our last transfer, we ended up just barely missing the last train… Or something like that."
"You even thought up an excuse for me… You haven't changed a bit, Haruki-kun."
"Did you memorize it? I'll give you a pop quiz, just to make sure. Where did we go today?"
"Okay, I'll start again from the beginning, then. We went to Hakone's…"
"I can't lie like that. There's no way I can lie as calmly as you can about that, Haruki-kun."
"Well… look, I'm sorry for lying to them. But this is only to make them not have to worry…"
"No… I can't tell such a happy and wonderful-sounding lie…"
"My face will give it away for sure. Telling a lie like that would only make me miserable and frustrated… I wouldn't be able to stop my tears."
"What are you talking about…? Didn't you have fun today?"
It must have been way more fun than the fake date I randomly came up with on the spot just now, right?
So what do you mean you can't even tell a lie as simple as this?
"Come on, let's go home, Setsuna. You must be freezing, right?"
"…Why don't you head on home first?"
"There's no way I can do that. How could I leave you by yourself after finally finding you?"
"It's fine. Just leave me here… that's what you've always been doing, isn't it?"
Get angry. Blow a fuse. …And start setting her straight.
Tell Setsuna that what she's doing is wrong. Tell her just how inconsiderate she's being.
Tell her how terrible her behavior is right now.
Tell her to stop being so petulant. And that she's way out of line.
Just this once, I need to be the pot calling the kettle black. Just this once, it's the proper way to handle this.
Just this one time… I need to be frank with her. I need to be angry with her. I need to show her how much she's worried me, how much she's made me go through.
Setsuna's trying to provoke me too, isn't she? In her own roundabout way, she's practically begging me to get angry with her.
I'll say it. I'm saying it… Because I am, Setsuna's…

"Setsuna… You're way out of…"

"You're not going to get mad at me after all…"
"Even though I'm being so petulant, even though I'm causing so much trouble for you…"
It was just a fraction of a second…
"You still won't tell me off or set me straight… You still won't treat me like you did back then…!"
We missed each other by merely a hair's breadth.
"I would have been so happy if you'd just yelled at me! I might have been even happier if you had just completely lost it and hit me…"
If I'd snapped just a tiny bit earlier… or if Setsuna could have held on a tiny bit longer…
But it's all too late now. That one fatal second made all the difference.
"Why couldn't I just get that across…? Why do we just keep going around in circles…?"
No matter how much Setsuna laments the whole situation…
Two people who have already missed each other once can never come together again.
Because now, my spirit's been shattered. And Setsuna herself has broken down as well.
"It was like this on Wednesday, too…"
That's the day my cell phone had a record of an incoming call from Setsuna.
That must be part of the reason for our collapse today, and not a trivial one either.
"Last week, we had a chance to share our thoughts over the phone… so I thought this week too, on the same day, at the same time, maybe… just maybe…"
During the whole time I was restlessly wondering if Setsuna would call again, Setsuna was suffering from a much deeper anguish.
"That's why I tried to build up my courage… Finding the resolve to do that took me an entire day."
…That much is a given. After all, I only thought about being on the receiving end. But Setsuna knew how I would respond.
"I really, really wanted to hear your voice, but… I was worried whether or not it was too late at night for me to call, and… choosing between calling or texting took me another three hours."
That's why she could only take the initiative… Left with no other choice, she could only build up the courage to make the first move.
"An hour before I tried, I realized that I didn't really know what to talk to you about, so I scribbled a bunch of keywords in my notebook, and buried my face in my hands…"
She couldn't just stay exasperated in the face of all the troubles plaguing her mind. She couldn't just brush it all off saying, "This is just stupid."
"And when I'd finally decided to give up and go take a bath, I caught a glimpse of just how much I'd been crying in the bathroom mirror…"
Even though this really is just the stupidest thing imaginable.
"So I couldn't help it. After hearing your voice once, I couldn't help but want to hear it again!"
"So I couldn't help it. After getting your text last time, I couldn't help but want to hear your voice!"
Even though there's nothing other than sheer foolishness that could cause her to remain obsessed over the cruel and utterly horrible person that I am.
"No… In the end, what I really wanted was to see you."
It's that ridiculous line of reasoning…
"Little by little, I grew incapable of resisting the desires inside me…"
That caused Setsuna's own tender but foolish feelings to stab at her heart.
And then there's me, only acting as I usually do.
I'm the very definition of a bystander who's neither able to bring himself to take a step forward to hold her in his arms, nor bring himself to turn back and just run away.
"Have you… found someone you like? Have you… moved on, somewhat?"
Setsuna gathered what little courage she had and pressed the call button in the middle of the night on Wednesday.
But the voice that she heard on the other end wasn't mine.
"If you did, could you introduce me this time? Don't worry, I won't say anything weird… I won't do anything that could cause you trouble."
She's not like that. We're not like that at all.
She's just a friend who goes to the same seminars as I do. We were too focused on finishing her paper that night, so we missed the last train like we did just now.
I let her use my bed, and I slept in the bathroom. I know how unbelievable it sounds, but nothing happened between us.
But… there's no point in making an excuse like that.
Not only would it prove meaningless, it would only continue to serve as a vicious curse that would half-heartedly shackle Setsuna to a state of uncertainty.
What does it matter if it was all just a misunderstanding? If this is what it takes to set Setsuna free, then I'll…
"No! Forget what I just said! Forget I said any of that!"
…But the moment I show even the slightest sign of backing out, Setsuna once again falls into denial and cuts me off.
"You didn't hear anything, right? I didn't say anything, right!?"
This is how we've spent the last three years with each other.
"Forget all of it… Everything I said here today was a lie. Please, I'm begging you, pretend you didn't hear any of that!"
I can't work up the courage to break up with her, nor can I work up the courage to say I still love her.
And because I keep leading her on like that, Setsuna can't take a step in a new direction either.
"I'm sorry I caused you so much trouble. …I'm going home."
Why has it turned out this way…?
We were supposed to have tried to get closer to each other.
And we should have gotten closer…
But then, why… has it turned out this way…?
"N-No, it wasn't that painful… maybe, sort of…"
"Hold on a little more, okay? I've finished disinfecting it, so all that's left is to put on the band-aid…"
"Shut it! If it hurts, it hurts, okay!?"
"It's just a little cut on your fingers, right? Stop making such a big deal out of it…"
"I've been getting cuts on them every week… It's already the eighth time now."
"Then shouldn't you be used to it by now? The only reason you're doing that is to get spoiled by Ogiso…"
"Okay, all done! Now then… Pain, pain, go away!"
"H-Huh? Did I say something weird just now?"
"N-No… If anything, that certainly seemed like something you'd say, Setsuna."
"My mom always does this for me, so I guess I picked the habit up from her…"
"So this is our school's idol, huh…"
"Jeez～! I don't think of myself as one."
"It doesn't matter if you do or you don't. Things are totally going to get even more hectic after tomorrow, for sure."
"Ugh… It still hurts a little. Did I cut all the way to my nerves or something? My fingertips are…"
"That's only because you're handling the strings improperly. I've never cut myself playing the guitar, not even once."
"Talk is cheap, Touma. Let's see your own fingers."
"Well, if my fingers were as well fortified as yours, I wouldn't have cut myself either."
"But they're so slender! And so white and pretty! How do you play all those incredible songs with fingers like these?"
"And your fingertips are so cold… Just like your personality, huh."
"Stop playing with my fingers, you two. …Break's over. Let's start again."
"You're right. We'll be doing the real thing in… how long, again?"
"We still have some time before the live performance, but it's getting to the point where we need to start finalizing everything."
"It's already this late, huh? I'm getting kind of hungry…"
"If you can finish playing through it once completely smoothly, you can go eat to your heart's content."
"If you really did that, you'd probably end up sleeping through the school festival."
"In that case, no eating until the school festival's done."
"Stop jumping from one extreme to another, would you?"
As my head gradually recovers from its hazy state, the inevitable reality of my current situation begins to settle into my mind.
I see, I fell asleep… I finally fell asleep.
And at the worst time possible… I've slept so much that I'm now left with only a few hours until the deadline.
Quite some time has passed since then.
After taking Setsuna back home by taxi, we ended up being scolded by her father until morning.
Her mother, who never actually slept, had already prepared a nice hot breakfast for us by the time it was all over.
Just like how it was three years ago. Strict, but warm…
By the time I returned to my apartment, it was already Sunday afternoon.
I turned on my PC right away and just stared at the display for a few hours without moving a muscle.
Time idly passed by with no progress on my part.

I've tried several things in an attempt to change my mood, including lying on my bed, drinking a whole can of beer in one go in a sorry attempt to emulate shock therapy, and staying outside in the freezing cold for several hours in order to cool my head.
And then Sunday turned to Monday, and night turned to dawn…
There was no fever, no discomfort, and I couldn't even fall asleep despite the fact that I was sleepy.
That's why even though it was almost time for class, I ended up skipping it the way an average university student would.
After that, I remember groaning to myself in front of the PC until about 11 o'clock.
And right now, looking at the clock, I'd say most people would unanimously agree that it's currently Monday evening.
Today's the deadline for the manuscript that Mari-san rejected a few days ago.
A special report on "Touma Kazusa," the promising young pianist who became famous almost overnight.
After waking myself up with a shower, I find myself facing the display of my PC yet again.
The product of exaggerated, flowery praise that had been rejected last week remains there in all its disappointing glory, a mockery of my choice of words.
No, it's not my literary ability that's ridiculing me hereーit's actually my cowardly self, who's somehow forever incapable of coming to grips with the truth about a certain person.
I need to write about Kazusa.
I need to write about herーabout the thoughts on her mind all those years back, how she lived, and what kind of person she actually was.
I have to remember the times we shared, much like what I dreamed of a while ago.
I have to remember the times when we still called each other Setsuna and Ogiso, Touma and Touma-san, Haruki-kun and Kitahara.

I have to remember what she said, both on the night we looked up at the stars and the time when she was in a daze from her fever. I have to remember the unreasonably pent-up resentment and pain she'd spilled out to me.
I have to remember the week we spent together before the day of the school festival.
I remember those days, days where I had the most fun, days that were the happiest in my life…
I want to go back to that day, three years ago.
"Yep. It's addressed to the editing department… The sender is listed as Houjou High School."
"It's the place where Kitahara-kun went to do the interview, right? So I thought I should let you take a look at it, Mari-san."
"Speaking of Kitahara-kun, today's the deadline, isn't it? Having gotten his first article rejected like that, he's probably pretty hurt."
"If that was enough to get him down, he wouldn't be able to handle working here."
"He said he'd be applying to our department formally next year, so I'm using this as an opportunity to prepare him."
"You can't say that he'll be guaranteed employment just off the fact that he has the intention to apply, though…"
"Of course he'll be employed. What kind of HR department would keep someone like Matsuoka and say no to Kitahara?"
"…Let's not mention this conversation to Matsuoka."
"You're already the fifth bunch to come to me after that Kaiou Graph article. Suwa even told me to dub some voices over it."
"Seeing how she took first place in Europe, I'm not surprised."
"You mean "European competition." And she only took second place."
"Sugiura just refuses to believe that Touma Kazusa and my sister were best friends. So I figured I'd show her some proof."
"…Well, that's one way of putting it."
"Your sister was a legend herself, too."
"…I don't really get you guys. My sister seems pretty normal to me."
"Then let me be her brother! Besides, she's the only person from our school who's ever won the Miss Houjou High title three years in a row."
"I don't think any other school would have a Miss Houjou High…"
"Now that I think about it, she didn't enter the actual Miss Houjou contest, did she? If she took that title too, she'd have no problem getting into television or acting and all that."
"Well, she has a boyfriend right now, and they're pretty crazy for each other. They even went out until 3 AM just the other day, and as expected, that really pissed my dad off."
"If you think about it, these are 'the' Touma Kazusa and 'the' Ogiso Setsuna performing together as a group. This recording might be worth a ton in the future."
"Stop bragging and show us already. …The Light Music Club from three years ago."
"Okay, okay. Let's see… I think the Light Music Club was the eighth segment, if I recall correctly."
"Well, I never knew my father's name or what he looked like. I haven't lived with my mother in years. The credit card she left me doesn't even have a limit."
"My family circumstances aren't that complex. They're really perfectly normal. In some people's eyes, they're no big deal at all."
"But that's exactly why… it's fine for me to be frustrated, right? It's fine for me to be angry at her for no reason, right?"
"Why didn't he tell… no… who wouldn't keep this a secret, actually?"
"I can't believe this guy. Well, this is pretty neat, at any rate. …Looking pretty cool on stage there, isn't he?"
"I… I thought about giving up on the piano."
"I thought about abandoning my place as her daughter."
"Oh, this takes me back… I watched this performance live, you know?"
"What a crowd… I don't think there was ever a performance during our three years here that got people as excited as this."
"The guy I know is always gloomy… He never laughs, tries acting cool, or gets self-absorbed like this at all…"
"But what they actually did wasn't all that amazing. The only instruments were a guitar and a keyboard, the rest of it was just synthesized. And the singer, I mean, it's just my sister."
"Isn't that the reason the crowd got so pumped up in the first place?"
"He's always removed, looking at others from a distance as if he were a complete stranger, absolutely terrified of getting close… A cold-blooded animal…"
"What did I tell you, Sugiura? My sister totally went on the same stage as Touma Kazusa. And the guy playing the guitar to their left is…"
"Is the person I saw in the music room back then…"
"In any case, for now… I want to remember."
"No… in the past, when I was sure I really loved the piano despite who I was."
"…How I felt like in the past when I stood in front of the piano."
"Oh? Ah! Finally back from your vacation, princess?"
"Eh? Weren't you on the radio just now?"
"It's just a recording. They took it last week… I was called to go on the show only because you ran off somewhere at the last minute, princess."
"Hmm… You've had it rough too, haven't you, chairman? From screenplay to production to promotion… Make sure to do your best on the ticket sales too, okay?"
"There's also a certain unbelievably selfish main actress here that won't listen to anything the chairman says, making my work even tougher."
"I feel bad for adding yet another entry to my list of selfish actions, but I probably won't be coming here again before the year's over."
"…How long do you plan on leaving us like this? Without you around, we can't really do anything."
"Just a little more, just a little bit more…"
"I can trust you this time, right?"
"I've found the perfect partner to practice with. I can't just ditch them…"
"And my mother… when I think about it, I don't really hate her that much."
"That's why I believe that taking my own path is the right thing to do."
"I'll repair the relationship with my mother. This time, I'll be a good girl, just like Setsuna."
I finally finished the manuscript that had me groaning in front of my desk because of how I've been incapable of progressing with it for almost the whole day, and it took me only an hour.
But, in that same hour, I've also spent an entire day's worth of mental energy.
Exhaustion and listlessness assault my body. If I were to relax just a little bit, I'd probably lose consciousness in an instant.
It's not just the fatigue that I can feel across my entire body, though.
I can feel a multitude of feelings piling onto my heart, as wellーI can feel something drilling into it, a stream of warmth coursing through it, and the excitement welling up inside…
This complicated barrage of emotions sends my mind spiraling in confusion, making me unsure of what I'm really feeling right now.
I sold her out. I revealed to the world the secrets that should only have belonged to the three of us.
And yet I fell into a state of ecstasy remembering everything about her despite having committed such a cruel act of betrayal.

I remembered everythingーhow she never opened her heart to anyone, her status as a prodigy of the music program, how she struggled with the regular curriculum, how she was usually irritable but mellowed out eventually, and how she was frank, yet not so honest after all…
Having remembered those days from three years ago, I grinned, laughed, and my tears flowed out as I sobbed, as well.
Even so, I have no intention of worrying about either my guilt or my satisfaction.
I need… to send her my second draft.
We're talking about Mari-san here. There's an obvious difference between an email sent at midnight and an email sent at six in the morning.
That's why I need to send it now.
If I pass out here, I won't be able to wake up by tomorrow morning for sure.
I feel so incredibly relaxed, after all.
Or our three years of frustrations together.
In this very moment, I've sublimated them all into beautiful memories.
Who did I say this sentence to just now? Was it to someone a 30 minute walk away, or to someone more than ten hours of a plane ride away? Was it to only one of them, or to them both…?
I neither have the means nor the need to know the answer anymore with the way I am now.
In the end, the second draft of the manuscript that I sent with every last ounce of strength I could muster…
"M-Mari-san… like I said, Kitahara-kun's merely a…"
"Yeah, yeah. You've gotta at least give him props for trying, right? He did make the deadline, after all…"
"None of you know what's going on, so keep your mouths shut."
…Ended up inviting nearly the same reaction to the one I'd received when I submitted my first draft.
…Well, in a way, I suppose it's to be expected.
"She enrolled in Houjou High only because her mother, Touma Youko, abandoned her? Her personal wishes were never taken into account?"
"At the very least, that's what she thought at the time… She did admit that it was just a misconception on her part later on, though."
"Because she was so far above her peers in terms of ability and her refusing to communicate with others, she spent a whole year without speaking to a single classmate?"
"From what I know, she did actually talk a little bit around the time she enrolled… but it was primarily in the form of arguments."

"She was constantly late or absent from class, abandoned by her teachers, caused a countless number of incidents due to her bad behavior, and was removed from the music program at the end of her second year?"
"She did manage to graduate one way or another, though."
"Wow… what's up with all this gossip? Just barely starting to get her name out there in the world and then suddenly all this?"
"'She certainly lives up to her title as Touma Youko's daughter…' is what people are probably going to be saying."
"Isn't this kinda bad…? The guys at Ensemble only gave us this job in the first place because the chief was on good terms with Touma Youko, right?"
But this time, it's not because of an issue with my enthusiasm, but rather the actual content of my submission.
Her evaluation does seem a bit more promising, so I suppose I managed to take a step forward.
…Though it's entirely possible that I'll end up taking two steps back as well.
"Where did you get all this from…? Did a faculty member at the school tell you this?"
"Well, it has been three years since I heard it, but all the events described here took place even earlier than that, so I don't think there's a problem."
Mari-san looks at me with her usual stern expression.
The other employees present also began taking a look at the manuscript Mari-san passed over, and they grasped at their heads in uncertainty as they attempted to digest the article.
…Ah, that metaphor turned out kind of weird. I guess that's because I used my head too much yesterday.
Mari-san's expression is clearly different from the one she had when she rejected my first draft, though. That much I'm sure of.
In any case, although she remains stern, there's no hint of regret or disappointment in her eyes at all.
"I can't make any final statement about that, given its current state. We should, at the very least, consult the school about this… I didn't use anything from the interview, after all."
"The school's comments and the things written here are completely unrelated, right? Then they have no grounds to complain to us about anything."
"…That's certainly one way of thinking about it."
"We can just tell them that we did the interview but didn't end up using any of it. I'll contact them personally about it."
On the contrary, her words no longer carry the tone of "How do we fix this thing?" but rather that of "How do we get this thing to pass?".
"I didn't mean it as a formality when I asked if we can really print this just now."
"What I meant was printing this and letting all of Japan know about it… Making it no longer knowledge that only belongs to you, Kitahara…"
This is a rare occurrenceーMari-san just brought back a topic that was supposed to be finished.
And she didn't do it out of anger, but rather out of an indescribable feeling of awkwardness and embarrassment.
"I treated you pretty harshly when you first worked on this. To be honest, I actually regret it quite a bit."
That said, she still hasn't really stopped speaking like a man.
"About that… I'm actually very grateful for the opportunity. It's really my fault that I wasn't able to produce something worthwhile."
"That's not it. That's not what I mean…"
Despite her forceful tone, however, she isn't speaking straightforwardly at all.
"I knew you'd be able to handle it from the very beginning, and you matched those expectations in the end. You accomplished the task flawlessly."
"I asked you earlier, didn't I? 'Are you really okay with this?'…"
Before I could finish and with her gaze still downcast, Mari-san hands me a flat, plastic case.
"Houjou High sent this to us yesterday. The letter that accompanied it mentioned that the eighth segment had one of Touma Kazusa's performances…"
Sealed within the case is a single disc.
On the cover, "School Festival 200x, Day 2 Stage Performances" is written in bold with a permanent marker.
"…And I watched it like the letter told me to. I'm really sorry about all this."
Rather, creating this awkward mood in the first place is what she should really be apologizing for…
"I told you before, right, Kitahara? As one of her schoolmates, I had high expectations of your connections. I wanted you to dig up things about Touma Kazusa that nobody knew about."
"I had no idea how much pain this would put you through… Even though I wasn't informed, it was still inconsiderate. I'm sorry."
"It's not your fault at all, Mari-san."
The words I wanted to say were sealed away by her logic before I even had a chance.
"I never thought someone as stiff and as stubborn as you and someone as talented and as attractive as her would…"
"Ah, my bad. I'm being inconsiderate again. It's not like I thought you wouldn't be popular with girls, or that you and someone as pretty as her wouldn't make a good match, or anything like that…"
"…Let me apologize again. It feels like I just keep digging my own grave."
People have been saying the same things to me since fall three years ago. I could even call it part of my identity now.
"To be honest, I'm rather shaken up by all this. Making such a critical mistake, delving so deep into your unexpected past…"
"I don't mind the former at all, and if possible, I'd prefer if you didn't mind the latter either…"
"How could I not…? I finally found a piece of the puzzle to the weird feeling I always get from you."
"Do I really have to say it?"
"…I won't know what you're referring to if you don't."
I should have changed the topic.
Even though she's my superior, and even though I'm just a lowly part-timer, I had no need to follow protocol there and ask for clarification like a proper employee.
"Kitahara, does the reason you're pushing yourself so hard at work have something to do with Touma Kazusa?"
How distasteful… That almost borders on sexual harassment, Mari-san.
"I might have mentioned this before, but in my opinion, I think you're treading on thin ice right now."
That's the only sarcastic reaction that could come to mind hearing what she'd said.
"If you were simply pushing yourself, I wouldn't have a problem with it. But I can't see what you're doing as being merely the result of the drive that you see young people having nowadays."
"So I act older than I look, huh?"
"Trying to exhaust yourself on a mental level… is what I think you're doing. But deep down, your values and morals as a human being overshadow it."
"So basically… I'm looking to mentally suffocate myself, but because of my naturally serious and careful personality, I'm incapable of actually pulling the trigger?"
"That makes me look a bit pathetic, doesn't it…?"
"See that? You didn't snap in anger, nor did you argue back with your logic like you always do, Kitahara… You're just standing there, silently grinning to yourself."
Only now did I notice that the corners of my lips were curled upward.
The other side of me that was laughing at myself as I wrote the manuscript yesterday is now standing before Mari-san, with an evil grin spread across my face.
Even if I've already admitted it to myself, if somebody else were to see through me and hit the mark, the only thing I could possibly do is desperately deny it like a contrarian.
With that, Mari-san seems to have finished what she had to say and is now simply staring intently at me.
She seems to be… seeking a reaction from me that's not just a hollow smile.
Even though I can't bring myself to admit everything, I can at least swear that I'll never wear that hollow smile ever again.
"Thank you for your concern, but I'm fine. I can take care of it myself."
I firmly reject Mari-san's concerns and stare at her with an equally firm gaze.
Although she's figured out one half of the whole story, there's no way she could figure out the other half.
I would have been able to get over it if it involved Kazusa alone.
You could even say that her current circumstances didn't really end up being the main issue for me here.
"Again, I don't mind what happened this time around. …Well, to be honest, what happened when I handed in my first draft did get to me a little."
But we were a group of three.
No matter how small a fraction of our lives it was, it was still a time when we laughed, struggled, and overcame our difficulties together. They're irreplaceable parts of our lives.
"However, I do think that I've already conquered this obstacle, in my opinion. …It wasn't bad, right? My article, that is."
"No matter what anyone says, the first draft belongs in the trash. But no matter what anyone says, the draft this time around gets a pass from me, as well. …It's a fine piece of writing."
That's why even if I lose hold of those wonderful times and memories, I can't rely on someone else's power to try and get them back.
"Now then, I'll be heading back to the office. Feel free to head home, Kitahara. Good work today."
"I can stay a little longer, right? Hamada-san mentioned that the proofreading will take place tomorrow."
"Do whatever you want… Well, do as you please?"
Did she accept my decision to reject her concerns, or is she shocked to the point of speechlessness?
Having finally corrected her forced tone at the last second, Mari-san finished her break and returned to her battlefield.
"I guess I should go give it my all too. …Without going overboard, that is."
Having celebrated my first job well done with a can of coffee, I immediately begin searching for new areas of conflict to serve as my battlefields.
"I've moved on already. Those things don't concern me anymore."
Even though I don't intend to admit to everything, I've decided to stop denying all of it as well.
I've simply stopped wearing that hollow smile. Without averting my gaze from Mari-san's eyes, I found the words I was looking for.
"Even though things look fine on the outside, there are still plenty of things bothering you on the inside, aren't there?"
That's why Mari-san isn't nearly as interested in what I had to say in comparison to the expression I said it with, so she continued with the topic yet again.
"Still… let me give you a piece of advice coming from my own experience. Trying to use work as an escape is useless, you know?"
Mari-san's words just now carried two important bits of information. It doesn't seem like she realizes that herself, either.
"Diving headfirst into your work or studies as recklessly as that will reflect poorly on the quality of the results."
After all, Mari-san sounded certain of what she said. The way she worded it left no room for me to form a counterargument.
"If you don't treat your work seriously, your work won't take you seriously either, you know?"
The reason she's so sure of her words is most likely because she's worked harder than anybody ever had before. The cumulation of all that experience is what she's drawing these firm conclusions from.
"And when it comes to relationships between men and women, I do think the same rules apply as well…"
She sounded a little less certain in what she said just now… It almost feels like I have some room for a rebuttal now.
"That's why if you can only put all your effort into one of them, you should give up on the other…"
Well, as I thought, she doesn't seem to have the same overwhelming amount of experience in this area as she does with working…
"But before it gets to that point, why not give both of them a proper try first? There's nothing wrong with giving it a shot, right? You haven't done it yet, have you?"
Only now do I notice the flush of red across Mari-san's face.
"Anyway, what I'm trying to say is…"
It seems like she's well aware that the words she's using right now are words that she isn't used to saying.
"Don't use your job as a way to escape from your love troubles. That's unfair to the job itself."
A week ago, I might have shouted "Don't touch me!" just now, just like a certain pianist would.
"…I'm getting a bit of an 'I just screwed up' sort of feeling. I'm actually really embarrassed right now."
"We'll forget all about it in a week. …As long as I don't bring it back up, of course."
There's a Japanese saying that goes, "the flow of the river carries on unceasingly, though the water is no longer what it once was."
"You know, I… I've always cared about you a lot more than you think I do."
Alas, it's already been a week since then, and I'm no longer who I was the week before, either.

"You have a bright future ahead of you. So I don't want to see you break down, nor do I want to see you keep forcing yourself. …I don't want to see you treat your job as if it were punishment or an obligation."
That's why, just like how that certain pianist changed as well, my hollow grin has since changed to a gentler smile.
"Oh yeah, take this. So you should cheer up now."
She hands me a keychain with some sort of doll attached to it. You could probably find one of these in a souvenir shop anywhere around the world.
It's not something that would make the recipient overjoyed, but at the same time, it wouldn't make them get any weird ideas either. It's just a plain, handcrafted gift.
"This isn't like that weird souvenir last time, you know? It's actually my favorite piece."
"So you're not actually trying to mess with me again like you did with that last time…?"
…Nothing that really warrants a drastic reaction.
"What even is this thing? An octopus… no, wait, a sea anemone?"
It has to be some kind of deep sea creature. This is supposed to be her favorite piece…?
"I'm not too sure myself, but the model looked well-made… You don't want it?"
"Of course not. I'll gratefully accept it… Though I don't really see myself treasuring it that much."
To think she'd give such a passionate talk to a part-timer. How should I put it? Despite her workaholic nature, she still does show a certain human side of her now and then…
"Now then, I'll be heading back to the office. Feel free to head home, Kitahara. Good work today."
"I can stay a little longer, right? Hamada-san mentioned that the proofreading will take place tomorrow."
"Do whatever you want… Well, do as you please?"
She's given me the determination to give it my all, even if it's only a part-time job. In a sense, she's a very important person in my life.
Having finally corrected her forced tone at the last second, Mari-san finished her break and returned to her battlefield.
But on her way back, she turns around again, as if remembering something.
"Heal scars left from love with love itself. Don't just rely on stuff like work!"
At the last moment, she says something she's probably regretting right about now. Passionate, full of youth, and above all, loud.
And so I find myself unable to move from where I stand for a bit.
Because if I were to head back to the office right now, Mari-san would almost certainly throw unreasonable amounts of work at me due to her embarrassment.
"Hey, Haruki, you didn't come to the seminar on Monday, did you? And there I was waiting for you the whole time."
"Izumi, you didn't come to the seminar on Tuesday, did you? And there I was waiting for you the whole time."
"Being kept waiting in vain for two days is really painful, you know? Besides, if the upperclassmen get the impression that I'm your woman, Haruki, I'm sure it'll inconvenience you."
"Yes, it was my bad for not showing up on Monday. I apologize for that."
"Well, even though we both missed each other one time, we finally managed to meet up on Wednesday, so all's well that ends well…"
"That said, I went to confirm with our upperclassmen about Monday… From what I heard, you just called to confirm that I really wasn't there on Monday and didn't actually show up yourself either."
"Everyone seems to agree on the fact that this is the first time you've shown up to the seminar this week. What do you have to say for yourself?"
"…Don't I give the impression of a young maiden by just making a call?"
"You actually planned to not come at all except for Wednesday, didn't you? That's how it is, isn't it?"
My third study session with Izumi is about to begin, and my repertoire of dinner meals is about to run out.

Given that I'd served her curry during our first session and curry again during the second, I've been worried about whether I'd be able to bring myself to make yet another dose of curry, albeit an extra spicy one, for this third instance.
…I imagine she'd just happily ask for seconds, though, even if it wouldn't exactly be the most interesting sight.
"From the looks of it, we can finish up the paper in just two more sessions, so you should be able to graduate this year… Still, Izumi, how do you even plan to get through the fourth year?"
Instead of worrying about what's going to happen to Izumi in the next few hours, I'm actually more worried about how she'll end up in a year.
"The others have already started to look for material for their graduation thesis, after all… What is it?"
However, Izumi seems to be completely ignoring my sincere worry, instead thinking about something I have no clue about as she stares at me with an absentminded expression.
"You know, Haruki… you seem to look just a little bit better than I thought you'd be."
"You're a literature student, so don't go off using such a disappointing choice of words. And this is just how I always am."
"I thought you'd be more depressed, though."
Even two days ago… no, even if she were to have brought this out last night, I probably wouldn't have been able to understand her then either.
"You're so stubborn. Even though it wouldn't hurt to show more of your own weakness."
"I can't even hear what you're saying this time. When you're speaking to someone, speak loud enough for them to hear, would you?"
"And also, when you're talking to someone, don't just ignore them and look elsewhere… What's the matter?"
I follow Izumi's gaze and look in her direction, toward the front gate of the university that I'm all too used to seeing.
A certain young girl who I've been seeing quite often lately is standing right in front of the gate, appearing to be waiting for someone.
And the cast on this stage is exactly the same as the cast involved in a certain past encounter.
Things should be unfolding slightly differently now compared to the past encounter, however.
"She's coming, you know? What should we do? Want me to chase her away again?"
"No, it's fine. She's figured us out anyway."
Sugiura Koharu approaches me as she spots me, not even giving so much as a glance to Izumi as she stands beside me.
…It's worth mentioning that she doesn't feel troubled at all by the fact that these are the front gates of the university.
"You were fine after all that, right? You rode a taxi home from the train station, right?"
After we found Setsuna, Sugiura disappeared without me noticing. That's why I couldn't even confirm if she made it onto the last train.
"There's no need to worry. I properly returned home safely and without incident."
"…Well, I suppose the taxi fare was really expensive, though."
Since she's right here in front of me completely safe and sound, though, I'm currently relieved of yet another thing I've been worrying about since that day.
"Excuse me, Senpai… I wish to have a word with you alone."
…It's fine if that's all she wants, though I can't help but feel that I'll get something new to worry about today.
"I won't take too much of your time. Five minutes should be enough."
Rather than say that she's taking an unfriendly attitude with me, though, I think it's more appropriate to chart her current behavior as an intentional attempt to avoid Izumi.
Well, it's not like I don't understand how she feels. …After all, she did end up believing the story Izumi made up last time.
"You're going to abandon me and go with the high school girl, huh…? I knew it, Haruki, you're a massive pervert and a criminal lusting after young girls after all…!"
"I won't be checking your papers ever again then. Run along now, 'underclassman'!"
"Haha, kidding, I'm just kidding, okay? I'll just kill some time at a convenience store for now, make sure you pick me up later! You two have fun～!"
"Do you see it now? That's the true face of the person you thought was my girlfriend before."
"…She does seem to be a rather interesting person. Though I wouldn't say she's the type I'd like hanging around me…"
Well, given that she's someone who's even more stubborn than I am, it's only natural that she wouldn't really get along well with someone who lies a lot and is irresponsibly happy-go-lucky.
"Well… do you want to go to a cafe? No point standing around here."
"It's fine if we talk here. It's nothing important. …I don't want to make your friend wait too long, either."

Still, well, I should say that the fact that she's capable of being considerate toward Izumi, as well as the fact that she simply recognizes her as only a friend of mine, are great steps in the right direction.
"…You seem to look a little better than I thought you'd be. I thought you'd be more depressed."
Their expressions are exactly the same. I'm sure this girl will be enrolling in the Literature Department next year, too…
"Well, everyone's fine, so… even though it caused a bit of a commotion, nothing much happened in the end."
"She's the only one that's fine. Everyone else who got involved in your crisis had a really rough time, Senpai."
"Not only did you threaten the manager at where the party was hosted, but you also made the organizer give you everyone's contact information, and you even dragged your friend into it at the end…"
"You spent a whole minute walking from the high school to here just to say that?"
When I'm with her, no matter how much our relationship improves, our blunt conversations never seem to change…
"I've come here to scold you, Senpai."
"See, exactly what I thought you'd say" …I almost said that out loud, since I saw it coming miles away.
"This isn't like the small issues from before. I'm here to make you reflect on your personality this time, Senpai."
"…I swear, you know no fear, do you, Sugiura?"
"I don't think I do, but… It's just that I can't stay quiet this time."
"Well, for the past few days, I don't recall ever seeing you staying quiet."
"Could you be quiet for a second, please? I'm still not done talking, you know?"
If she said something like that to me three years ago, our conversation probably wouldn't go anywhere no matter how long we talked afterward.
Since I've grown, I'll act like an adult and step back a little in order to balance things out.
"…I saw the video from your school festival."
Ever since Kazusa got a bit of recognition, everyone seems to be talking about that video.
"And I also heard about what happened between you guys from Ogiso, Senpai… Even though he doesn't know about anything beyond what happened during high school."
"But how did you manage to get that out…?"
I don't want to be reminded of that event… No, it's just something that I don't need to be reminded of since it's carved so deep into my mind.
"Do you think I'm being out of line here? I actually… think so myself, too."
"I could ask you the same. If you know about it, then how long do you plan on staying this way, Senpai?"
"You seemed to enjoy yourself so much during the school festival. You looked so happy…"
"Why have you two ended up like this?"
To think that the last person I wanted to know about the details of the event now knows something about it… This is probably among the top five mistakes I've ever made in my life.

"You've always told me that none of that mattered or that you weren't interested, but in reality you actually care a lot, don't you? When she was in danger, weren't you the one who tried to save her with everything you had?"
If I knew she was going to use my weakness like this, I would rather have become that girl's endless source of free school lunch.
"Since you regret your decision so much, I won't allow you to leave her! I definitely won't allow you two to break up now!"
Although I think she's overstepping her boundary into someone else's life…
I didn't expect her to overstep this far. Instead of making me lose my temper, it actually made me let out a sigh.
"Putting aside what you just said earlier, aren't you taking a stance that's completely wrong here?"
"No matter how much you try to hide behind logic, Senpai, I don't plan to back down on this!"
"If you had to pick between the two, you'd say you dislike me, right? Then why are you…"
"I'm not doing this for you, Senpai!"
"Then just who are you doing this fo… Ah."
"But she was crying, wasn't she!? Your girlfriend was crying, wasn't she!?"
Come to think of it, she has met Setsuna before.
She found her waiting for the last train in front of the ticket gate all by herself.
Setsuna had been right before her very eyes as her gaze was downcast, not appearing to have had any inclination of heading home as she was simply being left behind by the surrounding crowd.
"I can't stand watching stuff like this, you know. Since you two like each other, it bothers me that you can't be together."
"After all, if I were in that position… I couldn't stand being treated so coldly by the person I like."
In a way, she's butting in for a very selfish reason.
"Especially if I knew that that person still liked me and that it would only cause us more pain and confusion over time."
In order to defend her own perspective, she even resorts to involving someone who's involved with someone who's acquainted with her own best friend.
"That's why I hope you won't just give up like that, Senpai. If you think it's still too hard to face her by yourself, I can act as a mediator…"
"Whoa, wait a second. This has nothing to do with you, Sugiura."
"She's my friend's sister. I've also helped search for her. That, and… she's the girlfriend of my senior from work!"
What kind of twisted logic is that…?
If someone else were to tell me the same thing, I'd probably lose my temper and argue back.
"And finally, I'm also doing this for myself."
"Because if I can help lift the burden from your heart, Senpai, maybe you would stop being such a cold person and you would start being nicer to me as well."
What a roundabout way to put it…
And at the same time, what a useless and meaningless grand plan this is.
"You really are a piece of work…"
"…Tch, whatever. Just do whatever you want."
As I finally throw in the towel, Sugiura's knitted brows relax slightly as she stares at me.
"Seems like you really are getting better. Thank goodness, I was really starting to worry about you a little."
"Because today, you didn't start an argument with me like you did last time."
She opens her mouth slightly and shows a mischievous smile.
"Sugiura… Did you come here to provoke me just to confirm that?"
"Not at all. I meant everything I just said, you know?"
Even when she changes her attitude, it's very different from a certain strategist I know. She makes it feel much more natural.
If I knew this would happen, I would have seriously dragged her to a coffee house by force.

I can only imagine the misunderstandings, suppositions and delusions our strange argument has instilled in the minds of the hundreds of university and high school students who have passed through this school gate.
"I wasn't joking about what I said before though. If you're still hesitating, Senpai, I'll seriously go and meet with Ogiso-san, got it?"
"All right, all right. I'll accept your kindness and concern for the time being."
But now, I don't really care if people misunderstand.
"If you're making such a proud declaration, I expect to see some results soon, okay?"
Probably because I've been affected by Sugiura's overly frank, annoying kindness.
"Anyway, I should get going. There's still someone waiting for me."
"Okay, thanks for everything. I'll be going too then."
I didn't tell her that I'd do it, but I didn't tell her that I wouldn't either.
With that, the possibility is not zero yet, and if that's the case, I guess I don't have to raise my voice just because my heart is irritated…
As my mind drifts off to events that happened in the past, I hear a cheerful voice calling out to me from behind.
"I'll be going to work this weekend. Since you've been nagging about it so much, Senpai, I'll only be working the morning shifts on those two days."
Is she telling me not to come? Or maybe…?
"That girl from before… When did you two start getting along?"
"Well, there was an incident from before, or should I say there was a misunderstanding from the beginning?"
"Well, she heard someone claim to be my girlfriend… Then, some stuff happened after that."
"…Bringing that up again. As I thought, you're still so obsessed with the past, aren't you, Haruki? Do you act like that even when you're in bed with someone?"
"Jeez. Even though I acted like the bad guy for your sake, Haruki. This is what they call pulling the ladder up behind you, huh～?"
"I never said anything like 'No one would ever thank you for meddling in this, learn to read the atmosphere, you useless moron.' to you, did I?"
"And now you're taking it out on me for showing you kindness!?"
"I'm kidding. I'm grateful, Izumi. …But your hard work was in vain this time."
"Even though I tried my best to show my feminine side for your sake, Haruki… But not getting any reward like this makes me feel more like a woman, I guess."
"Ah, fine already, I'm absolutely sorry. I apologize, so could we please change the topic?"
Izumi is just like her usual self, making herself perfectly at home in my apartment, except her complaints sound harsher than normal today.
"But still… as I thought, you really have changed a little, Haruki."
"You don't seem to be as evasive when dealing with a woman other than me."
