If I recall correctly, I told that girl, which is why I couldn't keep it a secret from "her"…
"What do you want now…? I'm already half asleep."
"You have ten seconds. I'll pass out if you take any longer."
"Well, you know, the paper's done… So I don't really have a reason to keep coming here anymore."
Ah… Are those days from three years ago coming back to me yet again?
"…But can I still come and hang out?"
"…Just make sure to leave on time next time."
I must have cleared countless unthinkable milestones back in those days.
"Don't worry, I'll be on time. I'll be gone by the time the first train arrives."
When will I finally be able to put those broken fragments of my memories back together again, I wonder…?
Even though I made such a firm declaration, it was already noon by the time Izumi and I managed to wake up.
Mostly because her wanting to "make sure of something" ended up leading us into reminiscing about our childhoods.

By the time I could finally close my eyes after making sure Izumi was asleep as well, the winter sky had already been lit up by the morning sun. …And it was already far past the time I usually wake up.

Izumi lazed around in my room some more after that, eating the lunch I made and even stealing some of my share, too. It wasn't until the sky had been soaked in crimson that she finally left my apartment.
Thanks to Izumi, my long-awaited day off came to an end before I knew it.
Her cheerful parting words of "what a valuable waste of time that was" felt utterly superficial. I wonder if I'll ever be able to feel the same way?
"Hey, Mom? You sent me a text yesterday, right? What's up?"
"…Um, I'm at Minami-Suetsugu right now, so it'll probably be an hour before I get there."
"Okay, got it. We'll meet at the usual place in an hour, okay?"
"But seriously, what's the occasion? It's not every day that you take me out for dinner. Did something nice happen?"
"How am I doing? Well, I'm… Oh yeah, I should thank you, Mom."
"…Thanks for being a part of my little story."
"Okay, then just as you requested… Congratulations, Kitahara Haruki-kun!"
"Ah, my brother yelled at me just now. I guess it's a bad idea to light a few celebratory firecrackers when it's already past midnight."
"And when he saw the wine I prepared in my room, he even said that I was going way overboard with a face of complete shock."
"Well, enough about that. I guess we can start enjoying winter break now without having to worry, huh?"
"Do you have any plans for the break, Haruki-kun? Are you going to be working part-time like always?"
"I remember you saying before that Christmas and New Year's are always great for making money since most people aren't working."
"Is it the same this year, too? Have you thought about just relaxing through the break at all?"
"…I don't really mean anything by that. I'm just a little curious, that's all."
"Yep, no other hidden intentions at all."
"…I'm currently finishing my first glass and am about to pour my second～"
"I still have finals in the second term, but since I already have the credits I need, I'm more or less guaranteed to move on to my fourth year now."
"The paper was quite a challenge, but it helped me get some insight on how to tackle my graduation thesis, so even though it was quite the struggle, I managed to get something out of it after all."
"But more importantly, shouldn't you slow down a little, Setsuna?"
"Didn't you use to get drunk after just a single glass of wine? You do plan on waking up tomorrow, right?"
"Sorry, Professor～! I don't have an answer to that question yeeet～"
"I told you you'd get drunk! Your writing is all over the place, you know?"
"Stop drinking already, okay? I don't want to be responsible for any other weird things you might end up writing."
"What do you mean, weird? Is it really strange of me to ask about your winter holiday plans, Haruki-kun?"
"I just thought that if you don't take part in some more lively events like skiing or shrine-visiting once in a while, you'll go senile in no time, Haruki-kun～"
"Didn't you say you didn't mean anything when you asked that?"
"You used 'didn't' twice there, you know? Doesn't that sound weird, Haruki-kun? And here I thought you were a literature student～"
"Ahaha… You got angry! Haruki-kun got mad while trying to lecture me～ This is so fun～"
"I'm not mad! You should go to sleep soon, Setsuna. You won't be able to wake up otherwise, you know?"
"Yeah. I feel all woozy right now～ I even promised to go shopping with my mom in the morning, too."
"Hey, uh… Should I give you a call and wake you up in the morning?"
"…Were you really asleep up until now?"
Hearing Setsuna's voice for the first time after an entire week is so… How should I put it…?
I'm probably feeling the same things she is right now. Nostalgia, joy… and just a touch of pain.
"For our morning shift: Nakagawa-san, Shimamoto-san, Iiyama-san, and Sugiura-san will be manning the hall. Shimoda-kun, Hattori-kun and myself will be in the kitchen."
"The members in the hall can take turns taking breaks after the lunch rush… The kitchen staff will have to wait until the other helpers arrive."
"Oh, and also, Sugiura-san has completed her training period, so starting today she will be a full-fledged member of our team. …Sugiura-san."
"Could we hear a few words from you, just for the occasion?"
"Ah… Okay. I look forward to working with you all from now on, as always. …Umm, I can't really think of anything to say, so I'll leave it at that."
"Okay, that concludes our meeting then. Everyone, please return to your posts and begin the preparations for today's opening."
"Sugiura-san, could you restock the condiments and napkins for the tables?"
"May I ask if these are all the members that will be working here today?"
"I suppose. We're always short on people, really. So you'll need to put in 110% too."
"I don't think that will be much of a problem, but…"
"…I see you're as confident as always, Sugiura-san. I'm a little surprised, after the battering that Kitahara-san put you through."
"You had 'hurry up and notice it already' written all over your face, so why do you look so annoyed when I finally bring it up…?"
"There was no such thing written on my face. Also, I've had this look on my face ever since I was born."
"Even though you'd be so cute without it too. What a waste."
"I'm not interested in that kind of thing."
"We haven't really heard anything from Kitahara-san."
"Besides, we only dragged him here to supervise your training, Sugiura-san. Now that that's over with, there's no real reason for him to come over anymore, right?"
"…You seem awfully indifferent about all this, Floor Manager. Especially after all the stuff you had Senpai help you out with."
"Kitahara-san's about to go job hunting soon too. We can't just keep calling him back here all the time."
"Anyway, forget about those little details. The restaurant's about to open."
"I see, so you started working at Goodies again."
"But you haven't quit that job at the publishing company yet, right? The paper you were writing sounded really difficult too, so I'm a little worried. You're not pushing yourself too hard, right?"
"…Still, I know you'll just see through others' requests to the very end no matter what I say, won't you, Haruki-kun?"
"Actually, about a year ago, I saw you working through the windows one time when I happened to walk past the restaurant."
"It looked like you were lecturing the girls in there about this and that, just like you always do. Everyone looked so afraid of you, Haruki-kun."
"But whenever something happened, everyone knew to run to you for help. You looked really busy running between the hall and the kitchen all the time."
"I guess that's just something you were born with. Even if you are a little scary, people will always want to gather around you and ask you for help."
"I felt really happy when I saw that. After all, it reminded me how I once knew you in the past… a side of you that you're not showing me anymore, Haruki-kun."
"Umm, let's get back to where we started, shall we? Hey, will you be working during the winter break as well?"
"Um, if it's alright with you, and if it won't be a bother to you, then I…"
"No, it's nothing important. Talk to you later."
…You can edit a text before you send it, so why didn't she just delete those "unimportant" things?
She probably kept them there on purpose, thinking I'd be super curious about it or something.
There was the slightest bit of poison in Setsuna's text.
Is she being less reserved, if only just a little? Is she starting to show her true self?
If that's the case, perhaps it's a sign of good things to come, isn't it?
Keeping everything to herself without saying a word, to the point where she almost bursts, and exhausting her energy to suppress it…
Up until a few days ago, Setsuna's been repeating those actions non-stop, rapidly tiring herself out in the process.
We can't see each other face to face, nor can we hear each other's voices, but we can still feel that we're connected.
Considering our current situation, this text-only relationship might be the most comfortable solution for both of us.
For now, I'll put my thoughts on hold, whether it be thoughts of optimistically looking forward or pessimistically running away.
The weekend lunch rush. I should just forget everything and work like I've never worked before.
…I wonder how she's doing right now.
"Good morning～! We've been waiting for you, Kitahara-san."
"Oh! You're finally here. We have a huge backlog of orders waiting, so we'll need you to go all out from the very beginning, Kitahara-san."
"Come on, Sugiura-san, don't just stand there. Table 15's calling for you."
"Uh, um, Floor Manager? What's going on here?"
"We didn't have nearly enough members for the evening shift, so we arranged for him to come over in the evening. …But he wouldn't be Kitahara-san if he didn't come over before lunch even started."
"Oh? Aaah… You looked like you were really looking forward to it, so I didn't tell you. I thought that it'd be more interesting this way."
The certain person that I was worried about just now is trembling in front of me with a vivid blush on her face for some reason.
…Was letting her go off on her own on only the third day too much for her to handle after all?
"Please wait a little longer. I'll be done soon."
"…No, slow down and chew more thoroughly. It's better for your digestion that way."
The lunch rush is over, and the restaurant's staff are finally able to breathe sighs of relief as we enter the early afternoon.

With a level of expertise far above what you would expect from someone who's only been here for three days, Sugiura worked flawlessly through both morning and lunch, and is now enjoying her break in the staff room.
And she's also voraciously digging into my cooking at the same time.
I have a number of theories as to why she's eating with such abandon right now.
Maybe she tired herself too much working so fiercely through the lunch rush that by the time she could have lunch herself, her hunger became too much to bear.
Or perhaps she believes that she shouldn't be so brazen as to take her time with her breaks given that she's still new here.
"…Well, what did you want to talk to me about?"
"…So you were tired of waiting for me after all. You even tried to pretend to be considerate by telling me to chew thoroughly and whatnot."
Maybe it's because Sugiura decided to drag me into the anteroom with her while I'm in the middle of my esteemed work hours, even though she's supposed to be the only one having her break right now.
"Aaah, come on. My tongue's burnt now. Why would you do something like that?"
"Anyway, what did you want to talk about? I have to get back to the kitchen soon."
Satou's gaze of death as I left keeps flashing through my mind. He didn't get to take a break yet himself, after all.
"I'll get to the point then… Senpai."
"…Should we wait a little longer, maybe?"
The truth is, Senpai… I'm feeling a little pressured in the restaurant because of my position."
"Oh, did you get harassed by someone? You do seem like the type that others might have a problem with, Sugiura."

"You're the one who can't. Where did that sudden and selfish request come from all of a sudden?"

"You really can't, no matter what? It has to be now."

1. You should come here after all.

"You haven't spoken to the professor for a while either, right? You still have to bear with him for another year, so shouldn't you at least show up?"

"There will be plenty of chances in the future to drink with me alone."

…No, it's not that anything about her changed, it's just that I started to look at her differently.

"Please apologize to everyone for me. Just think of a suitable excuse, like I'm not feeling well or something."

"You sounded like an old man in his seventies just now…"

"Well, you've got your work cut out for you. She's a troublesome girl, isn't she? You have my condolences."

"Oh, and it'd be nice if we could go to a place where we wouldn't have to walk a lot. You know, we could take a car, or go to a hotel in front of a station, and ideally only for one night so we won't need to deal with any heavy luggage."

And who is it that made Setsuna unable to do just that, I wonder?
Who exactly is responsible for the grave crime of making her suffer all this time?
"Heeey! How long are you gonna gawk at that text and grin to yourself? Give it here, let me read it!"

The promise I made back then, when Izumi ended up staying at my place, had already become meaningless.
"Don't stand me up this time. I waited more than an hour already."
"That was because… Got it. I'll be there for sure."

Neither of us would be, in any case.

"Making me act like a woman who's above my own league… You're setting the bar awfully high, Haruki-kun."

If Izumi was still feeling down like how she sounded on the phone earlier, I'd be having trouble deciding how to cheer her up right now.
But this just ended up becoming another typical drinking party.
An unfair drinking party where Izumi is complaining as she continues drinking despite me being the one who's sponsoring all the snacks and drinks.
But I don't need to think about such trivial things. I'll just go along with her and get my wallet sucked dry, then unwind by lecturing her.

Izumi's shoulder flinched a little just now, I think.

Izumi's hand is moving differently than usual.
"I never stood out much in school. That's why not many of my classmates actually remember me."

Her small, smooth, and soft hand.

While continuing to stare at me.
"So what does being able to do that have to do with it?"

I never thought this kind of "seductiveness" would be coming from Izumi, both the liquor and the hot sweat are rushing out of my body…

"Ah, come to think of it, until when were you playing the guitar? You know, the one that's like a decoration in your apartment?"
No matter how hard I try to hide my feelings within my heart, I can't resist my reflexive answers to her questions.

Perhaps sensing my hesitation, Izumi once again stares at me intently.
That's why I'm pretending that I'm not hiding anything, pretending that nothing happened, and avoiding her eyes…
"You've… been looking away from me for a while now, you know?"

"You're the one who's constantly scolding me about 'look at the other person's face when you're talking to them,' you know."

As she looks up at me with those shiny eyes, her gaze pierces right through my eyes, as if trying to invite me…
"Hahaha… I'll give it to you as a token of remembrance."
My misunderstanding and delusion is completely cut off by Izumi's light-hearted joke.
"Yeah, let's get going. I'll miss the last train if I don't leave soon."

What excuse am I supposed to make up for the fact that our hands were clasped tightly for so long…?

"Hey, what do you plan on doing for winter break, Haruki?"
"Did I ask you about it before? That same question?"
As I enter the platform to send Izumi off, the cold air that pierces through my skin and turns my breath into white mist instantly sobers me up.

"I'm not exactly asking you to meet up with me or hang out with me…"
"But, well, if you're ever feeling really bored or find yourself with lots on your mind, feel free to give me a call."
As always, the way she makes sure there's still a little distance between us despite being so close to me feels quite nice.
"Your attention please. The train on Line 6 heading toward Aikawa will arrive shortly."

"I'll be whoever you wish for me to be, Haruki. Whether it's a good friend, or a bad one… or perhaps even…"

I'm worried that I'll betray someone again, that no one will be happy again, that I'll make the worst possible choice yet again.
And it was then that I arrived at the worst, most deplorable answer.
Izumi draws her body close to my chest.
It's the only thing she can do.
"I probably… won't be able to see you for a while."
Because our hands are clasped together so tightly, I couldn't shake her off even if I wanted to.
I no longer require the side of Izumi that's completely unfeminine.
I no longer have to rely on her to repel other women like I did in the past.
Right now, I can finally be my true self again and slowly become capable of dealing with women like I used to in the past.
"The doors are closing. Please be careful."
Why can I accept Izumi's "feminine" side now?
Is it because what I seek is Izumi's "feminine" side? Is that what I truly desire?

Everyone, except for one person. The one who always is, and forever will be, on the battlefield.

"Do you really not have anyone you'd like to share your joy with?"

"No, you should've let it slide by now…"
She's referring to something that I'd slipped out almost seven hours ago.
The monologue I had during the celebration, which had been slightly insensitive and a little difficult to take in.
"How about your parents? They're paying for your university tuition, right, Kitahara?"
"My mother lives nearby, but, well, besides paying for my tuition, she…"
"How about your friends? You're still in touch with your friends from high school, right?"
"Don't worry, we're still in touch. I don't have as few friends as others seem to think."
The way she cares about others makes her seem like a yakuza boss caring about her subordinates.
It makes me extremely shameful. But it's not like I can find myself making any excuses, either.
"Uhh… how should I put this? It's a little hard to explain."
It'd be nice if it were just a regular article.
It could have been gossip from the entertainment industry, a collection of scary prophecies, or even information about Onjuku's red-light district.
Takeya would definitely point his finger at me and laugh, and Io would laugh along for a bit as well before patting my shoulder to show her sympathy.
She'd buy a copy of such a lowbrow magazine with her own money regardless and hold it tightly to her chest… I think.
"How do I say this… the problem I have isn't really about the relationships I have with my family or my friends, but rather what would come after if I were to share this with them…"
However, this article's talking about "Touma Kazusa, the Emerging Star in the Japanese World of Piano," which changes things up quite a bit…
Takeya would probably fall silent feeling bothered by the whole situation, while Io would probably get extremely angry and leave without even saying a word.
"Well, the thing is… it's about the person who the article covered…"
It took me a while, but the moment I finally decided to tell her…
It seems like Mari-san saw this coming a mile away, and she takes a step back to distance herself from me.
"Hey, please wait up for a minute!"
Moreover, she seems to be quite hurt as if I'd accidentally said something to offend her, such that I can't bear to leave her while she's wearing the expression she currently has.
I hurry and chase after Mari-san as she walks away very quickly, although even if I do catch up to her, I don't know what I could do to stop her.
That's why I keep a little distance. I could reach her shoulder if I stretched out my hand, but I just kept walking after her long, swaying hair.
Then, she quickly changes direction and walks into a building that still has the lights on.
And I'd note that the stores around these parts seem to close quite late…
She walks out of the bookstore with a paper bag in hand and takes the new issue of Ensemble out of it, proudly flaunting it in front of her chest.
"There were only two copies left. That was close… As I thought, it's selling well."
"This is mine. A collector's copy, to preserve forever."
"You're such a liar, Kitahara. Isn't there someone who can share this happiness with you?"
At first, I couldn't understand what Mari-san was trying to say at all.
"This is my subordinate's first great success. Is it wrong for me to feel happy?"
"Even so, you didn't have to buy it… There are still leftover samples…"
"This is worth spending money on to me, you know!"
No, no matter how many times I try to think it through, there are still some things about her that I can't really understand.
"No matter the reason, I won't stand for my cute subordinate's first work not being acknowledged… How could I ever stand for that?"
"Come on, I'm not a spoiled child."
"And how can you be so calm about it!?"
Still, including situations like these, Mari-san's logic is incredibly forceful and senseless, but very convincing.
"Kitahara, you did a great job. It's on par with the first article I wrote. …Well, mine was just slightly better."
Even if it means I'm being tricked by her… I allow myself to be moved by her words.
"But you've worked so hard on this… What do you mean, no one would be happy about it? How can you say something so sad!?"
The reason why I hesitated isn't as simple as Mari-san assumes it is.
Still, regardless of whether she knows about my circumstances or not, Mari-san is getting really mad about the pitiable state she's convinced I'm in.
"Wh…Why are you laughing? I'm really mad at you here!"
As we keep talking, I notice that I'm feeling strange. I just started laughing at myself after realizing how lame I must look to others, and I can't stop myself.
"Mari-san… you're actually quite passionate, aren't you? The way you let things slip out like that might be your only fault."
"Y-You're the one who's acting cynical all the time! Do you think you're cool acting like that?"
"No, you're the cool one here. …And I really like that part of you, Mari-san."
Mari-san is the second woman who's ever made me think this way.
It's different from the composed, sharp way that I once saw in the first, however.
I'm not sure how to put it. I guess she's hot-blooded and strong-willed. She has an aura of old-fashioned coolness that carries with it a strange sense of passion.
…But when I put it that way, is it just me or does it feel like I'm not praising a woman at all?
"Once again, thank you very much. …You always find a way to cheer me up."
"I… I'm glad you understand. Still, keep in mind that you shouldn't be teasing your supervisor like that."
"Understood, I'm sorry. I'll be careful from now on."
"…All right, then. In that case, I'll forget the shame you brought upon me today."
"I don't recall doing something that terrible, though…"
"Ah… Excuse me. Just give me a moment."
"I'll go pick it up. …The very last copy, I mean."
"Thanks to you, Mari-san, I think I have a person in mind now… A person who might want to share this happiness with me."
Mari-san has taught me this, after all.
In the end, I can only go on the offensive. If I don't face it head-on, nothing will change.
"What the… So he does have a girlfriend, after all…"
"Making a fool out of me like this…!"
"It was released today. I bought a copy as a souvenir."
"Everyone from the editing department went out of their way to congratulate me. We had some snacks and drinks in the meeting roomーa modest party to celebrate a meager accomplishment."
"I'm sorry for not telling you about the title of the magazine and its release date."
"I didn't want you to get the magazine before I did, Setsuna. I wanted to give it to you myself."
"Well, that's about it. It's my first published article, so I hope you'll take it."
"It'll only take about five minutes of your time. Are you free tomorrow? I can stop by your house to pass it to you."
Perhaps I'm getting carried away… No, I most certainly am, actually.
Perhaps I really do want to brag about this to someone. Or perhaps, just this once, I want to share this happiness with her.
…No. I've always wanted to share my happiness with her. I really want to hear her voice instead of just reading her texts.
I want to see her smile for myself.
It's just that I've been stubborn and incapable of honestly expressing such desires on my own.
Perhaps my article will hurt Setsuna. Perhaps it will bring her pain all over again.
But right now, I want her to hear my feelings, including all of that.
That's why I want to give her this magazine. I want to talk to her. …I want to see her.
In the end, though, I'm still as incapable of conclusively expressing my sincerity to her as I've ever been, even after three years.
Although I don't know which meddlesome god was the one that lectured me not to stop halfway and keep going.
"I'm sorry, I can't make it tomorrow. I've made plans to go out with my family already."
But this situation… Just as I'd hoped, though irresolute as I may be, just cut off all of my escape routes.
"Would it be okay if… we met on the 24th?"
"Right, I'll make sure that I'll come today. I've already confirmed my shift for the day and called in as well."
"I'm working the evening shift so that I can match your arrival, so I intend to stay until the closing hours tonight."
"…You're still going on about that? Please, it's about time you made up your mind already! This is for your best friend's sake, isn't it!?"
"Ah, hold on a second. …What? Is something the matter? I need to head to work soon, so please make it quick."
"…Since we've pulled through the second term without a hitch, we were thinking about inviting you to go to karaoke with us, but…"
"…I suppose this is the part where you decline because you have to go to work."
"…I'm sorry, but that's how it is. I have to do this for our graduation trip."
"Well, I suppose there's no helping that, but still, don't you think you've been rather distant lately?"
"You immediately head home even when you don't have any work. And during the long-awaited lax period given that our exams are over."
"Aaah, I've got something I need to deal with before the end of the year. But I think all the pieces will fall into place and it'll all be solved pretty soon."
"Ah, give me a minute, sorry. I'm in the middle of a call. …Sorry about the wait. Yeah, let's meet at the restaurant afterward."
"Make sure you come, got it? I'll be waiting for you."
"Please do. For the sake of this relationship."
"Spending that time together is an absolute must. It's not every day that it's Christmas, after all."
"Sorry about the wait. Well, what did you two want to talk about?"
"We were just about to ask you if you had any plans for our usual Christmas party, but…"
"…We got our answer before we even managed to ask."
"Ah, I'm sorry. I can't make it this year. It's charity work… no, it's about my part-time job."
"…We absolutely won't be envious of you."
"I will do my best, of course, but I'm not sure I understand what you're trying to say."
"I'm sorry. It seems I've bothered you somehow."
"I didn't really mean anything special when I suggested the 24th. It's just that it's actually going to be the only day I'll be available."
"My family's planning to have a Christmas party on the 25th. My mom's gonna make fried chicken in the morning, and we're all having flavored champagne as usual."
"Mom has been telling Takahiro for a while now that it's about time he brought home his girlfriend, but it doesn't seem like that'll be happening this year."
"Maybe it's because she might feel too awkward to come over. Suddenly being alone among our family might make her feel rather uncomfortable."

"That reminds me, Haruki-kun. You weren't afraid at all. Even when you'd just met my dad, you were very bold and straightforward with him. It made you seem really reliable, but also made it hard to imagine we were the same age!"
"But I guess you didn't think much of it, did you, Haruki-kun? Back then, the only thing on your mind was the school festival, right?"

"…It seems I went off on a tangent there. Well, to put it simply, I'm only free the day after tomorrow. Nothing special about it, so don't worry about it too much, and don't force yourself to bring a present."
"Ah, but don't forget to bring the magazine, all right? After all, that's the main reason you're coming."
"That's about it. …If you can't make it, please tell me clearly."
No. There's no way I could ever ask that.
It's like she's trying to show off her perfectly sound explanation, then leaves a small opening on purpose. Or maybe she really doesn't realize it.
…She probably isn't aware of it. After all, it's not like Setsuna to be compromising.
…That's why our relationship has turned out like this.
If only Setsuna was a little more cunning. If only she were more self-centered…
Perhaps we would have been together up until this day, or perhaps we'd be completely alone without one another.
"I understand. The 24th it is. Nothing special. It's just that I've got work then and I can't get a day off."
"I don't know when they'll let me off, but it'll be late for sure, so I don't want to inconvenience you."
"Besides, I'd like to give this to you as soon as possible, that's why it might feel like I'm rushing things."
"The day after tomorrow, then. I'll call you if I can make it. But don't stay up waiting for me."
"Well then… I should be getting back."
The minute hand of the anteroom clock was pointing directly upward before I realized it.
If I don't get back to my post soon, a certain annoying junior will definitely use it as a reason to badmouth me later.
"Anytime is fine. It doesn't matter how late it gets, either. As long as I can have just a minute of your time, it's fine."
"But I really hope it'll still be the 24th when we meet."
The small opening that Setsuna left…
Is slowly getting bigger in a slightly mysterious way, regardless of whether or not she's doing it intentionally.
"Sorry about the wait, Sugiura. I'll take over from he…"
"Everyone's working desperately hard. What were you doing lazing around on your break for so long? What makes you think you alone have that privilege?"
I guess I jinxed myself there.
"All right, I'll take a ten minute break. We can't relax just yet. It's gonna get a lot busier during winter break, you know."
She's incredibly skilled, isn't she… in the use of sarcasm.
"The customers over at Table 12 still haven't placed their order. Please attend to them."
As always, she's meddlesome, nice, well-mannered, sharp-tongued, merciless, and really annoying.
But it's not like she has any ulterior motive. When a lump of good intentions like her is mad at me, there's not much I can do about it.
Rather, I should work hard now to regain her trust.
"Sorry for making you wait. May I take your orde…"
"I'll have beef stew in red wine, Burgundy-style."
"And I'll have an Okonomiyaki with meatballs in udon, Hiroshima-style."
"…You know we don't serve either of those, right?"
…There shouldn't be any ulterior motives, right?
"It's such a great tear-jerking love story. I hear it's the number one movie in Japan this year."
"Is it really a love story? The title sounds a little dark to me, though."
"Sure, I said it's a love story, but I didn't say anything about a happy ending."
Since these two annoying guests seem like they'll be staying until closing time, I waited for a proper opportunity to drag them into the anteroom.
I felt a cold stare on my back due to a misunderstanding that I'm taking another break again when I did that, but I really had no choice in this case.
"And what are you going to do with those two movie tickets?"
"…Actually, I think I'll pretend that I didn't ask that."
"Well, hear me out, they're selling these at 4000 yen for two tickets now, but I'll give them to you with a great discount for just 3600 yen! A bargain like this isn't easy to come by…"
"No, hang on. Why are you even trying to sell me movie tickets…?"
"Sorry, Haruki. You can have them for half price, 2000 yen, so wouldn't you please buy them?"
"The truth is, this guy was planning on going to see it with his supposed true love. But then the girl went 'I've had enough of you, Takeya,' which sort of brings us to this situation…"
"I guess there's really no helping that…"
Especially if something like that's actually coming from Io of all people.
Still, I can't believe these guys barged into my workplace and interfered with my work just for this nonsense…
"And there you have it, so I was hoping you'd help out this poor and lonely single man live through this Christmas."
"Why don't you go with him, Io…? It might not be a bad idea for you two to go out once in a while."
"Give me a break. Who'd want to go out with this guy?"
"It's just an act, an act! …I wouldn't go with you, though."
"Would you two start getting along already? It's like you haven't changed at all since high school."
I'm shocked by how perfectly synced their sighs were just now.
"I'm begging you, Haruki. It's not even about the money here. It's just that I can't stand to keep them with me anymore."
"You could sell them to someone yourself, or give them as a present. Besides, Takeya is already going this far."
The thought of saying "Why don't you buy it?" crosses my mind, but for the sake of Takeya's mental health, I decide not to try to shift this to Io.
Glancing inside my wallet, I bid farewell to the thousand yen bills that I'd been saving for situations like these.
"Here, go enjoy yourself by having a few drinks or something. …You'll tag along too, right, Io?"
Without showing any restraint, Takeya accepts the four 1000 yen bills that I handed him.
"Well… I don't mind as long as it's not a date."
After which Io takes two of the bills for herself and nonchalantly slides them into her own pocket.
And it's very like her to not give off the slightest inkling of wanting to return them to me.
When was the last time I went out to watch one? …Who did I go with?
"Wait, what? So this is only going to be aired once and only on a single day? It's the number one Japanese film of the year, is it not?"
I wonder if anyone I know from my seminars would want to go.
"It's actually a rerun. The first time it aired was about ten years ago."
"You… really are nothing but a shameless liar…"
I can't call someone out to meet me just to give them movie tickets. I'm not like Takeya.
"The seats are great, you know? Right in the middle and slightly toward the back. I reserved them by waiting in line in the morning right on the first day they were available."
Well, I suppose I could give her a call. She probably has more free time than I could imagine.
"Oh, and I forgot to tell you, the tickets are only valid on the 24th. Don't let 'em go to waste."
"But, well, if you're ever feeling really bored or find yourself with lots on your mind, feel free to give me a call."
Wait a second, I… What was I thinking just now?
"Oh, and also, you've got a reservation at Tenbou Restaurant for 7 PM."
"I'll be whoever you wish for me to be, Haruki. Whether it's a good friend, or a bad one… or perhaps even…"
Do I truly understand what seriously asking her out now would entail…?
"The reservation is for two people, under the name Iizuka. The table should be by the window, so you'll have a great view of the sea. Dinner is 20,000 yen per person, so 40,000 yen in total."
I have no idea why I'm even thinking of something like that. Am I actually getting carried away just because Christmas is coming soon?
And such a thought should be completely unforgivable to me as of now.
Maybe I should give them to someone in the editing department? They're always helping me out, after all.
"It's actually a rerun. The first time it aired was about ten years ago."
"You… really are nothing but a shameless liar…"
…Then again, if you ask me who's helped me out the most, the only person that comes to mind is Mari-san.
Not only did she buy the magazine that published my first article, she also held a celebration for its release, and always finds plenty of work for me to do, so isn't it normal to pay her back?
…It's not something I can pay back with just a movie ticket, though.
"The seats are great, you know? Right in the middle and slightly toward the back. I reserved them by waiting in line in the morning right on the first day they were available."
But if I gave Mari-san two tickets, who would she invite to go with her?
Amamiya-san… I doubt they'd want to watch a romantic movie together. As for a boyfriend…
…I guess I could just give her one of the tickets.
"Oh, and I forgot to tell you, the tickets are only valid on the 24th. Don't let 'em go to waste."
Wait. How did I come to this conclusion?
What would happen if I invited Mari-san to watch the movie together with me?
"Oh, and also, you've got a reservation at Tenbou Restaurant for 7 PM."
She'll probably complain like she usually does, but ultimately accept my invitation.
And since I'll accompany her when she's a bit more cheerful and vulnerable than usual, I might be able to relax a bit, as well.
"The reservation is for two people, under the name Iizuka. The table should be by the window, so you'll have a great view of the sea. Dinner is 20,000 yen per person, so 40,000 yen in total."
But to have such a good time… Can I really get away with it right now?
I wonder if Satou or Nakagawa-san would be interested in this. I'll ask them later.
"It's actually a rerun. The first time it aired was about ten years ago."
"You… really are nothing but a shameless liar…"
If that doesn't work, I can just ask the other part-timers. If I'm selling at half price, someone should buy them, right?
"The seats are great, you know? Right in the middle and slightly toward the back. I reserved them by waiting in line in the morning right on the first day they were available."
If no one wants them even after all that, I guess I'll just have to invite someone…
Right, how about… the junior who's been helping me out recently?
"Oh, and I forgot to tell you, the tickets are only valid on the 24th. Don't let 'em go to waste."
Wait. How'd it come to this?
If I invited Sugiura to watch this movie… I mean, I can't even imagine myself inviting her.
"Oh, and also, you've got a reservation at Tenbou Restaurant for 7 PM."
Besides, if I just randomly asked her, she'd probably respond with something like, "Do you seriously think I'm the one you should be inviting!?" and I'd get the lecture of a lifetime.
"The reservation is for two people, under the name Iizuka. The table should be by the window, so you'll have a great view of the sea. Dinner is 20,000 yen per person, so 40,000 yen in total."
If she's not the one I should be inviting, then who should I be inviting…?
"All right, just wait a… Hold it."
"Sorry, Haruki. You can have it for 10% off, 36,000 yen, so wouldn't you please buy it?"
"Now just hold on a second here…"
"You're a demon, Io! If we do that, then the money we got back for the two movie tickets goes down the drain again!"
"No, it's my money that's being thrown down the drain here…"
"It's for your best friend's sake, right? What are you being all stingy for?"
"Wait, how'd it come to this? And how is asking me to pay 36000 yen meant to be for my sake?"
"Damn it… fine! Like jumping into a freshwater spri… no, I initially planned to leap into Arumi's waters, but I'm okay with selling it to you for 36,000 yen!"
A whole month's salary just evaporated in an instant.
"Ah, Kitahara-san, can I… Whoa, what happened to you? Why are you staggering?"
"I'm blanking out because I'm feeling quite regretful…"
Takeya's movie ticket deal makes me feel like I was just in one of those restaurants that adds things to your bill without you being aware of it, gradually prying your money away.
Time-limited to 5 PM, on the 24th. And the tickets are only valid in the cinema located in the shopping mall near the bay.
Following that, a nice dinner at Tenbou Restaurant, in Arumi Integral Hotel… The price of which is ten times that of the tickets'.
Christmas Eve at the bay. Watching a movie and then enjoying dinner at a place with a great view at night. This is definitely a setup for lovers…
The goal of all this is obviously to set up a date, so there's no way I can sell it off to anyone, let alone give it away for free.
After being viciously caught off guard, I feel a sense of emptiness slowly taking over my entire body.
"Umm, I'd like to talk to you about something… Should I leave it for later?"
Thus, as I swear to myself that I'll never fall for such a thing again, still staggering, I realize that the number of customers in the restaurant has decreased.
"The truth is, at the beginning of the year… We're gonna be really short-handed for the first three days."
"Yeah, since we have so many student part-timers here… We'll be fine until the end of the year, but after that…"
"The restaurant is going to be open on New Year's Day again?"
"We always get a lot of customers on New Year's Day, after all. We got the orders straight from HQ."
"And the branch manager won't be here either, huh. Are you going to be alright?"
"That's exactly what I wanted to talk to you about… Kitahara-san, could you possibly come in to work then? I'm aware that this is an unreasonable request, and your salary will naturally…"
"Only until the end of the winter break, right? You won't keep trying to prolong my work after that, got it?"
Since I just got deceived, even though Satou is obviously rather reserved in front of me, I can't help but stare at him suspiciously.
"Of course not! I know you're going to be looking for a proper job soon, and the branch manager will probably be back by next month too."
"All right… I really need the money now, anyway."
I'll be struggling to pay next month's rent if I don't agree to this.
Perfect timing, too. If I work from dawn till dusk during the first three days of the New Year, I'll probably be able to make up for what I lost today.
"…You don't have any ulterior motives, do you?"
"I won't force you to come on any other days. I really mean it, it's just those three days."
I won't make any promises so easily anymore.
"…You're being unusually careful. Did something happen?"
"It's simple, I'm just wondering if a friendship where money only flows in one direction can really be considered a friendship."
"And I just learned that lesson the hard way…"
I paid 40,000 yen just for that lesson, after all.
"All right, I'll add you to the schedule, then. Starting from the 1st, please come in at 10 AM."
"This really is the last time. After New Year's, even if you call me, I won't be answering, got it?"
"I understand. I won't trouble you any further. …So then, thanks for your hard work this year. I hope we'll get along well in the next year too."
"Yep. I'll see you in January. I've already taken you off this month's schedule."
"I can't bother you all the time, Kitahara-san. I'll take care of the rest of this year's work with the current staff."
"I… don't have to come anymore until the end of the year?"
"And especially not this week! Please rest up!"
I made sure to listen to every word coming out of his mouth to prevent a repeat of last time, but I've got this strange feeling telling me that someone pulled a fast one on me again.
"Why the wrinkly face? You're still young."
"Didn't I tell you to not take the evening shift anymore?"
I know that I must be looking tired right now, but if I provoke her, I'll just make it even worse.
…Come to think of it, I haven't talked with Sugiura much today.
Well, I've had a lot going on.
The promise with Setsuna. Takeya and Io coming to the restaurant. And the shifts for after New Year's.
My mind is rather overwhelmed, so I really can't enjoy the pointless conversations I usually have with her at the moment.
Not that our usual conversations are ever fun…
Sugiura stares up at my face as I remain tired and dejected, her expression suggesting that she thinks I'm getting on in years or something.
An indiscernible expression, one that leaves me completely clueless as to whether she's worried about me or is trying to assess me.
"Want me to help you with cleanup?"
"It's fine, you've already changed. This is the kitchen staff's job anyway. Just leave already and be careful on your way home."
"…Seems like you still haven't figured it out. You need to be honest at times like these."
Sugiura continues staring intently at me. I still can't wrap my head around what she's talking about and can only respond with nothing but vague replies.
And she's wearing the same indiscernible expression of either pity or exasperation.
"Well, I'll just follow your orders, Senpai, and head on home. Goodbye, and Happy New Year!"
"Okay, make sure to take the well-lit roads…"
Just as I finish my thought, she darts out of my line of sight, and her footsteps resound throughout the darkened restaurant.
I can tell that something is off.
"This time, please be honest with your true feelings, all right?"
"If you don't, I won't be able to let go… I swear, making me worry so much…"
Then, Sugiura reignites my unease with yet another mystery.
I didn't get the chance to confirm it.
"This time, please be honest with your true feelings, all right?"
Was I not honest before? …Well, if that's the case, then we're no different.
"If you don't, I won't be able to let go…"
Why would you say that, Sugiura? What exactly did you do?
"I swear, making me worry so much…"
The fact that I won't be working here for the rest of the year…
My shifts were only decided just now, so how could she know…?
"Well, that's a job well done. And thanks for the meal～"
"Hey, we agreed to split it. I just suffered a great loss, come on."
"Gulp… Haah… Don't be so petty. It all went according to plan."
"…And thanks to that, Maiko is probably going to kill me tomorrow."
"It'd be nice if those two could use this chance to go back to how they used to be."
"It'll be a pain for me if they don't. My schedule is completely messed up thanks to this."
"Christmas doesn't always have to be fancy. Just going to a family restaurant or a ramen place is fine. If she's complaining just because of this, you might as well break up with her."
"But those two are different… They can't even hold a regular conversation properly if you don't force an opportunity on them."
"Is that why you picked that high-class restaurant in the hotel? You know that Haruki never lets his money go to waste, so there's no way he'd do so."
"Even if he wants to sell it off or gift it to someone else, it's pretty much impossible with how little time there is left."
"Is that for real, though? They seriously promised to meet on the 24th?"
"I got it out of Setsuna a little while ago, somehow. She also really insisted that I should absolutely not tell anyone."
"Now that's just dirty. …And you've even dragged me into this. Even though I made the reservation two months in advance."
"If you've got any complaints, save them for the girl you introduced me to. She's the one who came up with the whole plan this time around."
"As expected of Mini-Haruki… The way she butts into other people's business and uses whatever means necessary really reminds me of her master."
"Brrr～ It's so cold! I heard we're going to have a white Christmas this year."
The promise with Setsuna… The promise of meeting on the 24th with Setsuna.
"Kitahara-san, you're walking home, right? If I remember correctly, you live in the opposite direction from the station."
Takeya and Io came to the restaurant… And Takeya tricked me into buying some tickets for a movie on the 24th and some other stuff.
"I'll go get my motorbike from the back. See you later, then."
There's my shift on New Year's. …As well as the fact that my schedule until the new year has become completely empty. In other words, I no longer have any obligations on the 24th.
In just a few hours, even, the conditions to fulfill a certain promise have just been met. Am I reading too deeply into this?
"I know I must be getting annoying by now, but I'll be counting on you during the first three days of next month, all right? Oh, and Happy New Year!"
Didn't someone say the same thing just a little while ago?
Could there be some sort of scheme unfolding behind my back…?
"Sugiura Koharu-chan, was it? The girl who you desperately tried to coax, but who only saw us as a means to an end."
"Don't describe her in a way that makes all parties involved look bad."
"But this plan… What does she get out of it?"
"Unlike us, she's not really friends with Setsuna. And she was more of a nemesis to Haruki until recently. …There's no reason for her to meddle this much."
"Hmm… maybe she really gets nothing out of it? Maybe she's just doing it out of pure kindness. In other words, a busybody."
"No way… she's not Haruki, after all."
"Sure, she's not Haruki, but she's Mini-Haruki. She never considers her personal gain or loss when doing things."
"So, basically… she's just doing it for Haruki's sake?"
"No matter what happens to her, she's content as long as Haruki can be happy… Something like that?"
"I really want to think so too, but she's a girl too, you know?"
"Still, there's just no way. This is Haruki we're talking about. How could that dense brick make girls do so much for him…"
"You said the same thing about Setsuna too at first, Takeya. …And about Touma Kazusa as well."
"Excuse me! A double bourbon, on the rocks!"
"Aaah, forget that, just give us the bottle here!"
As the last train departs from Minegaya Station, the few people who got off stare at me because I was sprinting.
I don't recognize anyone among them, however, which leaves me at a loss, as expected.
My hands are on my knees, I'm deeply bending forward, and I'm panting heavily.
I figured out their plan exactly 30 minutes ago.
After forcing the truth out of Satou and berating him while I was at it, I sprinted toward the station. Then I realized that the next train wouldn't arrive until fifteen minutes later.
I sprinted into the train when it arrived and the seat kept making creaking sounds due to my impatient fidgeting. Just waiting for ten minutes felt like several hours.
Ten minutes later, I realized I had made a pointless trip.
I started chasing her twenty minutes after she'd left the restaurant.
Meaning that, if nothing went wrong, she will have arrived home by now, since her house is only fifteen minutes away from the station.
But even so, even though it might be a pointless trip, I have to chase after her.
I hadn't even thought of my cell phone until now, as it's my final hope. I press the redial button.
I won't feel satisfied until I at least say something to her.
All of the strange feelings I've felt today were caused by this junior of mine. The risk and ultimate cost of her trap is simply far too great.
I knew it, she's not answering.
Of course, Sugiura wouldn't take out her cell phone while riding the train. I'd probably believe that if she used it as an excuse too.
But since I've already made it to Minegaya Station, she must be ignoring me on purpose…
…Haven't I heard that ringtone somewhere before?
The call that I just made…
The voice from the phone and the voice from behind me both reach my ears at the same time.
"Thank goodness. It goes without saying, but I was a little scared of going home alone at this hour."
And just like that, Sugiura smiled and lowered her head apologetically.
I forget the words that I wanted to angrily shout at her, only capable of standing there while staring at her blinding smile in bewilderment.
"You offered to work every shift this week, including Christmas, in exchange for letting me take a break?"
"Well, if I don't work hard during the winter break to save up money, I'll probably have to work part-time during my vacation to earn enough money for a plane ticket back home."
"That's not an excuse for not letting me come to work…"
"If they don't stop relying on you soon, Senpai, they'll never be able to stand on their own."
"And the part where Takeya and Io visited the restaurant was all your doing too, wasn't it?"
"I have no idea what you're talking about. Why would I do something like that?"
"I'm the one who wants to know why here…"
In order to help Setsuna and me get together again, she went around and bothered so many people, all the while leaving the stage full of openings for me to notice.
She didn't plan out the small details. The plan was too straightforward and bold. This is a typical example of smart people falling for their own trap.
"I don't know who told you all this nonsense, but you wouldn't actually believe such a ridiculous rumor, would you?"
"It really is ridiculous. It's gone beyond the level of annoyingly butting into others' business. You're like a woman who's getting tricked by a marriage fraudster."
"…Must take a terrible man to do something like that. I'm sure that divine punishment will strike him down one day."
"You just said the rumor was ridiculous, right? Then no such man should exist."
…How come I'm not making any progress after questioning her for so long? If anything, I might have accidentally sealed her lips just now. Am I an idiot or something?
…No, the true idiot here is this high school girl. She's already made me want to deny even knowing her.
"That's why I told you to stop taking evening shifts."
"I guess so. If there's no point anymore, I'll stop."
"If you keep worrying about the small details, everyone's going to hate you, you know? That goes for the both of us."
Despite her words, she's so cold that she's blowing air to warm her hands. It's like I'm looking at the quintessential example of a listless, fleeting, yet beautiful girl.
"I guess… a rumor is nothing more than a rumor, after all."
"If there really is an idiot who used her conviction as an excuse to cause trouble for everyone, without the slightest reflection…"
"She… probably did it hoping to see that expression again one more time… And hoping to never see it again."
"I still have no idea what you're trying to say…"
Ignoring whether or not it made sense, Sugiura is trying her best to explain it in a very simple and logical manner, but it turns into a mystery when she expresses her feelings.
"You were looking out the window in the music room, remember?"
Sugiura did happen to see me when I visited our high school.
"I can't seem to get it out of my mind. Every time I remember it, I feel incredibly annoyed. …That's why I have to do something about it."
I had returned to three years ago. Back to when I was talking with Setsuna and Kazusa daily.
"About what? Please don't take a rumor so seriously, it's painful to watch."
That joyous time of my life, something that I've lost and have not yet recovered, has once again caused me so much pain.
For a while, I walked with my head hung low since I couldn't find my way around Minegaya anyway.
And in a row of similar pre-built houses, we arrived at a house with a nameplate that said "Sugiura."
"Thanks for seeing me home. …I'm really happy you did."
"Well… it is pretty late after all."
"One more thing. I was a bit mad when you told me to 'just leave already,' you know?"
"…I'm sorry, I wasn't thinking straight at the time."
"Well, what's done is done. It was karmic justice on my part anyway."
How me being unable to think straight was somehow Sugiura's fault, I did not ask.
"I might still show up at the restaurant before the year ends, you know?"
"As a customer, of course. I might start going off loudly again if the staff gets lazy, though."
"…Our establishment will be looking forward to your business. And we will do our utmost to serve you."
"Well then… Seriously, thank you for walking me all this way."
"It's no big deal. Don't worry about it…"
"You do know that the last train might have already left, right?"
I already confirmed that much when I got off at Minegaya Station.
The next train was to arrive ten minutes from then. And that would be the last train of the day.
Just walking Sugiura to her house took a good fifteen minutes, so obviously… there's no way.
After burning 40,000, I have to pay for a taxi too…
"I haven't really done anything that would warrant your thanks."
The date changed a while ago. But Setsuna still answered the phone after just one ring.
"Not really, no. I've been talking to you every day, Haruki-kun."
Just as usual, we normally… no, the usual has been anything but normal lately.
"Ah, that's right! Um… I know it's a little late, but congratulations on publishing your first article."
"You've already congratulated me through a text."
"But I haven't said it directly yet. …Really, congratulations."
"Thank you. But it's not a particularly amazing article, really."
I'm sure that next time we see each other, Setsuna will congratulate me once again.
She'll use "I haven't said it to you face to face yet" as an excuse, and let out a modest smile.
"I wonder what you wrote about… I'm really looking forward to it. Haruki-kun, you haven't even told me the name of the magazine."
"…I'm sorry. I've just got a lot on my mind."
"It's fine. Since you'll hand it to me directly, we're even. …I'm looking forward to seeing it."
"And once we meet, I would like to apologize to you. About what happened before."
"There isn't anything you need to apologize for."
"I think there is. If I don't apologize, we won't be able to start over again."
"Haruki-kun, I, well… I didn't really mean what I said back then, and…"
"Stop. Shouldn't we wait until we meet to talk about that?"
"There's nothing you need to apologize for… not now."
It's just a phone call, but we keep trying to correct our slip-ups over and over again.
It's as if we're walking on a curved plank that's barely the width of a foot, like we're always trying to get back to where we began…
But all the same, despite the imminent danger of everything easily being ruined, we still smile.
"Oh, and I'm sorry that it's on the 24th. I chose that date just because it was convenient for me. I didn't think about your schedule at all, Haruki-kun."
"No, it's fine. No problem, I can make it."
"I'm looking forward to it… Hey, you haven't come over in a while, right? Will you at least come in and let us treat you to some cake? Well… I'll probably treat you before my family does."
That's why we can't rush things the day after tomorrow.
We'll pick a casual place to meet up, chat for a little while, and then slowly bring our relationship back to what it used to be.
"But it's cold outside. Mom said she wanted to see you too."
We should take our time with getting closer again. We've failed countless times in the past three years.
We have another year left as students. We should just make use of this last year to the fullest.
"Besides, it's winter break, so you can stay over a little later than usual. My dad can give you a ride home too."
Because I've seen it with my own eyes.
The wound on Setsuna's chest is still open and has yet to be healed.
I want to meet her, but we can't be together yet. I know that there isn't nearly enough time for us.
"Ah, well… This is going to sound really crazy, so I'd rather you just ignore me, but…"
"I got some, uh… movie tickets from Takeya. They're only valid on the 24th."
A cruel, forceful coincidence. Or perhaps a miracle brought about by kindness and meddling.
"While we're at it, we have a reservation for dinner, as well. …This is going to sound stupid, but it's at Tenbou Restaurant, in Arumi Integral Hotel."
Carefully, slowly. And knowing that it can't be helped even if it won't result in any progress.
Although I have no idea how this is any different from running away, a powerful force is making me speak against the thought.
"The movie starts at 5 PM. And we have a reservation at a restaurant at 7 o'clock."
"W-Well, since I'm asking so suddenly, it's only natural that you don't know what to say, right?"
"Besides, after having dinner near the sea, it'll be very late, so what am I even saying…"
"I'm sorry, forget what I just said! That's it for toda…"
Since I've let it slip out, there's nothing I can do to fix it or take it back.
There's no way I can sell or gift these tickets away to someone.
But if I use them to invite someone…
That's not it. If I use them to invite a certain specific girl… It's the hardest, but also the easiest way to do it. They saw right through this.
"It's me… Mom's asking you to come down and at least eat some porridge."
"…I'm sorry, I still don't have an appetite."
"You've been like that since yesterday. If your stomach hurts so much, you should see the doctor."
"I'm fine, I'm fine… I'll be better by the day after tomorrow…"
"You've got to eat something tomorrow, okay?"
"Okay. Please apologize to mom for me."
"You bought a copy of Ensemble yesterday, right? Let me have a read too."
"I wanted to buy one too, but it was all sold out today. Normally they'd have some left over."
"But isn't Touma-senpai amazing? She's already on the front page of a music magazine."
"I'll give it back real quick. Come on, please?"
"…I'm sorry, I forgot where I put it."
"Well then, I take it that you have decided on this bracelet over here?"
"We're currently running a special offer for engraving initials onto any purchase. Would you be interested?"
"Yes, it could be the recipient's name, or perhaps a particular date… It will only take around 30 minutes."
"Certainly. Please wait for just a moment."
When I first reached this store, wasting around 30 minutes here would have been a trivial loss.
If I take the rest of the trip into account right now, though, the time looks pretty tight. …All because I spent a good two hours in hesitation while looking around here.
Noーin all honesty, that's not the only reason why I don't want to have her initials engraved.
It's been three years since then, but I see this store is still in business.
"Thank you for waiting. Here's your purchase and your change of 2000 yen."
Notably, even the store employee happens to be the same person who greeted me the last time. Perhaps this store is under her own private management.
"Thank you for your purchase. Please come again."
What I bought here three years ago was…
A silver ring with "SETSUNA" engraved on the inside, which was meant to be a birthday present.
But in the end, I never got a chance to give it to her that day, so I just stuffed it in my drawer…
Now, I don't even know where that silver ring is anymore.
Compared to the Christmas present meant for Setsuna I'm currently holding in my hands, that ring brought me so much more pain, anger, and hopelessness.
It was a present filled with my heart and soul, andーto an embarrassing extentーmy yearning for Setsuna.
That's why the moment those feelings became all for naught, our relationship simply shattered along with them…
That's why I can't give her a present that would invite such misunderstandings anymore.
Even so, I pushed myself to the limit and struggled for two hours only to end up choosing an ordinary bracelet in the end.
It's nothing particularly specialーthough I suppose it's just a little bit special.
It wouldn't be the rain on anyone's parade, but it wouldn't cause them to get their hopes up, either. It's just a simple Christmas present that's meant for a girl.
Setsuna will definitely accept it with a bright smile on her face, but would the smile she'd show me today be genuine?
If I remember correctly, the weather forecast did mention that the strongest period of cold of the year is approaching.
The host of the talk show I watched this morning was also excitedly talking about the possibility of a white Christmas this year, too.
However, I had spent two whole hours being at a loss inside that store.
So despite having known about the possibility beforehand, the sight of this snow-filled scenery came so abruptly that it stopped me in my tracks for a few seconds.
The first snowfall of the year.
White spirits manifested from the hopes of many who wished for their arrival, falling upon all on the most celebrated day in the world.
Students excitedly look up to the sky. Lovers gaze out the windows of cafes. White-collar workers wearing coats pick up their paces as if they feel a bit inconvenienced by it all.
Regardless of whether people are happy, excited or simply annoyed by it…
They seem to understand what the falling snow on this very day entails, if only slightly…
And so they feel a little happier, a little more forgiving, and a little closer to one another than usual.
"It's cold, it's so cold! We can have a snowball fight! We can build a snowman, too!"
"Ahahahaha, I messed up. I messed up big time. I guess I still have a ways to go."
"Setsuna, not yet, don't start enjoying yourself yet! We have to get the car out of the snow first! And you, Touma, stop laughing and help me over here!"
"I want to stay like this forever."
"We're currently conducting vehicle inspections. Therefore, both up and down lines will be experiencing delays. We apologize for the inconvenience."
The two train transfers I've made so far managed to operate on schedule somehow.
But at the station for my final transfer, the snow finally became heavy enough to start hindering the operation of the trains.
It's 4:10 PM right now. Had everything gone according to schedule, I would have made the 4:30 meeting time with about five minutes to spare.
…That said, not making sure I had enough time to compensate for unforeseen circumstances like this one is unmistakably an oversight on my part.
The time I wasted looking through the jewelry shop is really biting me in the back right now.
I hope I can at least make it in time for the movie…
Still, it doesn't look like I can avoid being late, even if only by a few minutes.
"Where are you right now? Are you okay?"
"I'm on my way… but I'm going to be a little late. The train schedules got messed up at the last moment."
"I see… I guess there's really no helping that given this weather."
"Yeah, I got here a little early and did some window shopping. …It only started snowing after I got here."
"Sorry. Had I simply arranged for us to meet up at noon, we could have done some shopping together before our movie too."
"It's because of this weather, so there's nothing we can really do about it. It's snowing so… there's nothing we can really do…"
"I might be a little late… but I'll be there as soon as possible. If the movie starts, you should head in by yourself first and…"
"I'll be late, but… I'll definitely be there. Even if it's after the party has ended, I'll at least show up."
"Ah, but I have the tickets… Damn it, I'm so sorry about this. And here I thought…"
"No… It's fine. If we don't make it in time for the movie, we can just go shopping, like you said."
"Sorry. I'm really sorry, Setsuna. It wasn't supposed to turn out like this."
"I'm telling you, you don't have to apologize so profusely…"
"…Stop that. Stop apologizing so desperately. I'm happy as long as you show up, so there's no need for apologies."
"…You're only going to be a little late, right? You're making too big of a deal out of this, Haruki-kun."
"That doesn't change the fact that I'm going to be late…"
"Now that's just really like you, Haruki-kun. You haven't changed at all."
"Anyway, I'll be waiting here, so don't worry about me, Haruki-kun. Ah, but I don't want you forcing yourself to run here or anything, okay? I'd be more upset if you got hurt over this."
"Ah… It sounds like the train will be about ten minutes late. So it'll be around the 40 minute mark when I get over there, I think."
"There, see? That's more than enough time to make it to the movie. You didn't even need to call me about it."
"At any rate, I'll call you again when I get there. I'm sorry, but maybe you could go find a nice, warm place to wait until I get there."
"Okay, I got it. Then I'll see you soon."
The train arrived at the station at 4:35.
After calling Setsuna, I learned that she moved from the seaside parkーwhich had been our original meeting placeーto a nearby shopping mall so she could take shelter from the snow.
Since I haven't been around here much, I got a little lost, but after a good five minutes of sprinting, I finally reached Setsuna…
"I told you not to run here…"
In a place where dozens of people pass by, devoid of any emotional or sentimental ambience…
"Aa-ah, you're all covered in snow. Bend down a little, Haruki-kun."
It's been two weeks since we last met each otherーbut it's also our first proper rendezvous in many months.
…Setsuna and I had shackled ourselves despite the fact that this was never supposed to have been forbidden for us.
"Wow, it's only been a few minutes, and your head's already all covered. The snow must be really harsh out there."
"…It's pretty harsh, yeah. It's gotten darker as well, so I couldn't see very well either."
But now that we're face to face like this, Setsuna's behavior isn't showing any signs of the heaviness it always had up until now.
"Now turn around. Wow, your coat's all white, too."
She's patting the snow off my hair and back like any considerate girlfriend would, and chatting with me unreservedly as if this was just a regular date.
"Now then, should we head over to the cinema? The movie before ours should be just about finished by now."
I have to respond to the way Setsuna's treating me now in kind.
"Since we're going to the cinema, we can't forget popcorn, right?"
"Don't mess up and get the large-sized one by mistake. They serve them in buckets here."
Regardless of whether or not her attitude is merely a facade, I have no choice but to accept her currently cheerful and carefree state as being authentic.
"I imagine we won't have the appetite for dinner if I were to do that."
"Let's try to avoid that, at least. The cost of that dinner is enough to buy dozens of buckets of popcorn…"
"…Wait, Haruki-kun. How much is our dinner today going to cost?"
"Now that I think about it, you said we were going to the Arumi Integral Hotel, right? Isn't everything in there super high-class…?"
"Don't worry about that. Besides, I'm the one who invited you out today."
That's why I'm going to assume the role of a boyfriend who's trying to go the extra mile to prepare a special date for a special day.
"You can't do that! You're even working several jobs just to cover your living expenses, Haruki-kun!"
"That's only half the reason. The other half is that I like doing them…"
"Okay then, we'll split the bill. I'll pay for my portion of the meal today. So, how much does our dinner cost?"
And by doing that, Setsuna will become the mature girlfriend who's more concerned about the situation than her boyfriend's pride for me in return.
"I can't have you do that! I'm sorry, but I don't think you could afford… Ah, I mean…"
"There's no point in spending that much money on me! I'm a girl who would be delighted to go out with you, even if it were just a ramen place."
We've been together for three years, so I suppose it's natural that we're on the same wavelength.
"But even so, I'd rather you be delighted today in anticipation of tonight's full French course. Even I know when to give up and put a little more effort into looking respectable for others, okay?"
"What do you mean, give up? So you are forcing yourself after all, Haruki-kun!"
If we wanted to, we could easily make anyone around us think that we're an intimate couple where the girl is just a touch more assertive than the guy.
"I am forcing myself to some extent, but it's totally not in the way that you're thinking of, Setsuna!"
…If only we could have deceived ourselves like this as well, maybe there really could've been a happily ever after for the both of us.
"Looks like the snow isn't letting up."
Supporting her cheek with her left hand, Setsuna gazes at the falling snow outside the windows on her right.

They might be able to paint the sky right above the sea in pure white, but those tiny specks of snow prove powerless against the dark, unlit waters below, and are swallowed almost instantly on contact.
The movie has ended, and we're almost finished with our meal as well. It's a little before 9 PM, and I'm finally able to relax a bit.
Setsuna also seems to have reined in her excitement a little as well as she presents herself before me, and is starting to let her genuine feelings of slight listlessness show.
Saying that, she lifts her left hand that she's been resting her head against, and with the help of the candlelight in front of her, gives me a good view of her bracelet.
It seems that Setsuna thinks that's the reason I've been staring at her.
"Looks great on me, doesn't it? A wonderful guy gave it to me as a present, you know? …Does that bother you?"
"Mmm～ So you don't get jealous over stuff like that, Haruki-kun. That's a bit disappointing."
"It made me so, so happy! And it's got me more interested in that guy than ever before! …Still not jealous after that?"
"Yeah, I'm really jealous and bothered by that. I really feel the urge to meet the cool, rich, and handsome guy who gave you such an amazing present myself."
"Here he is, then. …Rich might not be the most accurate way to describe him, though."
"…Put the mirror away. We're still in the middle of our meal."
Reflected in that small mirror of hers is a gloomy-looking young man, his face turned to the side as if out of embarrassment.
…Let me take back what I saidーit doesn't seem as if she's reined in her excitement just yet.
"It's just a cheap product, you know."
She put on the Christmas present I gave her before dinner started almost immediately, and she still finds her right hand reaching for her left wrist from time to time.
"Didn't I tell you before? It doesn't take that much to win me over."
Even though I still haven't managed to deliver that passionate present I put so much of my heart into, she's already accepted the present I only decided upon within a day that easily.
Things don't always turn out the way you want them to, I suppose…
"You've already put me under your spell with this thing. To the point where I'm so moved that I'm having trouble swallowing this fancy dinner."
"I'm not sure if I should say that this arrangement wasn't very cost-efficient or if it had the opposite effect, then… still, are you okay?"
"You said you were having trouble swallowing, right? But the truth is, you haven't been eating much at all, have you?"
That's rightーwhat's really on my mind isn't the fact that there's a new accessory around Setsuna's left wrist.
Despite having made a comment about not forgetting popcorn when going to the cinema, she didn't even bring so much as a drink with her when we went inside.
As for our dinner, she did her best to finish the soup and salad, but she ended up leaving more than half of her main course on her plate long after it'd arrived.
And she's only had a sip of the wine, too. But above all else, the complexion of her face seems…
"You're actually not feeling well, are you? And despite that, you still came out during this big snowstorm and…"
"I feel just fine. No fever, either. Want to check for yourself?"
With both of her hands on the table for support, she leans forward and pokes her forehead out.
After some hesitation, I press my hand against her forehead. And as she said, it doesn't feel like she has a fever.
"I didn't eat much because I've been on a diet recently. A bit of pasta in the evening is usually enough to fill me up, so I'm already really full now."
"That's not good for your body. You should take care to get enough nutrients and…"
"I kept quiet about it because I knew you'd say that. …But it looks like I just made you even more worried instead."
"…You're really okay, right? You're not lying or anything, are you?"
"I'm about as fine as your wallet, I suppose?"
"…Are you trying to give me a heart attack? I thought I'd have to call an ambulance for a split second just now."
"Hehe… I guess we were both being a bit ostentatious just now."
It's not that it doesn't feel like she's trying to hide something, but regardless, she rejects my intervention with a devious smile on her face.
I can't tell if she's actually completely fine or if she's actually feeling a little ill just by looking at her, though.

What she did manage to get across to me, however, is that she wants to treasure the time we're spending together right now, even if it means she'll have to grin and bear through whatever is troubling her.
"That bracelet looks pretty nice. Where'd you get it?"
"I know, right! Do you want to know more about it?"
That's why I have no choice; I should at least do my very best to answer her feelings.
I don't care how forced or stupid I look doing itーI simply want to treasure the time I'm spending with Setsuna as well.
We've finished our dessert, and the table's been cleared as well. All that's left is our remaining chatter after our meal and the bill.
"There's… one more thing I want to give to you, Setsuna."
But to me, this is precisely the critical moment that I've spent all this time and money in preparation for.
"I've actually been wondering when you'd give it to me since before the movie started. …You're quite the tease, aren't you, Haruki-kun?"
"Sorry. I didn't mean to… Or maybe I did…"
Even though I'd decided from the very beginning to give it to her today, I ended up hesitating right before I was about to give it to her time and time again.
Because the time I spent with Setsuna today was so reminiscent of the past. Because the thoughts of wanting these moments to last have been clouding my mind the entire time.
And because I was afraid that everything would come to an end.
"This is the magazine that has my article in it. Having a part-timer write an article is actually quite rare, apparently."
"Wow, this is special. It's not everyday that I get to see you brag about something, Haruki-kun."
"That's because even I think this is quite an amazing achievement."
Perhaps I really shouldn't be talking about this to Setsuna, and only Setsuna. Perhaps the right thing to do was to continue hiding it from her.
If I don't want to shut the doors to a potential future with Setsuna, that is.
"This month's Ensemble magazine. Featuring a special article regarding a certain up-and-coming pianist…"
Still, on the other hand, Setsuna is the only person that I have to tell, no matter what. I have to let her know, no matter what.
If I want to open the door to a potential future with Setsuna, that is.
"The bit about Touma in last month's Kaiou Graph made some pretty big waves. It wasn't long until the music department wanted to have a feature article done on her."
"That's actually where I've been working. I pretended not to know anything when you called me about it last time… Sorry I couldn't tell you about it."
Setsuna finally flips open the first page and starts looking for my article.
"The person who wrote the article in Kaiou Graph is both my direct superior and employer."
To be honest, I don't know what my chances are.
"Said person's quite sharp, you see. They immediately found out that I used to go to school with Touma and came to talk to me right after."
This is no doubt going to be an important crossroad in our lives, and yet I don't have the slightest clue of what's about to happen. How many years has it been since I last felt like this?
"Basically, I got the assignment purely because of my connections."
I'm sure that the last time I felt like this, I had to make one of two choices, and one of those choices would've led to Setsuna accepting me with a smile.
"If Touma hadn't become so famous, there's no way that I could have ever gotten this assignment."
…But it was a choice I did not opt for. That's why it's a future that's been sealed away.
"So I used her to my advantage."
"Because I thought it'd help me secure a job in the future. Because I thought that it'd be a good experience to have."
