"Pffhaha… ahahahahaha… haha… Wha-What is all this…? You sure wrote some crazy stuff!"
After waiting so sternly for my sentence, what came out of her mouth was neither anger, mockery, sorrow, nor scolding.
"Which part…? It's a complete mess from beginning to end! Ah, ahaha… it's making my stomach hurt… ahaha…!"
"Like the part about her grades flying at low altitude for all three years."
"If we hadn't looked after her, there's no way she would have graduated."
"And the part about her thinking that her mother had abandoned her, so she acted like a delinquent the whole time."
"It was all just a misunderstanding. Them living together now being the proof of that."
"How her meals consisted solely of fast food and convenience store bought meals… And she also had a crazy sweet tooth, always putting five spoons of sugar into her coffee, you say!"
"That's all true. You saw it with your own eyes, didn't you, Setsuna?"
"Should you really be writing about things like that? Isn't Kazusa still just a budding pianist?"
Looking down, with her hands on her stomach, her body ever so slightly trembling.
It isn't what I expected, but it's the reaction I had hoped for.
"I was only playing to the crowd."
And so, I return a reaction that she definitely isn't hoping for.
"I thought it would generate a huge buzz if I wrote it like that. You looked like you really enjoyed it yourself too, Setsuna."
As if trying to provoke her, I keep saying things that further erase the smile from Setsuna's face.
"That's all Touma Kazusa is to me right now. Someone I can write an article on to shock the world and make my name known."
And just like that, little by little, I delve deeper and deeper into Setsuna's and my wounds.
"It finally dawned on me after I took on this assignment. My feelings toward her have changed before I knew it."
It might look like I'm not putting much thought into it, but I'm choosing my words very, very carefully.
"So I just wrote the truth. Not just the good things, but the bad things as well. Actually, I might have even over-emphasized the bad stuff."
Pushing everything onto someone who isn't here, all for the sake of building a new relationship between us.
"Does it upset you? Me treating Touma so awfully like this?"
…In other words, just like I said, I'm using Kazusa.
"Seeing me writing these things and making fun of our best friend like this, does it make you think I'm a cold-hearted person?"
Setsuna might take my side, or she might defend Kazusa, and put the blame on me.
I've created a perfectly safe situation where I can handle whatever choice she decides to make.
Is she so mad that she can't even speak? Is she so hurt that she's at a loss for words? Or is she… desperately searching for a reason to absolve me from blame?
"Of course not. There's no way you would do something like that, Haruki-kun."
As if. There was hardly any point in making up all those possibilities just now. It was obvious that she would make the most foolish choice of them all anyway.
After all, Setsuna is never against me. No matter what happens, she'll always take my side.
If that wasn't the case, it'd be unthinkable for her to have stayed by my side all this time, ever since that day three years ago.
"…No, you did a good job. This is definitely the impression that Kazusa gives to people."
"I feel bad for Kazusa, but it's all true! I'm sorry, it's just too funny. You did a great job."
"Yeah, and it's even more interesting when you know her in person, too. Haha… I accept this with gratitude. And once again, congratulations."
But this time, Setsuna's way of covering up for me brings a slightly stronger feeling of uneasiness than usual.
"It feels a little unreal, doesn't it? We used to be best friends with someone who's now a celebrity you can find being featured in magazines."
Almost as if she was about to say something but nervously choked it back down right before saying it.
"No, we're still best friends now, aren't we? Even now, us three are still together, aren't we?"
Her words sound so carefree and unlike what she usually says. It's as if she doesn't know what she really wants to say and is only hiding behind an insincere smile.
"The snow's let up a bit… Want to go out for a walk?"
"Takeya-kun's definitely out on a date right now too, right? What did he say?"
As if. I wanted to just play it off like nothing happened, but my heart felt like it was about to pop out of my chest.
Th-Tha…That asshole…! He purposefully kept that from me the whole time, didn't he!?
"…The snow's let up a bit, so let's go for a walk."
"…But I invited you to do that just now."
"…It's only natural for the guy to be the one doing the inviting."
"It finally feels like a white Christmas now. …It looked more like a snowstorm until a little while ago."
Perhaps because the snow's lightened up to a point where it's finally suitable for walking outside…
Around us, dozens of couples are roaming about with linked arms or held hands, enjoying their evening walks and the scenery of snow slowly drifting into the sea.
I might ruin the mood if I tried doing something like that myself, but the couples around us don't seem embarrassed at all, paying no mind to our stares.
"Hey, doesn't it feel like we're on a date?"
"Instead of 'I guess,' you're supposed to answer with 'Well, it's a date after all,' don't you think?"
Treating the people around me like air in such a way isn't something I'm capable of doing.
I'd definitely end up making it embarrassing and awkward like I did just now.
"Jeez～! Why can't you read the mood? Stop being so reserved already. This is like a sacred place for couples, you know?"
"I didn't come here because I wanted to."
"I've always been this kind of person, haven't I? Stiff, plain, and a complete bore to be around."
…If I suddenly became all defiant about it like that, she'd probably bring up stuff like the dinner bill again, so there's no way I can say it out loud.
"Yeah, you have. And that's exactly what I liked about you."
"Ah… Pretty poor taste you have there."
But even if I make tasteless comments like these, Setsuna still replies so charmingly as if she hasn't caught on to the mood at all, and keeps driving me into a corner.
"If the roads end up freezing over today, we'll have a tough day ahead of us tomorrow."
"Too bad snow in Tokyo turns black almost instantly."
"Brings back memories of that Christmas three years ago, doesn't it?"
Setsuna is ignoring the mood on purpose, and she isn't letting me downplay the situation no matter how hard I try to.
"It was snowing back then too. It was a white Christmas back then, right?"
"It certainly didn't have the same feel to it though, location-wise."
"I know, right! A Japanese-style room, yukata, and an open air hot springs bath. You couldn't find a hint of Christianity there at all."
Setsuna is laughing pleasantly and in approval beside me.
It's because she thinks poking fun at our current topic is the right choice.
"Kazusa in the driver's seat, racing through the snow at a million miles an hour, before doing a few graceful spins and crashing into the wall of snow."
"That was definitely the scariest and most embarrassing day I've ever experienced in my life."
After all, it happened to trigger a switch that reawakened memories long pastーmy switch, and likely her own as well.
"Is that all? So it wasn't the greatest treat for your eyes that you've ever experienced in your life?"
"The flawless skin of two young maidens～!"
"I was dead drunk, so I don't remember anything!"
"Liar～! You looked like you sobered up the instant we got in."
"You were pretty drunk yourself too, weren't you, Setsuna? You shouldn't trust those hazy memories of yours."
"Oh, so I was drunk already? If you remembered that, then I guess you must have been sober after all, Haruki-kun."
"So you still remember, huh? My naked body back then?"
"Come on, let's not talk about these embarrassing things…"
"But it's too bad. My skin's probably not as smooth as it was back then anymore…"
"…That's not true, you know. Absolutely not. Your skin is still smooth even now. …Though it's not like I've actually confirmed it or anything."
"…Hearing you say it so passionately makes me both happy and embarrassed. Hehe."
"Let's drop it already. Everyone's staring at us."
Our loud voices stood out so much that we began drawing annoyed glares from the couples around us.
But that only means that we created a world just for ourselves, where we were able to tune out the couples around us.
"No, I won't drop it. It's the same day as it was back then, and the same snow that fell upon us back then too, after all."
That's why we ignore the couples around us and simply continue to talk about things that aren't merely enjoyable.
"I… don't really like it or dislike it."
This is something that I can't just laugh off. More importantly, it's a question that I absolutely cannot ask her in return.
After all, the snow had always been falling upon us whenever we stood at the crossroads that divided our fates.
"Don't you still remember it? The snow we saw outside the car's windows back then?"
The snow that fell as I embraced Kazusa, knowing that I would never be forgiven.
"How about the snow that piled up outside the inn? We all just sat there drinking, blankly staring out the windows."
The snow that Setsuna saw as she looked up through the window the very moment I betrayed her.
"How about the snow that just kept falling and falling, even though it melted as soon as it touched the water?"
And there was the time I was urged by Setsuna to look for Kazusa.
There was the snow that hid the long-departed airplane during the tiny period of time when I had all traces of Setsuna's existence erased from my heart.
"The same snow as it was back then" didn't only refer to the snow that fell on Christmas.
"I, you see, I… To me, snow is…"
"Let's stop associating the snow with what happened three years ago. The snow that's falling today isn't the same as the snow that fell back then."
"What's the difference? It's just as white, just as cold… and just as beautiful."
"That's not what I mean. What I'm trying to say is…"
What I'm really afraid of isn't her associating the snow with what happened three years ago.
"Are you saying that… it's because Kazusa was still here to watch the snow fall back then?"
But rather, her associating it with her memories of Kazusa.
"Hey, Haruki-kun. Do you still love the snow? And… do you still… love Kazusa?"
"Didn't I say it already? I've already forgotten about Touma."
…No problem. I've run this simulation in my head a million times, haven't I?
I didn't stutter a single word, nor did I come off as unnaturally cold.
"So could you stop being so fixated on what happened three years ago? …If you're willing to forgive what I did, that is."
With a natural, but slightly forceful tone of voice, I try to let her know that while it might hurt a little, everything that I'm saying isn't a lie.
"It's because of what happened three years ago that we're able to be here now…"
"There's nothing left of it to me, though. All that remains is the weight of the sin I have committed."
"Yes… The grave, indelible sin of having betrayed you, Setsuna."
"No such thing remains! You never committed any sin, Haruki-kun. There was no such thing from the very beginning!"
"You know that's not true. You know the extent of how much I've hurt you, Setsuna…"
"That's only because I stole a march on her despite knowing how both of you felt… Any pain I feel is just retribution for my selfish actions."
"See? How about we just stop? We'll just end up drowning ourselves in guilt at this rate."
As expected, I had to use an unusual method to prevent our conversation from continuing toward its expected direction.
"Setsuna… Why don't we just start over?"
"Start over…? You mean forget about everything that ever happened? That's… I, but that's…"
"No. What we'll be forgetting is the day when the three of us came together."
And all that will be left are memories of Setsuna.
My memory of meeting Setsuna and finding her again on the roof.

My memory of being entranced by her voice and trying my best to convince her. My memory of going so far as to take advantage of her weak points, and intruding upon Setsuna's true faceーone that no one had ever seen before.
My memory of finally getting her to agree to be my songstress, and taking her hand out of sheer happiness.
"Let's forget all about it. The snow that fell back then, and… her, as well."
And what comes after that will be a completely original story featuring only the two of us.
We're the only two left in the Light Music ClubーMe, the guitarist, and Setsuna, the singer. Together, we only managed a boring, unexciting, and overall mediocre performance.

But even so, we were more than satisfied with the results. And later, at our two-person after-party, our hands and lips eventually joined together before we knew it because the mood felt right somehow.
It's almost too good of a deal for me. You could call it the very epitome of opportunism.
The ultimate solution that would erase the guilt that's been burdening both Setsuna and myself.
"Are you… going to forget about Kazusa? Can you forget her?"
But haven't we had enough already?
Haven't I had enough of persisting with my sins, and hasn't Setsuna had enough of denying them?
We've been repeating these heart-wrenching conflicts for three years now, and we're more than exhausted from it all.
"We might not be able to come to terms with it immediately. I'll need some time to forgive myself as well."
"So let's just take it slowly. We can keep in contact with texts and calls. …Can't we?"
"You know I can't say no to that."
"Why is the hand you're extending toward me so gentle despite how cruel your words are?"
The promise to forget Kazusa and one day choose Setsuna…
Is something that should have been fulfilled long ago… A promise that remained unfulfilled for three years due to the rather poor way we handled things with one another.
"Even though it's wrong… Even though it's the most awful choice possible… I just can't go against what you just said, Haruki-kun."
"I'll repay you in time… Wait, that sounds weird, doesn't it? We just started over after all. Let's just try to get to know each other more, okay?"
Sneaking a look at Setsuna's downcast face, I can see a blush that surely isn't a result of the cold.
Her teary eyes, unsteady breathing, and shivering lips… Her expression reminds me of the moment right after one of our kisses from long ago.
The alluring, captivating, and evocative instability in her expression, normally hidden behind her pure and composed exterior, is enough to drive any man crazy.
If you show me something as amazing as this, I…
Because at this rate, I won't be able to hold myself back much longer.
I'll end up throwing away the plans I made when I was still calm and lose myself to my desires.
"I'll take you hom… Well, we're both going the same way, so that's a given. I hope the trains haven't stopped."
"Let's go, Setsuna. The station's that way, right?"
With a pained expression accompanied by a vivid blush, Setsuna stares me directly in the eye.
Unable to stand looking into those dangerous eyes that could almost suck me in at any moment, I hastily turn my face away, returning to the path from which I arrived.
Setsuna doesn't follow me as I cowardly retreat.
She turns her pained expression into something akin to a young girl's pout and casts an accusatory glare at me.
Her girlish and childish expression has spread to her way of speech, and through it, her thoughts are delivered to my ears.
First, the unreasonable bits of selfishness you would expect from a young girl.
"Watching a movie, having dinner, and taking a walk in the park… You can't just leave after making me steel my resolve so much."
And then, without changing her manner of speech, her words alone become those of a woman.
"That's… I'm sorry for inviting you out to a place like this. But I had my reaso…"
"You can't be apologizing for that. You said we would treat everything up until today as if it had never happened."
"That's why I'm saying we should just talk for today and…?"
Getting tricked by her way of speech and carelessly letting the distance between us shorten again was a fatal mistake.
"I haven't given you a present yet, Haruki-kun. I got such a wonderful gift from you, and yet I haven't given you anything in return."
"…Don't worry about it. It was something I decided all on my own."
"Just kidding～ I actually came empty-handed on purpose. Just so I wouldn't be able to give you something in return."
Because I can see it in her eyes.
"I… told them that I would be staying over."
I can see an extremely alluring charm within them, concealing something all too dangerous amidst its cuteness and selfishness, a sight capable of luring any man into the abyss.
"This is what I've prepared in return. An inevitable substitute for the present I forgot to buy."
"Something incredibly mundane, and incredibly selfish. It's something that I'm forcing on to you."
I'm no stranger to this, though…
"Will you accept it despite all that?"
An aggressive and unexpected sneak attack. The signature move of the mischievous Setsuna…
"I meant to give it to you three years ago, and to this day, the wrapping is still intact. Myself."
To the man I am now after these three years, it's more than enough to drive me crazy.
"I, I… don't know how long I should keep this up."
"I've done my best these past three years, you know? I've been restraining myself, and only taking slow, careful steps toward you."
"But I couldn't shorten the distance between us at all! I couldn't even get close enough to touch you like this…"
"Haah… Yeah… I couldn't do this at all."
And so, "like this," we can now feel each other's touch.
Just like how I was about to be sucked into her eyes, Setsuna found herself fully drawn into my chest.
If I hide her captivating expression inside my chest like this, all that's left are the selfish, albeit excruciating cries of a spoiled child.
"It's so warm… The snow doesn't feel cold anymore, and neither does the wind. All because you're here to warm me up, Haruki-kun."
But this actually calms me down. …In a different way compared to how Setsuna's feeling, probably.
"Until now, no matter how slowly we got closer to each other, we always ended up running away right before we could reach each other. You and me both, Haruki-kun."
But we can feel each other's touch now.
And so, Setsuna, maybe because she never wants to leave again, brings herself deeper and deeper into my embrace.
"I'm the one who should be apologizing."
"You can't… If you apologize like that, you'll make it seem like I'm innocent."
"If everything I've done has been right, then I won't be able to accomplish what I want to do right now. …That's why I'm the one at fault."
Setsuna's warmth, softness, and charm has… once again seeped into me, bringing my entire body under her spell.
"So before I have time to rethink things, and before my resolve fades, make me yours."
My mind, still calm, is desperately sending me warnings, saying that if I really value Setsuna, it's even more of a reason for me to not go through with this.
"I want you to relieve me of this pain."
Because Setsuna's not herself right now. She's forcing herself more than she needs to, doing everything she can to get closer to me.
Indeed, forcing herself way too much.
Too obsessed with trying to accept me, she hasn't realized that her own feelings have yet to catch up with her actions.
We didn't need to rush this. We had more than enough time.
However, the long and painful suffering that Setsuna went through until now had left her no other choice.
…So I guess, in the end, it's my fault after all.
But, if you were to compare it, this is without a doubt the wrong decision.
A substantially riskier choice among all the other alternatives. Like taking a powerful medicine with vicious side effects to treat an ailment.
Unfortunately, thinking about things like that is meaningless.
"Haah… ah… It's been a while, hasn't it?"
My body lets out screams of ecstasy as I help myself to Setsuna's lips.
"It's gotten harder to reach you, even on my tiptoes… You got a lot taller, Haruki-kun."
"Did I…? I only recall not really knowing what to do in the past and just bending down to your height."
"So that's what happened… hehe. You were always so kind and gentle, even when I couldn't notice it."
"Am I… not being gentle right now?"
"Yeah, you were so incredible, so intense. Not like a boy, but a man…"
I squeezed Setsuna's lower lip with my lips, moved my tongue about and licked at hers greedily.
I wasn't being gentle at all. Even though it's been so long since the last time, and precisely because it's been so long since then, I couldn't control myself at all.
"But, but… There are some things that haven't changed at all."
"Your left eye tooth… whenever we kiss, I can always feel it a little."
"Brings back memories… I'm… really kissing you again, aren't I… Haruki-kun?"
This time, I unhesitatingly stick my tongue in her mouth and skilfully explore the slippery texture inside.
"Ha, ah, nchu… mm… ah, npu, nn!"
After that, I suck her tongue into my mouth, attacking it in every way possible with my tongue, lips, and teeth.
"Haa… ah, haa, ahn… ha, ah, ah, ahaaaa…"
More intensely than just moments before, and much more intensely than I did three years ago, I send Setsuna even deeper into a trance with my passion-filled kiss.
"Haa, haa, haa… Ah, aah… Haruki-kun… I, I…"
"Haruki-kun… If you say you want to start over and forget what happened with the three of us back then…"
Beyond any of our choices lie even more decisions. Before we can even see the full consequences of our previous choice, we're confronted with even more unknowns.
"Then I… I have to take back these three years of emptiness."
The situation is progressing far faster than I can keep up with.
"I have to hurry and turn back into the me that loved you so, so, so, so much, Haruki-kun. The spoiled girl that couldn't stand being away from you for even a single second."
"Room number 1732. A little Christmas present from me to you. Don't worry, I paid for it already."
That's why… I don't know what's safe and what's not anymore.
I'm simply staying true to my desires…
I only know that I'm taking the path that my instincts demand me to.
I can see that it's still snowing through the window.
But the snow I see now seems lighter, as if it'll stop at any second.
A clear night view takes form as both the sea covered in a deep black and the bridge decorated in a dazzling white come into sight below me.
But no matter how much I force myself to enjoy this scenery through the windows of a high-rise, I can't quell the disturbances in my emotions right now.
As if I bet all my chips on black and can only sit and watch as the roulette spins, impatience and unbelievable amounts of excitement flood my mind.
When I got in the room with Setsuna just now… Even I was amazed at myself for being able to hold myself back.
Even as I suggested that she take a shower first, it was tearing me apart since I really wanted to just embrace her and make her mine right then and there.
Even now, I can't guarantee that seeing Setsuna walk out of the bathroom dripping wet won't awaken some sort of primal beast within me.
First, I should hold her down with my entire body, so that she can't fight back. After that, should I forcefully attack her, or should I gradually tease her…?
I might even be licking my lips thinking about scary things like that. I can't trust myself to act rational at all.
I've completely strayed from my initial goals. Right now, I can't see myself treating her with gentlemanly sincerity.
I can't do this. I can't do something that will only bring her discomfort.
But Setsuna, on the other hand, didn't shy away at all, even during the check-in.
As I shakily wrote down "Iizuka Takeya" onto the sheet, she unreservedly pressed up right against me, burying her face in my shoulder, not trying to hide what we came to this hotel for at all.
And when I struggled to come up with a second fake name, she took the pen from me and promptly wrote down "Mizusawa Io" right beside it.
Having forced down a few mouthfuls of cola, I let out a few carbonic acid-laden breaths.
I need to calm down. I need… to be gentle.
I can't turn back now. I have to go through with it.
But if that's the case, then no matter what, I can't let Setsuna leave here with painful memories.
Once morning comes, I want to smile and take comfort in knowing that the path I chose was the right one.
There's someone here to witness this desperate and pathetic side of me, with the same cold expression as always.
Because Setsuna couldn't fit it in her bag, I held on to the copy of Ensemble.
On the cover is a woman with long, black hair, wearing a black dress.
The color is just as reminiscent of a crow's sheen as it always has been.
"Stop looking at me with those eyes. You're always, always making fun of me like this."
And the fact that you always look so cool while doing so makes me even angrier.
Past the colored pages at the beginning, I can see her solo performance.
Kazusa, the piano, and the stage. The spotlight, the audience seats, and Kazusa again.
What's with this fulfilled look of immersion on your face?
Ecstatically playing the piano like this. You only showed me that side of you one single time.
…But I fell asleep in the middle of it, so I can't even remember it too well.
I'm… glad that you went to Europe.
I'm glad you found success. Gaining all this fame is simply… amazing.
Unlike amateurs such as myself, you're surrounded by people that truly understand your value. I'm… really glad…
You're a celebrity? A budding pianist showered with expectation? A thoroughbred blessed with beauty, talent, and lineage?
Stop making me laugh, you delinquent.
If I hadn't been there to guide you on the right track, right now you'd just be some shut-in going through life as you please with your mother's money.
This is so ridiculous, so idiotic…
These bits of dry laughter are all I can manage…
"He said he loved me back too. He… wanted me."
"So there's nothing standing between us. …We're only doing things that we naturally should be."
"Uncertainty? Not a shred of it. Regret? There's no way I would. Because I've forgotten all about what happened in the past."
"Today, I'm going to be taking Haruki-kun from you."
"I'm not going to hand him over to anyone anymore."
"It's okay. Let's take it slowly. We have plenty of time until morning anyway."
"…Ah, umm… H-Haruki-kun, you know, the shower…"
"…Yeah, you're right. Sorry, that was careless of me."
"Give me a few minutes. I won't take long."
"No, you can take your time. We have plenty of time before morning comes, right?"
"Should I just take it off now?"
"…Or maybe it's better if I wait for him to take it off for me?"
"～! I, I guess I'll get a drink after all."
"Sorry, Kazusa. Don't look at me now."
It's almost time… Tonight will mark the end…
We'll be able to be at ease from tomorrow onward. It'll really be just the two of us.
Since, well… nobody treats their own body as a burden, right? Nobody has ever collapsed under their own weight, right?
So if Setsuna becomes my other half, then I won't feel burdened anymore.
Both Setsuna and I will finally be free from the curse we placed on ourselves.
Today's the day that I'm going to forget you. From now on, I'll be writing my history with Setsuna, and only Setsuna.
This should have come about much earlier, really.
If you had just ignored me from the start, we would have been living much more happily than we are now.
…Yeah, right. Pinning the blame on you when it's really all my fault is pretty terrible of me.
But I won't apologize to you, okay?
Because while I'm the one who made Setsuna cry, you betrayed her with me as well, didn't you?

"This does seem like the kind of sarcasm Haruki-kun would use."

"…You two are going to be held back a year because you keep hanging around me, you know?"
"What are you saying? You've got it backward. You're the one that's going to graduate because you keep hanging around us."
"After the school festival is over, we'll tutor you personally, all right? I'm confident that I'm better at English than Haruki-kun is, at least."
"At any rate, our graduations and recommendations are pretty much guaranteed, so we'll be sticking with you through each and every supplementary exam you've got."
"There's no one here quite as stupid as you are, Touma."
"You're awful, Haruki-kun. You're always badmouthing Kazusa whenever you talk about her."

"She was the first person to ever take my guitar playing seriously."

"When Kazusa had first arrived at the school, due to the tension from the multitude of conflicts between her and her classmates and teachers, it only took a few days for her to be completely isolated from her surroundings."
"However, her high aspirations that wouldn't allow for compromises in the lectured material, practice schedule, and the level of her performance was also an important deciding factor."
"Touma Kazusa had inherited not only the incredible talent but also the troublesome attitude of her mother, Touma Youko."
"I said that although her personality is bad, the fact that she can't follow through with her cruelty due to her kind nature was interesting…"
"Who cares about her reputation or what rumors there are? The truth is, Touma's a really kind person deep down. Man, it's so frustrating that no one understands this…"
"The isolated and overly emotional Kazusa followed in the footsteps of the wild and equally emotional Youko, and chose not to restrict herself to Japan's musical world."
"But it's because of this that she was able to meet Youko's former mentor, Martin Flugel, who helped her talents bloom so beautifully."
"All we can really do is… respect her decision."
"That's why I'll… see her off with a smile, just like she wants us to."
"Currently, she's living in a detached house in the suburbs of Vienna. Along with her teacher, rival, and mother with whom she'd once cut all ties, Touma Youko."
"What footsteps will this budding talent leave behind in the world? You'll find the answers to that in the future endeavors of Touma Kazusa."
"And, at the end, an impudent postscript."
"Be it Kazusa herself, or the people watching over her journey from now on, they should all offer their gratitude to a certain person."
"No matter how much Touma Kazusa herself might deny this, if it were not for Touma Youko, she would not be who she is now. Both as an artist, and as a person in general."
Opening the bathroom door, I found the room exactly as I had left it: dimly lit and dead silent.
Setsuna seems to have seated herself on the bed, with her face turned away from me.
As I try to get a peek at her face after slowly circling her, she turns away even more.
Is she doing this out of embarrassment or some other emotion…?
As someone who's desperately trying to hold back his own emotions, I can't seem to tell.
She does give me a response in the form of her head shaking, but she's still unwilling to look in my direction.
She doesn't seem to be scared. She doesn't seem embarrassed, either.
But Setsuna looks visibly different from how she was ten minutes ago.
My hand that reaches out to her cheek in an attempt to get her to face me is slapped away almost instantly.
It was so far removed from what I had expected that it felt as if time stood still for a brief moment.
And yet, Setsuna didn't panic and say something along the lines of "I didn't mean that" like she always does.
Which means that she really did mean what she just did.
I've realized that Setsuna is rejecting me.
Kneeling beside the bed, I take a look at Setsuna's face from below.
The flushed red skin she had when she got out of the bath is gone, and replacing it is a porcelain-white complexion coupled with an ice-cold expression.
In contrast to the coolness of the rest of her body, her downcast eyes look heated and reddened…
Her swollen eyes are, without a doubt, a result of a particular thing that was left on the side of the bed.
Kazusa's gaze is set on both of us as she remains within the picture.
Should the person we don't want looking at us the most happen to stare at what we're about to do, we will definitely feel disturbed in some way, even if only a little.
So when her delicate hand gently pins down my hand as I hurriedly try to close the magazine…
An ominous premonition of impending punishment strikes my core, stopping me dead in my tracks.
It's only been ten minutes since I last heard Setsuna's voice, and yet it sounds so frail nowーso brittle.
Her feelings of uncertainty were laid bare for me to see.
"I've read this article dozens of times already. …I bought it the day it went on sale, you see."
In truth, it wasn't entirely beyond the realm of possibility.
It shouldn't have taken much to realize that Setsuna wouldn't miss a magazine that had Kazusa, of all people, on the cover.
"Especially the parts from page 12 to page 16. The bits detailing the time from her upbringing, all the way until she left Japan."
That's why even the fact that she's able to pinpoint the portions I was responsible for so easily should have been within my expectations.
"I've gone through it countless times. And every single time, I would start with a bitter smile and then start laughing out loud as it got sillier."
"And by the time I finished, I would always be drenched in tears."
"Hey, Haruki-kun… Answer me one more time."
The fact that she can't quite believe what I'm saying should have been obvious as well.
I need to put an end to this.
I should just stay silent, take her in my arms, gently pat her head and just stay by her side until she calms down…
"It's been three years already… All memories fade away with time."
Though the truth is that I can'tーtrying to trick someone without using words just isn't the way I communicate with others.
"Yeah, it took a whole three years… And in that time, I made you go through some truly painful experiences. I'm really sorry…"
That's why I have to use every word I know. I need to get her to accept what I say from the bottom of her heart.
Before I touch her body, I first have to touch her heart…
Once more, I tried to reach toward her face, and once more, my hand was pushed away, with a greater force this time.
"What do you mean, you forgot? What do you mean, they've faded away?"
But even if I'm using every word I can, if those words can't reach her, trying to touch her heart is…
"What part of you has changed at all these past three years, Haruki-kun…!?"
"Ugh, I'll just be honest with you, alright?"
Setsuna's no longer the same woman who so unabashedly entrusted her body to me as we entered the hotel.
"Since you won't tell me the truth, I'm going to snap now, okay?"
Finally facing me with her red, swollen eyes, she unhesitatingly rejects me, as if she's given everything up.
"I've read this article dozens of times. And every time I did, I laughed, and I cried…"
"Both my heart and body ached unbearably… And I'd spend the night alone hugging myself."
"After all… what you're saying hasn't changed at all. It's the same as when you went chasing after Kazusa back then."
"What…? There's no way something like that…"
Because I can't just trick her with an embrace anymore. Because the only thing I'm good at is defeating others with my words.
"I used her. I sold her out. I was just trying to get attention, so I wrote a silly and interesting article full of me badmouthing her, and…"
"With an article so filled with love? With an article overflowing with your feelings for Kazusa!?"
…But all it took was a single sentence from her to silence me.
"That's right… You were always speaking ill of Kazusa."
"You always felt embarrassed or proud, almost like you were talking about yourself…"
"It all seemed like insults at first, but you were also trying your best to defend her at the same time, and you tried to hide your embarrassment behind your excessive preaching at the end of it."
"This… This article… it's using the same words you used back then, Haruki-kun…!"
Even though words of rebuttal are coming to mind, my mouth refuses to say them.
"After making me read such a touching love letter, just how do you expect me to accept all this…?"
That wasn't what I had meant to do at all.
I just wanted them to use my article.
To exaggerate it a little bit, and if it came out poorly, just make something up. All I wanted was to make myself look good with it.
It had nothing to do with my feelings for Kazusa; I just wrote down a bunch of stuff that was well suited for a story.
You didn't have to go so far as to call out the lie I'd fabricated for myself, did you…?
"When I came out of the bathroom just now… Your face looked like that of a child who was caught red-handed doing something awful."
That must have been because I was hurriedly trying to hide it under the bed.
"I didn't realize the reason immediately… but I figured it out before you came back out."
The article that she's read countless times, through laughter and tears… The article that I wrote myself, that somehow still manages to make my heart waver.
"Haruki-kun. You were talking to Kazusa just now, weren't you?"
"You had Kazusa give you a push on your back, didn't you?"
"You got the courage to give up on Kazusa from Kazusa herself, didn't you?"
My message took the form of a feature article dedicated to her, and I've been talking to her with it ever since.
"You got encouragement from Kazusa just so you could embrace me, didn't you?"
Even now, her picture on the cover of Ensemble looks like she's making fun of me, but at the same time, unemotionally encouraging me.
That's why… I can no longer refute Setsuna's words.
"Even after all these years… you're just going to keep lying to me, aren't you?"
Because she has found out that everything has been a lie.

"That's what you planned all along, wasn't it? Fortifying the memories that you had no way of forgetting with lies of having forgotten them already, and just spending the rest of your days in a mindless daze."
Because the lie that doing this was for both our sakes ended up actually hurting one of us.
Yet again, it's all my fault.
It's the night of Christmas Eve, and the date is about to change.
The snow that was piling up on the streets a while ago is now simply continuing to pile up.
I can peek at the stars through the slits between the clouds, but in a place as lit up as this, only a few are actually visible.
The lights in the nearby station are still lit, signalling the fact that I still have a means to get home.
As if warmly welcoming me after I've been miserably forced out of this place full of lovers.
As I slowly make my way toward the station, I can hear the sound of the snow that's just beginning to freeze over being crushed beneath me.
But aside from that, I can't hear anything else, creating an illusion of me being the only person left in the world, which I couldn't be more thankful for.
After all, the snow that's piled up is willing to drown out any other sound for me.
Tell me, snow… since you're already going so far, would you be willing to listen to one last selfish wish of mine?
Could you drown out the wailing that's been resounding in my heart, too? It's been getting on my nerves with how loud it's been for a while now…
"Why did it turn out like this…?"
"My beloved was willing to lie to himself just to face me."
"He was willing to silence his own feelings just to repay me."
"The feelings I've been holding on to for these three years were finally about to bear fruit."
"I thought that would have been enough."
"I thought that as long as my feelings were answered, it would have been enough."
"So why… why did it turn out like this…?"
"The next train for Line 3 is scheduled to arrive at 12:55 AM. This will be the final train of the day. Please take care not to miss it."
Thanks to the snow messing up the schedule, I made it in time for the last train of the day.
But because of the snow messing up the schedule, transfers are going slowly, so I'm forced to wait at this station for fifteen minutes.
I rest myself on the seat that I somehow managed to obtain and stare at the floor, but I can't even last a single minute before standing back up again.
If neither the scenery around me nor my body itself are moving, all kinds of unnecessary thoughts will start popping up in my head.
In an attempt to distract myself, I flip open my cell phone with no real purpose in mind and start randomly pushing buttons.
While doing everything I can to avoid the "Messages" button…
It's not just Setsuna. I'm sure Takeya and Io must have noticed as well.
That no matter how much time passes, I can't let go of my feelings for Kazusa. They've become something that's simply impossible for me to forget.
Even so, Takeya and Io… as well as other unrelated people have continued to encourage me and urge Setsuna to move forward, all because they failed to notice one other truth.
They've failed to notice that I've been constantly hurting Setsuna, even now, over the fact that I've never forgotten about Kazusa.
Because she knows Kazusa just as well as I do. …Because she loves Kazusa just as much as I do.
It's because of those things that there's no way she would have missed Kazusa's presence inside me.
Whenever she tries to dig her way into my heart, she always finds herself face to face with the memories of Kazusa that reside there.
All the times I tried to force those memories out and put on a smile must have only seemed like pictures drawn over glass to her.
I can no longer walk beside her ever againーis that what this means?
That I can't walk beside this one person and this one person alone in the world, Ogiso Setsuna?
If said person wasn't Setsuna, I would surely be able to forget about Kazusa one day.
How, you ask…? The answer's easy. I'd just need to bury my thoughts about Kazusa deep inside, without forgetting them, and just find a new love instead.
Because if that were to happen, then the person by my side wouldn't notice how forced my smile actually is.
Even if I start remembering the past and end up being hurt because of it, she would be oblivious to the reason and simply smile and cheer me up.
So in time, she would slowly fill my heart, the pain from recalling Kazusa would dull, and eventually, she would take the number one place in my heart instead.
"Ignorance is bliss" isn't a phrase I particularly like, but…
By following this phrase, time would solve everything… if it was someone other than Setsuna.
"The train on Line 3 is approaching. Please stand behind the yellow line."
Because if it was Setsuna, there's no way we could make it through the transition.
If I reminisce about the past, if I end up hurting because of it, it'll just bounce between us, back and forth, hurting us more and more…
And just like today, we'd come to a standstill, both of us having lost the courage to move forward.
Surely Kazusa must have forgotten all about someone like me… She might have even forgotten Setsuna as well.
And yet we're still so hung up about the "three" of us, sending our foolish selves down this path of self-destruction.
There are things that can't be resolved even if you love the person.
I hate those words from the bottom of my heart.
But perhaps not being together anymore would be for the…
As if trying to match the train's rumbling noise in a chaotic harmony, I erupt in a voice resembling a scream.
I don't want to think about coming to any kind of conclusion about all this, so I should have just stopped thinking about it altogether, but…
Setsuna's smile, Setsuna's sighs, and Setsuna's face drenched in tears…
These images keep popping up in my head one after another, forcing my emotions to helplessly wander in all sorts of directions.
I want to feel warmth. I want to meet someone.
I want to connect with someone…
2. I'll show up at the editing department.
3. I can't be thinking about these things.
There's no way I'd be able to find anyone this late on Christmas Eve.
Furthermore, the very act of seeking out someone is simply unforgivable, considering how Setsuna must be going through what I'm going through right now as well.
In the end, after missing the last train at Onjuku, I took a taxi and went straight back to my apartment.
Without even turning on the lights, I collapsed onto my bed.
My body, having been chilled by the touch of the snow, is slowly returning to its normal temperature.
But even though my body is regaining its warmth, a single part of meーthe deepest part of my chestーis still ice cold.
There still seems to be some creaking somewhere in there.
Even so, it's still screaming out that I don't want to be alone.
"Both my heart and body ached unbearably… And I'd spend the night alone hugging myself."
So this is how it feels. This sucks… I guess this means I won't be able to fall asleep.
As if I've caught a terrible cold, every nerve in my body is pulsing with pain, and neither warming it up nor rubbing the pain away seems to ease my shivering body.
Gritting my teeth so hard that I can hear them grinding, I grasp my trembling body with both hands, but find myself unable to close my eyes.
Because if I submerge myself in true darkness, it will come back to me again.
The sight of Setsuna's face drenched in tears that I saw at the very last moment will always come back to haunt me.
For more than two weeks from now on…

I won't have to go to university, nor am I scheduled for any work at my part-time jobs; the "free time" that I loathe more than anything right now just so happens to strike me when I need to be rid of it the most.
I wonder how I'm supposed to spend my time from tomorrow onward.
Should I fill this loneliness, or should I just accept it head-on…?
I'm sure Setsuna's going through a sleepless night right now as well.
It's my fault, and it's Setsuna's fault. The two of us are being devoured by a vicious feeling of loneliness.
…We really are a good match, aren't we?
My voice is trembling because of the pain. It's definitely not because I'm holding back my tears.
Neither of those facts really change how miserable I am at the moment, but it doesn't mean a guy like me should be crying so easily.
It might be an old-fashioned way of looking at it, and I might even be laughed at because of it in this day and age, but there still exist people willing to acknowledge that side of Kitahara Haruki.
Once again… I wish you good night, Setsuna.
It'd be nice if we could both end up getting some sleep. It'd be nice if we could end up having pleasant dreams.
At the very least, in our dreams… it'd be nice if we could just stay in each other's embrace until dawn comes.
Christmas Day was nothing more than an ordinary winter day after Christmas Eve had passed.

The snow had stopped piling up by the time dawn arrived and only served to deliver the chill of winter and hinder the steps of passersby. By noon, it had completely dissolved into blackened slush that merged into the ground.
…I can't deny the possibility that my own mental state is responsible for my currently cynical outlook.
And today's just another ordinary winter dayーit's not even Christmas anymore.
It's been over a day since I returned home.
I'd spent a whole night engraving the period of the dark sky gradually brightening outside the window in my mind; I then came to the clear realization that nights are not eternal.
Watching a day of the sky covered with clouds darkening in real time also made me remember that daylight doesn't last forever, either.
During one of these long nights that are characteristic of winter, I remained wide awake with the lights turned off throughout, like some hellish torture.
I remained like that until the bright morning sun finally appeared a second time to burn daylight into my eyes.
I've yet to manage to get even a wink of sleep despite such a long passage of time.
I had hoped fatigue and sleepiness would cloud my mind. However, they failed to expel the memories of a certain someone out of it and only left me with a splitting headache.
If I keep spending my time alone in this room like this, my mind probably won't be able to take it…
In the end, however, I have neither a place to take refuge in nor a person to provide me the escape I need.
I remain trapped in the darkness, seeing no trace of an exit.
"The owner of this number is not available. Please leave a message after the tone."
"Hey, Haruki. I need to talk to you about what happened once you come back, okay? Call me back as soon as you hear this."
"I've already called you both here and on your cell phone, so don't you dare ignore me, you hear? Later."
The call on my cell just a while ago was from Takeya as well. This makes it the ninth time in two days that I've been running away, pretending to be unavailable.
At first, when I didn't answer the phone, he sounded as if he was teasing me.
His teasing probably stemmed from a naive, hopeful belief that I was still with Setsuna.
However, since yesterday night… after a call from Io, I realized that things had taken a turn for the worse.
Although her tone sounded strangely desperate, what she spoke about was not far from what I'd predicted she would.
She said that Setsuna told her nothing had happened. That Setsuna only kept smiling and didn't cry.
…And that she knew all of it was a lie.
She'd definitely notice the subtle changesーshe's been friends with her for so long. Her forced cheerfulness, slight traces of emptiness, her inability to hide the pain.
Various negative feelings are slowly eating away at Setsuna right now.
…After that, Io and Takeya kept calling me several times per hour until morning came.
They're not just doing this because they feel responsible. I can feel their genuine worry for the two of us through their frantic tones.
And yet, I've only continued to ignore them as if it was their own business that they were so panicked.
Because I don't know how I should answer them. It's because we're so close that I don't know what to say to them.
Because I know how they'll react.
Because I know their reaction will definitely hurt me, though it's also because it would put me at ease to some extent.
They'll likely punish me. They'll furiously lament and reprimand me, and desperately interfere in hopes of finding a solution somehow.
And I would likely accept their punishment and stop my own thoughts in response to their intervention.
That would only serve my own self-satisfaction, though. There's nothing worse than pretending an issue is already solved when it isn't.
Even if I can take on the pain directly, it would be pointless if I can't move on.
After all, even if I do get my moment of comfort, it would not solve anything for Setsunaーit wouldn't save her. A result such as this, my own salvation alone, would accomplish nothing.
That's why I… ultimately can't do anything in the end.
All I can do now is observe the sky above in real time, as it's wrapped by the gentle sunlight and dyed a warm red, before turning black.
And entertain myself with the question of whether or not I will be able to move forward, even if just a little, when the next dawn arrives…
A question I keep asking myself over and over again.
Unable to determine how far the source of the sound is from me, I blindly stretch out my hand in the faint darkness.
When I finally sense the rhythmic vibration of a solid object on my fingers, I know that I've found what I'm looking for.
After already having picked up the phone, I realized…
It's been days since I've last had a conversation with someone.
"…Huh? Are you awake? I thought it'd be alright since it's afternoon already…"
My mind can't keep up with the first conversation I've had in quite a long while.
Moreover, the fact that I just woke up also means my reactions are still dull.
…And having realized that I've just woken up, I reply with odd, redundant responses.
"…I'm sorry. Seems like you really were asleep, huh…"
"No, that's… no problem. I was just taking a nap, that's all…"
I was actually asleep… finally asleep.
"That means you're at home now, right? Are you okay? Can we talk for a bit?"
"…What is the date and time right now?"
"…Kitahara, just how long have you been sleeping? It's 1:30 PM on the 28th."
As I open the curtains, having been untouched for more than 24 hours, even the radiance of the gentle winter sunlight manages to dazzle my eyes.
If my memory serves me right, the clock pointed at twelve the last time I checked it. Meaning that I've been sleeping for about an hour.
"…You don't seem okay to me. Should I leave this for tomorrow?"
"Ahh, no, I'm all right, really. What's the matter?"
The truth is, my mind and my body haven't rested at all.
My head is still as hazy as ever. I still feel quite groggy. Such a half-hearted excuse of an attempt to sleep actually ended up exhausting me even more.
Nevertheless, the fact that I've successfully fallen asleep holds great meaning in itself. It gave me a chance to talk to someone, above all things.
I have my unconsciousness to thank for facilitating contact with another person after I've denied it for so long.
"No, it's nothing too important, but… it's just that you haven't been coming to work recently. So, um… are you feeling okay?"
The fact that I was quick to tell a lie in my first instance of communication in a while is somewhat awkward, though.
"Well, never mind that. So when will you be coming back?"
"Even if you've finished your work for the end of the year, that doesn't mean you've got time to rest. Everyone needs your help. Could you come over and help out if you can find the time?"
The way I am now, her previous sentence didn't come across as an annoyance or her just being nosy about it all.
Having someone unexpectedly tell me that I'm needed by the very outside world that I've isolated myself from is enough to elate me right now.
"Ah, but I won't be able to come this year anymore. I've got interviews scheduled in America from today onward. I'm at Narita Airport right now."
"Huh… Even though it's the end of the year?"
"I'll be going around places like New York and Los Angeles, and after I'm done with work, I'll take a vacation with my friend there. I'll come back around the 5th of January."
"I see… Thank you for your hard work."
I see, she called to tell me that… even though I'm just a part-time subordinate. She really is commendable as always…

"Ah, the friend I mentioned isn't a man, okay? I'm pretty sure you've met her before, right, Kitahara? You know, Amamiya Sawako? It's just an annual trip with two women together, not involving any men and…"
"…No, it's pointless telling that to you, Kitahara. Sorry, just forget about what I just said."
"Hm? I understand. Please say hello to Sawako-san for me. I hope you'll have a great trip."
"There's really no need to say anything to her…"
Mari-san's weird changes in her attitude really perplex me sometimes, and I still can't understand her completely to this day.
"Ah, but let's cut to the chase. I've sent something over to your place, Kitahara. I just received it yesterday, so I didn't have time to give it to you in person."
"It's… a ticket for Touma Youko's New Year concert."
"From what I understand, it came from Touma Youko Office, mailed directly to Ensemble's editing department. …She asked for it to be delivered to the person who wrote that article."
The moment I finally manage to keep up with the conversation, a name appears that makes my head go completely blank once again…
"That's pretty amazing, Kitahara. It's not every day you can get such a great response from your interviewee with your first article, you know."
"N-No… That's because this person was special…"
"It's a rare opportunity, so why don't you try getting backstage? If you tell them you're from Ensemble, they'll let you in for sure."
"It's important to have connections in our field of work. It's not like you have anything to lose by meeting them, right?"
Mari-san, who's lightheartedly telling me all this while being unaware of the whole story, is making it increasingly difficult for me to say anything.
If I were to meet with Touma Youko, she'd probably be shocked yet again, wouldn't she? By the fact that the author of that article was her daughter's… well…
…No, what would really be surprising is if she actually still remembers me. We've only met once, and three years ago at that.
"Um, Mari-san. I'm thankful you told me this, but I…"
"Just maybe… you might see Touma Kazusa there too, you know?"
"The truth is, you want to see her, don't you?"
"Being unaware of the whole story," huh… I can only say that I've underestimated Mari-san.
"Ever since that article was published, you haven't shown up at all… So I was guessing that you might have remembered something you didn't want to and ended up feeling depressed."
No, she couldn't possibly know the truth about everything. I don't recall telling her that much.
"If you had managed to laugh it off now, I would be feeling relieved, but…"
So it's simply Mari-san being perceptive, then.
And at the same time, it's undeniable proof that she's been worried about me.
"You're pretty naive, aren't you, Kitahara? You're quite fragile, and you always seem to only put the blame on yourself."
"You do. And whenever you're facing some hard times, you try to find an escape in working or studying. I figured that out quite early."
She's really been watching over me closely, hasn't she?
"Just because I'm hurt right now, doesn't mean that I'm the victim."
"Because… considering how deeply I've wounded someone else, the scratch I received is laughably light in comparison."
Even so, while I'm glad that she's favoring her subordinate like this, I can't help but think that it doesn't feel right.
"I feel that I'm undeserving of having you comfort me like this, Mari-san."
"Is that why you got so depressed? Because there was nobody to reprimand you for it? Because there was nobody you could ask for forgiveness afterward…?"
What Mari-san just pointed out is pretty much the same thing I've been thinking about until yesterday.
"In that case… I won't blame you. And so I won't forgive you either."
"All you need to do is talk, Kitahara. And all I will do is listen. Maybe you won't find the forgiveness you seek from others right now, but perhaps it'll put you at peace, even if only a little."
"It's just… being the only one who gets that peace wouldn't mean anything…"
"If you can't even find peace of mind for yourself, how will you ever be able to find it in yourself to make it up to the other person?"
"Well, I don't mind if you don't want to talk about it. This is a private matter of yours, and I'm just your superior at a part-time job, after all."
"…I'll hear you out. And I won't give you any advice."
"I've always been in love with Touma Kazusaーeven now."
"And someone else ended up getting hurt by me because of that."
Surprisingly, I managed to tell her everything.
I told her about the very first person I invited into our group, who happened to be none other than Miss Houjou High herself.
I told her how I quickly grew close with that girl who was unbelievably sociable despite her popularity and fame.
And how on that night after the school festival ended… it was that girl who I accepted and who accepted me in return, rather than Kazusa.
It wasn't Kazusa and I who were considered officially together by everyone around us at the time; it was me and the other girl instead.

And yet, I betrayed that girl for Kazusaーand then there was the period that lasted until today, where the both of us continued to hold on to all of our past regrets and never ceased to shackle the other.
And then there was Christmas Eve…
The day I betrayed her because of Kazusa yet again, the day the both of us realized once more that we're still strangling each other.
Mari-san ended up listening quietly, just as she promised she would.
She'd ask for some slight clarification at times where there was a jump in my story's timeline, but she'd truly listened to me otherwise.
That's why I've told her everythingーleaving nothing unsaid, even the most important part…
"Why are you apologizing? I only said I would listen, right?"
"Even so, I've said too much. It's not like we're out drinking together. Not to mention we're not even seeing each other face to face…"
"Don't you think it's precisely because we're not seeing each other face to face that you were able to say all that? We weren't able to see each other's reactions, after all."
"Besides, it's also because we won't be seeing each other in a while, right? By the time we see each other again, we'll probably both have forgotten about it."
I'm sure that the both of us will still remember our conversation today the next time we meet.
Even so, it will be easier for us to pretend that we've forgotten all about it after some time passes.
She's likely chosen to hear me out through the phone because she's gone as far as to consider all that… or perhaps I'm just overthinking it.
"Even so, you're still young, Kitahara. I'm relieved to hear such a youthful story from you for once."
"Do I… really come across as being that old most of the time?"
"Well, I don't mean anything bad by all that. Perhaps it's better to say you're a bit too composed, too argumentative, and too conscious of things sometimes?"
"Are you really sure you don't mean anything bad by everything you just said…?"
"Listen… Just like I promised earlier, I won't blame you, nor will I forgive you."
"That's why I was also thinking about what I would have done if I were in your shoes as you explained all that, Kitahara…"
"If it were you, Mari-san… what would you have done?"
"To be honest, I don't know either."
"The decision you've made… whether it's right or wrong, I can't say for sure either."
"I can't say 'That sounds terrible,' nor can I say 'I know how you feel.'"
"That's why I can't say, 'It's your fault' either. …No, I promised not to mention that to begin with."
"I'm sorry… It seems I really can't be of much help. Something like this is…"
"Thank you very much. You've done more than enough for me."
"How so? I didn't really do anything to help, did I?"
"I… I've always thought that maybe I was the only one at fault… that maybe I was the only one who didn't understand anything."
"But now you've convinced me that it might not be the case… Hah… it appears that I'm the only one who's been saved after all, even if a little. But that just won't do…"
"With that… we're around the C part of the PDCA, aren't we?"
"All that's left is for you to rely on your own strength to move toward step A. …You can do it, right, Kitahara?"
A cycle that, while originally intended for the management of manufacturing industries, is now applicable in pretty much any job in our modern day.
…A cycle she'd beat into my head during the first week of work.
"Well then, it's about time for me to go. …When I return to Japan, I'll have a ton of work for you to do."
I have a feeling that half of what she just said was an attempt to try and hide her embarrassment, though I know there's truth in the other half, nevertheless.
To change myself for the better. To work hard for that change…
"Well… it's time for me to go."
And that was definitely her trying to hide her embarrassment.
Even so, even if I did manage to read her like a book, I don't see myself being able to do anything other than following what she'd said.
"Aa-ah, jeez… I've been left behind. I wonder if there are any other planes still flying to New York today…"
A continuation of yesterday, is it…?
After finally getting some sleep, my now completely reversed sleep schedule is getting more and more out of hand…
"Aaah, yes! Alright, I'm coming, I'm coming… Just hold on a second!"
I steal a glance at my clock as I hop out of bed to see it's 8 o'clock. Judging by the color of the sky, it's 8 PM.
It's a time when it's natural for anyone to assume I'm awake. As such, it appears I can't be mad about this unannounced visit.
Then again, I can only think of a handful of people who would ring my doorbell, salesmen and swindlers aside.
She's… not among that handful of people.
After all, her paper is finished, the seminars have ended, the year-end party's over, and the year itself is also coming to an end…

I can't believe that she, the queen of playing hooky even on weekdays, of all people, would be loitering around near our university, and on a day that would otherwise be a perfect holiday for her, no less…
"Yay, you've got stubble! Hey, let me rub my face on it～♪"
"W-Wa-Wait! Izumi! What are you doing here!?"
…Well, having her hug me so suddenly and rubbing her face against mine is actually kind of scary in a way, though.
"It's pretty rude of you to ask what I'm doing here. Don't you know how much courage a girl needs to muster to come over?"
"Mmm～ let's just say I'm couch-surfing! And I've just about used up all my excuses to stay at other friends' places."
It appears that the rift between the mother and daughter of the Izumi family is still heading in a grave direction to this day.
…I hope she's aware that it's hard for anybody to give a proper response to that kind of excuse before she uses it.
"The girl who let me stay until yesterday has to go back to her hometown. It's pretty harsh living in that lab that doesn't have air-conditioning, you know?"
"That's easier said than done… The only people I have left are the ones from our seminar."
"Even though they're the same gender as you are, Haruki?"
"Well, I guess that's that, then. Let me borrow your phone for a second. Something terrible happened to my phone's battery. So I can't really get in touch with anyone～"
"W-Wait! The guys from our seminar barely even know you!"
"Sure, but they'll probably let me stay over anyway. Wanna bet?"
The only thing she's far better at than me is negotiating.
The hot water wakes both my body and mind up simultaneously.
As I rub my body with the soap and sponge to the point where it hurts, my sense of touch returns to my skin as well.

After letting a woman into my house, I hopped into the shower immediately. It may be giving off the impression that I want to engage in a certain activity with her, but I really have no such intentions…
It's just that I need to do something about both the existing problem that Izumi pointed out earlier and also why it happened; in other words, I'm just freshening myself up in the bathroom for a bit.
I really didn't conduct myself very well, even if only in front of Izumi… Then again, I can't believe she still nonchalantly hugged me despite how stinky and dirty I was.
For the record, I wouldn't say I've fallen prey to her sly tricks, nor would I say I've surrendered to her attempt at seducing me either.
It's just that as far as Izumi is concerned, I know that even if I try to complain, she'll shrug me off with a "Well, whatever" and just do whatever she wants to anyway.
Since that day, I've been forced to communicate for the second time now, and on two consecutive days at that.
And it's not just communication through voice this time; it's face to face interaction.
I neither hoped for nor approved this… but my life's gradually getting back on track.
"Mm～! Having pizza once in a while is great! I still think your home cooking would be more ideal for me, though, Haruki."
"Eat the salad too. Make sure your diet is balanced."
"You're eating more than I expected, Haruki. Even though you've done nothing but sleep recently."
"…My energy has just about run out too, so it's time for me to refill it."
It's been four days, and even though this food is too heavy for my stomach to handle, it just goes straight down my throat.
To be honest, my tongue hasn't recovered to the point where it can determine whether something tastes good or not.
Even so, my stomach, which had started to whine in the middle of it all, is now brazenly accepting chunks of cheese and dough.
"Don't put so much tabasco on… You're spilling it on my portion too."
I finally managed to get some sleep yesterday, and I've bathed myself and shaved my beard today.
And I can finally eat now as wellーperhaps it's better to say that my appetite has returned.
"I told you not to swallow it whole… Need some tea?"
It's likely because there's a certain someone who has a knack for really enjoying food right in front of me that I'm capable of eating normally like this, though…
"Gulp, gulp, gulp, gulp… Pwaahhh! Uwaaa～! That's the stuff～!"
"Who in the world would finish an entire can of beer just to flush food down? Did your objective change while you were drinking?"
I'm reluctant to admit it, but it's the truth.
"Ah, I'll let you have the last slice of pizza, Haruki."
"But in exchange, since you ate more than half of the food, I think we should split the bill 7:3… or at least 6:4!"
"…What kind of fussy calculation is this, Izumi?"
"Y-You know～ it's just that I've been sleeping over at other places for quite some time now, so I've made it kind of a habit…"
"It's fine, I'll pay for the pizza and all."
"Eh, for real? Regardless of how much I eat, you'll pay for everything, Haruki!?"
"…Don't forget I've already paid for the beer as well."
"Yaay～! You're so generous, Haruki～! I love you～! In that case, I might as well help myself to the last…"
"That's for the sponsor. It's the sole condition for him to provide his support."
"…What kind of fussy proclamation of your privilege is this, Haruki?"
Following Mari-san, now it's Izumi who's bringing me back to the real world again.
"Come to think of it, have you done anything fun this winter break?"
"I've been at home the entire time."
Given it's been a while since I last ate anything, it's natural that it's been some time since I last did any housework, as well.
The nylon sponge was completely dry. I could barely open the dish soap bottle in the kitchen. And I saw a bit of rust in the water in the sink…
"Huh? What about going out with your girlfriend?"
"…Where in the world did you get the idea that I have a girlfriend?"
All these are but some of the telltale scars of the fact that I've not done anything in this room for the past several days.
"I never said anything like that. Don't make such strange claims."
"Then, what? You don't plan on going anywhere this entire winter break, Haruki?"
"I've still got my part-time job. I'm quite busy."
"Didn't you just say you were at home the entire time, and just ten seconds ago at that?"
There's the fact that I'm not able to communicate properly, as shown from how I'm incapable of refuting even a simple argument like that.
"This time, make sure you don't lose the place where you belong, Setsuna."
"All right, another victory～♪! How long does that make my winning streak now?"
"Damn it! And I managed to get the joker on your side for once too!"
I toss the last card left in my handーthe jokerーand lament on how terrible my luck is today.
The session of Old Maid after dinner had ended with a score of 16 to 2 in her favor, which included a ten-round losing streak for me. Objectively speaking, the difference is unequivocally one-sided.
"That's because you're too easy to read, Haruki! The moment the joker ends up in your hand, it's pretty much game over."
"How can you be so good at this…? You haven't marked the cards, now, have you?"
It's true that the two same instances that I've won ended up with me not getting the joker in my hand even once and getting away with it to the very end.
"Remember the saying, 'You touch your ear when you lie'? Once someone figures out what your 'ear' is, it's easy to tell."
"…Do I have a habit like that?"
"No, it's not that simple. It's more like an instinctive human reaction."
"Actions and breath, speech and expression, and so on… If you don't consider all that information, it's pretty hard to perform an overall evaluation."
"And that's not all. I can take control of you by using that information and mislead you to think and act the way I want you to."
"You… Wouldn't it be better if you specialized in psychology instead?"
Though her method of manipulation seemed heavily exaggerated at first, I can't help but believe her, given I've ended up with such a big losing streak.
I'm really glad I rejected Izumi's initial suggestion of playing poker with "I don't play games that involve gambling" after all this…
"Hmm～ I'm not interested in the theory behind it. I'd rather experience it myself. You could say I'm more of a hands-on person."
"Do you plan on becoming a con artist in the future?"
"Well, I'm already… doing something like that right now."
This classmate of mine, who possesses detailed observation skills and a masterful poker face, suddenly laughs with an expression of self-derision.
"Well, leaving that aside～ I want to play games that are more competitive. Have you got anything else?"
"This room sure lacks entertainment devices as always. You must be my only friend who doesn't even have a game console, Haruki."
"If you're not satisfied, then go to sleep. Play those competitive games all you like in your dreams."
"Oh, well… I'll just change my goal to a twenty-game win streak and keep on playing Old Maid～!"
"…How far do you plan on making me suffer?"
I pull a 5 of diamonds… and make a pair with the 5 of spades from my hand and throw it out.
As for Izumi, after moving her hand across the mountain-like pile of cards in my hand, she pulls out the 8 of hearts and throws it out.
After that, I pull the jack of clubs, the card I want the most. So I make a pair with the jack of diamonds I've been holding for a while, and…
…None of this matters. The joker's in my hand, so whatever card I pick from her is harmless.
I can't do anything about it even if I start complaining now, but playing Old Maid with only two people sure is boring…
This time, she pulls the king of clubs from me. She just won't pull the joker, will she…?
In the end, we return to the usual situation where Izumi has two choices left. It all comes down to how good my poker face is.
The pointless conversation goes on and on, while our eyes never leave the cards.
…Even though the two cards themselves are already on the table and we can both see the numbers on them.
"I should be asking you, why are you saying things like that?"
Although we both omit the subject of that sentence, even I'm not as dense as to not realize what she means.
"Hmm～ Because you're looking so depressed, Haruki, so I was wondering if I should cheer you up?"
…Izumi's foot starts touching me under the table.
"You… Whenever you see a depressed man, do you always, you know… try to cheer them up like this?"
"No, it's the first time I've said something like this. It's only for you, Haruki."
"Because if I don't go all in now, I won't make the script in time, will I?"
"Hmm, but which one is my real intention, I wonder?"
"I'll ask again, what did you say?"
"Hey, Haruki… Do you think it will backfire on me eventually?"
"Don't push on with the conversation while you're being vague with your point."
Izumi's actions, breath, speech, and expression…
None of them look any different from before. Is it due to my lack of perception? Or perhaps…
"Well, who cares about that… So why not?"
"Why… Well, we're not going out, are we?"
As for my actions, breath, speech and expression…
"It's fine even if we're not going out. I just want to have a closer relationship with you, Haruki."
"…I don't understand you. How is this different from a confession?"
Even I know I can't maintain my usual composure at times like this. I wonder how it looks like to Izumi…
"There is a slight difference… Well, I suppose if you have to add a deeper meaning to it, I guess you can see it as the same thing, all right?"
The game is still in progress. But I'm slowly losing my ground.
"How about thinking of it from a more casual perspective, then? Like, it's just me repaying you for the pizza…"
"I can't see those two things separately. Don't you know that?"
"I know you wouldn't. I'm sure I know you that well, at least."
Chiaki's foot slowly slides toward my knees.
Her expression above the table hasn't changed at all, but her actions under the table don't hide her passion whatsoever.
"In that case… it's about time you pulled it back. I don't really hate you, which is why it's difficult for me to continue this conversation."
Since I can't keep up with Izumi's two-faced behavior, I already lost this game a long time ago.
I have already given up on using either observation or my poker face at this point.
"Then, if you can answer my following question honestly, I'll consider letting you off the hook."
"Hey, Haruki… do you have a girl you like right now?"
Even if I've given up on winning this game, there's an emotion that I must defend.
That's why I won't hesitate to answer this question in the least. Not just for Izumi, but also…
"…Then why are you shutting yourself inside your house?"
"…One step forward and two steps back, huh?"
"That's not how the proverb goes in Japanese, but it somehow sums up my situation perfectly…"
"But in that case, isn't this my cue to act?"
"Mm, well, that's… how should I put it…"
"You still love her nevertheless? Still can't give up?"
Even though I made up my mind, in the end, I still didn't know what to do.
I couldn't say it. I'm the worst…
"You don't need to apologize to me. I'm not that shocked about this result."
Even so, I'm able to properly let my feelings out.
Even if I'm not conveying my feelings to her, this is enough for now.
"Hmm, I guess the time has come."
Before I realized it, Izumi's foot had stopped touching me.
"The motif's become more and more fascinating, but as I thought, I just can't go through with this anymore."
She relaxes herself completely and stares straight at the ceiling with an expression that suggests she's finally relieved of something.
Even though this is completely different from the poker face she had before, I still can't see through her. Izumi's inner thoughts aren't simple enough for me to do so.
"With this, my greatest ambitions have come to an end… Thank you, Haruki… for allowing me to dream until now."
"I seriously can't understand a word you're saying."
"There are things in the world that you're better off not knowing, right? For example, I'm actually a wicked woman who's beyond redemption."
"That's impossible… I have confidence in that myself."
As Izumi lets those words slip out, the atmosphere around us becomes painful, yet gently silent.
Up until this point, there was an intense battle, but now it's gone without a trace… aside from the cards left on the table.
"Is it really okay for you not to stay the night? The last train is already gone, you know?"
"In that case, I'd have to quickly come up with another story, wouldn't I?"
"I told you to stop whispering and making it so that I can't hear you."
We're full from eating and drinking, and we've also played plenty of games.
Just as we were about to go to sleep, Izumi suddenly stood up and started getting ready to leave.
"It's hard to stay in a room with a man whose heart is with another woman…"
…Well, considering the conversation we just had, what she's doing isn't exactly a surprise.
"It'd be terrible if I jumped on you while half-asleep."
Even though we joke around like usual, it doesn't lighten up the mood.
We softly yet emotionally wave our hands and bid each other farewell.
Is it because she's departing from me that she seems a little lonely…?
"I know about the depth of your emotions, you know?"
"That beautiful feeling of yours that's on par with any of the world's many stories, you know what I mean?"
Izumi's eyes are full of emotion, and she starts tearing up.
"You've already come this far… so I hope you can dash toward the finish line and give this beautiful story the beautiful ending it deserves."
"This time, let me play a part in that story."
Still, even at the very end, she doesn't really explain the most important bit, not crossing the final line.
Without revealing the secret at the bottom of her heart, Izumi sublimates it.
"Good night, my Lord. It has truly been my pleasure to have been able to observe you these past few years."
