"Because the person you're interviewing is the Japanese pianist, Touma Kazusa. I recall she went to the same school as you, didn't she?"
Christmas Day was nothing more than an ordinary winter day after Christmas Eve had passed.

The snow had stopped piling up by the time dawn arrived and only served to deliver the chill of winter and hinder the steps of passersby. By noon, it had completely dissolved into blackened slush that merged into the ground.
…I can't deny the possibility that my own mental state is responsible for my currently cynical outlook.
In the end, as expected, I haven't been able to get even a wink of sleep since then.
I'd spent a whole night engraving the period of the dark sky gradually brightening outside the window in my mind; I then came to the clear realization that nights are not eternal.
I had hoped fatigue and sleepiness would cloud my mind. However, they failed to expel the memories of a certain someone out of it, only serving to give me a splitting pain.
I felt like I would've gone crazy if I remained alone in my room like that, so I decided to force myself to go outside.
It's been a few hours since then…
Watching a day of the sky covered with clouds darkening in real time also made me remember that daylight doesn't last forever, either.
I simply kept walking aimlessly until nighttime, and in the end, I ended up here.
I've been standing outside watching my busy coworkers working inside the restaurant the whole time.

The number of customers is slightly lower than usual, thoughーlikely because both Houjou University and its affiliate high school have entered winter break, as the number of employees on shift is also accordingly lower.
I don't see anyone resting in either the kitchen or the hallーnot Satou, Nakagawa-san, or any of the remaining staff.
That's why if I'm here… this should be an accommodating venue for my current state of mind.
My abrupt visit might instinctively strike them as unusual, but they'd probably direct me to the changing room and put me into uniform under the impression that I'm here to help on a rainy day.
Perhaps I can wholeheartedly distract myself by staying busy with work.
…Or so I thought. In spite of picturing such a scenario, my feet are unwilling to move an inch toward the entrance.
The girl who had worked hard for me so I wouldn't have to come to work today. The girl who had encouraged me and pushed me forward.
I can't meet with her right now. I don't know how to face her.
After all, I couldn't follow her plan to the letter.
I'm incapable of repaying her for her once-in-a-lifetime favor toward me…
While I was busy thinking about her this entire time, I'd failed to realize that she had already noticed me.
"You don't have work today, do you? Didn't the acting manager drive that into your head?"
"Do you have that little faith in me? The testing period is over, and I'm pretty confident that I'm doing well."
"The issue is that people can come to trust you too much."
"Even though I told you not to come again this year.
Come to think of it, Senpai, aren't you supposed to be…?"
"That's none of your business. Let's make it clear that I'm your senior here… Rather, I'm your senior in every situation."
Retorts surface in my mind, but I'm unable to speak them out loud.
Someone is desperately trying to suppress my desperate attempt to gloss over the situation.
…That someone unmistakably being myself, of course.
After all… the very reason I can't stay here is standing right in front of me right now.
"Then try showing me your smile, or at least be angry with me. …If possible, I'd want the former, but I wouldn't mind the latter either."
"…Get back to work. You're still on the clock, no?"
While I'd considered the possibility that something like this would happen, I hadn't thought about how I'd respond in such a situation at all.
"I was simply passing by, that's all. I have faith in your ability, Sugiura. Anyway, I should head home…"
While I figured she'd say something like that as well, I came here of my own accord nonetheless.
Am I really being more emotional than I expected? Am I really acting so differently from how I usually do?
…And to a level where her face is the first thing that comes to mind the moment I'm suffering all by myself, no less?
"The restaurant… isn't a good idea. Everyone's still in there.
…I know. Go over to the Bonanza over there, please."
She's pointing at the cafe across the street.
If I took a seat by the window, it'd be convenient, given that we could keep an eye on each other due to how close and well-lit the cafe is.
"I'm on the morning shift today, so I'll be done soon. I'll come see you immediately afterward."
"I'm alright, really. I honestly was just passing by…"
"You might think you're alright, but to me, you're not! In terms of your mental state, that is!"
"I'll definitely be there! Within 30 minutes! That's why you absolutely… you absolutely can't go home, okay!?"
Turning a deaf ear to what I'd just explained to her, Sugiura made that promise on her own and hurried back into the restaurant.
Am I really that easy to read the way I am now…?
Actually, I suppose it would be strange if she didn't realize something was up given how suspiciously I've been conducting myself.
Returning to the restaurant, she started working again as if nothing had happened, but she also sent an unceremonious glance at me and pointed to the cafe across the street.

She's a girl filled with contradictionsー"a charitable junior," so to speak, who's meddlesome, goes out of her way to know about things she shouldn't, and goes the extra mile for someone who's no more than an acquaintance to her.
Having lost all of my strength, my heart can't bring itself to accept such an unconditional kindness right now.
That's why I dashed away from my current location the second I noticed she wasn't paying attention to me for the slightest moment.
Had I accepted Sugiura's invitation and spent some time together with her, perhaps the wound I'm currently bearing would start to heal, even if only a little.
In exchange for getting peace of mind, however, I'd have to tell her everything.

And while I'm unsure as to who she'd side with between Setsuna and me, one thing's for sure: she'll lament, get angry and try to further involve herself into the affair after learning of the result I've brought about.
I can't let that happen to someone like her, who I can't really say is my friend, could never consider a lover, and yet I feel reluctant to consider her a mere junior of mine.
The melted snow weighs upon my footsteps and makes them heavier with each step, but I've finally managed to escape the Goodies' bindings.
Before I knew it, I'm right in front of Minami-Suetsugu Station…
With the way I am now, it seems I can only move toward places with large crowds, no matter what.
The unnecessary sprint here causes my already exhausted body to feel uncomfortable, and I'm so out of breath that I could start coughing any minute.
I'm feeling so hot that the chilly midwinter wind actually feels pleasant, while my forehead is getting slightly sweaty.
I bend over, placing my hands on my knees as I desperately try to catch my breath, all while regretting my meaningless and ridiculous escape.
Why did I have to run all the way out here? Why do I have to be tormented by such guilt over something as trivial as this?
Given that I was the one who put the distance between us, why do I myself suddenly want to go back there again?
"I said I'd be back within 30 minutes, didn't I!? It shouldn't be a problem for you to wait that long, right!?"
I sprinted across the road as fast as I could. I put as much distance between us with as much strength as I could muster.
And yet, she still caught up to me so easily… no, she's actually just as out of breath as I am.
"Haah… haah… and I'll have you know that going outside in this outfit is really embarrassing!"
She was desperately chasing after me… and in the end, she caught up to me.
"Yes, yes… I'm sorry. I'll take back my clothes tomorrow… Yes, I'll certainly be there…"
The first button I press is for a small can of black coffee. The second button is for a large can of milk coffee.
An especially sweet one, at that.
"I was having a bit of trouble with a friend of mine… It's fine now. I'm sorry for the inconvenience."
"Yes, yes… Yes… About today's wages… No, you don't need to…"
"…I understand. I just wanted to explain myself."
"Then… please continue to take care of me from now on. I am really sorry for what happened today."
"Good work. Which one do you want?"
"I feel warm right now. Thanks to a certain someone who ran away."
"I was just about to ask if you wanted my coat, too."
Sugiura snatches the small can from my hand, her tone as furious as ever.
Just as I thought, neither of us have a sweet tooth. …What should I do with this milk coffee, then?
"I've caused trouble for everyone. Thanks to a certain someone who ran away."
"He said that everything will be alright and they'll do their best to manage. …It doesn't seem like I'll be fired after all."
"There's no way they'll fire someone as useful as you, Sugiura. If I was the branch manager, I'd make you work even harder as punishment."
"As expected from someone you've taught… He even said that I'll have to continue working after April."
"Sip… Hot! Jeez, I told you I didn't want anything hot!"
It seems she's not a fan of warm beverages despite lacking a sweet tooth.
The two of us remain seated on a bench in front of the station, staring at the night sky while drinking our coffee.
Given that most of the clouds have gone and a large number of stars are now visible, I'm expecting tomorrow's weather to turn for the better.
However, when the weather becomes normal again on winter nights, there's also radiative cooling we have to worry about.
Then I'm sure tomorrow morning will be…
"It's become incredibly cold! What are you going to do about this, Senpai!?"
Actually, this isn't the time to think about matters like tomorrow morning and the like.
The sudden chill from the bitter cold hitting my body, which was already warm from all that running, was enough to tell me that…
"T-Then, why don't we go somewhere to warm up? To a cafe, or maybe a family restaurant?"
As she says so, she points at the miniskirt that's part of her uniform, to which I have no proper reply…
"All of this just because a certain someone decided to run away… This is really such a hassle!"
What I said was partly just me trying to act tough, while it was also partly true.
Easing this cold loneliness inside of me is much more important than simply warming my body at the moment.
"I… I think that was the first time in my life that I've ever ditched work."
"Well, you know, I guess there's no helping that. I just couldn't have left you alone, Senpai."
The moment she sat next to me and started talking to me…
There was no hiding anything anymore.
"When I saw you standing outside the restaurant absentmindedly, you looked as if you'd lost your heart."
"That's why I was spurred by the worry that if I lost sight of you now, I wouldn't be able to catch up to you ever again…"
I am currently being spoiled by my fellow charitable junior, Sugiura Koharu…
"…You didn't need to go out of your way to catch up to me."
"You know… for better or worse, you seem to be so serious all the time, Sugiura."
"And I think you always look so depressed, Senpai. I think you're the one being unnatural here."
I poured the lukewarm coffee into my mouth in one go and swallowed the words that were already on the tip of my tongue with it.
I suppose that's just the three-year age difference between Sugiura and me.
"I've been in the same class as Mihoko since our first year."
"She's been a Houjou student since kindergarten, while I freshly enrolled during high school."
"That was the case for me too."
About half of the students in our first year of Houjou High were new to the school, so by no means were we a minority.
Moreover, getting a recommendation to Houjou University was a very attractive prospect. If my memory serves me right, the entrance exam to the high school was quite a challenge.
"But despite the fact that she should have had a lot of friends, Mihoko could never really fit in with our class."
"Not to mention she has a frail disposition… After I enrolled, I immediately became the class president, and I ended up visiting her every month when she got ill."
"To give her notes and print outs, huh."
Although I was never assigned to visit a certain student's house on a regular basis, I do remember visiting the residences of more than ten people.
"That's how we got to know each other better, and we started hanging out more in class. …Although everyone found it rather strange at first."
"Your personalities are quite different from one another, after all."
I imagine that most people didn't expect Sugiura, who is the very picture of assertiveness and sociability, to pair up with Yada-san, who is her exact opposite.
"Still, we do have something in common. …What do you think it is?"
"The way you're both very serious about things, right? She's very studious, after all, as are you, Sugiura…"
"Well, there's that… but our most identical trait would be how stubborn we both are."
"You're not going to ask "…Sugiura, stubborn?" are you?"
"Because of my personality, I did everything I could to make sure Mihoko and I could be friends with the others."
Sugiura looked at me kindly for a brief moment before she immediately continued talking about the past as if nothing had happened.
"But Mihoko is perfectly happy being by herself or being alone with me."
"That's why she usually doesn't accept my invitations to hang out with others. Even so, I tend to insist on getting her involved, and we've argued many times because of it."
"That girl absolutely refuses to give in after she's made a decision. She can be obedient, but she usually rejects me by giving me the silent treatment."
"…I never thought she was like that at all."
In other words, that's the side that she's only shown to her best friend.
This is another notable difference between her and Sugiura, given that the latter can act so stubbornly in front of just about anyone.
"Even now, she's giving me a bit of the cold shoulder, you know? She's not responding to my calls and texts…"
"Mihoko can be so stubborn to the point where she refuses to compromise. This has caused a lot of misunderstandings between us."
"No, this is a problem between Mihoko and me. We'll make sure to keep it between the two of us and resolve it, so please don't worry."
When Sugiura changed the subject as if to intentionally avoid a certain topic, I understood the meaning behind her kind smile from earlier.
I also understand the reason why she's been only talking about herself since a while ago.
"While we were both in our second year, there was this one time where we ended up in different classes…"
Even though I questioned her suddenly, she picked up on my intentions perfectly and didn't hesitate to give me a plain answer.
"There's no way I wouldn't be curious, you know? That's why I chased after you like this."
"Still, even I'm tactful enough to know how to draw the line."
In other words… Even though she was worried about me, she took my feelings into consideration and didn't pry any further.
"To be honest, I'm really worried about what you've gone through because of my nosy actions."
She continues talking about her own life without stopping, unhindered by the usual possibility of me giving a light retort and potentially causing the conversation to go nowhere because of it.
"It's a bit different right now, though. Maybe the most important thing is that we didn't argue like we usually do."
She went from directly intervening to influencing from the sidelines.
"If that's the case, then maybe I didn't need to chase after you, but for some reason, that doesn't really feel right either… I can't really explain it well."
That's something I couldn't do myself.
"I don't want you to talk like you know everything about me. We've only known each other for a month."
"I'm only three years younger than you, Senpai, and I, too, have a long and deep history of my own."
"There are parts of my personality that will always be the same, but there are also parts where I've started to change a little."
"That's why what you're saying bothers me a little. Even though you don't know anything about me, you're acting so arrogant and self-righteous…
"…I'm sorry. Even though I said the most important thing for us is that we didn't argue right now."
"You really have changed, Sugiura. You're an even better person than you were before."
"…I can see that you've returned to your old self a bit, Senpai. Is it really that enjoyable to tease me?"
Sugiura looked down and fell silent.
However, right now, this silence feels more pleasant than anything else.
Although the thorns thrust into my heart can't be removed so easily, I can still feel the medicine beginning to work its magic on my wound.
"It's just like I said, isn't it? That we would resolve it between ourselves."
The phone's display that Sugiura held out to me showed the name "Yada Mihoko."
"Yeah, yeah… I see… yeah. Oh no, I spoke out of line as well."
"Like I said, don't worry about it! Like I said, let's bring this topic to a close!"
"Oh… so you're holding a party, huh? I see, today's Christmas after all～"
"Me? …Sorry, I'm still at work. I don't think I'll make it."
"Yeah, I'll call you later… I don't think I'll have time to meet up though, I'm working all the way through until the end of the year."
"Yeah, yeah… Well then, I have to get back to work, so…"
"Ah, I almost forgot… Merry Christmas, Mihoko."
"You could have attended, you know. Everyone's at the Christmas party, right?"
"It's just a party in name. They're probably just doing karaoke and having fun like usual."
"It's fine. I've decided that I want to be a companion that you can talk to for today, Senpai."
"I'm happy that I was able to make up with Mihoko. Just being able to talk to her is more than enough for today."
So it's not that "she's become a companion for me to talk to," but rather "she wants to be a companion for me to talk to," is it…
She's really changed, as I thought. She's gradually getting more and more kind before my very eyes.
…Or perhaps it's because I looked so pitiful that she just couldn't stop herself from becoming so kind to me.
"On straightening things out between you and Mihoko."
And she's not just kinderーshe hasn't lost the strength resting at her core either.
"I can't force you two to date each other, but she still looks up to you."
There are parts about her that stay the same, but just as she said, there are also parts of her that are changing little by little.
"I want her to properly accept that and for the two of you to go back to being friends again."
I've come to realize that the girl who I thought was similar to me is actually different, and she's continuing to diverge in her own straightforward direction.
"Because… both of you are precious friends to me."
"Jeez… I don't like the way you are today!"
"I ended up saying something really embarrassing since you keep giving me nothing but half-hearted answers, you know?"
"…My bad. Half-hearted answers are all I can give you today…"
"It's okay. I know that you're pretty hopeless today, Senpai."
Even while saying that, she's kept her smile today.
And it's because of this expression that…
She appears to be even much more attractive than usual… and even more reliable as well.
"Is it okay if I come back to work starting tomorrow?"
"So in other words… you're telling me to stay away from work starting tomorrow?"
It seems she misunderstood what I just said…
No, it's more so the fact that my response jumped ahead so abruptly that it was beyond her line of consideration.
She misunderstood my intention of going back to work as me being considerate of her.
She hasn't picked up on the pathetic intention behind that statement, that I genuinely want to be around everyone… around a certain someone.
"You're hopeless today, so I'll permit it."
"It's just that… I might not be able to… well… restrain myself like usual, so…"
"By all means, please do. We don't have enough manpower until the end of the year, so two people's worth of help would be greatly appreciated."
"Like I said… Don't worry about today."
"Getting angry won't solve anything. Okay, let's agree to stop arguing."
I really am out of it today… I can only give half-hearted responses…
That's why when Sugiura offered her hand, I couldn't do anything but hold onto it without offering any resistance.
"…I quit the tennis club. And given how simply chasing you made me so out of breath, I must be getting really out of shape."
That's why Sugiura was able to conceal her embarrassment quite skillfully.
Though whether or not she's actually good at hiding her embarrassment is another matter entirely.
"Oh… so you're holding a party? I see, today's Christmas after all～"
"Y-Yeah, so would you like to come too, Koharu-chan?"
"Me? …Sorry, I'm still at work. I don't think I'll make it."
"I… see. It's been a while since we've last met."
"Yeah, I'll call you later… I don't think I'll have time to meet up though, I'm working all the way through until the end of the year."
"Your job… seems tough. To be working until this late."
"Yeah, yeah… Well then, I have to get back to work, so…"
"I'm sorry. …I didn't mean to disturb you."
"Ah, I almost forgot… Merry Christmas, Mihoko."
"Alright, the reservation orders for lunch are finished. What's left on your end?"
"Eh? Ah, there's two more jambalayas and a lunch set…"
"…There's not a lot left, then. You can take a break, Honda. I'll take it from here."
"We didn't get as many orders as expected, so Satou and I should be able to manage from here."
"So you didn't leave me out of your calculations…"
"It's common sense for the acting manager to rest last. In fact, you should be thankful that you even have breaks."
"I'm not even second-in-command, let alone the acting manager…"
"But you've even gone as far as to take the evening shift in my place, Kitahara-san."
"It's fine. My plans for the end of the year have been canceled anyway."
"Well, excuse me, then. I'll be taking my break now."
"Well then, the afternoon rush is still going to last for about another hour, huh… Let's finish this quickly."
Despite having only slept for five hours in the past 40 hours, it's more than enough to charge up my stamina.
After all, I'm now calm enough that I can properly sleep again, and my body can now take some well-needed rest.
"Don't look so dissatisfied. You can rest during the next break before me."
"No, I'm not all that concerned about that."
"Is that so? I feel as if you've been giving me a rather cold look since a while ago."
My return to work after canceling my time off for the end of the year was welcomed in a relatively warm manner by all the staff members.
Though I suppose that's because they can't really complain about having an old, valuable veteran of a staff member provide an extra pair of hands during the intense year-end shift.
In any case, I'm grateful that I can go all out at work from the beginning of the day…
I'll be setting a specific goal for myself every hour, and I'll be evaluating myself based on how I perform.

If I manage to achieve my goal, I'll feel the satisfaction and exhaustion from completing it; if I don't, however, I'll reflect on myself, make sure I won't repeat my mistakes, and work harder for the next hour.
"Ask while moving your hands. I won't listen if they stop."
"I know. This skill has been drilled into me by you so much that I'm getting sick of it."
There are two advantages to working like this.
Not only am I able to keep track of my progress, I can focus on my objective and not have to think about anything unnecessary.
"About what happened three days ago… you know, the day when you ended up getting extremely mad at me when we were about to head home and left the whole thing up in the air…"
"Sorry about that! What's wrong with being strict with men? We're men after all!"
"Oh no, I'm not bothered by that anymore, you know. I wouldn't be able to keep working at this restaurant if I let you get on my nerves every time you get mad at me."
"Like I said, have I not apologized for that…?"
He's quite intolerant despite the post he's assigned to…
"Do you remember why you got so mad at me back then?"
"…Two jambalayas and a pork chop are ready."
"You're trying to dodge the question by working even quicker, aren't you?"
"In the first place, weren't you relieved of your year-end shift because Sugiura-san insisted on it, Kitahara-san?"
"Nothing's wrong with that, right? Even Sugiura agreed to let me come to work starting today anyway."
"No, that's exactly what I don't understand. She was extremely forceful in that regard back then…"
"Acting manager! There's something I need you for! Right now!"
"You should head over quickly, Acting Manager. She's calling for you."
Sugiura's "assistance" arrives at the slightest moment later than the perfect time.
This is to be expected, though; she's made a promise with me, after all.
"Answer within five seconds after you're called! That's what the training manual specifically says, right?"
She promised she would protect me.
"Please think about the way you're treating your subordinates. Sooner or later you're going to be promoted to branch manager, Acting Manager Satou."
"I feel as if my ranking in this restaurant has finally dropped below 4th place…"
"Anyway, try not to pry into Senpai's affairs unnecessarily. All the same, do make the effort to strike some casual conversation with him."
"Just make some small talk with him. Talk about things like entertainment, literature, arts, sports, fashion, nature…"
"However, I ask that you strictly avoid talking about your love lives."
"Is Kitahara-san having trouble with women or something?"
"I didn't mention so much as a single word that would suggest that, did I!?"
"I haven't heard anything like that. It's just that he doesn't look so well, so I'm unnecessarily worrying about him."
"In any case, I don't know anything. Well, I am a little concerned, but his relationships with other women have nothing to do with me."
"…Well, in that case, I could just casually ask him about it."
"Please make no attempt to do that. What in the world are you thinking, attempting to step into Senpai's affairs while casting me aside like this?"
"This doesn't feel like I'm talking to a subordinate at all…"
"You really let me see something amazing today…"
"I have never seen anyone spoil Kitahara-san before, or at least not in this restaurant…"
"Isn't it natural to nurse someone who's not feeling well, no matter how much you dislike them?"
"This is the first time I heard someone other than Kitahara-san say something like that…"
"…Anyway, there's absolutely nothing going on between Senpai and me like you seem to think. I'm sorry for disappointing you."
"During times like this, aren't you supposed to go all red and say, 'I-It's not like I like him or anything!' in an attempt to hide your embarrassment?"
"Mmnn～ You're no fun, Koharucchi. You could have given me a more innocent reaction."
"Please don't refer to me in such a nonsensical way. Iiyama-san also addressed me that way before, but I see now that you were the one behind it?"
"It's because I've been telling the others about these things that everyone's able to feel familiar with you. You could at least be a little grateful for that…"
"I don't plan to get along with everyone in my workplace."
"Wouldn't it be better to get along with everyone, especially since it's your workplace? Well, I guess that's too hard for you to understand, Koharucchi."
"…If you say that, then what about Kitahara-senpai?"
"He never goes out of his way to get close to anyone, but he isn't really averse when others want to get close to each other, you know?"
"You're avoiding the question, aren't you? You've intentionally left out something, have you not?"
"He never goes out of his way to get close to anyone. He isn't really averse when others want to get close to each other, either. …Then what if someone wants to get close to him?"
"Tanicchi-san, was it? Wasn't she trying her best to get close to Senpai? And what happened then?"
"Let me ask again. How can you explain the situation with Kitahara-senpai, given what you just said?"
"The wound Senpai received is much deeper than we could imagine. Although it's hard to notice because he's usually gloomy to begin with."
"I suppose it's just that I'm a little more aware about that fact than everyone else somehow."
"You'll nurse someone when they're not feeling well, right? Accordingly, is it not natural to want to tend to someone when there's pain in their heart?"
"But you just had to jump to love and affection… I hate simple thinking like that. Senpai isn't just a man to me, he's a perso… ah."
"You set me up, didn't you? Your little charade earlier… You intentionally said something incorrect so that I would retort and accidentally say something stupid."
"You really are smart, Koharucchi. That's the first time someone actually saw through my trap."
"Respecting someone as a person is also a form of love, right? And pitying someone is also a form of affection, is it not?"
"Is Kitahara-san not waiting for you at the Bonanza across the street?"
"Unfortunately, I have something else I need to do today… I have an important meeting alone with a guy."
"You don't mind me tattling on you to Kitahara-san, do you?"
"Be my guest. It's not like there's anything between us."
"Hmm, well… She only talked to Io on the phone, so we still don't know the details."
"That's fine. Even the slightest detail we have can be really valuable right now."
"If we are to take her words at face value, there's nothing. She just said 'nothing happened,' and no more than that."
"See? It doesn't tell you anything, right?"
"So, was there anything else that you gathered other than what she said?"
"Beating around the bush like this means that there's still something you haven't said, right?"
"Do all people start to speak in riddles when they become university students? …I really don't like that, to be honest."
"You must have a knack for conversations like these if you've managed to see through me immediately."
"How is Ogiso-senpai doing? That's all I want to ask."
"…At the very least, I think Setsuna-chan is blaming herself for this."
"I think there's a disconnect between them. One that's much worse than anything that's happened between them up until now."
"Haruki has always been the one running away, but this time it seems like it's the other way around…"
"Why…? Didn't you say that both of them still have feelings for each other…"
"That hasn't changed. I have no doubt about it."
"However… that's not all there is to it. There's more to what happened between those two within the past three years."
"That's all I know for now. Now it's your turn."
"I didn't ask him anyway. I promised him that I wouldn't ask anything."
"If Senpai wants to talk about it, I'll be there. That's the promise we made."
"Didn't you say you would do anything to make him talk? You were even so confident about him being obliged to tell you everything, given how you were the one who set all this up…"
"Ah, there's something else that I should make clear…"
"I'll have you know that even if Senpai did happen to explain everything to me, whether I'm willing to talk to you two about it is a different matter entirely, Iizuka-senpai."
"Dealing with Senpai as he is right now is a bit difficult…"
"Are things… really that bad on his end?"
"What I want to say is, even if you're his close friend from high school, I'd like you to avoid doing anything that would hurt him from now on."
"W-Wait a minute! How could I ever do anything that would hurt Haruki?"
"You said so yourself just now, right? Io and I have known Haruki for over six years…"
"You've been friends with Ogiso-senpai for a long time too, right?"
"That's why you don't want to hurt her either, right, Iizuka-senpai?"
"In that case, when the time comes when you have to choose which side you're on, wouldn't you have a hard time deciding between them?"
"This isn't a problem for me, though… After all, I've had no interactions with Ogiso-senpai whatsoever."
"There should be at least one person siding with him… Though I might be even more unreliable than some court-appointed attorney."
"What's the matter? Did I say something weird?"
"Don't get involved in this matter any further."
"…What are you saying all of a sudden?"
"Just leave the rest of this to us. Don't worry, those two will definitely make up."
"What's wrong with you? You're acting weird all of a sudden."
"It's my fault, is it not? I've done nothing but back them into a corner because of my shortsighted plan…"
"But didn't you do that with his best interest in mind? You don't need to feel guilty about it, Koharu-chan."
"It's not because I feel guilty about it, it's that I have a responsibility to help him get back on his feet."
"That's why I told you to leave it to us."
"I won't accept that under any circumstance. I'll take responsibility for my own actions."
"Yeah, yeah… that's right, it's about them."
"I've realized it'll be really bad if we don't act quickly. Things will take a turn for the worse if we don't patch them up immediately…"
"Eh? Ah, no. I still haven't contacted Haruki."
"I… think I might have made a fatal error in judgement."
"I've made sure that the windows and doors are locked."
"Okay, I'll turn off the lights, then. You can go out first."
Turning off the last of the lighting that's illuminating the hall, the interior of the store sinks into darkness.
As a result, I proceed carefully from the power switch to the exit since I can barely make out what's right in front of me.
If I were ever to be entrusted with this restaurant, I swear I'd propose the improvement of installing the power switch right next to the exit.
"…Still, it's kind of a waste. We would've been able to turn a real profit if we continued to stay open."
Sugiura lets out a sigh as she notices the unimaginable amount of people passing by the path in front of the restaurant, despite the fact that the date is about to change.
"I get what you mean, but… it's just impossible for us to extend our opening hours, even if only on New Year's Eve. The restaurant doesn't have permission to stay open that late to begin with."
"More importantly, we don't even have anyone who's willing to work during the transition to the new year."
With the exception of the people currently present, that is.
"I think it's from Suetsugu Hachiman Shrine."
Sugiura and I head toward the station, against the flow of the massive crowd that's bustling in Minami-Suetsugu for their annual shrine visit.
In the end, we've done nothing but work from dawn till dusk all week.
We started with the morning shift and worked until the end of the evening shift, working overtime and earning extra money as much as we wanted.

Our branch manager would have advised against it, but given our current acting manager's lack of overall influence, along with the fact that the restaurant is lacking staff during this time of year, we were allowed that exception.
In any case, anyone would be grateful to have two reliable assets that could be counted on out there in the field during this time of year.
"Just fifteen minutes left until the end of the year."
Sugiura ensured that her name was always next to mine for all shifts throughout the new year periodーmorning and evening shifts alikeー as if it were the most natural thing in the world for her to do.
It's not like I asked her to do so. And I'm sure Sugiura doesn't think that she's been asked to either.
Even so, despite the fact that it invites the suspicion of those around her, she seems to continue making this mistake without any hesitation… No, I wouldn't call it a mistake.
"It's not every day that it's New Year's Eve, so why don't we visit the shrine for the occasion? It's right behind the university, isn't it?"
She wants to welcome the new year alone with someone like me… and continue spending time together after that?
"It's fine. The trains today will run until morning. …The railway industry knows full well that this is the best time to make more profit."
Without any sign of hesitation, she innocently tugs on the hem of my coat.
"Not at all. I only waited here for 4 minutes and 45 seconds."
"…Why did you keep track of how long I took so specifically?"
"Isn't it obvious? It's used for evidence when people keep me waiting for too long."
"No, I'm just surprised to see someone do the exact same thing I would so close by."
The shrine visit ended pretty quickly without anything happening.
Suetsugu Hachiman Shrine, which wasn't particularly big nor famous, could be visited within ten minutes comfortably.
"Leaving that aside, what did you buy? If it's a fortune slip, let me take a look."
"I just don't like the idea of having my life be determined by fortune-telling. But I am interested in others' fortunes just as much as anyone else, you know?"
"That's a rather complicated way of thinking about it."
On our way home, she made a similar sarcastic remark when I decided to line up at one of the stalls in the vicinity to pick up a good luck charm.
…I wouldn't have minded it if I was the only one who heard it, but I think she went out of her way to make sure everyone around me did.
"They wouldn't actually put any 'bad fortune' slips in there, right? Then again, I doubt you'd pull a 'great fortune' one with how things've been going for you…
You definitely drew a 'small fortune'! Am I right!?"
"I'm aware that I don't have much luck right now. So I won't spend money on things that involve gambling."
That's why, even if I give her something like this, I might just get laughed at like before.
"You're going to be taking entrance exams, right, Sugiura?"
Even so, she accepted the tiny piece of cloth I offered her in the palms of her small hands.
"Do your best… though I imagine you'll still end up being my junior as a result."
"…You know I have a recommendation, right? It essentially confirms that I will be, you know?"
"But you'll still do your best, right? So having this around won't do you any harm… Well, it'd defeat the purpose completely if it did do you harm."
And then, her eyes become fixated on the small piece of cloth in her hand.
"Well, let's head back for real this time. I'll take you home."
And she followed behind me with small, brisk steps without giving me her usual "Alright!" in response, looking as if she were a little taken aback.
"By the way, Sugiura, what did you wish for? You said it wasn't about your exams, but you looked pretty passionate about it."
"You threw in 500 yen coins at the shrine, after all. Two of them, no less."
"You don't believe in fortune telling, but you sure are generous with your prayers."
To be honest, since she laughed when I lined up at the shrine stall, I waited for the perfect time to comment on her wasteful spending.
"That's because… it's about something that is out of my control."
"Yeah… I was frustrated by my own incompetence, so I had no choice but to rely on God."
"That's why I invited you out. So I could tell God 'This is the person!' and let Him see your face."
"What I wished was… 'For Kitahara Haruki to cheer up again.'"
For better or worse, this girl can't help being straightforward.
"You should at least pray for yourself during the first shrine visit of the year. You're taking entrance exams, are you not?"
"This is for myself, you know? Right now, this is the most important thing to me."
I mustn't read too much into it… There's no way she could say it so confidently otherwise.
"When we chat like this, it feels like you're back to normal, but somehow it feels a little different than usual."
"I don't want you to talk like you know everything about me. We've only known each other for a month."
I was just replying with the exact same retort that she used against me, but for some reason, I still felt guilty about it.
"Do you know what kind of emotions I've been harboring this entire week? Do you… Do you even…"
"That's why I said I'm sorry. I get it, I lose."
There's no way I could've won against her at this moment.
"It's not that I'm concerned about winning or losing… That's not what I'm trying to say…"
"Would you listen to what I have to say, Sugiura?"
"Before I can talk about what happened last week, I have to start with what happened three years ago."
"It all started at the school festival concert three years ago. The one in the video that you've seen."
"Back when I was in the same grade as you, I joined the Light Music Club, even though it hardly suited me."
From her silence I knew that I should keep going, so I continued with my story little by little.
The days when I was just like Sugiura Koharu.
I truthfully told her everything, starting from the very beginning.
I told her about not only Ogiso-senpai, whom she was familiar with, but also Touma-senpai, whom Sugiura had only known from rumors here and there.
I told her about how Kitahara-senpai experienced immense joy on the night before the school festival, in a way that was unimaginable to her given her impression of me.
I told her about the incident that happened around this time of the year three years ago, where those enjoyable days gradually slipped away from our hands.
I told her about Setsuna's old wounds, wounds that I've neglected and have yet to heal to this day.
I told her about the past three years I've spent selfishly running away from her, unwilling to come face to face with the wounds I've wrought upon her even as she smiled for me.

I told her about how I've even gone as far as to run away from anything that would remind me of what happened three years ago, which caused me to hurt not only her, but many others as well during the past three years.
I told her about how the two of us had gone along with Sugiura's plan and arrived at what seemed to be a final chance for the two of us.
I told her about how we desperately tried to turn away from the past and attempted to seize the present for us to start anew, to acquire a future that we could share together.
…And I told her about how the spider's thread that bound our hands together snapped at the very moment I was caught in the act of being insincere.
"They say you can feel a burden lifted off your shoulders once you divulge everything to someone… That's a lie."
"You just end up remembering it all again. The dizziness, the nausea, the chills creeping onto you… along with the unstoppable sensation of sweat dating to days past."
From the platform of Minami-Suetsugu Station, all the way inside the train, and even through the route from Minegaya Station to Sugiura's house…
Sugiura did not say so much as a single word throughout this completely one-sided conversation.
Her gaze was lowered the whole time, staring at the tactile pavement tiles on the platform, the floor of the train, and the asphalt road.
"Still, you know, I suppose it's an improvement for me to be able to tell someone else about this. …Though I suppose I may have just done something terrible to Setsuna yet again."
Even so, I definitely wouldn't be telling this to someone I don't consider a friend.
"To act so depressed over this even though it was all my fault… I really am an idiot, aren't I?"
While I'm at it, this story is so cruel that it's even difficult to divulge it to someone who's more than a friend to me.
"Even so, it was really traumatic for me… to the point where I might have ended up breaking down if you hadn't helped me, Sugiura."
It's because I consider her a friend that I'm able to confess my sins. That I'm able to ask for forgiveness.
It's because she's important to me despite being nothing more than a friend…
"Thank you for all you've done until now, Sugiura. But know that I'm alright now."
It's not that I'm alright because I've talked to her about this. It's because I'm alright now that I was able to talk to her about this.
Even so, the fact that I'm even capable of talking about this in itself is all thanks to the girl right in front of me, who has continued to support me for the past few days.
It's all thanks to this fellow junior of mine who has quietly watched over me and done her best to be patient with me, all while desperately suppressing her meddlesome and curious disposition.
"…What are you going to do from now on?"
"Honestly, I don't know yet, but I think I'll try to talk with her one more time."
"You're planning to meet her again? Ogiso-senpai, I mean."
"I have no intention of letting the problem fade away on its own. More importantly, I'd be insincere toward Setsuna if I didn't do this."
That's why I have to take the initiative and do somethingーwhether it's to part ways with Setsuna or to return things to the way they were before.
I have to do this for Setsuna. And I have to do this for my newest friend, who has devoted herself to protecting me up until now.
I imagine that it's difficult for Sugiura to understand the ups and downs that have transpired in my life, given her own thoroughly straightforward experiences.
Well, I guess it's only natural that she doesn't understand it.
After all, even I've come to question and reflect on why I've made those choices for the past three years.
"But that's just what I have to do…"
"I think… I'm starting to hate Ogiso-senpai."
Sugiura's dark, trembling voice shatters the thoughts I'd established in my mind.
"Even though you didn't give up this time, Senpai. Even though you've done your best to move forward."
I thought that Sugiura would surely blame me. I believed that it would be natural for her to do so.
"Even though you've faced Ogiso-senpai just like she and I wished for."
But the person who's causing Sugiura to shake in anger isn't among us right now, but someone who I've only described in my story…
"And yet… for her to shake off your hand this time the very moment you finally reached out to her… I just can't understand why she did that to you at all!"
The person who the meddlesome Sugiura had worked so hard for all this time… happened to be none other than Setsuna herself.
"Why are you apologizing, Senpai? Are you apologizing on behalf of Ogiso-senpai!?"
"It's not like that. I just think you're misunderstanding something, Sugiura. I'm sure it's because I explained it badly…"
This is my fault. Sugiura's losing sight of her own goal because of me…
"I'm not misunderstanding anything. Ogiso-senpai decided to hurt you, Kitahara-senpai. All so she could pay you back for what happened three years ago."
I must have unconsciously twisted the story in a shameless way of defending myself for Sugiura to have misunderstood all of this. I'm sure of it…
"What exactly about your current story suggests that you're in the wrong here, Senpai!?"
"Like I said, I've been hurting Setsuna all this time…"
"And haven't you known that fact all this time!?"
It's been a while since I've seen this. …Sugiura Koharu has completely snapped.
I'm now seeing her true nature, the face of a meddlesome girl who gets more passionate than the person involved.
"If she's not able to forgive you for that, she shouldn't have asked to meet up with you in the first place! She never should have acted as if she still had lingering affections for you!"
"You can't work this out through logical reasoning alone… Haven't I said that numerous times already?"
"I won't accept that. This time, without a doubt, it's her fault. You did nothing wrong, Senpai!"
"Then are you saying it's my fault, Senpai!?"
"…What are you talking about? You're not involved in this, are you?"
"Then what do I have to do to be involved!?"
This is the first time I'm seeing this. …Sugiura Koharu is being irrational.
It's rare for someone as smart as her to not think things through and just pour out all of her feelings.
"Sugiura… you're just investing too much of your emotions into me right now…"
"A-And what are you trying to suggest by saying that…!"
This is also a first for me…
Sugiura Koharu is lashing out at me despite having partially returned to her senses after realizing how emotional she's being, refusing to back down on what she'd just said.
"In any case, you're not in the wrong, Senpai, no matter what anyone says. I won't accept that you are."
Sugiura ran away with all her might, and I was no longer able to catch up to her amidst the darkness.

However, I managed to find Sugiura's residence by memory, and I was relieved to have coincidentally caught sight of the lights of her front gate being turned off and the lights of a room on the second floor turning on.
I wasn't able to see her home until the end, but it seems that she managed to reach home safely.
It's not every day that it's New Year's Eve and we get to visit a shrine.
It's not every day that I confess my sins, either, and in the end, we ended up having an inconclusive argument because of it.
Me aside, I'm sure Sugiura is also looking rather dejected, sighing while telling herself that things weren't supposed to turn out this way.
Things weren't supposed to turn out this way.
Oh well… I'll just apologize first thing tomorrow.
After all, we'll definitely see each other tomorrow.
I believe that she isn't so irresponsible that she would willingly take a break from work over something like this.
"Good night, Sugiura. See you… later today…"
Before I realized it, the New Year's bell rang, and it's already past 1 AM.
Even though I made up my mind to apologize to her first thing in the morning today, she completely beat me to it.
The moment I tried to enter the changing room so I could wait for Sugiura… just five seconds before now.
She pushed me into the room and locked the door from the inside.
"Last night, I… umm… said a lot of terrible things."
I initially planned to come more than 30 minutes earlier and be the first to arrive at the restaurant, knowing that Sugiura would definitely be the next to arrive after me.
But it seems I was too naive. …I have no doubt she came at least one hour before everyone and waited for me.
"Even though we promised not to argue… I couldn't even keep such a simple promise…"
Where did that exasperated look from last night go…
I thought she would've just calmed down after a night's sleep, but she appears to be extremely disheartened right now.
"I'm really sorry. I've reflected on my actions. I'm… truly reflecting on what I've done."
…No, from how red her eyes are looking, whether or not she even had a night's sleep is up for question.
I imagine that negative thoughts were swirling inside her mind the whole time, much like what I experienced a week ago.
…And all because of a quarrel where both parties were in the wrong and suffered over it.
"So… please don't hate me… I'd be really grateful if you didn't hate me, so…"
I feel like I've heard those words somewhere before. Words stemming from a juxtaposition of pain, embarrassment, sorrow and joy.
She's not merely being kind. She's not just being reliable. Nor is she simply being fussy about this.
She is so frail she resembled a small animal for the slightest moment, but that only added to just how charming she was.
"No, umm… I should be thanking you."
At a time like this, phrases like "it's not your fault", or "it was my fault", or "you don't have any reason to apologize" are meaningless.
I have to respond to her with the words she wants to hear the most, no matter how arrogant and selfish it may be for me to say them.
"Let's consider this matter settled, then! Everyone will be arriving soon, so let's get ready to open, shall we?"
I personally still feel rather uncomfortable with the fact that I've not managed to apologize to her at all, but given how our exchange proceeded, I suppose there's nothing I can do about it…
"Umm… I know it might be unfair of me to bring this up despite how you want to leave it in the dust, but…"
And right as soon as I say that…
"Just as I said before, I still don't think you were at fault, Kitahara-senpai. …That's the only thing I won't back down on."
The truth is, Sugiura might not be all that different right now compared to how she was last night.
"So please don't say things like, 'it was all my fault' again. I also ask this so that I won't break the promise we made again."
I actually have no doubt about it.
Sugiura Koharu is still the same meddlesome woman who laid bare her stubbornness and personal feelings last night.
Alright, let's start this year's first shift…"
"In that case, let me say one more thing as well."
I won't be saying this to Sugiura while seeing her as a friend or junior…
I wanted to express my gratitude to Sugiura-san while seeing her for the girl she is.
"Perhaps… you're the one and only person in the world who will stand up for me, Sugiura."
With that proclamation based only on my emotions, I wanted to convey this feeling of gratitude that wasn't based on reason.
"Only you can do that for someone like me, who doesn't even want to stand up for himself…"
I wonder if I'm putting on a kind smile right now.
Or maybe I look too serious, which made the words I just said lack credibility.
…That being said, the only way to know how I look right now is to look straight into her eyes, focusing on the reflection from her pupils.
I look so twisted in her eyes.
What the hell. It doesn't look convincing at all.
I can't look like this. Sugiura won't believe anything I tell her if she's faced with this.
The two of us realize simultaneously that something's wrong.
We realize that the very moment my twisted reflection in Sugiura's eyes falls and spills onto the floor.
"No, no way, no way… It won't stop… This is… This is so strange…"
The possibility that sprung to my mind was immediately confirmed by the second and third droplets that fell from her eyes.
Spilling onto the floor, dripping down her cheeks, welling up inside her eyes…
Her tears flow out uncontrollably… for no reason, but that can't be true all the same.
"It's so sad… It's so frustrating… Why would you say something like that…?"
"Saying that you don't like yourself… That besides me, you have no one who will stand up for you…"
What would sadden the class representative known as Sugiura Koharu the most would be the fact that there's a single classmate who's left alone in the classroom.
"Don't say things like that…! I don't want you to say things like that…!"
"S-Sorry! I won't say it anymore! I won't say it anymore, so please… Sugiura…"
"I'm begging you, seriously… Everyone will be here soon…"
There was nothing I could've done after that.
The dam holding back her tears collapsed and synchronized with the pent-up emotions stirring within her since last night, causing Sugiura to break down even more.
And I could only remain in place about 30 centimeters away from her, unable to leave her alone or approach her as she could no longer hold back her tears.
Satou and the others gradually arrived a few minutes later, and an unforgettable misunderstanding was etched into their minds.
Despite having fallen into such a tragic situation, I still felt a pleasant warmth spreading across my chest.
Why was she able to cry from the bottom of her heart for the sake of a friend that she had only made just recently…?
Even though the answer was right in front of my eyes, I never stopped wondering about it in my heart.
"It's finally our last year as students, huh? Well, assuming that we're not going to graduate school, that is."

"I know it's a difficult time right now given that there's a lot we have to decide on, from graduation, our line of work, and how we're going to live from now on, but I hope neither of us will come to regret our decision."
"…I'm really not pushing myself too hard, you know. I really mean that."
"By the way… I'm sorry about my late New Year's greeting."
"There's been quite a lot on my mind recently, which is why I've put off sending you even a single text for so long."
"In any case, I'm alright for now… Well, I suppose I can't really say for sure, but at the very least, I'm still living out my life as I usually do."
"I haven't had any time to relax at all given that I've been working non-stop throughout the New Year's holidays, but with the way I am now, I actually feel better keeping myself busy."
"Let's talk again after we've both calmed down. …That's really all I wanted to say today."
"Not at all. Rather, I'd say you've changed clothes really quickly for a girl."
Sugiura suddenly rushed out from the back door, denying me any time to further revise my text.
"Are my clothes or hair messy? I ended up being a lot less attentive than usual…"
She asks me that question as she turns around in front of me.
"Well, you could have just taken your time to tend to yourself before asking me to make sure…"
Her long ponytail swishes right in front of me, giving me a pleasant sensation whenever it brushes against my nose and cheeks.
"I'll leave it all up to you, Senpai. I don't have any particular preferences at all."
Today's the last day of winter break for both Houjou High and University.
School's going to be starting tomorrow, and I found myself inviting Sugiura out for dinner as thanks for her dedicated care of me throughout the holidays…
I brought it up on our way home last night.
It had been a final, additional remark to our usual banter, and the moment I suggested that we leave after the morning shift, she began to tinker with her mobile phone rather intensely.
And after fifteen minutes… she managed to find two substitutes for us with her unrelenting persuasion, thus confirming our auspicious arrangement.
After that, however, we were harshly told off for not asking for their help a few days in advance.
"Okay, how about we go to Onjuku? There's an Italian restaurant there that was used for a get-together for my seminar before."
"Yeah, their dinner courses are pretty sizable and tasty…"
"A full-course meal!? I don't have the money to afford that. And I've been working part-time for the trip with my friends, so…"
"It's my treat of course. I'm the one who invited you for this, after all, and I'm your senior as well. But above all, I wanted to thank you today…"
"It's even worse if someone else is paying for it! I'll just end up getting stressed out if I can't pay for my own share."
"…You could afford to be a little less humble, you know."
"I mean it, please, don't waste any money on me. I imagine you already have lots of expenses of your own to cover since you're living by yourself, Senpai."
You're not leaving the decision to me whatsoever, and you're trying to go out of your way to cover your share when I'm saying it's my treat…
Really, it's astonishing just how meddlesome she can be. She'll surely become the prime example of a "good wife and a wise mother" in the future…
The image pops up in my head, but I'm not sure if it's for better or worse.
"How about our Goodies then? We don't even have to waste time traveling."
"If we order a set and use refills off the drink bar, we can hang out there for hours."
"How would you feel if a customer stayed for hours just by refilling their drink?"
"Come on, isn't it the customer who's always right?"
I wonder how aware Sugiura actually is about the situation given how innocently she's smiling at me…
I'm referring to the rumors about us that are circulating among the staff of the restaurant.
…Or perhaps I should say that they used to be rumors, as they've become common knowledge by now.
"Then, want to go to the Bonanza across the street? The Spaghetti Bolognese there is quite a good deal, you know?"
"We'll be in plain sight of our restaurant if we go there as well…"
Apart from the fact that we've had nearly the exact same shifts from morning to evening shifts for the past two weeks, there was also that particular incident on New Year's morning…
But Sugiura doesn't pay any mind to the noise surrounding her, much like she did in the past.
"As long as the both of us are on the same page, what others say doesn't matter to us at all."

She might be fine with it, but I wish she'd put herself in my shoes, given all the teasing I get from Nakagawa-san, all the concessions I have to make for Satou, and all the awkward looks I get from the rest of the staff.
…I say that, but I actually do understand.
For me right now, that kind of easy-going atmosphere is important as it gently protects my heart.
"So, have you saved up enough money yet?"
"I guess I've saved up about 70% of it… I have the feeling that I'll just barely make it before the trip."
In the end, we went to Onjuku and had Tom Yum Goong at a small Asian restaurant.

My assumption that such a cheap-looking restaurant would be enough to fool even Sugiura's vigilance ended up being correct. …However, despite its appearance, I knew that this wasn't a cheap establishment at all.
She shot me a glare upon examining the prices on the menu, but I had her where I wanted her by then.
"The day after the graduation ceremony. At the beginning of March."
"If I remember correctly, you're going on an eight-day trip to Spain, Italy, and France, right?"
"We talked about stopping by Austria as well, by the way.
It could be like a tour to meet Touma Kazusa-senpai in Vienna!"
"But since we don't know her address or concert schedule, we gave up on it in the end."
"Serves you right for bringing me to an expensive restaurant. And after I went out of my way to tell you not to do this.
I thought I had her where I wanted, but…
"O-Oh, right, call me before you leave. I want to give you a farewell gift."
"Like I said, please don't waste your money unnecessarily. Your earnings are already going toward your living expenses."
"It's not wasteful at all. It's a gift in exchange for a souvenir."
"Ah, no… Just prioritize your friends first. You don't have to force yourself to get something. Even a weird-looking keychain from that area is enough."
My collection is about to exceed the number of fingers on one hand.
"Ah, no, that's not what I meant…"
"Does that mean… I can look forward to seeing you after graduation?"
The question had a bit of an unusual spin to it, coming from the usually straight-pitching Sugiura…
"Well, I mean… We'll be attending the same university when April arrives, right?"
"Even if we're in the same university, we'll still be in different years, won't we?"
"If we're in the same department, that means we'll be in the same building as well. We'll definitely see each other often in the hallways and such."
Although I couldn't keep up with her flimsy curveball, I managed to get away with a foul.
"Still, we'll be in totally different lectures. We'll only be able to meet for a short time during lunch break, right?"
"If you make it to fourth year… will you be quitting your current part-time job?"
Up next, she throws a straight, but rather high waste pitch.
However, it wasn't as sharp as her usual throws.
"…Well, I'll have to start job hunting soon, and I'll have to start writing my graduation thesis, too."
"You're right… That's true. I'm sorry, forget I asked."
As I dodge her questions with ease, she becomes so disheartened it's almost sad.
"B-But, I'll make sure to show up from time to time. I'll still need to continue working part-time every now and then."
Even though I try to follow up with, "Nevertheless, it was a good throw," it does nothing to cheer her up.
Where did all that excitement of hers from earlier go…?
With an expression so sullen it's hard for me to watch, Sugiura stares at her food and pokes at it without even taking so much as a bite.
To be honest, I don't want her to make an expression like that. …Even I'm feeling lonely seeing her like this.
A light sound of a notification silences the conversation we're having, as if to further exacerbate the situation.
"Happy New Year. And thanks for the text."
"I'm also sorry for the late greeting."
"I've been hesitating a lot. …I wonder if I even have the right to talk to you right now."
"That's why I'm grateful that you texted me. Really, thank you so much."
"I'm also living out my life like I usually do."
"Even now, I still think about what happened back then every single day. It pains me every time I think about it, though."
"Even so, I still wake up early in the morning and eat my breakfast like usual. And tomorrow I'll start going to university as usual."
"If we happen to end up meeting each other on campus, can I call out to you? And if you see me, could you call out to me?"
"Well then, good night. See you tomorrow."
It's not something I need to hide. Rather, it's not something I should be hiding.
After all, Sugiura had delightedly showed me the display of her phone showing that she was receiving a call from Yada-san back then.
Naturally, she'll be delighted about the fact that we're beginning to repair our relationship, even if only by a little bit.
"So… will you be meeting with her? Ogiso-senpai, I mean."
Unlike the last time, both the recipient and the person delivering the news look to be rather dejected.
"…It's thanks to you, Sugiura. When you told me that I wasn't in the wrong, I managed to gather the courage to contact Setsuna."
"I still feel regretful even now. However, I no longer feel that I can't face her."
"I've only decided to meet her. Nothing has actually started yet."
I wasn't able to put any emotion into that "Thank you."
Because I was so thrown off by the absolute lack of emotion she showed when she said, "I pray for your success."
"…Thanks for the meal. It was very spicy and hot, but it was also really delicious."
That's why I stand up from my seat as if I'm trying to escape.
I can't explain the uncomfortable feeling coming over me.
I'm honestly scared to think about Sugiura's slightly strange expression, which is different from her usual expressions of either anger or genuine concern.
"Have you already made up with Yada-san?"
"…We haven't been in contact since then."
"…It seems that she's on vacation with her family. She won't pick up no matter how many times I try to reach her."
"Whatever it is, she should be back soon. School starts tomorrow after all."
"Try calling her again when you get home…"
"Right now is not the time for this, is it? Your chance has finally come… after all."
"Anyway… I'm not in the mood for this discussion right now. I'm sorry."
My assumption is merely an act of me following my own intuition, and I imagine that it's a ridiculously false impression and an absurd misunderstanding.
But if what I'm assuming is neither false nor a misunderstanding, then…
"Tomorrow is a new school term, right…?"
We got off at Minegaya and walked to her house together, which took about fifteen minutes.
"You're going to university tomorrow too, right, Senpai?"
Right now, no one will blame me for going about this in such a roundabout way. No one will think that I'm wrong for doing what I'm doing right now.
However, it's only natural for my feelings to have become numb after all this.
"We won't be able to meet for a week starting from tomorrow, right…?"
We've spent the last few days together from dawn till dusk, after all. That's all there is to it.
That's why I'm sure that the warm numbness that's been building between us will cool and fade away again once we stop seeing each other on a daily basis.
Or rather, that's just how things must be.
"What should I do if I head over to Goodies tomorrow by mistake…?"
"I won't make that mistake. Since tomorrow my upperclassmen have their graduation thesis rehearsal."
We should preserve our relationship as "Sugiura and Kitahara-senpai." We mustn't become "Koharu and Haruki-senpai." We absolutely cannot.
There's too much at stake for the both of us to lose if that were ever to happen.
After all, we were never supposed to develop in such a way after meeting one another.
"Thank you very much for today. …It made me very happy."
"That was hardly enough to repay what you've done for me."
"When will… you come to work next?"
"…Sorry. I haven't decided yet. I've got final exams starting at the end of the month, after all."
That's why… today is the last day we can be together alone.
I won't go out of my way to meet her anymore. I'll also show up around Goodies less and less from now on.
This has nothing to do with her. It's to cool my own fever.
To think that I've come to feel lonely in the absence of the girl I've only been around to distract myself from my loneliness…
I'm really not setting my priorities straight here.
But there's nothing I can do about that, right?
We've been together every day from morning to evening for quite some time.
I've been watching her and her variety of constantly changing expressions all the while, and that alone has been enough to make me get back on my feet again.
…It's only natural to harbor such strong feelings toward her, right?
"I'll show you that I can immediately get a boyfriend after enrolling at university…"
As usual, I woke up at 6:30, took a warm shower, got dressed, had breakfast, and left my apartment at my own leisurely pace.
Such is my daily lifestyle that is no different from before the winter break. Such is my lifestyle that hasn't changed at all these past three years.
"That's only half right. …I was thinking that you'd arrive about 30 minutes before the first lecture, Haruki-kun."
And Setsuna seems to have grasped that particular habit of mine as if it were the most natural thing for her to do.
She's even grasped my intent to return to my usual self starting from today.
"For not greeting you sooner. …I hope we'll get along this year too."
"Is it weird for me to apologize to you?"
"Yeah, it is. Even so, it's still very much like you, Haruki-kun."
I can't say I'm sure whether we're actually meshing well together…
Nonetheless, the first time we're spending time with one another this year has begun smoothly, as if a certain event had never even happened at all.
"Did you visit your mother for the first three days this year?"
"It's like I wrote in my text. All I did was repeat the same cycle of waking up early in the morning, working until late at night, and going to bed as soon as I got home."
Setsuna sighs ever so subtly as she understands what I'm entailing from the answer I gave to her question, knowing full well about the distant relationship I have with my mother.
"We went to visit my paternal and maternal grandparents. …Since they don't live that far away, it was just a one-day trip, though."
I feel a mix of faint relief and envy as her answer is enough to tell me that she's back to her usual self, knowing full well about the close bonds Setsuna shares with her family.
Our exchange is shallow yet deep at the same time…
Despite merely exchanging greetings typical for a special occasion, our conversation is filled with intricacies that no one other than the two of us can understand…
"Well, I'll be heading this way now."
The 50-meter walk from the main gate ended in the blink of an eye.
That's because we have to take opposite paths after we reach the first intersection from the main gate, given that our own school buildings are on the south and the north, respectively.
But things are best left transient between us for now. What we have between us is just right for the moment.
We know from experience that if we try to hastily close the distance between one another, we'll end up rejecting one another unexpectedly.
As I stood in place to see her off, Setsuna turned back to glance at me several times, and then finally waved her hand at me.
I stood there until I could no longer see her… though I thought of how she'd probably feel uncomfortable about me doing that, so I stayed until she no longer turned back to look at me again.
"You've made up with each other, I see."
As I wallow in my loneliness and lethargy so early in the morning, a voice calls out to me that ends up immediately perking me up in a particular way.
"Happy New Year, Haruki～! I've taken good care of you in various ways last year, so I'm looking forward to you returning the favor this year～"
For her of all people to have actually caught us… Not to mention just how ridiculous her New Year's greeting was.
"Even so, you were quite cold during the winter break, huh, Haruki? You didn't even think to invite me out even once."
"That's because I seem to always end up being stuck in my own room with you every time I agree for us to hang out."
"And here I thought I was going to be able to eat the Christmas cake you made, as well as all the New Year's treats like soba, osechi, zouni, and shichigusa-gayu～"
"You didn't have to validate my concerns so brazenly…"
"Well, I suppose for the sake of making it up to me and for me to not say another word on the matter, let's go get the morning special!"
"I have to attend a lecture now. Besides, the coffee house is far away from here."
"The cafeteria is fine too, you know～? Since you'll be treating me to breakfast."
"So that's what you meant by morning special…?"
"Alright, let's go, let's go to the cafeteria! It'll be nice to have rice with miso soup, raw egg, natto, and curry～!"
As I stand in place and resist her, Izumi tightly links her arm with mine and tugs me in the direction of the cafeteria.
"You should attend lectures once in a while. Why do you even bother waking up early and coming to university?"
"Well, I just woke up in the lab, you see. So I'm really hungry right now～"
"Haven't you thought about fixing your lifestyle even a little for the new year…?"
"That's why I woke up early today. And it was even without you forcing me up, Haruki."
My first day of readjusting myself in the morningーand on the first day after winter break, no lessーhas begun in quite an intense way, though I'm actually kind of happy with what's transpiring.
"While I'm at it… About the breakfast menu you mentioned earlier. There's a limit to how far you should take a joke about…"
"I can't get my head to work properly if I don't eat my fill in the morning, you know. It's already hard enough to find good material as it is."
"Look, Haruki, that area is frosty～ Can you hear the ice cracking?"
After all, this meaningless bustling moment is making me realize something.
My actual everyday life has finally returned.

I'm now living out the days where I would typically chide on others, hurriedly go about my life and do everything by myself, rather than the days where I need to be comforted, protected and supported.
…I'm now living out my days where I'm not completely entrusting myself to a younger girl from the bottom of my heart.
"By the way… you said, 'You've made up with each other, I see.' earlier… Are you actually familiar with her?"
"I know! I'll give you a one-of-a-kind discount and settle with just the katsu curry!"
"…It's 8:20, y'know? It's five minutes before class starts, y'know?"
"You're always here 30 minutes before the first bell, so how come you're even later than me this time?"
"I don't think you should be saying that with confidence, Second Term Class Rep."
"No, this isn't about me right now…"
"I've just gotten a little sluggish after the break. Even I have days like these."
"…Ahh～! Sorry, my bad. I was really insensitive, huh?"
"I'd say that it was even more insensitive of you to assume something was the matter."
"Well, whatever. How was your winter break, Sugiura? I couldn't relax at all because I had winter prep school. I only went out when we visited our relatives."

"If only I'd studied hard and acquired a recommendation like you did… My parents have been really bugging me about how I can't retake my entrance exams. All our savings got eaten up by my sister, after all."
"Who knows? Though she doesn't seem to be here yet…"
"Ah, she's here… Hey, Sayuri, Koharu's here."
"Can you come over here for a minute, Koharu? Sorry if I'm interrupting anything…"
"Sayuri? But the first bell is about to…"
"We'll make it quick. …It's a rather complicated story."
"…If it's complicated, I doubt it'll be quick."
"About three days ago, I got a call… directly from Yada."
"I don't think it would've been easy for her to talk to you. …Assuming what she told us was true, that is."
"In any case, she said that she went out to eat with her family on the 25th, and on her way back… she happened to pass by the station at around 9 PM."
"She said she saw you with that prep school teacher… You know, the one who rejected her really harshly."
"Yada was quite shocked about that. She seems to be under the impression that you've betrayed her, Koharu."
"We understand. You were doing what you were doing for Yada-san's sake, right?"
"I think she's having another ridiculous misunderstanding again. Based on all our previous experiences with her up until now, at least."
"Well, she does make really outlandish assumptions."
"But she hasn't come to school again today, right? I really don't think we can just leave her alone right now."
"And we have less than two months before graduation. We also have our graduation trip after that."
"That's why I think you should let us sort things out between you two this time, as much as it'd be swapping our usual roles."
"She's not willing to talk to you right now, Koharu, which is why we'll listen to what you have to say and convey it to her in your stead."
"In that case, why don't you hang out with us after school today? Then you can tell us all the details."
"If we explain everything properly to her, I'm sure we can sort out this misunderstanding, Koharu."
"You're okay with that, right? Or do you have something to do?"
"I know you're quite shocked about this, but please don't let it bother you too much…"
"This is ridiculous… I don't understand what you're saying."
"Tell you in detail? Everything? …About what exactly? How does any of that concern you two?"
"I can't tell you the truth in detail when you're already so off the mark. …I won't talk to anyone about this, no matter who it may be."
"Like I said, though, if we don't talk about this properly, no one will understand what's going on, you know?"
"Is that true for you as well, Sayuri? And you, Ako? Are you saying that you won't believe me unless I tell you everything from start to finish?"
"So that means everything would be fine if Mihoko and I made up, right? And if that happened, I wouldn't have any reason to tell you anything, right?"
"That might be true, but… right now it's difficult for you two to even talk."
"It's not. It will be meaningless if someone butts in. Because Mihoko and I are best friends. She'll definitely understand."
"…Thanks for telling me. I'll talk to Mihoko in person later. This conversation is over."
"If I say any more, someone else will be hurt by this. I hope you guys understand."
"But you usually don't allow for such reasoning, Koharu…"
"Anyway, Mihoko and I will settle this. I won't talk about anything else related to this!"
"I'm sorry, you two… The teacher is almost here. Let's head back to the classroom, okay?"
"I hope… we'll get along this year too."
I examine the clock on my cell phone and confirm for myself that it is indeed that time showing on the display.
It was Friday yesterday… My return to Kaiousha after the long break was chaotic as always.

I had to deal with Mari-san unreasonably scolding me as well as a rather cryptic comment from Suzuki-san saying, "you neglected her," and it was 8 AM when I got home without being able to make sense of it all.
I'm supposed to have the rest of the week off, which is why I've decided to laze around, not think about anything and sleep in for today.
As I rub and open my sleepy eyes, I notice the keychain on the bed that Mari-san gave me in her fit of anger as a souvenir from Guam, which was about as distasteful as one would expect.
…Seems like one of the main reasons she got mad at me was that I didn't even know she had gone overseas to do an interview at the end of last year.
"Ah, Kitahara-san! Thank goodness I managed to reach you!"
My day off consisting of purposefully not thinking of anything has been cut short by a phone number that I've become so used to seeing since last week…
"You have reached the voicemail for the number…"
