"Well, relaxing in a hot spring with a pretty girl that has some unusually old-fashioned tastes doesn't sound all bad to me."
She's likely not going to agree with this. Nor am I going to participate, either.
It's a sacred place for us, after all.
"…Hey Haruki. Don't you think it's about time?"
"You only lost your way a little. I'm sure she would understand."
"Like I said, what do you mean…?"
"Since winter break ended, that woman never showed her face again, right? It must've just been a little fling to her."
"Once it turns into that sort of relationship, they'll swiftly put you on their block list and then fade out from your life. You don't have to think too much about it, it's a method I use a lot too."
I told Takeya and Io everything about my winter break.
I was slapped by Io, and Takeya defended me for some reason, but it really was a situation where all hell broke loose.
"Anyway, for now, we'll plan it for sometime around early March. Keep your schedule around that time open! Ah, well then, I'll see ya later. I have something I need to do."
More than one month has passed since winter break.
Even so, things have remained motionless around me.
After all, Io and Takeya never brought it up again, and Chiaki never showed herself.
During the examination period, she didn't show up in the examination hall, let alone at the lab. No matter how I think about it, she was already in a dire situation to advance to the next year.
At this rate, my only connection with her will be lost forever. Everyone will return to their original places and it will be as if nothing ever happened.
My sin, my new budding feeling, everything…
Even though that's not supposed to be alright…
Nevertheless, the fact that I'm able to retain my usual self right now is all thanks to that woman being there for me.
"Today marks the end of my exams. Looks like I'll be able to advance to the fourth year somehow."
"…I say that, but I think you already knew. I'm simply just making small talk."
"I don't actually think you would have a hard time advancing to the next year, Setsuna, and there's no way that I'd fail my exams either."
"…It's been quite some time since my last text, sorry. I've always been thinking about what I should say to you."
"Takeya and Io said that they're willing to be our mediators, but I think that's just running away."
"I say that, but in the end, the fact that I'm replying to you this late means that I'm already doing a lot of running away."
"Ummm… this will be a long story."
"And it'll most likely be a series of incoherent self-justification, self-deception, and self-pity. Only things that will make you feel uncomfortable, Setsuna."
"I revised it countless times and tried to keep it simple. Even so, I wrote down everything that happened and the things I felt without leaving anything out."
"About what I've been doing ever since parting with you that day. About how I felt during those days."
"And about how I betrayed you, Setsuna."
"I'm going to mail the letter now. If possible, I want you to read it."
"And if you do read it, I hope you'll be able to give me a reply telling me that you have."
"If you feel like you don't have anything to say, I don't mind a blank text from you either."
Even now, there are times when I'm assaulted by those "shivers."
Chills running through my body, sweating, trembling, and reaching my hand out into nothing, yearning for someone that's not by my side.
During those times, I will hug myself and dive onto my bed, close my eyes, block off all of my five senses… and then begin imagining it all.
The way she laughs as she teases me. The irresponsible way she conducts herself. The way she just seems so weary all the time.
The warmth, scent, and touch of her skin. The way she breathes and moans. And the feeling… inside her womb.
My body will stop trembling after a while. I'll return to my usual self.
I'm already able to get back on my feet by myself.
Thanks to the memories that Chiaki gave me, I am able to move forward even without her beside me.
And that's why I'm moving forward. Without fear of what lies ahead.
"I think this is probably the first time you sent me a hand-written letter, Haruki-kun?"
"Just like your class notes, your handwriting is beautiful and well-ordered like always. It really feels nostalgic."
"Ever since you changed to the Literature Department, I no longer have a chance to see your handwriting at all."
"The content was really easy to follow as well. Somehow it's written like an essay, and so I laughed a little thinking that's so like you too, Haruki-kun. Sorry about that."
"As I read it, the image of you speaking to me comes to my mind. Head down, both hands in tight fists, but still with a clear voice."
"I believe you're not lying when you said you revised this letter countless times. How many days did this one letter take you to write?"
"Anyway… onto more important matters. About the contents of this letter…"
"If I'm to sum it up in one sentence, it's that you're still so attached to the past and still blame yourself too much as usual. …Something like that?"
"Ahh, wait, let me add one more thing… You're too serious."
"If you were able to think about things more lightly, things would've worked out without us hurting each other."
"I say that, but I guess I'm digging my own grave here."
"I was the one who caused all of this, so even if I say something like that to you, you can only laugh, right?"
"But to tell you the truth, it'll take me some time to digest this harsh reality…"
"I've read it over and over, but I feel more troubled the more I read it. I get angry, I lament, I reflect upon myself… and become a person I dislike when no one is watching."
"But I'll definitely reach a conclusion. And I will let you know about it."
"Please wait until then. …Just like what you're doing right now, if possible."
"Well then, I'll contact you again. Good night."
"What are you going to do about Takeya-kun's invitation to go skiing? I've never gone skiing before, so I'm a little nervous…"
I wonder how many days have passed since Chiaki left my apartment.
She never showed herself at the lab, in the cafeteria, or anywhere on campus.
Her cell phone is always set to voice mail. And even when I send her a text, I never get a reply back.
Is it her trademark fickleness, or is she actually avoiding me on purpose…?
At any rate, that woman rejected all contact with me.
"Even though it was such a selfish letter, thanks for promising that you'll give me a reply."
"But let me just say one thing. I think you still pamper me too much."
"Well, I guess the person who gets carried away with getting pampered is the one most at fault. …And it's even worse when he acts the same way no matter who it is he is getting pampered by."
"Anyway, I'll wait for your reply. Well then, good night."
Isn't it about time you showed yourself in front of me? If not…
I feel like I'll end up getting back on my feet even without you beside me.
"Eh? You're not going, Haruki-kun? Then I won't go either."
"I mean, I don't want to bother the two of them. If I'm the only one who goes along, they'll definitely fuss over me."
"You went on a ski trip last year, right? Takeya-kun told me. I was kinda looking forward to having you teach me."
"If we leave those two alone, you realize it'll just be the two of us…?"
"You don't like being alone with me?"
"I'm the type to easily hold a grudge, you know?"
As I open the door to the editing department like I always do, I gain a brief, ominous premonition from the unusual silence of the office.
Maybe there's nobody here, or maybe there are people that I don't know all that well. Even now, I'm still a slave to the grip of anxiety.
It seems that I managed to luck out at the very last moment somehow.
"What's wrong? Why'd you come all the way here this late at night today of all days, and not to mention in this weather?"
"It's exactly because of this weather that I was able to make it here at this hour. …The trains are late because of the snow, so they're still running right now."
"You haven't answered the part about 'today of all days' yet…"
"Is there nobody else around? Is it just you, Mari-san?"
"…Suzuki's on paid vacation. Matsuoka and Kizaki both dashed out of here right after their shifts ended. Hamada said he wanted to spend some time with his family today, so he left at eight."
"What about the people in the other departments…?"
It's not just the editing department; the design department, photography department, and even the managing editors and chief editor aren't present today.
Well, the chief's involved in a whole bunch of magazines, so he's pretty much never around anyway.
"The photography department seems to be having a pretty big year-end party. …Though I imagine that going out drinking on a day like this is actually nothing but trouble, right?"
"…If you're going to start making more sarcastic remarks, I do plan on retaliating with some of my own."
"…Staying behind this late must have been tough on you. It's a big help that you were able to stay back."
"An acceptable answer, then. …And just for the record, it's not like I wasn't invited, you know? It just didn't sound as alluring as working was."
She played along with my obvious attempt at changing the subject just fine, without questioning that flawed part of my personality at all.
I'm so glad that she's here right now.
…And the fact that she's the only one here.
"By the way, Kitahara… What do you plan to do with that?"
Mari-san cast her eyes toward the red and white box that I'm holding with my right hand.
An obvious color scheme considering today's date. A little present that's meant for this day, and this day only.
"What should I do? I only bought this because I thought there'd at least be four or five people left…"
"True, there's no way the two of us would be able to finish an entire Christmas cake by ourselves. Who would buy something that spoils so quickly on a weekend…?"
"I got it at the open 24 hours supermarket around here for 1000 yen."
"Ah～ I saw those on sale too. It was still 2000 yen around noon."
"They've been quick with the price cuts lately, even though tomorrow is the 25th, which is Christmas Day. Ah, today's already that day, isn't it…"
"Is it just not worth eating unless it's Christmas Eve? Or perhaps it's only the fact that its expiration date just passed…?"
"What with something being worthless after 24, past the expiration date…"
Now that I think about it, a certain someone here is past 25 already…
"You're still trapped by such an old and outdated sense of value, I see. I'm so disappointed…"
"But you're the one who brought up the expiration date thing…"
"When you pity or make fun of someone's self-deprecation, it hurts more than it usually does, you know? You don't understand how women feel at all…"
"Mari-san, are you seriously worried about that?"
"…Well, I was just making a joke. I'm not interested in men or marriage anyway."
"Aren't those supposed to be developed at the same time? Both love and work, I mean."
"That only applies to young people. Such as yourself."
"So Mari-san… you're aware that you're not young any…"
"Kitahara… you want to watch what you're saying? When did you start speaking to me so disrespectfully like this?"
"It's because it's you that I can drop the formalities, Mari-san. I neither feel the reason nor the need to be worried."
"…Hmm, at least your lip service sounds like a guy with experience working in the media."
"I didn't mean that in a good way."
"…I'll cut the cake, so go buy some coffee. Black for me."
Whenever I talk to Mari-san, I always use some sort of lip service with her, and often times I'd even go as far as to annoy her a little with it.
…So I'm truly grateful to God that Mari-san was able to be here right now.
Unquestionably, I'm forcing myself to appear bright and cheerful right now.
But the fact I'm alone with Mari-san means that I can actually reduce the degree of which I'm forcing my facade right now, even if a little. And even if a little, I'm actually starting to cheer up.
I'll be able to mix in 1% of my real feelings amidst 99% of my acting.
"What are you doing, if I might ask?"
"Hm? I just thought the decoration was a little too plain, that's all. It's not every day you get to have a Christmas cake, after all."
Atop the paper plates we always kept a pack of around here were two less-than-perfectly cut and somewhat unequal slices of cake.
"Normally there'd at least be a Santa-shaped candle or something. And a little message card made with chocolate, and snow made from sugar candy, and…"
Since the cake was apparently too plain, Mari-san started enthusiastically decorating it in her vision.
"I crushed some of Suzuki's cookies to make the snow, threw on a business card for the message card, and as for the Santa-shaped candle… here!"
"What do you think, Kitahara? Now it looks more like it, huh?"
"…There should be a limit to how bad one's tastes can be. Just as always."
"Ahahahaha, I figured you'd say that. You always jump on any chance to laugh at my tastes."
Blowing away both the crushed cookie bits and business card is a Santa Claus of Mari-san's own design.
That was, of course, referring to the tasteless, foreign key-chain that perfectly represents her tastes.
"Doesn't it look good? It's my favorite one right now. I got it from a friend that was sent to Africa. …Said I'd absolutely love it."
Attached to the keychain appears to be some sort of dirty-looking doll made from cloth wrapped around some straw.
That's also what I've come to expect from Mari-san, though, and thus a twisted, distasteful grin emerges on my lips.
"Putting it on the cake probably isn't a good idea, so I'll just leave it here… All right, Kitahara, shall we have a toast?"
"…Merry… Christmas. Thanks for the present. I was delighted, really."
"…Well then, Let's eat. Mmm… It sure looks delicious."
Unable to keep up my normal, regular expression, I'm finally forced to turn my back toward Mari-san as my entire body starts to tremble.
It's just the two of us, so if I just blatantly turned around like this, there's no way that she wouldn't notice the state I'm in right now.
"…This butter cream is so heavy. It's also way too sweet. I can see why they lowered the price. There's no way they'd be able to sell it all."
Even so, Mari-san doesn't confront me about it, and is simply wolfing down the cake while frankly voicing her opinions on it.
And so I, with my back still turned, partake in some of the cake as well, nearly choking on the overly sweet and heavy cream she spoke of.
"Well, it's about what I would expect from one of your presents. You might be a serious and diligent guy, but your tastes are pretty terrible."
"…It's all thanks to the training I received from a certain supervisor of mine."
"If nothing else, you've certainly mastered the art of talking back. Never mind, though. I was feeling a little hungry anyway."
Feeling the sweetness of the cream and the dryness of the sponge cake slide down my throat, I finally find myself unable to stop the drops from flowing out of my eyes.
…I'm really, really glad I came here. This sense of distance between us is simply incomparable.
She doesn't force her way into my business, but she's watching over me. Just as always, our chatter is filled with her criticizing my faults, but it's also full of laughter as well.
Even if she did catch on to how I am right now, and even though it's not out of indifference, she would probably remain in her state of non-intervention.
At the start, she'll just grin and bear it like this.
"But seriously, this really is awful. I'll just throw the rest in the fridge for whoever might want to try it. I'm looking forward to the look on their faces when they come in tomorrow."
"I can't wait until Monday. How about you, Kitahara?"
Because I didn't want to be alone, I ran away to this sleepless building in search of more and more people to talk to…
But in the end, I could only find a single person, so my wish of finding more and more people vanished, but…
But this chance encounter made me as happy as someone who's won the year-end lottery.
Because right now, I'm really here with the person I want to be with the most…
"What's wrong, Kitahara? Are you giving up too?"
What was that just now…? What did I mean by that?
Am I just desperate to indulge in someone's company because of my current state of mind…?
"I'm serious. Let me give you a hand."
"Don't worry about it. They're counting it as a holiday anyway, so you're not going to get paid. Just head home for today…"
"It'll get finished faster if I help out too, you know?"
"Even if I get it done early, I still wouldn't be able to leave before the first train anyway."
"…That applies to me too. Which is why I pretty much have nothing to do before the first train starts running."
"Or maybe… am I being a bother?"
"Then please let me work. Otherwise, the only thing left for me to do is sit here and stare at you, Mari-san."
"…Am I imagining things? It kind of feels like I'm being hit on."
"If that makes it feel awkward, then all the more reason for you to let me work."
"…You've really thrown all formalities out the window when you're with me now, haven't you?"
"It's already been half a year, after all."
In reality, it has nothing to do with formalities and whatnot. I'm just desperate.
I just can't bring myself to leave this atmosphere we created, is all. …I'm not even considering the trouble I'm causing her.
3 AM… Two hours until the first train of the day.
At least, for these few hours… until I'm overtaken by exhaustion, and no longer able to think any more.
Because I don't want those tear-inducing thoughts of reality to show themselves in my head again.

"I'll be going around a couple of places such as New York and Los Angeles, and I'll be meeting up with a friend of mine in Guam on my way back as a vacation. I estimate I'll be back here on the 5th of January next year."
"…Ah, my friend's not a guy, okay? You've met her before, right, Kitahara? Amamiya Sawako. It's just our annual two-person trip without anything to do with guys…"
"There's nothing else to spend money on, so we splurge a little at the end of every year like this. …Even though being with Sawako is starting to get on my nerves a little."
Mari-san's soothing voice has indeed reached my ears, but my mind refuses to process those words.
The reason behind her working even harder than usual despite it being Christmas, as well as the weekend.
It was something I quickly noticed when I looked over the paperwork she asked for.
…Because it was paperwork for an overseas trip.

"I grabbed a bunch of jobs from the other departments, just like always. Thanks to that, I'll probably be spending New Year's on an airplane. …And thanks to the time zones, I'll likely be celebrating New Year's twice."
"It's a little too short for collecting what I need, but I had a pretty tight limit on travel expenses, so yeah."
"What? You've been quiet for a while now. Does me not being here make you feel that lonely?"
"H-hey, don't just stay silent! Stop looking so deep and mysterious! It's so unclear."
"Kitahara… you know, I've been trying to avoid the topic for a while now, but you really seem off today."
"Again, I'm sorry… and thank you, for watching out for me."
Mari-san's been fighting to preserve that delicate distance between us, but my overly gloomy expression has finally made her unable to bear it any more.
But breaking the barrier like that didn't really give me any sort of discomfort.
"Well, showing up all of a sudden in a place like this on Christmas Eve just screams 'something happened.'"
Because both of us are looking at our monitors, so we aren't speaking face to face.
Mari-san's using one of her special skills: focusing on idle chatter while focusing on her work at the same time.
"If you have something troubling you, just say it. …Well, I understand if you don't want to, though."
After hearing my honest response, Mari-san seems ever so slightly shaken up.
She probably thought there was no way I'd show her this weak and defenseless side of me so easily.
"So what's wrong? Did today being Christmas remind you of one of your past girlfriends or something?"
But right now, there's no way I'm going to let go of this incredible opportunity. My only choice is to take advantage of Mari-san's kindness.
Because if I let it go, I won't be able to meet Mari-san again for a while. I… don't want to spend New Year's while still holding on to these thoughts.
"R-Really now… Is it about Touma Kazusa?"
"…Did you remember a Christmas date with her in the past, perhaps?"
"We… went on a trip. An overnight one."
"…But it wasn't just the two of us. We had a friend with us, and we went to the northern part of Kanto."
"W-W-W-What the… don't scare me like that. Or is what's about to come even scarier?"
"Nothing happened, really. We took a dip in the open-air bath, had some drinks in our yukatas, and just partied."
"That's, how should I put it… not exactly the most Christmas-y of Christmas parties, is it?"
"It was snowing back then, just like today… The snow we saw through the window and the sight of the snow falling upon us from the open-air bath were both beautiful sights…"
I'm a little upset at my own deceitful words.
Leaving out the important details, not telling her the true meaning behind that trip of ours, and actually wanting her to understand my feelings with just that…
"I, even now I'm still in love with Touma Kazusa."
But even so, I still wanted to let these words be heard.
Even though I'm lying to Mari-san, I still wanted her to understand me.
"Pain from love cannot be healed by love itself."
"…Please stop bringing that up already. It's because I'm reminded that I was the one who actually said that line that I'm getting embarrassed."
I wanted someone to think of these feelings that Setsuna will never accept again as something "inescapable, without any other choice."
And I didn't want it to be from just about anyone, but someone in particular…
I'm just the worst. This is the absolute worst possible attitude I can take for everyone involved.
Before I knew it, the sounds coming off of our keyboards have ceased.
Even so, we haven't shifted our gazes from our monitors, so we aren't looking at each other either.
"You don't know what sort of advice to give me, right? You probably didn't expect me to talk about something like this."
"Seriously, what do you take me for…?"
"I didn't really say it because I wanted advice, anyway. It's just that I wanted you to hear me out, Mari-san. No matter what."
"…Why? The 'report, communicate, and consult' guideline is for the sake of getting further instructions from your supervisors, isn't it?"
"I wasn't trying to make a report to my supervisor. I just wanted you to hear me out, Mari-san."
"There's no difference, is there? I'm your supervisor, after all."
"I… like that part of you, Mari-san."
The way she tries to act tough regarding a few weird things. The way she acts all supervisor-like, even though she's just trying to look out for me.
The way she struggles with her private matters despite being perfect when it comes to her work.
The way she tries to hide her incredible charm as a woman and ends up showing such an adorable side of her because of it.

"…How many times do I have to say it? A younger subordinate who's still a student shouldn't be teasing his senior supervisor who's a full-fledged adult. I would've smacked you just now if you didn't look so down."
"…I'll be more careful in the future."
As I step outside, I can feel the half-melted snow underneath my shoes sending harsh creaking sounds into my ears.
The first train of the day should have started already, but Onjukuーenclosed in a shroud of darkness even nowーis still at the mercy of the freezing wind.
After a quick turn to make sure that the third floor's lights are still on, I curl up a little and depart from the Kaiousha building.
My heart feels just a little more at ease now. My pain that had been caused by love is healed, not by love, but by kindness.
So if it's just for a little bit… if it's just for a week… if it's just until the bell rings on New Year's Eve, I might just be able to get through it by myself.
I can hear the first train signal of the day from the direction of the station.
I slowly make my way toward the source of that sound, dragging along my body that's finally starting to become fatigued.
Since I can stand being alone now, I might as well go home and just confine myself within my dreams.
"He said the 'like' word! I definitely heard him say the word 'like'…!"
"Wait… Hold on a second, what in the world is going on? What… What did that even mean!?"
"Yeah, she'll just be taking care of the formalities with the others today and head straight home after that. She needs to prepare for the flight tomorrow, after all."
"Yes, this is Kaiousha's editing department for Kaiou Graph… Ah, hello."
"Besides, she finished everything that needs to be done this year during the last weekend anyway. Her work ethic is as impeccable as always."
The Monday of a new week.
With still three days left until the year end wrap-up here at Kaiousha, it was supposed to be another ordinary day.
Yet the one person here that would show up even with a 39°C fever is nowhere to be seen today.
"Yes, yes… a package? One second, please."
"She'll be running around the U.S. until the year's over, and once the new year arrives, she'll be vacationing in Guam.
Having a high salary sure is great, isn't it～?"
"What are you talking about? If you turn it into an hourly rate, Kazaoka makes way less than you."
"Ahhh… You promised you wouldn't mention that～"
"Let's see here ……… office. Ah, yes, yes, I found it."
I heard her flight is tomorrow, so I assumed she'd still come in today.
Besides, the talk we had on Friday really didn't feel like the last one we would be having before the year's over, so why…?
"…What's wrong, Kitahara-kun? Are you that shocked from not being able to meet Mari-san?"
"I haven't received my directions for this week from her yet, so…"
While I did camouflage it with the perfect excuse, it's just as Suzuki-san says.
I'm more shocked than I thought I would be.
"What? You're free right now, Kitahara? That's great news."
"Ah! You're planning to push all the layout work on him, right? Maybe I should tell Mari-san about this～"
"…It's okay. Feel free to push as much as you like on me."
I was planning to give her a parting gift.
I was even planning to invite her out to a meal, as I gave it to her. I wanted her to hear what I had to say again, with just the two of us.
"…Is that okay? Ah, I see. Yes, I'll take care of it."

"What are you saying? The person who's too caught up in her trip preparation to tend to her beloved subordinate is the one at fault here, am I right, Kitahara?"
"What you just said can be interpreted in quite a few ways, Hamada-san…"
I thought that with the way Mari-san is now, she might just accept this tactless idea of mine as a "good display of my fighting spirit"…

"Well then, have a safe trip. Oh, and Happy New Year～!"
"Do you have some things for me as well, Suzuki-san? I can get started on things that are scheduled after New Year's too, if you'd like."
"…Seriously? Can you keep it a secret from Mari-san?"
Back then, I got to tell her about my past. So this time, I wanted to tell her about my future.
I wanted to let the first person that's ever understood my lingering affections for Kazusa know about the troubles that I'm burdened with right now.

I thought that Mari-san would surely understand me… I thought that we could think about it together, and that even if it proves to be a struggle, she would still do everything she can to find the way forward for me.
I thought that she'd be able to save me…
I'd been in deep thought during the whole conversation without anyone noticing, and I was finally brought back to reality by an envelope handed to me by Matsuoka.
"Is that… Hey, it might even be…"
"Hey, can I open it? I'm opening it, okay?"
Brought back to reality would be an understatement. It turned my mind blank with shock for a moment.
"I had a feeling… It's Touma Youko's New Year Concert, right? The one that our company's sponsoring."

"And right after that, I went and listened to one of Touma Youko's CDs. I got totally hooked."

"Yeah, yeah～! Visiting the shrine with your girlfriend or whatnot."

"That call just now was from Mari-san. Apparently, she got a call directly from the chief editor over at Ensemble."
"That's amazing. I guess they really liked that article."
"It was filled with revealing details about her daughter, too. If it was somebody else, they might have even filed a lawsuit against us."
"That's why it was so loved by Touma Youko herself. She's quite the eccentric, after all."
Whether it be the article being a huge hit with Touma Youko, or the fact that I'm getting special treatment because of it, or the fact that this is an incredibly rare VIP ticket…
Those certainly are important occurrences for me right now, but…
"That call right now… it was from Mari-san?"
"Ah, yeah. She told me to give the ticket over to you and then hung up."
Above all, there was a small detail that caught nobody else's attention…
In actuality, it was an incredibly inconsequential fact that had the greater impact on me right now.
"I told her that you were here, but she said she didn't need to talk to you directly… She sounded a little jittery, like she was on the road."
Just two days ago, she was here with me, listening to what I had to sayーjust the two of us.
She was the first person to whom I was able to show the scars that I've never shown to anyone else before.
But despite having business with me and knowing that I was merely a few steps away from the phone, why didn't she just ask to talk to me directly?

Did my overly frank confession about my excruciating past turn her away, perhaps?
Is she troubled because the topic got too heavy too quickly? Or does she think this whole ordeal is just a waste of time and that she doesn't want to deal with me any more?
Around me, everyone's still excitedly talking about the concert.

I can't seem to stop that tiny… laughably meaningless bit of worry from slowly making its way deeper and deeper into my heart.
"Mm～ …Sorry, now's not a good time. I'm at work."
"The best time to make money is when nobody else is working. Besides, I'm pretty much broke over here."
"That's also no good… I have work starting on the 2nd. So I at least want to get one good day of rest tomorrow."
"Aren't you… working a little too much?"
"I only get to do this kind of stuff when there's no school. I have tests to study for at the end of next month, so I'm getting some working done while I can."
"You really are okay right now, right?"
"I have no clue what you're even worried about, but…"
"Did I… end up doing something unnecessary? On the night of the 24th, what did you two…"

"I'm at work right now, so I'll be hanging up for now. There's a few documents I need to finish before the date changes."
"…Got it. Let's have a good year next year too, Haruki."
Ever since "that day," I've been distancing myself from Takeya, who's been calling me every single day. And every time I hang up, the feeling of guilt envelops me, eating me alive.
He and Io must be feeling rather anxious, since they don't really understand how things are going between Setsuna and me.
Though I'm grateful for that. Their heartfelt kindness makes me really happy. I'm so glad we were able to stay friends all this time.
"Yes, this is Kaiousha's Kaiou Graph's editing department."
Even so, they're the exact people that I want to leave me alone right now…
These are nothing but my frank, direct and cruel feelings that value nothing of their friendship.
"Kizaki is… I'm very sorry, his winter break began yesterday."
I can't bring myself to tell them both about the distance between Setsuna and me right now… after how long they've been observing both of us from such a close distance.
Chances are, the reason they were so on point with their suspicions was because they already knew the answer to begin with…
And they probably would've also offered us some unreasonable or utterly infeasible ways to get out of this, too.
"Ah, if it's regarding that application, then I, Kitahara, can take care of it. Yes, at the latest, it should be ready on the 2nd… yes."
They'd only be urging us to try and cross an impenetrable barrier.
Without the slightest chance of letting us even think about stopping, avoiding it, or turning the other way.
"Yes, you can reach me with the number you're calling right now. Kitahara. K-i-t-a-h-a-r-a. My email address is…"
I only want to talk about this with someone who doesn't know about the two of usーsomeone who can look at our situation from an objective standpoint.
And at the same time, I want it to be someone who's caring, passionate, and someone who's willing to give it their all and break their back for my sake.
And while I know this is really unfair, and bordering the line of escapism…
If at all possible, I'd… like for it to be someone who's just the tiniest bit biased toward me.
"I look forward to the results of our collaboration. Now then, if you'll excuse me."
But for the next little while, there won't be anybody like that around, so all I can do right now is tough it out on my own.
…For one more week, at the very least.
I'm so glad that the editing department's still open on New Year's Eve.
The number of people who are still coming in even after finishing their year-end work has certainly gone down, but it's not zero, which is why I too am able to keep myself busy today.
Up until yesterday, I've been running around the other departments, and managed to get my hands on quite a number of miscellaneous tasks.
They all vary wildly in their deadlines, workload, and content. There's enough for a few days worth of work after New Year's too… I made sure I had enough to last until Mari-san gets back.
No matter where I went, even if I've never properly interacted with them before, their reply would always be a quick "Oh, he's with Kazaoka…" and they'd give me as much work as I wanted.
The fact that Mari-san's name is so revered throughout the company makes me feel a little proud as well.
…I'm sure that none of them have any clue that I'm doing this out of my own volition. They're unaware that Mari-san isn't backing me up at all.
That's exactly why I can't betray their trust. I have to do my utmost to ensure that everything is done on time, carefully, and accurately…
"Ah, hello. Tiring day today, isn't it?"
"There's nobody left on the upper floors, so… Are you going to keep going?"
Glancing over at the clock, I notice that it's only 8:30.
Normally, you'd be hard pressed to find anyone leaving this early, but it's understandable that there'd be hardly anyone willing to stay this late both today and tomorrow.
"I wouldn't recommend spending New Year's here at work. It might make you want to kill yourself."
I definitely have a ridiculous amount of things to do, but I already finished everything that needed to get done today.

"If you're planning to leave, then I'll wait for you. We can go return the key together."
"Sorry for the trouble. I'll be right ther… ah."
…I was about to pick myself up, but a single piece of paper that was left on the side of my desk caught my eye.
If I recall correctly, printed on that piece of paper is the name "Touma Youko."
It's been 30 minutes since the start of the concert, so I'm still in the "just a little bit late" category.
The concert's held at Onjuku Art and Culture Hall. Only a few minutes from here on foot. …Right on the path toward the station.
I'd be lying if I said I wasn't interested.
A live concert by a world-class pianist. A premium seat. It also happens to be a special invitation that's a result of the recognition that I'd gained through my first real assignment.
…But if I were to come face to face with Touma Youko herself and her performance, I'm sure it'd end up making me recall some of my past memories, even if I don't want to.

Having succeeded her bloodline and talents, I'm sure that I'd see a certain someone playing on her own stage on the opposite side of the world much like her mother, and much like her, she'd also grab the attention of her audience in a single sweep…
No, what I'd be seeing again are memories pertaining to a certain someone.
Could it be that Touma Youko still remembers me?
Even if she forgot, if I pushed my way to the waiting rooms and told them I was the one that wrote that article, I might get a chance to meet her.
And she might remember the moment she recognizes me.
And would she tell her daughter about me if that were to happen?
It's another link between Kazusa and me… a potential path that may lead me to meeting with Kazusa again…
"…Sorry. I want to get to a good stopping point before I call it for today."
"Is that so… I'll let you return the keys to security, then, alright?"
"Good work today. And Happy New Year."
Having betrayed Setsuna, I have no business getting involved with anything pertaining to the surname of "Touma."
"We're an hour earlier than Japan but Happy New Year! Glad we managed to find each other before the calendar flipped～"
"How was your trip? Did you take care of everything? …I had to pretty much abandon everything in order to get here."
"…Yeah, I finished. It went smoother than I thought it would."
"I see, I see… No matter what, I'm glad we made it. We were so caught up in our work last year that we couldn't meet up until the day before we had to go back～"
"Now then, let's hurry on over to the hotel. After we get there, we're going to drink till we drop and fully enjoy the coming of the new year by sleeping through the whole thing!"
"…Something wrong, Mari? Did you catch a cold?"
"Um… I was just wishing the day of our flight back would come quicker."
"Ah～ I can't believe there are still five more days. I shouldn't have come on this trip after all…"
"…Are you trying to pick a fight with me?"
It got too hard to stay in there with the security officer staring me down the whole time, so I made my way out of the building about ten minutes ago.
And before I realized it, I found myself in front of the Onjuku Art and Culture Hall.
Guests came pouring out of the hall and down the stairs, and a massive wave of people suddenly appeared before my very eyes.
In any case, it appears that the concert just ended. Looking at the clock on my phone, I see that it's 23:59 right now.
…Seems like the New Year's Concert was just a little short of the new year.
Swallowed up by the wave of people heading toward the station, my hastened pace slows down.
The people coming out of the hall have their faces flushed with excitement as they talk about how amazing the concert was.
The crowd's excitement floods my surroundings as it drowns out the sound of the New Year's bell meant for the first night of the year, bringing me the slightest bit of discomfort.
It must have been an absolutely amazing concert. …And I feel the slightest bit of regret for missing out on it.
As I was drifting through the bustling sea of people around me…
It was at that very moment that the new year had arrived.
And so, a quiet voice let out a brief "Happy New Year" in my heart.
To everyone who's taken care of me this past year. To everyone whom I will still be in the care of this year.
To that reliable person that's been supporting me.
To the person who's supported me without me asking for it. To the person who'd support me even if I didn't want it.
To that important person whom I've been giving nothing but heartache, despite being so close to one another.
To that important person whom I haven't seen for so many years and am unlikely to ever see again.
"Eh? What? My impressions? …You really want to hear that from me?"
"I get it. I don't want to admit it, but it doesn't seem like I'll beat you any time soon."
"Anyway, I'll be heading back to the hotel. Are you going to… Huh?"
"That's right. The seat on your left. Was no one there?"
"…Now that you mention it, it was empty the whole time."
"Why? Did you invite someone you know?"
"You could say that… So he decided not to show up, then."
"Your first husband? Your second husband? Or… my father?"
"Stop joking around. I have no idea how to react even if I met him right now."
"I see… It didn't work out, huh… I see…"
"Hey, want to go drinking after we're back at the hotel… Kazusa?"
"What are you saying all of a sudden?"
"Nothing wrong with that, right…? You're past twenty already. It's always been a dream of mine to go drinking with my daughter～"
"…I'm pretty sure you drink every day back home anyway."
"Being in Japan is what makes it special. We don't often get a chance to come back like this, so I want to try heating up a pot of it the old-fashioned way."
"Your age is showing… Even though your piano still sounds so wild and full of life."
"Did you have something you wanted to do? …Someone you wanted to meet?"
"There's no longer a place in this country meant for me."
"Okay, I got it. It's been a while since I've listened to you grumbling, Mom. That's fine. Let's drink until morning, then?"
"What are you talking about～? It was a huge success, wasn't it? Tonight calls for a celebration! All right, I'm not letting you sleep tonight～!"
"You're right… Congratulations. And here's hoping for another great year together, Mom."
"Yeah. Well, I'll see you at the hotel. I'll be heading over after I take care of some formalities."
"…What a depressing chime. I guess I really am back in Japan."
"Hey… I wonder if you're doing okay?"
"Happy New Year. Here's to another great year."
"…Though it's not like we're ever going to meet again, are we?"
"Ahh!? Ugh… What a mess. What, are you drunk already?"
"If you're looking for the sausages, they're over here."
"So he confessed, didn't he!? You did it, Mari. You did it～"
"Well about that… I got way too excited at the time, and after I found some time to think about it a little, the way he said it actually feels a little weird."

"So basically, he wanted you to understand that he still likes his ex to this day?"
"Well, if you take his words at face value, yeah."
"And… he liked how you, still so innocent and inexperienced, were rendered speechless from him telling you all these secrets?"
"He didn't say anything so specific. And don't randomly slide in an insult out of nowhere."

"What are you talking about. 'A bit' younger? He's still 21, so you're a whole fi…"
"That's divine punishment for your little unnecessary comments. Besides, you're the same age as I am."
"Happy New Year Birthday, Mari～ Another year older."
"Besides, if you're so concerned about it, then why didn't you get a clear answer from him before you left?"
"You could have just straight up asked him, 'Are you interested in me?' and been done with it."

"What if he wasn't interested…? Won't I look like some pathetic woman with a giant misunderstanding? I'm older, plus I'm his boss… It'd be sexual harassment and abuse of power at the same time."
"And so, you ran away from it all, only to end up getting more and more worked up over it, and now you desperately want to meet him again…? Hilarious～"
"Seriously… I hate how girl's talk can get so inconsiderate sometimes."
"Well, you know, isn't this still a good thing?"
"What is…? I feel so annoyed and I can't take it anymore…"
"The fact that you're so annoyed. The fact that you can be so serious toward a man."
"The fact that you have "I hope it really was a confession of love" written all over your face."
"It's been forever since I saw you like this, Mari. I've been really worried ever since you started purposely not letting any men get close to you."
"Isn't it about time? To bring out that womanly side of yours?"
"I never realized… that your sole weakness was younger guys forcing their youthful passion into you."
"The way you say it sounds so wrong."
"Are you actually drunk this time? Should we go to bed soon?"
"How long have we been drinking…? Got a watch on you, Mari?"
"Your phone's fine too. Let me borrow it for a second."
"Oh, sure. I have it set up with the time zone here too."
"I think we started back at midnight. We've been drinking for quite a…"
"This is no time for two women to be sitting around and drinking the night away. We're going to hear the truth from Haruki-kun right here, right now."
"What are you even saying!? Stop it! Do you know what time it is over there right now!?"
"Don't worry, don't worry～ We're only off by one hour anyway."
"It's the middle of the night here too!"
"Oh～ it's ringing, it's ringing. Hurry up and pick up, Haruki-kun～ Mari here can't wait another second～"
"S-Stop it… I have nothing to say. More than that, I can't just bring it up so suddenly!"
"But weren't you eager to go home? Didn't you want to meet him right this second? Maybe he's feeling the same way too."
"He's a university student, for crying out loud! And he's a whole five years younger than me, you know!?"
"You don't have to take it so seriously. Just playing with him a little isn't…"
"Kitahara isn't the kind to take these things so lightly! How rude!"
"That's why I… Didn't I say it just now? Now's not the time for this."
"Do you understand what I'm saying, Sawako?"
"I know just how important it is that you two talk this through.
Rubbing my weary eyes and looking over to the clock beside my bed, I see that it's past three.
I went home after the New Year's bell rang, took a hot shower, drank some alcohol that I didn't want to drink, and forced myself to lie in bed for an hour.
The sleep that's been eluding me for these past couple of days finally came within reach, and had already successfully robbed me of my consciousness, and yet…
I reach my hand out amidst the darkness, remove the beeping device from my charger, and flip it open…
I threw away the sleep I had longed for all this time in a mere instant.
The thought that's swarming my brain from seeing the displayed name isn't "I've been waiting all this time", or "Why now?", or even "Aren't you overseas right now?"…
It was the mere fact that "the call came from Mari-san, and it was for me" that excited me so much.
What awaited me after I frantically pressed the call button and brought the phone to my ears was a completely unintelligible span of three seconds.
"Owowow… Jeez, what's with you and your strength?"
"Where…? Where did my cell phone go!?"
"How would I know? You sent it flying off somewhere."
"It's ringing! That means Kitahara must have called me back… If, if I don't pick up soon…"
"Didn't you say you had nothing to say to him?"
"If you have time to make remarks like that then come help me find it!"
"W-Where…? I don't see it anywhere on the table…"
"No, it's on the table… and inside the decanter. Look, it's sinking in a sea of wine right now."
This marks my fifth try, and once again, I'm met with the same electronic sounds that signify a denied call.
Just when I finally got a call from Mari-san, whom I've been waiting so restlessly for…
It was as if that call was laughing at how excited I was when I picked up, seeing how it hung up in a mere three seconds. And now calls from my side are being ignored.
It being an overseas call shouldn't be the reason why it's not connecting. After all, her call managed to reach me.
Besides, Mari-san has been on overseas trips so many times, so there's no way she'd make the mistake of messing up her means of communication in any way.
The ring of the New Year's bell has ended, but we're still far from the first sunrise of the year.
But my heart is far, far separated from the merry words that usually accompany the coming of a new year.
Giving in, holding back, and coming to a conclusion. And just when I thought I've finally calmed my heart after all that, this gets thrown at me.
As long as these frustrating feelings still plague my mind, even if I sink my head into the futon and shut my eyes tight again, I doubt the sleepiness that I've lost will return.
I'm certain that this will be another sleepless night. …Unless I can drive these negative thoughts out.
Why did you call me so suddenly? It's past three in the morning on New Year's, you know?
We could have talked for as long as we wanted to before you left on the trip. We could have even met in person.
…This is way too much of a mystery.
Moreover, she hung up right after I picked up, and now she refuses to pick up when I call her back? What sort of harassment is this?
Did I do something that would make you this upset at me? Something that would make you want to avoid me?
I only wanted you to understand me…
What was that scream that I heard right before the call suddenly got cut off…?
She made the call despite knowing it was the middle of the night over here, but suddenly hung up, all while being overseas at that.
Could it be that… Mari-san is in some kind of trouble over there?
"…None of the buttons are working. Looks like it's done for."
"But the display is still faintly visible. …And I can see a bunch of missed calls from Kitahara."
"But I can't pick up. And I can't call him back…"
"L-Luck's not on our side, huh? Ahaha…"
"Haaaah～ …What am I going to do? Ugh, jeez! What am I going to do about this…?"
"H-Hey… I can lend you my cell phone…"
"There's no way I can remember his number. …Are you telling me that you know Kitahara's number?"
…Aaaaaaaahhhhhh～ What am I going to do?"
"I don't want to hear that from the person that threw my cell phone into the wine."
"H-How about this… I know Suzuki-chan's number, so why don't I call her and ask for Kitahara's number?"
"No way! Suzuki's extra sharp about those kinds of things! She'll get some kind of misunderstanding for sure."
