I hurriedly changed and ran out of my room after what happened back there.
I asked Hamada-san and Suzuki-san for a way to contact the particular venue Mari-san was staying at to make sure she and her partner were safe.
Without even considering taking the trains on the one day that they're under 24-hour operation, I came here by taxi as fast as I could and got the annoyed security officer to open the door for me.
I dug through my mailbox and finally found Suzuki-san's cell phone number at about 4:30.
And now… things have reached an incredibly anticlimactic conclusion.
"…But seriously, what time and day do you think it is right now? Why are you still at work, Kitahara-kun～?"
"That's because, well… I had some free time."
"You should tell that to Macchan. Even if he spends his entire life working at it, he still probably wouldn't be able to match you."
…As if I could honestly tell her the truth of what happened. All I can do is bite my lip in regret.
I knew that the chance was tiny.
I knew full well that nearly 100% of the worst case scenarios that I had pictured were from my absurd fear.
"Umm… was there anything else mentioned in Mari-san's text?"
"Hmm… nope. All it mentioned was her phone breaking and how to contact her now."
But even so, I never could've imagined that I'd be really off the mark, and all my efforts ended up being meaningless.
"What? Got an emergency? Or is it that you want to hear Mari-san's voice so bad that you can't take it anymore?"
"And there you go again about that…"
I want to hear Mari-san's voice.
"Why not just admit it? Say that you want to confess your love to Mari-san right now. If you do, I wouldn't mind telling you Sawako-san's number, you know?"
"Like I said… I was just wondering if there's any work she needed me to do. She's finished with her business trip, after all."
Even just a little bit would be enough.
Even if the words themselves are harsh. Even if she's just berating me.
"…You worked until morning on New Year's and you're still looking for more? You're going to be up to your neck in more than just work if you're not careful."
Did things fall short of my expectations yet again?
"Huaaaaahh～ Ah～ it's still pitch dark outside I see."
"Sorry for waking you up at a time like this."
Have you been purposefully putting me through this pain ever since Christmas Eve, Mari-san?
I don't know what's going on any more…
"Don't worry about it. Since I'm up anyway, I might as well go watch the first sunrise over at the city hall's viewing platform."
"Thanks a lot for your help. …And Happy New Year."
Are you teasing me, avoiding me, annoyed by me, laughing at me, or lying to me? I can't figure it out…
"I should be the one thanking you for your work. Hope we have another great year together. Talk to you later～"
Suzuki-san's weary voice disappeared, and silence returns to the office.
Standing in the room all alone… I glance up at the ceiling as I reap the solitude I have sown.
"I wouldn't recommend spending New Year's here at work. It might make you want to kill yourself."
Now that I think about it… it's only been a few hours since I heard those words.
…It's not like I've been stung by those words. Even now, things like that haven't crossed my mind even once.
No matter how much suffering I've been through up until now, and no matter how much suffering I've caused others, I believe that having that thought is a sin in itself.
So now and forever, I refuse to think about something so imprudent. I wouldn't even imagine it.
Just breaking the rules a little shouldn't be so unforgivable, right?
"Kitahara, are the documents I asked for ready? It's about time I left for my interview."
"Ah… Let me edit it a little and it'll be ready for printing. I'm sorry, please wait for a moment."
"Ok, perfect. Ah, and printing it out in black and white will suffice."
"Got it. I'll get to it immediately."
"I'm sorry. I asked Matsuoka-san to finish it."
"After we finally got such a convenient tool for this, you really ought to learn to do this yourself, Hamada-san."
"Kitahara's the one who made the tool. Why are you the one bragging about it?"
"…Right, Kitahara. How about the work I asked you to help me with in exchange? Converting it into text, the layout design, and PDF creation…"
"That doesn't count as an equal exchange at all."
"You're one to talk for someone who relies so much on others even though you're young."
"If you're gonna aim somewhere, it's gotta be the director's seat. Better start getting used to managing people now while we can."
"Get used to being managed before managing others. It's not like we have special titles or anything."
"Kizaki-san, Matsuoka-san, both of your assignments are complete. Sorry for the wait!"
"Oh, thank you. Well, I'm off to work now! I'll be heading straight home today～"
"Oh, thank you. I guess I'll just go wrap things up early today…"
"Hold up. I'm not done with you yet."
"Before that, I hope you can check it again…"
I pretend to sigh in resignation while I indulge in the fulfillment of being in the noisy editing department.
Because it's such a lively place.
"Give me a break, Hamada-san… I've got something extremely important today that might impact the rest of my life…"
"You mean the important task of recovering from that long vacation? You left around this time yesterday as well, didn't you?"
It's been a few days since New Year's. The editing department has regained its usual liveliness.
It's packed with people throughout the day, and the folks working outside call in frequently; the relaxing days have long since ended.
Even late at night, there's always someone who stays behind, the ringing of telephones and the clattering of keyboards always echo around the office.
That's why I'm here. …Because no matter what time it is, there's always someone around here.
If I continue working here, I won't have to be alone.
"Next week, alright! I'll work seriously starting next week, okay! Just don't say such stern things anymore～"
"Don't make me laugh! Compared to Kazaoka, I've been much more lenient with you. …And between you and Kitahara, I think being kind to you might not have been the right choice."
"Oh, speaking of Mari-san, she's supposed to return from Guam today, isn't she?"
Is that so? If I remember correctly, Mari-san's holiday was supposed to be…
"So she finally starts work tomorrow… Must be nice to have long holidays."
"But in her case, she won't even have a break for two consecutive days starting tomorrow and up until the end of the year."
"Good for you though, Kitahara. Starting tomorrow, you don't have to help us out anymore. You can start working on proper stuff."
"Being able to undervalue yourself so much… Well, I guess one could call it a talent of sorts, in your case."
"Well, I'm off to work now! I'll be heading straight home today～"
"Oh, speaking of Mari-san, she's supposed to return from Guam today, isn't she?"
"So she finally starts work tomorrow… Must be nice to have long holidays."
"But in her case, she won't even have a break for two consecutive days starting tomorrow and up until the end of the year."
"Good for you though, Kitahara. Starting tomorrow, you don't have to help us out anymore. You can start working on proper stuff."
"Being able to undervalue yourself so much… Well, I guess one could call it a talent of sorts, in your case."
"He… He's there. What do I do, he's there…"
"I wonder if he's angry about that call… Oh dear, I don't know how to face him anymore…"
"Even so… I'll have to explain it to him eventually."
"What are you having fun with, Mari-san?"
"Quiet! Be quiet and I'll spare your life."
"…Feels good to be back. The flight landed earlier than expected, so I decided to drop by along the way."
"Haa… ha… mm. Well, did you decide to gag me along the way as well?"
"Don't say it as if I had any malicious intent. Oh, I bought you some souvenirs, Suzuki. This is something I found in the convenience stores only the locals there seem to go to."
"You're getting so full of yourself around your seniors, now, aren't you?"
"Well, what in the world are you doing? It's obvious that you were acting suspiciously. What, will it inconvenience you to go in there or something?"
"It's just, well… yeah! I was looking for an appropriate timing. I wanted to give you all a big surprise… something like that."
"…There's really no deeper meaning to it. So please don't stare at me like that."
"You were with Sawako-san, and both of you drank to your hearts' content again this year, huh? …Your skin's getting ruined, you know?"
"I'm just kidding. I get it. This is about Kitahara-kun, isn't it?"
"You must be embarrassed to meet him, huh? …After all, you went on vacation without saying a word."
"…Could it be that Kitahara told you that?"
"Yeah, he was in terrible shape, you know? He said he was distressed about trying to contact you, something along the lines of that."
"What did he go telling others about that for…? He's really messing with me, now, isn't he…?"
"Well, you didn't give him any instructions, and he was worried about work for the New Year's holiday…"
"Ah, you're right. I really gave Kitahara a lot of trouble. I'll apologize to him properly later!"
"…That's an unnatural reaction. I can't help but feel interested, you know?"
"…No, it's true that I completely forgot to issue any orders to him. I even thought that he wouldn't be here during the winter holiday."
"Speaking about that… He's been working his head off during the New Year's holiday. He's been going around each and every department collecting errands."
"I don't think he's even taken a single day of rest, you know? He called from the office at four in the morning on New Year's Day."
"…Wait a minute. What is the meaning of this?"
"You sure you're not coming, Kitahara? It's not like I'm going to lecture you or anything."
"…I appreciate the invitation, but I should really finish these while I can today."

In the end, the discussion about Matsuoka-san leaving early seems to have resolved itself fruitfully with Hamada-san inviting him to go drinking together, given that he planned to leave early as well.
If I remember correctly, the company's New Year's party was yesterday, and considering the editing department's having one tomorrow as well, these guys are really energetic, in a way.
Well, I guess if we don't live in the moment of working and enjoying ourselves, perhaps we wouldn't be able to make it into this industry.
This, of course, isn't limited to men…
"Hurry up, Hamada-san. Perhaps I'll go have a hot pot today."
"Think about my stomach too, mind you… Well, see you later, Kitahara."
Just then, as Hamada-san and Matsuoka-san, with one of them in high spirits, were about to leave the office…
The door in front of them opens forcefully as if to ambush them.
My back was facing the door, so up until the moment I heard that familiar name, I neither noticed the person who opened the door nor the expression said person wore on her face.
"Welcome back. And so early, too, Mari-san…?"
At least, that was my intended action, but in reality, I slowly turn to face her as though I didn't want to see her.
While I wasn't aware of it, it seemed like my brain had conditioned itself in order to avoid giving her an excessive reaction.
Perhaps I would appear to be too expectant if I didn't do this.
Because the collapsing feeling of not being able to reunite with the person I had expected would be unbearable.
This time, it was the result I had anticipated all along…
The figure that I had been expecting was standing in front of the door with her hands on her waist.
"Hamada… do you want to work Kitahara to death? Do you want to use him then throw him away just because he's a part-timer? …Why did no one notice this!?"
…I don't understand why, but she's wearing the expression of a demon.
"No, hold on a second… What are you talking about…?"
"Don't directly give Kitahara work again! Not without discussing it with me! Whenever or wherever I am, that is absolute!"
"Uh, yeah… it's true that we did inconvenience him a little…
Hey, Suzuki! You were the one who exaggerated things, weren't you!?"
"I'm not exaggerating… We are all to blame for this. We've been completely fooled by Kitahara-kun."
"Wait, what? What's the matter? I don't get it at all."
The moment Mari-san and Suzuki-san shifted their gazes toward me, I understood immediately.
…I've been exposed. They know how I've been living my life for the past few days.
"Say… is there anyone here who stayed until the very end since New Year's?"
"Well, I've worked past midnight for two days straight since New Year's Day. There was a deadline for the cover of the special edition… Huh?"
Subsequently, Hamada-san's puzzled gaze also turns to me.
"Then, well… who arrives the earliest in the mornings?"
"…Sorry. Regardless of when I arrive or leave, the editing department is always full of people."
"The day before yesterday, well… I arrived at 7 o'clock. During the holidays, I was notified by the printing company about a mistake and that we had to rush it before ten in the morning."
With the exception of Matsuoka-san, I could feel the cold gazes of the other three staring daggers at me.
"You've been acting strange, Kitahara-kun. Whenever I arrive, whenever I leave, you're always here…"
"Me, acting strange…? That's mean of you to say, Suzuki-san."
I don't feel flustered by any of this deep down, though.
I simply manage expressions of "Aa-ah, I'm exposed," with a mere sour smile hanging on my lips.
"Mari-san and I circled around the office, asking around all branches of the editing department. Kitahara-kun's been handling an extraordinary amount of work."
"Speaking only by quantity, I'd say around Mari-san's level? About what Matsuoka-san manages in three months?"
"Please stop using me as a joke for everything…"
"And yet none of the assignments missed their deadline. And he looks as though he's not been having much sleep. It's possible he might not have even gone home…"
"It's really not like that… I did change, and everything's clean, right? See?"
Then, I dramatically tug on my collar for everyone to see, but I receive no response.
But she isn't addressing me in the kind way that I'd hoped for the most, nor was she using the reprimanding tone I would've settled for.
"When did you come to work and head home yesterday?"
"Uh… I don't remember it all that well, but I did head home safely by train."
I returned home on the first train just before 5 AM and came back on the train at 6 AM sharp.
"How about the day before yesterday? Three days ago? Have you taken a single day off since the new year? …Have you even slept at all?"
"Ahaha, that won't do, Mari-san… Why are you saying such mean things?"
"Because signs of your presence have been spotted throughout the end of the year. Even Managing Editor Sano from upstairs says he saw you on New Year's Eve."
"Like I said, it's really alright. I've really been going home properly, okay?"
I've been bathing every day, and I'm wearing new clothes every day as well.
What's the big deal if I don't sleep, then…?
Mari-san stands before me, clutching my hand that's over the keyboard.
Her fine fingers, stronger than I had imagined them to be, really managed to deliver the genuine feeling that she had returned.
"No, I have to finish this by today, so…"
Yet the voice that escaped her lips, while definitely one that was scolding me, had not the slightest hint of love in it.
"Kitahara, do you remember the promise you made with me last year? I told you not to take assignments from other colleagues by yourself…"
"…Did we talk about something like that?"
"…! If you're going to forget or disobey what your superior tells youーwhat I tell youーthen you fail as a member of society! I wouldn't hire a brat like that even if he had an outstanding work ethic!"
"Now, go home. You don't have to come tomorrow either. …Not like you'll be getting any work even if you do come."
"I'm telling you not to give me any more trouble!"
"I'm taking him home now. …He's dismissed now, do you understand?"
I had originally intended to resist.
Given Mari's strength, it's completely possible to pry myself away from her.
Yet… my hand is now clasped by a woman's fingers, dragging my body along with it.
I'm incapable of feeling either the tiredness or sleepiness as usual.
…Because in my body and soul, almost all my senses have been shut off.
The worst thing is, though… due to the warmth transmitted to my tightly squeezed hand from her own, it's as if only my heart has managed to recover a little.
I don't get why she's scolding me like this. It just doesn't make any sense.
After all, I don't matter to her, right?
That's why she didn't contact me and left me here, right?
"We've already reached Minami-Suetsugu Station… How do we go from here?"
"Ah, yes, um… Hey, how do you get to your apartment from here, Kitahara?"
We're in front of Minami-Suetsugu Station's roundabout.
Having stopped the car here based on Mari-san's instructions, the taxi driver asks us for the next set of directions.
…As for why all this is happening, it's because I'm not being clear with the directions to my intended destination, as I stare at the floor with a reluctant expression.
Considering the fact that she was the one who dragged me here in the first place, Mari-san also hasn't been saying anything harsh, resigning to my conflicted attitude in silence up until now.
"It's alright, I'll head off from here. Here's the taxi fare. I'm really sorry to have troubled you with…"
"No. I'll send you to your apartment. Now, where do we go from here? Opposite the station?"
Her merciful expression… or should I say her lack of intervention that's not due to her apathy… has come to an end.
"Like I said, it's really alright. My place is just a short walk ahead. …Besides, it'd be troublesome for the taxi to go through many one-way roads."
"Even so, just take the taxi there. I won't allow anything other than me sending you to your front door."
"Now, like I said… how do we proceed from here?"
This is really troubling for me.
"But… I wanted to head to the convenience store for a little while."
Because I don't have the slightest intention of going home at all.
"If you want anything, I'll just buy it for you when I head back. What's most important now is that you get home as soon as possible."
"I wanted to have supper before going home…"
"You don't want me to send you home no matter what… is that what you're trying to say?"
"You're overthinking things… I just wanted to stop by somewhere."
My experiences for the past few days speak for themselves. I can't get any sleep even if I go home.
"I guess that's that… I'm really sorry for today. For giving you so much trouble."
That's right, the manga cafe in the station…
I'd feel a sense of somebody being thereーperhaps I might be able to get some sleep, as well.
"Well then, I'll excuse myself now. Driver, please open the…"
Just when I thought I could finally open the door, Mari-san's grip tightens even harder than before on my wrist.
"Suguro! This time will be the last! I apologize for the inconvenience."
She's not just locking onto my hand this time.
Mari-san is now also sitting on the left side of the taxi, vigilantly guarding the door that can be opened from the back seat. So long as Mari-san doesn't move, I have no way of getting out.
"I understand. …Even if it's in the opposite direction."
I'm the one who's clearly being an inconvenience, though.
Yet not only did Mari-san not abandon me, she also took a step forward.
…Now of all times, and so suddenly, too.
"Leave that for later! Just come in!"
Regardless of whether I'm asking where I am at the moment or whether I'm shocked by the room I'm now in… I can only say that I've been asking a question I already know the answer to.
Because the moment Mari-san decided to change destinations, I already knew where she wanted to go.
"Make yourself at home. I'll go make something to drink."
"…That taxi driver definitely had a misunderstanding."
An apartment with a security system and a hall at the entrance… And she'd pressed the 10th floor button in the elevator that led to the top floor.
"Wasn't that the spitting image of an older girlfriend pressing an invitation to her home on her younger, unprepared boyfriend?"

The room that I've been invited in looks rather plain; though the living room is too spacious for a person living alone, it matches quite harmoniously with the pieces of the night scenery peering through the large windows.
Considering she said, "I live in a small apartment" before, it seems like I've been lied to big time. The rent for this place must be pretty high.
"…I guess I can't help it if we're going to be seen as such. Ah, what have I done…?"
"You don't have to apologize for something that I decided myself. …If you're going to be sorry, though, be sorry for breaking our promise on your own accord."
It seems as if there isn't a man in her life…
"Here, have a drink. Maybe it'll calm you down."
What am I doing? As I get lost in my everyday imagination, a steaming cup is placed before me.
I can detect a wafting fragrance from the cup.
As it seeps into my mouth, steam trickles into my nose, providing a gentle warmth to my face and throat.
I feel a gentle warmth, albeit with a slight tingling feeling to it, from my trachea to my stomach. I guess this is what it means to have warmth spread within me.
Though the taste and the amount of alcohol in this is obviously lacking, the warmth of it definitely refreshes my body and soul just right.
…If only I could've been saved by that, though.
"You can have more if you want. Drink this for today, and get a good night's sleep."
"I'm really sorry. After all, you must be tired from returning from overseas, Mari-san…"
"Don't worry about it. I'm returning from holiday anyway. Besides, the only thing we've been doing there is being stuck in the hotel doing nothing but drinking."
"…That doesn't sound like the best vacation for two young women."
"Well, that's… The way I am now, the only thing I'm capable of is being grateful for a person like that."
Mari-san's kindness spreads within me along with the diluted alcohol.
It's the same as that Christmas Eve, almost bringing tears to my eyes.
It seems that I've unconsciously managed to finish this odd beverage in one gulp.
"Ah… oh dear. I've actually got some souvenirs for you, but I left my luggage at the office…"
"You can pass those to me any time… Besides, I'm pretty sure it's a keychain or something like that."
"…Your guess is correct, but "besides" isn't something I'm actually inclined to overlook."
The inside of the cup placed before me is stained with a deeper red than before.
The taste going through my throat was also slightly closer to the taste of port wine, the sweet, slightly acrid aroma wafting in the air as it travels to my nose and through my mind.
Mari-san's silently watching me as I silently tilt the cup for the moment, though…
"Hey, Kitahara… what in the world is going on with you?"
"…What are you talking about? I'm completely fine."
It is as I had predicted…
Rather, Mari-san's concern for me was a given the moment she invited me here.
"There's obviously something wrong. You haven't been sleeping for a whole week. You won't know when you'll collapse, you know?"
"It's alright. It's not like I've been spending much time sleeping habitually, anyway."
"You'll die early, you know. You'll ruin your organs, you know? Your skin will become coarse, you hear me?"
"Speak for yourself, Mari-san… Aren't you in worse shape than I am?"
"I'm completely fine. I'm most aware of my body's condition. Even my health check-ups are all green every year."
"Well, I too, didn't have any problems during medical check-up. And…"
"It's not like it matters even if I end up like that."
"…! That's why I'm telling you that your resigned attitude is so strange! It's about time you realized your current condition now!"
She didn't do anything about it despite not being indifferent, but then she ended up getting involved with me after all. And now she's doing so with such a strong passion.
Mari-san has taken another step forward from what she's done in the past, edging toward me.
"Really, Kitahara, I'm begging you. If there's anything painful bothering you, just spill it out. You did that the last time, remember?"
The atmosphere changes from a comfortable one to a somewhat unnerving one… Our distance shortens by just a little bit.
She's so close that I can feel her warm breath reaching me.
"…In the end, this is what you've become. Even though I've said all that, I still couldn't help you, huh."
"It's really… not like that. I was really happy that time."
I was genuinely happy back then. During the time she took a step forward to get closer to me.
The nervousness of the atmosphere due to our relationship slightly deepening… that's precisely what I've been yearning for.
"Even so, I'll endeavor to help you in any way I can…"
I thought of that as the first step for Mari-san to save me.
…With a mentality of do or die, I immediately wanted to take the next step.
"…I'm really sorry. You were having such a tough time, and I left you alone for so long, Kitahara…"
"It's not like you could've done anything about it. You were busy with work, after all."
That's why I can't, I just can't… It's best if I don't expect anything.
"The latter half of it was just us having fun. And even if that was all I went away for, it would have been best for me to just cut the trip short and come back earlier."
"If you had done that, I'd feel even more depressed. I'd feel as though I'm being a huge burden to you."
I can't let this person see that side of me. I can't reveal the truth about me to her, the reality of the suffering that I've been through.
"It's not like that trip was anything special anyway. Really, Sawako's such a handful, babbling at one moment and causing loads of trouble at the next… She's such a massive pain."
"…Doesn't that sound fun? I'm envious about that."
Because who knows if I'd be shaken again.
"What's supposed to be fun about that? It's brought nothing but shame to me. Not to mention that it didn't solve anything and only deepened the mystery…"
"Mystery… huh. I guess it really was a mysterious trip, then."
I'd never know if she'd tear our distance and leave me immediately the next day after surrounding me with warmth like this.
"It's a completely incomprehensible and wasteful mystery to me. What with getting to know about the feelings of a younger man and whatnot…"
That's why this warmth, this expression of hers… I can't take it at face value at all.
Mari-san pours some wine into her own glass after that, finishing it in one gulp without diluting it.
"Well, so… I guess it's my turn to ask questions from here on."
Because of that, Mari-san's breath has the same sweet scent of the steam from a moment ago as I feel it on my face.
That sentence alone was enough for the both of us to decide the month and day of when it happened.
Yet the sentence she followed up with couldn't really convey what Mari-san was trying to tell me.
It seems as though Mari-san also realizes that she's not expressing herself well, as she lets out a somewhat disappointed sigh.
"Mmm… I guess I can't help, then… even though I'm a woman and all…"
To put it accurately, it's not that she can't express herself, but rather me continuing to avoid the subject.
Regardless of the subject, I remain apprehensive about resuming our conversation, even now.
I guess that's why we're bringing up the previous subject again.
"I've told you before, Mari-san… you and Touma Kazusa have some similarities."
"Eh, huh… how so? We don't look alike at all, and she's more beautiful and young, too…"
So as to avoid advancing to the next stage, I'm only here meaninglessly analyzing the current subject.
"It's not something that can be compared. Touma has her own pros, and you have your own qualities too, Mari-san."
"Flattery will get you nowhere, you know?"
(What specifically do we have in common?)
"Let's see… I guess I'll first talk about the way you two speak. Particularly, when you're being blunt and cold."
"And there's your demeanor, always so full of confidence. Not wanting to lose to anyone, thinking of yourself as a genius, and talking about these things without even thinking about it…"
"That might be my weakness. Perhaps I'm yearning for someone strong."
(Or perhaps it's better to say that I've never caught your eye from the very beginning…?)
"The real Touma is completely different, though. She looks strong on the outside, but she's actually weak…"
(I'm neither of those things in the end, huh…)
"And that's why I was confused by that gap… and ruined a lot of things that were precious to me."
The words of the past have since ended here. It's as if they've ended almost at the same place as last time.
I can't reveal what happened after that.
I really do want her to hear me out, but the way I am now, I can't muster up the courage to tell her.
Taking a sip from the wine that had been left there for quite a long while, I discover that the wine in the cup had long since cooled down.
I finish the drink that had become difficult to swallow in one gulp as the alcohol and sweetness faded, furrowing my brows slightly.
…During this time, Mari-san appeared as though she was contemplating something, lowering her head in deep thought.
Though I've been forcefully brought into Mari-san's room, thinking about it now rationally, this is a really unthinkable situation…
I'm in the room of a bachelorette. In the middle of the night. And with some wine, on top of that.
"…Perhaps it's too cruel to put it like that. Fine. I'm heading out for today. Have a good night's sleep here, Kitahara."
That was something that I was supposed to propose initially… No, it's better to say that this proposition puts me in greater consideration, more importantly.
"Do you even have to ask? Even if it is my own home, I can't be alone with a man until dawn arrives tomorrow."
"And it's not like you're my lover or something…"
Yet I can't put my finger on this sudden feeling of having an indigestible piece of metal stuck in my throat…
"Weren't you… going to become my strength…?"
"You can sleep on the bed. I'll check up on you in the morning."
I feel as though I've been betrayed "yet again," for some reason…
"If that's the case… If that's the case, why did you invite me into your room?"
"It's because you weren't willing to go back to your own home, no? The way I see it, you've really given me a lot of trouble."
"You must be tired now, right? Or are you saying you can't sleep until I sing you a lullaby? …What a child you are."
"That okay? Well then, good night. Ah, go home once you've woken up."
This person wants to run away again. To throw me away again.
To… give up on me, right here and now.
"Oh, and, um… you don't have to come back to work temporarily. Come back after your finals and when your mind has settled down a little."
Mari-san rises from where she was sitting. This is her own room, but she's leaving me here and getting out herself.
That's fine, however. I'm not harboring any expectations, after all.
That's why I won't feel hurt at all. Even if she changes her mind all of a sudden, I can still completely accept it the way I had anticipated it to be.
That's why I should've just said, "As I thought, I should go home."
And then things would go back to normal again starting tomorrow…
She'd return to being the normal, reliable superior of where I work part-time, albeit not one that I'd have a deep relationship with, and nothing more…
"Here, I've added some tepid water to wine. Let's think of it as us starting over."
It hadn't been five minutes since I ran out of the apartment before I got caught by Mari-san again.
To explain why, I was confused to the point where I didn't know where to go after I left the apartment, and I was in a state where I couldn't even take a step forward.
Forcefully, but gently holding my hand in my current state, Mari-san used the same action as before, taking me back to her own room once again.
"I'll go change for a bit… Don't even think about running away, okay?"
She never turned around the whole way as she took me back, refusing to let me see her expression.
At first, I thought she didn't want me to see her quivering due to anger…
The moment I realized the real reason she did so, knowing that she didn't want anyone other than me to see her back at that moment, I could no longer resist my tears.
She still had filthy traces of my semen on her back, and yet she didn't think for a moment to change, immediately going out of the house just to save me…
"Sorry for the wait… Alright, you're still there. That's good to know."
"Well, I'll admit it felt really hot at first, but it really became cold and uncomfortable after going outside."
"Oh, that's… It's not like I'm saying that because it's yours specifically…"
"…How about coming a bit closer to the middle? Why don't we talk for a bit?"
Mari-san's unbelievable kindness feels excruciating as I huddle myself in the corner of the spacious room, hugging my head.
"Perhaps you should take a warm bath first? After all, it was really cold outside."
"…Can't you manage a sentence or two? The fact that you're not saying anything makes things very discomforting."
"…Please report me to the police. Please appeal to charge me for my crime."
"As if I could do that. …I wouldn't want to steal your future from you."
"But I… I wanted to take you for myself. …It's no different than actually successfully doing it."
"Even so, there's no point in pressing charges about it."
"It's because I wouldn't win. That's settled."
"After all, I was the one who forcefully dragged you into my room, and I even gave you wine and asked you to stay on top of that. You have that taxi driver as a witness, no?"
She's always trusted me all this while. She's always seen me as her cute little apprentice.
"Like I'd have the time to fuss over such an unfavorable complaint, anyway. I'm really busy, you know?"

"No, you're not late at all. …According to the time we arranged to meet, that is."
It's 1:15 AM on Sunday at the moment…
At first, when Mari-san initially decided for us to meet up at the bar the three of us went to before, at 1 o'clock on Sunday, I suddenly asked the off-point question of "A bar open during the day?".
"I had some work that I couldn't put off, so there was a delay on my end. I'll likely need to take the day off tomorrow."
"Right, I believe you went all-out last Saturday, as well?"
"I've been off for five consecutive days before this. There's nothing I can do about it."
Working non-stop until 1 AM on Sunday is an impressive feat by itself… It seems that Mari-san's labor standards are full of holes, as always.
"Ah, I guess I'll have some beer first… No, actually, I don't think I'll have any alcohol today. I'll have some ginger ale, instead."
"…Is it really so surprising to see me not order any alcohol?"
"Do you have a fever? How are you feeling? You haven't caught a cold or anything, have you?"
"I've come fully prepared, so why are you…"
It's not that I'm trying to tease Mari-san's deliberate attempt to feign being strong. It's just that she really doesn't look to be in the best shape today…
"I'm not drinking for two reasons today. After all, Kitahara… you wanted to talk with me about serious matters, no?"
Mari-san takes a sip from the ginger ale that was served in front of us less than 30 seconds after she ordered it.
That's why I've put aside the unnecessary questions such as, "By the way, what's the second reason?" and the like, and brought my own glass to Mari-san's.
"I got really tired this week… and I didn't make much progress at work, either. I suppose I'm still feeling a little sluggish after having a few days off."
"If you put it like that, wouldn't that be cause for concern…?"
If she's working in a state like that, it's no wonder that she's not making any progress.
"Hehe… perhaps. I'm sorry to worry you unnecessarily. Still, I'm really not sick or anything."
"Is that so…? That's a relief, then."
"Well, what did you want to talk about? You sounded pretty serious on the phone."
"Ah, then… well, the truth is, I…"
"…! Ah, give me a moment! …I need to go to the washroom."
"I want to stop working as a part-timer."
Mari-san finally returned and sat on her seat when my glass of cola was about half empty.
Despite this, I knew I'd only be replied with, "I'm fine" even if I expressed my worry about her condition, so I immediately cut to the chase.
As Mari-san seeps into silence wearing a stern look, I can't tell if she's acting like that because of what I just said, or for another reason.
"I wanted to officially announce my resignation sooner or later, but I thought it'd be best if I told you first, Mari-san…"
"I specifically said you could only rest 'during your exam period.' I don't remember saying anything about letting you throw this job away, you know?"
However, Mari-san's clicking her tongue at me right now undoubtedly because of what I just said.
"I know this might be a bother to you, Mari-san, but…"

"Humph, it's not really a bother. The first two years of someone working under us are more akin to training, if anything. Otherwise, you'll just drag us down and not bring the company any profit at all."
"Look at Matsuoka, for instance. He's a good example."
"…I'd say he's not exactly okay with that. Constantly using Matsuoka-san as a joke isn't really appropriate."
"Training even a guy like him for two years can make him useful. That's what the company can do."
"Well, I already started standing out back when I was still just a part-timer, though."
Is that really all she had to tell me? And here I thought she was about to explain something more complex.
"Well, if it's going to be like that, nothing's wrong with me resigning, right? It's not like I've been capable of helping you out much anyway, Mari-san."
"…Why can't you get the bigger picture?"
"I'm just someone who's in it for the money, no?"
"To the company, you're an important investment that's bound to be utilized later. A rookie caring about things like that is ridiculous."
Mari-san, who didn't seem to look all that well from the start, is getting increasingly cranky, the thorns in her words getting sharper.
"But it's about time I went out and found a job…"
"You joined us, so working for us is itself your job hunt. If you keep blabbering on too much, I'll revoke your job offer even if you get one."
"I don't know what you're trying to say…"
"Our company doesn't need indecisive brats in its ranks."
"Keeping me here when I'm not needed doesn't really count as job hunting at all…"
"Oh, cut the crap, Kitahara. Did you really go out of your way to invite me out here just so you could piss me off?"
And with that, Mari-san behaves like a child looking sulky, puts her lips slightly to her glass, and puts on an exaggerated frown.
However, whenever she scolds me like that, I manage to cheer up, even if only a little.
I brought up my intention of resigning and ended up displeasing Mari-san to such an extent, and as paradoxical as it is, I'm admittedly a little embarrassed.
"Can I… really be a part of Kaiousha? After all, I might end up working under you, Mari-san…"
"Obviously, once you join us, you'll be in Kaiou Graph to the end. Why do you think I still keep up my relations with my friend in HR?"
"You don't like the idea? Working under me, I mean."
"No, I'd be glad to. Really. I'm also really grateful for what you said earlier as well."
"But that doesn't pardon the fact that I… Mari-san, I…"
"How many times do I have to tell you that it means nothing to me for you to be satisfied?"
"I don't think it's something that's so easy to wipe away. For me, or for you, Mari-san…"
"It went away easily enough with just a tissue. …Well, I did have to take my clothes to get dry cleaned afterward, though."
"What I did was the worst, most foul conduct that could be done to a woman. I shouldn't be forgiven for that."
"…Not if you didn't put it in."
"I can't do that… I can't pass this off as just some laughable matter."
Didn't your shoulders start to shake the moment I brought that up?
Haven't you distanced yourself slightly more from me compared to when we came here before?
"Still… this may sound shameless coming from me, but …I believe that I should make it up to you so that one day you can forget about all this, Mari-san."
Mari-san's current attitude admittedly makes me feel a little lonely, but I do my best to speak positively.
"I'm sure I'll return next spring. I'll put all my effort into working to pay back what I owe you, so…"
"Then that's what you should be doing right now. I'll push you past your limits to make you repay me."
"I can't… not now. I won't be able to bear it. My feelings are a mess right now."
"If it makes you that depressed, then you shouldn't have done that foolish thing. …That's not how you felt, though."
"I'm saying don't be so depressed! …No, it's my fault for bringing it up again. Forget it."
She's doing her very best to act cheerful around me, though there's one thing deep down in my heart that I can't ever forgive.
I did mean to do what I did back then…
Which is why my feelings are all over the place right now. It's why I can't remain calm in front of Mari-san.
I had acted the way I did toward Mari-san back then because I did indeed see her in that particular way.
For now, I need to put some distance between us and let things cool down. Until I no longer view Mari-san as a woman…
…Though I wonder if I can really do that.
"Please keep this a secret for now. In exchange for that, I'll become a more useful guy in a year… And then I'll puff out my chest and come back to work under you."
Mari-san's voice was sulky as it should be, but it was mixed with a little bit of an accent that sounded like a pout.
"You only talk about your own feelings but you don't take others' feelings into consideration. It's because of this that young people these days…"
"…Bourbon! The strongest you've got! On the rocks… No, I'll have it straight!"
"…Didn't you say you weren't going to drink today?"
"You think I can keep going without a drink? And after all the trouble I went to…"
Honestly, I shouldn't be thinking this, but… As usual, she's exceptionally cute whenever she pouts.
As I thought, they really are similar…
Even though she seems to be blatantly suffering, Mari-san has since then downed three glasses of bourbon in quick succession.
"Shut up. As if someone like you can claim to understand my feelings!"
"There's no way I'll understand if we don't talk about them. You don't understand my feelings either, do you, Mari-san?"
"I'm not done talking to you yet. So please don't drink any more. Earlier, with a sober face, you promised that you would listen to me, right?"
"…You can't say I'm drunk after only this much."
"Even so, please don't drink any more. I'll be drinking that after we finish."
While this certainly does appear to be about how much she usually drinks, she's clearly pushing herself today.
After all, her complexion is quickly turning pale. This isn't the time for me to just look at her with a pleasant smile.
"…Say whatever you want to. I'll listen carefully."
Having her glass taken by me, Mari-san gets increasingly sulky, puts her chin on her hands and turns her face away from me.
"Well then, I'll talk. About that night, how I ended up becoming like that…"
The glass that I took from Mari-san was marked with lipstick that seemed slightly brighter than usual…
As I raised the glass' kiss mark up to the light, I began to talk in bite-sized bits.
"What I was thinking that time, what I felt, everything. …Also, I think I'll get you to judge that."
Because if we don't talk this through, there's no way we'll understand each other. Even if me doing so happens to be the most despicable and selfish act in itself.
"This could get a little long. I'll be going back three years."
"Mari-san, you watched that DVD right? The live recording of the festival with Touma Kazusa in it."
Not only did Mari-san turn her back to me, but now she's even stopped giving a reaction.
"…And you've seen that I was present with her back then."

In spite of that, I still believe that she is honestly listening to me. I returned back to the way I was three years ago, as the class rep of Houjou High's Class 3-E, and the backup for the Light Music Club.
"I told you before about our group that was formed just a few days before the festival, right? That the original unit that was supposed to perform ended up disbanding due to a conflict with a girl…"
"After that, I dragged in Touma, and by cramming in practice, she somehow brought me up to the level where I could perform in front of a crowd…"
"In that sense… up until now, I haven't talked about anything but Touma Kazusa."
"However, there was one more person apart from the two of us that performed with us on that stage…"
"It was our singer, someone that stood out way more than Touma or I ever did. Someone who single-handedly earned the attention and cheers of the audience."
"The truth is… it wasn't Touma who was the first person that I dragged into the unit. It was that singer."
"She's attending Houjou University just like I am right now. And, well, she and I, um…"
The moment I was finally about to delve into the main point of our conversation…
Mari-san let out a sound that suggested she was about to throw up after listening to me speak for the whole time.
"I feel sick… and I don't think I can stand properly… I'm sorry, but could you please help me to the washroom…?"
"Look, we're here, okay? Please pull yourself together."
As I finally find the switch to the lights in the darkness, I discover the apartment where I was taken care of in the same state that it was back then.
…It really has returned to the way it was back then. It only took a week despite the fact that I cleaned it up so thoroughly.
"I'm letting you down, okay? Please ease up a little."
I loosen my arms that have been supporting Mari-san's body and slowly place her on the bed.
Mari-san's face is still pale, and cold sweat is dripping down her forehead.
"For now, let's get you some medicine. Where do you keep them?"
"I have some medicine on me. I have medicine for digestion, colds, headaches, and some turmeric. Would you like any?"
"Having this much is common sense… Here, I've brought you some water. Will you drink some?"
As I hold out a cup to Mari-san as she remains collapsed on the bed, she replies to my gesture only by slightly opening her mouth.
I reluctantly tilt the cup such that its edge touches Mari-san's lips without spilling any water, and she drinks the water in small sips as it slides down her throat.
"It doesn't seem like you have a fever… Do you still feel sick right now?"
"…Please, you can leave nodding or shaking your head until after you've finished drinking."
"C-Cough, cough… w-well, you were the one who was asking me questions while making me drink."
In any case, she still seems to be properly conscious.
"You didn't have to force yourself to come if you weren't feeling well… I could've rearranged the date had you informed me."
"Such irresponsible behavior just won't pass when it comes to work."
"This isn't work, but a private matter. Isn't it okay to be just a little irresponsible?"
"…You sure are annoying, aren't you, Kitahara?"
Seemingly sulky, Mari-san turns away from me, though she also relaxes her whole body and slowly stretches out her limbs.
…She's doing this right in front of the man who attempted to violate her just recently. I know she's not feeling well, but she's still way too defenseless.
"I think it's for the best that you go to the hospital tomorrow…"
"Nothing will be open tomorrow. I also happen to have the day off."
"Then you're going to get some proper sleep for the whole day tomorrow, right?"
"You really do love to lecture others, don't you? Even though I'm supposed to be above you in every way…"
"It's because I'm worried about you, Mari-san."
"I'm fine. Quite frankly, I've already gotten a lot better now. I could probably go out and get back to drinking again right now, you know?"
As I remain exasperated about the fact that Mari-san's whining like a child, I can sense signs of improvement from her, which is naturally quite a relief.
Her complexion still isn't looking too good, though, and she hasn't completely stopped sweating, either.
Even so, compared to her miserable state that was so bad that she couldn't even whine back at the bar, she certainly does seem to look a lot better…
…Doesn't she look a little too comfortable?
Before I noticed it, she's only wearing her shirt. She's unfastened her belt and even the hook on her skirt…
While I can't see anything critical, I can catch a glimpse of what's beneath the gaps of her formal wear. I shouldn't be seeing this, but her bare skin and underwear are…
"Yeah, there's no problem whatsoever now. Sorry I made you worry."
"Please don't mind me. So you're alright now, Mari-san?"
"I'm really a lot better now… it's thanks to you, Kitahara."
"I'm relieved to hear you say that."
Mari-san's unkempt state made me realize something.
"Well, take care. I won't be showing up at the editing department for the time being, but I wish you well."
The current scene I'm seeing that is no different from what I saw the previous week made me remember.
"What do you mean, why…? Isn't that the right thing to do?"
I just can't continue to be in this apartment.
After all… this is the scene of the crime.
"Is abandoning me and going home the right thing to do in your eyes…?"
"But you're alright now, aren't you? Didn't you just tell me that a moment ago?"
With the way I am now, I just can't think of a reason for why Mari-san's taking an accusing tone with me at the moment.

"Are you going to take my words at face value? You know I'm someone who will try to pass off pneumonia as just a common cold, right? And you know that I'm not someone who takes a day off because I have a 40°C fever, right?"
"That's why you should get some proper rest tomorrow. And if you're still uncomfortable even then, take Monday off as well."
"Didn't I stay by your side the whole time when you were crying before this…? How ungrateful you are."
Why is she taking an attitude with me that I can only describe as extraordinarily cute…?
"I'm… a man who tried to violate you, you know?"
Mari-san stops defending me the moment she starts pouting.
"That's right, I'm just the worst. That's why I shouldn't be by your side at all, Mari-san."
And once Mari-san starts pouting, she destroys herself with logic that's uncharacteristically full of holes.
I look at Mari-san once again while keeping my distance.
A prominent red has returned to her once-pale face, but on the other hand, her wet eyes are reminding me of another emotion right now.
While her expression is undoubtedly angry, it's difficult for me to make out the other emotion that's mixed in.
And it might be a blend of more than two emotions to begin with.
If I continue staring into her eyes like this, there's no doubt I'll feel drawn to her again.
"In any case, please get some sleep now. If you still feel uncomfortable when you wake up tomorrow, please give me a call."
And if that were to happen, I'd end up doing the same thing I did back then…
Rather, I might not even be able to restrain myself given how feeble Mari-san is this time…
"That's not it! It's not that this is… I haven't actually fallen ill!"
"Then how are you going to explain this? No matter how I look at it, you look miserable right now…"
"That's why I'll explain what this is… I think it's the side effect of the medicine I took."
"Please don't make stuff up. What medicine are you saying you've taken?"
I simply couldn't understand what Mari-san was trying to tell me at all.
I can only deduce that she was confessing something ridiculous to me from the way she seemed deep in thought and how her complexion flared up instantly…
"I… started taking them the day before yesterday. I went to a gynecologist for a prescription when I had a break at work."
"I had no idea where to go back then, so after crying to Sawako about it, she referred me to a hospital where I could get a prescription after a simple talk with the doctor."
"I had to skip my meal and wait in line during my break, and Sawako was giving me that kind gaze of hers all the while. It was so unbelievably embarrassing…"
"Why are you taking something like that…?"
"You're asking me why…? You have the gall to ask me why? There's only one reason I'd get something like that, don't you think!?"
And she mentioned she started taking them the day before yesterday… The day after I called Mari-san saying I wanted to meet her…
With all that said… what are you trying to convey to me?
"That's why… don't say you're heading home."
I was completely rooted to the floor the instant Mari-san murmured those few words to me.
"But why, I… after all, Mari-san, what I did to you…"
"I just can't afford to quit my job right now. That's why getting pregnant isn't something I can afford."
"That's just how it is… There's no other reason that I couldn't accept you that day."
The thoughts in my head vanished once more.
It's because she unveiled a trump card that completely invalidates the sin of my deplorable actions back then.
"No, I'm sorry. There's still one more thing I've been hiding from you. I drank every day while I was on my trip and that did a number on my skin. It was why I was a little hesitant…"
"Suzuki was terrible, you know! When I finally saw her after a long while, she said to my face, 'Your skin's getting ruined you know'…"
"That's why I stopped drinking for a while. That, and after work, I would go into beauty salons on the way home…"
"Wait a minute, Mari-san, just wait a minute!"
"S-Still, I ended up going all out with drinking earlier… to have both my mood and my skin ruined, it's just the worst…"
"T-Those trivial things don't matter! More importantly, about what you said earlier…"
Before I knew it, Mari-san's face was right in front of me.
Even though I'd only sidled up beside her bed to witness her feverish expression up close.
"W-What's so trivial about that!? What should I do if I expose my body while it's not at its best and get rejected by you!?"
That's why I can hear Mari-san's angry, shrill voice ringing in my ears.
And I can feel Mari-san's warm breaths teasing my cheeks.
"I've blown almost 100000 yen just this week… all because you said you wanted the two of us to meet alone…!"
Why would someone like her waste so much money and time for my sake…?
If she's gone so far and even forgave me after what I've done to her, does that mean she's…
"You're telling me that you've forced yourself to do all that so you could cover for me…?"
She's offering her body as the ultimate form of protection, all so she can relieve me of any thoughts of guilt…?
"You're the one who's saying such boorish things! Why do you keep beating yourself up like that!?"
As I thought, my attempt to belittle myself was cut down in a single stroke.
It's the one thing that's just typical for Mari-san to do.
"Even so, you're just that precious of a subordinate to me. …So precious, in fact, that I just can't refuse you when you want me."
"That's not a thought a superior should be having. And it's not something that a subordinate should be allowed to do, either."
Words like those just can't come out of my mouth anymore.
The only thing that's happening is that my hands are unknowingly reaching out to her…
No, I don't have any excuses anymore. Without hesitation, I willingly reach out toward Mari-san's cheeks.
"As I thought… you're so foolish, Mari-san."
I don't know a superior who's spoiled by her subordinates. And I can't imagine myself meeting a superior like her ever again in my whole life.
"After all, I'm, well… quite a bit older than you."
As my hands tickle her cheeks, Mari-san averts her gaze from mine.
"I'm an adult, so there are various countermeasures I should put up…"
"That's normally something the guy should be doing."
"What would you do if you just kept on waiting only for nothing to end up happening? …Wouldn't you feel frustrated?"
I won't let her turn her face away like her eyes, so I put my hands on her cheeks.
"Is it alright if I… kiss you?"
"U-Umm… Why are you going out of your way to ask me a question like that? Aren't you someone who goes straight to violating others without a word?"
"…I'm really sorry for what happened back then. It's just that I don't want you to hate me anymore, Mari-san."
After all, this is different from the horrible way things transpired back then.
I'm quietly desiring her from the bottom of my heart and I'm calmly realizing what that means.
I understand what I'm trying to do right now.
…And I understand who I'm trying to betray right now.
That's why even if she rejects me before I can do that, I'll do my best to not let that happen.
With the way Mari-san's lips are dyed red right in front of me, it's difficult to resist the urge to make an advance at her…
But with the way Mari-san is right now, I absolutely can't force the issue. I just can't commit an act of betrayal again, and upon two people, no less.
But the determination I've built up was destroyed by Mari-san's words filled with even more determination.
"Kissing as we are now is… after all, earlier at the bar, I…"
She felt sick and rushed into the washroom…
"Why did things turn out like this…? If only I'd realized this sooner…"
"Even if you don't mind it, I do!"
Once again I can feel Mari-san's breath on my face as her voice rings in my ears.
I can detect the slightest scent of alcohol, but it isn't repulsive in any way; it actually smells quite nice.
"Give me a moment… 30 minutes! I'll take a shower while I'm at it. I'm going to clean myself up completely."
"Don't run away, now, you hear me! If you go home, I'll tell the police what happened a few days ago!"
It seems that I've been worried for nothing.
It seems that her condition is something entirely trivial to her given how flustered she is right now…
"…As for me, it's because my work is becoming more and more interesting. Gradually, I've been unable to squeeze out time for the both of us."
After we finished, Mari-san didn't take any time to linger and immediately bolted for the bathroom, saying she needed a shower.
She's trying to act nonchalant, all while hiding the bedsheets behind her back…
I'm not sure what she's trying to accomplish by that. She'd be better off wiping off the part where I went inside her if she wants to hide anything…
"Our time apart grew from one month to two, and when we finally met each other again after half a year, we both knew we couldn't continue like this…"
Having come out of the bathroom, Mari-san looks at me as I'm lying on the bed, and this time, she faces me directly and buries her face in my chest after a moment of hesitation.
There is no way I could possibly complain, being able to touch Mari-san's burning hot skin after her bath.
"Even so, this is something we should really discuss later on."
After a moment of sharing each other's warmth, Mari-san begins to talk bit by bit.
"More importantly, since long ago, while getting hurt by the distance we had, I continued to work to try to forget about it, and it became a vicious cycle where we couldn't meet."
She's telling me something dating back years ago.
According to her, it's an event that didn't occur either recently or very long ago. She doesn't want me to bother wondering about the exact time it happened.
"Moreover, the quality of my work was pretty bad back then. It meant that it was a period of time where our current chief editor, who was the managing editor back then, was really mad at me."
"So is that why you have… the principle of never running away from one's problems by working?"
"Now that I think about it, what I did was really terrible. …Not to him, but to the person I was interviewing back then."
I can sense nostalgia, a bit of regret, and a bitter aftertaste from her tone. And perhaps an attempt to come up with an alibi, or an excuse…?
I'm sure it was quite the drama, but she clears it up briefly and concisely, almost as if trying to be considerate, or perhaps trying to make someone jealous.
"I can't forgive those who run away by immersing themselves in work. I also can't stand those who should enjoy their work but don't."
And finally, she looks toward the present.
"That's why I hated the way you acted back then. I really hope that you won't behave like that from now on."
And thus, she ends her narration with the slightest feeling of nostalgia.
But this isn't what I had in mind when I decided that I needed to talk to Mari-san today.

That being said, given all that's happened, I can't bring back the conversation to my intended trajectory right now. I wasn't even able to tell her what I was originally prepared to tell her in the first place.
After all, "the way I am now" from two hours ago has now become "the way I was a little while ago."
It's no longer a topic I can discuss with Mari-san.
"You see… well, with the way things are now, I'll separate my work and my private life. …But let me be clear that my work comes first."
I don't feel that her strong words match up well with the amount of strength she's putting into wrapping her arms around my back, though…
"…For example, would we promise to submit our marriage registration at the city hall when we have our lunch break?"
"H-Hey! What I just said has no other meaning to it whatsoever! Don't lose your head over something so absurd!"
Well… she did bring up quite the absurd suggestion…
"W-W-Well, let's get to the main topic. …What would you do if you were assigned a special report just twelve hours ago and had to fly to the scene no matter what?"
"That's… well, I haven't been in that situation before…"
"Well, that's true. By the way, if it was me, I'd head there no matter what. It wouldn't matter even if I couldn't contact them."
"I might go as far as to ignore the death of a relative if I don't get it right. That's who Kazaoka Mari is right now."
"But when I go back to my private life, I'd kneel before yo… I mean, I'd kneel in front of my boyfriend and weep for forgiveness."
Perhaps there are times where our enthusiasm is a little different.
"…Well, this is something we need to discuss beforehand. I can't be in a relationship with someone who just can't understand how to work."
But I imagine Mari-san really believes that what she's telling me right now is true.
"…I'll make myself clear, but these aren't questions, alright?"
After all, even though I've only known Mari-san for half a year, she's given me plenty of reasons to put my faith in her, and she's the epitome of an ideal workaholic to me.
"By the way, right now I'm in the process of 'trying to understand.' …That wasn't an answer just now."
She relaxes her arms, and her hands touch my cheeks.
And as she inches her face close to mine, she initiates a kiss for the first time.
"As I thought, you're the man I've been looking for… Well, I should say underling."
With the way I am now, everything about my world, including myself, has been a lie.
The real reason why I desired you wasn't because I wanted to heal the wounds I have.
After all, I'm scared of losing these wounds despite how painful they are, and I'm only fooling myself that they're hurting so much.
What I've received from you isn't a cureーit's only an anesthetic.
"…Don't treat me like I'm someone fragile. You're making it seem as if I'm the younger one between us."
"That's exactly what I was referring to…"
And yet, this anesthetic just feels so good…
If this continues on, I'm going to be dependent on her. And I'm going to pass the point of no return…
When I came out of the bathroom, the room had changed to indirect lighting.
Since then, it's been an hour… Mari-san used the bath and then she let me use it as well.
I properly filled the bath with water, made sure to heat it up, and slowly, slowly calmed down my racing heart.
…Because it's the same situation as back then, so I don't want to make the same mistake I did that time.
The bump in the futon above the bed doesn't move an inch. But that part also brings up memories of that time…
But I don't stop there. I've already gone past that point…
…By hurting the person in front of me.
"If you don't face this way… we can't even kiss."
