I had to think about a present to give her that would not only make her happy, but would also not cause her to get carried away or misunderstand my intention.
I'm afraid of widening the gap between the two of us, but I'd also feel guilty if I ended up getting too close to her…
Unable to decide, I ended up going in circles.
And even though the gap between us is far wider than it was back then, and even though my own guilt has me on the brink of collapse right now, her birthday has inevitably arrived.
With the way I am now, I wonder what I should give her as a present?
I wonder if giving her a present is even the right thing to do in the first place?
The reason I'm hesitating now… is because I just don't see an outcome I can look forward to, no matter what I choose to do.
It's cold today, too. Just as the weather forecast had announced, it's going to be the coldest day of the year.
…I wonder if I'm stressing that it's cold today "too" because I'm comparing it to another day from years past?
I check the time on my phone and see that it's already a little past 4 PM.
In the end, and with the spoils of my efforts in my pocket after an hour's worth of hesitation, I leave for the train station's ticket gate.
"West Virginia Airlines, Flight 206. It's set to land at Narita Airport at 6 PM local time."
I received a short text from Mari-san that only wrote about her circumstances, which is typical of her.
…While I'm at it, it's also quite like her to be unconcerned with my own circumstances.
She sent her estimated arrival time at almost the exact same time as her flight departed.
She probably waited for people to cancel their flight at the airport… That's why she couldn't confirm her estimated arrival time until the last minute.
She did all of this just so that she can stay in Japan for one day.
I promised to meet up with Setsuna at 5 PM. And the flight's estimated arrival time is 6 PM.
Why did it have to be such a cruel coincidence once again…?
If only Mari-san would arrive at least two hours earlier… If only my promise with Setsuna was for a time at least two hours later…
But I've already experienced this before back then.
On the day I made the biggest mistake of my life, the exact same choices had appeared before me.
Why do things always have to be like this when it comes to the two of us…?
"Ah, t-that's… I just arrived here too."
"I-I'm sorry…! I didn't mean to react so strangely all of a sudden."
"No… I did the same. It's been quite a while since we last met, so I didn't know what I should say at first either."
"That might be a part of it… but it's a slightly different reason for me."
"I don't know why, but I was thinking about something terrible up until a moment ago… I was thinking about the possibility that you wouldn't be coming."
"It's strange, isn't it…? We've already made proper arrangements. What's wrong with me? I'm acting so embarrassingly. Aha, ahaha…"
"Sorry for replying to you so late."
"Welcome back. I know the trip must've been tiring."
"I know you've told me that you would be arriving at 6 PM, but as I mentioned in my previous text, I have an appointment an hour earlier. It's a promise I can't really go back on."
"I think I'll be able to meet up with you at around 8 o'clock. Text me where you'll be at that time and I'll head over there, Mari-san, whether it's the company or your apartment."
"I'm really sorry I'm unable to take out some time for you right now. But I'll make sure that I'll meet up with you."
I'm very sorry for not being able to welcome you back. I'm very sorry for making you wait so long.
But I've decided to talk to Setsuna. I need to put an end to everything before I can come clear to you about all that's happened.
I need to uphold my promise with Setsuna, at least. I think this is more important than anything else right now.
Even if it means that only painful times lie ahead. Even if it means all that's waiting for us at the end of it all is a sorrowful reality.
No, that is exactly why I simply can't run away from Setsuna…
I can't repeat the mistake I made three years ago.
"I need to wait two hours… huh."
"Eh? Ah, ahh… actually, we're in the same time zone. It's 6 PM here too."
"No, um… I'll explain the details when I get back there. Do you mind doing me an urgent favor for the time being?"
"The chief editor should be here today, right? Yeah… I'm sorry, but could you help me arrange a meeting with him? He'll likely wait for me if you just tell him that I've returned."
"Let's see… Just in case, let's meet at 9 PM."
"Ah, it's fine, I'm not planning on drinking…"
"Come now, take it, even if only for our toast."
"I do recall you going on about studying hard for your entrance exams up until a moment ago…"
"You were the one who told me that I had to be present because we're having a celebration, Mom… Ugh, don't just pour cola in my glass!"
"You only needed to make an appearance, Takahiro. Go back to your room immediately after we're done with our toast."
"You're asking me to leave immediately after you forcibly called me here, and as my parent when I'm about to take my entrance exam, no less…?"

The star of today's celebration, who happens to be huddled right next to me, weakly pokes at my shoulder with her finger and murmurs to me in a soft voice, unfitting of the bustling atmosphere surrounding the table.
"It wasn't supposed to end up like this… I really just wanted the two of us to meet up alone together."
"I couldn't go out because they're having a party for me today. And then things just turned out like this all of a sudden…"
The moment Setsuna asked me if I could come over to her place today…
No, even before that, back when we arranged to meet up at the nearest station, I've already predicted as much.
"I should have arranged our meeting on a different date. How can I ever make it up to you…?"
I take out a small paper package from my pocket. Setsuna's eyes widen at the sight of it, and her cheeks are reddening quickly.
…I let out a slight smile as I witnessed Setsuna's response, though I also feel a little choked up.
That's right… This was what I should have done three years ago.
If only I had rushed to give her my present immediately after buying it, just like what I've just done…
If only Touma Youko hadn't recognized that I was "Guitar-kun"…
And more importantly… if only I'd been faithful to Setsuna alone, then…
"Well then, let's have a toast, shall we? Um… would you do the honors, Kitahara-san?"
"Eh? Wait… how could we make a guest do…"
"It's fine. If you're okay with me doing it, that is."
I could've had a calm, enjoyable time surrounded by the members of the Ogiso family back then.
And if I did that, I could've slowly and gradually shortened the distance between Setsuna and me.
"Well then, once again… Happy birthday, Setsuna. Cheers!"
"Kazaoka? Huh, I thought you were supposed to be spending the entire month over there…"
"I took a short break and came back for a little while. …I'll have to head back tomorrow morning, though."
"Hmm～ how should I put it, I have to deal with something minor yet important, I guess?"
"What's that supposed to mean? 'Don't use weird grammar if you're a writer,' that subordinate of yours will scold you like that, you know."
"Ah, since you're here early, want to go speak with the chief editor right now? I don't think he has any other meetings tonight."
"Ah, no… I still… haven't decided yet."
"What I meant was that I haven't finished the task I brought back yet!"
"I'm sorry… I think I got a bit carried away."
"It's alright for you to let loose as much as you want for today. After all, today's a day that's meant for you, Setsuna."
Setsuna has drunk quite a lot today.
And she's smiling without a care in the world.
"Here, sit down. …Would you like some water?"
She helped herself to food and drink and frolicked around… and she became heavily drunk before she knew it.
But no one was able to bring themselves to stop her.
After all, the others who celebrated with her just couldn't help but smile at the sight of the birthday girl simply acting as she should on her special day.
Setsuna sits on her bed and lets out a warm sigh, still immersed in the aftermath of the party's lively mood.
She shuts her eyes as if to remember the enjoyable time she had just a short while ago, and her wet lips move very slightly, seemingly mumbling something.
She might be singing somethingーthat I've never been able to listen to for the past few years.
"I finished my exams, I've managed to advance to the next year… and I got to celebrate my birthday with everyone."
"I got to celebrate it with you, Haruki-kun."
Setsuna's fingers are touching her earlobe.
"…You've said the same thing a while ago."
"I'll say it as many times as I need to… Thank you, Haruki-kun."
…To be exact, she's touching what she's put in her earーthe earring I've gifted her.
I had a fleeting glimpse of Setsuna looking quite amorous, and it caused me to reflexively look away from her and look around the room.
It's already been three years since I last visited Setsuna's room.
It hasn't changed since then. It looks girly, but not particularly fancy. Though I wouldn't call it simple either…
The room feels just right; it doesn't feel unfashionable or too over the top…
Though if I had to point out one thing that's just a little out of place, I'd have to say it's the kotatsu that is in the same spot as three years ago…
The atmosphere we shared when the three of us studied together and got excited as we talked about various things together still lingers here.
The first time I came up here, I was suddenly treated to Setsuna's homemade cooking.
I wouldn't say her cooking skills were exceptional, but she did have the fundamentals down…
And the food she served at the party today is proof that she's since improved by leaps and bounds.
As I indulge myself in this warm feeling of nostalgia…
Things between us shouldn't be allowed to be as they are right now.
"I haven't moved forward since three years ago."
"That's why even this room hasn't changed at all. I couldn't even change the layout of the room or anything."
"…I'm sorry. What am I even saying?"
"I'm sorry… I did it again. I ended up destroying the two hours we've had up until now in a couple of seconds."
"I don't mind it at all. That's why, Setsuna, please, just forget about it."
Is it because she's drunk? Or did she have to get drunk in order to say things like this…?
And just like that, Setsuna goes back to destroying herself in an instant.
She's hurt by her own words, and her attitude wounds her even more.
Inevitably, she's revealing that the bright and lively persona she donned up until a short while ago was only temporary.
"You've been just sitting there irritated since a while ago, how's the work you brought back with you going?"
"…I just got back, and all you're talking about is work. Is this how you're going to treat your coworker who just got back from abroad even though she's not used to living there?"
"No, the one who always talks about work is…"
"Well, how should I put it, it's almost time for you to meet with the chief editor…"
"That can wait a little. He doesn't have any appointments today anyway, right?"
"So what? Can't you see I'm busy here!?"
"What kind of power balance is this?"
"Well, when we set up meetings, we have to pick the time Kazaoka is free, remember?"
"Will we be fine starting April at this rate? After all…"
"Well maybe having him wait a little wouldn't be a problem, but can you contact him to tell him that you'll be late? I don't want to get yelled at afterward, you know?"
"I got it already. Jeez, you guys are being so cold to me even though we haven't seen each other for so long."
"Like I said, it's not like it's…"
"Thank you for celebrating my birthday with me."
Setsuna seems to be saying thank you to me over and over again today.
She's said thank you to me for giving her a shoulder to lean on. She said thank you for giving her that present.
She said thank you for coming. She said thank you for celebrating her birthday. She said thank you without any particular reason…
"I'm sorry for not being able to celebrate with you until now."
"I'm sorry that I couldn't celebrate with you on your most important day more often, Setsuna."
I don't know how to respond to her, given that she's being grateful for something she's supposed to be condemning me for.
"I'm sorry that I didn't come… on this day, three years ago."
"Even though I told you that I would make it no matter what. Even though I told you that I would show up, no matter how late…"
"Come on, it's alright. After all, you've already properly repaid me today. You've managed to make me relive that day."
The very day I betrayed Setsuna for the first time was the longest and most cruel day of my life.
"My father, mother and Takahiro are here."

It was the day that sparked the beginning of everything collapsing around us. Having betrayed her on that day, I only ended up betraying her again and again and condemned Setsuna to three years of nothing but pain and sorrow.
"And you're here, too, Haruki-kun… Everyone's gathered here to celebrate my birthday with me."
Something like this isn't even remotely enough to earn her forgiveness.
"…What am I saying? I lied when I said I was able to relive that day."
I was the one who lied that day.
So why am I not the first between us to confess my sin?
"On that day three years ago, my family wasn't here. I was the only one who was waiting for you, Haruki-kun."
"Everyone else in my family went to Hokkaido for a trip. I didn't call any of my friends or anyone else either. …I was waiting for you all by myself the whole time."

"I told you it was a party in order to surprise you, you know? That's why I lied to you and said that we'd be celebrating with my family, so you would be innocently unaware and be surprised when you realized that I was the only one here when you arrived…"
It's something that's completely meaningless with the way things are now, and it's something so heavy that I don't even know how to respond…
"No… that's not the truth. It's just that I couldn't make up my mind. …I just didn't have the resolve to tell you that beforehand, Haruki-kun."
Back then, I wanted us to stay together…
That was exactly why I was furious at Kazusa for disturbing that harmony; it was why I chased after her.
I thought that it just wasn't right for only the two of us to spend that time alone and believed that it had to be the three of us together.
And then what happened next was…
"Aa-ah, why did I keep talking about that now…?"
I wanted to spend that day alone with Setsuna. I desired Setsuna.
Regardless of my intention for seeking Kazusa out back then, that feeling I had was real, no matter what anyone says.
"Why am I doing this…? It's not supposed to be something that matters to you at this point, right, Haruki-kun?"
If that surprise had never meant to be a surprise…
I would have had no reason whatsoever to act the way I did back then, no matter how much time I had before the party.
I would have immediately rushed to where Setsuna was and embraced her with all my strength…
"I'm really sorry. Please forget about what I just said. …Please don't take a single word of what I've said today to heart."
My cell phone is vibrating in my pocket.
But I'm unable to take it out right now. I just can't bring myself to do it.
"…There was a bug there. Don't worry, though. I've already properly squashed it."
"If Mari-san said there was, then of course there was. …Where it got under her skin."
"Like I said, you don't have to apologize anymore."
"I'm sorry for not being able to see you until today."
"You've been busy, so there was nothing you could have done."
"You know full well that's not true."
But I just couldn't bring myself to look away from Setsuna with the way she is now.
I just couldn't muster the strength to let go of her hands that are intertwined with mine.
"You know full well that I was just running away, I was running away because I was afraid of what you had to tell me, Haruki-kun."
In other words… Setsuna herself is also fully aware.

"You wouldn't be able to talk to me about that important thing if I decided to meet you today, Haruki-kun. After all, you're so kind that you'd just swallow your words. …And that was the cruel calculation I made."
She knows exactly what important thing I intend to tell her. She understands the meaning behind the conclusion I've made.
"That's why I wanted to meet you today of all days, Haruki-kun. I know I can only use this day once a year, but with the way I am now, I had no other choice."
Despite knowing full well about those facts, she'll continue telling me that she doesn't know anything until I spell it out to her.
Setsuna's clinging onto that social rule.
"Ahaha… we might only be able to meet once a year from now on, huh? We won't be able to see one another until the same day next year… Just like Orihime and Hikoboshi."
"For Orihime to keep running away from Hikoboshi for the entire year… Hehe, it's just so disgraceful, isn't it? It's just so miserable, isn't it…?"
"That's enough… today's supposed to be an auspicious day, just like you said, right, Setsuna? It's not supposed to be a day where you're blaming yourself like this, right?"
"To think that even though I was the one who pushed you aside, I just can't accept you leaving me Haruki-kun…"
"No, it's not… I'm just the worst…"
No matter how I think about it, I'm the one who's the worst between us, aren't I…?
"Happy birthday, Setsuna. Let's just leave it at that, okay?"
Who am I kidding? Even if I say something so obvious, Setsuna absolutely won't admit it.
"I'm sorry, I'm sorry… Uu, uuu… uaah-aah-aah-aaah…!"
That's why I can delude myself into thinking that the Setsuna I'm seeing today is not her real self…
…And she's merely a sorrowful illusion I'm seeing under the haze of alcohol.
"It's the chief editor. He's ready to see you."
"He needs to go home soon, so please head over right now."
"…Not a single care for his subordinate's problem… What kind of superior only thinks about going home?"
"Is that so… It's already that late…"
"Haah… I see. The date already changed, huh. I see how it is…"
"I'm heading over now, so don't worry. …I'm sorry for doing this to you."
"No, that's fine… but could this be…"
"Mari-san… that thing, are you going to refuse it?"
"I'm the one who's been saying I wanted to do it."
"Still… that may be true. But Mari-san, just now you…"
"Yeah… Why am I hesitating now? I'm really an idiot."
"I'm very sorry for making you stay over this late."
"No, not at all… if anything, I should be sorry for keeping you up until so late at night."
"Nee-chan ended up enjoying herself too much… To think that she just drank until she dropped and just left her boyfriend aside…"
"That's not true at all. We've been talking up until a while ago. I wonder if she's simply tired because she's just finished her exams."
Tens of minutes passed before Setsuna had finally shut her eyes that were red from crying and fell into a tranquil sleep…
And it was then that I finally let go of Setsuna's hand before leaving her room and the Ogiso residence.
After all, Setsuna's hand was tightly holding onto mine up until her strength slacked from falling asleep.
I couldn't bring myself to let her go up until she fell asleep and no longer sought my hand.
"Ah, by the way, here, have some apples. You have to make sure you have enough vitamins, given that you're living alone."
If I recall correctly… these are from their relatives in Aomori.
Setsuna said something similar three years ago; she said something along the lines of me having to take enough vitamins since I lived alone.
I couldn't help but let out a grin upon realizing that she really took after her mother.
"Well then, I'll be off now. Good night."
"See you, Kitahara-san. I'll make sure to invite you next time when we celebrate me passing my entrance exams."
"Assuming that you'll be able to do so before Setsuna's birthday next year, that is."
"Parents with this kind of attitude can easily affect their child, you know? If I happen to fail, you're the one at fault, Mom."
"Yet you're the one who's at fault for not getting a recommendation."
Right when I felt like smiling and crying at the same time, I hurriedly turned around and went on my way.
The stars seem to be shining brighter than usual upon the sky of the quiet neighborhood, perhaps due to the cold freezing everything in place.
It's snowing, just like it did back then three years ago. My wavering heart causes my feet to slip and stumble forward.
The date's already changed. The last train is also going to depart very soon.
But there are still several hours left before Mari-san's departure.
I've failed to meet her at the time I promised to meet herーby several hours at thatーbut there's still time for us to meet up with one another right now.

I believe that there's still time for Mari-san to forgive me for what happened today… even if I have to apologize, drop to my knees, and plead to her that I'm willing to do anything she wants to compensate for it.
…But how do I even talk to her about this? How do I explain that I couldn't bring myself to end things with Setsuna?
In the end, I didn't make any progress whatsoever.
I was unable to tell her the important thing I needed to tell her. I was unable to act on the conclusion that I'd decided on.
All I know is that Setsuna knows exactly what I want to tell her. And I know that she doesn't want the conclusion I've decided on to become a reality.
And with the way I am now, I just can't march up to Mari-san with full confidence and tell her that I'm a man who's already made up his mind about everything.
Mari-san has tried to contact me so many times, almost as if she was desperate…
But she's not answering right now, no matter how many times I've called her.
Even though I pressed the apartment's number and tried to use the intercom, I didn't get the response I'd hoped for.
The automatic door at the entrance was tightly shut, denying me entry into the building.
In a rare turn of events, the editing department was also empty.
Because of that, there's no one who could tell me if Mari-san ended up coming to the department or where she was right now.
She probably went back to the editing department at least once, though, since there are traces of her being there.
Her cabinet was slightly dented. It's as if someone kicked it with a high heel.
That dent wasn't there before she went on her trip.
I press the button for the second, third, fourth and fifth time…
But no matter how many times I pressed the button of Mari-san's apartment's number, the irritated voice I longed for didn't come through the speaker.
Has she already returned to the airport? Or perhaps she's rented a hotel room nearby to prepare for her departure tomorrow?
Come on, nothing's going to change if I'm only going to hesitate.
I'm hesitant to use this key given that I've not received Mari-san's permission to do so, but…
I have to check if there's someone inside her apartment.
No, I don't need to justify my actions with a sense of duty or whatnot. …I have to find Mari-san.
I have to meet up with her today.
If I don't, it might be too late for me…
I can't really explain exactly what it is, but I have a very ominous feeling.
The door chain is not locked.
And I discover that there's no light on in the apartment.
As I thought, she's not here either…
The moment I turn on the lights, I am at a loss for words at the spectacle before me.
I was expecting to see her apartment tidied up, given that I cleaned it thoroughly when we were preparing for her trip together two weeks ago. But that's not what I'm seeing right now.
Isn't almost everything within her apartment strewn across the floor right now?
Her clothes, her underwear, her books, and other accessories…
More importantly, even the bookshelves, cupboards and dressers that were supposed to be keeping those things are also on the floor.
And they've been scattered, shattered, damaged, and knocked over… There's no room for me to even stand on the floor…
It's going to be very dangerous to even walk about the area at this rate.
As I somehow manage to recover my rationality after my mind went blank upon witnessing this devastation, a grave thought comes to my mind.
Did someone infiltrate Mari-san's apartment during the long period she was absent…?
What if Mari-san returned home without knowing anything and saw what happened…?
Fortunately, however, the worst possible scenario that I'd imagined is immediately proven wrong.
In the corner of the apartment…
The moment I find her hugging her knees under the kitchen counter, looking smaller than she usually does…
The moment I examine her and detect no signs of injury on her body or her clothes…
And the moment I turned on the lights, she was supposed to know that I'd arrived.
Even so, Mari-san seemingly maintained her current position without responding to my arrival.
I carefully avoid the shattered pieces of glass and ceramic scattered about the floor as I approach Mari-san, extending a hand to her as she remains slumped over on the floor.
Even so, Mari-san doesn't seem to be able to hear me, as expected.
In other words, perhaps her mind went blank just like mine did the moment she discovered the state of her apartment…?
Perhaps it wasn't someone else who had reduced her apartment to that state, but Mari-san herself?
"You told me that we'd meet at 8 o'clock, so where have you been up until now…?"
"What do you mean, thank goodness!? What exactly about this warrants that statement from you!?"
Her words and the way she said them are all I need to confirm that she was indeed the one who devastated her own apartment.
"Alright? Alright, you say!? You have the gall to even say something like that after coming here right now and pretend nothing happened!?"
"You have yet to answer my question… What have you been doing up until now? You left me all alone and ignored all of my calls…"
I was the first to ask a question. Though she instead replied to me with a question of her own.
"I wasn't paid by the company for this, you know. I paid to come back here on my own… You know that I've spent almost 100000 yen just for this, right…?"
"How much money do you plan on making me spend on you until you're satisfied!?"
At first, she had to spend money on consulting a doctor, prescriptions, and for personal cosmetics. And now, she had to pay to travel back here.
It's true that Mari-san has already put an unusual amount of money on her tab for my sake.
"Why do you think so little of me…? Is it because you think I belong to you and you alone?"
"I've… never thought of you that way. How could I ever think of you that way?"
"Answer me, then! What exactly is so important that it precedes our promise…?"
I can no longer continue hiding the truth behind my self-righteous excuse of keeping it from her until I've settled things.
"It's the singer from my band three years ago… the other girl apart from Touma…"
I can no longer put off telling her the truth, given that Mari-san's already endured so much from me.
"She's someone important to me, almost as important as you are, Mari-san…"
Regardless of what result may come from me doing this.
I hold nothing back as I divulge everything that I haven't told her up until now.
I tell her about that Christmas evening, about the very night I made that horrible mistake… and about the night that became the start of things for us…
Words that I couldn't tell her back then despite having tried many times to say them out loud are now flowing out from my lips.
I told her about the very first person I invited into our group, who happened to be none other than Miss Houjou High herself.
I told her how I quickly grew close with that girl who was unbelievably sociable despite her popularity and fame.
And how on that night after the school festival ended… it was that girl who I accepted and who accepted me in return, rather than Kazusa.
I spoke about how when I went for that overnight trip, it wasn't just Kazusa who was with me, but that other girl as well.
And I told her that the people around me knew that I was in a relationship with that girl back then, rather than with Kazusa.
I spoke about how I ended up betraying her with Kazusa, how we've been keeping in so much since then, and how we've only been dragging out our situation.
And then came that Christmas evening…
I explained how I came over to see Mari-san immediately after I left her.
I explained how I'd fallen for Mari-san because the pain of not being able to connect with her was too much to bear.
In other words, I explained how my act of seeking out Mari-san was an attempt to alleviate the wounds and pain I shared with that girl…
I did so because she was there. I did so because I loved her.
And that's why I came to fall in love with Mari-san…
The moment I finished telling her everything, Mari-san began to laugh.
But her smile isn't her usual, reliable smile that I longed to see from the bottom of my heart.
It's not the same, satisfied smile she lets out whenever we tease one another and inevitably embrace each other whenever we're in bed together either.
It only took a moment before her smile disappeared without a trace.
"So you're telling me that you came to me to cheer up because you had a rocky relationship with your girlfriend?"
"That might have been what I sought at the very beginning. But…"
"So you're telling me that your girlfriend refused to make love to you, and in response, you sought out an older single woman who would give in if you were just a little pushy with her?"
She can easily strike down "that's no longer the case as things are now" as an attempt to explain myself.
She can strike it down just as easily as whenever she plays the usual role of my strict superior, who can refuse any reason I come up with to explain why I've failed to meet a deadline.
"You're telling me that you were laughing at me the whole time while you were looking at me as you manipulated me with words of love that you never really meant?"
"I was only a replacement to you, wasn't I!?"
The glass she threw flew right by me and smashed into the wall behind me, shattering into pieces with a loud sound.
"You said that I reminded you of Touma Kazusa, and you said that the fact that you wanted to embrace me had nothing to do with that fact…"
The white wall is now stained with the red of the wine. …Mari-san has been drinking.
"But all of it was just a ruse to hide the truth about your real girlfriend, huh…!?"
"You're wrong… that's not true. Mari-san… please, listen to me and let me finish…"
"You expect me to listen to any more of this!?"
This time, even the wine bottle was shattered.
The red stain on the wall is spreading even wider, to the point where it can no longer be wiped away to return the wall to its original state.
The sweet scent of alcohol wafts around the room from the spilled wine as shattered glass is scattered across the floor.
"I have to say… this is the first time I've witnessed such an interesting circus act."
I expected her to be angry.
"I haven't seen a clown that can make someone laugh so much. It's almost genius."
"Calm down… please. My feelings for you are real…"
"There's just one single problem… It's that the clown herself can't bring herself to laugh at all!"

"…It would seem that the reality is a lot more interesting than the actual jokes about it."
By the time I went outside, the ephemeral winter sun was already setting.
Having not gone outside for some time, the piercing cold of the harsh breeze permeates through my body painfully.
The pain feels more extreme than I expected it to be, perhaps because it's amplifying the tortuous, anxious feeling that's festering within me.
I'm very anxious right now because what I've been doing in relation to the situation I'm in doesn't make any sense.
What have I even been doing?
And this is while I know just how selfish, biased, cautious and reckless I've been.
"We'd rent a car, just the four of us, and we'd be spending the night… at least, that's what she told me."
"She also told me that Takeya-kun would talk to you about it, Haruki-kun. I wonder if you've already heard about it?"
"I've never gone skiing before. Of course, I've never tried snowboarding either. Have you ever tried them before, Haruki-kun?"

"The truth is, I've been meaning to try something like this for a long time. It's just that everyone's had the perception of me being an indoorsy person, and it wasn't exactly wrong either, so I never asked anyone to do it with me."
"But what if I finally got started now? Would I manage to keep improving? Would I be able to glide on the snow at some point?"
"Those two are both really athletic, so I imagine if we casually followed them, they'd bring us to the summit and leave us behind, don't you think?"
"What do you plan to do, Haruki-kun? I'm kind of hesitant, myself."
"…The moment I heard you weren't going, I found myself at a loss."
After Setsuna's birthday party… After the horrible mess that transpired between Mari-san and me…
We started casually texting each other once again.
Though we clearly couldn't bring ourselves to do it immediately after Christmas, we've returned to being able to continue having simple exchanges about our daily life just like we used to.
And this is despite me knowing that the feelings I have aren't meant for Setsuna anymore.
And this is despite Setsuna also knowing that she's wavering because my feelings are no longer directed at her.
Even so, we've been looking away from those days where we suffered with emptiness in our hearts.
"Though I ended up berating him for asking me whether I'd go when he hasn't even decided when or where we'd be having this trip in the first place."
"…And while I'm at it, the one thing he did mention he'd decided on was that we'd be going to a place with hot springs to lure you into coming along, Setsuna."

"I've never gone skiing or snowboarding before either. Someone did throw around the idea for a group overnight skiing trip in one of my seminars, but the event coordinator shot that idea down pretty quickly."
"That said, I'll put a hold on my response for now. I haven't decided whether I'll be going yet."
"That's why you should decide whether you want to go without worrying about me, Setsuna."
"Sorry for giving you such an unclear answer. But this is about as good an answer as I can give you right now."
Before I pressed the button to send my text, I deleted a single line.
Was I talking about my "answer" to the invitation to the skiing trip, or my "answer" to something else entirely? Even I'm not sure anymore.
As I finally click the send button, the ever-so-slightly shorter text is sent.
I wonder what's going to happen to us from now on.
Will Setsuna and I slowly thaw out the snow around us… in hopes that someday, once we've both made some progress in our lives, we'll find a new world waiting for us there?
Or will the snow only reveal the filth beneath us once more, just as it did when it melted three years ago?
Or will we, perhaps, continue to drag out this agonizing limbo, where time seems to have frozen, for all eternity?
But if I happen to choose such a passive path, I'll never be able to meet Mari-san again.
If I choose her, I'll have no choice but to plow through the snow myself. I'll have to desperately keep trying through my own blood, sweat and tears.
After all, she's gone somewhere that's far beyond my reachーand quite literally, at that.
What am I doing right now? …What do I want to do?
I had so many reasons for coming out today the way I did, but in the end, I don't even know if anything I've done today has actually caused me to spill any of my own blood, sweat, or tears.
I just don't know what the right thing to do is.
The moment I was about to board the train, my cell phone rang, its tune so soft that it was drowned out by the noise of the train.
But while I expected to see Takeya's name on the display, I instead saw an unfamiliar ten-digit number.
And the voice I heard the next moment was…
An unfamiliar, friendly voice that I vaguely remember hearing before.
"Hey there, Haruki-kun. Long time no see～"
This time, the unfamiliar, friendly voice that I'd vaguely remembered hearing before greeted me at a bar in the middle of the night.
"Well then… Mari's not here, so let's enjoy this evening that's meant for the two of us."
"I'll leave that to your imagination, Haruki-kun. In any case, good work."
"I'm already on my spring break. I haven't been working part-time recently, either."
"I was supposed to be working under Mari-san anyway. Since Mari-san is no longer there, I may as well be considered unemployed."
When I was in the middle of explaining that Mari-san is no longer working there, Sawako-san grimaced, as if the wine in her glass had suddenly turned bitter.
And I can feel that same bitter taste rising in my own mouth as well…
"By the way… was it Mari-san that gave you my phone number?"
"No, I got it from Suzuki-chan. She seemed to be very interested in what I had to offer in exchange, you see."
What she had to offer in exchange?
"Is that a problem? Still, I'm the one who forced your number out of her, so don't hold it against Suzuki-chan, alright?"
"I don't feel that way. It's just…"
What does she mean by "what she had to offer in exchange"…?
"Besides, I've actually already called you once before, Haruki-kun. It was back when I was in Guam very early in the year."
"…!? So you were the one who made that call, Sawako-san?"
"Although, in the end, her phone ended up sinking to the bottom of a wine glass…"
And it caused me to feel so upset at Mari-san of all people…
At the same time, it was the alarm that signaled the beginning of something, as well as the explosion of my complicated thoughts…
"Mari's gotten even more vigilant since then, you know. She'd rather die than give me your phone number, Haruki-kun…"
I never would've imagined that these emotions were the result of a third party's manipulation…
Mari-san never bore even a shred of responsibility for the beginning of our relationship.
Back then, I simply forced my negative emotions upon Mari-san one-sidedly, even though she had done nothing wrong.
"…You aren't taking that part well, are you?"
"Well, how about we just let bygones be bygones today, and drink until we drop? Whoever survives can worry about what to do next."
In contrast to Sawako-san's cheerful mood, I just couldn't bring myself to cheer up.
After all, I've realized why she had me come here today, at this exact time.
No, I actually had my doubts at the very beginning, but by now I'm entirely convinced.
"Huuuh～ I'm drunk. I can't go on anymore."
"I know you've already drunk quite a bit, but the truth is, you're actually not drunk at all, are you?"
In less than ten minutes after our first toast, she'd already gone through three drinks.
And even after that, Sawako-san single-mindedly maintained a pace of one drink every five minutes, downing glass after glass.
"…You really are meticulous, aren't you, Haruki-kun?"
"I know how much alcohol Mari-san can handle. So naturally, if you can drink with her until morning, Sawako-san, that gives me an idea of just how much you can handle yourself."
And yet her tone remained as impeccable as ever. I could clearly tell that every joke coming from her mouth was deliberate.
"Hmm… So you know that Mari can hold her drink. You've gone out with her and saw her drink until she dropped."
"I'm just kidding. There's no need for either of us to drag this out even longer at this point."
"So what you're trying to say is…"
"Even if your relationship as superior and subordinate is no more due to her transfer, your relationship as a man and a woman isn't something that can fade away that easily, right?"
And 30 minutes after our first toast…
Sawako-san finally throws down the gauntlet.
"And it wasn't just a one-night stand…"
"I've stayed over at her place many times. …I even had her key."
And I respond to Sawako-san's confrontation, unfazed.
It's because I want to just get over with confronting her about her true intention of inviting me out here.
After all, as much as she has many questions she wants to ask me, I, too, have a mountain of things I'd like to ask her…
"Hey, Haruki-kun. Do you know that I'm really pissed at you right now?"
"And do you know that I don't think that simply hitting you a couple times will be nearly enough of a retribution?"
"You're welcome to put your thoughts into action. In fact, I'll even ask you to do so."
"You know Mari's wounds won't heal even if I do hit you, right? …Though I suppose there's still hope for you if you're ready to face the consequences."
Sawako-san's impish tone fades away, and she instead attacks me with a torrent of heart-wrenching words that stab into my chest like blades.
"I'm on Mari's side, so I won't say anything that could put her in a bad spot."
But as far as I can say as the one who's supposedly getting stabbed, her words feel terribly dull.
"Especially considering how severely disadvantaged she is right now. …It's just impossible to persuade her."
She's not out to kill me because of the weight of my sins. She's not even leaving me with a single wound.
"That's why I only want to find out how you feel right now."
No matter how I look at it, she's simply asking me "You regret it, don't you?" in the kindest way possible.
"Haruki-kun… how do you feel about Mari…?"
"Well… what I'm about to say may come across as extremely disrespectful or make you feel I'm slighting her, but…"
She was cute in the way she showed me her disapproving, pouting expression when I professed how guilty I felt toward her, albeit not for the reason I expected.
She was cute in the way she broke character and found herself at her wits' end, and in the way she became seriously depressed when she realized what she was doing.
"The fact that I feel that way about a woman who's older than me might be a testament to how tactless I am, but…"
And when I forced myself upon her…
The way her voice and breathing were when she succumbed to pleasure despite being so embarrassed and bewildered…
"She exposed herself that much…? So Mari's really serious about this."
"…It made me so happy. The fact that she'd shown a side of herself that I couldn't see at work to me alone."
Whenever I was in her apartment with her, it felt as if she belonged to no one else in the whole world but me.
"The fact that Mari-san seemed so taken by a man like me, despite having the broad horizons of the world in the palm of her hand for her to roam freely…"
Whenever I was in bed with her, it felt as if she had eyes for no one else in the whole world but me.
"It all affected me very deeply. …So much, in fact, that I'd forgotten why I even sought her out in the first place."
As I finished with my revealing confession…
And she still doesn't seem like she's getting drunk in the slightest.
She gazes at me with a resolute look in her eyes, though the glint in them has changed just enough that they no longer look like they're condemning me.
"I sure didn't expect you to be able to say that you love Mari so frankly."
"I was expecting you to say something along the lines of 'I don't hate her,' and be unable to continue from there because you were uncomfortable with or tired of the subject."
"What I've done is no different from what you just said…"
"You think so? I honestly don't think it's all that bad, you know?"
"Regardless of whether or not I could say I love her, it doesn't change the fact that what I've done to her was absolutely terrible."
"This isn't about me being unable to tell someone I love them. It's a matter of who I could tell that I loved them…"
"But that doesn't change a thing. You've just been made to gloss over that fact, Sawako-san. …Just like Mari-san was."
"You're capable of analyzing what you did… And you can clearly look at your own mistakes with composure."
"No matter how clearly I can see them, it means nothing if I can't correct them."
Ever since I betrayed Setsuna and got separated from Kazusa…
I've always been aware of my own flaws.
I've been aware of how my attitude, my words, and my decisions have been gradually wounding Setsuna, and how the distance between us came to be because of it…
I've remained aware of what kind of person I really am, as well as how much sorrow I've been putting Setsuna through for the past three years.
But I've been unable to correct any of itーin that sense, I've been cruel and incompetent.
"That's why my words hold no weight at all. …They're meaningless."
And despite how pointless this is, I've been repeatedly spewing out meaningless words today.
Word after word describing things that I cannot tell Setsuna and Setsuna alone keep coming out of my mouth.
And I'm telling all this to the best friend of the person I love… even though I've only met her once in the past.
The moment I stopped talking, Sawako-san looked away from me and looked straight ahead, looking as though she was thinking about something.
Is she fed up with me? Is she giving up on me? Or does she still harbor some resentment toward me…?
With the way she's getting deep into thought and continuing glass after glass, I just can't understand what it all means right now…

"She'll be coming back to the country temporarily. …She'll be making her final preparations for her transfer with her return, and I think we won't be able to see her for quite a while the next time she heads back to the United States."
"That's why when that time comes… I want you to talk to Mari one more time."
"I'm asking you this as Mari's best friend… please give her one last chance!"
But the feelings that Sawako-san are harboring right now are not those of discontent, resignation, or hatred.
Rather, she's making a request of me that I can't understand, as if she's the one in the wrong in this case.
As if she simply doesn't understand what I just said… No, it's as if she had no intention of understanding me in the first place…
It's generous yet foolish, just like how Mari-san unconditionally stood by me, and how Setsuna showered me with her unyielding kindness…
She's offering me terms that completely ignore how the world actually works and are incredibly convenient…
But with the way I am now, they come across as painful instead.
"The truth is, I never should have started meeting with her in private. …At the very least, I never had the right to do so as a man."
"Nothing has changed about me ever since I hurt Mari-san… Even if we were to see each other again, nothing would change."
"…Is this because of Touma Kazusa? Or is this because of the girl who's currently by your side, Haruki-kun?"
"…I see Mari-san really does tell you everything, Sawako-san…"
"Does that offend you? I apologize if so."
"No… I don't feel offended at all. If anything, I really appreciate it."
After all, Setsuna and I are both the kind of people who can't really do that; instead, we keep everything bottled up and harm ourselves in the process.
"I see someone I used to be in love with in Mari-san. And I'm in love with someone else simultaneously, even though I'm still in love with Mari-san right now."
Before I could realize it, I found myself attracted to her dignified, straightforward attitude and her forthcoming personality that allowed her to share everything with her best friend…
"…How can I ever bring myself to ask for her forgiveness while I'm still in this state?"
"…Then, when will you be able to do it?"
Sawako-san falls for any attempt at deception as long as it's positive, but she sees right through any attempt at deception that's negative.
"How much time needs to pass before you can finally bring yourself to face her?"
"When are you going to decide? Will you choose Mari, or will you abandon her…?"
If I tell her that I can't see her "right now," she's not going to let that slide.
"I'll make this clear, alright…? Unlike you, Mari doesn't have all that much time left."
"It's true! Frankly speaking, if you round it up, Mari's already 30!"
"Do you have any idea how long this'll keep dragging her down if she keeps this up? She's made up her mind not to even look for another man for the next five years!"
What came out of her mouth was something completely unexpected.
"Five years for you and five years for Mari aren't the same thing, Haruki-kun! Can you even fathom how old she'll be in five years?"
"Oh, you think that won't happen? Okay then, prove to me why it won't!"
After all… someone as beautiful, cool, and smart as her…
Someone as awkward, adorable, and silly as her…
Could never end up like that… is what I want to end my sentence with. But I suddenly feel myself break out in a cold sweat with my heart racing.
I know she's extremely awkward when it comes to love.
Wasn't it precisely because she's so awkward that she's been alone until she met me…?
And wasn't it precisely because she's so awkward and so easily flustered that I was unable to resist embracing her…?
"She'll be over 30 by the time a new man comes by in her life, you know? Her twenties will end up going to waste because of you."
She's acting like this… because she's her best friend.
She can criticize her without mercy and picture the worst possible future for her…
Even though she's being brutally blunt, I can see just how deeply she cares about her.
"That's why I want you to make your decision as soon as possible. …If you decide to abandon her, then do it in the worst way you can think of. You can callously mock her without mercy, if you must."
"How could I do something like that…?"
"Well, that's the only way you can do it! You need to push her toward her next love; you can't let her give up on falling in love for the rest of her life!"
As I remain as indecisive as ever, Sawako-san proposes a way to put an end to everything in an absolutely unimaginable way.
"Don't you get it? What happened between you two is something that will deeply affect Mari for the rest of her life. …You were the one who made her fall so deeply in love with you."
She's never once scolded me for being indecisive, only blaming Mari for letting her emotions run so deep while wielding her words more like blunt instruments than blades.
"I told you before, didn't I? The reason why Mari accepted you…"
"She must've either blindly fallen in love, or that man must've been a good match for her."
"…I never would've thought that you would fit into both categories."
What Sawako-san just told me was utterly ridiculous.
She said that she wouldn't say anything that would put her best friend in a bad spot, but she's exposing all of her weaknesses right now.
It's as if she's pestering me to strike while the iron is hot…
No… she's outright telling me that I have to do it.
She believes that what she's doing is for her best friend's sake, and she needs my cooperation to make it come true.
"I'll leave the decision to you… Apart from work, Mari just doesn't have the guts to make such a heavy decision."
I can't really bring myself to agree with her perspective, though.
Even so, they really are best friends…
She's clearly conveying just how much she loves her from the bottom of her heart.
Why are you doing this…? Why are you saying so many things to give me hope?
Why are you forcing me to make such a terrifying decision in the name of my own happiness?
"If things between Mari-san and me don't end up working out in the end… could you please take care of her?"
Of course, I couldn't let her hear that…
"That has always been my role. Please leave it to me."
Even so, the answer she gave me back then was extremely warming for my heart.
It was much more pleasant than the wine that I had in my hand…
"Well, how is it? How's work over there?"
"I lost count of how many days I haven't spoken Japanese for… ugh, I've just been so busy that it's dizzying."
"Seems like you're having it rough immediately after starting there…"
"For now, I suppose I've gone through about 90% of my clientele this week? I printed 300 business cards, but I already ran out."
"Is that so… So your work is going smoothly."
"I wouldn't have expected the opportunity to work overseas if I didn't have the confidence. I want to at least be promoted to managing editor before I turn 30."
"It's fine if you're keeping yourself busy… but have you been sleeping properly?"
"Care to tell me exactly how much?"
"What are you doing!? You know that you'll end up breaking your body and mind if you suddenly push yourself so hard in an environment you're still not used to, don't you?"
"I, I'm fine… I'm fine… How many years do you think I've pushed myself for up until now?"
"Weren't you absolutely fuming when Haruki-kun worked so hard that he didn't get any sleep!? Way to scold someone for something you're doing yourself."
"Ah～ Kitahara-kun, Kitahara-kun. I didn't call him by his name. Really."
"Kitahara, Kitahara, Kitaharaa… hic… uuee… hic, uu…"
"T-This is bad… it hasn't even been a minute and you've immediately switched to your sobbing mode…"
"Oh, for crying out loud. You're only crying so much exactly because you haven't been getting enough sleep, you know?"
"It's not just that I haven't been sleeping because I don't want to… I've been having trouble falling asleep too…"
"Does having to go to sleep alone really make you feel that lonely?"
"…This might be the first time I've felt this lonely spending the night alone in all of my 26 years. It's strange, isn't it? It's not even all that different from usual…"
"Damn, well, I wasn't expecting such a serious answer there."
"Well, what kind of answer do you want, then!? God, stop teasing me so much already…!"
"Aren't you drinking too? You're even more cynical than usual."
"I wonder how she'd react if she found out who it was I was just drinking with…"
"Haah… the only thing I have left to cheer me up is a phone call with you, Sawako… You must, absolutely… never abandon me, okay?"
"Now listen here… If you're going to be that depressed over it, you really shouldn't have told him you were going to break up with him in the first place…"
"No. Even I have a little bit of pride as a woman. No matter what, I can't cling onto someone who's already dumped me."
"Why can't you just try thinking about this a little more flexibly? He's younger than you, isn't he? Why don't you try cutting him some slack? You're being far too blunt and stubborn."
"Not to mention you're head over heels for the guy. You've exposed yourself way too much. It's almost enough to make me want to ask you what the deal is with that damsel in distress routine."
"I… He was the only one who was taking the initiative throughout this relationship…"

"Being wrapped around his little finger by his nonchalant words or behavior, or feeling a sense of bliss from a single word he'd say, or feeling like I'm sinking to the bottom of an abyss because of his aloof attitude."
"You're still wrapped right around his little finger even now."
"He always made me feel like I was a lot younger than I really was. …Ah, just remembering it right now is so embarrassing."
"Oh, grow up. You're old enough to know better."
"But then… the embarrassment started turning into pleasure, of all things…"
"…If I calm down and think about it, I guess it's possible that that's the sort of relationship we had…"
"Even though he was always so rough with me, and even though it was always so intense that it almost made me lose consciousness…"
"In retrospect, I don't remember any of those things we did as anything unpleasant."
"In fact, it's almost like my body has gotten so used to those sensations… that I can't even satisfy this craving on my own…"
"W-What kind of crazy things have you two even done!?"
"Not telling. That's not something I can tell even my best friend. …Haaah～"
"Well, that's all the more reason you should talk things through with him. After all, you still have such strong lingering feelings for him."
"If he comes to see you out of his own free will… saying everything was his fault and kneels to you for forgiveness, it'd satisfy that twisted sense of pride of yours, wouldn't it?"
"Aren't you going to be coming back for a while next month? Send him a text when that time comes. As for whether he'll come to see you, then, that's on him."
"If he doesn't come, then just pull the plug and give up!"
"But as long as there's still a chance, work hard for it, alright? It's not like you to give up before the outcome is decided, Mari. …Though I suppose that only applies to your work."
"Oh, knock it off with the 'what ifs' already!"
"Even if we manage to talk, it doesn't change the fact that I'll have to go back to America…"
"Didn't I tell you before…? He doesn't want a long-distance…"
"It's not like you to give up before the outcome is decided, Mari. …How many times do you plan on making me repeat that?"
"Besides… I'm sure he'll come to see you. I bet he's still thinking about you even now, Mari."
"Oh yeah? And where's your proof to back that up…? That's just your own wishful thinking, and there's no way I'll get my hopes up over that…"
"I do happen to have just the proof to back that up…"
"…I just can't do it. I can't bring myself to contact him. I don't have the courage."
"I know… why don't you contact him, Sawako…? If you can drag Kitahara over, then…"
"Don't ask someone else to do this for you! He's your man, isn't he!?"
"But I can't, I'm just so scared…"
"Oh, come on! You decide everything for yourself whenever you're at work! Why do you become like this when it has to do with a man…!?"
"Because I… feel as if he's turned me into a woman."
"What do you mean you feel it's that way? That's just the truth, isn't it, you iron maiden?"
"You absolutely must keep that secret! You can't tell anyone about it! If you ever spill this, our friendship is over!"

"Really, you're lucky that Kitahara-kun happens to be someone who's hard-working. If you happened to get involved with some no-good-man who can't even look out for himself, you'd have to be the one carrying the financial weight…"
"I've already been doing that for a long time! I've spent almost three months' worth of my salary!"
"Wasn't that because you got caught up in the moment and decided to lavish him?"
"Anyway! Once you decide the day you're returning, give me a call! Him and me both!"
"For crying out loud, she's so annoying…"
"But… I suppose this is about as much as I can do, right?"
"Whatever happens from here on out is up to the two of you now… I hope you'll do your best."
"…By the way, have you talked with Setsuna-chan already?"
"Ghaah～ How long are you gonna keep dragging this out, you idiot!?"
"I know full well that I'm an idiot, you idiot!"
People tend to lash out at others even when they're being rightfully criticized for their mistakes.
Having answered a call from Takeya for the first time in a while, I found myself raising my voice rather unpleasantly.

"You said you'd talk things through with her a month ago. Sure, you said it had to be after your exams were over, but it's already been a month since then, right? What in the world have you been up to?"
"I've been busy with… a lot of stuff."
Even after our exams ended, our circumstances just haven't been kind to either of us.
Just when I thought that I'd finally found a day when I could properly meet her, it just didn't turn out to be a day where I could actually have that serious talk with her.
Even so, it's exactly because we didn't manage to have that serious talk that our barely budding relationship is now on the brink of collapse.
I've spent many days in turmoil, knowing that getting to the point would take only a few seconds, but not knowing how long it would take before I could spur myself to do it.

"As much as I did say I'd keep an eye on you two, I do have my limits, you know. Heck, it's because of this that the two of you haven't given a response to the skiing trip in the first place, isn't it?"
"Like I said, you haven't even decided anything about that trip, like the schedule or whatnot…"
Setsuna hasn't given me a reply yet either, huh…
"Didn't I tell you to make some free time for this? What happened to giving me a response on that front?"
"I'm alright with whatever time you decide. It's almost March, you know?"
That's exactly why I'm unable to make a decision right now.
And just like Takeya had just said, it's going to be March the day after tomorrow. …It's going to be the month where Mari-san's going to return temporarily.
However, neither Mari-san nor Sawako-san has made any form of contact with me, so I don't know exactly which day of March she'll be returning on.
That's why filling up my schedule for March would be…
And that's not the only problem I have.
This time, I'll need to have that important conversation with Setsuna before I meet with Mari-san…
"It's about time you made up your mind, Haruki…"
Takeya's words suggested that he was enquiring about my availability for the skiing trip, but I know he's actually trying to bring me back to the conversation we had earlier.
"It's about time you made a decision, whether to fix things with Setsuna-chan, or to…"
"When are you going to decide? Will you choose Mari, or will you abandon her…?"
I had been confronted with two different voices referring to two different people, but they felt as if they were talking about the exact same thing.
I know what Takeya has told me. I know what Sawako-san has told me too.
And I know what it is that I must do.
"Care to elaborate what you mean exactly when you say you'll think of something?"
"For now, let me just finalize my schedule."
I'll talk to Setsuna. I'll make sure that I'll do it properly this time.
"Well, when can you decide on that, then?"
At this point, I'm sure that both of us are well aware that we're no longer talking about the schedule for the ski trip.
What we have isn't quite like the completely sincere friendship that Mari-san and Sawako-san share, but…
I think the two of us understand one another entirely, from the way we lie or the way we word things.
"Well, whatever… I knew that you'd never be able to finalize your schedule if I left the decision to you…"
"Well, I'll hang up for now. I'll get in touch with you again soon."
I apologize to Takeya in my heart one more time, hang up the phone, and…
The moment I open the door…
I become lost for words for a moment at the sight of my utterly unexpected guest.
"That's why I decided to make that decision for you. We're heading out right now, so get ready."
"You're not going to refuse me, now, are you? All you're doing is staying at home without anything to do. Besides, we've already reserved accommodations for tomorrow."
"I imagine Io's also secured Setsuna-chan right about now. Come on, pack your things!"
I was just thinking about how the two of us understand one another entirely, from the way we lie or the way we word things…
But I could not have possibly anticipated this turn of events.
"Didn't you decide to come back a few days later than this?"
"After confirming next month's schedule, I realized that I couldn't take a single day off, so due to that, I have no choice but to take time now…"
"…Though your official assignment starts on the 1st of April, more or less."
"So are you going to show up here? I'm here. …As you'd expect, they only work on the last days before the deadline, so nobody has come."
"I wonder if it'd be a good opportunity…"
"…I'll show up for about 30 minutes. I'll be finishing up all the remaining procedures, and after tidying my desk, I'll head back to my apartment and pack up overnight."
"I see… How long do you intend to stay?"
"Until the day after tomorrow… I'll go back on the first of March."
"There's nothing you need to apologize for, Setsuna. We're both victims here…"
"B-But… I was just wondering if any of this was bothering you."
"Bothered…? No, it's more like I'm at a loss… B-But I guess you're feeling the same way, aren't you, Setsuna?"
"I-I'm, uh… I think I feel more or less the same way about this, yeah."
"Does our commentator, Mizusawa-san, have anything to say about that exchange just now?"
"Hmmm, it's so pure and innocent that it even made me a little embarrassed! It almost makes me want to butt in and ask them how long they've known each other, you know?"
"It feels like a situation where total newbies went on a blind date and somehow ended up alone with each other, then made a big fuss inside the car!"
"And whose fault do you think that is, huh!?"
"We're about to get on the highway, but let's find a place to have a late-night snack before that."
"Ah, I'd like some Chinese food. I think there's a place that's open even late at night around here."
Even if I complained to the driver or the person by his side, they'd both just shrug my complaints off without a care.

It's been over an hour since I got dragged into this car. And the date has already changed, so it's the last day of February. We still haven't been able to catch up with how fast things have been developing.
After being hurried by Takeya to get ready for the trip, and being forced into his car, we traveled to a familiar place…
"…Come to think of it, I can't believe you got Setsuna's family to agree to this, Io."
When we picked up the girls in front of the Ogiso residence, I could tell that Setsuna had been rushed to pack just like I was, and she looked as if she were bound to Io.
"I told them we were planning on going skiing in advance. I wouldn't make a silly mistake about something like that."
"Even so, it's so sudden… Wouldn't her parents be mad?"
"I just told them that Setsuna had completely forgotten about the planned date, then her mother started apologizing to me. That was pretty embarrassing…"
"Doesn't that mean you lied to the entire Ogiso family!? How could you do that with such a clear conscience!?"
I can't believe these two… Would they really go so far as to cause trouble for their friend's family to achieve their goals?
"Setsuna, is this really okay? You haven't lied to your family once up until now…"
"There was nothing I could have done… She said that they'd already reserved our accommodation. I'd feel bad if I refused."
"You don't have to feel bad for them. They just rushed into this headfirst without even asking us anything…"
"Mizusawa-san, any comments on that statement just now?"
"Hmm, it's just one of those things someone who can't read the mood would say."
"Would you two just keep quiet for a second!?"
"It's fine, Haruki-kun. I don't mind it, really."
"I… don't mind traveling together with everyone like this."
"Haruki-kun, does it bother you? Or did you have something you had to do, maybe?"
That's right. It has happened before. Setsuna has lied to her family before.
Back when we arranged for a trip to the hot springs during Christmas. And back when she turned down a trip with her family and ended up being left alone in her house on her birthday.
Ahh… Seems like it was my fault every time.
And I imagine Setsuna didn't refuse this extremely rushed trip this time because…
"…It would appear that the problem is resolved, huh?"
"Let's just enjoy the trip. It's been a while since all four of us spent some quality time together."
The two perpetrators turn their heads around and smile at us.
The smiles of these terrorists are far too overbearing and self-centered, stabbing at the weak spots in our hearts.
Nevertheless, we know that their true intentions are earnest, and for that, it's not like we can say anything harsh to them either.
"Is there a guy out there who would go as far as to clean up the place of a woman he dumped so meticulously?"
Following Setsuna's line of vision, the sight of countless snowflakes descending from the sky fills my vision.
We've been on the highway, in the car of an amateur driver for three hours now. Tokyo is already far behind us, we're now at Yamanashi and will be at Nagano soon…
I suppose this place is called "snow country" for a reason. Before we knew it, the snow began to coat our surroundings, and it's only going to get stronger by the looks of it.
Between us talking about the snow and making non-committal replies, we continue our awkward conversation, as usual.
But to the two of us, the things we said probably shared hundreds of words' worth of information.
Watching snow fall through a car's windows, no matter when, will without fail evoke that day from our memories.
That view from three years ago… Back then, when the three of us stared at the sky together.
Although we're at a distance so close that our shoulders are almost touching, neither of us tries to take the initiative to touch the other.
Without a doubt, we're reliving the same memory right now…
No, it's exactly because we're thinking of that same memory right now that an invisible wall has come to form between us.
"The snowflakes are pretty big. It might even be wet snow."
It seems we're fine with normal conversations like these now. We no longer lower our heads, and we can look at each other and smile…
"You two should go to sleep for now. We're hitting the ski tracks as soon as we arrive!"
"You mean we don't need to take turns driving?"
"It's fine, no worries. Considering Takeya's the one who forcefully dragged you guys out, let him take responsibility."
"I… was hoping that you would help out a little, at least…"
The clock on the dashboard went past 5 o'clock before we knew it.
"Here, if you're cold, use this blanket. There's only one, but it sure beats having nothing."
Setsuna seems hesitant and apologetic, and I don't know if the way she's looking at me with a troubled expression is something that I should have expected.
"They're right. You should get some sleep, Setsuna."
I took the blanket from Io, spread it with my hands and laid it on Setsuna.
"When you wake up, the world will be blanketed in white all around you."
This time, even if just a little, is the first time I've touched Setsuna today.
In the dim light, Setsuna stares at my profile.
I pretend not to notice, and let go after putting the blanket onto Setsuna's lap.
But even after I let go, Setsuna doesn't break her gaze away from me.
The glint in her eyes makes me feel as if… she's both blaming me and worrying about me.
Although we're at a distance so close that our shoulders are almost touching, neither of us tries to take the initiative to touch the other.
…But now, that's no longer the case.
As soon as she fell asleep, Setsuna leaned her head on my shoulder.
But I couldn't even bring myself to embrace her, I only supported her with my body.
The blanket that was meant for Setsuna somehow ended up on me as well, and now we're sharing it.
Setsuna must have done this on purpose. It's like she's frustrated at me for hesitating, that's why she's doing something so pushy.
Soon after our distance was reduced to zero by force, Setsuna's head leaned onto my shoulder, and soon enough, she leaned onto me completely.
Setsuna's body is warming me up.
We're simply using the most efficient way for the two of us to stay warm and nothing moreーby sharing a blanket between the two of us.
…Who am I kidding. We're not just keeping each other warm, and I'm sure everyone here knows that as well as I do.
Long eyelashes arch from her closed eyes. Sweet breath spills out from her wet lips. Not a man in this world could deny that Setsuna's face is adorable right now.
Any man would love to take on the task of being her pillow, without a doubt, and I'm sure that anyone would feel bliss at this moment.
Even… me. In fact, it's exactly because it's me that this feeling is all the more intense.
Because Setsuna… is a very precious girl to me.
No matter how many times we've clashed. No matter how many times we've hurt each other.
And even if I ever meet another person in my life who I'll love more than anyone else.
And as for that serious talk I need to have with Setsuna, the conclusion between the two of us…
With the distance between us being what it is right now, I wonder what form it'll end up taking.
Will it be the distance between Tokyo and Tokyo, or the one between Tokyo and New York?
"So the TV was over there… and the fridge was here. The cupboard, the dresser, the table, the floor lamp…"
"All I did in this place was have sex with him, huh…"
"We found a spare key to this apartment. It was inside your mailbox…"
"That should be all of the keys, right? Well then, I'll be holding on to this."
"Did that… did the key holder come with something attached to it? Like, um, some sort of doll…? It was pretty unique…"
"Now then, what's left is to check the apartment. If you'll excuse me."
"All right, it looks like you have been keeping it reasonably clean. It doesn't seem like there will be any need for repairs."
"I see… there was nothing there, huh."
"Ah, no, er… I don't really expect to get my deposit back."
"That's why I'm here to check things thoroughly. Although, since you're going through an agency, there are definitely situations in which you wouldn't get your money back."
"Nothing wrong with the shower curtain either… The bathroom's good too."
"There are some dents in the flooring, but it's nothing we need to go out of our way to fix."
"Ah, there's a stain over here, though. This might be a bit of trouble…"
"Look, over here. This part's turned a little red, see?"
"What is this… juice, perhaps? Aa-ah, and it's quite a large stain, too."
"Sorry, but we'll need to do something about this filthy part here. Hmm… I wonder how much this'll cost."
"Yes, I think it's quite plain to see that…"
"…What are you talking about? It's not filthy at all."
"It's been scrubbed clean… Polished to perfection. By him…"
"But look, there's… a red stain right here… you can see it, right?"
"I don't see anything of the sort. It's pure white."
"Well, that's an issue. Look harder, please. Maybe try going a bit closer…"
"What do you mean, you won't stand for this…?"
"This is the one thing I won't budge on! How does that not look perfectly clean to you!?"
"Whoa… it's snowing quite heavily. It seems we'll be able to ski on fresh snow again tomorrow."
"It'll be a real pain if the snow blows too heavily and the ski lifts become inoperational, though."
As expected, the set of equipment we rented didn't fit us as well as I would've hoped…
Particularly, the ski boots were extremely tight, and they were quite agonizing to have on since noon.
"I should've known that skiing for the first time after turning twenty would be too much, huh…"
"Come on, don't say that. You guys learned how to do a wedge turn, right?"
"That's right! Now the two of you don't have to feel embarrassed whenever you go out skiing anymore."
"I'm saying that you shouldn't have taken someone up to the summit on their first day. …Of all the decisions I could've imagined you to make, that was the worst."
"Seriously, I can't even count how many times I fell over."
"And I imagine you couldn't count how many guys offered to pick you up, too. …You couldn't catch up with her the whole time, you know, Haruki?"
"Setsuna goes too fast. Haruki stops too often."
"I'm glad I didn't ask you to drive. I'm sure we wouldn't even be here by now if I had."
We've arrived at a small boarding house near the ski slope of a ski resort in Shinshuu.
Takeya illustrated just how much of an amateur he was at driving with the way he kept skidding on the pavement, which had become stark white as we were nearing our venue.
With the way we ended up reaching our venue without accident, the memory of a certain someone inevitably popped into my mind.
…Though I wonder why I'm remembering something like that right now.
"Ah, but still, the hot springs felt so good! They weren't quite like the open air ones, but they had a nice atmosphere to them, like those natural ones surrounded by rocks!"
"…Are you fine with anything as long as there are hot springs?"
And so, after we arrived at our destination, we had to put on equipment that we were not familiar with whatsoever before exposing ourselves to the freezing, bitter cold of the snowy mountains.
"Didn't you enjoy the bath, Haruki-kun? You spent a lot of time in there too, didn't you?"
"It was that beer Takeya brought… It tasted great at first, but I think I had too much to drink, so I'm kind of exhausted…"
And the rest of the day went by at a dizzyingly fast pace.
"Man, that sure was something, huh? I was wondering just how blissful it'd be to pass out in there…"
"Me too, me too! I was feeling so warm from within, and the fact that I didn't get enough sleep actually made me doze off in the bathtub…"
Having tumbled down the snowscape, we dragged our roughed-up bodies back to our lodging.
"I'm not sure how long her face was underwater, but even after I slowly counted to 100, she still wasn't coming back up."
"That was terrible, Io! How could you just leave me be like that? I nearly drowned back there!"
We entered the hot springs, shared a meal, picked out some souvenirs, and ended up buying a lot of booze and bringing it back to our rooms while we were at it…
"Wait, wouldn't you be able to realize that you're drowning before she could even count to 100? How did you even manage to breathe, Setsuna?"
…I can't say this wasn't quite enjoyable.
I laugh, and Setsuna sends a slight smile back at me.
We're no longer forcing ourselves when we're around each other, just like when we were at Setsuna's birthday party before this… No, I'd say it's even less forced for us to be together right now.
Setsuna's not acting more cheerful than she should be. But the way she's smiling and engaging in chatter with us now is just right.
And she's doing this among people where she needs no reservations, as if they were family. People who are closer to her in age than they are…
"What, seriously!? You want to go into teaching practice too?"
"Well, I'm already in the department where I can get a teacher's license. It's better to expand your range of options."
"I see you still have that rigid way of thinking, huh, Haruki?"
"…Sorry. I don't really like being addressed that way."
We had no sleep last night, but we're currently losing track of time as we engage in conversation.
"I attend seminars every now and then, but maybe I think it doesn't really help me or… I guess I just think I should still be working."
"You say that, but isn't attending lectures praiseworthy in itself? Like, I haven't even bought a suit for job interviews yet."
"Same here… I've gotta get one during spring break, or else…"
"By the way, didn't you want to make a career in mass media or something, Haruki? Have you already decided on it as your first choice?"
"…I've yet to make a decision. I've been thinking quite a lot about it, though…"

"Well, you're you, after all, so you'll just open yourself to a lot of options, think it through carefully multiple times and finally make your choice. One way or another, I imagine you'll be the first among us to get an offer."
"But you're probably better at interviews and such. You seem like you could do whatever you want as long as it's sales."
"Up until the point where he has to help a client, that is."
"…I'd appreciate it if you also realized how mean you're being by laughing so much at it, Setsuna-chan."
Our careers, our futures… we're dealing with the anticipation and unease of going out into society.
We're able to relate to the same feeling because we're all from the same generation.
"Ohhh, I see. Hayasaka-kun went to a university in Kyoto."
"Before this, when I called him, he started babbling on in Kansai dialect."
"Chikashi can speak in Kansai dialect!? Does he say things like 'howdy'? Wow, I'd ask him who he was if he ever said that to me."
"It's exactly as you said… To tell the truth, I didn't know who it was for a bit even after he told me his name."
"If I remember correctly… Hayasaka was dating Nagisa from our class, wasn't he?"
"Yup, that's right. They were in the same class in second year, after all."
"Ehh? By Nagisa… do you mean Katou-san? Jeez, I never noticed…"
"Katou-san and I weren't even in the same class. We were farthest apart on attendance numbers…"
"Well, Setsuna-chan, you've been ill informed on this stuff for a long time. So I guess you could say it's not your fault."
