"But Nagisa got into a vocational school here, right? I wonder if she broke up with Hayasaka… At that time, did he say anything?"
"Do you think I'd ask such audacious questions?"
"Well, I guess not. Expecting Haruki to ask questions about that is pointless, huh…"
"So why don't we check on him right now ourselves then?"
"H-Hey… It's late at night already, wouldn't we be disturbing him?"
"Ah, Nagisa-chan? Long time no see! How've you been? …Now then, a question. Who on Earth could I be～?"
"Why do you know her number…? She's a girl from way back then and from a different class, you know?"
And we're not just from the same grade…
We talk excitedly about our relatives in a way no other group can imitate, for the four of us have spent the past six years living in the same place.
We're immersing ourselves in a profound world that's exclusive in a way, free from intrusion as we talk about things that only we understand or have promised.
We help ourselves to drinks and grow delirious…
It was as if we went back in time three years, to a time where it was nothing but fun. We spent the night exhausting all the words we had.
"Thank you very much for using our services. I'm Sahashi from Onjuku Transportation."
"Yes… to a hotel that's right next to it."
"Ah, so you plan to fly tomorrow?"
"Is that so… I do hope that your flight will be operational…"
"It seems there's going to be some heavy snowfall in the city center tonight."
"I've heard it's already falling in the west. Services may be suspended tomorrow."
"Though I do wish that I didn't have to deal with the snow. While there are more customers, driving's going to be tough… In any case, though, I'll still take you to Narita no matter what happens."
"So I might not be able to… fly tomorrow."
"I swear, how much shopping did they go out to do?"
"I wonder if there are any shops that are open at this hour?"
"Right…? It's not like there are any 24-hour convenience stores like the ones we have in Tokyo."
"And the stores below us have closed long ago…"
"Maybe they were so focused on looking for shops that they got lost?"
"Even so, don't you think they're old enough to at least contact us about that?"
While I understand that they're drunk, it's been over 30 minutes since they went out to do some shopping…
As we ended up face to face, we occasionally took sips from our glasses, reminisced about the past, and spent our time in an unusual silence that would have been impossible before.
"…You think you'll be able to reach them?"
Nevertheless… the fact that we're alone together is starting to feel quite difficult.
It's not difficult because we can't get into conversation. It's difficult exactly because we're capable of having one.
If the two of us continue off from when there were the four of us, enjoying ourselves and happily pass the time alone with one another…
If we take advantage of our ideal circumstances and forget about everything that happened up until now, enjoying ourselves until the next morning just like we used to…
My betrayal and my sincerity would both be left unresolved.
"Where are you right now? You're not going to tell me you got into an accident or something, are you?"
"A convenience store? Just how far did you…"
"…We went back to our room. It's room 202."
Room 202 is anything but far from hereーit's literally on the other side of the hallway.
"…Io's also here. Right now, next to me."
It's one of the two rooms that the four of us rented. It was supposed to be the room where the girls were going to stay the night…
"Well, um… I'm sorry, but could I ask you and Setsuna-chan to just use that room for the night?"
And now, according to Takeya's plans, that room would become his and Io's.
"What's going on? Are Takeya-kun and Io okay?"
"Do you even understand what you're saying right now?"
Setsuna's voice had completely fallen on deaf ears.
"I'm begging you, Haruki! Let me become a man!"
…After all, everything Takeya's telling me right now is utterly absurd, but also strangely vivid all the same.
"No, I've already become a man long ago… anyway, let me get what I've always wished for!"
"I told you to hang on. Just wait a minute, Takeya…"
"I'm going to hang up in a second… Also, I've locked our room, so please don't knock repeatedly or anything like that."
"Hey, what happened? Did something happen to the two of them?"
I'm not sure if we should be wondering what's happened to them or if something will be happening to them…
Or perhaps this is something they've set up…
Having learned of the conversation I just had with Takeya in full, she was naturally at a loss for words.
"Io and Takeya-kun… could it be… could it be that they…!"
However, when she asked "What should we do?"…
"You see, Io's noticed for quite some time now, actually. No, I suppose it'd be odd if she didn't notice something was up…"
…Her words were filled with an unbelievable kindness, one that's well-deserved for the two of them.
"But they've come this far as 'good friends,' so maybe they just couldn't keep it to themselves anymore."
I'm sure that Setsuna also believes that there's a 99% chance that this is a result of their scheming, much like I do.
Even so, unlike me, I imagine she's holding out hope for the remaining 1% possibility that it isn't.
"I hope things will go well between the two of them."
"Now then… what happens next is up to the two of them."
"Leaving that aside, would you care to explain why my hands and feet are tied? Are you into this sort of thing?"
"If you'd prefer some neglect play, perhaps we could try that instead?"
"I'd be very interested to hear exactly how your conduct up until now gives me any reason to describe you with the word 'trustworthy.'"
"…If you're not going to let me do anything, then I'm hitting the sack. And just so you know, I'm not going to do anything if you happen to change your mind and end up crawling into my bed later on."
"Hey, Takeya… do you really think what we did was a good idea?"
"…Beats me. So much has happened throughout their relationship that it's become so messed up, so I honestly can't even imagine what's going to happen."
"This whole plan was your idea, wasn't it? Don't say something so irresponsible…"
"Still, I know one thing, and it's that they can't stay the way they are right now."
"Sure, the reason why they're the way they are now is because of Haruki. He's half-heartedly distancing himself from Setsuna-chan while at the same time half-heartedly trying to reach out to her."
"And all the while he knows… how much pain he's causing Setsuna by doing that."
"But Setsuna-chan's not making things easy either… Even though she refused Haruki, she just won't accept Haruki distancing himself from her either."
"Well… if only Haruki could have stayed loyal to Setsuna three years ago, then…"
"No one made Setsuna-chan leave Haruki back thenーshe did it of her own volition."
"The thing is, she was supposed to have already forgiven Haruki back then."
"It's not that easy of a thing to get over though… No matter what she does, she'll always remember."
"But that's just the way Setsuna-chan is, which is why she's been putting Haruki in such a bind. And now they've gotten someone apart from us involved in this as well…"
"What do you mean when you say someone apart from us?"
"It's like there's an unsynchronized tug-of-war going on between them… One end gets no reaction when tugging on their side, but the moment they ease up, they get dragged along."
"All that's left is to wait for tomorrow. That's when they'll decide if they want to move forward or put an end to it…"
"That in itself can be considered a step forward. If only because it means that they can stay beside one another without feeling hurt…"
"For me… I just want to see them go back to how they used to be. I want to see Setsuna laugh once more from the bottom of her heart."
"I want that too… Come on, let's go to sleep. I hope that the four of us can spend some time having fun tomorrow."
"By the way… what did you mean by what you've always wished for?"
"…Go look it up in a dictionary."
"You've been looking at me… for quite some time now."
"Eh…? Ah, w-well… you're the only one here, Setsuna, so…"
"Ah… S-Sorry… Now that I think of it, it's only natural, huh…"
"N-No… I wouldn't say it's something natural…"
"I'm being overly self-conscious, huh… How embarrassing…"
"No, don't worry about it… It was my bad for staring at you for so long."
"I never said it was bad, you know!"
"Ahahahaha…! Aah, what's going on? We're so weird, aren't we?"
We really are acting like idiots.
The two of us are being ridiculously conscious about one another, paying incredible attention to each other's gazes, mannerisms, and breathing.
We're all alone in a place meant just for us where no one should be able to interrupt in any way because a certain duo just happened to be far too considerate of us.
After all, it's not like we have a choice… We both end up staring at each other for some reason.
"It seems things have turned out in quite an unexpected way."
"Someone barged into my house uninvited all of a sudden…"
"And I got put into a car and was forced along for the ride."
"And before we knew it, we were thrown out into the snowy mountains…"
"Tumbling and falling over from the summit…"
"And before we knew it, we became a third wheel."
And before we knew it… we were able to consciously and properly look at one another without it simply being a coincidence.
"Lately… so many fun things have been happening it's actually concerning. Like the birthday party, and now today…"
"That's nothing to… be concerned about, right? It's never bad to have fun."
"I'd be glad if that were the case. It'd be fine even without a rebound."
At that moment… Sure, I was at a loss for words, but I did not avert my eyes from her.
And at that moment… a deep sigh escaped Setsuna's lips as she peered into my eyes with her upturned gaze.
"Hey, given the circumstances, what do you say to the two of us keep talking the whole night? …It seems like I can't go back to my room after all."
"By 'keep talking'… do you mean until the morning?"
The real meaning behind her behavior and the depth of it… For me, it's probably something that can't be fully understood.
"That was the general intention, yes… though I suppose we could talk until one of us gets tired and falls asleep?"
"…If you say that, it's obvious that you're going to be the one who falls asleep first, right, Setsuna?"
"…I'll try my best, I can stay awake until 4, no, at least until 3 AM, so…"
Even so, at that moment, the only thing that I think I clearly understood was that I was relieved by something.
"I don't really mind. No matter what time we fall asleep, I'll wake up at 6 o'clock anyway."
"Using an alarm clock as usual huh, Haruki-kun? I guess I've always been the one who woke up tired after our usual late-night calls…"
Setsuna's probably… thinking that she can get away with it today too.
"So then, what will we be talking about?"
"Right… So, Haruki-kun, how's your job hunt going?"
"Didn't we talk all about that earlier…?"
I'm making sure that I'm currently the same person who attended Setsuna's birthday party just a few days ago.

I'm making sure that I'm the same person I was back thenーthe person who didn't hurt Setsuna when she was happy, who didn't neglect Setsuna when she was suffering, and who could only hold her hand without saying anything…
"Then… let me listen to what you have to say this time, Setsuna."
But what exactly is wrong with me saying that?
"No, rather than that… About last year, or anything."
Am I aware that I'm currently in the middle of a trip?
How long has it been since I last went out and had fun with Setsuna like this?
"We haven't been in the same department since April, after all…"
Both Takeya and Io were driven to desperation and went out of their way to do something for us.
"Well, the number of courses we're taking haven't gone down at all, so the amount of time we've had to see each other has also lessened quite a lot, huh?"
It's been really fun. I'm sure tomorrow will be fun as well.
"Yeah… that's right. I… wasn't able to see you."
That's why… it's alright for us to do this today, right?
"I don't actually know a whole lot about "Setsuna, the third year university student". Could you tell me what kind of person she is? Anything is fine."
After all, Setsuna is, without a doubt, a very important girl to me.
"…Well, I was the one who put that distance between us in the first place, so this might sound convenient coming from me."
"No, that's not it. It's really not…"
…Just not a guy who can keep on longing and waiting for the return of a girl who's already left me and went to some faraway place.
"Right… For starters, then, let's talk about the mixer that was organized by one of the guys from the Medical Department…"
"At least spare me that… Now that I think of it, I already know all about that!"
To attempt a long-distance relationship… would be impossible. I know this from experience.
The love I had with her was one that was destined to end from the very beginning.
That's why the decision I should be making…
"Only for today, the preparations for my move are all done. All that's left is to get on my flight at 1 PM."
"Truth is, I got back the day before yesterday. And to be honest, I didn't plan on contacting you again."
"I'm going. No matter what anyone says now, it's already been decided. I'm not a woman who can sacrifice her job for a man."
"If somehow you appear in front of me at the airport before my departure…"
"And throw a tantrum because you hate the thought of being separated from me…"
"If you go that far, I guess I just won't have a choice. It's not like I haven't thought about what would happen after this."
"Yes, Tokyo and New York are far apart, but I still think I can come back for a day or so every month."
"West Virginia Airlines Flight 302 is scheduled to depart Narita at 1 PM."
"You're not… the kind of person to not follow each and every one of my instructions, right? …At least, I don't remember training you that way."
"The deadline is in… half a day."
"West Virginia Airlines Flight 302 is scheduled to depart Narita at 1 PM."
The contents of Mari-san's text were blunt, as usual.
And yet, I felt like I understood exactly what she was thinking, and what she's currently looking for.
Looking at my watch, I see that midnight is long past. Today is already March.

"She'll be coming back to the country temporarily. …She'll be making her final preparations for her transfer with her return, and I think we won't be able to see her for quite a while the next time she heads back to the United States."
It's true that she said sometime in March, but who would've known it would be scheduled in such a way…?
She's only giving me half a day.
And to make matters worse, I'm currently in the mountains in Shinshuu, which is almost half a day's drive from Tokyo.
My surroundings are covered in fresh white snow, but it's so dark right now that you can't even notice how white it is, and the last train of the local line left a long time ago.
Success hinges upon being able to get on the first train tomorrow, and even then, my prospects of making it in time are looking slim.
But Mari-san… it's already too late.
It's too late to be giving me a push on the back at this point. It's too late for you to be giving me a chance now.
"We were still in the middle of a conversation, right…? Let's continue, then."
"She's… five years older than me. She's my superior at my part-time job…"
"I said that's enough! You don't have to tell me!"
I've already told Setsuna all about you.
Because I've decided to move forward. I've cut off my own escape route.
After Setsuna finished talking about how she'd spent the past year, it was my turn to talk about how I'd spent it.
It all began in spring. At the time, I was gradually fitting in with my new colleagues as a new member of the Literature Department.
A certain woman suddenly walked up to me and addressed me in an overly familiar manner, and I ended up spending an excessive amount of money under the pretext of a welcoming party.

She ended up asking me for a lot more favors following that incident, and that may have been why I was eventually seen as someone reliable. This unexpectedly closed the distance between me and my peers.
Next was summer. With my sights set on my future, I spent my summer break considering my prospects for employment.

I took the plunge and applied for a position at Kaiousha, where I ended up being so busy with work that it was dizzying. It felt like I'd spent 24 hours a day working without thinking about anything else on a regular basis.
It was there that I cultivated a connection with someoneーmy talented superior, who, despite being ridiculously harsh, was capable of bouts of kindness.
Autumn followed. It was during this season when all things wither away and when my lab seminars officially started that I was finally able to give everything some proper thought.

Following the end of the school festival, that song of ours started going on air on the university's own FM broadcast. It was then that I crossed paths with Setsuna once more, but we missed the mark yet again.
And it was then that I'd met a certain young girl who happened to be my junior both at school and at work, who simply couldn't tolerate how indecisive I'd been and all the mistakes I'd made.
The season of reminiscence, during which memories of a certain someone inevitably surface in my mind no matter how many years pass.
I'd been unable to reconnect with her, but I got back on my feet, and did my best to get close to her…
And it led to that Christmas eveningーour final, most destructive breakup yet.
However… while that may have been the end of that day for Setsuna, the truth was that it still hadn't reached its end for me.
And the very moment I told her about what followed, Setsuna finally lowered her gaze after looking at me this entire time, refusing to face the confession of my sin.
"The way she was strict, uncompromising and full of confidence reminded me of Touma."
Even though I can no longer see Setsuna's expression, she's gasping in pain, and I know exactly what sort of emotions are behind those gasps…
"But… memories alone aren't enough to fall in love with someone. It's not as if I could bring myself to have feelings for someone if they were just an escape for me."
"I… was genuinely in love with her."
I can't count the amount of deplorable things I've done to her…
"Even though I've betrayed her. Even though I've deeply wounded her. …Even though she's about to head overseas now."
She scolded me, encouraged me, pouted in front of me, acted spoiled around me, teased me, and embraced me despite everything…
"But I loved her. …I truly believe I did."
I love that adorable older woman who's ridiculously kind, yet also capable of bouts of harshness.
"In the end, I decided to be together with her, and betrayed you once again, Setsuna. I can't count how many times I've managed to hurt you…"
Before I realized it, her breaths had turned into sobs, shaking the silent space meant for only the two of us.
"And I know you won't be able to forgive me… I'm sorry."
Even if I apologize… no, to apologize to her in itself is unforgivable.
It was supposed to be a clear-cut conclusion done three years ago…
And yet, I've only continued to hurt Setsuna throughout these three years. And to make things worse, I'm trying to end things in the worst way possible right now.
"W-Why are you telling me all this right now…?"
Setsuna's sobs are tinged with a resentful tone.
"Didn't you say you were having fun, Haruki-kun? Weren't you laughing the whole time with all of us…? Weren't you laughing with me…?"
"I did have fun. I was happy, truly."
"But I've always been waiting for this opportunity. I just had to tell you about this very important subject."
It's precisely because we're having fun right now. It's exactly because we're sharing a nice atmosphere between us. And it's because telling her this right now would hurt Setsuna all the more.
After all, haven't I been simply using excuses that are convenient for me, such that I'd only been delaying the conclusion at every turn?
That is what resulted in our half-baked situation right now, where neither of us know where or how to advance.
"I know I've betrayed you with what I've done, but I'd be betraying you even more harshly if I were to hide the truth."
Regardless of whether we'd be happy or hurt… what I really need right now is time meant for the two of us to talk things through like this, is it not?
"That's why I'm coming clean with you now. I'm sorry, Setsuna."
"L-Like I said… why are you apologizing?"

"I thought that we could just drop the subject if you said it had nothing to do with you. I thought we could laugh it off if it was just a terrible misunderstanding on my part. However… I just had to tell you all this."
"I didn't say that it had nothing to do with me! I just said that you didn't have to apologize for it!"
"Because all of this is my fault…"
She adamantly refuses to admit it's my fault.
"I distanced myself away from you, while not wanting our relationship to be destroyed… Part of this is my fault, isn't it…?"
Setsuna, who broke down that Christmas evening…
"Because I unusually delayed things, I ended up hurting you, Haruki-kun, and that's why you were separated from her as well, isn't it?"
…Is now relapsing to that state, where she endured with all her might, hurting herself to forgive me, before consequently breaking down.
"It's not like that. It's not your fault, Setsuna…"
"Then there's only one thing I can think of right now… the fact that I should console you…"
No matter how many mistakes I've made, she's forgiven me at every turn; and even though it must be unbearable to her, I keep on repeating the same mistakes.
"Back then, I was crying so much that you didn't even get the chance to cry yourself, did you, Haruki-kun?"
It's like a microcosm of the vicious cycle we've been repeating for three years now…
"So right here, and right now… You can cry your heart out. You can embrace me. You can… use me as a substitute for her."
"I was only a replacement to you, wasn't I!?"
…Culminating in the worst and most despicable decision Setsuna's ever made.
The snowfall outside the window is getting heavier.
The snow and the wind blow against the building unrelentingly, bringing the slightest noise to the otherwise quiet room.
Though our hearts are likely shaking more wildly and fiercely than the blizzard that's blowing outside.
"I… I… don't have the courage to connect my heart with yours right away with the way you are now, Haruki-kun…"
Setsuna places her hands on mine on the table.
"But even so… if I could be a refuge for you, Haruki-kun… if we could first become one in body, then…"
I manage to reject her with words, but I fail to shake her hands off of mine.
"If it's impossible for the both of us to face each other directly… rather than mutually hurt each other, why don't we just not care about it and just accept…"
That's why Setsuna only puts more force into her hands, unconcerned by the fact that I'm raising my voice.
"Why? Aren't you in agony, Haruki-kun? Aren't you sad?"
This is the very definition of a compromise that's placing the cart before the horse.
Having been unable to connect my heart with Setsuna's or be physically intimate with her, I made the mistake of seeking out a substitute for her.
…And even though that was exactly what brought about such a sorrowful development, at least in her eyes…
Right here and right now, Setsuna herself is offering to become a replacement for her…
"Don't do this, Setsuna… please, just stop this…"
"After separating with her… you want to feel warmth, don't you?"
"Please stop… if you say any more…"
"If only with my body, I can warm you up, you know? That's why, Haruki-kun…"
"I haven't given up on her yet!"
I never wanted to hurt Setsuna. But it seems that it's inevitable that I'll hurt her now.
That's why I had only hoped to cause as little damage as possible. But Setsuna is violently resisting my attempt to do that.
Setsuna's wounds only continue to rapidly fester before my very eyes, beyond my control…
She buries her face into my chest, hugging me with every ounce of strength she can muster.
Setsuna desperately tries to hold in her voice, crying instead through her entire body.
"Even after we've broken up… even after we've severed our ties… I'm still hugging you so closely like this…"
"For you to have wronged the one you love now… for you to comfort me like this…"
"That's because you're important. You'll always be important to me, Setsuna."
"Even though I'm important to you, you don't love me anymore, do you…?"
"I do love you. That's a given, you know."
"But you don't love me the most right now, do you…?"
And so we maintained our embrace like this, not knowing if we had spent countless minutes or hours in this painful, bitter, yet precious situation…
"Heh… I'm sorry. However, I have to refuse this no matter what."
"To refuse the fact that we have to inevitably part despite knowing that we mutually love and value each other…"
I'm sure that the next time I hear Setsuna's voice, it will mark the nearing end of our calm, yet sorrowful time together…
"Hey, Haruki-kun… please let us stay like this until I fall asleep…"
I'm going to let go of Setsuna soon. I'm going to tear away my arms that are embracing her right now.
"Everything will end after I fall asleep. The next time I wake up, I'll have forgotten about you. That's why, before I tire of crying, before I fall asleep…"
And I'm sure that doing so will feel utterly excruciating, like having my own skin ripped off.
"You loved me, right? You did love me, right…?"
"Of course I loved you… I've always loved you all this time…"
"Thank you for… your cruel words. That alone is enough for me…"
Once more, Setsuna saves me from my fears at the very last moment.
We willingly shift our tightly intertwined hands away from each other.
Even at the very end, Setsuna's still so strong.
And while her strength is undeniable, no doubt…
It's nothing more than a fragile strength that's only enough to remind herself that she's merely putting up a front.
"You were smiling… Haruki-kun. When you were talking about her."
"You were always happy, even when I couldn't muster up the strength to smile with you…"
"And yet, you weren't smiling because of me, were you? Instead, you were talking to her, even when she wasn't there, right?"
"That's why I understand now… She is the one who should be staying by your side now, Haruki-kun."
"I can tell just from how you've described her, Haruki-kun; she's cheerful, just, reliable… and an adorable person, isn't she?"
"You would only smile for such a wonderful person, right, Haruki-kun? I understand that she's the one that will make you happy…"
"She brought you back to your old self. The cheerful, just, reliable Haruki-kun from three years ago. …She managed to do what I absolutely could not."
"That's why I, I… know I have no choice but to move on now, Haruki-kun."
"Do you know how envious I was seeing your dreamy gaze the moment you spoke of that person earlier?"
"After all, you never show that face when you think about me."
"That's the face you show when you talk about Kazusa. The face you show when you speak of the girl you truly love."
"You've fallen in love again, huh? Rather, you've managed to fall in love again, right? …And all because you met her."
"I guess I wasn't meant to be the light shining on you after all. I've been nothing more than an existence that's been blocking it."
"That's why… I'll be leaving you now."
"Goodbye, Haruki-kun. I know it's already far too late for this, but… I'm going to break up with you now."
"That's why I wish you luck in getting back up on your feet. And I hope you'll experience a wonderful love…"
"I just got a text from Haruki, but…"
"He's walking toward the station… then he'll take the first train headed for Tokyo."
"W-Why? But that's… what in the world is he thinking?"
"I told him I didn't want to see him anymore. I told him I never wanted to see him again."
"That's why Haruki-kun has gone back. He's gone back to Tokyo, where someone he cares about is waiting for him."
"I'm sorry, I'm really sorry… It's all my fault that the vacation's ruined. I've ended up giving the two of you a painful memory, haven't I?"
"Come on… I'm alright. You don't have to go that far."
"It's going to be a while until morning, so rest up, Setsuna-chan."
"Come, Setsuna… and you too… you really should get some rest."
"I'll contact you when I wake up tomorrow. Until then… just leave us alone."
"…What did you just say? Where in the world are you right now?"
"You heard me. I'm heading to the station. …On the local line of Nagano prefecture, I mean."
I can clearly hear the flabbergasted voice coming from the other side of the line.
It's almost 6 o'clock in the morning… there wasn't any sign of dawn replacing the night in these snowy mountains, and the powdery snow around me was far from gentle as it danced about.
My footsteps make crunching sounds as I walk across the snow in the deep darkness…
"…Didn't she say she would come back in March!? Why is she leaving her apartment open like that!?"
I can hear a loud noise through the receiver of my phone, unbefitting of where I am at the moment.

"Ahh, no, there was nothing you could've done, Haruki-kun. It was that idiot who didn't even say anything about the day of her departure who's at fault here. …She didn't even go out of her way to contact me of all people!"
Instead of being tense due to it being early in the morning, Sawako-san was in a state of irritation in which all she could do was rattle on with her quick talking.
But it's not like I don't understand her feelings. …In fact, I can feel them through the core of my very being.
"Have you managed to get in touch with Mari-san?"
"She's turned off her phone. Chances are high that she's just going to fly off like this."
"As I thought, that's how it's going to be, huh…"
I hurried out of my lodging and headed for the station. I tried many times to find places with cell coverage, but I could only find the sounds of announcements coming from machines.
So in other words… I have reason to believe that that text was Mari-san's last notice.
"Hey, Haruki-kun… Let me confirm this just one more time."
"You do intend… to meet with Mari again, right? You do want to talk to her one more time, right?"
Everything I've done up until today would be meaningless otherwise.
I've cut off my own escape route. I've acted upon various assumptions. And right now, I'm at the mercy of the cold as I'm walking through the snow.
I've cut her off. And with her, I've cut off a part of myself.
Even if I don't know what part it is I've cut off, the exposed nerves of the wound are still throbbing in pain.
Setsuna's tear-stained face from that moment surfaces in my mind every time I close my eyes.
Even though it's only been an hour since I parted with her… I can no longer remember the way her face looked when she smiled.
"That's why I'm heading to Tokyo right now. …I'm going to meet Mari-san."
But the only thing I can do right now is move forward.
I have to act as a professional and fully functioning member of society and produce results regardless of what stands in my way, no matter how sly, tactless or despicable I have to be to do so.
She's the textbook definition of a professional, and she's taught me by example.
"…I understand. If that's the case, I'll be sure to do what I can on my end. I'll do my best to keep her here!"
"Thank you very much. But I'm sure it'll be alright."
"Why do you believe that? You're in Nagano prefecture right now, aren't you?"
"…I've arrived at the station. Somehow, I think I can make the first train."
After walking down the twists and turns of the mountain road and eventually reaching roads that definitely feel paved, I finally lay eyes on the station.
"…So from there you plan to travel by train?"
"If I transfer two times, I can get onto the Chuo line. I can reach Narita Airport in twelve hours, though that's only what I deduced from looking it up on the internet earlier."
Fitting of the remote location, the roundabout in front of the station didn't have a single taxi, and the shutters of a small souvenir store were, of course, closed.
"So I think I can make it just in time. Even if it's just a few minutes before Mari-san passes through the boarding gate…"
"…If the trains will operate on schedule, that is."
"I'll think of something. The trains here happen to be resistant to the snow, after all."
The shutters to the station have finally opened, and I can see the figure of an attendant at the ticket gate.
However, Sawako-san is responding to my optimistic tone in the exact opposite manner.
"I see… I should've known. You are in Nagano, after all."
"I can't say it's unusual that you're not aware of the situation in Tokyo right now…"
"For the first time in the year, at that. Almost all of the first trains in the capital have been delayed other than the subway."
As I look at the sky above me, I can see that the clouds seem to extend toward Tokyo as well.
"Even if you assume you reach Tokyo via express train or something, you can't tell if you can make it in time to Narita."
However, the fact that it's snowing at a ski resort and the fact that it's snowing at the capital mean completely different things.
Basically, the transportation network of Tokyo, which does not expect snow apart from once or twice a year, can be paralyzed due to unexpected events like this.
Particularly, the stations usually have an overcrowded schedule to begin with, so a single delay would lead to a second or a third…
I just can't imagine how much delay I'd be looking at before I could finally arrive at Narita.
I didn't even have an hour's worth of leeway for this task from the very beginning. But even though I could say my situation is critical…

"S-Still! This might be a blessing in disguise! If it's snowing right now, the flights may become inoperational. And even if the flights are permitted, the chances that their schedules will be delayed for quite some time are…"
Should this unexpected situation give me fear, or should it give me hope…?
Whichever of those is the case, am I doomed without a means to catch up to Mari-san at the moment…?
"D-Do your best! Keep chasing after Mari with all you've got! Please… go catch up to her!"
"This is an announcement for all customers of Narita International Airport. As of now, due to the snowfall, all scheduled flights will be postponed."
"We apologize for the inconvenience and humbly ask that you wait until operations are restored."
"So that's how it's going to be…"
"I wonder… whose side is the sky on?"
Time continues to tick by with uncertainty as I anxiously race against it.
It's almost 9 o'clock… there's only four hours left before Mari-san departs. But the time I have left is even less than that.
For the time being, things have been proceeding on schedule.
As planned, I've made two transfers on the local line and hopped onto the express train on the Chuo line toward my destination.
But… it's from here on out that the battle truly begins.
I can feel my neck gradually stiffening over the steep hurdle Mari-san's set up for me, as well as the various unexpected circumstances.
She only contacted me with half a day to go. I'm dealing with a very long distance from my destination. And there's also the fact that it's snowing in Tokyo right now.
"If you want to be with me, then show me you can get over these hurdles."
…Is that what you're trying to tell me, Mari-san?
Why are you saying such selfish things now, of all times?
Even though you were so happy to have my homemade cooking? Even though you were so happy about celebrating my first assignment?
And even though you were letting out moans of pleasure when we were in each other's arms…?
…How am I supposed to accept that selfishness of yours?
Given that I've been one-sidedly manipulating you all this time up until now…
How exactly should I respond to you, given that for the first time, you're now the one manipulating me?
What am I saying? There's only one answer. I already promised this to Sawako-san earlier, after all.
"Haruki-kun? Are you listening? Answer me, Haruki-kun!"
"…Thank you very much. I'll… do my best."
Even if you're being stubborn, I'll catch up to you.
I'll show you that I can definitely make this absurd deadline that you've set for me…
"The train schedules are all a mess, and the taxis weren't moving at all. It took me three and a half hours to get here, you know."
"Still, what gives? Has no one from the editing department arrived yet? Did you manage to contact anyone so far?"
"But why? What happened to giving you three cheers and tossing you into the air and whatnot?"
"I asked the chief editor to keep it a secret. Both the fact that I'd even come back here and that I'd be leaving today."
"Having to deal with send-offs is kind of hard… and I don't want everyone to get all gloomy."
"You're right, Suzuki-chan does seem like someone who would cry."
"Of course, I really don't want to be tossed into the air or have them shouting three cheers in my name, either."
"What a lonely way to set off on a trip… sent off by only one friend."
"As long as you're here, Sawako, that's good enough for me… I don't need anyone else…"
"I see… I see how it is…"
"I just had a call with Haruki-kun earlier. You only told him about today, didn't you?"
"I see… So he went skiing. Hehe, it must be nice being a university student."
"He did see your text, Mari, and he's rushing your way right now. But… he might not be able to make it in time because of the snow."
"Why didn't you contact him immediately when you arrived in Japan…? This wouldn't have happened if you just did that…"
"…My schedule's always been packed. Even if I did contact him immediately, I wouldn't have had the time to meet him. That's why I didn't do it, at least…"
"In any case, there's just been so many bad coincidences… Hey, Mari… how about not flying out today?"
"Think it over just one more time… Wasn't it your policy to get a hold of both your work and your love life?"
"Am I right? Mari… stop being so stubborn and just give Haruki-kun a call, okay?"
"…I really have to go. Well, if the planes can actually take off, that is."
"But why!? You know you might not be able to see him ever again, right? And all over the simple reason that the snow happened to fall today?"
"Even if that's the case… that's just how it's fated to be… for us…"
"We apologize for the wait. As the removal of snow on the runway has been completed, we will now begin boarding for each flight."
"It seems this is how it's going to be…"
Before I knew it, the sky that I saw from the station platform had cleared up.
Chances are, I can't hope for the flights to be suspended anymore. I have to put all of my strength into catching up.
I break out into a full sprint on the Chuo Line's platform, pass through the ticket gate, and head toward the final platform transfer, all while running with all the strength I have left.
The last train left headed to my destination… is the airport-bound express.
If this train leaves the station according to schedule and without delay…
"This is the last chance for boarding for passengers heading to West Virginia Airlines Flight 302, headed to New York. Please hurry to Gate 90 for boarding."
"The fact that Kitahara can't make it is fate as well."
"And the fact that my flight will be leaving on schedule is also meant to be."
"Even if he just happened to go skiing today, even if it happens to be snowing in Tokyo, and even if that's why the trains are late…"
"If that's how it's going to be, then… isn't my only choice to accept that fate?"
"Then… if Kitahara-kun happens to make it in time, you'll consider that fate, too, right? And you'll accept that fate when it happens, right?"
"…He won't make it, Sawako. It's just impossible that he would."
"He'll make it… he's almost here, he'll definitely make it!"
"Well, it's about time I should go…"
"Just wait a little longer! Just a little more!"
"In any case, the time's up. …It's game, set, and match."
"See you, Sawako… I won't be able to see you for a while, but I hope you'll be okay."
As soon as I get up this escalator, I'll arrive at the airport.
Please let me make it… please let me make it in time…
"Your call cannot be connected at the moment because the number you have dialed is outside the service area or the cell phone may be switched off."
"Didn't I tell you to make yourself always reachable! You're… you're… a disgrace of an editor!"
"Sawako, you liar… Like I said, it was pointless, wasn't it…!?"
"Uaaaah… Uuu… Why…? Why… didn't he come…?"
"…In that case, please head this way, as the flight is about to take off."
"What's wrong with me…? Has he affected me so much that even my ears are playing tricks on me now…?"
The moment Mari-san widens her eyes upon noticing me…
I brush my body against hers without the slightest hint of reservation, embracing her body with all the strength I can muster.
Mari-san's body… stiffens like a young girl's.
Furthermore, her voice rises, eliminating all traces of the composed, confident woman she is at work.
Leaving behind only someone who's deep in my embrace right now… quivering like a baby bird, my adorable and beloved girlfriend.
However, the moment our eyes lock onto each other's and our lips naturally inch closer together…
"What kind of foolish joke is this…?"
Mari-san changes her mind, stopping me before our lips could touch.
"What do you mean, joke…? I'm really serious about…"
"Well, this is… we're in New York right now, you know! We're in America right now, aren't we!?"
"What are you doing here? How did you even fly over here!?"
"Just like you said, Mari-san, I flew over here…"
"Don't toy with me! Don't mess around! Is it really fun for you to play around with an older woman like this!? I… I… I…!"
I put my strength into my hands in an attempt to convey my intention to atone to her, though Mari-san struggles a little within my grasp, as if she feels reluctant.
However, the strength she's putting into her struggle doesn't suggest that she has any intention of wrenching my arms off of her.
"I don't get you at all… why did you chase after me to a place like this…? T-This… this isn't supposed to be the place you should've come for me!"
The moment Mari-san's hands escaped my grasp, I understood her true intention.
…Her hands are now tightly wrapped around my back.
I had my passport right from the start. Reluctantly, I had acquired it last year under Mari-san's threat of "you might have to go on overseas trips even if you're a part-timer."
As for the visa and the rest of the necessary procedures, I had them sorted out on the day I fell out with Mari-san…
At that time, I couldn't see it being the end of our relationship. But I had yet to convey to her that we had to see each other.
Everything I've done is linked together now. What I'd done back then did not end up being futile after all.
"I went on the 11 o'clock Detroit flight, then took the domestic airline heading for New York…"
I left Japan earlier than Mari-san did.
Attempting to escape Tokyo's snow would have been hopeless. That's why I'd rushed toward Nagoya right from the start.
It would've taken approximately twelve and a half hours to reach New York from Narita Airport. Taking the Detroit flight from Chubu would've taken an hour less.
Adding together the commute and embarkation times of that domestic airline, I determined that it would take roughly the same amount of time to get here.
…This was the plan I had devised with Sawako-san.
Actually, I unquestionably owe all of this to her because she's a travel agent; it was why she managed to arrange the proper route and prepare the tickets for me.
"S-S…Sawako! S-She… she knew about this the whole time!?"
I indiscreetly brush my cheeks against Mari-san's yet again, finding her begrudging tone rather endearing.
"I managed to make it time, huh…"
Going from Narita to New York takes about twelve and a half hours. Tokyo is fourteen hours ahead of New York.
"Didn't you do the same thing as well, Mari-san…? With the 'real deadline' you set, that is."
…Like negotiating with the president of the printing company, buying the manuscript herself, and extending the deadline for several more hours.
In addition to all the other things there, just how many days in succession did we stay up all night, laughing and talking afterward…?
"I learned just by watching you, you know? This much is easy."
"But, but that's… I've only done this two or three times myself…"
"Anyway, I've caught up to you. I came to give you my answer, Mari-san."
As I let those words out of my mouth, Mari-san's body, which I held so firmly in my arms, began to twitch and shake at once.
It's all because of that, the reason I chased after Mari-san in desperation, the thing that caused us to be separated.
"W-Wait, hold on. I'm not ready for…!"
"I… I know for sure that I can't keep this long-distance. If I'm not next to you, if I can't see you all the time… I'd be hopeless."
Once again, Mari-san shook more than before, though her shivers remained light.
"That's why… I've come over to you."
The moment she heard my next words, the trembling went away, and she looked at my face, puzzled.
"I'm going down my own path. …My own path, in which I follow you, Mari-san."
"What exactly do I mean, I wonder…?"
The "What do you mean?" that Mari-san said had neither expectation nor anxiety within it.
She genuinely cannot understand my words, which makes me think that they came out with a strong and weird accent.
"…! W-Wait, are you saying… that you want to freeload off me!?"
"…I really don't know. I haven't really decided anything yet as of now."
I haven't decided on where to study, where I'm going to live, or even my life from here on out either.
Without settling on anything, I boarded a plane and flew all the way here, all so I could catch Mari-san.
There was only one thing I could do in Japan… and that was to break away from the past.
"The way I am now… I only have prospects for the future."
It's a classic, reckless act of a ruined young man with no plans or outlook for the future.
A textbook example of a loser who ended up straying from his intended path due to his obsession with a woman.
"T-This is… it's not like you at all, Kitahara…"
Despite saying that, I feel no wavering from the strength of her arms wrapped around my back.
On the contrary, her grip grew tighter as though she would never let go.
"…Do you hate the way I am now?"
"If I said I hated it right now, what would you do…?"
"Don't say it! …Did you even think that I would let that go by? That's cowardly… very cowardly, Kitahara!"
As if she had anticipated my answer, Mari-san stops me from answering.
In other words, by her hand, I'm now branded as a good-for-nothing, cowardly, and thoughtless freeloader.
"I miss the food back in Japan…"
We continued our embrace for several minutes in the airport lobby.
Even though we were fully aware that we were not in Japan right now, and with our luggage tucked between our legs.
"Just don't abandon your higher education, okay?"
"Of course. I'll consider taking a break or being a foreign student here."
"Also, you've got to pay for your daily needs, okay? You don't have to worry about the rent, though."
"I want to work part-time too. Though I'd prefer having a superior that can speak Japanese, ideally."
"…I do know someone, but you'll be worked to the bone, you know?"
"…I'll show you that I can be useful, alright?"
Another day begins with my habitual hot morning shower, which, as always, washes my sleepiness away and gives my body its sensation and warmth back.
It's very cold in my room, and it's still dark outside; even though I've been doing this every day, it's still pretty hard to get up during this season.
But today is Friday… After this one last day awaits the weekend that I've been looking forward to.
…Well, I still have work on Sunday though.
"Hey, Kitahara, about the poll statistics I asked you to do yesterday…"
"I've already uploaded the information to the server. I've also added a comment on the aggregate study for different age groups… I thought I already notified you through email last night."
"This is the original draft from another publisher. I'll leave the editing to you, it's due by 8 o'clock!"
"…Got it. I have a meeting at 4 o'clock, so I'll get right to it afterward."
"Hey～ hey～ Kitahara-kun. For the next issue of the Town Information Corner, don't you think it'd be a good idea to do one on Suetsugu-chou?"
"…I don't think there's anything special about my neighborhood aside from Houjou University, though? I'll still take that into consideration, of course."
"I'm sorry, but please condense it into one page! Just use your usual method.
…Whoa, this is bad, I've got less than two hours left until my appointment!"
"…I'm sure yellowtails taste delicious this season."
"Oh come on, that's not it at all. That guy won't write me anything unless I bug him incessantly… so I'm going to head over immediately today!"
"I'm supposed to condense this to one page…? Just how much do you want to cut out!?"
Kaiousha Building, third floor. Kaiou Graph editing department.
My daily life hasn't changed since my days here as a part-timer…
Kaiousha PLC, Kaiou Graph editing department, Kitahara Haruki.
It's my first year in the company. In the editing department, I'm the youngest, or lowest, so to speak.
"Also, Kitahara, can I take a bit of your time? About this proposal, can you give me some feedback on it later?"
"I can do it after I come back… But are you sure you're asking the right person, Matsuoka-san?"
"Please help me… You're the only one who would give me any constructive feedback. Hamada-san only points out the flaws, and Suzuki-san is vague about everything…"
"That's because the proposal Macchan wrote can't even be considered an actual proposal."
"You need to work on articulating your information into words. I can't even understand what you're trying to communicate with it."
"That's because no one taught me anything～ If only I got to work directly under Mari-san like Kitahara did…"
"Hospital admission fees nowadays are 100000 yen, keep that in mind."
"As if you'd last long under Kazaoka with your work ethic. You always leave as soon as you can even when you have work piling up…"
"See? Everyone's horrible to me! The only one I can count on is you, Kitahara. The legendary workaholic Kazaoka the Second."
"…No, I'm still quite far from that level."
"I wouldn't be able to stand it～ having a junior instruct me every step of the way."
"Don't say it like that. His lack of pride is actually one of Matsuoka's strong points. Besides…"
"You won't be able to slack off for too long either, you know? From what I'm seeing, Kitahara is already at your level, Suzuki."
Thanks to the ubiquitous reputation of my master when I was a part-timer… No one in the editing department actually sees me as a newcomer.
"Um… I'll head to my meeting now. I should be back by 6 o'clock."
"Uh… Is that the one where you're substituting for Ensemble's chief editor?"
"Yes, I think we're going to sign some magazine and commercial contracts there. So we need to have an official employee present…"
Since she's famous to the point where every single editing department knows about her, her influence has way too much power…
No matter which editing department I went to, my job was made much easier by simply bringing up the nickname Kazaoka the Second.
"Aside from the chief editor, everyone else there is a pro at editing. The chief grumbled earlier about wanting someone to work directly under him."
"…Don't get ahead of yourself, Kitahara. If you don't want to go, do you want me to go refuse it for you?"
"That's not a problem! I'd rather not transfer responsibility in my first year working here properly! I'll head out now."
"Make sure you come back! I'll be waiting for you all day here… until 8 o'clock, that is."
I graduated from university in March, and just as I planned, I managed to secure a job at Kaiousha.
As such, the atmosphere of my workplace is no different from my part-time days, so I'm getting my taste of life as a working adult without noticing much change.
Except for one single… not-very-small detail.
My mentor, who trained me when I was still a part-timer, was invited to work at the American branch, so all that's left here is her legend.
That's why, instead of being left with an "enormous mountain of organized work," I am left with an "enormous mountain of disorganized work."
And so, the first-year rookieーmeーis supposed to find work within that mountain that's suitable for me, set priorities and slowly work toward achieving them.
…I'm not trying to steal Matsuoka-san's line, but Hamada-san never makes these decisions for me.
As usual, today I picked what's highest on my priority list…
Actually, ever since my "first job," Ensemble's chief editorーwhom I owe a lot toーhas asked me to have a business discussion with the sales manager of a certain record company.
But sending a newcomer like me as the substitute for the chief editor… I just hope they won't be offended…
"I'm very sorry for being late. I'm Kitahara from Kaiousha's Ensemble's editing department…"
"Nice to meet you. I'm Ogiso from Knights Records' public relations department. It's a pleasure to meet you."
She handed me her business card with a smile on her face, but I ended up leaving her hanging for a whole three minutes.
I'm definitely not cut out for this…
"This is bad… only five minutes left!"
We graduated from university in March, and took our first steps into society down our own separate paths.
Takeya is working for a cosmetics company as a salesman and frequently visits many stores in the city.
Since he's just as skillful of a womanizer as he used to be, he's rather popular with the female sales staffーsetting aside their age. He's gotten good reception all around in his first year.
He still doesn't have an official girlfriend… but unlike before, now he doesn't have a mountain of unofficial girlfriends either.
He settled all loose ends with those girls once he graduated, and now he's trying to appeal to a certain someone with his newfound uprightness.
That certain someone… being Io, who successfully realized her ambition of getting a job at a sporting goods maker.
She wanted to work as a designer, but since it's too competitive, she's now busy working in the HR department.
Due to her already frank personality further accentuated by her looks, she is popular among both her male and female coworkers.
Her lack of interest in love hasn't changed though. She doesn't have an official boyfriend either.
So he should still have a chance, but who knows for how long things will continue like this.
Knights Records' public relations newcomer, Ogiso Setsuna.
After that Valentine's Concert, she started to look for work related to singing, and she finally picked a decent record company.

During her fourth year, she decided on her future career path. They hire very few people for this position, so I was a bit uneasy about her working in such a competitive field, but she succeeded magnificently in the end.
It goes without saying that her grades and interview scores were great, but I'm also sure that a certain, very visible strength of hers helped her along too.
The proof is that the moment she started working there, she was instantly assigned to the public relations department, and was put in charge of negotiating with other companies.
Of course, the company wasn't hoping to utilize only her ability to negotiate…
"A very cute girl just joined Knights' public relations department!"
"At first, I thought she was some sort of celebrity."
"We've invited her out many times, but to no avail…"
…And that's not coming from just one or two people in the industry.
It's not an environment that promotes becoming an artist, nor does it usually make distinctions between people…
But still, she's enjoying a lively day-to-day life, working at a place in constant contact with music.
And now, that rumored public relations beauty…
"Heey, you're late! You barely made it in time!"
…Is currently making dinner for me in my apartment.
Following Setsuna's finger, I can see that the clock's hands in my room are pointing directly at 12 o'clock.
Sometimes Setsuna has to head directly to work from my apartment. In order to overcome her habit of staying in bed too long, she bought an alarm clock with a snooze function.
"Last week you worked the weekend, Haruki-kun. You were this close to breaking our rule."
"You swear it? You promise that you'll meet me once per week?"
Last time we met was last Friday. I sent Setsuna home before the day was over, so if we hadn't met then, I would have broken our promise.
"D…Didn't we just meet each other earlier… in Kaiousha's meeting room…"
"That's Knights Records' Ogiso, she's not your Setsuna, Haruki-kun～"
I was going to let out a sigh, but the exhaustion from my sprint got in the way.
"Haruki-kun, you're starting to not take our one-week rule seriously anymore… You were close to breaking it twice last month."
Incidentally, Setsuna's indignation also got in the way.
But still, Setsuna knows full well that it wasn't my fault. After all, we're both now working members of society.
After I finished the proofreading Matsuoka-san asked me to, I checked the materials Suzuki-san asked me to look over. As for Kizaki-san's layout… I'll get back to him on Sunday.
And from 10 o'clock, I reviewed Matsuoka-san's proposal together with Hamada-san and Suzuki-san. For some reason, I was given the role of editor.
At 11 PM, I felt that Matsuoka-san was being slightly ridiculous when he casually thanked us for our hard work and promptly left.
…I couldn't do anything about that, right?
"Now that we've been dating for so long, maybe you really have gotten bored of me. If that's the case, I'll never be able to recover…"
"Can you truly say that with certainty? That you still love me…"
Even though many regrettable things have happened…
I will never waver in my answer if someone asks me whether I still love Setsuna or not.
"Mm, huu… haah, ah, ah… Setsuna… aah, nn…"
As the sound of the kitchen knife stops, I capitalize on the moment Setsuna "stops cooking" as she gives non-stop complaints, hugging her from behind.
"Nn, jeez… You always try to distract me… like this."
Because Setsuna is so charming when she's sulking…
There's just no way I could do something as wasteful as getting tired of her, slighting her, or getting too used to her.
…Actually, that last part might not be so bad.
"That's because I ran all the way from the station."
I decide not to ask which part of me she thinks is warm.
"That too… but I also wanted to do this with you, Setsuna, if even a moment earlier."
I tightly adhere my entire body to Setsuna's back.

I bury my face into her hair, and suck in her fragrance with each heavy breath. I push my abdomen against her soft back. My toes on her heels, my thighs on the back of her thighs, my knee on the back of her knee.
There is no way I could get bored of her. On the contrary, my feelings and my desires only deepen as time passes.
To the point where I can't calm myself down until I go all the way right now.
"Haah, haah, ah, aah… ah, nn, nn, kuu… hey, w-wait…"
"Haah, ah, aah…! Wait, stop it, Haruki-kun!"
Or at least, so I thought.
"…Dinner is ready. Let's hurry up and eat."
I'm already completely in the mood, while Setsuna, on the other hand, pushes me away with a composed demeanor.
"But… rather than food, right now, I…"
In the beginning, there was a purpose in trying to distract her.
But now, my feelings toward Setsuna are overflowing, and I've reached a point where I can't hold back anymore.
Setsuna knows full well that I am on the brink…
"But if we don't eat now, the food will get cold."
"But I'll always be steaming hot for you whenever you decide to eat me up, you know?"
My head was so filled with thoughts of disappointment…
…That I almost failed to hear that last line.
After we made love, we decided to bathe together to rid ourselves of the impurity we bestowed upon each other.
Only to… stain each other once more.
"This was originally planned by Kizaki-san, who's a senior of mine. Of course, he's the one who's supposed to be going, but he suddenly decided to get engaged that week."
"Oh… He's getting married. Good for him."
After we got out of the bath and dried ourselves… we both crawled into bed without putting on anything.
After all, there's no need for us to put anything on. Having our bodies touch one another is more than warm enough.
"Good for him, sure, but does that mean he can just push an overseas business trip on the newcomer?"
"They really have high expectations of you, don't they, Haruki-kun? They've never let me leave the Kanto region."
"That's because the scope of our jobs is different…"
"But the higher-ups are flying all across Japan. That means they just don't trust me that much yet."
Thinking it a waste to fall asleep on the night before our days off, it happens pretty often that we talk the night away in bed, and before we know it, the sun is already up.
And when we finally do fall asleep, Setsuna will usually remain in bed until evening, after which she will lament having wasted the weekend away.
It's just that Setsuna is having a harder time finding a proper topic of discussion than usual today.
"That's pretty far away, Europe… When we were still students, we couldn't go even if we wanted…"
"But now you can go. In terms of money and freedom, you're so much different from back then. So you can go wherever you want…"
"Hey… I'm not sure what you're so worried about, Setsuna."
"I'm not worried… There'd be no end to it if I worried about every little thing like the plane crashing down, or there being some terrorist attack."
"How many countries do you think there are in Europe? How vast do you think it actually is…?"
"…We're not talking about the same thing anymore, Haruki-kun."
Setsuna is probably thinking about one single country.
An EU member state, with German as the official language. Its capital city is also known as the "City of Music"…
"I'm only visiting Spain, Italy and France."
That's why I told her this trip doesn't include that certain country. It's like I'm giving her the itinerary of my graduation trip… honestly, and straightforwardly.
"I promise I won't set foot in a single country outside of those."
"I'm not worried about anything like that. You just have to come back in one piece, that's enough for me."
Even though she said "I'm not worried about anything," Setsuna contradicted herself by making a wish.
In order to put Setsuna's mind at ease, I let go of her shoulder and hold onto her hand.
When I find Setsuna's hand, she slowly intertwines her fingers with mine.
"I'll be looking forward to my souvenir, okay?"
"Of course. If you have anything specific in mind, just let me know."
"Hey, can you buy something for my family too? I think my mom wants a bag… and one for Takahiro too… I'll get you a farewell gift."
There's nothing to worry about. And there's nothing to lament.
Because it's already been five years.
In these five years, we've formed an unbreakable bond that no one can cut through.
In truth, what worries me the most this time isn't where I'm going, but the scheduling…
"…Is when I'll depart from there. By the time I land at Narita, it'll probably be the evening of the 25th…"
The nails of her hand that's entwined with mine suddenly dig into me, and her resentful scream reverberates painfully in my ear.
Well, it's only natural for her to be upset.
"What about Christmas Eve? What about our one-week rule?"
Even though I managed to keep it just earlier, she still got sulky. But now our one-week rule is truly put to the test.
On top of that, not being able to see each other on Christmas Eve, that's fatal for a couple.
"Sorry won't cut it! Didn't we already make a reservation at Arumi Integral Hotel!?"
"Well… if we cancel now, we won't have to pay the cancelation fee."
In order to make up for what happened there two years ago, since last year, we planned on going to that hotel every year.
In other words, this year, we can't even celebrate the overcoming of our trauma there.
"Is there no other way? Can you make it home somehow on the 24th?"
"Well… I'll still be working in Paris till noon on the 24th…"
In order to make the trip more efficient, I received work from other editing departments as well. And before I knew it, my schedule had gotten longer and longer, but that's a secret…
Given that I've been dubbed Kazaoka's successor or Kazaoka the Second, I would never allow myself to tarnish the name of my esteemed superior.
…Because if it was her, she could handle going to two or three additional countries with ease.
Setsuna slowly releases her grip from my hand.
As well as the head that was on my chest, and the legs that were wrapped around mine…
I thought she would move herself away from me, but all she did was turn around.
…Along with the blanket that was wrapped around us.
When I try to talk to her, or shake her shoulder through the blanket, she just shows me her back and pretends to be asleep.
When I found out about my trip's schedule, I already knew this ordeal was coming…
But now that it's actually happening, it really does feel draining…
"I'll buy whatever you want. Even if it's from Louis Vuitton or Gucci or Prada or Hermes…"
So please, at least share the blanket with me…
"Haruki-kun, you don't understand me at all! I'm not so cheap that I'd forgive you just because you bought me an expensive gift!"
From under the blanket, I can hear that Setsuna's voice is tearful in earnest.
So I try to put her heart at ease, by putting my hand under the blanket and gently patting her shoulder…
"Don't touch me with that obscene hand of yours! …I'll start to feel happy, and you'll have me completely distracted before I can even realize it."
What she said made me happy, but at the same time, I pulled my hand back.
If just the slightest touch can quell her… doesn't that make her even cheaper…?
Well, I know for a fact that someone like me just isn't a match for someone like Setsuna at all.
If I'm the customer, she's the woman putting discount after discount on herself, selling herself at a loss.
But as for me, I betrayed the love and trust she placed in me…
If I don't get it back somehow…
"When I come back, I'll come to you right away… We can take time off from work and spend the week together."
"How about this? Let's go on a vacation when I'm back. I'll follow you no matter where you want to go, Setsuna."
She took the bait! Now's my chance!
"We can ski, we can have as much fun as we want at a theme park… Ah, spending New Year's in a hot spring sounds nice too. Setsuna, you prefer more relaxing places, don't you?"
"Want to start planning tomorrow? For New Year's, that is."
Well, it seems like that's it. Setsuna is definitely interested.
"Should we go to a travel agency? I know someone who can get us a good price. She's friends with my previous superior, she helped me out on this business trip too…"
I already got my winter bonus money, and I don't plan on putting a price limit on Setsuna's smile.
"…So we can go wherever I want?"
"Of course! Not only Hokkaido or Kyuushuu! If you want to travel farther away, we can even go to Hong Kong or Guam…"
Because, just like how Setsuna always devalues herself for me, I always see her as the most valuable thing in my life.
"December 24th… I want to attend the Christmas Mass. …At Strasbourg Cathedral."
The wish Setsuna mentioned is beyond the issue of just the price…
Just as she said, she's definitely not a cheap girl.
"…Y-Yes. Um, I would love to go on this trip with Setsuna-san. That is, if you're okay with it, Father…"
"Why are you speaking so stiff all of a sudden? Haruki-kun, that's not like your usual self."
Well, of course I'm going to act stiff…
"Traveling overseas…? Alone, with my unmarried daughter…?"
And with that, our Sunday date went something like this…
After going to the travel agency, our next stop was the Ogiso household.
"Hey, you're going all the way to France, so why would you pick such a backwater place to visit?"
"That's right. I've never heard of that Stra-something place before. When you go to France, isn't it normal to go to Paris? Especially if you're planning on doing some shopping…"
"Jeez～ you two sure don't know anything. Don't you know that it's a World Heritage site? There are some streets that remain unchanged since the middle ages!"
"Kyoto has places unchanged since the Heian period…"
"That's right, Kyoto is super popular among foreign tourists. It's the same thing."
"But still… I don't want some local folk art as a souvenir."
"That's right. If you buy us some weird quilt, we won't even know where to put it."
"All of you be quiet! I'm trying to have a conversation with Kitahara-kun here!"
I don't even know why I'm apologizing, but if I don't take the initiative to apologize, I don't think he would be able to calm himself.
"Well then… Can you tell me more about it? What intention do you have with this trip…?"
"Since I'll be on a business trip during Christmas, and I'll be in Europe for a while… I would like to spend Christmas with Setsuna-san at the place where Christmas originated."
"The one who came up with this plan was your own daughter…" that's something I'd never allow myself to say, as a man…
"I've always wanted to see it once, a real Christmas Mass."
"But isn't that a hotspot for tourists? I'm surprised you managed to get a reservation this late."
"Yeah, it was supposed to be full several months ago, but someone just canceled their reservation recently…"
…Or rather, it's most likely Sawako-san abusing her power…
At first, when we were talking with the agent there, it seemed almost silly because we were asking for the impossible, but the moment Sawako-san showed up, everything changed…
How should I put it, she just spoke in several different languages on the phone for a bit, then she finished reserving Setsuna's ticket and a hotel room for two in less than ten minutes.
…For an unreasonably low price as well.
"Isn't this going too overboard? Taking your girlfriend to your business trip. That's mixing private matters with your work…"
"By the time we meet up, I'll have already finished with my work. I also got approval from my superior yesterday. …So there shouldn't be any problems as far as my company is concerned."
Perhaps feeling guilty over pushing this business trip on me, Hamada-san acquiesced rather easily.
"But it's overseas… if something ever happened to Setsuna…"
"When we're together, I'll ensure Setsuna-san's safety. …I'll do everything in my power to ensure that."
If I say "I'll put my life on the line" here, I'll probably get approval from the ladies, but I'm sure that'll have the opposite effect on Setsuna's father.
…Even though that's what I'm planning to do anyway.
"They'll go on a honeymoon sooner or later. You're really grasping at straws if you're acting worried now."
"…! W-Well, you haven't made any future plans of that sort with Setsuna yet, right? Just the two of you traveling now is…"
"This isn't the first time either. Nee-chan is never home during the weekend, after all."
At this rate, I'll soon be leaving the realm of being able to calmly persuade him with reason.
"Yet whenever I tell you that she's with Kitahara-san, you never have any qualms. So if she sticks with Kitahara-san all throughout this trip, everything should be fine too, right?"
"T-Takahiro-kun… let's just leave it at that…"
If it becomes a matter of emotional arguments, I stand no chance. …Setsuna will have to stand up and convince him, but then it'll turn into a family feud within the Ogiso family.
Most likely, neither I nor her father wish to see that happen…
"As for Haruki-kun, he needs to go to Spain, Italy and lastly, Paris before we meet up."
"Ah, is that so? You should've mentioned that earlier. I thought you weren't going to Paris."
"Ooh, you're going to Italy as well～! There are some shoes I really want! They're made by a small manufacturer in Italy…"
"No, you two… Kitahara-kun is going there for a business trip, if you mix it with personal things like that…"
"That's fine, just tell me what you want. If it's too much to carry, I can just mail it back."
After Setsuna said that one sentence, the victory was pretty much ours.
"I'm so relieved. We finally got approval from my dad without any trouble."
"Can you really call that 'without any trouble'…?"
In the end… her father still had a very stern look on his face.
Since I had her mother and Takahiro-kun on my side, under the relentless assault from everyone aside from me, her father could do nothing but remain on the defense…
In other words, they did the one thing I feared the most, winning an emotional argument.
"Don't worry about it. I'm sure he'll be his usual self again after receiving a brandy as a souvenir from you."
Well, it's true that by the time I was going home after they had treated me to dinner, he was already drunk on the brandy he had…
"That's exactly what the problem is… I'll come back in one piece. And we'll make many memories there. There's no reason to be mad about having such a great thing happening."
"But I… how should I put it; I can't help but sympathize more with your father. I can't feel content knowing that he lost despite his more correct reasoning."
I have always held the conviction that "The person who says what's right is right."
…Well, setting aside my relationships with women.
"It's fine, don't worry, Haruki-kun. I'll talk to him later; I'll convince him through logic this time."
"Because I… no, none of us actually hate my dad. In fact, we love him a lot."
"I'll make sure he understands, so feel at ease, Haruki-kun."
To be able to say something like that so unabashedly is one of the amazing aspects of the Ogiso household, and Setsuna.
Something I… or any other slightly bitter person could never emulate. It's a beauty that can never be replaced.
I already know this… but I can't simply accept it, even now.
Setsuna is staring at me with a confused expression.
"You really do look a bit similar, you and my dad."
"You're both serious, strict, and never known to compromise."
She says that as she lightly pokes at my nose repeatedly.
