"Then go toward the window this time. Look out through the window."
"There won't be an idiot dangling from the window sill, will there?"
The room that was occupied by a single student five years ago. One of the seven mysteries of the school, and the room that no one dared to enter.
The cold winter breeze blows in through the open window, swaying Kazusa's long hair.
I don't let that photo opportunity go past me, so I take a picture from the side right when Kazusa holds back her hair.
"It's going to be below freezing tonight too. Keep yourself warm when you go to sleep tonight."
In Music Room 2, where the heater has long since been turned off, the freezing air envelops the room in an instant.
Outside the window are the sports clubs about to wrap up their exercise, and the sky slowly changing from red to dark blue.
A spectacle is unfolding, one that's identical to what happened two years ago… One that hasn't changed at all since five years ago.
The only difference is the girl who wasn't here two years ago, but who was here five years agoーand how she looked different back then.
Kazusa shivers from the cold… but the cold most likely isn't the cause behind her crumbling expression.
"Today… is the last day of your coverage, right?"
"You'll be rehearsing all day tomorrow, and your concert is the day after that. I can't be dragging you out with me any more than this."
Due to our time together ending at the end of this week like Kazusa decided, today must be the day everything ends.
"You really are vulgar. To think that even at the very end, you'd take me to the number one place I want to forget."
"See, you just admitted it. This place is 'number one' for you."
I always planned to bring Kazusa here no matter how she felt about it.
If she's going to insist that this is our last day together, then I'll choose a place suitable for that end. I'm certain I made no mistake in this choice.
"This is the place you spent the most time in during your three years at this school… probably more than your time spent in the classroom."
"I was really irritated during my time here. I kept stamping my feet in frustration because nothing ever went well."
…Though perhaps my only mistake is that this place is too appropriate.
"You keep saying that, but the music you played in your irritation gave me the impression that you had a lot of fun."
"There was this crappy guitarist who could never match up to me no matter how much time passed… That only added to my irritation."
While saying that, Kazusa clicks her tongue with a hint of nostalgia.
…I do think her expression is a bit strange, but that's how she really is, so it can't be helped.
"Did you get a bit better? Did your skills improve enough that you can play along with others?"
"Even five years ago I could do that…"
"Oh, I know! How about you play for me? Look, there is a guitar there."
"What's the problem? I'll only laugh, but I won't instruct you on every little thing."
"A single song is fine. You can even play Romance de Amor if you want."
"I said I can't. I haven't played once ever since I got a job."
"Why won't you play for me? Does Setsuna have exclusive rights to listen to you playing the guitar?"
I don't know what Kazusa just discerned, but this time she clicks her tongue with a hint of sadness.
…I wish she wouldn't make that expression.
Choosing this place was definitely not a mistake, yet I'm starting to regret it.
With a sigh Kazusa puts her hands on the window frame, and then turns back to me.
"If you're going to be so stubborn, then I have an idea of my own."
"Don't get angry… about something like this."
Her hair that was blowing backwards earlier is now blowing in her direction, brushing gently against her cheeks.
Gently, just like Kazusa's current expression…
"This is… the last time. This will mark the end, so I can tell you everything now, right?"
But her voice is as cold as the wind blowing against her hair.
"We won't ever meet again, so I can cross the line just a little bit, right?"
The words "of course not" refuse to leave my mouth.
This isn't the end. She has an additional concert to play… She might even return to Japan again sometime.
Am I just trying to contradict Kazusa's resigned feelings? Or am I perceiving a different meaning behind her enigmatic smile?
That uncertainty was cleared up the next time Kazusa opened her mouth.
"Hey, Haruki… You kissed Setsuna for the first time on that day we were on the stage, right?"
At that moment, all I could do was desperately grasp after the camera that fell from my hands.
"That night, right here… This is where Setsuna confessed to you, where you two kissed… and where you two became lovers, right?"
"H-H-H…Hey! What's this about all of a sudden?"
My voice ended up betraying me because of how sudden that statement was and just how unlike her it was to make it.
"I'm talking about five years ago… That day five years ago when everything ended."
She's letting out a vague smile that can be seen as proof of either malice, a desire to tease, or countless other emotions.
"If I'm wrong, you can deny it. But if you're going to lie, then make sure it's not an obvious one."
"L-Like I told you, back then… I was the one who confessed…"
No matter how much anyone tries to press the matter, I just can't admit the fact that it was Setsuna who confessed to me, which would make nobody happy…
"Doubtful. As if you had the guts to do something like that back then… You were completely indecisive between Setsuna and me."
Look… Not even Kazusa is happy to hear about it.
That's why I just can't admit it.
"Since it's you we're talking about, that was probably your first kiss too, right? You could never initiate something like that yourself after all."
I have no clue about the reason behind Kazusa bringing this up.
Why would she decide to talk about the day of our first separation… in the middle of what should be our final meeting?
Besides, that wasn't just my first time back then. Setsuna too had never…
Even though she's not happy in the slightest, she lets out an empty laugh.
"It's as I thought… Setsuna must've been looking. She saw me."
Just when I'm on the brink of losing all understanding, she throws an insinuating line at me like she's doing it on purpose.
"I always thought that might have been the case; that perhaps that was the reason Setsuna did as she did… I suppose you could call this the shock of realizing a five-year-old truth?"
"I don't understand it at all… What in the world are you…?"
I'm sure she's doing this to mess with me, but the atmosphere she has created is far too pitiful.
"There's no point in telling you now… but since this is the last time, it's fine, right?"
"Don't come to your own conclusions! What's so wrong about that? What's so funny? …Why are you talking about Setsuna that way?"
That's why I'm the one who's irritated right now.
"No, there's nothing wrong with it… Nor is it funny… Setsuna didn't do anything wrong either."
As she mutters those words, Kazusa takes a nearby chair and puts it in front of me. Then she sits down on the piano chair for some reason.
Unable to understand anything, I nervously sit down on the chair Kazusa prepared for me…
"I just think that it's a shame. Not for me, nor for Setsuna… but for you, Haruki."
"All your first experiences were with me. That really must be the worst… Serves you right."
I am left completely bewildered by Kazusa's nonsensical confession.
"It means that your past is defiled by me near every corner. Just like that night during the graduation ceremony, or that time at the airport the next day…"
And the path I turned away from, despite knowing that doing so is a mistake…
"I'm sorry for toying with you all this time… despite being a woman with no ties to your future."
Kazusa denies my sin as if my divergence from the correct path was a trap laid by her.
"…I have no idea what you've been talking about up until now."
"Then can I tell you from here on out? You won't regret hearing it?"
If you're going to ask in that way, then don't look so insinuating…
With Kazusa's insinuation firmly on my mind and expressed on my turned face, I urge Kazusa forward.
Though with my face turned, my intention can never be conveyed to Kazusa.
"Back then… I was playing the piano here like always."
"No… it wasn't quite like always. I was more irritated than usual because I had been forced to wear a thin and skimpy outfit."
When Kazusa said "from here on out," she wasn't talking about the future, but the past.
About that day we were on the stage.
"As I was doing that, the usual nuisance came into the room. No matter how many times I chased him out, he never learned his lesson and came back. What a stubborn person he was."
A short while after our song was met with roaring applause…
The exhilaration from my time on the stage wouldn't go away, so as I was walking around the school hallways immersed in the aftertaste of our concert, I heard a melody from the usual music room.
"I was feeling more irritated than usual, yet he didn't know about my feelings, so he started talking to me, getting all excited by himself."
When I opened the door, the person I wanted to see the most was inside.
"He was more annoying than usual, so I answered him half-heartedly. But despite that, he wouldn't stop talking."
That's because I was happier than usual. It didn't matter if her answers were half-hearted; I just kept talking to her.
About how I wanted to stay like that forever. With the three of us.
She rejected that idea from a rational standpoint, but I kept on telling her about my egotistical dream.
"At some point I stopped hearing his voice. When I turned around, I saw that he had dozed off while still sitting."
Because I had gone through countless all-nighters…
"Yes, he was sleeping. Around the same time as right now."
Because of that, our memories after this point diverge.
The next time I reopened my eyes, Setsuna was suddenly right in front of me, and…
"I only got more annoyed… I thought about giving him a piece of my mind, so I went to him."
But it's not Setsuna who's here right now.
It's not Setsuna, but Kazusa who's standing up from her chair, and slowly walking toward me.
"I went closer to him, then leaned forward to take a closer look at his face. He was facing down, so I had to do it like this, from below…"
She comes closer to me, then she leans forward to take a closer look at my face. With undiluted eyes, she looks at me from below…
"And then right before my eyes, I saw his incredibly defenseless and half-witted face… Yes, just like right now."
"Don't move… Otherwise, this won't be a repeat of back then."
Right now, Kazusa is in the exact same posture Setsuna was in back then.
It's as if she knows what happened here five years ago. No, it's as if she saw what happened here five years ago.
"Otherwise, I won't be able to show you what I did after this."
No, no, that's wrong, that's wrong too. There's no way Kazusa could've seen what happened back then.
Who saw Kazusa when she was here back then?
The moment that thought enters my head… I can see the awaiting future… as well as the past.
The scene that I didn't see… and the scene that Kazusa and Setsuna did see.
"I was the one who did it first… I was the first one."
This, too, might be a reenactment of what happened five years ago… of those few minutes before I woke up.
"Kissing him, making love to him… and falling in love with him."
"I knew that it was cowardly… and unforgivable."
Kazusa's breath touches me every time she speaks.
"But there was no way I could confess to him. I hated myself so much, so I thought that there was no way he'd fall in love with me."
Kazusa's lips come close enough to nearly touch mine.
"That's why I did something so awful and so fitting of me. That's how much I was at my wits' end. It hurt so much."
Kazusa's expression is now all that is visible within my field of vision.
"…I didn't want anyone else to steal him away."
I sense a sweet scent coming from Kazusa's body.
It's a scent that shakes me to my core, to the point that I'm unable to explain it away by saying that it's just because she likes sweet food.
"But Setsuna stole him that very day. Setsuna took everything."
Kazusa's voice resounds in my chest.
Along with her pitiful words that in utter contrast to her sweet scent make me grimace.
"After all, I didn't think it was possible… That there'd be another weird woman like me…"
The way she makes me falsely believe through her words and movements that nothing has changed these past five years hurts so much.
"That such a good person, such a good woman… would have such terrible taste in men. Who could have possibly known that…?"
The way she cried as she lamented to me five years ago hurts too…
As well as the way she's making me falsely believe that her warmth, coldness, sadness, and pitifulness haven't deteriorated one bit since that night we parted.
When I see Kazusa's eyes slowly water right in front of me, I let out a voice that proves that my own eyes are doing the same thing.
"You're messing with me, right? You're trying to get even for what I've done, right? That's what this is… tell me that it is."
I'm sad because, while my time has moved forward, Kazusa's time has remained stagnant. A divergence between our paths that's so decisive.
At least… that divergence was supposed to have taken place.
"Do you think… this is a joke? Are you going to laugh this off as a joke, even when I'm telling you all this, Haruki?"
"Of course I can't laugh it off… So I'm begging you, laugh at it for me."
I can feel a single drop fall upon me from Kazusa's wet eyes.
"If you don't laugh it off, I won't know what to do…!"
"You can't do anything anyway. Don't talk so thoughtlessly about not knowing what to do when it's already too late…!"
"Then don't thoughtlessly talk about this either if it's too late! If today is our last day, then you should have carried that knowledge with you to the grave!"
"You're… you're the one… who's cruel… Kazusa… You're the one…"
The tip of her nose lightly hits mine.
Her tears go down even my cheeks.
"All that is left is the concert. Everything'll be fine. We'll never be alone together after this."
"I just said I'll never acknowledge that!"
"If I just hold your hand… If I just tell you my feelings… If I just kiss you once more and for the last time…"
My vision turns to darkness. My eyes are shut.
And then I feel a warm and soft sensation on my lips…
But I only felt it for a single moment.
It was my cell phone that was flashing the moment I opened my eyes.
Even if it's only spam mail, the timing of which it was sent was far too miraculous and precise, and it was both great and awful at the same time.
The name of the sender far transcends any mere coincidence…
2. I look her in the eyes.
I feel Kazusa's breath on my right cheek.
"…But if you say anything more, I might actually try hating you."
But I desperately eject those lips and eyes from my field of vision.
"I might do my best to hate you."
Physically, I know that I'm only giving a fleeting resistance, but I imagine as far as my attitude goes, it's at least stronger than that…
Kazusa was the one to finally submit.
"I really am… hopeless, aren't I? I'm completely hopeless."
With her hands still on my shoulders, she distances herself from me.
"You're right, it was a joke. I'm just messing with you. I tried to get back at you, Haruki."
Along with excuses that come far too late… which no one would ever believe.
"Although, it failed completely until the very end… You really don't know how to spot a joke."
…Her eyes redden, yet she still shows me an indecipherable smile.
"So, you know, this marks the end of our last interview… Good work."
She's trying to act strong in front of me, and she's being considerate of Setsuna.
And she's harboring a strange feeling that's neither quite resigned nor sad.
And then I feel a warm and soft sensation on my lips…
But I only felt it for a single moment.
"I really am… hopeless, aren't I? I'm completely hopeless."
With her hands still on my shoulders, she distances herself from me.
"You're right, it was a joke. I'm just messing with you. I was getting back at you, Haruki."
Along with excuses that come far too late… which no one would ever believe.
"As proof of that… Haha, hahaha. Look, I'm laughing, am I not?"
…Her eyes redden, but her smile is probably from the heart.
"So, you know, this marks the end of our last interview… Good work."
She's trying to act strong in front of me, and she's being considerate of Setsuna.
Along with a happiness within Kazusa from having a miniscule wish granted.
We were both completely silent on the way home… until Kazusa finally opened her mouth during our parting.
"It's enough that you come. All you have to do is listen to me play the piano."
"…Since it's you we're talking about, you'll probably fall asleep halfway through out of boredom though."

"That's why, this time… is our final farewell."
And then, once again… she persistently makes the same declaration that she has undone countless times herself, and which also has been undone by me.
And perhaps because we've already shared countless final farewells already, Kazusa's last parting words come off as thoughtlessly cold.
"I was the one who did it first… I was the first one."
What are you saying after all this time?
"Kissing him, making love to him… and falling in love with him."
"…I didn't want anyone else to steal him away."
Had she… told me that five years ago, I would have…
No, nothing would have changed. Nothing can be allowed to have changed.
To cross an even farther line than what I initially desired under the pretense that it would be the last time…
To engrave a feeling within the both of us that we can never forget…
"If I just hold your hand… If I just tell you my feelings… If I just kiss you once more and for the last time…"
Why does today have to be the last…?
This shouldn't be the end. We should go more slowly…
Does there not exist a choice within you to sublimate our relationship as friends…?
Are 1 and 0 the only choices when it comes to me…?
When I look at the clock as I'm trying to calm my breath, I see that multiple hours have passed since then.
…But not even 30 minutes have passed since I last checked the time.
And here I was thinking that I finally managed to fall asleep.
Ever since Kazusa's farewell, that same scene has repeated itself in my mind.
That unbearable, pitiful and beautiful scene.
In order to chase that thought from my mind, I exhausted every alcoholic drink in the room, which only served to make the image more vivid.
Her voice, her breath, her expression, and even her thoughts that should be unknown to me. I added those details in a way that was convenient to me.
…No, in a way that was very inconvenient for me.
I gulp some cold tea down my sore throat to desperately cool my head.
One moment I prepare the tea cold, and then I prepare it hot the other. Even I think my actions are not making sense.
For a while now, I've been trying to find the best way to stop myself from thinking through trial and error.
The response from my mind and body is terrifying. My wavering heart despises the actions I take against my instincts.
A feeling of exhaustion is overwhelming my body. A result of my extreme emotions and feelings of pleasure that stem from my mistakes.
The proof of my violently shifting emotions is inside my underwear.
I thought about Kazusa… I thought of someone other than Setsuna.
All because I closed my eyes for a few minutes.
"Good morning. I'm Ogiso from Knights Records. I look forward to working with you today."
"Ah, good morning… Wait, isn't it usually Onuma-san who comes here today?"
"I've been assigned to this task from now on. There might be some things I'm not accustomed to yet, but I hope you'll accept me regardless."
"I see. Likewise, then. I was wondering why Knights-san was so beautiful at first. You were Ogiso-san, right? Do you appear on stage too?"
"Ah, no, I leave the event procedures to the professionals. I operate behind the scenes more than anything…"
"What a waste… It wouldn't hurt to make an occasional appearance. I'm sure you'd gain a lot of fans."
"…T-Thank you very much. But the main role goes to the artist, at the end of the day."
"Well, that's true. Now let us arrange the procedures moving forward. Could you follow me to the office?"
"Yes! I hope for a fruitful day of work!"
"Perhaps you should lower the brightness a bit? The reflection might be a bit too strong."
"Hm… Let me check the images again at 1 PM. For now, we'll leave things as they are until noon. Good work."
"Good work to you too. Hey everyone! One hour break starting now!"
"…Good work you too. Come, let's go grab a bite."
"Because we're going to sell the concert recording of tomorrow on blu-ray, obviously."
"I'm your company president. I have a duty to make sure my workers can eat, not to mention that I have to earn enough money to pay for my daughter's education."
"If I can do what I want, then don't complain when I do."
"…If you want to eat, then do so alone. I'll practice until I'm satisfied."
"…You've been at it since 5 AM, you know?"
"This is nothing. Everything will end tomorrow anyway."
"You still have an additional concert though."
"Tomorrow is everything… I don't care about what happens after that."
"I have a good feeling about my performance just now. Leave me be."
"I also have a good feeling about it. That's why instead of improving on it, you should preserve your strength for tomorrow…"
"…Fine. Just make sure you don't overdo it, okay?"
"This is no different from any other day."
"In what way? It's true you're doing well, but you look possessed."
"…I'm just a bit tense since the real deal is right around the corner."
"I'd appreciate if you didn't mix your personal feelings with your job. Well, I suppose your music wouldn't be the same if you didn't."
"If all you're going to do is talk nonsense, then leave already. I want to play the piano…"
"Yes, yes. Well then, everything in moderation, okay?"
"Try to keep the pace, would you?"
Throughout the whole day, I didn't hear a single sound that suggested that my neighbor was going about her life.
No sounds of doors or windows opening. No sounds of banging on the walls to catch my attention.
…That's why I couldn't get a wink of sleep. From night to morning, and then night again.
Truthfully speaking, I did get about ten minutes of sleep. But that sleep brought forth nothing but regret, disgust, and anguish.
I tried distracting myself with work, but I was done with all the magazines before noon. The only job remaining was the compiling of the interviews.
But I couldn't bring myself to listen to her voice. In the end, I found myself just lying down on the bed like this.
But unable to close my eyes, let alone fall asleep, I kept staring at the ceiling until the sun set.
"Since that's how it is, I won't be in Tokyo this Sunday, so I won't be able to attend Kazusa's concert."
"You said you weren't going, Haruki-kun, but I actually managed to get some tickets. I was planning on going to listen to Kazusa play."
"If possible, I wanted to go with you, Haruki-kun."
"You might be wondering why I'd decide something like that on my own. You might even be angry at me."
"I'm sorry. But if I was going, I absolutely needed you with me. Because…"
"I didn't want you… to go to Kazusa's concert alone, Haruki-kun."
"Because I know how you will feel if you go to listen to Kazusa's performance alone."
"Your heart will leave me and it'll be sucked in by her playing. I know that."
No matter how many times I re-read that, the words won't come out.
We haven't maintained a relationship this long just for nothing. Setsuna knows everything about me.
She has no way of knowing about Kazusa and me, but she's fully aware of the fact that I feel lost.
But because our relationship is so close, I've realized something too.
Setsuna's wavering. She doesn't fully trust me.
The fact that she contacted me now is proof that Setsuna feels lost too.
She would've done so earlier if she had forgiven me. And she would've done so much later if she began to trust me again.
But that doesn't mean I can blame Setsuna.
After all, I'm currently harboring suspicious feelings and conducting myself in a way that's deserving of her doubt.
I've become so passionate about a woman other than Setsuna, so it's only natural that she can't forgive me.
In that case, the course of action I should take is…
…To try and understand everything about Setsuna. To accept everything about her, no matter what happens…
Because whenever I close my eyes, I can see it.
I can see the vague smile Kazusa let out when we parted… back at the station last night.
I can see Kazusa's impish, yet painful gaze when she looked up at me… back when we were in the music room that evening.
I can see her tear-filled eyes. Her sweet, warm breaths. And her lips, which I'm sure would have felt soft and warm.
In the blink of an eye, an unforgivable passion envelops my entire body…
And in response, I rush into the bathroom, swiftly turn on the faucet, and soak my face in cold water.
I do this over and over again… even through the numbing sensation of my hands and the stretching sensation of my face.
I attempt to spread the chilling sensation to my head in an attempt to freeze the unrelenting images that keep on surfacing inside my mind.
I shake my head, scattering the drops of water still on my face. Then I start speaking to the mirror.
I rebuke my miserable reflection showing my pale expression and bloodshot eyes in the mirror.
I tell myself that it's alright. I tell myself that I've only lost my sense of reason temporarily.
Because over the past five years, we've formed an unshakeable bondーan unbreakable connection that no one can come between.
"That's why, this time… is our final farewell."
It's over now. Nothing ever happened.
And nothing will happen from now on. After all, there won't be another chance to…
Why am I trying to convince myself that everything's alright…?
I should be telling someone else that everything's alright, shouldn't I? It's something I should be telling Setsuna to put her at ease, isn't it?
"Hey, it's still not open. Wouldn't it have been better if we took our time and went shopping instead?"
"No way. Nothing good would come from being with you."
"That's because you keep cutting me off whenever I try to talk about something."
"That's because you keep treating me like other women. It feels weird to have you act considerate after all this time."
"…What do you want me to do?"
"Besides, I wanted to come here before the concert hall opens."
"No idea. He said he's not coming when I asked him over the phone last week."
"I've noticed Setsuna is acting strange too… It feels like they're going through something, those two."
"If only they could resolve it by themselves, with just the two of them…"
"Don't say anything weird… The third person is a world-famous celebrity now."
"And even then, she was the daughter of a world-famous celebrity."
"I told you to stop saying that. Their homes, situations, and even the worlds they live in are completely different."
"Why did you come looking for Haruki this early then?"
"It feels pretty bad for us to be saying this when we used to be Touma's friends, though…"
"But what should we do if he does come…? What should we tell him?"
"That's simple. We'll greet him and say 'fancy seeing you here,' then we'll be with him throughout the whole concert and make plans to all go home together once it's over."
"Please, Takeya… Make sure you find Haruki, okay?"
"…Will you do anything I tell you if I find him?"
"Alright then. I'll keep my eyes wide open."
"…No, I'm sorry. Even if I say that, I'm sure that in the end I'll just…"
"Stop talking like other women. It feels weird hearing you act so delicate."
"Y-Yes… Yes, I managed to get the other party to forgive us somehow."
"I see… Well, then I'll go ahead and make a call to apologize."
"Please do. I'm really sorry about this…"
"Oh, everyone makes mistakes. It's more understandable given that this was your first event. We've already taken that into consideration."
"But I did cause a lot of trouble for the person in charge there…"
"Just make sure it goes well next time and everything will work out. You still have work left to do over there tomorrow, so wrap things up for now."
"Oh, right, how about going to a karaoke place? I've heard that you can manage just fine alone."
"Well then, good work. Forget about today and rest, then do your best tomorrow."
"I always hoped for and wanted this job, yet nothing went well at all."
"I'm such an idiot. I had all these delusions about success, never realizing I'm still not worth half a person."
"Why am I so different from you, Haruki-kun? We went to the same school for seven whole years…"
"Tell me, Haruki-kun. Do you ever fail at your job? If you do fail, how do you move on from it?"
"I want to use it as a reference for tonight. If you see this text, then…"
"No… Not yet. After all, nothing has been solved yet."
"The seats are almost full. Though that's a given considering the ticket sales."
"Did anyone come to the dressing room?"
"No one's allowed entrance except for you."
"I made sure to tell the staff to make an exception for a single person. I even sent a text to him."
"Perhaps he's restraining himself. Or perhaps he'll appear once the concert is over."
"We don't have quarrels. Our relationship wasn't like that from the start."
"But I don't really care anyway. I'm satisfied as long as he comes to the concert."
"Did you perchance find him in the audience?"
"No, I haven't seen him since I haven't left this place even once."
"We don't have quarrels… Our relationship isn't like that, but… he'll come. I'm certain he'll come."
"I'm sure he's listening somewhere. He's listening to me play the piano…"
"Ogiso-sama, I see. Here, this is your key. I wish you a good evening."
"Also, since some time ago, this guest has…"

It took three hours to go all the way to Shin-Osaka Station by bullet train. From there, I had to take another fifteen minutes on a private railway. And then I had to wait in the hotel lobby for an hour.
Yet the time spent doesn't matter, because we've been apart for much longer.
Setsuna is finally right in front of me again. I'm finally able to meet Setsuna again…
As Setsuna stirs the milk she poured into her coffee, she finally speaks.
"To think you'd only appear when I failed at my job. Not to mention the distance you traveled to come here."
The first part is just a coincidence. The second was an inevitability on my part.
"It's almost as if you're my savior now… It makes me want to cling to you."
That's why being seen in such a favorable light is honestly troublesome.
"I can't. I kept encouraging myself up until now that now alone, I can't be relying on you, Haruki-kun."
I'm the one who came to cling to her.
Yet Setsuna is creating an atmosphere where she won't rely on me, and she won't let me rely on her.
"How did you know this was the place?"
"I called the Ogiso household. They told me you were on a business trip in Osaka, so…"
"Jeez… I'm absolutely sure that my family trusts you more than me, Haruki-kun."
"I'm aware that that's breaking the rules. I just felt like I had to see you in person, Setsuna…"
"You used that trick half a year ago too when we had a quarrel… I said that I didn't want to talk to you, yet my entire family dragged me all the way to the phone."
"I'm sorry… I ended up using an unfair method."
"You really are unfair… Thanks to that, I'm wavering a lot right now. Enough to make me hate myself."
As I thought… this really is a troublesome situation.
How much have I betrayed Setsuna up until now? How much have I wavered beyond what Setsuna is even capable of?
Even so, Setsuna remains unaware of my terrible actions, and puts herself down as if she's the one at fault.
"Then, next question. Why did you come for me?"
I came because of an absurd reason, yet she devalues herself by saying that "I came for her."
She's creating a situation that's only getting more and more convenient for me, but also more and more disadvantageous for Setsuna herself.
"It's not like you came because you… knew I was feeling down, right?"
"Hehe, obviously. I hadn't told you anything yet… I was getting my hopes up over something absurd."
In this situation… will Setsuna accept everything even if I don't explain my own circumstances?
If I tell her that I simply missed her, that I felt lonely without her, will she embrace me without prying any further?
Will she… make me forget about Kazusa?
I want to embrace Setsuna. I want to apologize to Setsuna.
Normally I'd be able to do both those things… but right now, I feel like those two choices are two mutually exclusive urges.
If I pick one of them, and forget about the other…
1. I simply wanted to see you.
2. I will be honest about Kazusa.
I simply ran away because I've reached my limit.
"I've gone for so long without seeing you, Setsuna, without hearing your voice…"
Being next to Kazusa. Listening to Kazusa's piano playing.
"I wanted to hear your voice right away, Setsuna. I was ready to go anywhere to achieve that."
As I am right now, I can't listen to her piano. I can't go to her concert.
"Because I thought that if I were to meet you, and you were to call my name…"
Because had I gone to her concert, and listened to her performance filled with her feelings…
"Of course you'd get mad at me, and you'd sulk about it. But if you were to smile for me even for a little bit in the end…"
Had I stood in the waiting room once the concert was over with a bouquet in my hands, waiting to receive her with a smile on my face…
Then I can't be sure if I'd be able to hold back my own feelings.
"I'd be able to remember the obvious fact that… you're the only one for me, Setsuna."
The fact that Setsuna's the only one for me. An obvious feeling that I need to be constantly carrying with me.
I'm not sure who was first to stretch out their hand…
Before I knew it, Setsuna's hand had tightly intertwined with mine upon the table.
Setsuna's fingers are now wrapping around the same, traitorous hand that had held Kazusa's just a few days ago.
"And that's all there is to it…"
There is no way Setsuna has forgotten that today is the day of Kazusa's concert.
"I see… so that's how it is. I'm the only one you need."
"I've been telling you that all this time."
There is no way that Setsuna isn't suspicious about the fact that I've left Tokyo as if running away on a day like that.
"We're supposed to be in a spat right now, so it's really frustrating how happy I am."
Despite that, Setsuna doesn't attempt to touch the subject.
She stubbornly refuses to bring up the very name that was the reason for our spat.
"I'm frustrated at myself for feeling so good about being able to touch you like this, Haruki-kun."
She doesn't attempt to see through my lie…
"Let me make up for it. I'll listen to anything you want tonight, Setsuna."
"You… plan on spending the entire night with me."
"You… plan on not letting go of me all night…"
"That's strange… You're going to listen to everything I have to say tonight, right? Why are you asking me for permission then, Haruki-kun?"
Setsuna covers our entwined hands with her other hand.
Of course, she expects me to cover that hand with my own too.
"My room right now only has a single bed… I need to get it changed."
"I took care of that before you came back… there was a room with a double bed available, so I reserved it."
And of course, I make sure to not betray Setsuna's expectations.
"I've been meeting Touma again. These past few days, every day."
"I didn't tell you that, Setsuna. I hid something from you again."
But it didn't end up stopping because it froze over. It was more so as if it dried up.
Because Setsuna is staring at me without surprise, without anger, and without grief.
Instead, she just keeps slowly digesting the truth laid before her.
Which is why, in her place, I relieved the time between us of its frozen state.
"You see, Tomo… told me that she met Kazusa twice. Once in front of your apartment, Haruki-kun, and once in the audience at my concert."
Kazusa had offered me a ticket to attend Setsuna's live performance under the pretense that someone had asked her to pass it to me.
I had given Kazusa that ticket because I just couldn't see Setsuna while we were still in the middle of a cold war, and I was still spending time with Kazusa…
There's only one person who can connect the dots from the fact that Kazusa was seen in both of those places.
"You knew I was with Kazusa all this time, Setsuna…"
I finally give up on calling her Touma.
Because there's no point in me putting on airs anymore.
"You knew everythingーthat I'm absolutely despicable and a cruel traitor, Setsuna…"
"And then at the beginning of the week… Kazusa moved into the apartment next to me. Youko-san… Touma Youko apparently signed a contract for it at the time."
"…Now it sounds like I'm putting the blame on her. If I hadn't accepted the exclusive coverage job, Kazusa would never have moved in."
I confess my sins to Setsuna…
Even though I was supposed to have fully divulged them when I fell out with her for the first time this year.
"For two weeks after that… I was with Kazusa the whole time."
The sins I've committed over the past two weeks up until now are so grave that what I did back then just can't compare.
"She's picky about her diet… so I've been making breakfast and dinner for her for a while. I cut the sugar off her diet as much as I could and included more greens."
I knew it was going to be Kazusa from the start, and Kazusa knew it was going to be me.
"Besides, she became such a celebrity before I realized it, so I did my best to make sure that her identity wasn't found out."
I had plenty of chances to refuse. And I was supposed to have properly refused.
"She always started spewing things she didn't need to talk about during the interviews, so I ended up abridging a lot of it for her own sake."
I kept telling myself that we just couldn't meet one another, and we had to conduct ourselves professionally if we absolutely had to meet.
"Whenever I pointed the camera at her she turned away, so I had to take pictures when her guard was down. That earned me a lot of glares."
I told myself countless times that I couldn't make Setsuna sad because I love her so much.
"I felt so guilty, and I could barely keep myself from running away. The thought of you flickered in my head countless times, Setsuna, and it caused me so much pain."
Yet, in the end, the reason why I accepted the assignment of interviewing her was because I didn't want to make Kazusa feel lonely.
"…And I felt happy. Happy for being able to spend time with her."
It was a reason that should never have managed to persuade me, for my heart was supposed to be Setsuna's.
Just like that time, she listens to me in complete silence.
"Do you feel fed up with me?"
She responds to me with only a slight shake of her head.
"…Do you never want to see my face again?"
All she does is sway her head left and right, with more and more intensity.
"…I'm sorry. I know this isn't something that can be forgiven just by apologizing though."
"There's nothing you need to be sorry about. There's no need for that at all."
In the end, she finally becomes incapable of holding back any longer, and with an intense tone in her little voice, she tries to defend me.
"Because I understand. I know that you're not in the wrong, Haruki-kun."
"That's not true. I've wronged you. Horribly, at that."
"I know that you must have felt really troubled."
"That doesn't make my sin any lighter."
"I also know that it takes a lot of courage to talk to me honestly about it right now."
"I merely couldn't bear hiding it anymore. I'm just a coward."
"I know that you treasure me from the bottom of your heart… You've conveyed that to me clearly."
"Don't defend me so much. I don't have any right…"
I'd received the punishment I desired, but…
The pain that I yearned for was very far off from what I was expecting.
There was an audible sound when Setsuna slapped me, but I doubt that the strength she put into it would've managed to kill a mosquito, and it must've hurt much more for her instead.
…Unlike a certain someone, she's not used to hitting people.
Setsuna, who got up to slap me, slowly sits back down on her chair with her head down.
The guests around us direct their attention to us. And I imagine Setsuna's the one who's suffering the most from their staring.
"In truth, I have no right to do this. But I couldn't bring myself to forgive you no matter what."
Setsuna had forgotten about public appearances and condemned me…
"Because, Haruki-kun… you came here to run away, right? You came here to run away from Kazusa's concert, right?"
"You were with her until right before the concert. You supported her all this time, yet you let go of her hand at the very last moment."
"Why would you do such a thing? No matter what happens today, and no matter what happens to you, you have to listen to her play the piano, don't you?"
"I'm sorry, I… didn't want to betray you any further, Setsuna."
"That doesn't mean you can betray Kazusa instead… That's wrong, right?"
"But, but… if I remained there any longer I…"
I felt irritated at Kazusa for trying to distance herself from me, and I felt bewildered when Kazusa tried to get closer to me than I expected.
My own actions stopped making sense, and my heart fell into disarray.
…I became unable to trust my own feelings.
"Setsuna… imagine if I had gone to where Kazusa was, and not come back to you…"
"Don't ask me that! If my true feelings come out, something awful's going to happen!"
Just because Setsuna says she's capable of lashing out at me, doesn't mean she has the confidence to do it.
"I… am aware that I'm saying something really cruel to you right now, Haruki-kun."
"Not to mention something very scary… enough to make me ruin things for myself."
As usual, she's letting out strong words with her little voice.
But I can tell from her tone that her voice had been gradually starting to shake.
"But right now, let me pretend that I'm angry at you. Let me admonish you with my principles. Let me say only the right things."
The trembling rapidly invaded her lips and her throat, and in the blink of an eye, grew so vicious that it'd become impossible to hide.
Her words are reminiscent of what she said on the day we separated…
No, I could even say that if I were to recall them in the future, I might actually remember her saying them back then rather than today.
My stomach, my chest… they hurt as if pierced by countless needles.
"There is no point in going now… the concert's already begun."
I turn my back on Setsuna's correctness and Kazusa's pain in an attempt to run away from that excruciating pain.
"You might not have made it in time to see the concert start, but it'll be alright if you make it in time before it ends…"
"Where do you think we are…? I won't be able to make it to her last song anymore."
"Then at least show your face in the dressing room. At least congratulate her… At least apologize for not being able to go."
"Enough… that's enough already. I came here to meet up with you because I'd fully gathered my resolve, Setsuna. There's no point in going back at this point…"
"You're not prepared… Haruki-kun, you're not prepared at all."
Her statement hit me right where it hurt the most, such that I wasn't able to immediately deny what she said or snap back at her.
Although I'd hoped for her to understand me to such an extent, in a way, it's also one of the reasons why I can't say anything.
That's why I take a deep breath, and squeeze out different words from my lungs.
"Even then, this marks the end. I will never betray you again, Setsuna…"
I'm neither denying her nor snapping back at her. I'm simply becoming defiant.
"I see… You won't forgive me anymore."
But as I thought, Setsuna still refuses to accept it. She won't give me any affirmation.
But that too is only natural.
I'm likely the one person who's hurt Setsuna more than anyone else throughout her short life.
And even Setsuna's incredibly compassionate heart was bound to wear out eventually, for she was not divine, only human.
"No… Kazusa is the one who won't forgive. Kazusa is the one it won't end for."
"Kazusa is the one who won't give up."
But Setsuna's kindness once again proves my despair-filled expectations wrong.
"It won't end. It's not over yet. The three of us will never be over because of something like this."
I've known that someday it will wear out, but it seems there's still some time until that day.
"That's not true. It's over. It ended five years ago."
"I guarantee it. Kazusa would never give up on you just because you did something like this, Haruki-kun."
"How can you be so sure of that…? You haven't even met her since then…"
"That's because Kazusa won't come to see me. She only looked at me from afar, and never called out to me."
"That's… because she is afraid of facing you, Setsuna… Even that is my fault."
"That's wrong. She hasn't forgiven me yet… She hasn't forgiven you and me, Haruki-kun."
"Kazusa hasn't forgotten about what happened five years ago at all."
"She hasn't forgotten how she was betrayed by me, and how she had you stolen from her."
"I just told you that's wrong… She… Kazusa doesn't resent you at all, Setsuna. She has kept loving you ever since that time."
"One doesn't bear just one single feeling. Everyone is like that."
Setsuna… is too kind, and too strong.
"Even I love Kazusa. I've loved her since back then."
She bears the form of the ideal woman who hasn't changed since the day we met. She's still completely wasted on me.
"But that's not everything. I bear feelings that I can't tell anyone about… especially not you, Haruki-kun."
She's a misguided, yet utterly virtuous woman who's degrading me into a miserable man who only wants to take advantage of her. She's turning me into someone who will give her nothing but excuses.
"That's why this isn't a matter of not meeting her again… Even if you run away, even if you distance yourself from her, time won't solve anything."
"Kazusa, you and me… we must firmly settle matters about our futures…"
I've taken advantage of that kindness, and made her suffer countless times. I've let myself be spoiled by her strength, and abandoned her countless times.
"That's why you should go back to Kazusa now. And then you must reassure her."
There is no guarantee that I won't do that again in the future, yet Setsuna keeps repeating the same mistake.
That's why today, once again, I'll become the me that I hate today.
I'll let her turn me into a miserable man who can only run away, unable to solve anything by himself.
I'll become such a person because of none other than Setsuna herself.
"I love you, Setsuna… is that not enough…?"
"It's not enough… because that isn't all. You still love Kazusa."
"But… I'm afraid of making a mistake. I'm afraid of everything going back to how it was five years ago."
I know the right choice. It's right before my eyes.
But when I'm next to that girl, I always make the wrong choice… I end up wanting to make the wrong choice.
"It's okay. I have faith in you… No, I'm sorry, I really can't say that."
"…Just so you know, it's not because I don't have faith in you. It's because I do have faith in you, Haruki-kun."
She can't have faith in me because she has faith in me…
"I have faith in the strength of your feelings toward Kazusa. I have faith in your love toward Kazusa…"
"That's why I can't have complete faith that you'll return to me."
Setsuna spoke those linguistically incorrect words with both distinctness and correctness.

"I see, not yet… Then what about Youko-san… President Touma?"
That's why Setsuna wouldn't mind me simply being worried about the whereabouts of my friend.
"Then if you do get in touch, please tell them to call Kitahara immediately. I'll tell you my phone number…"
I'm… only doing the natural thing as a fellow human being.
"…I see. Yes, that's fine. Thank you very much. Goodbye."
As I'm speaking on the phone, I lower the heat on the stew that had started boiling at some point.
When I open the lid, a pleasant spicy fragrance fills the air.
I called everyone in my line of business that I knew, but in the end, it was all pointless.
Though that's about what I expected…
There is no way the young pianist who earned the title "enemy of the media" in just a few days would ever carelessly leave any traces of herself.
…I guarded her until the day of the concert myself, after all.
"My name is Kitahara from the editing department of Kaiousha. I'm always obliged. Excuse me, but is there an Itakura from Shandy Editing of The Orient Magazine…?"
And in the end, it has backfired on me right now. It seems that finding out Kazusa's whereabouts from the mass media is going to be a difficult task.
Perhaps I have no choice but to find Youko-san tomorrow after all.
That's probably my only choice, and the most safe and certain method.
"A business trip…? I understand, that's fine. I'll call back tomorrow, so please let her know that I called. Goodbye…"
Either way, I should give up on recklessly looking for her outside.
I should stay in this room, with the mindset that she can return at any time.
Because there is no real reason to be worried.
If she truly has decided to disappear, it's probably just because she's sulking a bit.
If I talk to her, if I apologize to her… the misunderstanding will be resolved. We can reconcile as "friends." We can reach an agreement as "business partners."
That's why I'm just slightly worried about my "friend," and I need to back up my "business partner."
I decided to go with curry for dinner today, one that can be eaten immediately. I made so much of it that for a single person to eat all of it, it'd take more than a week.
But there is no deep meaning behind that… is there?
As I'm speaking of the devil, I hear a sound coming from the door of the other apartment.
"Kazusa, hey, Kazusa! Where the hell have you been up until now!?"
Look, there was no deep meaning behind it after all. I always knew she'd come back if I waited.
But my mind won't be put at ease until I give her a piece of my mind.
After all, she decided to disappear for the whole day, causing countless people trouble.
"Open up! You're back, aren't you!? I told you that I want to talk to you, didn't I!?"
As my neighbor, my friend, and my business partner, it's only natural that she gets lectured…
"…I'm sorry for the racket. I truly am sorry!"
…It was the resident of the apartment two doors away. Seeing myself in such a cliched situation gave me vertigo.
"Yes, yes… then if anything happens call my cell phone. I'm sorry for the trouble. Goodbye."
"I'm back… huh? It's been a while, Kitahara-kun!"
"…We've been talking every day over email. I finished the task you gave me last night, so make sure to double check it later."
Recently, Suzuki-san has rid herself of all reluctance in the way she hands out tasks. She's truly become a professional.
But still, in my unreasonableness ranking, she still only places third after Hamada-san and one other person.
"So, why are you here at work? Aren't you supposed to be glued to Touma Kazusa right now?"
"They say she ran away… She apparently got involved in some blind romantic affair."
"Huuh!? You mean someone took advantage of their position as her ex-boyfriend and made her do this and that!?"
"Don't make up random stories. If being in the same class as someone means that you're dating them, I'd be called Iizuka Takeya by now."
Did my expression look normal just now…? Did my voice sound superficial…?
"It's just that I've been unable to get in touch with her… for a mere two days."
In the end I couldn't find out Kazusa's whereabouts yesterday.

I contacted everyone who might have had a clue in vain, and everything I thought was a hint led to nothing. There was no sign of anyone around the time the last train left Minami-Suetsugu Station either.
In my room devoid of any color or sound, I waited for Kazusa until dawn. I started moving once the sun started to shine through the window.
I didn't get a wink of sleep last night, but my mind is unnaturally awake.
"Two days… Isn't that a big deal!? Does that mean no one knows where she's been since the concert ended?"
"We can't reach the office she's affiliated with, right? Perhaps we should file a missing persons report to the police after all…"
"If you file a report to the police and the mass media gets a whiff of it, then what will you do? That would be the absolute worst."
"No, well, that's true, but I can't say I'm content with that answer either…"

"She's obviously just doing this on a whim. Now that the concert is over, she's probably off on some aimless vacation by herself. That girl's never stopped to think about the trouble she causes others."
Putting it that way is nothing but an insincere act, but…
By reassuring myself with it, I manage to just barely retain my sanity.
Because I don't want to acknowledge my own responsibility.
To admit that what I did was a fatal mistake. To admit that it had a powerful impact on Kazusa's performance…
That can't be. She is not such a weak-willed person.
She is a genius, inconsiderate and self-centered…
She's not the type of normal girl that would be influenced so easily by an average guy like me.
…That's what I wanted to believe, at least.
…Seriously, what is that idiot doing? She's always been inconsiderate of others.
"I'm always much obliged. My name is Kitahara from Touma Youko Office."
"People get stingy about personal information when they're talking to the media. Maybe he thinks their tongues will loosen if he claims to be affiliated with her…"
"He has a lot of pride about his work, doesn't he? He's turned into a splendid hyena right before our eyes…"
"Yes, yes… is that so!? At the backdoor of the concert hall at that time?"
Ignoring the concern from the seniors holding second and third place of my unreasonableness ranking, I strengthen my grip on my cell phone.
It was a callback from one of the taxi companies I made numerous calls to first thing in the morning.
"And the driver… yes, Muraoka-san… He'll be back at 1 PM? I understand, I'll be there right away!"
Late at night the day before yesterday… there was a taxi that picked up a woman with long black hair near the backdoor of Onjuku Art and Culture Hall.
"I'm heading out! I'm done for today!"
Yet another long battle has begun today.
But unlike yesterday, this time I won't be stuck in a cycle of wasted effort.
However, what awaits me once the problem before me is solved… is something I decide not to think about right now.
"I told you I'm not her ex-boyfriend."
…However, I only felt free from that cycle of wasted effort for only a few hours.
In the end, the moment I thought I'd finally gotten a hold of a thread of hope, it ended up snapping easily in my hands.
The day before yesterday, there was indeed a woman similar to Touma Kazusa riding a taxi, and she was indeed dropped off at the Onjuku Imperial Hotel where Kazusa was supposed to be staying.
However, there was no trace of Kazusa at the hotel, and I couldn't find anyone in the neighborhood who had seen someone that looked like her.
…It was merely the description of the woman that the taxi driver gave me that weighed heavily on my mind.
Apparently she was trying to conceal her voice as she was crying…
"Ah, am I speaking to Hamada-san? It's Kitahara."
In the end, my search returns to the starting point, without any progress.
"After that, did you happen to get any calls from Touma Youko Office…? I see. And you still don't know Youko-san's whereabouts either?"
I begin to be tormented by my fruitless effort, wondering where in the world Kazusa and Youko-san went.
It's starting to get dark. The cold winter night is approaching.
Please, at least be somewhere warm, Kazusa…
After losing the few leads I had, I rummaged through my memories.
All the places where both now and in the past… I recall Kazusa being at.
First I went to Houjou High before closing, checked the classrooms, gymnasium, and Music Room 2. …She had been to those places both a few days ago and many years ago, but she was nowhere to be found.
After that, I checked Suetsugu-chou, Iwazu-chou and Shibata-san's house. …I chose my words carefully when asking the two elders so they wouldn't realize.
Just in case, I went back to Minami-Suetsugu to the apartment next to mine to see if she had returned. I'm not sure if it's a good thing or not that the moving company hadn't been there yet.
And here… is the final fortress… 6-2-12, Iwazu-chou.
I feel dizzy from the overwhelming realization.
Dizzy from the idiocy that made me neglect to search for her here, because I believed what she told me.
Left for years without any maintenance, the fences are covered in ivy.
A single section has been scraped off, and it clearly happened recently.
…There are three spots where ivy has been grazed by having a shoe rub against it.
I put my hands on the top of the fence, and put my foot on the scraped off part.
I knew it, the height of this spot makes it a perfect foothold.
Like that, I raise my body to the top of the fence, and nervously jump down to the other side.
…This goes without saying, I'm intruding on private property. If my company found out about this, I'd certainly be punished.
But right now, I don't have time to worry about breaking the rules.
And then, my reasoning was proven right in a way I never wanted it to be.
When I crossed the overgrown garden, and reached the window facing the living room…
I was met with something that I knew was out of place even with nothing but the moonlight to illuminate.
Broken glass. An unlocked window. Fragments of glass scattered around.
That alone is absurdly thoughtless, impulsive and foolish enough, but there is another idiotic trace of her that outdoes even those things.
On the broken glass are stains of red…
I pressed against the window with all my might, but as if to signify the amount of years it has been left abandoned, it wasn't easy to open.
The first thing I feel on my skin when I enter is a piercing chill that might even be colder than the outside air.
Once, the pleasant Touma residence had been bathed in the sunlight from the windows. Now those are blocked by the overgrown vegetation. Add winter to that, and the temperature gradually decreases.
Forget calling this a "warm place," this is a place cold enough to kill you.
"Kazusa! Answer me! You're here, aren't you? You're here, right!?"
I don't even think about the possibility that someone other than Kazusa might be here, nor do I have any need to.
No one else would try to get inside this hollow, empty house so hard that they'd hurt themselves.
The traces of blood I found on the window continued on the floor this time. They seemed to go from the living room down the hallway.
Not even the moonlight reached that place, so I had no choice but to follow those red stains using the light of my cell phone.
Unlike my restless heart, my feet only moved very slowly.
The unreliable light from my cell phone caused me to lose sight of those red traces, so I had to crawl on the floor and proceed cautiously.
The floor didn't feel that dusty. Perhaps the real estate agent has been cleaning it regularly.
And when I reached the less labyrinth-like hallway, I was guided to my destination slowly but surely.
…In a way, it was as I had expected; it led me to the stairs going down to the studio in the basement.
Darkness completely blocked my vision, and I could no longer tell which direction I was facing. I couldn't even tell if I was moving forward anymore.
By relying on just the memories of the few times I was here, I reached out for the wall to find my way to the door of the studio.
And then… I finally reached my destination.
The place where she… the idiot known as Touma Kazusa is waiting.
It's the basement, which hasn't had any electrical supply for a long time…
Since there is nothing to heat the room with, being here gives me the cold, scary, and lonely sensation of being locked inside a fridge.
Since I can't illuminate the whole of this vast room with such a faint light, I call out to her in the hope of a response.
"You can hear me, can't you!? That's enough already! Stop sulking already and…!?"
Unlike the other rooms, this pitch black room doesn't seem to be empty. I trip on either a cord or the broken remains of some instrument.
Finding a person under these circumstances is near impossible, but I encourage myself with the fact that the space is limited. I once again crawl on the floor, nearly tripping countless times.
I've finally reached my real and true destination.
The biggest idiot in the world, sleeping while leaning against the wall with her arms around her knees…
From the same height as my hands are, I hear Kazusa's breathing.
Kazusa doesn't answer my call, but she is close to me in this darkness…
"Kazusa, Kazusa! Hey, get it together, hey!"
Her body and breath are warm. I can tell that much by just moving a bit closer to her.
Now the piercing cold room from earlier actually feels nice.
I carried Kazusa on my back and left the studio, climbed the steep stairs and made it back to the living room through the labyrinth-like hallways.
Then I gently put Kazusa down. Just like in the basement, I leaned her against a wall.
Her eyes still won't open. Her consciousness won't come back.
Her temperature is higher than I thought when I carried her, which makes me even more restless.
How many times has it been already…?
Once five years ago, when she had multiple sleepless nights in order to ensure our success in the school festival.
Once a few days ago, when she couldn't find her way back home, shivering in the cold rain pouring down on the city.
She's so unfair with the way she always, always tries to act tough but collapses in the end, and I just can't bear that side of her…
When I get on my knees and touch her forehead, I feel sticky sweat along with her heat.
The breaths coming from her slightly opened mouth are as dangerously faint as ever.
The thing that tears at my heart more than anything, is the blackish red coloring the back of her hand.
That part was cut deeply by glass, so even though its surroundings have dried and become black, there is still red liquid spilling out of it.
She probably broke the glass with a stone in her hand, decisively wounding the right hand that has led her to fame…
What she has done can't be described as anything other than unbelievably idiotic, unthinkable coming from someone in her trade.
"You absolute… moron…! What were you thinking…!?"
A drop of liquid resembling sweat falls on her red hand.
A single utterly idiotic teardrop attempted to laugh at her ridiculous recklessness, only to fail.
Those feeble, slender fingers in my hands move a tiny bit from that slight stimulus.
A normal woman's fingers could be described as "white and delicate," but…
Kazusa's fingers have that same whiteness and slenderness, yet at the same time I can feel an overwhelming strength, stiffness and flexibility.
Those delicate yet powerful works of art are now brutally wounded and stained in red.
It's far too unreasonable, far too sad, and far too frustrating to see this.
Before I know it, I taste something metallic in my mouth.
At first, I was just trying to wipe the tears that fell on her.
I was just trying to disinfect her wound. I was just trying to make sure there aren't any glass fragments remaining.
I'm being far too selfish for this to be me wiping away my guilty conscience. I'm being far too rough for this to be me trying to reassure her.
And I lack the resolution for this to be me trying to convey a stronger feeling.
But this still crosses the line I drew myself.
This isn't just me being worried about Kazusa. There is a different feeling I have as I commit this act.
I have to scold her, I have to lecture her… and I have to apologize to her.
But none of those things apply to what I am doing right now. They have nothing to do with my kiss against Kazusa's wound, and Kazusa herself.
Spurred by the sensation of warmth, ticklishness, or pain…
Kazusa's right hand finally starts to properly move as I lick it.
Her arms are still weak, but the strength is returning to them. And her downturned head gradually turns up.
Her closed eyes slowly open, and the moonlight reflects in her eyes.
Amidst the darkness, she blinks three times, and then she slowly focuses on the face she should be sick of seeing by now…
She forcibly pulls away her right hand from mine, and then swings it with an exaggerated motion.
I feel an impact greater than expected on my left cheek, knocking me off balance and forcing me to put my hands on the floor.
Even though her mind is in a haze, she certainly didn't mistake me for some unknown intruder.
"Haruki, Haruki! You, you…! Aaah, ah… Uaaaaaaaah!"
Those eyes look at me with an overbearing light. Her mouth screams the name of none other than me.
She punched me with all her strength in the cheek… with the very right hand that's supposed to be seriously wounded.
"Why, why…? How could you, damn you, Haruki, Haruki… Uaaah… Why!?"
"…I told you to sto…! Stop hitting me. Stop trying to hit me!"
As I'm lying knocked down on the floor, she gets on top of me and this time even swings her left hand at me.
"Why didn't you come!? It was my… my…!"
I'm probably being hit pretty hard, with a strength that one wouldn't expect from a woman's fist.
But right now, I can't afford to feel that pain…
"I told you to stop! Do you have any idea how much your fingers are worth!?"
"…You think saying that will make everything okay!? Cut it out already!"
"Let go of me… Let go of me!"
"Like hell I'll let go of you!"
After grabbing her right wrist, I managed to get a hold of her left wrist as well, robbing her hands of freedom.
…And in exchange for robbing her hands of freedom, I give up the freedom to move my own body.
"Let go of me! Let me hit you!"
"Those hands of yours aren't for hitting people!"
"Are you, are you… telling me that… when you didn't even come to listen to me play…!?"
Kazusa presses her own body against me as I'm lying face up.
Since both of our hands are occupied, we can't separate our bodies.
"I told you to come… to listen… over and over again, didn't I? You promised, didn't you!?"
She twists her legs sticking out of her skirt around my legs.
Her breasts, pushing up against her clothes, press against my chest. They softly lose form, yet still exert pressure on me.
Her exquisite black hair flows down, softly stroking my face.
"Liar! Haruki, you… Haruki, you… Uu-uaa, uaaah…!"
…Are countless wet drops falling from Kazusa's eyes.
"Uaaaah… aaaah…! Uua, uua, uaaaaaaaah! Aaaaaah! Uaaaaah!"
Streaming out along with the deepest lamentations of her heart.
It's surely due to her high fever.
Her abnormal condition has caused her to become unable to control her emotions.
I'm sure that once she calms down, she'll recall this moment as something foolish, and ask herself why she ever got so angry.
"Uh, uaaaah, aaaah, huah, aaaaaaaah, uah, uah, uua! Uuuuuuuuah, haaaa…!"
There really is no reason to get this upset. There's nothing to cause her heart to get so torn up.
I'm not a man capable enough of breaking Kazusa like this…
"Uah… kh, khhh… Uu… You… You're cruel… You're so cruel… Uaah, uahh…!"
It's been ten minutes since then… yet Kazusa's wailing hasn't stopped.
My cheeks, forehead, and my entire face is wet from Kazusa's tears.
"Did you… hate me… that much…? Is it that fun, making me suffer?"
"Of course… not. Of course that's not…!"
…I can't differentiate them from my own anymore.
"I can't… bear that… I don't want to… be hated by you… I don't want to… I don't want that… uuah…!"
Even though it's such a sorrowful scene…
Since both my hands are tied, I can't even stroke Kazusa's head as she cries and shouts.
…Of course, I'm aware that if I stroked her head right now, I'd be doing something I can't undo in so many ways.
Despite that, I loosened my grip on Kazusa's wrists countless times, only to clench my teeth and strengthen my grip again every time.
"Stop it already… Doing this will only hurt you."
"I know that, I already know that! That's why I decided it would be the last time! That's why I swore to never see you again!"
"Yet, yet… even though I desperately tried to give up, you were the one who went and ruined everything!"
She's acting as if the whole world has denied her existence.
"You're the one… who turned me back into this selfish little child!"
As if everything has been destroyed. As if nothing remains for her anymore.
It's like I'm the only one in the world to her…
"Uah… ua, uuuh… S-Stop it… Stop ignoring me."
"I'm not ignoring you… How could I ever do that?"
"I'm not strong like Setsuna is… If you reject me, I won't know what to do…!"
"You were… doing fine for five whole years, weren't you? You forgot about me and did your best, didn't you?"
After five years, the world is supposed to have changed. No, Kazusa is supposed to have changed.
"Like hell I was fine! I was never able to forget…"
And after five years, Kazusa managed to reach the top.
"But you succeeded. You became a world-famous pianist, didn't you?"
High enough that her popularity couldn't be contained in just Japan. High enough for the rest of the world to want Kazusa more than Japan…
"Even that ended two days ago. The facade I desperately tried to keep up was fully exposed. And that's… it's all your fault, Haruki!"
Despite that, just like five years ago, Kazusa doesn't try to associate with the world…
She never got down from the stage at the school festival all this time.
"Why did you appear before me again? Why did you stir me up?"
When we had our reunion in Strasbourg, I wasn't the only one trying to hold back my tears.
"It was my job. Once I graduated university, I got a job at a publishing company. Even when you disappeared, I tried to do my best…"
"…Like I care about your effort. You undid everything because you keep doing unnecessary things."
"You broke the sturdy wall… holding back the feelings I was desperately trying to repress."
That goes for when I was giving first aid to her foot, and when I was interviewing her too…
"No matter how much I said the right things, you made it so that my body and my heart weren't able to follow along at all…"
I wore an expression that I couldn't show Kazusa, and because of that, I couldn't see what expression Kazusa had.
"Why did you accept being with me?"
When Kazusa moved in next to me, I wasn't the only one with an unconcealable happiness behind my confusion.
"Why did you keep leading me on? Why did you… act like you don't hate me?"
"If you don't hate me, then don't mess with my heart! Don't get my hopes up, and don't delude me into thinking that I'll be able to reach you if only I stretch out my hand…"
Even when she was defenselessly sleeping in front of me. Even on the way back from Shibata-san's house.
Even when time stopped for a single moment in the dusk-colored Music Room 2…
"Yet, you always run away at the very end… There is no way I can endure such painful and agonizing torture, is there…?"
I was unable to see the feelings Kazusa was hiding, because I was too desperate to hide my own wavering feelings.
"Why didn't you come to listen to my piano…?"
When the curtains were raised in the concert hall…
I was the only one who ran away.
"Even though the only reason I came back was to play for you… Even though I was supposed to finally give up by showing you the last, and the absolute best performance…"
Kazusa put her soul into her performance. And yet when she was looking for me in the audience seats…
"But you didn't come, and I ended up showing the absolute worst performance. This time, I have truly lost everything."
I "wanted to pretend" that I never noticed Kazusa's all too pure and simple feelings. I disappeared from her side, and out of her line of sight.
"Let go of me… I'll destroy everything. You, me… these two hands."
She lamented, she cried, she screamed, and she grumbled…
After letting her feelings erupt for another while, Kazusa reasserts strength in her body.
Her eyes hold a resentful glint. Her hands hold weapons ready to exact revenge.
"Let go of me… If you don't… I'll kiss you."
And her breath… holds her burning, ever-fervent feelings.
Kazusa's sense of reason has completely collapsed.
"If you're not going to move… I'll steal you away for real, okay?"
She's laying bare just how much she hates and detests me…
Yet her words still express her longing for me, and she continues waiting for my response, no matter how long it will take.
"I've been regretting it for five years."
The sweet expression she's making as she appears to have given up on thinking stirs up my desires in a maddening frenzy.
"I… abandoned you, you know? I abandoned you five years ago, and two days ago. Don't you know that all I've ever done is make you cry?"
But even so… these feelings of hers are wrong. Even Kazusa herself knows that she's making an absolutely terrible mistake.
"I thought that I'd come to hate you one day…"
"I thought that I'd look back, and wonder why I was ever stupid enough to fall in love with a guy like you…"
"Someone who's unaccommodating, annoying, has bad taste, always irritates people when he's trying to be considerate… Someone who's not even popular yet has a girlfriend who's way beyond his league."
"I saw no value nor reason to continue longing for you, so I would finally get tired and see it all as ridiculous. Then I'll be able to look back at everything like a nostalgic story to laugh at…"
"That's what I dreamed of, at least…"
The ideal future you have always dreamed of is one where you hate and have forgotten me…
Reality can't possibly be different from that.
"That's just what you've led yourself to believe."
"That's just something you've learned to think. You were all by yourself back then, so…"
"You're just being delirious. Let's get out of here and rest, okay?"
"I'm a traitor, aren't I? All I've done is hurt you."
"I never want to let you go…"
"You let me go for five whole years! What are you saying after all this time?"
There is no longer anything but me reflected in Kazusa's eyes.
She's close enough for our noses to touch… The same distance as that time in Music Room 2.
Kazusa's tears have dried up, but my cheeks are still wet.
"That's right, you're in the wrong… It's your fault, Haruki…"
Kazusa is no longer reflecting on her mistake.
"So make amends for it. Don't run away anymore."
She's projecting nothing but a direct and single-hearted passion to my eyes.
"What am I… What am I supposed to do?"
Her wet lips open, and she blows an incredibly warm breath at me.
"This moment alone is enough… All you have to do is love me for this moment alone."
But this wasn't what I expected.
I don't mean that Kazusa's breath isn't warm; rather, something even warmer has made its way to me.
I'll burn myself if I accept them. The flames of her passion might even end up scorching my entire body.
"It doesn't matter if you don't want to, or don't have any interest… as long as you make love to me right now."
If I accept Kazusa here, I won't be able to tell why I ran away in the first place.
I won't be able to know why I sought out Setsuna…
"If you dislike it that much… If you want to run away from me as far as possible…"
But the contradiction has been present since long ago.
"If you don't want it, if you have no interest, you should have just left me be."
I can no longer reason that I did it because of my job, because I was simply worried or because we're friends; after all, those feelings just aren't correct.
"Then you wouldn't be in this situation with me either."
"Do you think… I'd be capable of something like that?"
Because the moment I found Kazusa…
"I've never once come to hate you… and I've never once lost interest in you."
A powerful feeling other than relief doubtlessly welled up inside of me.
When I stroked her cheeks, grabbed her hand and licked her wound, the feelings I held in those moments were unshakeable.
The pitch in Kazusa's voice conspicuously goes up.
Just as I thought, her excited breathing further heats up my cheeks and my feelings.
"After all, I'll be able to interpret that as… you've always loved me, and you still love me."
"Is it okay for you to be saying that…?"
That's why I'm sure that my excited breathing is also heating up Kazusa's cheeks, and her feelings…
"…But this is the only thing I can't lie about, so what choice do I have?"
Like that, we both come close to crossing the line into a vicious cycle, where our burning feelings only burn more and more powerful.
I can't stand any more than this. I won't be able to turn back.
It would be the point of no return.
"Just now is enough. All you have to do is love me like you did five years ago…"
And in an attempt to block my escape…
"I'll give up on you truly loving me. That privilege belongs to Setsuna. …But I want you to give me your fake love."
…And without any hesitation, Kazusa says something that she can never take back.
"Only until I leave Japan… Until the end of winter is enough."
What she desires is an imitation.
Despite her claim that it would be the same as what we had five years ago, it's something completely different. She wants us to connect in body alone.
"Embrace me. Desire me. Whisper sweet words to me…"
It would be a fake love. A self-aggrandizing love. Love that would only deceive ourselves…
"Make me lose myself. …Deceive me until the very end, okay?"
It's an option that would hurt everyone equally despite the fact that she doesn't want to hurt anyone. An option that's deplorable, realistic, yet so enticing…
1. I let go of her hands.
Kazusa's breath touches only my right cheek.
Because I turned to the side. Because I averted my gaze away from Kazusa.
Because I've shown Kazusa that I can't accept her.
"You said that you don't hate me, didn't you?"
"No… I said that I love you."
"You acknowledged that it's your fault, right?"
"Five years ago, last year, the day before yesterday… it was all my fault."
She pushed me down, pleaded for us to kiss, and sought a relationship built on a purely physical connection…
She says she desires such extreme things, and sets them up to happen. Not only that, her appearance, social standing, and attitude all point to her being an eccentric…
I know that she'll get cold feet and hesitate right at the very end. I know that she's so timid that it's actually adorable.
I know that so well that it makes me want to cry.
"What's the problem…? I just told you that you can choose Setsuna…! What else could you want!?"
Kazusa's eyes turn wet once again just as soon as her tears have dried up.
Her fresh teardrops fall on my right cheek, and my own tears drip from the corners of my eyes.
I can see Setsuna's smile when I close my eyes.
"There is no point in saying something so obvious."
I can see her innocent, mischievous smile from five years ago. I can see her miserable smile from two years ago that showed how tired she was of waiting.
"I love Setsuna more than anyone in the world…"
"I told you that you can still love Setsuna. She can still be the one you love most…"
I can see the genuine smile she lets out in the present day that expresses the faith she has in me.
"I love Setsuna. I don't want to betray her anymore."
"This isn't betrayal. This won't count as a betrayal… No one will become unhappy because of it…"
I can see the most precious thing in the world. I can see the very thing I've desired all this time right in front of me.
"I just said that I know! Stop using that word! Stop bringing up that name!"
Something… worth throwing away everything else for…
"Setsuna is the only one for me… Setsuna is the only one I have now…!"
It's right there, behind the person who "used to be" the most precious person to me…
"Shut up, shut up, shut up! S-S-Stop it… Stop it… Uu, uaah, aaaaaah…!"
My entire body starts to tremble.
