I'm not sure if I'm the one trembling or if it's just Kazusa's trembling that's being transmitted to me. Or it could very well be both.
It's not something that I need to know anymore. …I know that I've made up my mind now.
"I can't say that I love you as a lie… I can't separate my heart from it."
I can't run away, or even deceive her anymore.
"This winter is all I need. If you just tell me that you love me for a little bit…"
"If I say that I love you, you'll become the most precious person in the world to me! If I make love to you, I won't ever be able to let you go!"
Back when I put the two of them side by side in my mind, when we were connected once again.
I found myself afraid of delving deeper into my feelings. Afraid of looking at the direction they were facing.
"It won't end as a lie. It won't be able to end once winter is over."
"That's why I can't do what I did five years ago. I can't make love to you knowing full well we're going to separate."
I can tell that Kazusa is gazing at me more intensely than she was earlier.
"I can't experience a love that won't hurt anyone anymore. I can only choose who I have to hurt."
Not because of her breaths or the sensation of her tears, but from a dwelling heat in my body.
"That's why I… can't accept you right now… I'm sorry."
"Could it, could it mean that… even if it's the tiniest hope…"
"Don't say it! That could never happen!"
The reason I instinctively raised my voice is because she proposed a possibility that would be far too painful.
She proposed the possibility of a preposterous choice.
She proposed a possibility that defies common sense, one that would only serve to make even me delirious.
"No way… What was I just trying to say? How could I say something so unthinkable…?"
Even Kazusa shrinks upon realizing that she had stumbled upon that forbidden, evil option…
"That's enough, stop it. I don't want to think anymore today."
"You were just being delirious, and I just happened to lose my composure. Let's just… leave it at that…"
My entire body starts to tremble.
I'm not sure if I'm the one trembling, or if it's just Kazusa's trembling that's being transmitted to me. Or it could very well be both.
It's not something that I want to think about anymore. I don't want to think about anything or anyone.
I don't want to make a decision yet.
"The taxi… will be here in ten minutes."
I let go of her hands, and she moved away.
We both sat against the wall, and then brought ourselves close to each other again.
We don't hold each other's shoulders, and we don't hold hands.
Kazusa rests her head on my shoulder, and continues her usual feverish breaths.
But I don't hold her anywhere. I don't warm Kazusa up.
Our screams and lamentations are over. In the darkness illuminated by the moonlight, the room returns to the usual quiet…
"If… if by any chance, I return to Japan not to play a concert, but to simply run away…"
"If by any chance, I fail even as a pianist, fall to ruin, and come back in despair…"
"Would you pity me, and embrace me then?"
"Would you kiss me out of sympathy…?"
Kazusa's faint murmurs are sucked in by the vast room.
"That will never happen… so it's pointless to think about it."
A true silence settled between us.
"She fell down some stairs right after the concert…"
"A-And what about the additional concert? N-No, I should ask about the injury first."
"She cut herself on the back of her right hand and sprained her left wrist. Though it looks like there's nothing wrong with the bones in either hand."
As Hamada-san's face turns pale right in front of me, I have no choice but to accept whatever comes my way, all while being tormented by numerous painful thoughts.
"…What about the additional concert? It's in a month. Will she be alright?"
"Her wounds will probably have healed by then, though I can't say she'll be able to play in the best condition…"
"I-I see… You're right. Imagine a pianist who can't even practice…"
The few lies I'm telling and the many secrets I'm keeping… weigh heavily on my heart.
"Even then, why didn't I get a call about this until now…?"
"I'm not blaming you. I'm talking about the Touma Office. We had an agreement that we'd keep close contact."
After all, who could possibly imagine the improbable truth of the matterーthat it's actually all my fault that all this happened?
Would he even understand if I explained it to him?
"Apparently, they felt guilty about causing you trouble, so they planned on keeping quiet until they could take the bandage off."
"That would only cause more trouble! What are they thinking?"
"I keep telling you that I don't mean you! Ah, no, I suppose I can understand why you'd think I was directing it at you."
That's why I can only lie to everyone around us right now.
As for my persuasiveness, and the situation around us…
…And my understanding of Kazusa's feelings, I remain unable to grasp them fully yet.
"Anyway, go report this to Ensemble's chief editor first. It seems they couldn't get in touch with Touma Youko either."
Because I didn't know what excuse to tell her… when I couldn't protect, nor even reject Kazusa.
"Well then, it's about time for my coverage."
"Are you going to check up on Touma Kazusa?"
"Should I come along? I'll probably need to brief you about the coverage going forward."
"No… It seems she doesn't want to meet outsiders right now."
"I see… Then tell her to get better for me."
"I will… Now, if you'll excuse me."
"She doesn't want to meet outsiders right now, huh?"
"You just implied you're not an outsider, you know…"
I manage to breathe a sigh of relief, but inside my heart, I still feel out of breath.
No matter how many pointless apologies I made, no one could possibly have comprehended them, and the feeling of guilt within me never eased up.
I'm sorry. I'm really sorry, Hamada-san.
I never knew she was this lacking in professionalism. I never knew she had become more of an amateur than ever before.
…I never knew she was so frail that she'd become unable to play all because of a single guy.
The scent of spicy food fills the room.
…Of course, this is the third day in a row I'm eating curry, so I can't bring myself to get excited about the stimulating fragrance.
So while boiling the mild curry, I start cutting some vegetables I happen to have in the fridge.
The light on my rice cooker indicates that it has finished cooking. All that's left is to put it onto a plate, then the belated dinner will be finished.
As I leave the movements of my hands to muscle memory, and my thoughts about the present decrease, my mind insists on recalling the memories of last night.
The Touma residence, after five years.
Kazusa, sitting all alone with her arms around her knees, down in the studio where we have so many memories together.
Even though that place wasn't supposed to be where she belonged, that place was all she had left at the time.
Compared to the world that knows and wants her, I was in shock at how confined the world she knows and wants is in comparison.
She told me her true feelings for the first time since our reunion.
She said that she's continued having feelings for me these past five years…
I couldn't bring myself to accept the painful and miserable truth about her feelings, even if they were very elating to me.
I already have Setsuna, after all, which is why the only option for us is to break apart.

We hurt each other so deeply that day that we couldn't maintain our relationship as neighbors anymore, which was already hanging on a thin thread… No, it's perhaps more accurate to say we were living together.
That's why Kazusa's still in this apartment…
"…Wake up already and eat something. Enough pretending to be asleep already."
…Kazusa's still in this apartment despite everything that's happened.
She hasn't given up on being my neighbor. I guess it's better to say that I was the one who refused to let her go.
"You didn't even eat lunch, right? Your temperature is down too. I bet you can get up just fine."
After all, there's no way I could let her go.
She had a fever. Both of her hands are injured.
…Not to mention the fact that I can't get in touch with Youko-san. She would never go to the hospital by herself either.
So no matter how little sense this all makes, I have no choice but to do something right now.
"You can't stay this way forever. This goes not only for your food, but with how you're recuperating from your injury, too…"
Even if that entails the fact that ever since I got home… I've been measuring her temperature with my hands, wiping off her sweat, and gazing intently at her face.
Regardless, Kazusa has kept her eyes stubbornly closed, seemingly asleep.
I knew from the beginning that she was awake all along.
Because I could feel Kazusa's gaze every time I turned away from herーpainfully so.
"I confessed my feelings to you, you know? …And got completely rejected, you know?"
In complete contrast to the cries coming from the innermost depths of her heart back then, the first thing Kazusa says in over a day is little more than a vigorless murmur.
"Is having the person who rejected me look after me not anything but torture?"
She's desperately trying to prevent any anger or sadness from being infused in her voice…
But those involuntary feelings are conveyed clearly through the shaking of her voice.
"Don't look at me… Don't look at me with gentle eyes, Haruki. Stop pitying me…"
"If you don't want me to look after you, then get up. Stand up by yourself…"
"Will you go away if I do that? Will you disappear from my sight for all eternity?"
"…That's not what I want. I'd never want that."
"Then eat. Let me change your bandage… Let me take care of you."
"…I don't want that either. I absolutely don't want that right now."
"Go home. Leave my apartment. I'm begging you, leave me alone."
"But what about food and your medical treatment…? I also want to measure your body temperature…"
"You're annoying, you really are annoying… Give me a break already…!"
…However, when she tried to stop her emotions from appearing in her voice was only the beginning.
Before long, countless painful feelings seeped into that faint voice, stabbing at me.
The thing that was hiding them was Kazusa's kindness. The thing that exposed them was my inability to read the atmosphere.
I returned to my room, turned off the light and put myself under the bedsheets, but that didn't mean I could fall asleep.
From what I felt from her forehead, her temperature was down.
From what I can judge from treating her hands, her right hand hasn't experienced any suppuration, and the sprain on her left hand doesn't seem to be too serious either.
I'm still a bit nervous about her additional concert a month from now, but as far as her being able to continue playing the piano is concerned, there should be nothing to worry about.
…At least, as far as her physical health is concerned.
As I repeatedly turn and toss in bed, I feel an instinctive desire well up in me apart from the desire to sleep.
Come to think of it, I didn't eat anything either. I wonder when all that curry is ever going to be fully eaten.
But going over to the other apartment now at 3 AM to fetch the saucepan would be problematic, both on a personal and a practical level.
I curl up into a ball and hold my empty stomach, then I put the sheet over my head and forcibly close my eyes.
Both the curry and our discussion will have to wait until tomorrow.
Her apartment wasn't closed with a chain today. She created a situation where only I can enter since I have a key.
That isn't entirely safe from a security standpoint, but right now I'm more happy that she has opened up the door to her heart a little.
Tomorrow morning, I'll see if curry makes a good breakfast or not, so for now, I will make myself comfortable and let my consciousness fade…
…It seems I won't get to do that quite yet.
It's been an hour since I left Kazusa's room as she was muttering in sadness.
And now, before me as I once again appear in this room, lies a pitiful scene that makes me astonished that this is even the same place.
"You just had to leave this thing in my room!"
Forget curry-stained clothes, even her hair is covered in thick curry.
The pot, the plate, and their contents are all on the floor. The room is filled with the smell of three-day-old mild curry.
"It'll take a long time until the smell disappears…"
"The room smelt like this even before I dropped it."
"Why would you… try to throw all this away?"
"…As if… As if I'd do something so wasteful!"
"The room started smelling… so I started to get more and more hungry…"
From what I felt from her forehead, her temperature was down.
So there would be nothing strange about her appetite returning to her. In fact, that would be a good thing.
"That's why I, uh… thought about bringing the saucepan to the table."
…Though, I would have been happier if she understood the state her hands are in.
"Why would you make it so thick…? You keep saying that everything's fine, but your actions are full of holes!"
"Aah, fine, fine. Let me clean this up for now, so go ahead and take a bath. Wash your body and change your clothes…"
Saying that, Kazusa shows me her originally white, but now yellowed bandage with a spiteful glare.
"That's why I keep saying your words are full of holes…"
"Hey, are you… are you really sure it's okay?"
"What are you saying now? It's not a matter if it's okay or not. There is no other choice, is there?"
"I'm sure I'll catch a glimpse. You won't be able to conceal it all, you know?"
"It's not like I plan on concealing anything."
"That would actually be problematic for me…"
"Are you that much against seeing me…?"
"It'll be problematic because I do want to…"
"You already saw all of me five years ago. It's too late now."
"Hurry up. Even the bathroom will stink of curry soon."
I put three times as much shampoo as usual in my hands, and rub it against the spicy black hair in front of me.
Obviously, I can't work on her hair like a hairstylist with my eyes either closed or averted. In other words, Kazusa's white back is right before my…
"You can do it a bit more roughly. It's not like you're usually being this considerate."
Inside the bathroom, where everything we say comes with an echo, the only sound that can be heard is that of my finger rubbing against her hair.
If someone who knew either of us saw this, they'd certainly faint at the sight.
The only thing Kazusa is wearing are the bandages on both her hands.
…And since both her hands are incapable right now, I had to undress her with the exception of her underwear.
Kazusa never laughed at me as I desperately tried to close and avert my eyes in the dressing room, but she made sure to make things as difficult for me as possible.
"In a sense, this could be my lucky break."
"I hadn't taken a bath in two days, so both my hair and my skin were starting to feel sticky."
Am I supposed to wash her there too?
"I didn't want you to see me in that gross state… This was just as well."
Is that why she never faced me all day?
Does that mean that she'll show me everything as long as she looks good? And that she'll even allow me to wash her?
Is she more ashamed about having me know that her skin is dirty than she is about having her skin exposed in the first place?
And does that mean that in your eyes, I'm…
"I was talking about my head. What are you getting so flustered about?"
"You coward… no, perhaps you simply hate me."
"Yeah… stick with that pressure. Scrub a little bit more."
My fingers are covered in a layer of Kazusa's black hair. They twine around me as if binding me to her.
I know that I'm just overthinking it. I know that I'm making a large leap in logic.
And I can't deny the possibility that it's a desire buried deep in my heart…
"This moment alone is enough… All you have to do is love me for this moment alone."
"Embrace me. Desire me. Whisper sweet words to me…"
Far too much happened for me to forget, not to mention the intensity of what happened…
"That was all nonsense. I was being delirious."
Those words were powerful enough for me to remember them for a lifetime. Telling me to forget them in a mere two days would be unbearable.
Hearing the vague response I made at the end of my anguish…
"You don't understand… You don't understand at all."
…There is no way Kazusa would overlook it.
"I would never lie during a delirium… and I could never make up nonsense during one…"
Because she's an idiot who etches every word, and every action of mine into her mind.
"Don't let my bluff slip by. Don't take it at face value… It makes me want to cry."
While murmuring her complaints, Kazusa's voice had already grown tearful.
The white shoulders in front of me start to shake, but I'm not allowed to put my hands on them.
"I was rejected, I was discarded, yet I'm still this reliant on you. I'm so overbearing, aren't I? Enough to make you wish I was dead, right?"
"Being annoying and overbearing is my specialty, isn't it? You're ten years too early to surpass me in that regard."
"Don't pick a half-baked number like that. Ten years is nothing at all."
These past five years apart might as well not have happened… We might actually be able to overcome ten years with ease.
After washing Kazusa's hair, I used up more courage and self-restraint than ever before as I washed her body.

The smooth curves and sudden changes in elevation I felt through the sponge challenged my restraint a great deal, but I managed to close both my eyes and my mind, and made it through without an incident.
"I didn't have enough time or ingredients, so I made some salted onigiri. I'm sure you'll… want to complain, but hold back on that."
Once we got out of the bath, I had to clean up the disastrous state of the room, and deal with the root behind it all.
To put it more specifically, cleaning up the floor, and preparing a late-night snack for Kazusa…
"It'll get a bit noisy in here, but hold back your complaints about that too. You don't want to live in a room filled with curry, do you?"
"Ah, leave two for me if you can. I'll eat them once I'm done cleaning up."
I clean up the pieces of the shattered plate, wipe the curry using a kitchen towel, and then I use a cleaning agent to try to wipe the stains away.
When I turn on the ventilation fan and open the window a bit, the whole room is filled with the cold winter air, but right now there is no choice but to bear that.
"You know… If you're hungry, just call for me."
"I thought that it'd be fine, since all I had to do was to heat it."
"Sure, if you hadn't injured both your hands."
As both the plate and the curry are quickly picked up and wiped away, the floor returns to its usual pretty state.
"You're useless even under normal circumstances, so right now you're on par with an infant. You should at least be aware of that."
"Waking people up in the middle of the night is what I'd expect of a newborn infant."
"It's not like I did it on purpose…"
"Stop whining and eat already. Aren't you hungry?"
I wipe it one last time with kitchen paper and spray deodorant around the whole room, which marks the end of my temporary emergency measures.
In truth, I want to pull out the vacuum cleaner too, but it's the middle of the night, so I'll have to do that tomorrow.
"…What's the matter? Are you going to tell me that you can't eat without a side dish?"
I glance toward Kazusa as I wipe the floor, and see that she hasn't eaten a single one of the onigiri on her plate.
"I want to change your bandage, so I'd appreciate it if you got this over with quickly…"
And then, as if ignoring my complaint, Kazusa reacts in the usual way… by turning in the other direction.
"I'm sorry for comparing you to an infant… is that good enough?"
She's sulking again. Seriously, what a pain.
"You were hungry enough to spill a whole saucepan of curry, right? Hurry up and eat and then go to sleep."
"I didn't spill it on purpose. And it's not like I don't want to eat."
"I… I can't eat with these hands."
"Can't you just eat with your left hand? The wrist is the only part that's bandaged there."
For some reason, that really made her angry…
"Weren't you the one who told me to not use my hands, Haruki? All I'm doing is abiding by that order."
"But something as light as an onigiri should be…"
"Either way, I'm not doing it. I can't be careless with my hands, of all things."
"Had you had that mindset last night, I wouldn't need to be so…!?"
It seems that made her even angrier.
…As usual, the intensity of her glare is leagues above anyone else's.
"Now listen here… why do you have to be so selfish now of all times? Just earlier you were trying to eat curry all by yourself."
"Just earlier I was trying to eat curry by myself, and that decision ended up being completely unsuccessful."
And her stubbornness is leagues above anyone else's as well.
But for the most part, when she picks up that attitude…
"What is it? Are you telling me you won't eat unless I feed you?"
In truth, it's not like she's… not angry, but there's a more prominent feeling within her too…
That's why she's looking at me with upturned eyes right now.
"Didn't you say so yourself? You said I'm on par with an infant with the way I am now."
"You told me to be aware of that. You told me to call you in case anything happened…"
"No, but… I made sure that even you could eat this properly…"
"That's enough! I'm going to sleep! And I'm going to starve to death!"
And then her expression shifts to a second, different one. …Something's pooling in her upturned eyes.
"Tell me to get it together. Tell me that you can't be bothered to watch over me anymore."
And immediately afterward, she lets out her third expression… and what was pooling in her eyes is now falling to the floor.
It's staining the floor that I just cleaned up.
"Tell me you're going to abandon me… Say it right to my face."
"Just like what you did last night."
When things come to this, I have no way of fighting back.
In the right hand is a half-eaten onigiri. In the left hand is a half-empty cup of tea.
…And those hands, of course, belong to me.
"Then go ahead and eat. I never told you to give me everything."
With my hands occupied like this, I can't eat my own portion…
But nothing can be done about that. I have no choice but to become Kazusa's hands, for now…
"It's salty. Are you trying to kill me with high blood pressure?"
"High blood pressure isn't a direct cause of death. If you're going to berate me correctly, then name the diseases that come from high blood pressure, such as cerebral hemorrhage, and heart attacks."
"Your sophistry is so predictable. You're such a bore."
Everything about this is so predictable, that my heart can't endure it.
"On top of being a bore, you're an idiot, a massive idiot. You're still giving food to the dog you abandoned…"
"If you do that, I'll inadvertently start liking you more. What are you thinking, you…!"
I wonder if the salty taste is caused by the salt alone…?
"But you said you weren't able to eat…"
"It's only natural for a dog to open its mouth. The owner has to… discipline it, doesn't he?"
You've never been my pet. And you've never been mine, not even once.
…If I tell her of those feelings within me, I'm sure they'll be outdone by Kazusa's much more powerful feelings.
That's why I can only distract her by passing the time in a peaceful way right now.
Without any conclusions, without any resolve. Still loving her, and still unable to love her…
That's why, right now, I grab the last onigiri just as Kazusa urges me to.
…So that we can divide it and eat it together, just like the last one that disappeared into my mouth.
Actually, it hasn't been that long for me to write that.
But I get the feeling that it's been a long time since I last talked to Setsuna like this.
"I'm sorry. The situation right now is terrible."
"I didn't make it in time for the concert."
"I managed to meet Kazusa last night, but obviously, she didn't forgive me."
"I had a fight with Kazusa. Thanks to that, Kazusa hurt her hand."
"The injury itself isn't anything big. She'll make it in time for the additional concert, but she'll be unable to do anything by herself for a while."
"That's why I'm next to Kazusa right now. I'm taking care of her."
"She hurt herself because of me, and we're still working with each other. This is both my duty and my responsibility."
…I'm astonished at what I've written and how it shows how I'm trying to run away.
The details are far too lacking. And I've only bothered to write about how I don't want to talk to Setsuna.
Setsuna can obviously see through all my excuses.
"I'm sorry for worrying you up until now. And I'm sorry for all the worry I'll be causing you from now on."
She knows that Kazusa didn't forgive me; she also knows that Kazusa hasn't given up on me.
"But right now, giving Kazusa peace of mind and talking to her is my top priority."
Setsuna knows that time didn't solve anything. She knows that everything turned out exactly how she expected it to.
That pain isn't the only thing I'm dealing with… but that I'm also feeling comfortable with Kazusa.
"I'll send you a text tomorrow. Good night."
I won't look forward to a reply. Because if what Setsuna said is true, she won't send me anything.
It's not that she's not angry. It's not like she doesn't feel betrayed.
But there's one thing I can't keep on doing anymore: I can't hide any further betrayals… I can't hide the fact that my heart's wavering.
I can't tell her about my feelings honestly, but I don't want to say nothing to her either.
I want Setsuna to see through me. I want her to doubt me.
Because I want to see Setsuna.
Good night, Setsuna. And… good night, Kazusa.
Even if I fall asleep now, I won't get more than an hour's worth of sleep. But I'll sleep anyway.
After all, I finally feel like I can fall asleep now. Because by being with Kazusa, my heart was put at ease.
"Can't anything be done? …Can you not even call her?"
"No, like I said, I can't answer what I don't know just because you keep asking…"
It's almost been a week since the concert…
Ever since that day, I've been unable to find anyone who can tell me where Touma Youko is, no matter how dependable the source is… Not even her own company.
"I promise I won't cause any trouble. If you tell your company president that I'm Kitahara from Kaiousha, I'm sure she'll have no issue."
"Listen here, Kitahara-san… Since I've already gone over this with you countless times, I've been made plenty aware that you're someone trustworthy."
"However, not even I can get in touch with Touma at the moment. I'm in a real bind, as embarrassing as it is to admit…"
Judging from what this employee is saying, something like this would concern the survival of the very company, but I can't sense any nervousness from her tone.
That's why I'm not sure if her answer is true, or if it's some organized plan they're all in on.
"Yes, I'm truly sorry, but that's how it is…"
Is she aware of the state her precious daughter is in or how much she needs her mother right now?
Or perhaps she thinks that everything will be fine as long as she leaves everything to me. Does she still have that kind of careless attitude?
Even when the situation has changed so drastically…?
"I'm sorry for not being able to help…"
"No, it's not your fault… Kazusa-san wanted me to tell you that she'd love to see her mother, but I suppose that's impossible."
That's a shame, really… I hoped to get through this without resorting to dirty tactics.
"Well then, if you'll excuse me. If you ever do get a call from your company president, direct her to Kitahara for me…"
"Wait I said! No, don't hang up! …Uh, I mean, please wait."
"…But I wouldn't want to bother you any further."
"Ah, no, I have a question for you this time…"
"Ah, could it be about the article inspection at Ensemble? In that case, you can do so at the end of the week…"
"…Did you get in contact with Touma Kazusa from our company? When?"
"Eh, ah, is there a problem with me contacting her directly? But when I first met her, she said…"
"No, no, no! That's not what I meant! …Do you know where she is?"
"Huh? That's strange… I swear she just came back to her residence."
"W-Where is she staying? Is she alright? How are her injuries?"
"…How come you don't know that? I thought you were in contact with her, or am I wrong?"
While they're perfectly willing to acknowledge Touma Youko as missing, they're reacting differently to the more significant disappearance of Touma Kazusa.
"You see, Kitahara-san… The truth is, I'm in a bind."
In other words, their lackluster reaction toward the other missing person, Touma Youko, suggests…
"…If you get to contact our company president, we get to contact Touma Kazusa. Am I getting this right?"
"I heard, Kitahara-kun! Apparently you're doing the special issue for Ensemble!?"
After finishing a task that may or may not be related to my actual work, I am greeted by an onlooker by the name of Suzuki-san, who was waiting for me to finish the call.
"The ones making it are the professionals at the editing department. I'm more or less just helping out."
"Eeh, but from what I've heard, you're making it all by yourself. You're writing the articles, taking the pictures, compiling it, printing it and selling it…"
"Do you take me for someone who's self-employed…?"
However, I can't say that I don't feel somewhat unsettled by the fact that I'm in charge of over half of this project.
This certainly is outside the normal process of a major publisher. More like an idea a minor publisher would come up with…
"The workload will be high, that's all. The professionals at the editing department will follow me up on the basics, and the chief editor will supervise the whole thing…"
"But still, you know what this means."
"You're in your first year, yet your name will appear first on the end credits!"
"No one pays attention to that part…"
"What are you talking about!? Macchan is in a state of shock! He's in his third year, yet he's never risen above third place, you know?"
"You've never risen above second place either, have you, Suzuki-san!?"
"Please don't rub it in right in front of him…"
"Eeh, but I'd be talking behind his back if he's not around. I hate people who do that."
"That doesn't mean that I enjoy having you bully me while I'm right in front of you…"
The Touma Kazusa special issue that was originally supposed to be Ensemble's main article…
But at some point, it turned into a special issue boasting over 100 pages.
Even though I'm receiving help from the professionals, this is pretty much a magazine of its own. Though it's worth celebrating because this is the first big project I've taken part in.
The deadline is the end of February. The release will be in the beginning of March. A rather tight deadline established in order to not miss out on the Touma Kazusa craze.
And right now, the woman on the cover is making fun of me right to my face.
She made me wash her face and body just earlier, then she described the curry I made again for her as "terrible after all." And right now, she's making me change her bandages.
"To think that the first book you'll write is going to be a special number on me."
"The only reason they gave me this job was because I happened to be a former classmate of Touma Kazusa."
The swelling on her left hand is mostly gone, so I just left her wrist supporter on. Now I'm disinfecting the wound on her right hand.
"The reason they made me a regular employee from a part-timer in the first place was because of the article I wrote about your runner-up victory in the international contest."
"Then be more gentle yourself. Every movement you make stings."
"Bear with it. You did this to yourself."
She relies on me for everything, yet her attitude goes beyond just complaining.
The spoiled Kazusa is back. The selfish Kazusa is back… Her vigor has come back to life.
"What a cruel remark. You're talking to your benefactor."
"From what I just heard, all your successes in your career are undoubtedly due to me, right?"
"That's wrong. You were just the catalyst."
"So are you going to stand here and say that your employment in that publishing company, and your pretension of being an editor is all due to your own ability?"
"That's wrong too… The reason I made it so far up is due to a certain person."
Feeling happy that Kazusa is starting to go back to normal, I counter her complaints like usual.

"When I was a part-timer, there was this senior who watched over me. That senior gave me the task of writing the article about you, and they were the one who recommended me to the editing department."
And as I do that, I begin to talk about myself.
"That senior was still young yet so talented, and strict too…"
…Come to think of it, in the past, didn't Kazusa call me annoying because of this habit?
"Not to mention cool and courageous… and even incredibly beautiful too."
"She's now working at a subsidiary in the USA. There's a rumor that she'll become the chief editor and return eventually."
If I remember correctly, the thing that annoyed her the most was…
"Don't… pass it off as a joke."
Thinking back, maybe that really was the reason…
When I was talking about myself, there was a moment where Kazusa looked particularly annoyed.
"How do you expect me to remain calm, when you're making me listen to a story about a woman I don't know…?"
"Anyway, I'd just like to have you listen to her sing just once… I'm sure that would change your mind."
That was when I talked about Setsuna… a girl she didn't know back then.
"Come to think of it… the way she spoke and the way she carried herself was a bit similar to you."
"Did you like her because she was like me?"
Kazusa must've felt conscious about me pretty early on… right?
"I did indeed like her, but that's not because she was like you, you know…"
"…Don't strain your hands. What if your wound opens?"
And then, with her hand free from her bandages for the first time in a while, she comes at my hand with her nails.
"Let go of me… I can't wrap the bandage like this."
It's not just her nails. Even her fingertips feel hard as rock. This part of her body alone is completely lacking in femininity…
But that's precisely why they're so precious. I have no choice but to watch those fingertips dig into the back of my hand.
"The wound will become infected, you know? It'll fester, and pus will gush out of your wrist."
"Whatever, I'll deal with it when it happens."
No matter how much I joke around, Kazusa will only respond in dead seriousness right now.
This situation is almost identical to the time of our reunion, but Kazusa is almost like a completely different person from back then.
…Perhaps in a sense, she has transformed into the real Touma Kazusa.
"How do you plan on making a living without the tools of your trade?"
"That has nothing to do with you, now does it?"
"Haah… I never thought you were really this stupid."
That's why I have no choice but to respond to her in a tasteless, and ugly manner.
"Of course I do. These two hands of yours don't belong to only you anymore…"
"What if I said that… there's something more important to me than these hands?"
Because her attitude is so half-assed, I have no choice but to accept any fastballs she throws at me.
My only response was that my heart skipped a beat and it was difficult for me to breathe.
"You really hadn't realized…? I don't think I've been trying to hide that fact from you, though."
"You're just deluding yourself… You're just overly romanticizing your memories. We're both getting excited over a misunderstanding because we've met each other after five long years."
Putting all her power into her pitch, not worrying about appearances, she manages to catch me off guard using my own words against me.
"You'll forget about me. If you let some time pass and calm down, you'll forget about someone like me…"
"How am I supposed to forget about a man in a few days when I couldn't forget about him for five years?"
"I've told you this countless times, haven't I…? If you want me to forget so badly, then you should take the initiative."
There is no room for doubt anymore.
Right now, Kazusa is unquestionably a woman in my eyes.
"If you would only tell me that you hate me."
"If you would only tell me that you don't want to see my face again. If you could look down on me and laugh…"
"If you did that… I might be able to forget."
"That's enough already. I don't even want to imagine that…"
No matter how much I try to escape with my words, I can't let go of the hand I'm holding.
"Haruki… you're a cruel man. You're cruel to both Setsuna and me."
At some point, Kazusa's fingers entwined around mine, but I can do nothing but pretend not to notice.
"That's not what it means to be kind, you know? That's nothing but the selfishness of a man."
I can't even grasp back at the fingers entwining around mine.
Even if she puts her other hand over them. Even if she then rests her forehead on our hands.
"Those are the actions of a terrible person who only appears good on the surface. A person who's pretentious, greedy, and who just wants to think of himself as a good person."
"I've always known that I'm a terrible person… That's why it's only natural if people hate me."
"I'm telling you that the way you expect other people's feelings to change is what makes you so terrible."
"You're terrible, Haruki… That's why there is no way I could hate you."
Even if I feel the warm and soft sensation of her lips on the back of my hands…
"She has started eating again. She has also started to let me treat her hands."
"Although as expected, she still won't talk to me properly. That will probably take a bit more time to solve."
"Kazusa is a bit weak-hearted right now."
"Due to what happened with the concert, her homesickness, and well, a lot of other things, she's become unable to restrain her feelings."
"That's why I can't tell her directly yet."
"I'm sorry for not being resolved. I'm sorry for making you suffer countless times over countless days."
"Well then, I'll talk to you tomorrow."
"My new project has been decided on. They're going to let me write an entire issue."
"Though I think you can imagine what it's about. You might even have a bad feeling about it."
"It's the bimonthly Ensemble special issue. That is to say, a special number on Touma Kazusa."
"I do think that it's beyond my means. Most likely, I didn't get this job because of my hard work and sheer ability."
"But even then, this is my chance. I still want to give it my all."
Once I told Kazusa that I had gone out of my way to contact her office, she started complaining a lot, as expected.
Once I finally told her that it's about time she dropped by the office, she started grumbling which made me an hour late for work.
"Hey, what kind of excuse should I tell them?"
"Well, I suppose you'll have to be honest. If you show sincerity, I'm sure they will too."
"…So I should tell them that I was dumped by a man, and felt so shocked that I lost my ability to think rationally?"
…Though I'm actually still in the middle of being late for work right now.
"You told me to be honest. That happens to be my truth."
"…You don't have to be that honest, do you? Besides, you had a fever to begin with, so you can just honestly tell them that you were sick and bedridden…"
"My fever, my injury, and my being bedridden was all because you didn't come to my concert…"
"Ah, fine, fine already. Everything is my fault, your Highness!"
"Ah, ouch! Hey, do it in a straight line. You're terrible at this…"
"I wouldn't want to be compared to a hair stylist."
Kazusa's beautiful long hair slips through my brush.
Just by lifting a single strand of hair, I can see the sunlight reflected in it. And like water, it flows smoothly down my palm. A work of art whose peculiarity is that it has no peculiarity.
If someone asked me what the greatest accomplishment of the genius pianist Touma Youko is, I'd undoubtedly pick this hair and the woman it's attached to…
"Besides, even if I did drop by, there'd be nothing to talk about."
"What will you do about your additional concert?"
"What will I do about it, I wonder… After all, I can't imagine myself playing the piano at all right now."
"Do you even consider yourself a professional…?"
I wonder what her fans would think if they heard her say that…
This fickle genius whose ability and determination are completely disproportionate.
I can't feel anything but the deepest sympathy toward the people who found themselves charmed by this irresponsible pianist… That includes me.
"…I did until Christmas last year. Back then, I told myself that the piano was all I had."
"That's how I managed to make money playing the piano. Ten hours every day, without skipping a day. I sucked it up and did my best."
"Not yet. You should apologize for what I'm about to say next. …All of that was ruined by you, Haruki."
In other words, this person isn't the young and energetic pianist Touma Kazusa…
She's the delinquent girl in Class 3-A of Houjou High… for whom being late and sleeping in class is something natural. A girl five years behind the times, still struggling against society.
I couldn't see through her exterior. I simply saw her as my crush.
…I never knew that the girl of back then was so fixated on me.
"Right now I have no reason to play in Japan anymore. I don't feel a thing at the mention of an additional concert."
"Why are you saying that? I know that's not how you truly feel, so don't force yourself to act reckless."
"It has nothing to do with you, Haruki… You have nothing to do with me at all."
"How many times are you going to make me say it…? Don't put your piano and me on the same level. The scales are far too unbalanced."
"And how many times are you going to make me say it…? The one who gets to make that judgement is me, not you."
"Obviously you don't get to decide your own value. If you can't accept me, then just shut up."
"Isn't your perspective far too narrow? Isn't your world far too small?"
"There are still people feeling grateful about the performance of a pianist who has no interest in anything. …It's a mockery of art, isn't it?"
"I wish everyone would open their eyes… Don't they know that I'm completely unqualified? …There is no reason to come to see me play at all."
Five years have passed, and she has entered adulthood… yet for some reason, she has only become more and more like an unmanageable child.
How did this immature person ever manage to express herself so well?
…It really is a mockery of art.
"You can go… the rest of the way alone, right?"
Touma Youko Office PLC is around a ten minute walk from Nishi Onjuku Station. It's located on the third floor of a rather small building.
The office is a bit underwhelming considering who it belongs to, but since their actual base of operations is overseas, this shouldn't be much of a hindrance.
Apparently Kudou-san is the only employee working there on a regular basis, routinely managing any domestic affairs.

In other words, her job left her with a lot of free time until last year. However, these past few months I'm sure she's been overwhelmingly busy… In fact, she even picked up the phone in seconds when I called her in the middle of the night.
And the moment we reached that building, Kazusa's feet became glued to the ground for a good five minutes.
…She was a bit more confident about this when she was first called to the faculty room.
"…Should I come inside with you after all?"
"…I'll go. I'll go and get scolded alone."
"I might even get fired. She might even sue me for damages…"
"That obviously won't happen. Anyway, open the door and then bow your head right away. After that, shout out your apology."
When Kazusa turned on her phone for the first time in days this morning, the amount of missed calls from her office exceeded three digits.
In the end, that bombardment of missed calls was the decisive blow that made Kazusa come here…
Even now, that very bombardment of missed calls is what's making Kazusa unable to move forward.
"Hey, Haruki… If I really were to get fired. If I really were to lose the only place I belong…"
"I have an appointment with someone in the evening. I don't know when I'll be home."
Her bitter reply is probably not because of me coming home late, but because I interrupted what she was about to say.
She was able to grasp the fact that I didn't want to listen to the rest of what she had to say, and that I consequently ran away from those words.
"It's only normal to meet with your girlfriend on the weekends. Why are you trying to hide it? How ridiculous."
Kazusa's anger seems to run pretty deep. She's not only sulking, but is even firing back at me with good precision.
"…I'll be back before the date changes for sure. I'll make you something to eat, so wait for me."
"I don't really mind. You can sleep over if you want… Or perhaps I should leave the apartment for tonight?"
"Spending the night alone every now and then might be good for me… Without you around, I can cry to my heart's content."
"Like I said! Stop saying things like that!"
And like that, her attack against me ends up dealing twice the damage to herself. I bear witness to a spectacular self-destruction.
This is precisely why I can't leave her by herself…
"I'll definitely be back sometime today! I'll call you no matter what happens! So wait for me!"
"Anyway, apologize properly, okay!? You can put the issue of the additional concert on hold for now. You can take your time to think about it tonight!"
When she took a step back, and even when she turned around, Kazusa's uneasy gaze did not look away from me.
In truth, I really do want to go with her. I'm so worried I can't bring myself to take my eyes off her.
But even so, I have to do it today. It's for Kazusa's sake as well.
The reason I was at a loss for words wasn't because she was right on the mark. It was actually the opposite.
I was feeling relieved that Kazusa hadn't realized I was meeting up with "her"…
Kazusa's guess was half right, but also half wrong.
Normally, I would indeed meet up with Setsuna during the usual time in the usual place tonight.
But I wasn't at a loss for words because she guessed that I was meeting with Setsuna.
I was relieved that she didn't realize that it was someone else…
I can't carry Kazusa's burden alone anymore. The idea that I should carry it was mistaken in the first place.
I'm the one who hurt her more than anyone in the world. I'm the worst offender in the world.
"Ah, yes, Kazusa just entered the office. So where should I go, Youko-san?"
That's why I need to rely on the person Kazusa needs more than anyone.
"…Suetsugu? Oh, so you're in the neighborhood. Yes, yes…"
The person who has watched over her for the past five years, and by extension also the past twenty years. The person who understands her the most.
The only person in the world right now who can support her moving forward…
"Where did you just say you were…?"
"Sorry, I can't come. They arranged a meeting at my job all of a sudden…"
"Yes, I think I'll be able to show up tomorrow. But tonight is…"
Our first meeting after a dozen or so hours happened in front of Minami-Suetsugu Station, five minutes away from our apartments.
"Why are you here before me? You said you didn't know when you'd be home…"
Most likely, after seeing me wave to her with a tired expression on my face, Kazusa accepted it with a bit of astonishment.
"I have no reason to lie to you, or to wait for you."
What an outright lie. I'm sure Kazusa would see through me straight away if she touched my ice-cold hands.
After all, I came to this place a mere two hours ago…
I first returned to my apartment, and after ascertaining that Kazusa wasn't home yet, I turned back and came straight here.
"Let's go home then. You're hungry, right?"
"Kind of. You ordered me to never eat out after all… I'm sure there's a grand feast awaiting me."
"…You're fine with something simple, right? Hunger is the best appetizer, right?"
All that, so I could spend five minutes longer with Kazusa.
"Yeah, I've decided… Actually, I had made up my mind from the start."
Apparently, Kazusa bowed her head and apologized the moment she opened the door, just like I told her to.

After that, Kazusa's worry was proven wrong, and my prediction was proven right. Not only did she not get fired, but Kudou-san was so worried that she cried, which made Kazusa feel more guilty about her than me.
After that, they talked about all sorts of things for hours. She made decisions about her future with her own will.
…She talked about how she'll resume practice immediately after her injury heals, and that the additional concert will proceed as planned.
"I'm sure it'll be a disaster. I haven't practiced enough, and my motivation is the worst."
From Kazusa's perspective, and from the perspective of someone looking at this objectively, that is all my fault as a matter of fact.
Because a certain person said the exact same thing, setting aside whether they were being objective or not.
"But that's my true strength right now… I'll face it head on."
Until yesterday… No, whenever we two were alone, Kazusa kept pouring out every emotion in her heart.
When she was thrown out of the narrow world where only she and I exist, she did her best, and has splendidly managed to make herself appear as someone grand.
"To be honest, my feelings still aren't in order at all."
Seeing Kazusa like that made a thought flash across my mind.
…Perhaps having me around isn't actually the best thing for Kazusa.
"But as I thought, right now I'm causing those around me far too much trouble."
Perhaps all my actions are motivated by self-satisfaction. Perhaps Kazusa really is fine on her own now.

"Miyoko-san, the staff working on the concert, the eccentric sponsors who try to make money through me… and then there are the even more eccentric people who actually come to listen to me play the piano."
Perhaps the feeling of loneliness welling up in my heart is the primary, and only reason I can't let go of Kazusa.
Perhaps I'm doing the wrong thing.
Perhaps I'm only making Kazusa suffer for nothing in the mere pursuit of finding peace in my heart.
"…I don't feel bad for mom and you, Haruki, just so you know. Because we're even now."
"She's still enjoying herself in some hot springs, you know? Neglecting her own daughter like always."
Most likely, the reason Kazusa interrupted me is because she thought I was about to defend Youko-san.
"Well, whatever. I'll have her repay me threefold. I'll continue to cause her endless trouble."
She's not wrong in a sense, but right now it's impossible for Kazusa to perceive my intention 100%…
"I get that you love your mother, but you shouldn't put all the burden on Youko-san…"
"What else am I supposed to do…? Half of my world until now was just decimated."
"…Like I keep telling you, try to broaden your horizons already."
And right now, it's impossible for me to convey my intention to Kazusa 100%.
"It's not just Youko-san, but your staff, your friends… even your fans. There are tons of people who like you."
That's why right now, I can't utter anything but laughable truisms.
"People can look forward to me at their own leisure, but it's not like there is anything for me to look forward to."
"You don't have to sound so lonely… Kudou-san is a good person, right? And there's even the Shibata family…"
"…I like both Miyoko-san and Shibata-san, but once the concert ends, I'll never see them again."
"Then, then… Even in Vienna, there must be people who like you…"
"Don't give me instructions… You're the one who made it impossible for me to stay in Japan."
Not only is my truism laughable, but it also only manages to hurt Kazusa…
"What would you know…? Touma Youko and I were connected before I was even born."
"Touma Youko is the person who shows me the way forward… That's how it's been ever since I was a child."
Even in a situation where she would have broken down crying normally, she glares at me intently from the side and rejects my reasoning with a harsh tone.
"It's true that for a period of time we lost sight of each other, but even that was a mistake born out of consideration for the other."
"…Wasn't it you who told me that?"
Even when she rejects my words, she also affirms them. Even when she acts strong, she also relies on me.
And even though I can't be allowed to feel happy about that tendency of Kazusa, I can't stop those feelings from welling up in my chest.
"That's why I'll walk alongside that person from now on too… And one day, I'll surpass her."
"Because to me, Touma Youko is my goal, my teacher, my rival… she's everything to me."
I can still remember the day I first heard her say that.
Right before the school festival, in the Touma residence's basement studio.
Kazusa became delirious with fever, and I seem to remember her telling me things she would never have said normally.
"I just returned to the past. That's all."
And it's been five years since then…
And as expected, the only person Kazusa can open her heart to right now is me.
"This time, this time, this time… I'll definitely disappear from your sight."
Kazusa did her best. She endured as much as she could.
And now that she has done her utmost effort…
"There is no point in me being here anymore."
What am I supposed to do…?
"Having you treat the wound that you gave me yourself isn't going to heal it."
Even if she manages to hide it until the concert, what about after the concert…?
"Not only will they not heal, they will only give me further wounds… Every time you treat me with kindness, they grow in number."
Can I really… set this woman aside?
"That's why I'm going to get this concert over with, and return to Vienna."
Can I let her go? Can I leave her alone?
"I'm going to discharge myself from the Kitahara hospital. I'm going to slowly heal my wounds over time at home."
"I'll return to my normal, peaceful life, where I'm not tempted by an awful man like you."
"Do your best, do your best… Kazusa, do your best!"
"S-Sto… Stop it. This will only… make the pain worse later."
"This is your rematch. Show Japan just how amazing you are!"
"This is too much… You're putting me in a limbo. You'll only make me feel hurt again."
"What's wrong with encouraging my 'friend'? …What is wrong with it?"
"But I haven't given up at all, you know…?"
I put my arm around Kazusa's shoulders.
"I can act like normal right now, but I'll start crying once I'm alone, you know…?"
Having her body forcefully pulled onto my chest, Kazusa twists around in resistance.
But the force she puts into that resistance isn't her whole strength. Kazusa's indecision, and her slight happiness is conveyed to me…
That's why I don't falter at the sound of Kazusa crying and gradually put more strength into my arm.
"Besides, besides… What will you do if someone sees us?"
"I said I won't do anything. I don't plan on hiding this."
The thing Kazusa is worried about is completely irrelevant to me right now.
Because we're outside… It's precisely because there's a chance someone might see us that I can touch Kazusa like this.
If we returned to my apartment, with just the two of us.
If I knew that no one could question my actions, I wouldn't have been able to stop myself.
"Even though you rejected me. Even though you made it clear that I don't have a chance."
The force within her that tried to get away from me flips around, and is instead used to press her body against my chest.
"…Despite that, I can't contain my happiness when you embrace me like this."
The happiness she concealed inside bursts open.
"Having you spoil me, then acting tough, then getting excited. I'm becoming such an overbearing woman…"
"Aah, for crying out loud! Damn it, damn it…! Why!?"
And the moment she gets my permission, both her happiness and sadness gush out at once.
"Even though I… Even though I love you this much! Why won't anything work out!?"
I'm sure the people living in the neighborhood can hear her.
Despite the fact that Kazusa was afraid of being seen by someone earlier, she's completely open about having her feelings heard by anyone right now.
"Do you hate me that much? Do you reject this overbearing woman, Haruki…?"
"I bet you haven't… because you were waiting for me, right? In truth, you have been waiting for me in front of the station all this time, right?"
"Don't lie. Your hands are so cold after all. You were… outside by the station all this time, weren't you?"
With my hand still around her shoulders, I can feel Kazusa's hand on top of mine.
Kazusa rests her cheeks upon the space between our touching hands.
Kazusa's palm is warm, but her cheek is as cold as my hand.
That's why I desperately hold down my other arm and avoid embracing Kazusa with both arms.
I can't say anything yet. I can't allow her to realize it.
My true feelings, and… Youko-san's true feelings.
At least, I can't until the concert is over. That was what I promised her.
The second hand of the clock has spun around countless times as I've been staring at it.
…Actually, I've been watching the minute hand spin around a few times too, but I still can't fall asleep.
Kazusa had already fallen asleep long ago.
She was still rather tense, but today, she chased me out of the bathroom and ate her food with her own hands.
Even after she slipped into bed, she glared at me for a while, and spoke to me at length about her additional concert and her plans for when she leaves Japan…
Tired from both speaking and her time outside, she defenselessly fell asleep right in front of me with soft breaths.
That's why I was finally able to relax today, and thought to myself that I'd be able to fall asleep easily…
But my memories are getting in the way.
Memories of the bombshell dropped on me this late in the game. The words that Youko-san spoke.
"Like I said, leukemia. Usually it's the unhappy heroine who falls ill with this disease, but it seems God has made a mistake yet again."
After forcefully tracking down Youko-san, who had concealed her own whereabouts, I came here to meet her in person toーof courseーtalk about Kazusa.
I wanted to tell her in earnest that I can no longer support Kazusa, and ask for her help…
And I wanted her to take the responsibility she had forced upon us up until now.
"It was about half a year ago, I think… My body felt unsteady from just playing a two-hour concert."
I wanted her to take responsibility. That way, Kazusa would have been saved… Yet…
"Around my third and fourth piece, my heartbeat went up and I couldn't breathe properly. Even when I was done with the concert it continued for about an hour."
Youko-san called me to a location I could never have imagined.
"At first, I thought it was diabetes finally catching up to me."
"…Anyone would have thought that. You two should have more self-restraint."
"Haha, you never change, Guitar-kun. You act all high-and-mighty even to me."
"…I'm sorry. I haven't been able to take in the situation yet."
"…Well, I suppose so. It took me a decent while to accept it myself."
A fifteen minute walk from where I live…
Within the Houjou campus which I commuted to and from for around seven years, there is a hospital. In a private room of that hospital is where she lies.
"They told me I had anemia when they did some light examinations overseas. After that, I started eating much more… I even changed the wine I drink from white to red."
"But my symptoms still didn't get better. Just a year ago, I could play the piano all night without any problems too."
Being able to do that in the first place is what is strange… Enough for Kazusa to view her as a hard wall to climb.
"So I started thinking that this might actually be pretty bad, so I decided to have Doctor Takayanagi, whom I trust, examine me here in Japan."
I know a Takayanagi Norimasa. He was the chief of the medical faculty in my university.
"They say he's very authoritative on diseases like this. And not least of all, we had an eventful relationship way back…"
And now in the strangest way possible, he's yet another candidate for being Kazusa's father…
"I've been hospitalized for inspection countless times since I returned to Japan, so now we have a decent grasp of what the disease is…"
In other words, the reason she disappeared without a trace so many times wasn't so she could catch up with old friends, or spend the whole night drinking…
"When we were considering our options, a pretty bad symptom hit me… That was during the night of Kazusa's concert."
"I don't have any memories of the two days after that though."
When Kazusa was overcome with sorrow because she had no one to support her…
There was a person who was in even greater need of her daughter's support.
"Well, I'm fine now. I'll be able to leave the hospital next week."
"Do you think I can tell her? With the way she is now?"
I was planning on blaming this person.
I was ready to look down on her and give her a lecture or two.
Despite that… I've figured out just how little I knew.
"Could it be that Kazusa's concerts in Japan were…"
"I planned on bringing her here with me someday regardless. But this is the reason I was in such a rush."
The reason these concerts in Japan were organized wasn't simply to cash in on her popularity. It wasn't simply the judgement of a producer.
"I wanted to ascertain whether Touma Kazusa would be accepted in Japan, and whether my idiotic daughter would be able to live in Japan once more."
She doesn't know if she can be there to experience her daughter's future…
And so this was the shock therapy that a mother had devised after carefully thinking about how she would ever convey this news to her daughter.
"…For as long as I'm still alive, that is."
Although everything she's done up until now in that regard has failed horrifically, I can't bring myself to blame this doting parent after knowing about her circumstances…
"Just so you know, I'm not planning on dying right away."
"The fatality rate for this disease has gone down considerably in recent years. And I've been using plenty of both medications and money. I'll make it to a hundred at the very least."
With her words, I manage to perceive her strength. A strength that makes me think "Since it's Touma Youko we're talking about, everything will be fine."
"It's just that… I won't return to Vienna anymore. I don't plan on leaving Japan anymore."
But despite that, I can no longer see the once triumphant and carefree pioneer who once abandoned Japan anymore.
"It's the country I was born in. Despite everything, it's the country I love more than any other in the world."
I can't blame her judgement. As a compatriot I can sympathize with her, and the more I find out about her circumstances, the less I can bring myself to oppose her.
She spoke with a hint of humor, but I'm sure there wasn't any falsehood in her lamentful words.
"Right now… Kazusa's only life goal is to overcome you, Youko-san. But the only person she can rely on is also you…"
And Kazusa will probably be able to detach herself from any lingering regrets in Japan…
"I see… You rejected Kazusa, didn't you?"

"Tell me, what is it about her you don't like? Well, I do understand that she has no merit outside of her piano, she's gloomy, selfish, stubborn, and her ability to give up is bad enough to make anyone take a step back…"
"That's not… the problem. I have no complaints about her."
"You're the only person in the world who can say that confidently, so you were the only person in the world I had hopes for."
We both relied on each other too much.
"So my daughter lost once again… to the same person she lost to five years ago, no less."
I thought that this person alone could…
I thought she alone could do something about that moody genius' inability to become a part of society. Never once considering that…
"It was a gamble on my part too…"
"I am a parent after all. I want to be with Kazusa until she can become independent."
But I can't blame her for that at all.
"But I can't make that come to fruition in Vienna anymore. This might sound a bit selfish, but this is about my own life."
Because we're both relying on each other for the sake of our own lives.
"That's why I forced Kazusa with me to Japan… So we could stay here permanently."
If I could accept those words in full earnesty, I would find them joyous from the bottom of my heart.
"As far as her career as a pianist is concerned, with how Japan is right now and the way Kazusa is, she should be able to do well even if she leaves Europe."
Kazusa, who separated from me in such a sorrowful way five years ago. Kazusa, who I thought I'd never see again, will be within a reachable distance every day from now on.
"Old man Flugel will retire this year anyway, and I've already found another teacher in Japan."
"…It's an older French woman who raised Hashimoto Kenji to become the number one young pianist… Though we used to fight a lot over boys back in the day."
During our commemorations… or even whenever I feel like it, I can call Kazusa to join our gatherings.
"That's why my main worry is whether Kazusa can live here again."
We can restore the "three," consisting of Kazusa, me… and Setsuna.
"…But it seems it didn't work out in the end. I couldn't make Kazusa overcome her feelings, nor could I fulfill her wishes."
We can go back to being three again.
But that won't be the same "three" who swore eternal friendship five years ago in the hot springs inn.
It will be a "three" where no one can consider the others as friends…
"You were my last hope to bring Kazusa back to Japan… and you were also the greatest impediment."
"Even if you say that… Even if you say that to me so suddenly…"
"You heard her feelings, didn't you? And you couldn't accept them… Well, then that's the inevitable result."
"…Do you think I can accept them? She broke all contact with me for five years. How am I supposed to believe that!?"
"I've been with her all this time, so shall I confirm it for you? Do you have any idea how much that person has been obsessed… about a single man she can't even meet?"
"She was talking to you ten hours every day, you know? That's why her feelings for you couldn't possibly have faded away."
That's the time Kazusa spent with her piano.
The time when she wasn't rebelling against her mother… and the time when she wasn't hurling abuse at me.
"Like that, she felt a love that would never freeze over. Because of that, her piano style grew more and more suggestive, and at some point the whole world accepted her for it…"
"You heard Kazusa's confession, didn't you? You can't say you can't believe it now."
It's because her sensibilities are so infantile. It's because her outlook is so narrow.
It's because she had no interest in anything else, that Kazusa's piano outshone others so much…
It really is… a mockery of art.
"But still… Her choice of a partner was terrible. He was far above Kazusa's league."
"Because you're an ordinary person, Guitar-kun. Being with someone so troublesome is impossible for you, just as I suspected."
"After all, the two of us have the power to ruin the lives of ordinary people. And it's not a power that we have control of."
"That's why if that girl ever tries to make you hers, she'll end up destroying the whole world around you."

Her lifestyle of playing concerts that makes it impossible to remain in just Japan. The enormous cost of maintaining her ability and lifestyle. The media commotion these past few days that not even she herself desires.
Her lifestyle, her life goals, and even her standards for happiness are completely different from me.
She lives in a world I'll never be a part of, and never be accustomed to…
"To other people, that would be a very brutal, heartless and terrible thing."
Even if I jumped into it with full awareness of the risks, what about the people who were around me when I lived an ordinary life…?
There's no point thinking about it after all.
Kazusa didn't fall in love with the true me. It's no more than an idealized image of me that Kazusa invented.
After all, Setsuna was made to walk around in circles because of the real me these past five years.
She suffered due to the difference in ideal and reality, and only through repeated dialogue did we manage to get to this point.
That's why Setsuna's feelings… Our relationship established through long talks is the actual truth.
No matter how much Youko-san tries to defend Kazusa, and no matter how pure and genuine Kazusa's feelings are.
No, that's precisely why the answer is clear before my eyes.
Choosing Setsuna is the correct answer, one that is totally free from mistakes.
That's why I have to tell her.
I must tell her that Setsuna is the only one I have.
I must tell her without muddling my words, that I must say farewell to Kazusa.
"That's why, Guitar-kun, now that things are the way that they are, you should reject that girl without hesitation."
"Cut her off completely, so that her wounds may heal faster, even if only a little."
I knew that much, but even so, I failed again.
"Don't ever think of healing her wounds by yourself. If you show her even the slightest opportunity, she will never give up."
In the end, I could never say out loud what I had determined in my heart.
"Do you think that no such thing would happen? …I suppose that's the sensibility of an ordinary person."
Because of that, my position returns to its original state, and I find myself once again defending Kazusa.
"Kazusa is in her essence just as sex crazed as I am. She doesn't share the logic of the general public."
I find myself put in a difficult situation yet again by Youko-san.
"Otherwise, she wouldn't have kept loving a single man she hadn't met for five years… Can such a woman exist according to your common sense?"
"So make sure you don't forget that. If she's unlucky… No, it's almost certain that she'll never fall in love again her whole life at this rate."
"How could that be…? I was just her classmate for a single year. I haven't done anything that would warrant such powerful feelings from her…"
"The one who gets to decide that isn't you, but Kazusa, right?"
Why do mother and daughter always have to say the same things…?
It makes it sound like what Youko-san is telling me is all what Kazusa truly feels.
"I'll say it once more… Kitahara Haruki-kun."
"If you cannot accept that girl, then abandon her immediately… That is for her own sake."
If I do that, then what… what will happen to Kazusa…?
If she becomes unable to rely on not only me, but Youko-san too…
If her goal, her only guidepost, disappears like a mirage…
Who will be able to protect her…?
"…!? Eh? Ah, ah, sorry. What is it?"
"…I was saying that you look kind of tired, but I feel like I've got my answer already."
I was absorbed in my thoughts, and when I came to, night had already fallen.
I was thinking about Youko-san, Kazusa, and the promise we made tonight.
So many thoughts were chaotically mixed up in my mind, and I went to Kazusa's apartment without sorting any of them out. That's when I saw a piece of paper taped to her door.
"I'm in a meeting with Miyoko. I don't need dinner."
After relentlessly gushing out her feelings at me, she acts all considerate when I really do need her. What a misguided, weak-hearted girl…
"You haven't been using your chopsticks a whole lot. Perhaps you're unwell? Setsuna, could you bring me that measuring thing?"
"It's not a 'measuring thing,' it's called a thermometer."
"Ah, no, I appreciate the concern, but it's not that big of a deal…"
"…Could it be that Nee-chan didn't let you sleep last night?"
The food I had trouble swallowing up until a moment ago is now completely stuck in my throat.
"What am I going to do with you…? You're almost twenty, yet you talk like you're in middle school…"
"Could you cut it out? …We're in the middle of a meal here."
"How do you know that I'm asking something that's inappropriate to bring up during dinner? For all you know, I could have been asking if she was forcing Kitahara-san to play video games all night."
"Even the way you make excuses is like that of a middle-schooler. You'll have no one to blame but yourself if your girlfriend dumps you."
"H-Hold on a second! Just because I brought her over ten times doesn't mean she's my girlfriend!"
"U-Um, it's really nothing like that at all! I was just thinking about something, that's all."
Leaving aside what "nothing like that" is referring to, this family talks about things like that sometimes without any discretion, and it always leaves me baffled.
…Well, on the other hand, it's precisely because this family is the way it is that I can manage to stay in Setsuna's room overnight all the time.
"Thinking about something, huh? About the future?"
"Wait a minute, Takahiro, be a bit more…"
"What are you two on about? Even though you've been dying to ask that all evening."
Setsuna and I look at each other in confusion in an attempt to see if the other understands what's going on, but the effort is in vain.
Because out of the entire Ogiso family, who had all gone completely silent, Setsuna was the one who looked the most embarrassed, hanging her head.
"Ehm, Kitahara-san. Could it be that… you've proposed to Nee-chan?"
Over the table… Setsuna quietly hides her left hand with her right.
…In an attempt to conceal the sparkling ring on her ring finger.
"My sister won't give me a straight answer when I ask her about it. Dad's also been in a really gloomy mood this week, you know?"
Come to think of it… this is the first time I've been in the Ogiso household since I gave her that ring.
"T-Takahiro… you didn't have to do that… we're in the middle of a meal. Look, you're putting Kitahara-san on the spot."
"Aah! Why are you trying to save face all of a sudden? You were the one who just earlier asked dad and me about the best way to get them talking!"
"…Ehm, that doesn't mean you should be so blunt about it, and there is no need for us to find out over dinner."
I know that the bond between these family members isn't so weak that they won't notice a change on her ring finger when they see each other every day.
Though pretending not to know anything until someone points it out isn't exactly good for Setsuna, nor for anyone else.
"H-Hey, stop it! There's no particular meaning behind this ring…"
"…There isn't? It looks really expensive though, doesn't it? It looks completely different from the cheap trinket you had before."
"…I got that one from Haruki-kun too."
"Ah, oh my… is that so? That's uh… well, you know, right, Takahiro?"
"Basically, if you had only let us know about this in advance, Nee-chan, Kitahara-san could have avoided this utter embarrassment…"
"T-That's right! Oh, what will I do with you? Always so obstinate when it comes to the most important things."
"L-Like I said, you've got it wrong! This doesn't mean… that it'll happen immediately."
"Setsuna… if you put it that way…"
"Uhm… If it's not going to happen immediately, then…"
"In other words… you've talked about your future?"
"Aa-ah… the cat's out of the bag…"
"What did I tell you, Takahiro? It's precisely as I said! I knew something was up from the very start!"
"Calm down, Mom. You didn't even ask them yourself, so don't get carried away."
"Cut it out, both of you! They just said that nothing was set in stone!"
"No, they didn't. They didn't say that. They said that they've more or less decided!"
"Dear… I understand that you don't want to accept it, but don't get the wrong idea just because it's convenient for you."
"H-Hold on a second… Like I said, like I said… could you stop talking about it in front of us?"
Amidst this heavy atmosphere, and in this place where my once in a lifetime choice could be made…
I instead remain quiet and hang my head, unable to grasp the flow of the conversation or stop it entirely.
I can only desperately put on a fake smile with my feelings hidden deep inside.
"Sorry about today… things got really weird back there."
"Everyone is so eager about everything, getting all excited like we weren't even there."
"Like I said, don't worry about it."
There shouldn't be anything wrong with being eager. In fact, it was probably the best way to go about it.
After all, they were merely eager. What they actually said wasn't wrong…or at least it shouldn't be.
That's why I'm sorry. I'm sorry for being quiet. I'm sorry for not saying what I should have.
"I'm really sorry. But mom and Takahiro's hearts were in the right place. As for dad… I'll talk to him about it later."
Yet Setsuna makes it look like my unforgivable mistake was her own fault and keeps apologizing.
So as to not burden me. To not push any responsibility on me.
What she desires, what she wants me to do…
Sometimes those true feelings of hers leak out ever so slightly, but she passes them off as a slip of the tongue, and continues to conceal them deep within herself.
Dinner at the Ogiso household was more heated than usual… though one family member left the dinner table halfway through.
Setsuna's mother started talking about the future of the household, putting her in direct opposition to the children who insisted on talking about that with only the family around.
Takahiro claimed the right to Setsuna's room for when she moves out, putting him in direct opposition to the women who wanted it left as is.
Her father didn't seem to want to join the conversation, but when I was about to leave, he muttered to me about needing to talk to my mother.
A kind of conversation that is natural in the Ogiso household, but does not exist in the Kitahara household.
I was supposed to be taken aback by this family, feel envious, and then I'd eventually join them.
I was supposed to become a part of that warm, gentle circle of people.
The time I chased after Setsuna, and made love to her in Osaka…
The time we confirmed our feelings for each other… That was supposed to have happened a mere week ago.
Now I don't even know how much time has passed since then.
The resolve I was supposed to have in my heart. The love I swore would never go astray again.
I feel like I'm at the edge of a violent passion. One that is trying to make me forget about everything…
Perhaps I have turned the bond I wanted to form, and the heart that I wanted to connect to, into something vague.
"Alright then… Thank you very much, Nori-kun."
"The only ones who still call me that are cabaret hostesses and you…"
"Doesn't that mean there are still quite a few?"
"…Forget that, it's the future that matters, Youko-chan. Your true struggle lies ahead, and so does my true time to shine."
"I'm counting on you, okay? This is the reason I came back to this remote country in the first place."
"I understand that from a business perspective, but you shouldn't describe the home country of someone you have a special bond with as 'remote'…"
"If I used that line of thought for every country, all of them would have a special place in my heart."
"…You never change, do you? With that spirit I can guarantee you another ten years."
"Ten years is not enough. I need another 80. I've made up my mind to live past at least 100 years old."
"…Even this late in the game, you're still inflating the numbers, I see."
"Now then, since that's how it is… let's make our next meeting next month."
"At least take an examination once a week. I'll be around during the afternoon on Wednesdays…"
Youko-san greets me with a somewhat blank expression after seeing me poke my head out from behind the nurse.
…This might be the first time I've seen that expression of hers.
"Good grief… So this time it's a boyfriend the same age as your daughter? You never change…"
"…The only thing that never changes is that rotten, perverted brain of yours."
"We're headed for the studio. Kazusa resumed her practice yesterday."
"That's not what I was asking. Why are you doing Miyo-chan's job, Guitar-kun?"
At first Youko-san was just gawking at me, but once we got in the taxi, she started to leer suspiciously at me.
Well, I suppose that's only natural…
"Kudou-san has her hands tied all day today. She's primarily arranging matters for the additional concert."
"I have permission from the company. I told them I'll be running errands for Touma Youko for a while. I told them that this is the condition for making the additional issue."
