"Of course, I haven't said anything about your hospitalization, so don't worry. The chief editor and even my superior were completely convinced, saying 'that's just what Touma Youko would do.'"
In times like these, her usual jokester-type personality really is useful.
…After all, I can convince anyone of anything by just saying Touma Youko said so.
"I thought we should have a meeting about our plans moving forward."
She's not just an ordinary troublemaker, but rather a quick-witted, ill-natured troublemaker who knows full well what she's doing. For the first time, that has saved me.
"First and foremost is your illness… Let's keep that fact hidden from others for the time being."
"I've already spoken to Kudou-san. She was convinced."
"You did all that when the person in question wasn't even around…"
"I told her that we should give our undivided attention to Kazusa's additional concert, and she agreed."
"Well, that was my intention from the start, so I have no objections."
"Moreover, I'd like to minimize contact between you and Kazusa for the time being, Youko-san."
"I suppose it'd be a problem if I collapsed right in front of her."
"The standard should be one hour a day. It'd be best if you just watched her practice in the studio. Please avoid eating with her."
"I have more than ten types of after-meal medication, after all."
No matter how roundabout or blunt I am in my phrasing, she understands the gist of everything I tell her.
"Also, you will have examinations in the hospital three days a week, on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays in the morning. I'll pick you up at the hotel, so avoid staying anywhere besides the hotel."
"This is until her additional concert is over. Bear with it until then."
"I'll be fine even if I collapse a few times. Nori-kun will be able to help me even if my heart stops beating."
"Any actions that will reduce your lifespan are strictly forbidden… For Kazusa's sake too."
"What if my condition gets worse because all the fun is sucked from my life?"
"I won't allow that to happen. If you're planning on living for Kazusa's sake, restrain yourself that much."
"At the very least, put yourself under my management until the additional concert is over. Is that okay?"
"…That will be decided in a different conference."
My speech, which was eloquent until now, becomes muddled at this point.
"…If you can't come up with a conclusion by yourself."
As I suspected, Youko-san's perceptiveness lets her understand everything.
She understands that this schedule doesn't even allude to what will happen after the additional concert is over.
She understands that once three weeks have passed, and Kazusa no longer has a reason to stay in Japan, there will still be no clear solution.
Will she make Kazusa return to Vienna? In that case, will Youko-san stay in Japan?
Will Youko-san tell Kazusa about her illness someday…?
"Tell me, Guitar-kun… Don't you think that it's unnecessary for you to get involved in this any further?"
"That may be… but I can't just leave it be."
Because even Youko-san is at a loss.
"Is it because she was your first woman?"
That's why I can't let Kazusa leave Japan with worrying prospects like that…
"My feelings for her… are that of eternal admiration."
"That's why I want her to remain cool no matter how much time passes. I want her to become happy…"
"That's why you've decided to make her happy by your own hand? Even when you have rejected the one method she desires more than anything else?"
"…Ah, I spoke out of line. Please forget that."
That could never be happiness for her… No, it wouldn't be happiness for anyone.
Because such a decision would make enemies of the entire world around us.
Not only those we don't ourselves view as enemies, but even those precious to us…
"…Well, let's think about it step by step. After all, it seems I'll have to meet you three times a week from now on."
"…Thank you very much. I look forward to meeting you during the next month."
That's why I need time. I need time to talk.
The two of us might not be able to come up with anything wise, but I'll give that girl a happy life no matter what it takes…
"Ah, could you go to the convenience store? I want a pack of cigarettes."
"Lifetime ban on smoking from now on."
"Decide after you've asked yourself if you value him or Kazusa more."
"…I've never seen such a strict manager."
"Ooh, I heard you injured yourself, but it can't have been anything serious if your performance is anything to go by."
"Welcome back. How have you been, Kazusa?"
"'Welcome back' is what you say when you've returned before the other person."
"You sure came back early. You must've enjoyed your trip to the hot springs. Or rather, you must've enjoyed being with the person who was with you."
"You're right. He just wouldn't let go of me."
"What? Are you still worried about how you got slammed by that critic?"
"It's okay, it's okay, that guy is just jealous. He was never a match for me in his heyday, so he's probably trying to satisfy himself by going after my daughter."
"I slept with him twice in the past. And then he…"
"…That's enough. You don't have to say the rest."
"Ah, here's a souvenir. Hamamatsu special unagi pie, Sendai special Hagi no Tsuki, Okinawa special mimigaa, Hokkaido special Marusei Bata Sando."
"…You have a lot of guts enjoying your time in Japan this much."
"Though you too were driven out of this country when you were young."
"…Do you hate this country that much?"
"Yeah, I do hate it. I want to get this additional concert over with quickly and return to my home in Vienna."
"Well, I suppose I'll only get in the way of your practice by being here, so I'll be off."
"Aren't you going to criticize my playing?"
"It's just rehabilitating practice, so there's no point. I'll be in the resting room, just give me a call when you're done."
"It'll take another eight hours for me to be done, you know?"
"Make it two hours for today. It'll all come crashing down if your wound reopens."
"See you then. Do your best, just don't overdo it."
"Didn't I tell you? He just wouldn't let me fall asleep."
In the end, Kazusa left the studio at 8 PM.
Even though I told her that she should take it easy considering her wounds…
"Could it be that… you were waiting here all this time again?"
"No, I just came. I left the office 30 minutes ago, and passed by here in case you were around."
"Yes, really. I swear to both God and the devil."
After all, I made Youko-san leak the information about when Kazusa will leave.
Kazusa peers at me from below, with an expression that can both be seen as teasing or expecting.
She envelops my right hand with both her hands.
Again, she touches both sides of my hand with her stiff fingers, and gently caresses them.
Kazusa's hands are warm. In fact, you could even call them hot.
Perhaps it was due to her passionate practice up until now, or perhaps the result of an inflammation in her injured hands. I can't think of any other reason…
"Didn't I tell you? I just came."
Instead of her hands, she brings her face closer to my chest for some reason.
"You said you didn't care if anyone saw, didn't you? Lend me your chest for a while."
"Hey… that doesn't mean you should all of a sudden…"
"…Then let's go. I'm really tired today."
…Before I can even process what is happening, she pulls away in an instant with a completely different expression, then she walks away as if nothing happened.
Just like usual, she's terrible at conveying her feelings through her actions. Or perhaps it's more appropriate to say that her actions sometimes make no sense at all.
"Hey, Haruki… You don't have to pick me up anymore."
"What do you want to eat today? …Though the only choices are curry, chicken stew, Korean stew, oden, and pot-au-feu."
As you'd expect of a sad man living alone, I have no confidence making any food that isn't stew.
"My hands have healed, so I'll be returning to the hotel soon."
"But we had water-boiled chicken yesterday, and we've had curry three times now. Kazusa, choose between meat and fish today…"
"You don't have to keep looking after me all the time. Don't you have a job?"
"Yeah, I do. My job is to write a special number on Touma Kazusa."
"The truth is, the final checking of the articles will take a while if I do it at the office, so I wanted to do it directly…"
No matter how much I try to change the topic, Kazusa just refuses to get a clue.
That's why I opt for a different strategy, facing her head-on and attempting to shave off the strength of her words.
Unfortunately, I wouldn't just be toning down the tension. The amount of damage she would receive really makes me not want to resort to this tactic.
"…But you can't live alone, can you? You don't have any attendants here anymore."
"I can… I got by just fine even while I was overseas."
"Getting by isn't enough. You have a concert coming up soon. You need to be in your best form."
"I am in my best form. It's nothing for you to worry about…"
"What about food? Can you eat three balanced meals a day?"
"I promise. I'll eat breakfast, lunch and dinner… with lots of vegetables, and moderate sugar."
"What about caring for your hands? You'll have to go on about your days with your injury in mind."
"I'll go to the hospital every day after practice. I'll even regularly change my compress."
"What about your measures against the mass media? Will you be able to respond to rude people surrounding you with a smile on your face?"
"See, I can't trust you after all. That's why I keep telling you that you need a manager."
"I don't need such a thing! I can make do by myself! At the very least, I don't need you anymore!"
"You say that, but you utterly failed your last concert."
"That was only because you refused to come! …Ah."
"Why didn't you come to listen to my piano…?"
"As long as you want me to, I'll do my very best for you, Kazusa… This time, I'll be by your side."
That statement may be arrogant, presumptuous… and excessive.
But despite that, the both painful and happy fact that it works on Kazusa is evident.
"That's why it's okay for you to remain in that apartment. Until the concert is over, it's okay for you to stay there."
Until the concert is over, I won't leave Kazusa's side.
That can also be interpreted as me not making any promises about what will happen after the concert…
"Because I want your concert to succeed. I want the people of Japan to understand your greatness."
Kazusa realizes the deceit behind those words. She realizes that I'm still taking a step back.
"I want you to come to like Japan once again…"
But I have no choice but to separate my feelings from what I need to do.
Even if she manages to see through my cowardly behavior. And even if that means she'll run out of patience with me.
There is a truth I need to hide from her, even if it means using a despicable version of myself as a front.
And in response to that, Kazusa…
"I'm sick of stew. I've had enough of curry too… I want meat, a thick steak."
…Bears with me for another while longer.
"I see, you want steak. Yes, making that should be a piece of cake… no, you should probably avoid cake."
"I hope you're not underestimating steak. Don't think you can satisfy me just by roasting some meat."
"Leave it to me. Rare, medium and well-done are all my fortes. I can even do flambe if you want… not that I've ever done it."
"…I have a bad feeling about this, but let's see what you've got."
"Alright, let's buy some meat at the underground department store along the way, okay? I'll get something expensive like sirloin."
"That's why I keep calling you poor. How can you use sirloin and 'good meat' in the same sentence?"
I still don't know if she decided that she still needs me, or if she just gave up on trying to convince me that she doesn't.
Regardless, she'll allow me to meddle in her affairs… something that should be nothing but torture to Kazusa.
That's why I'll make Kazusa suffer with all my might… and from the bottom of my heart.
Until her last concert in Japan. Until three weeks from now…
"…Also, if you're going to the department store, get a dozen of Rascal's smooth pudding."
"Not a minute ago you told me you'd avoid sweet food."
Kazusa, Youko-san and me… thus begins our life on a tightrope that may snap at any moment. A tightrope smeared with lies, hypocrisy, and makeshift solutions.
"I've got some good news today. Kazusa is resuming her practice now."
"Her injury isn't fully healed, but it seems most of the pain is gone. She says that the rest of the healing can happen as she reaccustoms herself to playing the piano."
"I wish from the bottom of my heart that doing so will lead her in a good direction."
"I've caused you a lot of worry until now, Setsuna. But I'd be overjoyed if you could partake in the happiness over seeing this progress happen."
"…Though, starting with the good news will make what I'm about to say much harder…"
"This year… I might not be able to celebrate your birthday."
"Right now, I think that Kazusa needs my support in order to focus on her concert."
"That might sound excessively arrogant, but right now I simply can't pull back. I'm sorry."
"Let me apologize in advance for now. Goodbye."
"I'll play until the end of the song. Just a bit more."
"Doesn't it hurt? You'll look like a fool if you push yourself any further and worsen your injury."
"I said I'm fine. I know myself better than anyone else."
"The trustworthiness of that statement is in a nose dive. Especially ever since you came to Japan."
"Either way, call it a day for now. You should treat your wrist, and then give it your best tomorrow…"
"At least let me play the piano when I want… It's the only thing I have left now."
"Much unlike yours. So you can stop bothering me."
"Will you be able to go through the rest of your life when you've wilted like this?"
"Why should I think about such a faraway future?"
"Because you're not like me. I'm unsure whether you'll ever fall in love again, or find another man."
"…Even if I don't have a man, and even if I can never make a family, I'll always be there to take care of you when you get old, so don't worry."
"I'm worried about when you get old though, not me…"
"That's nothing to worry about at all. I'm sure you'll still be alive when I'm dead."
"…What kind of vampire do you take me for?"
"Take care of yourself, and live a long life. For my sake too."
"…So, for how long do you plan on playing?"
"Like I said, until the end of the song…"
"I looked out the window just earlier. I saw Guitar-kun freezing outside in the cold."
"That was about 30 minutes ago. I did tell him to come and wait inside, but…"
"…Why didn't you say so from the start?"
"Because you told me to let you play the piano when you want…"
"I've told you countless times. My schedule is completely full this month!"
"Don't say that. It absolutely has to be today."
"I told you I'd listen, didn't I? Out with it already."
"And I've told you countless times too. It's not something I can tell you over the phone!"
…This is the fourth time we've repeated this back-and-forth.
Takeya called me as I was waiting for Kazusa outside the studio, and his tone seemed pretty serious.
"There's something I absolutely need your advice on today" was his message. It sounded desperate enough to make me falter a bit, but…
"Listen here, Takeya. The truth is that I've been entrusted with writing a magazine. It's a special edition of an already quite exclusive magazine."
"Yeah, I've heard about that. Congratulations, Haruki. You made it in life before any of us, just like I thought you would."
"Thanks. Anyway, the deadline is the end of this month. The magazine is seriously never getting released if I don't put all my effort into it."
Right now, I have such a convincing excuse available to me.
Not only is it a half-truth, but it's also an excuse that manages to wipe away half of my guilt.
"Just one hour is all I need. Once our conversation is over, you can go straight back to work."
But Takeya doesn't relent to that perfect excuse. His persistence is impressive today.
…He really has started to act like a middle-aged man.
"You're still in Onjuku, right? I'm right by the station, so we can meet right away. I'll let you return by 9 o'clock."
That would delay me a little bit, but I suppose I'll still be able to prepare dinner.
"I'm begging over here, Haruki! My life is on the line. I'm not exaggerating this time."
"Like I said, I'll tell you once we meet. Anyway, I'll take that as a yes."
I suppose so. As long as I contact Kazusa in advance, I'm sure…
"Until 9 o'clock, alright? I'll walk out the moment it turns 9 no matter what happens."
"I know, I know! Where are you now? I'll head there right away."
"Ah, um… I'll head toward the store from here. The usual one that… Ah."
As long as I contact Kazusa in advance…
"What's the matter, Haruki? Should I come pick you up after all?"
"…I'm sorry, Takeya. Just now, I became unable to go after all."
"Hey… You were talking to the President just now, weren't you?"
"…You were the only one who called him that, you know."
I endeavored to make steak during the beginning of the week, but it was way beyond both my repertoire and my budget, so we're stuck with regular old stew again.
"You should have gone. He went through the trouble to invite you."
"Don't just eat the meat. I've got some Napa cabbage boiled here, look."
"Hey, don't put in so much. Ah, I said I didn't want any konjac noodles! …Actually, that's besides the point."
Although Kazusa is undoubtedly hungry, she's moving her mouth more than her chopsticks.
"It's okay. We still see each other almost every month even now."
"Then you should see him this month too. What if today causes you two to become estranged?"
"Like I said, don't put sugar in your ponzu sauce! …For as long as you keep that unbalanced diet up, I'll stay right here."
"Here, eat some fish too. Also, here are some radishes, carrots and crown daisies…"
"W-Wait. Anything but crown daisies… I'll eat everything else."
In the first place, she glared at me with tears in her eyes when she saw me on the phone. For her to tell me this now feels a bit off…
"Besides, Takeya isn't that kind of guy. We've been friends for almost eight years now, you know?"
"You… not only have a lot of friends, but your friendships last a long time too."
"The amount of friends I have has nothing to do with how close my relationships are…"
There is also a person right in front of me who not only has few friends, but they also don't last long at all.
"Back then, those who were close to you were mostly people who wanted to take advantage of you at first."
"That's just your imagination. Do I look like such an idiotic people-pleaser to you?"
"…Why are you sighing at me like I've said something astounding?"
"Because you did say something astounding. Nothing more to it."
Left wholly dissatisfied with her statement, I move the pieces of crown daisies from Kazusa's plate to mine.
And in exchange, I replenish her plate with kombu, with the hope that it will help preserve her rich and beautiful hair.
"But it's because you're always like that, that makes people trust you so quickly… They rely on you from the bottom of their hearts."
"…Do you think it's time for rice porridge?"
"At first, I looked down on you. I thought that it served you right. I thought that it's only natural that idiots get taken advantage of."
"But gradually, I found myself irritated at how people were tricking you. And before long, I found myself even more irritated by those who gathered around you."
When she first met me, Kazusa had no one she could call a friend or a mentor.

The teachers who knew of her circumstances treated her like a stone on the roadside, and her classmates who heard rumors about her treated her like a pest. No authentic communication existed between them.
"Back then, I didn't know what that feeling was. I just felt irritated and pointlessly angry… I'd always pretend to be asleep and look at you from the side."
"That's just your imagination. You romanticize your perception of me too much."
"You were the only one who would look at me, so I looked at only you too."
The only communication she ever received in abundance was the unbearable lecturing of a teacher's pet.
However, one month before the school festival, she reluctantly came to socialize with that teacher's pet, and also an idol…
After that came Takeya, Io, and Chikashi. After the school festival, she even managed to amass fans. She was able to make friends like most people.
If that was what she truly wanted however, I still don't know…
But despite that, Kazusa did indeed once overcome her loneliness.
"Even now… I'm only looking at you."
She was supposed to have overcome it…
"The me you're looking at right now isn't the same person as back then."
But now… Kazusa's loneliness is right back where it started.
"I've changed twice these past years. I've ceased to be the person you knew back then."
She's back in Japan. Her old friends are just close by.
"The person I was until two years ago was despicable… He was just like your old self that you hate so much."
Yet Kazusa refuses to meet any of them but me.
…No, she can't meet them because of me.
"I was caught in the past, and I couldn't be kind to people. There was a person who cared about me more than anyone, yet I hurt her more than anyone…"
"Does that past perhaps… have to do with… me…?"
"Do you think I can tell you that? Regardless of if it's true or not."
I understand that that's what Kazusa wanted herself, but the more I see her the way she is now, the more helpless I feel.
In the end, Kazusa couldn't find anyone special to her besides her mother, even in Vienna… no, she never even tried.
"The me you're looking at right now is someone who was saved by her."
She's in utter contrast to me, who has managed to find countless people I consider precious to me here in Japan.
"I was able to become a little kinder thanks to her. The person I am right now is someone who is kind only to her."
"That's enough. You don't need to say anything more."
"I'm different from how I used to be."
"Didn't I just say that you don't have to say anything more!? Shut up!"
"…Go home. If you're done eating, then go back to your apartment. I'm tired."
In contrast to how I was saved by Setsuna, Kazusa is…
She just told me to leave…
When I stand up to leave the room, Kazusa looks at me with sulking, teary eyes.
"No matter how much you change, you will never be able to deny my impression of you."
She just told me to leave, yet…
I'm still in Kazusa's room, tightly grasping her hand as she's lying on the bed.
"You will never be able to wake me from these feelings that are trapped in the past…"
Our trivial and pointless argument had a devastating effect on Kazusa's loneliness.
I resolved to protect her until the concert ends, yet I've become the very person who hurt her.
"It doesn't hurt when you hold it like this."
"I see… then I'll stay like this until you fall asleep."
"I know, I'll go home… once you fall asleep."
"I said it's okay… I'll make Setsuna upset if I make you do this."
Of course this is not okay. Just how long do I plan on remaining here?
I'm in the room of the woman I supposedly rejected. In the middle of the night, no less.
"But I won't be able to fall asleep if you don't go home… I'll start wanting to look at your face all night."
"You may say that, but you'll get bored after ten minutes. Don't worry about pointless things."
There was a proper reason behind preparing dinner and picking Kazusa up.
It was for Youko-san's sake. For my job's sake. And for the sake of making Kazusa's concert succeed.
"Wanna bet, then? Whether I can stay up until morning or not?"
But right now, there should be no reason for me to look at Kazusa fall asleep like this.
"Alright, you've got yourself a bet. I win if you fall asleep within the hour."
…Even so, I can't leave Kazusa alone.
I don't know if Kazusa can bear the loneliness. But I know that I can't bear leaving her.
"I said until morning, didn't I? I don't need a handicap like that."
"…I just said I wouldn't fall asleep."
It was at that moment that I realized. I'm sure that Kazusa has realized it too.
The only one who can observe this bet is me.
The bet won't proceed unless I remain here until Kazusa falls asleep.
Kazusa doesn't point out that contradiction. All she does is tighten her grip around my hand.
That's why I stop talking too, and respond with the warmth of my palm.
Kazusa… finally fell asleep two hours after that.
No one knows if she won the bet or not.
"I remembered my old self a little today."
I can hear Kazusa's breaths next to me.
She finally fell asleep two hours after that. The outcome of our bet has become hazy.
"The same me who was so terrible to you until two years ago."
"The same me who distanced myself from you, ignored you, and only spoke lies and heartless words whenever I opened my mouth. The me who was a failure of a human."
And now the time has finally come. The time dedicated to only me, where I can speak to Setsuna.
"It's not something I wanted to remember, but it's not a past I can avert my eyes from either."
The few minutes out of the day where I can allow myself to think about Setsuna.
During this short time, I put my whole heart into sending a text that Setsuna has promised not to respond to.
"You saved me back then, and I was able to return to my usual, overly rigid self."
I became Setsuna's. I became someone who belonged only to Ogiso Setsuna.
"That means that the current me only exists thanks to you, Setsuna."
After that, we never separated for longer than a week.
Setsuna became such a natural part of my life, that it wouldn't be strange if I started feeling withdrawal symptoms without her.
That's why I want to hear her voice. I want to see her face.
I want to hug her tightly and press my lips against hers. I want to taste her warm and sweet saliva. I want to lick her soft and somewhat coarse tongue.
"I feel like this text is starting to become incoherent. I'll call it a day for now."
I want to make love to you, Setsuna…
"Come to think of it… it's only a week until your birthday."
But I promised that I wouldn't meet her… not until I put Kazusa's mind at ease.
"If you have any requests for your birthday present, then tell me. I'll arrange anything within my budget."
And I haven't even found a hint about how to do that.
"Hmm, beef curry along with the salad set. I'll have milk tea to drink."
"…Ah, can I also get a fruit parfait?"
"Then add a mini-sized fruit parfait to my order. You can bring everything at the same time."
"…Certainly. I will be back shortly with your order."
The waiter, who was only supposed to come to our tables to clean up the tableware, forgot completely about his job and left with a stiff expression on his face.
"…I'm amazed you can eat so much."
Looking at my own emptied lunch plate in front of me, I make the same expression as him.
When I went to pick Youko-san up from the hospital, she was just about done with her medical checkup, and only had to take out the IV from her hand.
It hasn't even been 30 minutes since then, yet her appetite is as strong as ever…
"…Just kidding. I don't think I can eat it all. I actually still feel nauseous."
"But I'll still force myself to eat it. I'll eat from dawn till dusk, with proper nutritional balance and large portions."
"So people don't ask me whether I've lost weight."
…Though that seems to only have been my misunderstanding.
"Like hell I'd let this illness get the best of me. I don't mess around. I'll fight it."
As I thought, I really respect her… or perhaps the word "revere" would be more appropriate.
This emotional strength of hers must be the reason she was able to travel the world all by herself.
A certain other woman on the other hand…
All she has is effort and talent. She's rowing throughout the entire world without her emotions catching up…
"More importantly, I'm sorry, Guitar-kun. For getting you mixed up in this fight of mine."
"But now you're not only taking care of Kazusa, but me too… Should I at least buy you a car so you can be more mobile?"
"Don't talk so casually about costs that could be in the millions of yen. I'm just a lowly middle-class citizen."
If she's the one footing the bill, she probably won't settle for a mini car, and she'll most certainly rule out any domestically produced car.
"Don't worry about it, really… I'm doing this out of filial piety."
"How about you practice filial piety toward your real parents?"
I expected her to make a "mother-in-law" joke.
But I never imagined she'd come at me from that direction…
"You were on bad terms with your parents, weren't you? You've intervened in the lives of me and my daughter so much, yet you're pretty obstinate about that. What kind of joke is this?"
"Who cares about my personal affairs? We're not on bad terms either. We just have no interest in each other."
"…That sounds even more twisted than I thought."
"Do you really not hold a grudge against me?"
After finishing her beef curry, she drank her black tea in a single gulp. She happily helped herself to her parfait like a schoolgirl, before turning to the ceiling and staring at it motionlessly.
Her expression is pale despite the fact that she just ate. The way she's profusely sweating from her forehead proves that she was forcing herself to eat.
"You didn't want to know, did you? About my illness, I mean."
Of course. I never would have wanted to see Touma Youko like this.
"Why would you tell me about a secret so serious… that you're even hiding it from Kazusa?"
Also, I never wanted to learn about Touma Kazusa's current situation.
"You know, I was supposed to have become the happiest man in the world soon… In a world different from where Kazusa lives."
"I was supposed to forget about Kazusa, and live as an ordinary Japanese person, protecting a humble yet priceless home. Yet…"
"You're unfair. What do you take my life for?"
"…That's what I'd love to shout at you, at least."
"You really should shout at me, so why are you taking care of me?"
"It's only natural to be considerate of the ill. Everyone is like that, right?"
"You really are twisted in so many ways. …You're quite the amusing child."
"…That's partly just my official stance though. The truth is, I'm the slightest bit grateful."
"You told me everything honestly. You taught me about the problem Kazusa is facing without hiding anything."
"I might have just wanted to find someone to drag into this mess, because I didn't know what to do by myself, you know?"
"That's fine, because Kazusa's happiness is my lifelong wish too."
That's right, I… didn't want to find out about Kazusa's situation.
Because I knew what I'd end up doing if I did find out.
"Should you really be saying that, when you're trying to live in a world without Kazusa?"
"Have you ever thought that… being together isn't the only way for two people to be happy?"
"Setting me aside, I can't imagine that girl having that mindset."
"But if she can still find another answer. If she can only understand something so obviousーthat there isn't only a single path toward happiness for her…"
"What if no such different path existed in the first place?"
"…I wouldn't know what to do anymore."
I also understood that the action I'd end up taking would be different from "the action I should be taking."
"Are you sick of me? Do you scorn me for being an irresponsible man who's just all talk and no action?"
I'd be responsible for the result of that action, yet I'm not even confident that I can bear that responsibility.
…Just like I told Youko-san, I really don't know what to do anymore.
"No, that's not it… I sensed danger."
"You're an honest, funny and dangerous child… I might even feel a bit scared of what I just did. I feel like a patient with terminal cancer who just discovered a bottle of morphine."
"Do I really give that impression? No one has ever told me that before, though."
"Not as far as looks are concerned. But at your core…"
"I'm just a boring guy who opts for stability. I'm sure I must be extremely boring for girls."
"I don't think so at all. After all, you have courage."
"You wouldn't walk on this tightrope if you were. You would have abandoned Kazusa ages ago."
"That's wrong. It's my cowardice that prevents me from doing that."
"But doing so would undoubtedly be the most stable, and 'correct' choice."
"…Are you the one to tell me this?"
"Yes, I don't have the right to say that. Not when I'm the one responsible for dragging you into this."
And Youko-san managed to point out perfectly where my apprehensions lie…
That's why I had no choice but to get irritated and refute her.
"Even then, watching you right now makes me a bit afraid of myself."
"Perhaps people need the weakness to pull back at the last moment."
"Perhaps people need the weakness to lament about how the impossible is impossible."
If you've hesitated many times before reaching the top of the cliff. If you've been pushed forward toward the top through conflict after conflict…
"It's okay… to pull back, you know? It's okay to abandon Kazusa."
Then it's that very trouble that reaches out its hand toward you when you fall off, with much more strength than it had when it pushed you forward.
"You can grasp that small, yet priceless happiness you told me about without reservation."
"I won't bear a grudge against you as her parent. Besides, 90% of the things happening to that girl is her own fault."
"If I could pull back that easily, I wouldn't have forced you to meet me."
"…I suppose that's true. You really are a twisted person after all."
But ultimately, I'm sure she knew I was going to say that.
There is neither surprise nor dejection in her eyes. There is only the calm of someone reaffirming what they already suspected.
However, that calmness shouldn't be mistaken for coldness…
"But still… I have to thank you for thinking so much about my idiot of a daughter. Thank you for treasuring my biggest masterpiece."
"If you had always said things like that to her, she would have grown to be a more honest and strong girl… Someone who would have been fine without us."
"Life really never goes according to plan, does it?"
Reaching this fruitless conclusion, we both drop our gazes toward the table…
A weird feeling of solidarity grows between us, as if we're both guilty parties in some war crime.
"I'll ask and see if they can make it without sugar."
"Hey, you haven't even eaten half of it yet."
"I have no appetite. Perhaps I'm a bit tired."
"Then at least eat a smooth pudding."
"…Don't be so surprised. Wasn't it you who told me to avoid sweet stuff?"
After witnessing Youko-san's gluttony during noon, seeing Kazusa eat this little tonight feels bizarre.
"W-Where is the thermometer? What is the phone number for the nearest emergency center…? Damn, what if it's influenza…!?"
"Like I said, what do you take me for…?"
Indeed, she's never been much of a heavy eater, but she's relentless whenever it comes to anything that's sweet…
"I said I'm fine. I'm just a bit tired. I'll be alright if I get a good night's sleep."
"You're not forcing yourself? You're not in terrible pain and just hiding it from me?"
"But you know… there's only two weeks until the concert."
"I played once two weeks ago too. What's the point in worrying about it now?"
But thanks to you not worrying about it back then, the result was…
"Regardless, I'll go to sleep now just to be safe. You should return to your own apartment too."
"You can do that tomorrow. Anyway, hurry up and get out."
"I feel like being alone right now… please."
She wouldn't let go of me yesterday, yet today she's being uncomfortably blunt about throwing me out.
She really is fickle, always ignoring my feelings completely…
But there won't be any progress if I let myself get discouraged by this.
"Call me immediately if you feel ill, okay? You absolutely shouldn't keep it in, you hear me?"
"How persistent. I just said that it wasn't anything serious."
Because spending time with Kazusa means having to face her uneven temper.
"See you then… Make sure you're warm when you sleep, okay?"
Well, I suppose I'm being overly worried.
I almost expected her to throw a pillow at me with how things were going, so I closed the door with some reluctance.
"…Go meet Setsuna. It's the weekend after all."
"Don't come back! Go to where Setsuna is already."
"Why are you blurting that out all of a sudden…? Didn't I already tell you that I'm not leaving all month?"
"I'm telling you that I don't want that. Having you around against my will is a nuisance for me too. Go to where Setsuna is already!"
"Kazusa…? Why are you talking about that all of a…"
The feelings that made Kazusa want to throw a pillow at me were boiling within her all this time, and it took only an instant for them to burst.
"It's not sudden at all! I've told you that from the start! You're just bad at listening!"
"You promised to always meet her once a week, didn't you? She spends most of her weekends at your place, doesn't she?"
"That's not true… I was here all last week too."
It wasn't fatigue that was accumulating within her. It was stress.
"Ah, I see. She can't come because I live next door. Sorry, I'll leave right away."
Her stress grew so strong, that while she was able to keep her mouth shut about it, she was unable to hide it from me to the very end.
"Stop being with me… out of sympathy. It feels terrible… There is a limit to how pathetic I can be."
I never talked about Setsuna with her much. We only ever discussed her when Kazusa brought the topic up.
Did I only end up striking an even bigger nerve because of the way I'd been tiptoeing around the issue up until now…?
"You were typing them all the time here, weren't you? You were talking to Setsuna… right in front of me."
It seems I have underestimated Kazusa as a woman.
"You looked so pained, yet happy… With your back turned to me in my own apartment, looking only at Setsuna."
Kazusa wouldn't let go of me. I couldn't leave her alone.
I was with her in this room, from when she fell asleep to when she woke up.
The meager 30 minutes I had while Kazusa was asleep… that was when I spoke to Setsuna.
Although she promised not to reply.
But despite that, those mere 30 minutes out of the day were my moments of bliss, when I could think about only Setsuna.
"It hurts me more when you act so sneaky about it. Don't be with me if that's how you're going to do it. Haven't I told you that I can leave whenever you want?"
She's right. One can only be so careless. One can only be so cruel. What the hell am I doing…?
"You can't, you can't do that… Your injuries have only just healed, and you aren't prepared yet…"
"I'll be fine. I'll have mom take care of me from now on. She's the one responsible for bringing me to Japan in the first place, so that's only natural, isn't it…?"
And as Kazusa is feeling hurt, her train of thought only leads to an even worse choice.
"So you don't have to hold back until the concert or anything. I'm sorry for making you keep an eye on such an overbearing woman…"
"You can't, you can't… think this over again, Kazusa."
"Why can't I…? She's my only friend in the whole world, you know?"
I've tried to increase the distance between the two of them, but all it accomplished was to make Kazusa long for Youko-san even more.
"Youko-san is really busy these upcoming days! That's why you shouldn't cause her trouble."
"You seem to know a lot, Haruki."
"Well, because… I have a lot of connections through work and…"
"Well, I suppose so. You've been seeing mom every day… Probably more than you have been with me."
I've failed. My expression doesn't look natural at all.
Kazusa can clearly see my mouth is twitching, and she can clearly see that my gaze is wandering away from her.
"Haven't you had the scent of my mother's perfume on you everyday? Haven't you had the scent of a woman other than me?"
I really… really… have been naive.
"Even today I saw you from the studio window. You got out of a taxi along with my mom. You had no business with me, yet you were with my mom."
I never truly realized that Touma Kazusa at some point had become a woman through and through…
I never truly understood what it meant when she displayed that woman's intuition to me…
"I understand that you don't have that kind of relationship. Even I wouldn't be so indiscriminately jealous."
"But you're keeping something secret from me, aren't you? I'm not wrong about that, now, am I?"
"What are you two doing in secret? …Tell me."
"Just kidding. I already know without asking… Mom is probably trying to gain your sympathy."
"Mom put you up to this, didn't she? She told you to be with me until the concert ends. She told you to whisper sweet words in my ear."
"I just said that's wrong! Shut up!"
At that moment, it was not honeyed words that spilled from my mouth, but an angry scream.
Because I haven't made a promise like that to Youko-san. I have no reason to whisper sweet words to her.
"So basically… The reason you are with me right now is because mom asked you to, and you had no choice. This is all for the sake of the concert."
Before I knew it, I tightly wrapped my arms around Kazusa.
"Shut up… Don't say anything… Don't hurt yourself, Kazusa…!"

But despite the fact that she'd normally get flustered, scared, and start trembling while letting out warm breaths in a situation like this, Kazusa simply remains still, neither accepting nor rejecting my embrace.
"I'm sorry for giving you such an awful job. My mom is strangely overprotective sometimes…"
"She never asked me to do this. I'm with you out of my own free will…"
"Then why are you hiding the fact that you're meeting my mom? Why won't you tell me what you're talking to her about?"
That was the reason Kazusa felt suspicious of me… That was the reason Kazusa felt there was a different reason for me getting involved…
It's only natural for Kazusa to arrive at that conclusion from the information she's gotten.
"Go to sleep now. You're tired… Didn't you say so yourself?"
"I am tired, but I also know that you won't answer my suspicions. I know full well that you're trying to deceive me, Haruki…"
But her suspicion is off the mark by a mile. My determination has no influence from anyone but myself.
The truth is, I'm the one holding Youko-san down. I'm by Kazusa's side despite her objections.
"Kazusa, Kazusa… I'm begging you, please calm down. Don't think about anything. Doing so right now will only lead to negative thoughts."
"But that's the truth, isn't it? That's why you can't say anything."
The tears falling from Kazusa's eyelashes dampen even my cheeks.
Despite that, I don't correct Kazusa's sad misunderstanding. I absolutely cannot tell her the truth.
"I beg you, rest for now. Let's talk again tomorrow."
"Today, I'll be next to you all day again. Whether you're asleep or awake, I'll look only at you… I won't think about anyone else."
"You're feeling nervous about the concert. Don't worry, I'll be right next to you."
I put even more force into my arms around Kazusa. With my body heat, I calm down the body that previously couldn't shiver nor be scared.
"Good night for real this time… Kazusa."
For only today… No, for the upcoming two weeks, I thought about becoming the me that belongs to Kazusa.
I thought about stopping my texts, my calls… even my thoughts about Setsuna in the back of my head. I thought about only ever showing affection toward Kazusa.
But… what will happen after that?
Will everything be alright as long as her concert turns out well? Even though Kazusa's problem won't be solved even then…?
"Hey, give me another. I'll make this my last one."
"This is the third one! You haven't even eaten all your food, so how come you can eat so many of these smooth puddings?"
"Because I have no appetite. I might be a bit tired."
"No, that's no reason to eat all those puddings…"
This family just can't get enough sugar…
"My brain craves sweet food. I've worked hard enough to deserve this, so view this as my reward…"
"My stomach is tired, so it can't accept anything but liquid food. This is the only measure possible to counteract that."
"I say this and you say that…"
"My teacher is a master in sophistry. I've learned a thing or two from him."
"Next time you meet that teacher, call him a 'piece of shit fraud' for me."
"Alright, itadakimasu. You piece of shit fraud."
Day by day, Kazusa returns more and more to her usual selfish self, and I find myself lecturing her more and more.
I don't know if this is because she has given up, is able to separate her personal feelings from the way she behaves, or if she is desperately trying to hold her emotions in.
Whatever it might be, being able to see Kazusa's smile every now and then is something incredibly joyous for me.
It makes me unable to stop the thought welling up inside of me. The thought that I want to see her smile forever, and that I'd do anything to make that happen.
…All while knowing what a destructive action such a thing would be to the other world I live in. The one without Kazusa.
"Don't glare at me like that. Fine, I'll give you a piece too."
"I don't need one. Also, don't report to me every single time you eat something."
And I'm deeply fearful of this joyous me. Before I know it, I find myself with the opposite expression on my face.
After all, today is a weekend night. I had to call Setsuna to tell her we "can't meet" again.
When I made the excuse that I'm busy with my magazine, Setsuna rejoiced as if the honor was her own, congratulating me and wishing me good luck countless times.
Every time she congratulated me, it felt as though my heart was pierced with a drill. I sat crouched down on the streets of Onjuku for a while, unable to move.
Setsuna accepted me, and she took pride in me. She never blamed me or grumbled about not being able to meet me.
Like an innocent and clueless angel, she simply tried to cover me with her warm smile and gentle voice.
Even when she was being deceived and betrayed again, by the devil who tricked her with lukewarm crocodile tears.
The additional concert ends in two weeks…
Can I bear the guilt until then?
And if I am able to bear it… will I be able to return to Setsuna's side as if nothing happened?
"That's not what I meant. Are you really not… today…"
"I was really busy too. We had an intense editing conference starting at 7 o'clock in the morning. Ah, sorry for leaving for work before you."
"Like I said, this isn't about work…"
"Unfortunately, work is the only thing I can tell you about. I have no time to do anything else… except for making you food."
This is bad. This is bad.
Whenever I let my expression turn gloomy, it immediately spreads to Kazusa, who is always looking at me.
And just as I say that… She was smiling just earlier, but now she's looking up at me with tears in her eyes.
"Ah, but you know, I don't need an entire pudding. Will you eat half of it for me?"
"…Is it okay if I eat three and a half?"
"In exchange, you'll only eat two and a half tomorrow."
"Wait a minute! Tomorrow is tomorrow, isn't it!?"
I press the answer button, relieved that the phone call swept away the gloomy mood around us. But I also feel a bit frustrated since I was so close to salvaging the moment by myself…
"…We spoke the day before yesterday, didn't we?"
From the speaker I hear Takeya's ear-piercing voice. Even Kazusa reflexively frowns at the sound of it.
But the reason Takeya is speaking so loudly is clear. The sound of clatter around him is ridiculously loud.
"I'm out drinking with everyone right now. It's super crowded since it's a Friday night."
I can hear the sound of applause, cheers, clinking of glasses and the loud voice of the bar owner. He's clearly inside some cheap bar.
"What about you? Still at work? When can you come?"
"I'm not only still at work, I'm not even close to being done. In fact, I'm in a conference with the chief editor."
"You wouldn't say that if the chief editor was right next to you. So, what? Are you busy today too?"
"Didn't I tell you earlier? This whole month I'm…"
"Why not just go? I don't mind."
After all, today I've broken a promise that's much more important than going out drinking just to stay here and make food…
"Hmm? What was that? I didn't quite catch that."
"Ah, sorry, just talking to someone here. Like I said, the deadline of my big project is…"
"Ah, you did mention that. So what, are you always working late nowadays?"
"I am… Well, I've had tons of special assignments and work at home to do… Ah, don't eat it all. Only half of it, okay?"
"That's how it is. Sorry, I don't think I'll be able to meet up today either…"
"Ah, fine, fine already. I'll give up on that end, so could you listen to what I have to say?"
"Hey, didn't I tell you earlier? I have an urgent thing I need to consult you about."
"Ah, you did say that. I'm really sorry for not having the time to meet you directly…"
"Anyway, with how the circumstances are, I'm wondering if you could listen to me over the phone instead…"
"Yeah, that's fine. If you could call me once your get-together is over…"
"No, here is fine. It's a topic that will be over in a heartbeat."
"What is it? You want to consult me about something so short?"
At that moment, I let my guard down.
"Well, it'll be over in a heartbeat. So listen closely, okay?"
Even though Takeya said it would be okay to take it here, I should have returned to my own apartment.
"Haruki, Haruki…! I'm happy for you, I'm so happy for you! To think this day would actually come…!"
"Hey, hey, what did you say when you proposed? Reenact it for us now."
"Why, you ask? …Because you proposed to Setsuna-chan, obviously."
"Just kidding. You never gave Takahiro any hush money… Not that it would stop him from spilling the beans."
This all started in the Ogiso household last week.
The situation with the ring spread from Takahiro to Takeya, and after that, it kept spreading faster than the speed of light.
"Anyway, I've had a trap set up since two days ago. But you just refused to get caught in it."
The facts became truth, a promise became a binding contract, and everything just continued to develop even more quickly than I expected.
"Anyway, I'm keeping the hostage. If you want her back, you'll have to come here immediately and pay for our drinks."
"Don't worry, we haven't taken her life. Anyway, I'll let you hear her voice, okay?"
That voice is just as I imagined. Nostalgic, and pleasant…
"Just earlier, Io suddenly called me and told me to come. She told me she needed to consult with me about something immediately, so I thought it'd be only her and me…"
But to me right now, it only feels heavy, and painful…
"Apparently, Takahiro went and said something strange to Takeya-kun, and that's why this is happening now…"
I regain awareness of my surroundings by the sound of a closing front door…
"I'm really sorry. This is such a difficult time for you, yet we have…"
"It's not… your fault, Setsuna. No one has done anything wrong, have they?"
"Everyone is trying to congratulate us. No one should have to apologize for that."
That's right. This isn't Setsuna's fault.
Not only that, she has done the right thing.
This is something happy, somewhat embarrassing, and wonderful.
At least… that's what it should be.
I run down the stairs as fast as I can, shouting her name with a shortness of breath…
The back of the person desperately running away from me starts to tremble, as if there is a crack in her determination.
"Wait, hold up, Kazusa. Where are you going…?"
Her body, not covered by a coat, continues to shiver, and likely not just because she's cold.
She's probably way beyond just being teary-eyed at this point…
"You'll catch a cold like that. Let's go back…"
The moment I grabbed hold of her shoulders and forced her to face me…
Kazusa congratulated Setsuna and me with a loud voice similar to Takeya's…
Her expression is just as I imagined it would be, and it hits me like countless needles piercing my heart.
"It's about time! Your wish has come true! Congratulations, really!"
"Stop it… you're being a nuisance to the neighbors."
Her voice really is loud, yet also incredibly hollow.
"I, I'm… seriously happy. I mean it!"
I don't want anyone to hear this voice of hers… But I am the very person who made her let out these terrible screams.
"To see my only two friends in the world get together… To see the thing that was bound to happen from the start finally happen…!"
"You did take your sweet time though! Haha, haha…"
I can't stop her with words anymore. I'll have to physically cover her mouth.
But because I was so reluctant about how to cover Kazusa's mouth, I ended up making the worst possible choice, by forcing my right hand on her mouth…
"Stop it, stop it…! You're, you're such… a bastard! Ua, uaah, uaaa-aah…!"
She bit my finger with all her force, but unable to do anything about it, I could only stand there paralyzed.
"I've had enough, I've had enough… I'm leaving… I don't want to be here anymore…!"
"You can't, you can't do that… Your injuries have only just healed, and you aren't prepared yet…"
I can't embrace her myself, but neither can I stop Kazusa from clinging to me…
"But, but… I'll break if I stay here… I can't take it anymore…!"
That shallow premise is broken down almost immediately, as I tightly embrace Kazusa with my left hand.
To make sure she doesn't run away from me…
"I'm leaving, I'm leaving… I can't stay in Japan anymore…"
"Kazusa, please… rest for now. Let's talk again tomorrow."
"It's okay, I'll be by your side all day today. Whether you're asleep or awake, I'll look only at you… I won't think about anyone else."
Kazusa's pained wailing pierces through my chest…
But even then, I can't let go of her hand. For Kazusa's sake, and for Youko-san's sake.
…And most importantly, for my own sake.
It's been an hour since then… Kazusa has finally calmed down and is now breathing peacefully in her sleep.
While gazing at her swollen eyelids, I think about the tough battle awaiting me from tomorrow onward.
A crack has appeared in the dam. If things go on like this, it'll break down sooner or later.
I have to do something… something…
I have to come up with a solution until Kazusa wakes up.
So I can't allow myself to sleep today. I have to keep thinking until dawn… about a way to make Kazusa happy.
There are stories of charms being broken the moment one falls asleep. These tales are widespread in both the west and the east.
The creator of these tales toys with us, as if to mock my apprehensions.
The moment I came to, I had already committed my fatal mistake.
During those mere 30 minutes of sleep… Kazusa had disappeared.
"It must have been a week since we last met here."
I couldn't reach Youko-san's phone throughout the morning, so I had to go ask Kudou-san and even Hamada-san to find out her whereabouts.
It was 5 o'clock in the afternoon when Youko-san finally called me, but the place she was in at the time was…
It was the same hospital room she was in a week ago.
They told me she wasn't there when I asked in the morning. She must've been transferred there from an emergency hospital at a later time.
In other words, we were back to square one… No, we were actually in an even worse situation.
"Oh my, even this late in the game, you're still willing to prioritize me?"
"Of course. Aren't you in pain? Is it okay for you to be talking to me like this?"
"…It hasn't gotten worse. One step forward, one step back is what they call it."
"…You don't think anything will happen to you right now, right?"
"Indeed, I only feel a bit anemic. I got some bed rest with the drip-feed, so I feel better now."
Perhaps remembering the fact that lighthearted chatter doesn't work on me, Youko-san doesn't try to dodge the question.
"It's simply that she called for an ambulance even though it wasn't anything serious, so I'll be stuck like this for a while."
"After all, that was the first time Kazusa saw me like that. She got in a bit of a panic…"
"I'm sorry, Guitar-kun. I collapsed right in front of her."
Kazusa couldn't endure being endlessly hurt by me, so she broke away from my supervision and returned to Youko-san.
That was during the morning when Youko-san was asleep with the help of pills… And due to the short notice, she had no time to adjust her condition, nor to pretend that she was fine.
"You even worked so hard to hide it from her, but it seems that I have undone all of that."
I was supposed to be Kazusa's anchor back then, and I was naive enough to think that I had calmed her down. That's when I carelessly fell asleep.
If anything, I fiercely provoked Kazusa's feelings. I was the one responsible for tearing off the chains of her anchor.
It all had to happen at such a vital moment… At this point, I can't describe myself with anything else but pure vitriol.
"Perhaps this is punishment. I tried to deceive my own daughter."
"That is my fault too. I was the one who thought of deceiving her, and I was the one who made you agree."
"You burden yourself with guilt too much. Doesn't it feel strange for her old flame to be more involved with her than her own parent?"
"…Apologizing there is a crime of conscience too. Never once complaining about how I dragged you into this mess."
"…If you're going to go that far, then that goes for the both of us."
"You're right. Let's make that our common ground."
If Youko-san is being punished for deceiving her own daughter, then I should be punished for hurting the person precious to me.
"I don't know where she went. But you'll probably have an easier time finding her than before… She had trouble even standing up, after all."
"…Youko-san. What am I supposed to do?"
"If you can tell me what I'm supposed to do, I'll answer your question."
This isn't about accepting my punishment.
It's just that the fact that there is a deep wound in Kazusa's heart is paining my heart too.
"…I'll administer the same medicine as last time for now. Contact me directly once she wakes up."
"Ah, we'll do that once my diagnosis is finished. For the time being, I'll stay here the whole day."
"Wait a minute… What in the world is the meaning of this?"
"Ah, everything is fine. Your mother will be able to leave the hospital once she gets some rest."
"Please don't make so much noise in the hospital room. The patients will wake up."
"Well, calm down. These things might look serious, but they actually happen quite often."
"What do you mean, 'happen quite often'? Has this happened to mom many times before!?"
"Ehm, Kazusa-chan was it? Shall we have a cup of tea in the cafeteria?"
"Mom is… mom is alright, isn't she? She's just a bit anemic, right…?"
"…Let's calm down for the time being. Let your mother rest for now."
"She's only sleeping right now. She's fine. Come on now, follow me…"
"…Don't try to ensnare a girl young enough to be your granddaughter. You never change, do you?"
"…It seems like I've caused you unnecessary trouble again. But I'm alright now. Thank you, Nori-kun."
"Please leave me alone with my daughter… I'll tell her myself."
"…And that pretty much sums it up."
"Indeed, this is a terrible joke… But would you believe me even if I said that?"
"That can't be… Why… Why does it have to be now…?"
"It's strange for you to be more shocked than me about it. I'm the one actually experiencing the symptoms."
"You promised, didn't you!? You told me you wouldn't die before your daughter, didn't you!?"
"Life is in its essence mere postponement. Isn't it a bit pathetic to actually believe such a promise?"
"Humans are abrupt creatures when it comes to death. I've witnessed that kind of thing happen countless times myself."
"Although… that's not to say I was very keen on becoming ill, nor to have you find out about it…"
"But now that you do know, I want to face it with a bit of optimism. You too should prepare yourself for the worst…"
"Uu, uah… aaah, hic… uah, aaah…! That can't… be… that can't be… you're lying…!"
"Mom… Mom, Mom, Mom…! No, no… Don't die. You can't die…"
"You told me you'd live a long life, didn't you…? You told me you'd take care of yourself for my sake… Yet, yet… Uaah, aaah, uaaah…"
"What should I… What should I do…? I've lost everything… I've lost everything I can cling to in a single day…!"
"…Ah, I'm sorry, I'm sorry. There, there! Hey, come here!"
"Jeez… You weren't even like this when you were a baby, you know?"
"…Though I suppose that's the reason you grew up to be like this. I'm sorry, Kazusa."
"It would indeed be too early if I died right away… but relax. I won't kick the bucket that easily."
"For what it's worth, I plan on living up until I'm 100 years old."
"Y-You won't betray me again, right? You won't call me pathetic for believing you, right?"
"…Aah, I went too far earlier. I'm sorry."
"You'll… be with me, right? You alone, Mom, you'll always be with me…"
"Let's go home… Let's get this concert over with and go home to Vienna. You'll get better if you take a good rest at home."
"And once you get better, let's play the piano again. I'll take care of you from now on, Mom."
"That's right. We could even stage our own concert. We've never played a piano duet before, have we?"
"I'll have to improve a lot so people don't consider me a mere sidekick. I'll participate in tons of concerts and contests from now on…"
"I'll work hard, I'll work hard so I can stand on equal ground with you… No, I'll surpass you."
"That's why, that's why… I want you to keep being my…"
"…Keep being a goal that's far beyond my reach. …Be a rival so strong I'll lose heart…"
"I won't hide anything from you anymore. I don't want to deceive you any further."
The sun had already set when I left through the after-hours entrance. Now, the cold winter wind blows against my face without mercy.
Looking at the clock, I see that it's well past 10 PM.
Come to think of it, it's well past visiting hours. It seems that the hospital gave me special treatment in more ways than one.
I leave the hospital grounds and step onto the Houjou University campus. Since it's nighttime during the exam period, there isn't anyone else around.
Despite that, there are still some illuminated windows in the school buildings. They indicate that more than just exams are closing in, but also the deadlines for bachelor's and master's theses.
I recall spending countless nights under those lights too.
"Alrighty then. Wake me when you go to eat breakfast. Good night."
I seem to remember a strange caterpillar always hanging around my feet though.
A classmate who brought her sleeping bag to the lab, even though she never actually bothered to write her thesis.
She did successfully make it to the fourth year, but I started seeing her less and less after that. I never saw her at the graduation ceremony either.
Now that I mention it, I do believe I once ran into her in the streets after I got employed.
She had become unbelievably beautiful during the time I hadn't seen her… No, she was probably exceptional to begin with.
When I asked how she was doing, she avoided the question by suddenly licking my ear before disappearing into the crowd with cackling laughter.
And before I knew it, I had two tickets for a play in my pocket. They were platinum tickets for a troupe even I knew about.
I have absolutely no clue what she was trying to tell me, but I suppose that was proof that she hadn't changed one bit…
"I know about the depth of your emotions, you know?"
"That beautiful feeling of yours that's on par with any of the world's many stories, you know what I mean?"
"You've already come this far… so I hope you can dash toward the finish line and give this beautiful story the beautiful ending it deserves."
Back then, she was a precious female friend to me, someone who I didn't really see as a woman.
At times she'd say something strangely clever, making me wonder sometimes whether she truly knew everything about me.
Right now, I'm suffering because my feelings are as deep as you've described them to be.
And I'm unable to produce a beautiful ending to this supposedly wonderful story just like you hoped I could.
What did you know about me back then?
And right now, do you know exactly what it is I should do?
Looking at the clock, I see it's almost 11 PM.
Since I'm walking so slowly… and also immersing myself in nostalgic memories, it took me a whole 30 minutes just to leave the university grounds.
The cold wind chills me to my core like always, making me loathe the idea of staying in this place.
…But I also know that my thoughts will grow dull the moment I think about where to go instead.
Youko-san said she had a clue about where Kazusa is. And I have a good idea about where that place is myself.
But I don't have the determination to go there right now.
Because I still don't know what will happen once she comes out to the world. That's why I can't knock on her door just yet.
I need to make my resolve about everything by the next time I meet her.
Not about our plans for the coming two weeks. Not about what I'll do until her concert in Japan is over.
It must be about the rest of Kazusa's life, and my own life…
About where I'll live, and who I'll live with…
I can't go see her until I've fully made my resolve.
Given that Kazusa admired her and viewed her as her rival, it's not something she can ever bring herself to fully accept.
Because Kazusa never had her eyes on anything else. To one day surpass Touma Youko while she is still in her prime in a direct confrontation.
To be able to sneer at her own mother, for them to insult each other, honor each other, hug each other, and cry together.
Her aim was so focused on that specific goal that it might be accurate to call it her final goal as a pianist.
The summit Kazusa aimed for vanished without warning.
It's closed already. This restaurant really has no interest in making money during nighttime, just like always.
…Though there really is no need to complain about that.
Because I'm not actually hungry. Also, this place is located on the way home, so I didn't waste my time coming here.
"Please don't look so gloomy in front of the restaurant. You'll scare the customers away. Please only act like that when you're in the kitchen… every now and then."
…Someone might be here to cheer me up.
Without any good reason, I might've led myself to believe something so convenient.
The junior who started working here "without a choice," so she could pay for her graduation trip.

With a naturally overserious, diligent and fearless attitude, she managed to take over the reins of the restaurant before we knew it, and became someone absolutely vital to the restaurant in a mere three months.
Eventually, the other employees begged her to stay after she graduated, which she did. And soon after, she became the poster girl for the restaurant, attracting dozens of repeat customers.
I came here two or three times after I got employed, but she just lectured me with a sulky expression, just like old times.
Come to think of it, Setsuna, who was with me at the time, muttered something on the way home.
"That girl is still in love with you, Haruki-kun, I'm sure."
I have no clue what gave her that idea…
I was just some good-for-nothing guy in her eyes, but that was precisely the reason she could never let me out of her sight…
"Because I want to know more about you. I don't want to know someone I can't understand."
"Well, I feel bothered when you act like that around me."
"Because I can't get it off my mind. Because I'm very interested in you, Senpai!"
She was a troublesome junior who would poke her nose into the business of anyone, regardless of who they were… No, the weaker the person was, the more invasive she became.
…I wonder what she'd do if Kazusa appeared in front of her.
Kazusa might be a stranger to her, but would Koharu be able to ignore her, when she has lost all faith, and everything precious to her?
What would you think if you met Kazusa? You, who are widely regarded as being similar to me…
"That girl loves the piano. But unlike me, it isn't her whole life."
If one were to ask Youko-san…
Then she isn't someone who can live as long as she has her piano. She's not such a pure musician.
"That girl loves the piano. After all, it's only when she plays that she can communicate with the one she loves."
"Well, I was indeed one of the few residents in that girl's world. However… I wasn't referring to myself with that last example."
Reality is terribly harsh, and it's terribly lenient on me…
That's why Youko-san didn't try to hide her irritation about my indecisiveness.
"It's because there were people she could communicate with through her piano, that she could play all day every day without getting bored."
Someone who does exist in reality, but can only be met in her fantasies. Someone who'd be by her side and guide her.
…Even when fantasy and reality are put together, only a few people comprise her entire world.
"Although annoyingly enough, that girl doesn't love the piano like I do, yet she has more talent than me…"
She played the piano without rest every single day just so she could communicate with a small number of people…
In a twist of irony, her exceptional talent led those performances to be accepted worldwide.
"The truth is that I'm not sure myself if… that girl can find her path on her own."
Even if she still has her piano…
If there is no one she can communicate with through those sounds, then there might not be any purpose in it at all…
"This will be the final train of the day for Line 2. Please take care not to miss it."
"The doors are closing. Please be careful."
What will happen to Kazusa from now on…?
I'm sure those who know her only as "Touma Youko's daughter, world-famous young pianist" would say something like the following:
"Take after the path your mother took", or "Travel the world like your mother", or "Your mother can't keep at it anymore even if she tried."
And in response to those people, I'd probably say something like, "Don't go running your mouth about something you know nothing about" in an indignant rage.
It's nothing so simple. She doesn't have that kind of resolve.
After all, she actually is a really weak person. She's incredibly naive, and without determination. She doesn't live in the normal reality most people live in.
Not only that, even in the unnatural reality she lives in, she still is a true genius who managed to improve through effort, independent of her talent and painful fantasies.
"The train on Line 1 toward Onjuku will depart shortly. Please stay within the white lines."
She has broken down at her very foundation, losing everything she built up… All because of a nobody like me.
Can I still ask her to gather her resolve despite that?
Can I ask her whether she still intends to hold the concert as planned? And how she plans to live her life from now on?
Can I ask her whether she'll live in Japan with her mother just as Youko-san wants her to, or if she'll convince Youko-san to return to Vienna with her? Or perhaps…
If she plans to go down the path Youko-san was supposed to go down, standing above countless people, and challenging the world together?
Or if she plans to go down the path Youko-san was supposed to go down, but unwilling to rely on others, and challenges the entire world by herself?
Am I supposed to tell her to give up…?
Am I supposed to tell her that the man she loved, the man who loved her… doesn't exist anymore?
Am I supposed to tell her to face the fact that our feelings just never came to fruition?
And that goes for the both of us.
"The train on Line 2 is departing. The doors are closing. Please be careful."
This really is the worst imaginable possibility, but…
She might end up abandoning both her mother and her piano.
Will she turn her back on the world she has lived in up until now, and shut herself into a new, tiny world that she herself desires?

Will she turn her back on the expectations her surroundings have for her, as well as the feelings of her family? Will she feign strength despite her weak heart and approach a future where any semblance of a normal world would be ruined?
Of course she isn't capable of that. She could never make such a dreadful choice. She will stand still in place, crying all the while.
That's why such a possibility is impossible.
In other words, that's not something she is capable of alone. It's a future that is physically impossible for her to reach.
…Assuming that no one gives her a push from behind.
If she can't decide by herself, will someone else decide her life for her?
Will someone tell her what to choose?
But wouldn't that be the same as determining her life for her…?
Doing so might be arrogant. It might be the deed of a devil who toys with the lives of people.
But does that mean that it's okay for "that someone" to do nothing?
Is it okay… for that someone to not protect Kazusa?
At some point, the date changed.
Regardless, the windows of the editing department are lit up like always.
But the person I want to rely on the most isn't there anymore… It's been two whole years, after all.
The person I owe so much to. The person who taught me how to survive in society before I entered it.
"Leave it to me. Even if the chief editor says no, your article should be in the magazine on release."
I've worked the hardest I can so I could follow in your footsteps, even if only a little bit. I'm still only in my first year, but I've gained a bit of confidence.
Thanks to that, I've fostered valuable bonds with people… and lots of precious ties of obligation with society…
What would you do right now?
Would you still choose work? Would you choose your bonds with people? Would you choose your obligations to society?
So could you come back? Could you become my superior once more?
And could you guide me again?
"You're pretty naive, aren't you, Kitahara? You're quite fragile, and you always seem to only put the blame on yourself."
"Is that why you got so depressed? Because there was nobody to reprimand you for it? Because there was nobody you could ask for forgiveness afterward…?"
"In that case… I won't blame you. And so I won't forgive you either."
…That's right. I made a promise back then.
I promised to decide by myself. To not leave things in the hands of others. To not pander to other people's opinions.
Even if that means… ignoring the thoughts and feelings of everyone around me.
I promised to resolve myself, and carry all the responsibility by myself.
The streets of Onjuku, where the last train has already departed.
Without looking for a warm place, I aimlessly sit down on a roadside guardrail.
Exposed to the cold wind, the canned coffee in my hand is the only thing keeping me warm. Even when I look up, the thick clouds conceal every star in the sky.
A night unbearable for people to loiter in…
But in my thoughts, I see the warm expressions of all the people I've come to know, entering and leaving my mind.
Takeya, Io, Yanagihara-san… and the people I've known since high school. Classmates, upperclassmen and underclassmen.
Hamada-san, Kizaki-san, Suzuki-san, Matsuoka-san, the managing editor, and the chief editor. My coworkers and superiors who are where I should be right now.
Aside from them, there are many people whom I've met during work, as well as people whom I met in private. People of all ages and genders.
And then… there are those who are more like family to me than my real family. Setsuna's mom and dad, and Takahiro-kun.
There's the person who I treasure more than anyone in my life, and who has treasured me more than anyone in her life.
There were of course times when there was trouble between us, when we were annoyed at each other's attitude, and when we made each other mad…
Things were not perfect, but through communication and honesty, we always made up. We always returned to our usual warm smiles before long.
Some day, she will learn to naturally smile warmly in front of other people, just like everyone else.
Even if it's painful for her, even if she's forcing herself, she'll definitely be able to live with a smile, I'm certain…
How many percent is "certain"? Is it 100%? Is it absolute?
Will she of all people manage to connect with many others? Can she show them her smile and make them happy…?
And as a result, will they make her happy in return? …What kind of fantasy is that?
Can I believe such a pipe dream? Am I even allowed to make myself believe it?
I have memories with countless people. I have an innumerable amount of connections with society.
That doesn't just go for the past; even now, I meet new people every day, and through those meetings I establish more connections with society.
My world may be a small one that bears no resemblance to Kazusa's world, but I'm thoroughly connected to every corner of it.
Unlike Kazusa's world, mine is a world that is open to the outside.
When I live in such a vastly different world from her, it's not possible for me to say "She'll be fine" as if I know what it's like…
As I was trying to pass the night walking around in circles as I was…
God decided not to forgive me.
It fell on the day we made our promise to always be together. The three of us.
It fell on the day when three became one, as two broke away.
It fell on the day when two, separated, became a pair of ones.
It fell on the day when the pair of ones tried to become two again, but couldn't bring themselves to forgive each other.
It fell on the day when the pair of ones swore to become two again, after having hurt each other countless times.
It fell on the day when two became three again.
That's right. It has to be today.
Today, I arrive at the crossroads of my life… as well as that of the three of us.
The decision I make today will end up affecting the lives of the many people around me.
"Weren't you the one who left me first!? Weren't you the one who went to a place beyond my reach first!?"
"What's wrong with me falling in love with a loser!?"
After all, ever since that day…
Winter has always been what set my fate into motion. It was always snowing on those days.
Something presses against me; something much more bitter and painful than the permeating cold of winter and the freezing snow.
It's telling me that I can't run away anymore.
It's telling me I have to make one of two choices… and one of those choices is one I thought I already made.
A pain intense enough to tear off my heart and tear my body apart assaults me from within.
Why… Why do I have to hesitate so much when I'm supposed to have made up my mind once in the past already?
I know what the right thing to do is. I know that it's right, precious, and joyful.
Because this will be my final choice…
If Kazusa can't decide, then I will.
I will obey only my own feelings… and choose the one person more precious to me than anyone else in the world.
Who do I want to make happy? Who can I be with, and not regret it even if it is the wrong choice?
I can't back out anymore… This will be my final choice.
Let me think about this… until the snow stops falling.
Don't stop falling until sunrise, at least…
"I see… It's as I thought. You did say the deadline was this week."
"I'm sorry… Could you apologize for me too?"
"It's nothing to worry about. I even said from the start that it might be difficult. There is no reason to entertain Dad's selfishness that much."
"I don't think he's being selfish at all. Tell him I'm sorry for not being able to go when he went out of his way to invite me."
It's been a year since then…
"Ah, but what about tomorrow then? We did promise to meet up at 10 o'clock."
"I can do that. I'll finish everything up today… In fact, I passed up on coming today just to make sure I get everything done."
"Haha, I understand. I'll very carefully apologize to Dad for you."
My life is the very picture of a happy, smooth sailing ship.
As an editor, I'm in charge of some rather demanding work and my days are very busy, but I'm living every day to its fullest.
"I look forward to seeing your dress."
After going through the proper, formal procedures countless times and making ourselves fully prepared, I proposed to her in a rather formal and stiff way…
I, Kitahara Haruki, finally made a big promise with herーOgiso Setsunaーat the end of last year.
