And now, half a year later, we're signing contracts and making lots of different arrangements in regards to the June bride.
I used to be concerned about my relationship with Setsuna's dad, but now we're on great terms. Recently, we've been drinking together on an almost weekly basis.
Setsuna's mom and Takahiro-kun began treating me like family a long time ago. And now with Takahiro-kun's girlfriend in the mix, the Ogiso household never faces an uneventful day.

We've been worn out talking about our program for the ceremony, the guest list, the destination for our honeymoon, our new home, whether we should both work, and about our plans regarding children. But these conversations too fill us with happiness.
After all, it's been a year since then…
This is a Japan where the name Touma Kazusa has been completely forgotten…
Ever since that night when we bade each other farewell, Kazusa's fame came to an abrupt end among the Japanese mass media.
Her additional concert was canceled with the excuse of her feeling ill. There were many loud complaints targeted toward her and Touma Youko Office for a while because of that…
But since Japanese people forget as quickly as they get heated up, that topic was forgotten in less than a month.
Nowadays, the name Touma Kazusa is only written in German or English, even in Japan. It's no longer written with Kanji.
And I… Although I, too, happen to be a Japanese person who forgets as quickly as I get heated up…
"…Okay, you've finally reached the quota for today! I almost thought you forgot about it."
I love Setsuna. I love her so deeply, and those feelings are unchanging.
…I still can't bear not putting those feelings into words, every day and every night.
I also have another feeling within me that is unchanging…
A feeling I couldn't forget about for five years, until I met her again.
A feeling that flared up violently when I did meet her again.
A feeling that I couldn't extinguish, not when I found out that her feelings were unchanging too.
A feeling that I can't possibly extinguish in a single year.
A feeling that might take ten years, or perhaps twenty years to extinguish. Perhaps it will stay with me forever…
Even during our usual peaceful days, when there were no crossroads.
Even during the days where it's just the two of us, deepening our love.
Even during the days when we look up at those same snow-laden clouds… and she is somewhere so far away that the snow doesn't reach her.
"I'll hang up now then. You're working, aren't you?"
"My feelings won't change. I will never tire of happiness."
"Even if we fight, even if our feelings don't match up… and even if it snows."
"…Just kidding. I'm sorry for being so serious."
I'll probably never be able to forget.
I'll carry these unforgivable feelings with me for perhaps another ten or twenty years.
I'll continue betraying the person I love. Even as I'll stay by her side forever. Even as I'll be together with her forever.
Even so… although I'll keep having this terrible feeling throughout my whole life…
I'll only think of you during my dying moments. I'll spend my final moments looking only at you…
So I'm sorry, Setsuna… I'll carry my lingering feelings toward her with me.
But in exchange, I'll always love you. I promise to make you happy.
That's why I look forward to spending the rest of my life with you. And I hope you'll accept these feelings.
"…Are you certain that you got such a call, and that it came from one of our guests?"
"That's why I'm in such a hurry! Every second matters here!"
"However… I still haven't confirmed that you truly have any relation to our guest…"
"Didn't I already tell you to confirm it with her agent? Did you get through to them?"
"No, I couldn't possibly… After all, it's 2 AM."
"I'm telling you I have no time to lose! Didn't I explain to you earlier exactly the kind of things she said over the phone?"
"It would be very grave if it was true… though I'd note that just the other day, we had a journalist pretending to be a friend of hers and made it all the way to her room."
"Fine, then! I'll do it on my own. You can go ahead and call the police. If it turns out I'm lying, you can just have me removed on the spot."
"…Alright then! However, I'll be the first to try to reach out to her. Is that okay?"
"…Miss Touma? I'm sorry for bothering you at this hour."
It seems that from my insistence, the gravity of the situation has finally come through to the room clerk. After nervously clearing his throat, he begins to knock on the door.
"Miss Touma, Miss Touma… I apologize for the intrusion, but if you are awake, could you please open the door?"
However, neither his knocks nor his calls are loud enough to go through the bulky door and reach the other side of the spacious suite.
"I keep telling you she isn't responding! We couldn't get through to her even when you called her on the phone by the front desk!"
"Kazusa! Kazusa! I'm begging you, please answer!"
"H-Hey, stop that! You're disturbing the other guests."
"This is not the time to worry about that! If she's hurt, it'll be on your conscience!"
From the very start, the hotel staff have been on alert ever since I rushed in to the front desk.
When I told them I was acquainted with Touma Kazusa and that I needed to enter her room right away, their suspicion only grew further.
"Kazusa! Are you okay!? I know you're in there. Talk to me!"
"If it turns out that something awful has happened and you didn't help, I'll never forgive you…! I'll put a curse on those very rules of yours."
"…! Miss Touma, Miss Touma! Are you okay!?"
I spent dozens of minutes having a fruitless exchange with the front desk employee, who told me that the rules meant that giving her a phone call on my behalf was the best they could do.
When I told them that I hadn't heard from her since she sent her farewell on my answering machine, they finally became more cooperative.
However, their doubts were still very strong.
"Damn it… damn it! What am I supposed to do… What the hell am I supposed to do?"
"How strange… No response even with all this noise we're making."
"That's what I've been trying to explain to you all this time!"
They followed me all the way to Kazusa's room, but still insistent on following the rules, they refused to do more than wait for Kazusa to open the door.
They value their guests above all else, and have no reason to trust a dubious stranger who showed up in the middle of the night.
"Damn it… better call the police. No, an ambulance! Excuse me, go to the front desk and call…"
"…Let's try to open the door first. At this point, we have no other choice."
Up until now, he had been adamant about following the rules to the letter, but now it seems my desperation had finally reached him.
"However, I will enter first. I can't have anyone but staff entering someone's room without permission."
"If you can't promise me that, then I'll have no choice but to see you out."
They were afflicted with the same feeling of uncertainty, yet I could sense their doubt in me disappearing, if only a little bit.
"I'll leave it to you… Please help her!"
Perhaps my desperate pleas had finally reached the human side of the employees.
"Now then, Miss Touma. I am really sorry about this. But due to this being an emergency, I'll be entering your room."
He then grabs a key out of his pocket, and begins to move it toward the keyhole.
But at the very moment the key is about to enter, the keyhole moves backward as if avoiding it.
"He put on a really convincing act, didn't he? But he's just another journalist… and a big, fat liar."
And out of that door came a figure I hadn't seen for a whole day…
"He's acting all surprised. But that's all part of his act. He's been using you from the start."
"I was so worried about you… I'm so glad, Kazusa…"
Her "farewell" wasn't as profound in meaning as I had thought.
Instead of piling up, the snow melted onto the road. The wind, too, is unreasonably cold.
The sky is starting to clear up. By daybreak, I'm sure we'll be able to see the bright sun again.
As I breathe into my hands for warmth, I see a white puff that soon disappears into the darkness of the night.
"Making such a scene at this time of night… You'd have no right to complain if the police came and took you away."
After that ordeal, rather than pressing me for answers, the employee just turned bright red in bewilderment at the sight of Kazusa.
"I wanted to see you right away…"
In the end, Kazusa brought the whole fiasco to a close with the single, dull statement of, "this guy is with me."
"…It's been a whole day since I left. How is this right away?"
The room clerk chalked it up to it just being a lovers' quarrel. He's probably heaving a sigh at the front desk as we speak.
"You're right… sorry for taking so long."
"Idiot…! No one was waiting for you…"
…The problem is, he wouldn't exactly be wrong in that assumption.
Amidst the cool night wind, I walk around town with Kazusa at my heels.
"What are you thinking? Bringing someone out in this cold."
Her mood must be soured by being called outside in the middle of the night.
And overwhelmed from all the things that had happened.
"Want to stop by at a family restaurant, then? We can talk there."
"It's not like we… have nothing to talk about."
"…So walk a bit slower, would you? Try to imagine what it's like having to catch up with you."
In spite of that, Kazusa continues to follow me.
She's desperately trying to match my pace so she won't get left behind.
"Come here. I should be able to protect you from the wind, at least."
At last, she lines up perfectly next to me.
"It was snowing up until a while ago…"
"I know… I watched it from the hotel window."
Because she has no one else but me right now.
Because no matter how much she curses at me and no matter how much she tries to push me away, deep down, she wants me by her side.
I wonder if things would have been that much easier for the both of us if that self-aggrandizing conclusion was merely something I'd conjured up…?
"How long have you known? About mom, I mean."
"Not very long… for about a week."
"Why would my mom tell you, when she kept it a secret even from me? Why?"
"She trusts you more than she trusts me, is that it? Because you're more reliable than me…?"
"I practically forced it out of her. Just like how I forced you out here tonight."
"Then why didn't you tell me… Why did you keep it a secret from me!?"
"Because I knew you would react like this…"
Sure enough, she goes quiet, and all but outright admits that I'm right by hanging her head.
That without Youko-san to cling to, she no longer has any idea how to move forward.
Only stretching her hand out to the empty air in the vain hope of someone grabbing it. Walking all alone, crying, and lost.
"So that's why… that's why you've been so nice to me recently. That's why it all felt so forced."
"Of course I didn't hate it… How could I ever hate you treating me nicely?"
…Only stretching her hand out to seek me out.
"But I wanted you to act more natural. I never wanted to find out that you had an ulterior motive."
"Acting the way you want me to is easier said than done…"
I could no longer immerse myself in these convenient delusions.
"Kazusa has been in love with me for the past five years."
That dream-like reality. That one unbelievable delusion that could never come true.
And yet she herself reaffirmed those emotions with such unbelievable fervor.
"You thought I was insufferable, didn't you? But you had to stay with me because of what happened with mom."
"I've already told you, that's not the case…"
"Because if I knew the truth, you thought I might try to kill myself. That's what you thought, wasn't it?"
"No, it wasn't. I know that you're not that inconsiderate of others."
"…But I don't think you can recover on your own two feet, either. You just don't have the courage. And you're not strong enough, either."
The person in front of me truly is as lost as I imagined she was.
She's too afraid to go forward, but also too afraid to give up. So she ends up stuck in place…
"…Looks like you've got it all figured out. Do you take yourself for my guardian?"
"…Yes, I do. Because I want to protect you."
"I… I don't need that sense of obligation from you! Not even I would stoop so low as to accept being protected by a man who doesn't even love me."
"Get it together, then! Show Youko-san and me that you can manage to live on your own!"
"You can't, can you? You could never manage to do that, could you!?"
"That's… not true… After all, I've always been alone… Up until five years ago, I've been living all by myself…"
"You weren't alone at all. You only convinced yourself that you were."
"You were living on Youko-san's money, and not least of all her kindness. You were living life as you saw fit, and all the while you hated her for it."
"What… What are you trying to say!?"
If no one reaches out a hand to her now, then she's going to rot away without taking another step forward.
Even if nothing happens to cause her harm, it wouldn't surprise me if she still ended up that way. That's how weak she is.
"You've always been like this. You're selfish, you're a slob, and a failure of a human being. …Just having to look at you is getting me irritated."
"And you're a bad person too. Your personality, your attitude, and your inability to see anything through. The only things you have going for you are your looks and your piano!"
That's why when I push her away even a little bit, her voice starts shaking in an instant.
"You look beautiful, but you're rotten on the inside. Even if people accept you as a genius musician, you'll never be accepted as a proper member of society."
Unable to maintain her facade of vanity, she becomes unable to hold back her shock and tears.
"On top of being awful, you've made it even worse by falling in love with me. Do you have any idea how much pain you have caused me because of that?"
"You don't have to be so mean… It's not like I don't already know that."
Moreover, she's looking at me with desperate, upturned eyes full of tears, as if she were an abandoned pup clinging to me.
"That's why people like you struggle so much! On top of being talented, you stubbornly refuse to fit in with the rest of society. You're left with almost no social skills whatsoever…"
"I already know that… Why are you telling me this now…!?"
The image I had in my head of the cool, dignified lone wolf that I used to have a crush on crumbles away.
"You can't live on your own, yet you're so picky about those who try to help you that you ruin things for yourself."
"I said stop already! Just shut up… please, just shut up!"
She's a rabbit in wolf's clothing… Acting like she prefers solitude yet dies if left alone. The kind of odd species that would inevitably go extinct.
"How were you planning to live on without Youko-san and me!?"
"I don't know! I've never thought about something so ridiculous!"
"It's because you are so helpless, because you are so unbelievably weak that…"
"That… I have to do something, right?"
…I just can't bring myself to abandon someone as hopeless as she is.
If Youko-san can't do it, then I will. I'll have to be the one to reach out to her.
"You know… I, as awful as you are, I love you. More than anyone else in the world."
No… I want to be the one to reach out to her.
"If I am what you need to be happy… No, if I am what you need to continue living…"
"Then I'll be there for you. …Even if it means I have to throw everything else away."

No, let's not even think of that possibility. Nothing is decided yet.

"It's because I feel like I might wake up from this dream… I'll wake up and be reminded that this could never happen."
Because Kazusa herself has stopped hiding her feelings, and has stopped pretending to be strong.
"Don't promise me things that can't happen. There is a limit to how cruel someone can be, you know?"
Instead, she put all her energy into looking at nothing but me.
…Removing anything from her vision that wasn't me.
"Even so… I'm sorry to say that you're completely mistaken."
"I'm not lying at all. I'm not messing with you either."
So I too will answer Kazusa truthfully. I'll remove everything from my vision but her.
"From now on, I'll always be with you. I'll follow you wherever you go… Even to Vienna if I have to."
"Whether it's the famous pianist Touma Kazusa, or the ordinary Japanese girl Touma Kazusa. It makes no difference to me."
"All that matters is that I'll support that one person. From now on, I will live solely for her."
Yet, the more I answer her feelings…
The more I promise to fulfill her wishes…
The air around us grows colder, but for a different reason than the weather.
We're walking down a road that leads to no happiness…
Only despair, enveloping dark clouds, and unimaginable pressure await us on this path.
"But that's only the dream I desperately wished for, it wouldn't actually happen, would it…?"
"Even abroad I'll be fine… I'll probably have a lot of difficulties at first, but I'm sure I can get proper employment there eventually."
"You don't have to worry about my family. I've been away from them for the most part anyway…"
"…! That's not what I'm talking about at all! You're misinterpreting me on purpose again, aren't you?"
"…!? Don't tell me… you can't have…!?"
Kazusa got the wrong idea for a short while, but then immediately understands.
That true cruelty isn't in promising to fulfill a dream that can't come true.
"…You don't have to worry about that. I'll… manage that by myself, somehow."
Because the very moment that dream does come true, it'll also mark the beginning of a time of true despair.
"Boarding for East Japan Airlines Flight 248 to Vienna is now open. Passengers of this flight, please head to Gate 82."

"I'm not talking about myself… I'm talking about you! It's too much for you!"
"If you did that… You'd make everyone miserable for my sake. Setsuna… yourself… everyone!"
"Of course you won't be fine! You'll be the worst off in all of this!"
"But you love Setsuna; you both wanted to be with each other for the rest of your lives!"
"If you do this… If you abandon the person who has loved you so earnestly for five years, you'll regret it for the rest of your life."
"It's not too late at all… You haven't decided anything yet! You don't have to…"
"There is no choice I can make anymore that I won't come to regret."
"If I abandon you now when you need me so much, I'll never be able to forgive myself."
"No matter what I do, it's hopeless. It's far too late to make things right. That's why I…"
"I've decided that, if nothing else… I'll save the person who's most important to me."
"You… You can't do that… You can't… Haruki…!"
"Don't… Don't make me… even more dependent on you…!"
"…! It's because you always put things that way, that I can't bring myself to leave you."
"Of course, even if that's my choice, it's pointless if it brings you no happiness."
"If you feel like you'll be happier without me…"
"If you feel like you can manage on your own, then push me away."
"All I care about anymore is your happiness. That's all I need to make my resolve."
"But that's, that's, that's… How could… I, how…"
"…In the end, I'm only causing you more pain. I'm sorry."
"But I still want the final choice to be yours."
"I think that like me, you'll regret your choice no matter what it is."
"That's why at least… Your regret should be of your own choice. That when you betray those you love, you'll remember that."
"I've already betrayed them. The rest is up to you."
"Will you decide to continue living in despair as you are now? Or will you choose to live a life filled with greater pain, but also one filled with greater happiness?"
"No matter what you choose, I'll do everything to see it through."
"Even if that means I have to make a deal with the devil."
"This is the final boarding call for East Japan Airlines Flight 248 bound for Vienna. All passengers, please proceed immediately to Gate 82 to board. Thank you."
"Hey, Oda! The gate is not that way!"
"Huh? But it says the flight to Frankfurt is at Gate 70."
"Yes, but it's the wrong airline! Check your ticket, would you?"
"Oh, you're right. Why do they have to make things so complicated…?"

"Be more careful… Are you sure you won't get lost on the way back?"

"So why do you keep saying that you can't make it? At least say that you might be late…"
"I've told you already. We're nearing the deadline, so I don't know when they might need me. I need to be available within 30 minutes of being called."
"Then just shut off your phone or something. You're efficient enough to make up for a day's work."
"I can't do that either… This is the first time they've entrusted me with the front page."
"Is your job more important than your girlfriend? Have you forgotten what day it is?"
"Of course I remember… what kind of day today is."
"Your voice has been sounding faint since we started talking, you know."
"Or perhaps it's just that your voice is getting drowned out. I can hear your surroundings."
"You're feeling down about something… Do you really…"
"The train is leaving on Line 2. Please mind the closing doors."
"Ah, sorry… I have to get off the train. I'm hanging up."
"In any case, come! Io and I will go ahead…"
I end the call and rush toward the door before it closes, as if to attempt to avoid hearing the rest of what Takeya had to say.
This week is the first time I'm able to go home before midnight… No, normally I wouldn't even go home today.
It would usually take me a station's travel from Minami-Suetsugu to Suetsugu-chou, after which I'd need to take a fifteen-minute walk.
It's February 14th… Setsuna's birthday, and there's a party for her every year.
The idea of holding a big home party on your birthday past the age of twenty might be laughable for those uninvolved…
Even so, to the participants of this party in particular, it's an expected, sacred and sublime event that they look forward to every year.
Both family and friends gather in large numbers, casually chatting and eating from the grand buffet that the birthday girl made.
The party itself feels very western, yet contains something very uniquely Japanese, like a perfect blend of traditional Japanese and western styles.
I was at the center of the celebration last year and the year before that as the number one target for the other guests who had attended those parties.
…All because I dared to make the birthday girl mine.
"Your voice has been sounding faint since we started talking, you know."
"Or perhaps it's just that your voice is getting drowned out?"
How could my voice not grow weaker…?
After all, I… as things are now…
A few days have passed since then… I haven't heard anything from Kazusa, and I haven't contacted her either.
Back then, Kazusa merely glared at me with tears in her eyes, neither throwing herself into my arms nor rejecting me. Instead, she merely turned her back toward me and walked away in silence.
It was so the both of us could have time to think about things. So we could dedicate everything to ensure that we both know where we stand.
We never set a deadline for such a conclusion.
My hopes and anxieties for this situation to resolve within a day or two were for naught, making me realize that I'd need to steel my resolve for much longer on the fifth day.
Her next concert is in two weeks. And today, having still not heard any decision from Kazusa, I head toward Setsuna's house.
Perhaps I can find solace in knowing that we're surrounded by friends and family, or…
I can't see a trace of her anywhere when I'm dying to meet her, but she always happens to show up when I least expect it.
"It's been five days. Have you been doing well?"
"I should be asking you the same thing…"
"Of course I haven't been well. Not when you pushed that awful choice onto me. I thought that I too was going to get sick and collapse."
Almost as if she had forgotten how cruel a choice I had made…
As if not even aware of how I have felt these past days waiting for her, Kazusa merely looks at me teasingly.
"Why are you looking at me like that? It's almost like you're regretting your choice, like I said you would."
If you know already, then don't bring it up…
How could I not be regretting this? I said from the very beginning I would.
"When thinking about the weight of what you said, it'd be weirder not to regret it."
Why do I… have to separate from Setsuna?
I love her… I could never come to hate her.
I swore to her that my feelings would never change again. …And I believed in what I promised her.
Why am I forced to make this decision… for the sole reason that I love Kazusa too…?
But I understand now. Kazusa has made her resolve.
"You're going to give an answer soon, right? About whether you'll choose me or if you'll abandon me…?"
She's aware that my feelings would waver over the few days that she was given to come to a conclusion.

She's aware that after the day I'd said what I'd said to her in the heat of the moment, I might have spent the painstaking days that followed trying to put my feelings in order and come back to reality.
"I didn't plan to return to Vienna or anything. I didn't even have a ticket."
"The sadness I felt when we parted five years ago… That painful feeling that could tear my body apart."
"And I tried to compare it to the pain everyone else would feel from my foolish choice."
Kazusa was trying to respect my resolve more than her own feelings.
And if I were to suddenly change my mind, she would have accepted it.
"You never asked, did you? Why I was waiting here for you…"
"You knew I'd figure it out, didn't you? About the place you are most certain to go to today."
"Haruki… You were planning on going to Setsuna's birthday party, weren't you? That's why you got off at this station."
"You were going to see her, but you wouldn't be able to say anything about me. You'd just hand her a present, eat together, and then finally, give her a kiss goodbye, right?"
"And then you would regret everything. You'd tell yourself to give up on me, and reaffirm that you love Setsuna more than anything after all."
"I knew. I knew that your feelings were still conflicted. I knew how much you would regret your choice."
"I came here as fast as I could from the airport. I came here by train, taxi and on my own two legs, and just barely made it in time."
"I came here to stop you… I came here to take you away."
"Please… don't see Setsuna from now on."
Kazusa tried to respect my decision more than her own feelings.
And if I were to suddenly change my mind, she would have accepted it.
"Haruki… I want you to betray Setsuna. And I want you to choose me."
But it seems I've managed to overcome Kazusa's trap.
I've won this game of deception with the devil, and signed a contract in the depths of hell.
"Please… Always, always be by my side…!"
"You'll be left with nothing but me and your piano. You're okay with that?"
And in that moment of victory, Kazusa looked very pained and sorrowful…
At that moment… we exchanged our vows in each other's embrace, and the natural next step would have been to share a passionate kiss…
But instead of moving any further at this stage, she merely puts her lips against my finger.
Nothing is over yet… And I know how horrible it will be to end it.
Even though I can sense hesitation in her lips, I can also sense she desires more.
The finger touching her lips soon becomes enveloped by her mouth, and I feel the force of her teeth.
I can feel the tip of my finger getting licked, and then suddenly, a sharp pain.
The strength of her teeth grows gradually stronger. And once blood starts flowing from my finger, Kazusa swallows.
"From now on… you belong to me."
And with this, we establish an oath signed in blood.
"That's right! Kazusa-san is focusing on her practice again…"
"Since yesterday, I think. I noticed that she hadn't returned to her hotel room, so I looked for her all day, then it turned out she was in the studio."
"…I wonder what spurred such a turn of events?"
"She's back on her feet again! I think your feelings for her have finally reached her!"
"No, she hasn't actually left the studio yet… But I can tell!"
"Kazusa-san's feelings! I can tell how she's holding back her tears, and doing her best out of kindness for her dear mother…"
"How can you claim that when you haven't even spoken to her?"
"I can tell from listening to her piano playing… After all, I, too, am a part of Touma Youko Office."
"Come on, you listen too! Can you hear how hard she's working…?"
"…The sound of a girl fighting back her tears out of kindness to her mother?"
"The train on Line 1 is leaving shortly. Please mind the closing doors."
The gates shut as the bells ring, and the unmanned vehicle quietly slides along its tracks.
…That's the third train I've let pass.
I even decided to leave home 30 minutes early to make sure I had time to spare, but once I reached the transit station, I just collapsed.
"Oh no… Is it already so late?"
The first time I felt that something was off was yesterday night. But back then I thought I was just imagining it.
But today when I got on the train at Minami-Suetsugu, I was made aware of how optimistic my self-diagnosis had been.
On top of a headache, nausea and a chill, my heart was beating like an alarm bell. And my shivering hand looked almost funny as it tried to grab onto the hanging train straps.
At first, I thought that it was the train's heating that was too strong, and that I'd feel better once I got used to it.
Yet it seems that the heat emanating from my body wasn't going away that easily. And before long, even the other passengers started noticing the paleness on my face.
And the closer I got to my destination, the worse I felt.
When I got off to switch trains, I was overwhelmed by a numb feeling in my entire body, such that it hurt even to walk.
Then, when I finally reached the platform where the next train was going to stop, I breathed a sigh of relief and sat down on a nearby bench.
And almost as if roots sprouted from my legs, I found myself in my current situation, unable to move.
What's happening to me? I have no time for this…
"Thank you for the text. Don't apologize so much."
"It's not your fault that you couldn't come. It was unreasonable of me to hold the party on a weekday to begin with, so I don't mind."
"I also heard from Takeya-kun. Is it really true that they entrusted you with the front page?"
"That's amazing, Haruki-kun! To think they entrusted you with so much responsibility in your first year. Io and I are super excited about it!"
"Congratulations! Your work finally paid off. I'm so happy for you!"
"Changing the subject, remember when you invited me out on Saturday?"
"Don't take this as compensation for that, but I'd like to see you again if you have the time. Actually, it has been so long I'd love to!"
"It might be a bit unfair of me to say this even though I already said I didn't mind. Hehe… I'm sorry."
"In any case, given that you've allowed me to decide on the time and place we'll meet up, I'll take you up on that offer."
"1 PM, in front of Arumi Station. It's a bit far away, but I hope it's fine."
"We've spent every Christmas there together up until now, yet we haven't been there once this season, and I feel a bit down about that."
"Let's go to the Arumi Integral Hotel like always, enjoy a wonderful dinner… No, a wonderful lunch."
"Does that sound good? I'll be waiting for your reply."
After all, I started feeling sick around the same time I got this text yesterday.
It's because I accept Setsuna's innocent words, an invitation she had meant from the bottom of her heart.
Ever since then, whenever I think of Setsuna…
Whenever I think about her, worry about her, feel guilty about her, I remember what I am hiding from her.
I feel a restlessness in my body and heart.
This must be punishment for straying from the right path.
"I feel a bit under the weather. I measured my temperature and got over 39°C."
"I'm really sorry, but I don't think I can come. So we should probably postpone our date for today."
"You're probably already there, aren't you? Sorry for the late response, and I'm really sorry for keeping you waiting there."
"Also, don't worry about coming and tending to me. It might be the influenza."
"I'm going back to sleep. I have my medicine right here so don't worry. I'll call you once I feel better."
Forcing my fingers to move, I write the text.
It'd be much faster to just call her, and it probably would be the right choice.
Despite that, I focus my weary eyes on the cell phone, and continue typing.
…Because hearing Setsuna's voice is too hard for me.
Going outside in this state was impossible from the beginning.
My shivering and my cold sweat won't stop. And I can't stop the nausea and the thirst in my throat.
Going to that windy coastal park in Arumi would be suicidal.
I can't help it. Things are painful enough as they are.
I'll send this text to Setsuna, and go out some other time.
I'll sleep in a warm bed for a day or two. By the end of the weekend, I should be back to normal.
And if possible, I'll be back to work on Monday, and get my first draft checked…
Next time I'll be able to see Setsuna will be next weekend. My present will be rather late. I hope her mood won't be too soured by it.
And without settling any matters, we'll be able to continue as a couple for the winter…
Am I feeling relieved over not having to settle anything today? Am I taking delight in postponing the pain?
"Sorry, I missed the train. I'll be ten minutes late, so wait just a bit longer."
What purpose would that serve… How can I let such a mild punishment make me give up?
If I run away from painful encounters now, if I develop a habit of turning away from that which I need to face…
Then who's going to protect her…?
To where Setsuna is. To where my judgement awaits.
I have to accept my punishment.
Because I have someone I need to protect. Someone who is not Setsuna.
"Did you call my name just now?"

"What's the matter? Did Guitar-kun give you sweet whispers of love in your sleep?"
"When I came in, you kept playing without noticing I was here. And then you suddenly collapsed."

"Of course you're going to pass out without a single sip of water or any sugar. Here, take this sugar cube."
"And here I was thinking you were skipping practice again, only to see this absurdity."
"I'm not being absurd. I'm just trying to make up for lost time."
"No, it is absurd. Your playing isn't even like usual."
"You think so? Maybe I'm just a bit rusty."
"No, the sound itself was almost perfect. But the person playing was a different Touma Kazusa."
"I'm really not smart enough to understand what that means."
"It's like you're desiring some kind of punishment. Your playing has that kind of tragic feel to it."
"Personally, I don't care for it. But I'm sure there are lots of people who would love it. To the point of reaching into their very souls."
"What are you trying to atone for?"
"If I told you I wanted to make up for all the trouble I caused you… would you believe me?"
"I'd believe half of it. But if you're saying that's everything, I won't."
"That's my mother for you. She can see through everything."
"I'm sure that applies to all mothers."
"Though you haven't done a single motherly thing for me up until now."
"I guess so… I just wanted to try using that line once."
"I suppose the difference is paper thin. I only wanted to try bragging about it."
"I think that, perhaps… I won't be able to become the Kazusa you want me to be."
"Do you mean… the successor that Touma Youko wants? Or the daughter your mother wants?"
"Sorry for being an unworthy disciple. Sorry for being an ungrateful daughter."
"Now then, good work on your job this week!"
"And congratulations to you for your first magazine, Haruki-kun. I hope your first big project sells well."
"…Ah, thank you for the Valentine's chocolate."
"I'm sorry too, for picking such an expensive place."
"Don't worry about it. We've been coming here once every year."

"Okay! I've actually been hungry for a while now. Itadakimasu."

Getting caught in the relaxed atmosphere Setsuna created, I kept on toasting with her. A natural smile appeared on my face, and talking became easier.
"Wow, this is delicious! I can understand why the lunch set alone is so expensive!"
"…I already told you not to worry about the price. This much really isn't an issue."
"Ah, sorry… I always get bothered by the prices in places like this."
"Stop worrying about the cost of food today. I don't want to be reminded of who's paying for it."
I sigh with a smile on my face, and start eating.
"…But it really does taste good. Definitely worth the cost."
…And then I realize that I've recovered enough to be able to discern the taste of food.
In 30 minutes, I forced it out of my body.
I found a way forward in my heart, and blocked any path back.
When I came to our meeting spot, and apologized to her, she wiped off the sweat on my forehead. But that sweat was from running as fast as I could.
Right now, I don't have a headache, nor do I feel cold. Because I closed it all off in my mind.
A closed off part in my mind where Kazusa's faint smile, her unabashedly angry expression, and her childlike tear-stained face are all stored.
And a place for the way she looked at me when we made our oath.
…So I can recall them whenever I want to.
"It's right next to the sea, after all."
"The sea breeze is really strong. Are you okay, Haruki-kun?"
"I'm fine. I always wanted to come here at least once this winter, after all."

"In this cold… why does fashion have to be in such a hurry all the time?"
"Well, I've never heard of fashion that is behind the times…"
"Come on, hurry up! Actually, why not take it slow? Fashion comes and goes, but the shop won't go anywhere."

And I naturally accept that she isn't doing any of those things.
Is it because it's evening? Is it because we haven't seen each other for so long she doesn't know how to gauge the appropriate distance?
Does she feel so secure in our relationship that she doesn't feel the need to be clingy?
"Do you think this necktie is too flashy?"
"No, not really… If anything, I'd say it's quite classy."
"I see… If you like it, then I'll go with this. Let me take this to the register."
"Eh? W-Wait a second! Isn't this place Barbares?"
"Right. It's an English brand, isn't it?"
"Give me that… Look at the price of this thing! You don't need anything this expensive."
"It might be expensive, but these things are made to last. I'd probably get more value out of this than a cheap one."
"That may be true… but this is far too expensive! Akagi or Unipool should be more than good enough."
"Weren't you the one telling me not to worry about money just before…?"

"This is for my dad. His birthday is next month."

"If I was buying you a present, I'd never show it to you in advance."
"Hehehe! Yay, you fell right into my trap!"

That usual motherliness she has, and also a type of familiar attitude a bit different from what I'm used to. Both combine to make me feel better.

I find myself in an inescapable dead-end, one filled with contradictions.
"The sea is right in front of us, after all."
After we finished our shopping and drank our tea, the sun had already gone down by the time we left the shopping mall.

…It's a testament to how long we have been here together, yet during all that time, I found myself unable to bring up what I came to tell her. As far as anyone is concerned, I'm just having a date with my girlfriend.
Before I knew it, I felt happy, I felt peaceful.
"It's because we always come here on Christmas."
"It was even snowing here two years ago."

After the two of us spent Christmas not here, but in France…
We're no longer capable of preventing the cogs of fate from creaking.
"I hope you don't feel bad. I was completely in the wrong back then."
"No, you weren't. Because that time, I…"
"No, I was in the wrong. But I won't apologize… because that is also a part of our history."
"Both the good and the bad… The times we fought. The times we avoided each other. The times we made up… It's because so much happened between us that we are here now."
As Setsuna raises her hand to hold up her hair, a radiance unlike any other I've seen until now shines from her finger.

"A lot of things happened. But we got through them together."

I can now say with certainty that I love her from the bottom of my heart.

"Let's continue walking slowly. We don't have to rush. Go at your own pace, and I'll always keep up with you…"

I'm abandoning the best woman I know and choosing the girl who's nothing but a burden to me…

I know that it is a ridiculous choice.
"I have something to tell you. It's something important, something you absolutely have to hear…"
"Ah, aah! Dear me, would you look at the time!"

"I'm really sorry for leaving so suddenly. I'll make it up to you next time."
"…Won't you listen to what I have to say? We can do it on the train."

"You can't! You just can't! I don't want to hear anything else today!"

"Putting it off won't change anything. I've already decided."

"I… can't be with you anymore, Setsuna."

"Because… the one I love the most in the world is the Setsuna who can happily sing in front of me."

"It's fine, Setsuna… We'll be fine now…"
And the feelings that should pile up over such a strong foundation…
"From now on, I'll take whatever happens. I won't ever let you go, Setsuna."
I once believed that our bond was irreplaceable and unshakeable.
"Let's get married. Let's get married, Setsuna…"
But the truth is, it's nothing more than a sandcastle on the coast. All it took was a single sweep of a wave for it to vanish without a trace.
The records of the bond I share with Setsuna are being erased from our new history…
I wonder how much time has passed since then.
"I could tell from the slightest changes in your behavior, Haruki-kun. From your eye movements to the way you looked at me."
My heartless words caused Setsuna's feet to halt the moment we reached the station.
"I knew you were wavering. I knew you were thinking about someone else. …That you were thinking about Kazusa."
She collapsed right then and there, unable to continue supporting herself with her own strength.
"Realizing that your heart was straying further and further away from me was just so painful!"
Her shoulders shudder, and she does her utmost to prevent herself from losing her voice. But she is unable to control her feelings, as she cries quietly, yet intensely.
"…Ever since the new year, since your reunion with Kazusa, ever since then!"
Whether we stood there for a few seconds or a few hours was something completely unknown to us. The difference had no meaning to us.
She finally stands up again with eyes red from tears, and a voice almost torn apart. Yet she still tries desperately to string together some meaningful words.
Her current self is unlike anything I've seen from her in the past five years I've known her.
"Tomo said… that she had already seen Kazusa twice. Once outside of your apartment, and once as a guest at my concert."
I've hurt Setsuna more times than I can even count up until now.
"At that time, I didn't believe it… no, I tried desperately not to believe it…"
I've done things I thought I could never take back more than just once or twice.
"But the time you came to me in Osaka… when you really desired me…"
"That confirmed it for me… You were trying to run away to me… because you were already leaning toward Kazusa."
Still, no matter what happened, Setsuna has always been strong for me.
"Yet I didn't talk to you about it. Even worse, I slept with you knowing how much you desired me."
Bearing her tears, straightening her back, and acting the role of her usual, gentle self.
"…Because I knew it was the day of Kazusa's concert. I didn't want to let you return to Tokyo."
When she should have let her feelings out, she held them back until she was alone with me.
"Was that… wrong, I wonder? Should I have asked about the truth back then?"
Setsuna has always been strong. And I became dependent on that strength.
I became spoiled by it, relied on it. I believed in her strength…
"We shouldn't have met back then after all."
Yet, when I look at Setsuna now…
"I should've kept my distance for a while. I should've kept running away from you."
With no regard to the people giving us strange looks, she continues crying, regretting the past, blaming herself, gushing out all her feelings in plain sight.
"I thought that this might happen… I knew that things might end this way."
"Yet, yet… I couldn't resist the temptation of seeing you again!"
She's almost like the "helpless" girl that Kazusa is…
"I couldn't let go of the faint hope that you would embrace me…!"
Am I responsible for turning Setsuna into this? …The same way I've turned Kazusa into the woman she is?
If she hadn't met me, if she hadn't fallen in love with me…
If I wasn't there, would everyone be happy?
"Hey, Haruki-kun… What should I have done…?"
The sound of Setsuna crying resonates with the sound of the sea breeze.
"Where… did I go wrong…? Where did I mess up…?"
The chill of the breeze and the sadness in her voice envelop me and cause me to shake violently.
"How can I… make you take back what you said earlier? How can I make you return to me?"
Vigorously, violently, and not caring what she looks like…
Her feelings, as strong as the north wind, relentlessly blow upon my despicable self.
"You… don't have to do anything. You haven't done anything wrong, Setsuna. There's nothing wrong with you at all."
"…! But then I can't fix anything. If you don't tell me how, I can't fix anything…"
I've already chosen the worst possible choice. I've chosen to throw away everything other than Kazusa.
"…I won't be able to change for your sake… I won't be able to turn into the girl you'll like."
"I'll say it again. There's nothing you can do…"
That's why the howling of the wind can no longer blow anything away anymore.
Not the coats of passers-by, nor my determination.
"It's all my fault… So I'll do anything to atone for it."
"But you just rejected every single thing I wanted you to do, didn't you!?"
Yet the wind doesn't give up. It continues blowing with the faint hope of getting the one thing I cannot give it.
And it will continue to do so until it runs out of breath.
"Why…? What's wrong? Is it just not acceptable for me to be around? The three of us… can't stay together?"
I could confess to Setsuna everything about why Kazusa was driven into a corner… and all about Youko-san.
Setsuna could potentially be of help to Kazusa. All three of us could support each other.
I contemplated that kind of future many, many times.
But that burden is for me to carry alone… I can't have Setsuna carry it with me.
So I can't say anything about it.
"I can't? Has Kazusa still not forgiven me…?"
…Or perhaps that's just an excuse I'm telling myself to justify my actions.
After all, I don't actually have a reason for picking Kazusa.
…Other than the fact that I love her more than anyone else.
Once I get out of the taxi and check my watch, I see it's almost half past one.
By the time I left Arumi, it was already past midnight. Once I got to Onjuku, the last train had already left.
…Because once Setsuna left, I was unable to move for a while.
I wonder if she got home safely…
The trains were still running by the time she left, but I wonder if she got on it. I wonder if she's at home now.
I should call her, or her parents, or perhaps Takahiro-kun…
…I have a strong desire to make sure, but what right do I have to do that now?
At long last… I've finally done it.
I finally did the unthinkable. I chose the path in which very few people have found happiness going down.
I went against the better judgement of society. …I made a decision that's just unbelievably cruel to Setsuna.
Setsuna refused to accept it until the very end.
Even when she left, she kept saying to herself that she wouldn't give up, all while crying.
She never blamed me. She never spoke ill of me.
Like always, she was unreasonably kind to me…
But that's why it only makes things worse.
The chill I had this morning comes back to me. My heart starts racing, and my nausea goes all the way up to my throat.
Perhaps it's the result of standing in the cool air for so many hours.
If that's the case, I wonder… is Setsuna okay…?
I can feel the weight of the stress from my concern for Setsuna, and the feeling of wanting to check up on her even though I'm not able to.
And the more I think about her, the more I lose control of both my body and mind…
That's why I resort to the only antidote I know to rid myself of these painful memories.
A spell that I really shouldn't be using…
Though it seems there was no need.
"Mom threw me out of the studio. She said I wasn't to come back until noon tomorrow."
No… It wasn't a spell to dispel painful memories at all.
"I didn't have any place to go, so I came to you. Be my bed for tonight."
Instead, I had unknowingly cast a summoning spell.
"…It's okay, right? You wouldn't mind having me over, right?"
"How many hours have you been waiting there?"
"There is no point in telling you. I'll always be waiting for you until you come home, regardless."
I bend over in front of Kazusa and pet her, and she squints her eyes at me in pleasure as if she truly was a dog.
"Look at how cold you are… are you stupid?"
When I stroked her slightly red cheeks with my hand, I could feel just how frigid they were despite the fact that my hand's already numb from the cold.
"You're even colder than me… You look like you're freezing… you look like you're suffering…"
However, Kazusa grabs my hand that's touching her cheeks and exhales on our intertwined hands, rubbing them together to give me warmth.
The summoned is ever subservient to the summoner.
When Kazusa asked me to "be her bed," she didn't mean for me to lend her my bed.
So, just like she wanted, she rests her head on my chest, and I warm her cold cheeks.
She wraps around me, and brushes herself against my body, warming me up in return.
"I didn't expect her to go along with it."
I tell her everything about what happened today in a low voice, all while feeling the warmth of her body on my skin.
I won't hide anything from Kazusa. After all, she's the person this is all for.
We'll get hurt together, and overcome those wounds together. That's what we swore to each other.
"…I didn't expect her to blame you either. It's Setsuna we're talking about, after all."
"…I wanted her to blame me. I wanted punishment."
That's why we lie here and get hurt together, in silence.
For the fact that Setsuna didn't blame us. For the fact that she tried to blame herself for what happened.
…For not getting even a glimpse of punishment.
"After all, in dramas and movies… side characters like me whose role is to interfere with the plot only end up retreating and disappearing, right?"
"Yet I'm still here, making the main heroine miserable, and taking the main character for myself."
That's not true. What would you even know about movies?
"The only part of me that is true to being a side-character is how I never do anything by myself… Always expecting the main character to fix everything… I'm that sort of repulsive woman."
That kind of thing would only happen in a world where only happy endings are allowed.
That kind of development would only work in a cliched Hollywood movie.
"Whether you're a side-character or not, is for the main character to decide… no, it's for the director to decide."
…We can go back and forth for as long as it takes, but I decided to conclude the subject.
"Had you just done what I told you to… Had you just pitied me and comforted me with your body, before you got too into me…"
"Then I would have been satisfied. I might even have been able to get over you."
"I might have been able to go on living alone, with you in my memories."
"No… I wouldn't want that! If you're not able to go on with life still smiling, then I…"
If I try to contradict her, I'll end up admitting it…
That the two of us being together is not a happy ending.
It won't make a single member of the audience happy. The story will just follow the direction that the director stubbornly decided on.
Just like I did to her before, Kazusa clumsily tries to reciprocate in kind.
"Are you cold? Are you in pain? Why are you always holding things back…? Are you stupid?"
That means… she calmed down when I did it to her.
Having me stroke her cheeks made her relieved. That's what she's saying by doing this.
"I'm fine. I'm really fine. I've calmed down a lot compared to before… thanks to you warming me up."
"Don't push yourself, okay? If you're in pain, tell me."
"I'm fine. I'll never break down. How else can I protect you?"
I'll take the place of your mother. I'll take the place of your teacher.
If I don't do that, then there's no point in throwing everything away.
"If you were to break, then I'll be the one protecting you."
"I'll make it my next life goal to do so. So whether you break or not, always stay by my side."
A short while after that, peace returned to my body.
I think that my illness, caused by more reasons than I can name, won't be bothering me anymore.
Because from now on, Kazusa's wild assumption will protect me.
"Ah, good morning, Takahiro. Curious to see you up this early on spring break."
"Same goes for you… I never see you on Sunday mornings. You're either oversleeping or staying out."
"Well, what are you doing? Making a bento?"
"Yeah, something like that. Okay, I'm finished! Hey, don't you think it looks good?"
"Didn't you have a date just yesterday? There's no separating you two, is there?"
"It's not like that. Haruki-kun's just very busy these days, so he isn't eating properly…"
"That's exactly what I mean when I say you two are inseparable!"
"Um, I'm not sure. We haven't decided anything yet…"
"You have no plans for today? Then why not just make the food in his apartment? That's what you've done up until now, anyway."
"…Shut up, would you? Why do you care?"
"Ah, okay… Wait, aren't you going to clean up after…"
"Oh, Takahiro. Rare to see you up this early. Are you going on a date?"
"The one going on a date is Nee-chan… she was so excited she even forgot to clean up after herself."
"That's okay, I'll take care of it. And I'll make you some breakfast while I'm at it."
"Ah, no need. I'll eat the leftovers from the bento…"
"Stop with that. I'll make you something proper."
"Eh? But… wouldn't it be a waste to throw it out?"
"Listen to me, don't eat that… You'll only cause me more worry…"
By the time we woke up, the sun was already nearing its zenith, so after we ate our late breakfast, it was almost noon, as Youko-san had mentioned.
"If mom chases me out of the studio, yes. So don't worry about dinner."
"Even if I don't go home, you don't have to wait for me. Actually, go to bed early. You didn't get a wink of sleep last night, did you?"
If you know that, you couldn't have gotten much sleep either.
"In exchange… I hope you won't mind it when you find someone strange sleeping next to you once you wake up."
Even so, Kazusa's faint smile and the way she's teasing me with her words ever so slightly eases my worry a bit.
"Okay… come back safely, and good luck."
Because Kazusa no longer looked as if she was forcing herself.
Two weeks remain until her additional concert. Physically, it's probably going to put a strain on her. But at least mentally she seems to be doing fine.
If I managed to make things easier for Kazusa yesterday, then there is no greater happiness for me.
As long as I can be the place she can always return to…
Now, and from this day on, forever…
"…We had a lot of leftovers yesterday, and I thought it'd be a waste to throw it all out."
"You don't have to eat it if you don't want to! You can throw it away if you're not hungry."
"You've got it all wrong. There's no deeper meaning behind this."
"My mom! That's right, my mom told me to get this for you."
"She said that you probably haven't been eating properly, with how busy you are all the time. I didn't think so though…"
By the time I had seen Kazusa off and had done the dishes, the clock showed precisely twelve o'clock.
Like Kazusa said, I hadn't gotten a wink of sleep since last night, yet I didn't feel like going to bed just yet.
I have so many things to take care of now that I have some free time. In fact, I'm going to be completely occupied for the next few days.
Besides, even if I did lie down and close my eyes, I wouldn't be able to fall asleep.
I put on my shoes and opened the door, but when I turned back to look at my room, time suddenly seemed to stop around me.
Reflected in my eyes is a simple and lightly decorated room.
A bed, a closet, a bookcase, a TV, a fridge, a rice cooker, a microwave…
The bare minimum for any home. And half the clothes I have are work clothes and dress shirts.
…Still, this unappealing room sometimes also has a mixer, electric griddle, a pressure cooker, and a whisk in it.
…Items that the other tenant staying here had brought into the room.
I still can't feel nostalgia welling up within me because it hasn't truly sunk in yet. I can't feel any feelings of sorrow because my determination to leave isn't complete.
Until a few days ago, it wouldn't be inaccurate to describe this place as our nest.
Everything within it appears natural in every sense of the word, the odd juxtaposition of items both simple and fancy providing it some semblance of appeal.
However, even the ability to feel that appeal from such scenery is…
"It's been a while… or well, since your birthday party. I've been looking for you."
"Because you haven't answered a single phone call since yesterday. I called your family earlier."
"They said that you made a bento you were planning on giving to Kitahara-san."
"That's right! I'm going to Haruki-kun's place. I'm sorry, but I don't have time to talk today…"
"Then what are you doing here? Kitahara-san's apartment is over there."
"That bento is for Kitahara-san, right? Why are you opening it here?"
"…No, I tried going into his apartment building, but my feet stopped moving."
"…Be honest with me. I'm on your side, Setsuna."
"I told you earlier, didn't I? I talked about how he might be seeing Touma Kazusa."
"I'm probably wrong about this… but, Setsuna, about yesterday, did the two of you…?"
"When I tried tasting this bento… it didn't taste good at all."
"It's so bad it's almost inedible. To think that I made something like this…"
"What is this… I don't even remember how I made it… What is happening to me?"
"Hey, get it together! What are you saying?"
"And you're absolutely certain that you don't want to renew your contract?"
"The current contract runs out at the end of next month. You'll have to pay that month's rent too before the end of this month."
"That will be fine. I'll make sure everything is settled."
"Going to work abroad, I see… Where to?"
"Yes, I'm going to Europe… to work in Austria."
Both the memories that I've built up for the past five years as well as the history I've shared with that apartment I've lived in…
Will no longer exist after a few days. They will all disappear without leaving so much as even a trace.
After sunset, the tempo at the office went up, and about when the editing department just got even livelier…
Hamada-san's enraged voice cut through all the bustle.
"You have so much potential… You haven't accomplished anything yet, right…?"
"…! Kh, kh… follow me to the conference room!"
Surprisingly… the news spread around sooner than I'd expected. I'd hoped I could carry on worry-free at work for a little while longer…
After leading me to the conference room, Hamada-san took a while to calm himself down, finding it difficult to delve into the matter at hand.

He takes out a cigarette, despite having long ago promised to quit after being scolded by his wife, though the moment he remembered that smoking is forbidden in the conference room, he gets even more irritated…
"Submitting a letter of resignation for your editor position… why would you do that?"
As if left with no other choice, he finally cuts to the chase, despite not looking all that eager to do so.
"For personal reasons… I'll have to resign from this job."
…He averts his gaze from me just like I'm looking away from him.
"…Did you hear that? You heard that, right?"
"I did… and judging by your reaction, Suzuki, I don't think I'm hearing things…"
"What is this…? Do you think he's being headhunted?"
"No way. The only one who saw that much value in him was Kazaoka-san."
"He is rather new… I doubt anyone outside of our office knows about how hard he works."
"But still… is this some kind of joke? I mean, this is Kitahara we're talking about!"
"That guy values responsibility to an absurd degree. He follows every rule to the letter."
"I'm really sorry for quitting on such short notice. But I'll make sure to finish all my current assignments before I do so…"
"That wasn't my question. What's your reason?"
As I expected… What I want to talk about the least is what he wants to hear about the most.
"Family matters? But you live alone, don't you? Did you hear something from your parents?"
"This doesn't relate to my parents. It really is a purely personal matter."
Well, it doesn't relate to my own parents…
"You think we'll be content with that kind of justification? Or do you intend to shield yourself behind company and labor laws?"
If you give notice of your resignation a month in advance, the company has no right to refuse.
"This is your first year, isn't it? Do you have any idea how much potential you have here?"
But of course, even I know that a written contract isn't everything.
"Do you know how many years it takes for a single employee to be profitable to the company? Do you know that we're employing you at a loss until then?"
I've managed to find and keep many valuable things through this job.
The skills I have learned from both seniors and juniors, the connections, and the bonds I have formed.
"Even as you are now, you're still a rookie around here. You haven't given back anything yet!"
It was because I was going to plant my roots here… for the sake of myself, the company, and for society. That's why my superiors, my company accepted educating me for free.
"Then why…? Didn't you work all the way up here from your part-time days? Wasn't getting here always your goal?"
"Ever since the beginning, I thought you were different from others… You had this old-fashioned air about you, in a good way."
That beginning was three years ago.
It was back when I was tasked with simple physical labor, such as printing copies, running errands and fetching papers.
But at some point, a certain devilish superior of mine that I specifically requested for decided to force more mentally strenuous tasks upon me.
"You were diligent, but also quick to make friends. You were argumentative, yet you never tried to lie yourself out of work."
A year after that… she got a promotion and left for America, and since the editing department lost an employee, I was officially employed.
"There were times you did too much on your own, but not in a way that took too much initiative from yourself. Rather, you were very serious about your job."
And since then, and up until now…
I've been surrounded by a strict yet somewhat questionable group. And every day has been both a struggle and a joy, not to mention busy.
"That's why Kazaoka always gave you special treatment… and that goes for me too, and everyone else too, even the chief editor…"
It's a bit melodramatic, but I liked working here so much I could imagine investing my entire life into working here.
"So how the hell comes that without a single word with your superior, you all of a sudden decided to quit?"
"Stop messing around! Why didn't you ask me for advice? Did you have that little faith in me as your superior?"
"Sorry ain't gonna cut it… Tell me why, Kitahara…"
All the skills, connections, and the bonds I have formed… all these things that bring value to life.
"That's not possible. This is not something that can be solved by asking for advice."
All of it is undone by a single letter with "Resignation" written on the front.
"Even then, it's something to consult with your superior about, isn't it? Something you should talk to me man-to-man about, right? Weren't you the kind of guy who could do that?"
"What's gotten into you!? Fine, leave then, see if I care!"
Hamada-san was completely outraged. And he finally gave up.
Because for an entire year… No, for the three whole years we've known each other, he already knows how I am.
He knows that I'm not the kind of exemplary employee who would let go of his resolve just because he was told to by his superior.
In a way, I expected this.
And from the looks on the faces of my coworkers, it truly set in that this was no longer a place I belonged in.
Even though he knew I was awful at making jokes, Matsuoka still asked.
I was supposed to have felt truly grateful for Matsuoka's words that were attempting to reaffirm the persona he's known me as up until now in place of my current self, which he currently rejects.
"It's been… a pleasure working with all of you. By next month, I will…"
"What… the hell is this? Why are you leaving before me? Shouldn't it be a given that I'm supposed to get the boot before you do!?"
The Houjou Graph team will never go back to what it once was.
Not while I'm around, at least…
As the night grew late, and the hotel cafe became deserted with the exception of us two, we sit in greater silence than usual.
Because for a while, Youko-san had been staring at the ceiling in silence.
"Are… you really sure about this? Throwing away everything for her sake."
"We were talking about you, not me, Youko-san."
"Won't you return with us? Together with Kazusa and me… to Vienna."
I told her everything about all the things I had done the past few days, without hiding a single thing.
"So you… finally went and did it. You accepted her… to the point of destroying your own brakes."
"I should be the one who's sorry… I should have done everything in my power to stop you the moment I realized what a dangerous person you could be."
"Are you against it…? For Kazusa and me to…"
"I couldn't be against it. How could I be? My daughter is now happier than she has ever been in her life."
"But… it's unfortunate. The resolution she wished for is different from mine."
With a very difficult look on her face, Youko-san voices her opposition to my actions with those severe words.
…Just like all the people I betrayed.
"If you didn't have any other people precious to you, then I would have desired this too."
However, I do have people I consider precious from the bottom of my heart.
"If only Kazusa could have gotten over you, this wouldn't have happened."
However, Kazusa's feelings are too pure, too strong.
"Most of all, had I not fallen ill, you wouldn't have had to get involved."
"My conclusion is that my illness is to blame for all this."
As expected of Youko-san, she is able to summarize the current situation.
"One by one, the cogs got screwed loose. And everything is moving in a direction that no one desired, and I was powerless to stop it."
That including herself, there is no one in the wrong.
That the fault lies in the situation, and the turn of events that lead to it, or perhaps some childish idea that society is ultimately to blame.
…A point of view that is almost the complete opposite of mine. A difference in opinion that could make one wonder who is the more mature one.
"…In the end, my daughter has ruined your life."
Since no matter how you look at it, I truly do believe that everything is my fault.
"Had I been the one directly responsible, I would accept any divine punishment awaiting me. However, I couldn't bear seeing that happening to my daughter."
Everything was my decision, my responsibility.
On top of that, I truly do believe that I've made the best possible decision.
That's why I have no right to be apologized to.
"In the end, neither you nor Kazusa will be able to stay in Japan…"
"It's not like we're running away. The two of us talked about it and concluded that it was the right choice."
"So just because the two of you talked about it, that means you're not running away? That makes no sense at all… and while I'm at it, that's a lie, is it not?"
Her tendency to guess what I'm thinking despite the complete discrepancy in our perceptions has always been something I've been weak to.
"Youko-san… I really think Kazusa needs you."
That's why I forcibly change the topic.
"I'll make sure your medical needs are looked after. You won't be any less free than in Japan. No, I'll make sure you have even more freedom."
No, the one who diverted the conversation in the first place was Youko-san. I am merely steering it back in the right direction.
The reason I came to see her was to get an answer from her in regards to Kazusa.
"So… would you please come with us? Would you… protect Kazusa with me?"
Of course, with the goal of getting her to agree.
"So she doesn't have to suffer anymore, be there for her, and guide her like you always have…"
"How good-natured can you possibly be? …No, how ill-natured could you possibly be?"
"The person who's going to suffer the most from now on isn't Kazusa, it's you."
But as I try to rush a solution from her, Youko-san keeps stopping me in my tracks.
Do I look… that helpless right now?
"As for Kazusa, ignoring how people around her will react, she herself will be the happiest she has ever been. After all, she'll be with and protected by the man she loves more than anyone else."
"But you… there'll be no one to protect you. After all, Kazusa doesn't have that kind of strength."
"She can do nothing but stay by your side and play the piano at her own leisure even as you're going to be working yourself to the bone."
"True hell might be awaiting you in the future."
Youko-san… is telling me things that no longer hold sway over me with the way things have turned out.

"As you'll be busy protecting Kazusa, you'll be unable to communicate with anyone else. You'll be stepping into a place where everything you come across will be new to you. It's fair to say it'll be more difficult than living alone…"
An ant works restlessly in preparation for the winter, while the grasshopper sings with grace and spends its days having fun.
That's why only the ant will survive the winter, or so the fable goes.
"You also can't afford to give up on your decision. After all, if you were ever to collapse, it would mean that she would collapse with you…"

And outside the world of fables, in the real world, the grasshopper will revel in the enjoyment of playing the piano, while the ant will do everything it can to fill the stash of food to last the winter.
And from now on, it will have to provide for the grasshopper as well.
All while having to abandon its own nest… and alienating itself from all the other ants.
"You'll be bearing an unimaginable pressure in a completely different land… Even if it's you, I would question the possibility of you being able to survive…"
"As long as Kazusa is by my side, I'll be fine, you know?"
"I never expected her to protect me. As I always have, I'll find my potential in my life by myself."
That may be simply an attempt from me to put up a front before Youko-san.
"I'll make sure to find employment over there, I'll learn the necessary language, and the two of us… no, the three of us will bear it all together."
Even though I have been adamant about this since the beginning, she has diverted the thread of the conversation to the bitter end. This is my tiny form of revenge for that.
"As long as she's with me, I'll be capable of all that. And she can just sit there close to me, and play her piano all day if she wants."
However… there wasn't the slightest hint of a joke in what I said then.
"And if it's to protect Kazusa, I'll help you out too."
It's truly an arrogant thing to say to someone who makes probably a hundred times the amount I make, and has many decades more experience than me.
But I was completely serious about taking responsibility for her life. It's because it's a way that I can make Kazusa even happier.
"So please, come with us. Make her the happiest grasshopper in the world."
The elated grasshopper will survive the winter with a smile with the ant by its side…
Youko-san looks me straight in the eyes once again.
I notice a slightly exhausted smile spread across her face, not knowing if she's finally given up on trying to dissuade me or if she's just tired of my stubbornness.
And with the same soft expression…
She finally said it. The answer she had avoided giving all this time.
"Why are you apologizing, Haruki? Is it not my fault for putting all the responsibility on you?"
"The sins I committed, the absurdities I asked of you… that's something the daughter should be talking to her mother about."
"I knew from the beginning. I was prepared for the worst ever since I heard about her illness, so you don't have to give me that worried look."
Even as Kazusa hears about the devastating results of my conversation with Youko-san, she still does her best to encourage me.
"But, I see… Mom isn't leaving Japan anymore…"
Though in the end, that forced strength of hers didn't last more than a few seconds.
Youko-san had stubbornly kept to her own resolve.
Her resolve to "die in the country she was born in" took precedence over anything else, and as a Japanese person myself, I could not do anything but to accept that.
"It's not like it's decided she won't come with us. I'll try talking to her again next week."
While the fact was obvious to Kazusa, I was unable to hide my shock when I learned her verdict.
"Youko-san isn't feeling very well right now, but her point of view might change when she feels better."
Only Youko-san will stand up for us no matter what…
Despite everything, I thought she would stay by Kazusa's side.
"That's not true. We can't give up."
I was under the naive delusion that the chain reaction of negative events would take a break in this instance.
"Isn't it said that people become more honest when they're weak…?"
"I did, of course… Haven't I proven that to you already?"
"So I understand… Mom really wants to stay in Japan. That's more important than anything to her."
"But if Youko-san is alone in staying in Japan, then you…"
Then Kazusa won't be there during her final moments…
"Don't worry, even if the European branch of Touma Youko Office becomes completely inactive, I'll still be able to provide for myself somehow."
Yet to Kazusa, that possibility is too cruel to even come to her mind.
"Somehow…? How, exactly? Are you capable of operating an office?"
"I'll do a much easier job. Perhaps I'll teach the kids around the neighborhood how to play the piano. I'll be able to make enough money for myself then, right?"
"You, a teacher? …Perhaps it'd make for a good comedy."
So I go along with Kazusa, and divert the conversation.
"Those quips of yours are really lame, you know? I should be fine with dealing with kids somehow. Don't underestimate me."
After all, if she starts to agonize over that possibility, then we might be unable to move forward.
For as long as she decides to make Japan… or rather, Houjou Hospital her own battleground, we will be unable to stay by her.
"You yourself shouldn't underestimate kids. You'll need to be able to communicate with them in a way that's more complex than dealing with adults."
The two of us no longer have the choice to stay in Japan.
We cannot commit any more sins than we already have…
We cannot plant our roots in a place where Setsuna is present.
"Can I sleep at your place tonight?"
"Only sleeping. I won't break the promise we made."
"I wasn't really worried about you… but I can't guarantee I'll be able to hold myself back…"
"Even less reason to worry then. You're not that weak-willed, and you were the one who made me swear that stupid oath in the first place."
"…And all without even a hint of consideration about how I felt."
"It's okay, I understand. I've known that you're that kind of person for a long time."
We cannot plant our roots in a place where Setsuna is present.
"Sorry. I forgot to put it in silent mode."
"No, it was from work. And it's probably not anything urgent either."
There was a slight glint of doubt in her eyes.
However, what I said was the truth. It wasn't from Setsuna.
…But it was also a lie. It wasn't a call from work either.
"…Let's go home. You must be hungry."
The truth is, I had hoped for a little more time. I wanted to think about what I would tell them…
I turned off the power of my cell phone that had the words "Iizuka Takeya" written on its display.
"Uhm… Anyway, here's to a day's hard work! Cheers～!"
Takeya is desperate. He's desperate to try and keep everyone in high spirits.
…Almost as if trying to deny the reason the four of us are gathered here in the first place.
"Alright, let's start ordering. I'm in the mood for some Korean Jjigae, what do you guys think?"
"I see… Then let's just order a large variety of stuff instead. Let's see here, french fries and cold tofu…"
"Fine, I get it. You want some Dashimaki eggs, right? No matter where we eat you always…"
"We'll handle things from here. You can just sit there and drink."
He was desperate to hold back Yanagihara Tomo, who seemed ready for a fight. And Io, who looked like she was dying to say something.
From the moment I showed my face in the meeting spot by the station, to the moment we reached the bar table.
It was Takeya's idea to discuss this in a bar. A bit unlike himself, he's going above and beyond to make things easier… for me alone.
But once our toasts were said, there was no longer any stopping these two.
"Kitahara-san… what did you do to Setsuna?"
"Ah, I'll explain from the start. Thing is, ever since the beginning of the week…"
"No, I keep telling you it's all a misunderstanding, yet Tomo is jumping to all kinds of weird conclusions…"
"Do you have any idea what state Setsuna is in right now? …It's all because of you, you know."
"I do think she's exaggerating a little bit. But it's true that Setsuna isn't answering any of our calls."
"It's probably because of something stupid, right? It shouldn't be anything worth getting so worked up about. Tomo is just being overly nosy as always."
"Hold on a second! Don't interrupt me… Didn't I invite you guys so you could hear what I have to say?"
"But the one who invited Haruki was me."
"And the one who convinced Takeya was me. So we can't let you just throw around accusations unchallenged. Though I'm not going to defend Haruki to the same extent as Takeya."
They all looked like they had many questions to ask me, but it was too disorganized to get anywhere.
But everything from their opinions to their information was completely scattered.
The difference of opinion between Tomo and the other two was like night and day.
"You can't… get in touch with Setsuna?"
"I asked her mother, and it seems she is at least still going to work. So I think she might just be sulking a little bit."
"I keep telling you I saw her! She was crying her eyes out, right in front of his apartment!"
"…She has been like this since the beginning of the week. So we thought we had to talk to you about it, at least."
"I've never seen Setsuna like that before… Even back then, two years ago, she was never like this."
This Sunday, she was in front of my apartment…?
"What did you tell her? …No, there is only one thing that could put her in that state. You broke up with her, didn't you?"
"Like I said, calm down. Why do you always have to go with the first thing that comes to your mind?"
"Well, something could have happened which ultimately led to the topic of breaking up in the heat of the moment, but obviously they wouldn't mean it."
"That's not true! You're only saying that because you haven't seen how bad Setsuna is doing right now."
Tomo uses every fiber of her being denouncing me, yet it still isn't enough.
Or rather, the harder she pushes against me, the more the other two come to my defense.
"Tell me, Kitahara-san… You're together with Touma Kazusa now, aren't you? You've been seeing her in secret, haven't you?"
