"Yet… even though we differed in almost every aspect, your awful taste in men was frighteningly similar to mine…"
"That's why I betrayed you. You tried to understand me, to love me, yet I betrayed you in the worst possible way, twice."
"I know it's not the right thing to do. I know no one will accept it. But I can't help myself from betraying you."
"It's because I'm weak. It's because I'm an awful person that I can't help but to take Haruki away from you."
"That's why the three of us can't be together anymore. It's not your fault, it's not Haruki's fault either… It's my fault."
"That's okay. I'm speaking on my own accord."
"If the strong Setsuna I once knew and adored has lost her strength because of me…"
"I'll make up for it… with my life as a pianist."
"Yeah, you're right. It's just for my own self-satisfaction."
"I can't do any house work, in fact, I'm probably incapable of doing anything that helps others."
"I know that compared to what I did to you, Setsuna, this isn't nearly enough to make up for it…"
"But my piano is all I have going for me. Without it, I'm completely useless…"
"So… it's the only thing I can give up. I'm sorry, Setsuna."
It truly had been a while.
Getting wasted like that, talking that much, laughing, and letting loose my feelings.
And the first time in a while I showed such a pathetic side of myself, and the first time I felt relief from pain.
Even though I was supposed to throw everything in Japan away, I made a few memories I can take with me when I leave.
They might have just sugarcoated their words. They might have simply said what they should as proper adults.
Yet I was grateful for their regard for me, from the bottom of my heart.
My entire body feels like it's burning. My face, my throat, and even my eyes.
I've been unable to sleep for the past week, and should be sleep deprived, and yet…
I don't feel like I can fall asleep for a different reason tonight. Perhaps it's better to say that I don't want to sleep.
I feel dizzy from just taking a step out of the elevator.
Normally, I'm the one who lectures my friends and coworkers for drinking this much, while supporting them on my shoulders.
I heave a drunk sigh and lean on the wall, and walk alongside it.
All while trying and just barely managing to make as little noise as possible.
She has a concert tomorrow. I can't wake her up today of all days.
It'd be fine if she was sleeping in her own apartment, but if she's in my bed, then…
She has a concert tomorrow. I can't wake her up today of all days.
If she's sleeping in her own apartment that'd be fine, but if she's in my…
"Kazusa! Hey, what the hell are you doing?"
This was no time to think of being delicate in my phrasing.
"You have a concert tomorrow and you're trying to freeze yourself to death? Come on… Could you please stop being so unreasonable, for once?"
Kazusa completely ignores my clumsy outburst and smiles at me gently.
…An expression that radiates loneliness, and pain.
"Ah, I have the keys for both apartments… I think."
"Then why aren't you inside? Literally all you had to do is to turn the key and open the door! How lazy can you be?"
"About that, I, uh… really wanted… to see your face, Haruki."
"Ah, uhm… I told you I was going to show up tomorrow."
"I wanted to see you… right away… or, as fast as I could."
I certainly could sense that her feelings came from a desire to be spoiled by me.
But her voice isn't just conveying her desire to be spoiled; something completely different is spreading across her expression…
"N-No… I'm fine. I'll stand up on my own."
Without even attempting to grab my outstretched hand, she sits completely still.
She said she wanted to see me, yet here I am, and the uncertainty and bitterness in her eyes have still not gone away.
Almost as if trying to get away from my hands, she puts her own hands behind her back and hides them between herself and the wall.
Her behavior was unreasonable as always, yet my intoxication did away with any patience left in me.
"You're going to catch a cold! Get a hold of yourself and stop sulking for no reason!"
I kneel in front of her, wrap my hands around her back almost as if embracing her, and feel for her hands.
She resisted, of course, but compared to the strength of a man… or the strength of anyone at all, considering the state she's in…
Eventually, I grab onto her hands and let out an anguished expression…
"Your hands are almost like ice! Can you even play the piano tomorrow like this? Seriously, what were you thinking…?"
"Why… do I have to be so healthy."
And then, she mutters something incomprehensible.
Kazusa's hands were incredibly cold… but like always, they were thin, white and smooth.
"I'm sorry. I dropped this glass. I'll clean it up right away!"
"Ah… N-No! I'll take care of it. Don't touch the glass."
"I took away all your happiness! I ruined your life!"
"Moreover, this is the second time I've done that. All I've ever done is to get between you and Haruki."
"Don't you… feel at least a little bit of hatred toward me? Don't you want to make me feel the same pain you feel?"
"I barely understood at all. Nothing you said even registered in my head. None of it mattered to me at all…"
"I just said I don't know! I was holding on to your hand before I even realized it. I was desperately trying to stop your idiotic act."
"…Even though it wasn't supposed to have anything to do with me."
"I don't understand… I don't understand anything!"
"Haruki, Haruki, Haruki… Uu-ugh… I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I've…"
"Don't cling to me so much right now. I reek of booze."
"I broke Setsuna… I tried to protect you, but I only made things worse."
No matter how many times I tell her to get off me, or try to push her away, she ignores me completely and rubs her face against my chest.
Almost as if trying to keep the smell of me from escaping, including the smell of alcohol.
Kazusa went to see Setsuna in secret.
It seems because she saw how I was suffering from the ordeal with Setsuna, she tried to go out to protect me herself.
That sounds exactly like her… a thoughtless, rash and pointless action.
"I didn't expect her to forgive me, but I still wanted to apologize. I wanted to make up for it… I wanted to talk to her."
Obviously, they'd both just end up getting hurt.
Yet the idea of saving me completely took control of her. She did something that had no meaning at all for Setsuna, but something that meant all the world to herself.
In the end, she only made things worse for Setsuna. It was plain as day from the start that Setsuna would completely break down.
"No matter how hard you think, you'll never find a good solution. In fact, you'll only make things worse."
"You're completely useless when it comes to things like this."
"Hey… just because it's true… doesn't mean you have to be so extreme about it."
"You're the one who's being extreme. Always thinking of these idiotic things."
The more I lecture her, the more absurd her actions seem.
"You even thought about abandoning the piano for my sake. Really… you're just so silly that I can't let you out of my sight."
And right before the day of the concert, of all days.
"That's because it's important to me… So it shows just how important you are to me."
And even though her hands were spared, I still have doubts if she can play tomorrow from the pure psychological stress.
"…Drop the idea that in order to gain something valuable, you have to throw away something of equal value."
I have some words about her overestimating herself… but right now, I won't touch on any subject heavy in emotion.
If I do, I'll be the one to break down.
"Think of it like this. If you need your piano to be happy, keep it. If you don't need it… then you can throw it away."
Because even now, the warmth of Kazusa's skin, her softness, her sweet smell… light up my senses all in harmony.
"I don't know… I still don't know…"
That warm breath touches my chest, and I find it even harder to restrain myself.
"It was always there since the day I was born. I spent more than half of the time in my life working with it… much more than the time I spent with you."
It is probably not Kazusa's intention to make me feel that way. I'm making a big deal out of it by myself, but it's still cruel.
"And it's not just you. The whole thing with my mom… with Touma Youko, and…"
"Then you don't have to come to a conclusion right away. Once we're back in Vienna… you can take your time and decide."
Doing my best to prevent my inner conflict from becoming apparent to her, I slacken the muscles in my arms and pull Kazusa toward my chest.
I feel her warmth. And allow myself to be restrained.
"That's precisely why… you should forget about everything tomorrow and just play to your heart's content."
"Show us what you're made of… and give your Japanese audience your final goodbye."
In my arms, I feel Kazusa growing warmer.
"I'll play. I'll show you I can. As long as you're by my side, I won't be afraid of anything…"
"So be there to watch over me during the concert… and all the other times too."
"When I lie down like this being embraced by you, I can feel my wounds heal. I can get back up on my feet, even if I feel miserable."
"And I'll… keep doing this for you from now on. I won't let you feel lonely anymore…"
"How do you think… Setsuna will heal her wounds from now on?"
"She got hurt so badly because of me. And yet she hasn't changed at all deep down inside."
"She teases me without even realizing it, yet when push comes to shove, she just can't help but destroy herself."
"Not even thinking about how it's breaking her apart…!"
"She's strong, and always sees through people. She is always a step ahead of everybody, and prevents them from getting away…"
"That's why I really don't know how to handle her. I somewhat dislike her, I am jealous of her, and I admire her…"
"But she was hopelessly kind to me, even up until the very end. She refused to admit I was wrong, she let go of my hand, and she stopped me in my tracks…"
"That's why in the end, I couldn't hate her. I loved her…"
"Haruki… if you hadn't come into the picture, perhaps the two of us might have become the best of friends."
"…No, if you hadn't been around, I wouldn't even have met her in the first place."
"You were the one who brought Setsuna and I together. And you're also the reason we ended up severing our ties."
"…I'll resent you for that, you know."
"Yeah, resent me for the rest of your life."
"You're fine with it, right? I'll remind you of it for the rest of my life. I'll be by your side, and tell you about it at every opportunity, forever."
"In exchange, I'll defend myself. Like that, we can bicker over it for as long as it takes."
That's right, let's bicker. As many times as it takes.
Let's overwhelm ourselves in a love so powerful that we can get hurt, quarrel, and get sick of each other, and still go on despite that.
"Even if my love can't reach you… will it one day reflect back to me…?"
"Let's see… You'll be sitting here, Youko-san. You can go in a bit further, Takayanagi-sensei."
"I don't think this is the most pleasant way to get seated."
There's only 30 minutes before the concert.
The VIP seats were almost completely empty compared to the regular ones.
"That's because you aren't exactly in good shape. Be good and let us guys escort you."
"How wonderful, looks like you've got two dashing gentlemen tending to you from both sides… Of course, I'm not at all happy about having to be compared to someone so much younger than me."
As expected, Youko-san didn't have kind words to say about being dragged by the underarm to her seat, almost like a sick person.
…Not to say that she isn't sick.
"I'm sorry for making you do this despite your busy schedule, Doctor."
"You're not making him do anything. He's an old senile doctor who retired ages ago."
"Setting your abusive language aside, which clearly only exists to hide your embarrassment, I fully understand why you'd go this far to see your daughter's shining moment."
"…I do feel that you went a bit safe though."

"Why do you always have to interpret things in a way that suits you? This is precisely the reason I cannot stand old men past their sixties. You can't even get it up, yet your mind is as dirty as always."
"…Don't get so worked up about it. I'll throw you out before the concert starts if you get too rowdy."
The intensity of their verbal battle didn't suggest that she had gone a bit safe at all, or that he couldn't get it up anymore.
"Either way, be good today. If I see even a hint of your health failing, I'll force you down on my bed."
"…Like I'd let you do that. Besides, if my health were to fail, it'd be your job to take care of it on the spot."
"…Careful not to ask too much. Remember that others might be looking."
Yet, behind Youko-san's attitude lie feelings that only I could see. There was a disconnect between them.
That this could very well be the last time Youko-san could hear her daughter perform live.
I look around and see that the seats are about 70% full.
Whether this is a good amount or not is impossible to judge for someone who doesn't normally attend piano concerts…
But considering all the noise that was made when the tickets were still on sale, I doubt the beginning of the concert will be a quiet one.
I don't want to think about it that much, but perhaps…
This is the result of the mediocre reception that the last concert got…
Perhaps she had enough of me looking around the theater restlessly, thinking about things I shouldn't.
"Aren't you going to pay her a visit? You haven't seen her yet, have you?"
Youko-san interrupts me, but probably with the best intentions in mind.
"You won't be able to do so right before they start, you know? You should go while you still can."
"Eh, but… are you sure I can?"
"The one guarding her room is Miyo-chan, so you'll be fine. Besides…"
"That girl won't ever close a door to you again."
"Why don't you go there and give her your prince's kiss? I'm sure it'll motivate her greatly."
"You should be doing that after the concert as a reward, when she's done good."
"…I'll be right back! I promise it'll only take a short while! It's nothing major, really!"
Remaining stubborn with her, or being forced to sit by and watch these two restless adults go after each other was far too unbearable to me, so I got off my seat and left.
When I woke up this morning, Kazusa muttered "good morning" to me with her face still buried in my chest, as if waiting for me to wake up.
Her expression was sleepy, calm, and very relaxed; it was definitely not the look of a musician with a concert to perform the same day.
It's been half a day since then… I wonder if she was focusing properly. Did she get back that look that tells me she's prepared for battle?
It's not like I can advise her on anything, but if I can improve her mood somehow…
Or maybe I'll be able to put my own mind at ease by seeing her face…
And just before I started to open the door to the dressing room…
A loud ringing came from my phone, which I forgot to turn off.
The moment my phone rang, my first thought was that of relief that it didn't ring while I was still in my seat in front of everyone.
But once I saw the name displayed on the screen, a name so utterly out of place for the present situation, that feeling of relief disappeared in an instant.
I heard that rude and harsh voice just a few days ago.
…One that declared that our friendship had come to an end.
"Are you working? Even if you are, there's just one thing I want you to tell me."
"No, I'm free right now… Well, what is it?"
"…Can't you guess, considering it's me who's calling you?"
Having someone I never expected to ever hear from weighed heavily on my heart, but…
"She's not… with you. She's not… with you either…"
"I keep asking… what do you mean?"
And as if her reaction further shrouded everything in dark clouds, I found myself even more distraught.
That's why it didn't take me much time to finally understand the meaning behind her words.
"She hasn't been home all week, but she still went to work as usual."
"But today she didn't even show up for work, and we can't reach her on her cell phone either…"
"It's your fault… It's all your fault, Kitahara-san!"
…I didn't want to understand what she was saying.
"Calm down, Youko-chan. If you get any more worked up, I'll have to take you back to the hospital."
"They probably just have a lot to talk about. They're young, after all."
"I have no idea what you're fantasizing about. What are you saying they could possibly be doing three minutes before the concert?"
"In that case, maybe he just left for a smoke in the lounge? I'm sure he'll come back once the concert starts."
"He doesn't smoke, and he's not that inconsiderate, besides…"
"If he doesn't come, there is no doubt this is going to end just like last time. That alone must be avoided no matter what."
This isn't the first time this has happened.
"Everyone is worried. Please contact me as soon as you read this."
Two years ago when our relationship was uncertain, we kept ignoring each other… Setsuna disappeared twice.

The first time was simply because of my own eagerness, when Setsuna disappeared from the mixer with the medical students. I traced her steps, and the search developed into a search party that involved everyone.
The second time was none other than Yanagihara Tomo's fault, when Setsuna was almost forced to appear on stage, and ran away.
Each time I involved everyone around me, and organized a search on a large scale in an attempt to find her.
I'd coerce the medical students, force freshmen I'd just met to help me out. I'd call old classmates of mine to help out. Ridiculous things like that.
And they would usually be forced to join in on my absurd efforts during times like those…
"…Why are you calling me? I thought we settled everything."
I used to have precious friends.
"Of course I'm worried. That's why I'm doing everything I can to search for her right now. Tomo is even calling everyone she knows for help."
"I see… you still haven't made up."
"And whose… whose fault do you think that is?"
These friends of mine who are truly precious and irreplaceable to me despite the fact that our bonds have more or less collapsed at this point because of me…
"So, how's the search going? Do you have any leads?"
"…What do you intend to do if I tell you, Haruki?"
"This has nothing to do with you anymore, right? What do you think you'll accomplish by looking for Setsuna now?"
When I thought I was going to lose Setsuna, the hands that Io and Takeya reached out to me in my moment of utter anxiety was so reassuring.
"I told Tomo to not contact you… I told her to not do something so pointless…"
The everyday banter that would have no meaning to anyone but us three. The lighthearted atmosphere that softened my desperation, and eased the pain from my heart.
"I'll ask again, Haruki. Why did you call me?"
Those conversations that we took for granted are now nothing but a nostalgic memory.
And those days will most likely… no, most certainly never come back.
"Are you sure you should be saying that? Isn't her concert about to start right about now? Isn't that the most important thing for you now?"
"Do you have any guesses on… where she could be?"
Yet, right now I have no choice but to ignore her reaction, as if I never heard it.
"For how long have you been looking for her? How close are you to finding her?"
"I don't have to… tell you anything…"
"This isn't the time for that! I thought you were worried about Setsuna! You should be accepting help from any source you can get, seeing how desperate things are, shouldn't you!?"
Up until now, she has told me as little as she could get away with, but now I have to force it out of her.
"I know Setsuna better than anyone. There's even a chance she might contact me… I'm the only one who can find her!"
"If you trust her so much, then why… If you understand each other so well, then why…!?"
Because I absolutely have to find Setsuna right now.
The two of us can't reconcile, yet we still have to work together to achieve a common goal.
"Tell me… Where have you called about her? Where have you still not looked for her?"
"Tell me then, Haruki… what will you do when you find her?"
"Talk about what? Are you going to promise her that you'll never hurt her again? Are you going to wrap your arms around her and tell her that she never needs to worry again?"
"Setsuna isn't as strong as you think… you know this already, don't you!?"
"…In any case, I'll talk to her. I can't promise anything other than that."
"I'm begging you, Haruki… don't make her cry any more than she already has…!"
"Don't go to Vienna… Your elopement will not bring a single person happiness!"
"You and Touma-san don't suit each other anymore… She'll only get hurt from this in the end too. You'll both be crushed under the pressure."
"We can talk about it once I've found Setsuna."
Io's words have been repeated to me by countless people. It was a truism without any originality.
Yet, I couldn't bring myself to find those words boring or tedious, and I couldn't say with certainty that I felt nothing upon hearing them.
"…Tell me where you've looked up until now. Also, call Takeya and ask him to help out. If you don't want to, I'll do it."
"…I'll do that. So you should try to contact Setsuna. Call her, text her."
"I've already done that. And I'll continue to do that."
"I'm begging you, Haruki! Everything is your fault, but you're the only one we can rely on… Find Setsuna…"
I wonder if my dry voice managed to deceive her. I wonder if I could prevent my feelings from reaching the other side of the line.
"You have reached the voicemail for this number. Please leave a message after the beep."
"Where are you right now? If you can hear this, call me… I'll come for you right away."
"Everyone is really worried about you. Your family, Yanagihara-san, Io, Takeya… and me too, of course."
"Do what you want to me, but don't cause too much trouble to everyone else. It's not like you to do that, Setsuna."
"…I know I'm being hypocritical. But if you're safe, I want you to contact me…!"
"That's it for now, I'll call you again."
When I cut the call, the display changes to the home screen. The time is written in the middle: 19:00."
It doesn't simply refer to the fact that it's 7 PM; it's the time we made a promise for…
I ignore it, put my cell phone back in my pocket, and rush to the station.
To find Setsuna… to check all the places she might be.
"It's fine… Have some faith in your daughter."
"And have you considered… contacting the police?"
"You're right… Things have changed since yesterday, we should start considering it."
"Yeah… I think it might be a good idea. I can go ahead and do so if you want."
"Thank you very much. But it's fine, we'll call the police ourselves."
"I see, very well. Then I'll keep checking…"
"So please, you should go home, Kitahara-san. I am deeply grateful for your concern… Good night."
"Mhn… It's fine! I'm begging you, please…"
"It's okay, it's okay… Setsuna is a strong girl. I'm certain… she'll come home."
"So please, don't worry… Don't bother yourself with us…"
"Aaah… I… I'm sorry…! I'll end the call."
Once the Ogiso family came to a dead end in the search for their daughter, they decided to report her as missing.
That's why Mother… Setsuna's mother told me that I had done enough.
This was no longer a matter for family or friends to handle. This was a job for the police…
That's the reason she refused to see me. There was no other reason for her not to look me in the face, even though I was right outside her door.
There is no point in thinking about that. Right now, I can't worry about anything other than finding Setsuna.
"If you see this text, contact your family immediately."
"I was just over at your place and talked with your mother. After some consideration, they decided to call the police."
"Everyone is really worried about you. Your mom hasn't slept all night because she's worried that something's happened to you."
"So if you can see this text, and still haven't contacted her even though you could…"
"Quit screwing around! Don't cause so much trouble for everyone."
I came off as really arrogant, and beyond hypocritical…
I sent her the text which contains my all too familiar lecturing.
And I prayed. I prayed that Setsuna would respond immediately and in that all too familiar way.
Just when I was starting to be at a loss after searching every location nearby that I could think of, it finally came.
"I just called my family. You can stop worrying now."
Setsuna is a good girl. She's diligent, and strong.
That's why when she understands that she's causing everyone to worry, she'll react immediately.
That's why I used that tactic. An underhanded tactic that I was sure would be impossible for her to ignore.
My five calls earlier got transferred to voicemail, but now my call is continuing.
It's probably because I called her right after I got her text, so she didn't manage to turn off her phone in time.
Seeing my name written on the screen must be giving her pause right about now.
So it's only a matter of whether she responds or not. My chances are good.
Because I'm not hanging up the call from my end…
"To go as far as calling the police… all of you were going way overboard."
This is the first time I've heard Setsuna's voice in days.
"No, it's not… everyone was extremely worried."
She's sulking, and she sounds tired. There is a sadness in her voice.
"I'm an adult now, you know? I can take some alone time if I want…"
"Then make sure people can reach you first. If you don't, then you aren't being an adult."
"Where are you right now? I'll come get you."
"Yes, I do. I'm coming over there, and I'm taking you home."
Is it from being lectured by me of all people, or is she shivering from the utter cold?
"Why are you trying to do this? What does it matter to you if I don't go home?"
"If you don't go home, Setsuna… I won't sleep in peace."
"And why would that be the case…? I already said that you don't need to worry about me anymore…"
"I don't need a reason. I'm just worried about you! Everyone else is worried too, so give us some peace of mind. Show us that you're doing okay…"
On the other end of the line, Setsuna sounded calmer than I expected.
"Where are you…? Where in the world are you right now, Setsuna? Please tell me."
I use that fact to lift my spirits, and I try to connect with Setsuna.
"I do want to see you, Setsuna."
To look for the severed end of the thread that once bound us together.
"Then, I'll give you hints. If you don't get it right after the third one…
"Eh? No, wait a minute! Is this song of yours that important…?"
"Hint number one. Our… place filled with memories."
"…I can't guess from just that. We have too many of those."
I heard her gulp on the other line.
Almost as if wordlessly telling me "You're really going to say that?"
"Sorry… but this quiz is the one I simply cannot get wrong."
But there really are too many places to count.
Places I visited with Setsuna by my side.
Places where we grew closer, where we drifted apart, where we shared our love, where we argued.
Just within this city there are too many to count. If you include places we've been on vacation, it'd take more than a day just to list them all.
That's how deeply engraved it is, the history between Setsuna and me. Engraved in this country…
"…Then, second hint. I'm looking at the sea right now."
"Don't move! Stay right where you are! I'll be there right away!"
After transiting from one train to another twice…
Once I got off at Arumi Station, I knew the way.
Because only two weeks ago… Setsuna was here.
"Let's go home… it's cold out here."
"Let's at least go somewhere warm… Don't you feel under the weather?"
Setsuna's face was white as snow.
Normally, I would put my hand against her forehead against her will and measure her temperature. That's just how worried I would be.
But I threw away the right to touch Setsuna by my own will…
"There was no point in running away."
"In the end, I only made you worry, Haruki-kun. I got in the way of Kazusa's concert. It all came to nothing."
"It means when something that you worked hard on is undone."
"I'm always like this. I try to make things better, but only end up making things worse. It's really no wonder things turned out this way…"
"Saying that I wasn't thinking is really nothing but an excuse. I'm really stupid, I know."
"No… I was purposely trying to avoid thinking about things turning out this way. After all, I'm filthy."
I didn't understand what Setsuna was talking about.
The words that Kazusa told me creep up in my consciousness, saying "I broke her."
Yet the expression on her face and her words sounded normal, just like the usual, kind Setsuna I've come to know.
…She was still the woman I knew better than anyone else.
"Were you… looking at the sea all this time?"
"When I left Kazusa, I couldn't bring myself to return. Not to my hotel, not home."
"So I asked myself where I wanted to go."
"This wasn't the only place that came to mind, I thought of a lot of places."
"For example, the park near my house… the place where you saw the real me."
"So you knew about it all along… this side of me."
"You've known about me for so long, Kitahara-kun…"
That was where I got to know Setsuna for the first time… the place where I met her in her casual wear.

The school idol who would work part-time in disguise. The school idol who would complain about things that were her own fault. The school idol who would worry about her hungry brother waiting for her to return for dinner…
"The karaoke bar in Minami-Suetsugu… where I went on a date with a boy for the first time."
"With this, Ogiso Setsuna's last secret has been revealed… You've just learned all about me."
An idol whose inconsiderateness when it concerns singing almost made me flinch.
Singing for as long as the reserved time would allow, and even picking a song right before the time was up just to sing for a few extra minutes.
And when I looked at her dumbfounded, she teasingly stuck out her tongue at me. No longer did I see her as an idol, but as a girl by the name of Ogiso Setsuna.
"I thought of many other places too. Kazusa's house, the school… Did you know today is the graduation ceremony?"
"So many places came to mind… all the roads I walked with you, all the places I visited with you."
All of those are places we made memories in together, and places where memories of the three of us rested.
And out of all those places, she chose…
"Before I realized it, I was here…"
This place was indeed a place of many memories for Setsuna and me. It was, but…
"It's strange, isn't it…? There are still so many… so many other fun places!"
"The amusement park, the zoo, the cinema… memories of us laughing together, loving each other are imprinted on so many other places too."
"Yet, no matter what, no matter what… I came to this place."
"It feels like everything was overwritten, don't you agree? It feels like this is the only place our memories together still remain."
"When I'm here, I recall that day."
This is the place of our most recent memory, and the place of our saddest memory…
"It happened just the other day, yet it feels like ages ago. It actually happened, yet I remember it like some bad dream… No, perhaps that's just what I want it to be."
"So it's really painful, and sad. I feel like I'm about to lose myself… no, I think I've already begun to lose my mind."
"So I thought to myself that none of it mattered… that everything is just too much trouble… that I don't want to see anybody… that I want to be alone."
"You're only thinking that because you're in this freezing cold…"
It's because you're in this awful, cold place.
Why are you doing this to yourself…?
"For three years, we kept missing one another. For two years, we were in each other's arms."
I'm sorry for those three years, and I'm… grateful for those two years.
"We piled up a hill of so much happiness, and so much sadness."
"We are bound in both body and soul. It can't be torn off now, after all this time."
Our history together, that cannot be surpassed by anyone.
"I wouldn't be myself anymore if I let that bond be torn off."
"What about you…? Can you say you're truly Kitahara Haruki if you tear off that bond…?"
"Will you be able to remain yourself?"
Right now, I'm not the Kitahara Haruki you see.
"Was I that ineffective at leaving an impression on you? Was our bond… so fragile that you could just tear it off like that?"
Five years ago, I chose Kazusa, not you…
I'm… the Kitahara Haruki from a different history. A me that you don't know anymore, Setsuna.
I'm hit by her questions like a blade piercing my chest, and I bear it in silence.
Because if I let the thoughts I keep repressed gush out, my terrible resolve will be for nothing.
But neither am I strong nor correct enough to coldly deflect her questions in order to protect that resolve.
And as a result… I continue leaving Setsuna in a state of uncertainty in the most despicable act.
After letting herself be swept away by her emotions, she speaks in a light voice.
And then she takes a deep breath, calms herself down, closes her eyes, and stops her tears.
"I'm overwhelmed by so much sadness and yet…"
And a few seconds later, when Setsuna spoke again…
"I feel a sadness like the whole world is ending. I feel like I'm losing something just as important as the whole world…"
Her voice was shaking, but just barely.
"Even so, I turned on my phone earlier… and I called my family."
I could feel a hint of anger and irritation… and the slightest bit of relief in her voice.
"My mom was crying. My dad was happy about my well-being like it was his own. And they told me that Takahiro had been out looking for me all night…"
I did everything in my power to hide my relief at those words, to hide the smile that was creeping up on me.
Even if I am happy, I have long since given up the right to show her that.
"I'm sorry, Haruki-kun… no, perhaps this has nothing to do with you anymore."
It has… everything to do with me…
"Remember what I told you? That I was going to abandon Japan, and follow you two along. That I was prepared to do even that…"
"But that was a lie. I can't bring myself to cease being a child of the Ogiso family. I can't bring myself to stop being Japanese."
I wanted to nod with every fiber of my being.
Even if I no longer had the right, I didn't want to think that this had nothing to do with me.
I only wanted to one-sidedly let out my thoughts, only to have her watch as I try to stop myself from saying too much.
"At the very end, I never broke completely… I couldn't obsess about you to that degree…"
Because she wouldn't be Setsuna otherwise.
"I feel so much sadness, and I feel like my heart is about to burst open…"
She wouldn't stray away from rationality and intuition.
"But I thought about it… that my mom, dad, and Takahiro were worried about me."
Always adhering to both those things, and always wavering.
"I thought of how Io, Takeya-kun and Tomo were probably looking for me. I thought of the people at work, who tried to contact me but received no answer."
Always compromising, always naturally finding the balance.
That's the kind of girl Ogiso Setsuna wasーthe girl I loved.
"I couldn't bring myself to throw everything away and decide that none of it matters anymore…"
I loved her so deeply because that was the kind of girl she was.
I loved her more than anything.
"What's the matter with me, I wonder…?"
"It was pointless. Even when you abandoned me, I couldn't separate myself from the world."
It wasn't pointless at all. It was just like you to draw that conclusion, and it was the correct choice.
"So in the end, I couldn't win against Kazusa. I couldn't surpass Kazusa, who is capable of throwing everything away for your sake, Haruki-kun."
…But unable to tell her that, I simply hang my head.
"As I thought, my feelings weren't as powerful as Kazusa's… I wasn't that serious about you…!"
One after another, her words enter my head, and one after another, they wreak havoc.
Because I was the one who rejected Setsuna's feelings. I'm the one who tore the thread that bound us together apart.
"Tell her I'm sorry for getting in the way of her concert again."
By now, the concert should be in its final stage. I won't make it in time, even if I leave right now.
Just like that night in Osaka.
"This is the second time I lured you away from Kazusa… even though this day was so important to you two."
Just like on that day that marked the very beginning of the end, where something important had to be destroyed for the sake of recovering another.
"I'm sorry, I'm so sorry, I… on top of saying such cruel things to Kazusa, I've…"
Setsuna's apology came from a one-sided interpretation, one that is exactly like her to make.
"We promised… that she would play, that she would show the audience the best she's got, even if I'm not watching her."
Even so, I answer her words with a complete lie.
As I look down on my phone, and read the text that just arrived.
"I'll play. I'll show you I can. As long as you're by my side, I won't be afraid of anything…"
"So be there to watch over me during the concert… and all the other times too."
"Yeah, I'll watch over you… but that doesn't mean I'll always be there by your side."
"I'll be living for your sake from now on. All so you can still find the strength to smile and be happy in that tiny world of yours, even as you've cut yourself off from everything."
"I-I'll go! I promise I'll go! Didn't I just say that?"
"B-But you just said… you wouldn't be there by my side."
"Don't interpret things in the worst possible way… I meant that there might be times like that in the future… not tomorrow."
"It could be tomorrow, it could be a year from now. It might not even happen at all."
"But aren't you going to protect me from now on? Aren't you always going to be by my side?"
I already vowed to do that when I decided to pick Kazusa.
"But there might be times where protecting you and being with you aren't the same thing… and during times like that, I'll prioritize protecting you."
And so I made another vow, to never do anything that would get in the way of protecting her.
"There might be times when I'll have to be away for the sake of protecting you. From now on, there'll be times like that."
"I already told you I don't know. I can't predict the future, you know."
It might have been me being overly cautious and bringing up something with only the slightest possibility.
"Hey, Kazusa… From now on, my life will be dedicated to you… dedicated to living with you."
"But if there is something more important than being with you to make you happy, I might not be with you then."
"Like I said, why would that happen…? Where would you be if not with me?"
"I could be off working for you, I might be distancing myself for your sake, I might even be out there fighting for you."
Or perhaps I had a premonition something was about to happen.
"So I want you to trust me when that happens… that my absence is for your sake."
"That it's the best outcome for you that I'm not with you at that time."
"But my heart will always be with you. Even if I'm not physically there, we'll always be connected. Trust me already, would you…?"
"So you can stop worrying about that. Just be there and shine. Make a legend of yourself."
"Also, don't ever think of protecting me, or sacrificing yourself for my sake again. It's nothing but a bother to me."
"You're incapable of anything anyway… other than grinning as you play your piano. You don't have the ability to save me."
"Doesn't that… mean that I'm completely useless?"
"Be useless, for my sake. Be my reason to work as hard as I can."
The sound of Kazusa crying, along with her tears leaves a wet stain on my chest, and becomes my strength.
Something that is of absolutely no use to Kazusa, yet gives me a powerful energy.
"Uaaaah… Haruki, Haruki… I love you, I love you… uuh, haha… ahaha…!"
Those tears and that piano of hers… and that smile she shows ever so rarely.
"I might be unable to do anything but play the piano from now on… actually, that is probably most likely."
"I'm not good with money, I can't do chores, I might not even be able to make any money with my piano. I might be doing nothing but making your life a living hell."
"I've taken that into account ages ago."
"You'll push yourself to the limit for my sake, ruin your health, and maybe end up dying young."
"Hey… keep saying things like that and I actually might."
"However… if there is one thing I can take for certain it's this… if you die, I'll follow you right after."
"…Moron. You're awfully bold for someone who hasn't even lived half her life."
"And you can say whatever you want. I'll do everything I can to make something of myself… and if you think you can stop me, I dare you to try."
"Just so you know, I won't follow you. If you were to die before I do, I'll just go on through the pain and continue living out my life."
"Yes, I want you to do that… You'll be free from me then, and you'll be able to relax. Then you can live for as long as you want."
"You don't have to tell me that…"
"And if something like that were to ever happen… go and make up with Setsuna."
"If I'm dead, I'll allow it… you can go back to Setsuna then."
"You're an absolute moron, you know…? You really think Setsuna would be okay with that?"
"You know, there… there was a different path, a happier path we could have taken."
"…Go to sleep already. It's beginning to get bright outside."
"Setsuna would be there, crying in front of the altar, you'd get embarrassed, and I'd be there playing the organ."
"That future would have been the happiest future for the three of us… only if we could have managed to keep the balance between us."
"I don't think I've seen such a positive reception since… your own performance after your tour abroad."
"What spell did you put on her, Guitar-kun…?"
"It was a massive success, you bastard."
The text contained only one sentence, but to us, it conveyed countless feelings.
"How nice… I should've known she'd pull it off."
"I get it. She's capable of anything for her dear Haruki-kun."
She smiled as she looked like she was being torn to pieces by a blade. A blade born from the words, actions, and the bond between Kazusa and me.
"It's just like five years ago. No matter how much I tried to get in the way, nothing changed."
With that very same strength that I loved her for, she takes a step away from me.
"I'm glad… I'm so glad. Right, then… I'll leave you in Kazusa's care."
And in my eyes, she wore a smile that could tear herself apart.
"Just kidding… I was the one who stole you in the first place. I'm the one being unreasonable."
"Let me rephrase it. I'm sorry, Kazusa… I borrowed Haruki-kun for far too long, but now I'll give him back to you."
I shouldn't be feeling so much pain. I shouldn't reach out my hand to her.
Yet Setsuna looks as peaceful, and as kind as a saint.
"Congratulations, Kazusa. I'm glad your concert turned out well."
"Perhaps what I did paid off in the end? Perhaps it wasn't all for nothing."
It lasted for only a fleeting moment.
"I'm so glad I didn't get in your way. I'm so glad."
"I'm so glad no one found out. Not Kazusa, not Haruki-kun, not anyone…"
"Ah, can you see me? Do you understand me?"
"Don't try to stand up! Lie down! Someone call an ambulance!"
"Ah, no, wait… this isn't… The traffic light was green! This person came out of nowhere!"
"That doesn't matter right now! Call an ambulance already!"
"Don't argue and stay down. We'll go to the hospital and we'll see if it's anything serious, okay?"
"Can you recall the number to your family? Or perhaps your friends, your place of work…?"
"I can't…? You must still be very confused…"
"I'm not… It's not that big of a deal. Don't contact anyone!"
"Ah, wait a second… you shouldn't be standing up!"
"Look, I'm sure you have a concussion. For now you should just…"
"I'm really grateful… but I'm fine. Look, I'm not even bleeding."
"What if you have internal bleeding? Stay still until the ambulance arrives!"
"…No ambulance! I absolutely won't accept it!"
"No one can know about this! Tomorrow is the day of Kazusa's concert!"
"But this… if my family or my friends find out about this, so will she…"
"Ah, listen… calm down. Why are you running?"
"They cannot find out! Not Kazusa, not Haruki-kun… never!"
"Stop it! You shouldn't be running! Come back here!"
"Huh? Ah… Sorry, I spaced out for a bit."
With a fleeting smile, she closed her eyes, and for a few dozen seconds…
Almost as if she fell asleep on the spot, she completely lost touch with the outside world.
"I'm not cold, I'm not cold. That's not it at all…"
"But you're right. There is no point in being here anymore… we're finished with our conversation, after all."
And once she came back to her senses, she acted like nothing had happened.
"You can go home now. You can go back to Kazusa."
She begins our check-out from this place.
"I'll stay here… for a short while longer."
"You can't… not in this cold. If walking is too difficult for you, I'll call you a taxi."
"That's not what I meant. I actually just got a text from my mom… They're coming to pick me up by car soon."
"Don't you agree that it's just like my family to do that?"
I always liked that about them.
I long admired the family that had what I did not.
"They should be here soon. If you stay any longer, you'll have to face my dad, you know? That would be painful for you, wouldn't it?"
"So we should say our goodbyes here… okay?"
That's right… I no longer have the right to grab her hand.
"I'm fine… I'm going to be fine… I have everyone else, after all."
"Family, friends, coworkers… they all support me, they protect me."
"So no matter how badly I get hurt, I'll heal in time."
In the true sense of the word…
I have given back Setsuna to those who love her, to those she needs.
I no longer have anything to do with Setsuna…
As I'm only a few steps away from the station, it started falling.
The curtain of white that always appeared during the crossroads of our lives. Snow that only ever fell during times of hardship and sorrow.
A white, transient, and a kind… yet still relentless cold.
She said that she'd be fine. But right now, she's going up against not just the powerful sea breeze, but also against the enveloping snow.
It probably won't be much more than putting a bandaid on a large wound, but if I can do something for her in even the slightest way…
How many times do I have to go back and forth about this?
I can no longer be with Setsuna. That's what she herself has said to me.
Just as it fell on the day I had to sacrifice the most precious thing to me, in order to obtain something just as precious.
It fell as if to wash away my sins. Almost as if trying to shroud away my memories in a thick layer of snow.
Be happy. Find happiness, Setsuna…. It's the greatest wish I'll ever have in my life.
I can only regret that I'm no longer the one who can make that happen.
Even so, I'll still be praying forever and ever.
That if you were to stumble upon hard times, or if you were to ever find yourself in sorrow…
That you'll remember me. That you'll hate me and resent me as much as you can.
I want you to use that anger and turn it into strength. Strength that can help you get back up on your feet again.
I want you to work toward a path to a world where your heart rejects me… A world where you'll think nothing of my absence.
So please, please… hate me, hate me for all time. And surround yourself in a new, warmer happiness…
And maybe someday… forget about me.
"This powder snow falls on me without end."
"Just like… that… warm kindness… of yours…"
A time where instead of snow, cherry blossoms fall from above.
Yes, the snow is no longer falling… we've already passed that crossroads.
Indeed, for the legendary homecoming pianist, her leaving party was far too desolate.
"You're the one who set it up… though I'm glad we get to leave without a big fuss."
Kazusa's additional concert at the end of February received critical acclaim and was considered to be a great success.
And in order to further increase the buzz around the event, Touma Youko Office made an explosive announcement just a few days ago.
"Touma Youko is staying in Japan permanently."
This news succeeded in bringing on a massive misunderstanding among the mass media, as the fever from Kazusa's concert hadn't died down yet.
From sports weeklys to gossip magazines, it was reported as "Touma Kazusa confirmed to settle down in Japan." And this misunderstanding has already spread to the general public.
And thanks to that, Kazusa's popularity in Japan experienced another boom, with blu-ray recordings of her concert being announced.
I wonder if anyone realized that all this was just a camouflage to make sure Kazusa can leave Japan quietly.
And if any of them know that she's never planning on coming back again…
"I wasn't talking about her when I said lonely. I was talking about you."
There wasn't a sight of a single journalist in the whole airport, having been so utterly deceived by Youko-san.
So the only one here to see us off was Youko-san and…
"…I suppose no one else would come."
My coworkers couldn't possibly come in the middle of the day, on a weekday… and even if it was a day off, there'd still be no guarantee.
All my friends are busy at work… of course, I'm aware that work isn't the only reason they wouldn't show up.
And then there is family, or those close to family.
…I no longer have anyone like that.
"For completely destroying your life. I made you choose a path that you cannot turn back from."
"By being with me, she'll be happy. She'll smile for me just by being next to me…"
Youko-san looked as if she wanted to say something, but she went quiet.
Because "she" came back from the counter.
"I see. No reason to tarry, then."
Once everything was in order, I slowly stood up with a stretch.
All that's left is for us to get on the plane.
…It's the only thing left for us to do in order to leave this country.
"Thank you for seeing us off… We'll be going, then."
"I'll take care of her no matter what… Mother."
No, I do have a family… or something close to family still.
After all, I just gained a new family member right here and now.
Even if it's just family for one day. Even if I may never see her again.
"I'll be waiting for you by the gate. So… don't hold back and let your mom spoil you a little."
The two of us can experience a happiness that doesn't only involve the two of us. Our world became larger, if only by a little bit.
"Pretty good. I've been feeling pretty healthy ever since the beginning of spring. I'm planning on going back to work come April."
"Well, I do plan on living moderately long."
"Make sure to take your medicine. Get your check-ups regularly. Listen to what the doctor tells you."
"…Now you're starting to sound like him."
"You left the Vienna office to me. I won't be able to do anything useful for it, but Haruki will be able to do anything."
"I never had any expectations of you anyway. And I never doubted his ability."
"I'll continue playing the piano… not that that will wash away my sins."
"No one wants to hear a musical performance born from a desire for atonement. If you're going to play, make sure you enjoy it… and make him happy."
"Yes, of course I will. So make sure you release tons of CDs."
"…If you feel any better, come back to Vienna. Then I'll let you hear me play in person."
"No taking it back now, you promised. I'll play all night if I have to, or a whole week. I'll play all the songs you like."
"Sounds dreamy… Alright, I'll make sure to stay alive until then."
"You know, what I'm trying to say is… basically…"
"No mother could be unhappy if her daughter is happy."
"I'm sorry for abandoning you. I'm sorry for not being with you…!"
"It's fine already… I'm guilty of the same. Go and be happy, even if it's somewhere far away."
"I'll be waiting for the good news."
"…I was thinking about the face of my grandchild."
"Is the scenery outside really that interesting?"
"Not really… I was just dozing off."
Through the airplane window, I see a dreary scenery.
The scenery of the airport I've seen countless times… I can't say it's not a bit lacking for being the last place I ever see in Japan.
"You regret it, don't you? That you might never be able to see the sights of this country again."
"Of course I regret it. I can't count the amount of times I lamented over this."
"…I-I'm sorry! What was the point of asking you that, right?"
"But I… I wanted you… no matter what, so…"
"As long as I can hear you say those words to me, I'll be fine, no matter how much I regret it."
"…You did that on purpose, didn't you? You wanted me to say that!"
That's right… I can regret it as much as it takes. I can reminisce as much as it takes.
Because I don't want to forget about Setsuna. There is no way I'll ever forget about her for the rest of my life.
The dreary scenery outside starts moving.
It's moving in order to exile us from this tiny island nation.
This is your country. And it's no longer my country.
That's why I'll never come back.
The airplane gradually increases in speed, and starts rolling across the runway.
It was already too late by the time I embarked, but now, it truly is out of my reach.
"Ah… it's okay. I only forgot to throw it away, after all."
And the thing I forgot truly is something trivial, something not even worth returning for.
When I had carried out all my luggage and handed over the key, it was the only thing I wanted to keep, only so I could give it back to the manufacturer.
I imagine the management company is handling it with a rather troubled attitude, though I also trust they'll handle it appropriately.
Because I'll never play it again. Because I am not Guitar-kun.
That alone is something I'll never take back, no matter how much Kazusa wants me to.
Because… it's something I dedicated to Setsuna.
It isn't anything even close to making up for the five years I spent with Setsuna. A laughably bad skill that doesn't even make a dent in the scales.
But Setsuna always loved hearing me play.
She always listened with such enthusiasm to my guitar, through the phone, in front of me, from behind me with her head on my shoulder.
So this alone… this one thing alone…
Along with my farewell with Setsuna, I'll put it to sleep forever.
The sensation of Kazusa's warm, gentle breath touches my ears, and I feel something running down my cheeks.
Then when I realized… I was crying again.
"It's okay… you don't have to hide it."
Perhaps the reason I was staring at the window all this time was because I was unconsciously trying to hide it from her.
Because these aren't the tears one sheds when they move somewhere new. These tears don't have any hint of optimism toward the future.
"I'm not wrong. I'm not wrong at all."
That's why… Kazusa was the only person who could not be allowed to see them…
"It's okay to blame yourself. It's okay to cry. It's okay to regret everything over and over again."
"But just don't forget that… none of it was your fault."
Kazusa twists around under her fastened seat belt to reach out her hands to my cheeks.
She wants to hold me tight, but she can't bring herself to…
The frustration from those feelings reaches me through the shaking of her cold, hard fingertips.
Even though she's awful at it. Even though she couldn't possibly persuade me of anything.
"I've committed three sins in this country."
"My first sin was to make the girl, who tried to become friends with me despite my moodiness, the girl I loved, the girl who truly was my friend, into the unhappiest girl in the world."
"My second sin was to make you, who gave me your earnest feelings, and helped me become earnest in return, you whom I loved for all this time, into the biggest sinner in the world."
"And then worst of all, for turning this despicable girl, who is incapable of anything but resenting and envying others, into the happiest girl in the world…"
Yet now, she gathers all her faculties, and makes a once-in-a-lifetime proclamation.
"That's right. I'm the happiest girl in the world right now…"
Her words are clumsy and lack persuasiveness.
"It's a happiness I attained by making everyone else suffer, but still, I truly feel that from the bottom of my heart."
But I can feel her sincerity permeating my chest.
"The sadness and regret I feel right now, can never be relieved by any amount of happiness, fun or optimism."
"That also means that this happiness I feel now can never be undone by any amount of sadness or regret."
"I'm happy. I'm happy right now, Haruki."
"I'm happy that I was able to come back to rest my head on your chest. I'm happy that you came back to me."
"I'm… I'm happier than I've ever been in my life."
Kazusa's words overwhelm me with the love I have for her.
But none of it undoes what I felt for Setsuna…
It was the three of us back then…
I can still vividly remember the memories of the few days we shared that were so fun and exhilarating, even though our relationship was hanging on the thinnest thread.
Even the feelings I had for Setsuna are overwhelming me.
There's no stopping the sweetness of the overwhelming, never-ending love I have for Kazusa.
There's no stopping the pain that will never heal from the love I have for Setsuna.
But for one of those, this'll be the last time.
This is the last time. The absolute last.
The next time I step on land, I will no longer be the weak Kitahara Haruki who breaks into tears upon remembering his former lover.
The next time I see the ground again, I will be a strong man who'll do anything to protect his current lover.

"By the way, about this phone call… they were asking questions about your next performance in Prague…"
"Oh, you can just answer whatever you want."

"But if I give some half-assed answer to them, you'll have to fix everything. So me talking to them is completely pointless."
"You're absolutely right. The reason it all comes to nothing is because your answers are always half-assed."
Kazusa understands. She knows I spend almost all day working.
Because the pianist in the center of it all can do nothing else but play the piano.

"What's the problem…? You were the one who said I only have to play the piano… I'm just being the woman you wanted me to be."
"…Seriously, for how long do you plan on spoiling me?"
"Don't ask questions you know the answer to. You already know I'm the most clingy person in the world."

"If I do that, you'll just be up to more mischief. I won't be able to do my job at all."

"Oh, it's from mo… I mean, from the President."

To the point where we can't forget about it even for a moment…

"You don't have any pictures of the crime. Your only comments come from official responses… How much research did you actually do on this? Have you ever heard of surprise interviews early in the morning or late at night?"
"Vulgar material deserves to be in vulgar articles. If you want to write some high-class thesis, then do it once you've gotten at least one scoop."
"But I asked myself when I was researching this article… that maybe this kind of article doesn't suit our Kaiou Graph."
"If it doesn't suit us, then just submit it to the editing department next door. You're much more an employee of Kaiousha than a member of Kaiou Graph."
"But I'm new here. I don't have those kinds of connections."
"Then ask your superiors for help! I'll help, so will Kizaki-san. Our managing editor, Hamada, is always available… even Suzuki-san would help."
"Hey, why am I below you in the list?"
"You think you can get away with keeping the mindset of a salaryman here? Don't underestimate this business."
"You thought it was going to be an easy job at first too…"
"Stay out of it, outsiders! Did I say anything wrong?"
"I was just so moved. To think our little Macchan has grown so much."
"I have responsibilities too, you know. Not just for myself, but also to educate the new guys. We have the responsibility now to maintain the company."
"But that article was supposed to be your job! You didn't want to do it so you tossed it to someone else, didn't you!?"
"Like I said, it's all part of their education!"
"He's really grown so much. Just perfect at his job."
"You sure did! I've been stuck shivering in this cold forever!"
"Sorry, sorry. Cleaning the seminar room took longer than I thought."
"Just look at how cold my hands are! I can barely feel them anymore."
"Still, so much happened. So many things."
"U-Um, anyway… where do you want to go today?"
"Do you want to eat out somewhere? Or if you're okay with waiting, perhaps I can make something for you?"
"Actually, while we're at it, do you want to spend the evening in my room? Perhaps we could buy some wine. You can stay, right?"
"Alright, it's decided! Then let's go to the supermarket by the station…"
"Sorry! Today I really have to be at home!"
"I'm really sorry! After keeping you waiting this late for me."
"Why? Why? Didn't you promise to decide on our graduation trip with me today?"
"Tomorrow! I promise I'll do it tomorrow!"
"Is it really that important? More important than me? More important than being with me?"
"Today is the only day I can't. It's an important day… for my family."
"Hey, Miyo-chan, try naming all the famous products from Hokkaido."
"Are you going to tell them you're in Hokkaido this time? You really should stop putting on airs for your daughter already."
"You're right. She should be honest and tell her daughter she's in the hospital and getting all the best care she can get. I'm sure that would put her more at ease."
"Don't talk about me like I'm not here, Miyo-chan. If something were to happen to me, you'll be the one who will have to learn to imitate my writing style."
"If you end up dying, I'm afraid we couldn't keep it a secret for longer than a measly three years. All the newspapers will be writing about it, after all."
"That's why you should listen to everything the doctor tells you so you can live much longer, President…"
"Ah… by the way, Nori-kun. Are you really free next month?"
"Indeed… if you absolutely insist on going, I'll follow you. I've even talked with the hospitals there, so you'll always be able to check in if something happens."
"…Right after I told her to live longer, she decides to come up with this nonsense."
"All the preparations are in order, but I agree with Miyo-chan… Are you sure you want to go to Vienna?"
"…This might be my last chance, after all."
"Why now? Why not wait until the weather is a bit warmer?"
"Could the letter you received last week have something to do with it?"
"You started bringing this up after you got that letter…"
"Being a mother means being responsible for your child, no matter what."
"If I need to be there for my child, then I should set everything else aside to do that."
"That's my god-given right as a mother, and I don't plan on letting anyone take it away from me."
"It looks like… Tomo is coming today."
"She said she'd 'come no matter what, so don't start without me.'"
"She's as selfish and inconsiderate as always… no one could guess from looking at her on TV."
"Well, no harm no foul. Let's wait for her. It's been a while since I saw her last, anyway."
"…When you put it that way, these gatherings have become kind of lonely. There were five of us back then."
"Nowadays, it's only you and me every time."
"Almost like a date, don't you think?"
"…What are you saying? Your girlfriend would be hurt if she heard that."
"You have a girlfriend… yet you're meeting up with another woman every month like this…"
"If she gets angry about something like this, I don't want her as my girlfriend."
"Whether you're only going to stay as my friend or be degraded to a total stranger from now on, I can't think of a better friend than you in my life."
"D-Don't try to use me as a replacement for Haruki! I… I…"
"I was just kidding, let it go."
"So what do you want to do until Tomo arrives? Wanna pass the time over some tea?"
"Are you serious about your current girlfriend…?"
"…Is a day meant only for Setsuna."
After a long update on her condition filled with boasting and complaints, there was strangely enough a URL posted in the middle of the email.
"How suspicious can you possibly be of your own mother…?"
Looking at it closely, there's a compressed file format written in the URL.
In other words, it's a link to download a file stored on some server somewhere.
I click the link and save the file on my computer.
A few dozen files appear on my download bar.
Under the link… and under numerous blank lines, Youko-san's message continued.
"It's been two years, so I thought it was about time."
The contents were completely different from the rest of the message, and were completely unlike her.
"This is about Ogiso Setsuna. About how she's doing after that time."
It's the name that we've sealed away along with that country.
It's the name of the girl who ended up being hurt worst of all on the day when everyone ended up getting hurt, including ourselves…
The girl who I still couldn't bring myself to separate fromーthe girl who remains a part of me to this day.
The girl who makes me repress her in my heart so that my words don't leak from my mouth, the girl whose figure is still vivid in my mind two years later.
But when I click to decompress the file, I start shaking from a premonition I don't understand myself.
Because the weight of Youko-san's words put Kazusa and me on edge.
With my shaking right hand, I aim my cursor at the file, and double click it.
I grabbed Kazusa's hand, which was shivering just as much as mine on my shoulder.
Once the file was decompressed, I could see the file format. It was a video.
"Hey, Setsuna… don't frown like that, look into the camera and smile!"
"Don't tell me to do the impossible… I absolutely can't fail at this."
"So what if you make mistakes? We can just redo the video."
"That's not the problem. Today is the day I have to give my best performance…"
"I haven't seen Setsuna-chan this tense in ages. Must've been when she was rehearsing for the school festival last…"
"Huh, what's that? Let me hear it, let me hear it!"
"Ah, I want to hear it too. Setsuna is always really calm on stage nowadays."
"Come to think of it, didn't you really hate Setsuna back then, Tomo?"
"Right, right! She'd say things like, 'You've breathed your last, Ogiso Setsuna' and wouldn't mind tricking anyone to put her down."
"Ooh, what's up with that? Let me hear it, let me hear it."
"…Takahiro-kun, you'll listen to anything as long as it's amusing for you."
"Wait a second. I'll just adjust the camera… Alright, let's go!"
"Good luck, Setsuna… Show us the results of all your practice."
"While you're at it… show us your own self too."
("Are you doing well? I'm still singing.")
"We bring you the news for February 14th, Valentine's Day."
"Let's start with a report from Miley Sports… 'Touma Kazusa's Additional Concert to be Canceled?'"
"Following the positive reception of her first concert in Japan held in January, pianist Touma Kazusa had made plans to hold an additional concert near the end of this month."
"However, recent statements made by related sources have cast doubt on any future performance being held, due to poor health."
"Neither Kazusa-san, nor her producer and mother, Touma Youko-san, have made any appearances before the press since the previous concert…"
"Thus, it is likely that her health has indeed deteriorated since the previous concert, and that she is currently recuperating in a hospital somewhere within the Metropolitan Area."
"In fact, just last week, an ambulance was dispatched late at night to the hotel where Kazusa-san was thought to have been staying."
"Eyewitness reports on the scene expressed the possibility that the woman carried out at the time was Kazusa-san herself, adding further concerns to whether the additional concert will be held."
"Furthermore, a statement made by Touma Youko Office last night had this to say regarding the issue: 'We have received no such report and are currently investigating the matter.'"
"Tickets for Touma Kazusa-san's first concert in Japan sold out within an hour, putting the demand for her performances at an unprecedented level for a classical musician…"
"What's the meaning of this advertisement…? It was supposed to be 2100 yen, right? Why does it suddenly cost 3150 yen now?"
"Even if it is a special issue, the price for this is… Eh? You're saying that I strongly insisted it be so? What do you mean by that?"
"…Huh? I haven't heard anything about that at all! How did things end up like this?"
"Yeah, yeah… What did you just say? But that's… Wasn't that all already decided in the plan from the very beginning?"
"Did Yoshimatsu-san tell you about all that? No, like I said, it wasn't me…"
"…It seems that the both of us have been deceived by our subordinates. Yeah, yeah, I totally understand. At any rate, I'm going to discuss this with him in person now. Well, if you'll excuse me."
"Kitahara! Where did you run off to, you bastard!"
"If you're looking for Kitahara, he went home immediately after the briefing earlier. He did show his face before you came to work, though."
"The special issue of Ensemble is already nearing its deadline anyway, so I'd say you can't expect things to not be busy on his end."
"Although he's at the bottom of the pyramid when it comes to work on Kaiou Graph, he has the widest scope of work capability among all of the members here, huh?"
"I guess they don't call him Kazaoka the Second for nothing…"
"This isn't the time for this nonsense. Things suddenly just got really awry with that special issue."
"What do you mean, really awry? Are you telling me we've suddenly got our hands on Touma Kazusa's nude gravure photos?"
"No, I imagine we'd get rewarded by the president for that…"
"Sure, I guess this can be considered a scoop in some ways… still, how did a plan like this even get approved? How did they suddenly decide on a collaboration out of the blue?"
"A collaboration? Things are suddenly really escalating now, huh?"
"Can we please not forget something? You know that he's still a rookie in his first year, right?"
"And while all this is happening, rumors about the additional concert being canceled are all over the place… I just don't get any of this. What in the world have you done, Kitahara!?"
"You have reached the voicemail for this number. Please leave your message within 30 seconds after the beep."
"Sorry for keeping you waiting. I've finally settled things on my end."
"What's wrong? You still can't reach him?"
"I've only been receiving voicemail requests throughout the week. What in the world is going on with you, Haruki…?"
"Hasn't he been working overtime for the past couple of days due to his deadline approaching? If I recall correctly, he's responsible for that issue that's coming out next month, isn't he?"
"He'd still at least say something to us even if that were the case. And even then, today is… Does he have any intention of making it?"
"We can only trust that he will. There's no way Haruki would ever forget what day it is today."
"Still, don't you think those two have been acting strangely recently?"
"It seems that they're wary about meeting us, and Setsuna-chan didn't really give me anything to work with when I inquired about things on her end."
"Well, you know, she said 'we're both busy,' didn't she? So it's only the fact that they really can't help it at the moment, that's all…"
"…Could he have gotten himself involved in Touma's affairs again?"
"Well, come on… there's already news about her public performance being canceled, right? He's absolutely going to be bothered by that. Maybe he's even gone off to where Touma is right now…"
"Like I said, just stop! You're going to make me feel uneasy too at this rate!"
"Ah… well, regardless of all that, there's no way things can happen between Touma and Haruki the way they are now… Yeah! It's just not possible!"
"…And you can't even reassure yourself properly despite causing me to worry."
"At any rate, we have to make sure that everything's alright today. It's about time we headed over, right? I assume Setsuna-chan's already returned home as well?"
"Now that you mention it… actually, ever since this morning, she…"
"Well, I take it you were the one that let that report slip, Miyo-chan?"
"Whispers were spreading amongst the media that your health had been failing recently, so I thought that I'd mislead them with a false clue."
"…I see. Once it is made known Kazusa was fine all along, people will be less skeptical when my illness is reported on."
"It was you who taught me how to turn a crisis into an opportunity."
"I would expect no less of Touma Youko Office's best employee. Thanks!"
"I also happen to be the only employee in the Japanese branch."
"Yes, she hasn't taken so much as even a step out of the guest room. …She has been keeping this up for a week by now, though."
"I do check on her three times a day, but she still refuses to open the door for me."
"I'm sorry, Miyo-chan. My daughter is causing you a lot of trouble."
"It's okay. I understand her feelings almost too well."
"I'm so shocked I want to cry too. What would happen to Touma Youko Office if you retired…?"
"Well, let's worry about that when I leave the hospital. More importantly, how's preparation for the next concert going?"
"All preparations are already in order on that end, be it to commence it… or to revoke it. Part of the reason I spread that report was in order to do this."
"…You truly are Touma Youko Office's best employee!"
"The moment you made your decision, I started working on everything on all sides, minimizing the possible damage."
"Thank you, Miyo-chan. …But don't worry. The additional concert will commence on schedule."
"…Is it really possible? Truth be told, the way that Kazusa-san is right now, I can't see her returning to her usual playing quality within two weeks."
"The show must go on nevertheless. While I'm at it, I've assigned her with an errand before the concert. The person responsible for the affair will be heading your way tonight."
"Huh!? What are you saying, President!? Do you not understand the current situation at all?"
"Mother and daughter of the Touma family are now terminally ill and lovesick, respectively, and their lives as pianists are thus on the line… Did I get that right?"
"If you understand that, then please reconsider! What were you thinking, adding an extra burden onto her when we already have to be so careful about how to go about her next concert!"
"…Well, the truth is, I'm actually quite nervous myself. I did wonder if I ended up going too far this time."
"Still… it's paramount that we actually use such a drastic measure this time. After all, it's not something that can be solved unless we're in Japan."
"But she's not willing to see anyone in her current state, you know? She doesn't even allow me to go in her room and check on her, so…"
"…I don't think we'll have any problems with that in this case. At any rate, Miyo-chan, when the person in charge arrives, you can simply lead them to her room."
"I won't be responsible for anything that happens thereafter, alright?"
"Yes, that's fine. …After all, the person arriving is someone who my little girl won't see herself running away from."
"…I don't really get what's going on, but I'll listen to you. That's my job, after all."
"I'm really sorry for troubling you all the time, you know? I'll give you a raise for your severance payment, then."
"Even if you're joking, please don't take it in such an ominous direction!"
"That will be all, then, Miyo-chan. I'll be leaving the rest to you～"
"There's a guest waiting for you in the lobby right now. The president has also given me directions to tell you that you have to meet with this person."
"Please, come out already! Even if only to eat something, at least!"
"Today… Today I won't back down so easily, okay? Until you give me a response, I'll be waiting right here, alright?"
"Are you alright? Are you awake? …Are you even properly conscious right now? I'm begging you, don't make us worry any more than you already have…"
"Ah… thank goodness… in any case, that means you're okay, right? Are you hungry?"
"It's fine… I don't want to eat anything."
"…I don't know anymore. I don't know anything anymore…"
"…For now, please open the door. Let's just calm down and have a little chat, alright?"
"I can't… I simply can't see anyone right now. I wouldn't even know what to say and what to do if I did."
"That's exactly why you need to get into contact with someone… You won't come up with a good solution all of a sudden just by brooding all by yourself in there, you know?"
"But, but… but… I just can't anymore… I don't want to stay in this country anymore… I want to go back to Vienna."
"But the president… what about your mother?"
"…I don't know, I just said I don't know anything anymore! It's because I don't know what to do anymore that I have to run away from here!"
"And yet, I can't even bring myself to run from this hopeless state I'm in. I've already finished packing a long time ago, but I can't even get out of here…"
"I can't do anything. I can't decide anything. I can't even move. There's no value in living on anymore…"
"Go home… for today. Don't worry, I'm still alive… and I'm still living my life shamefully…"
"Y-Yes, she is in this room, correct… but as I thought, she's still under the weather…"
"Yes, so I can't do anything more for today… eh? Ah, but that's…"
"Y-Yes, it's true that Touma told me that. …Is it okay if I put my faith in you?"
"Ah, please wait a moment, Kazusa-san. I'm giving the phone over to someone else right now!"
"Thank you for taking care of me all this time. I'm Ogiso… from Knights Records."
The snow stopped falling before the hour was even over, a far cry from my hope that it would last until morning.
There's still some time before the first train departs, and I feel tired enough to want to call a taxi.
I only remain alone in the cold, sitting on a bench in this vacant park, gazing at the sky as the clouds gradually drift away.
And yet Setsuna had rushed to where I was in a taxi as I stood helplessly in the middle of the night.
"Here, take this disposable heat pack. Put it in your pocket and you'll feel nice and warm… oh, what am I saying?"
Setsuna's hand sends a warmth across my entire body that's stronger than the heat of the heat pack she handed me.
As I thought, her voice, which I haven't so much as heard in two weeks, is still full of the undiminished tenderness it always held.
"I'm sorry for not contacting you all this time. I'm sorry for letting you suffer."
However, Setsuna has no need to apologize to me for the two weeks she'd spent being absent from my life.
"Sorry… I'm sorry, Setsuna… I really am incapable of supporting her."
I made a promise, after all.
That I wouldn't run away from Kazusa. That I'd stay by Kazusa's side from now on.
I'd promised to put Kazusa at ease.
And I'd promised that I wouldn't meet Setsuna again until I'd accomplished all of that.
"No, perhaps it was a mistake to even suggest that I would be able to support her in the first place… In the end, it was all pointless."
"It wasn't pointless. It's really nothing like that at all."
That's why Setsuna didn't reply to me no matter how many times I sent her texts filled with more excuses, just as we promised.
"I can't do it after all… I only cause her to suffer more by being with her. I'm turning into a bed of thorns for her…"
And yet it didn't even take five minutes before she called me back after I sent her a short "Help me."
She must've seen all those texts… even though she hadn't replied to any of them, Setsuna must've seen all of the texts I'd sent her.
"Can you… talk to me about it?"
And so she'd come here… Setsuna had come back to me.
"Tell me everything that's happened these two weeks. How much you've worked hard, Haruki-kun, and how much you've been held down as well…"
Setsuna accepted me when I, like Kazusa, ran away from the painful reality and sought salvation from her.
"Tell me… what you desire now, Haruki-kun."
Setsuna is looking at me with a compassionate gaze.
