So as I lie down while being held by Kazusa, I lose my strength, and invite Kazusa with me to oblivion.
"Is it okay if I stay like this…? I'm not heavy, am I?"
"I want it to be heavy. I want to be able to feel you, Kazusa."
"…Thank you. Then feel me with your whole body."
Along with those words, Kazusa relaxes her whole body on top of me, and as expected, I'm enveloped by a pleasant weight.
It's almost as if her body will never let go of me again. That soft, warm, captivating and sweet-smelling body.
She touches my cheeks, strokes my back, pushes against my chest, touches my abdomen with her own, rubs my lower body, entwines her legs with mine, and breathes in my ear.
"If you could listen to one more favor from me…"
"If you could send me not a flower, but a new sprout… then I'd be even happier."
She could have been pretending to be asleep.
It could have been a way to keep the meaning behind her words ambiguous.
But as I am right now…
No, as I had done before, I swore to never look into the meaning behind those words.
"Are you sure you should still be sleeping? You know today is…"
"Nhm, mmh, ah… aah… Haruki… ahm, mhh, ah!"
"Ah, aah… ah… haah, ah… Good morning, Haruki."
"Don't you 'good morning' me… what are you…"
The kiss was far too intense for a good morning kiss. The sides of both our mouths are completely covered in saliva.
"Ah, well… you wouldn't wake up when I called your name, so…"
"You put your tongue in people's mouths just because they won't wake up?"
"Haaaah, well, it doesn't matter. So what time is it?"
"That's what I was about to tell you… it's 8:30."
"I see… It seems like I overslept quite a bit, even though it's Sunday. I'm sorry."
It might be my day off, but it's still completely unheard of for me to sleep longer than Kazusa.
Perhaps it has something to do with my health recently…
"Your alarm clock went off at 6 o'clock, which woke me up… then I went back to sleep and woke up again just now…"
"You said last night that you had to go to work today and that you needed to take care of something in the morning, so we should sleep in your apartment."
"M-My shirt! My socks! Huh? Where are my clean clothes?"
Something like this is simply unheard of.
"Hey, you don't have to be in such a rush. It's not that big of a deal for a journalist to be late. Most of your work is done at night, anyway."
"I'll correct your distorted understanding of my job some other time. I have a meeting with Hamada-san first thing in the morning today."
Not because I slept longer than Kazusa, but because I overslept so much that I'm late for work.
Usually I always wake up at 6:30 every morning…
"Ah, by the way, since you look so busy, I'll make breakfast. You should grab a…"
"I'll pass on that for more reasons than one! Alright, I'm off!"
"And yet you get mad at me for skipping breakfast…"
"You'll have to go back to work from today, will you be okay?"
"Did you measure your temperature? What did it say? Did you go to the doctor?"
"Haruki-kun, I'm worried because you always keep everything bottled up during times like this… In any case, please don't overdo it, okay?"
"Your attention please. The train on Line 1 heading toward Onjuku will arrive shortly. Please stand behind the yellow line."
Somehow, I managed to make it in time… If I get on this train, I'll be able to get to work by 10 o'clock.
"I'm sorry for always causing you to worry. I'm commuting to work right now."
Once I'm there, I'll go straight to the conference room and report my progress.
"I feel better now. My temperature has gone down significantly since yesterday. I'm pretty much back to normal today."
Then I'll get back to my seat and get to work.
…I left early on Thursday and barely even made any progress on Friday, so I'm a little afraid of looking at my inbox.
"More importantly, I'm really sorry about last week. I'll make it up to you next time. Let your family know that as well."
In the afternoon, I'll have to go straight to Ensemble's editing department for a meeting… The topic is our approach on compiling the special number on Touma Kazusa.
This current job might be one done along with professionals, but it's also my first job as a direct participant, which ought to be commemorated.
"The train just arrived. I'll contact you again."
Although that might just be because of my connections to Touma Youko Office and their strong desire to have me on, I still can't let this chance go.
The deadline is at the end of February, and it'll go on sale at the beginning of March. All while the Touma Kazusa craze hasn't died down yet.
Everything is going at a rapid pace already from the beginning of the week. There's no point in even thinking about taking sick leave.
It's my first editing job with this much responsibility. And it's not even for Kaiou Graph with which I'm so familiar with, but for Ensemble.
The amount of support Hamada-san can give me is limited, and I can't rely on the usual gang for help. I bet that things are going to get quite hectic from this week on.
Will Setsuna be alright? Will her family be alright? What about our future? What about our promise?
What am I saying? There's no point thinking about all that. For now, I'll have to start with the things I'm able to take care of.
First, I'll go to the office, then I'll start working. I'll go back to how my daily life used to be.
I put some force into my knees to stand up from the bench, and head for the train…
"The doors for Line 1 are closing. Please be careful."
"It always looks so easy when he does it."
"How do I… turn off this alarm?"
"…Maybe Haruki was right, and I shouldn't be cooking after all."
From the burnt smell coming from inside the apartment, I could feel the same sense of foreboding I had just a few days ago.
"What's the matter, Haruki…? Didn't you go to…"
"We'll talk about that later! Open the window now!"
…Not that I wanted to be right, though.
"Look, it's done. This time it's light brown."
You could say she lacks the skills to make fried eggs, but it takes a special kind of carelessness to burn regular toast coal black…
Seriously, she's known for her skills all over the world, yet the utter contrast between what she's good at and what she's bad at is straight out of a manga story.
"So, back to what I said… Why did you come back, Haruki? …Don't tell me you saw the smoke all the way from the station?"
"Why would you come all the way back for that? Surely you don't need it…"
"…The things you talked about last week, about your teacher. I had it stored on the recorder."
"But you weren't recording back then, right?"
"…I quietly recorded everything I remembered by myself after that, once you were already asleep."
I can feel Kazusa staring at me from behind.
Probably because even I would find my answer unnatural…
"Here, your fried eggs. Out with your plate."
But I ignore her doubtful look, and instead put the eggs I just finished frying on her plate. Once that's done, I look through the fridge for vegetables.
"So… did you find what you were looking for?"
"So… are you going back to work when you're done eating?"
"Isn't it… about time for you to start practicing too?"
Because I was so worked up about the possibility of being late for work when I left my residence, this strange atmosphere wasn't present earlier.
This indescribable sense of loneliness, this strange feeling where we reach out our arms and lightly clutch the hem of each other's shirts, though only in our hearts.
This feeling of waiting for one of us to break the silence, wondering how we're going to settle things, swaying from side to side as we look for the right words to say…
"The truth is… my superior gave me permission to come back. Once I called and reported to him, he told me I didn't need to come in for today."
And in the end, the path we ended up on was a comfortable one.
To me right now, it's the most pleasant path; a peaceful one without any storms.
"He's out for an interview during the afternoon, and since I can't attend any meetings today anyway…"
"And it's almost like I'm on a business trip in the first place… handling Touma Kazusa and all."
"T-Then… does that mean that doing this is your work?"
"Obviously I can't get away with just this… I'm doing my regular job at home today… You know, working on the interview I held with you last week."
"So uh, I'll be at home today. Nowadays, you can work from anywhere as long as you have access to your email."
"Haruki… you're going to be at home all day?"
And I'm sure right now, Kazusa too, likely finds this path to be…
"Since you're at it, why not do your job at my place? I won't get in the way."
"Forget about getting in the way. Don't you have practice?"
"I'll just look at you. If it gets distracting, I'll move to the corner, so you can focus on your job."
"…It's fine as long as you don't distract me, just don't go pouring coffee for me out of consideration. There's no undoing it if you spill it all on my PC."
And there's no one to upset this atmosphere. This path is both pleasant and peaceful for Kazusa.
Because this is the path that lets the two of us be all alone together.
"I got it already! Why would I even bother doing housework when you're around? I'll leave all of that to you."
And just like that, I affirm Kazusa's attempt to run away.
After all, I of all people have no right to criticize her for that.
Not when I ran straight back home within minutes of being outside, just so I could escape and return to the world made only for the two of us.
"Aren't you going to listen to the recorder?"
I'm amazed at myself for how poor that excuse was…
"I see… That's just like you, Haruki."
But Kazusa simply admires me for those words, and with a bump, she puts her head on my left shoulder.
It's likely that it's not that she isn't doubting my words; rather, she's given up on thinking about things altogether.
"Hey… is it okay if I write about this? Fluegel's evaluation of Touma Youko."
"You mean about how I was born as a result of her time of promiscuity? I don't mind."
"…No, not that. I meant how he thought she had the ability to win the contest without trying."
"You don't need my permission to write about something that boring…"
"Also, what about the part where unlike your mother, you haven't skipped a single lesson?"
"If you write that, it'll look like I'm trying to make up for my lack of natural skill."
"It's the truth, so what of it? …No matter how you look at it, you're much more of a hard-worker than Youko-san."
"She's more of a genius than me…"
"I really like how you're kind of an upstart in that way, though."
Kazusa starts sulking a bit and bumps her jaw against my shoulder a few times.
"Well, of course you have talent. It's not even comparable to the average person, and maybe even compared to other pianists…"
"But I think the reason you finish in similar positions to her is because you put in more effort…"
"In that case, how would you explain the fact that I skipped practice for three whole years back in high school?"
Bump, bump, bump… her head rises up and down on my shoulder again and again.
"What's up with you? Would you rather be seen as a genius instead?"
"Didn't I already tell you? I don't care what anyone thinks of me other than you."
…She's completely letting herself loose around me.
"So what do you think about my evaluation that Touma Kazusa is an upstart? You care about what I think, right?"
"I'm half annoyed, half angry… and half happy."
"But you're an even bigger upstart than I am, Haruki. Yet you're treating me like I'm the inferior one and protecting me even though it's beyond your means…"
As I turn to her, she lightly pushes her lips against mine, and then immediately bumps her head back on my shoulder.
But this time, she doesn't keep hitting me; instead, she rubs her hair against me.
The second half of that comment is not something I could put in an interview article, though.
Though perhaps… I can keep it in my memory as a third-rate article forever.
"I thought so. This much is fine, right?"
The woman who kept verbally abusing me five years ago is letting out an expression befitting of a girl's at my immediate reassurance.
"…There's only two weeks left. You can handle this much for that long, right, Haruki?"
"I've never felt that way in the first place. I don't even feel like I'm forced to bear anything right now."
Ever since I crossed the final line with Kazusa, the feeling of her skin and the warmth of her body has never caused me pain again.
"In fact, I find it more annoying that you keep repeating 'two weeks, two weeks' all the time."
On the contrary, whenever Kazusa gently pushes her skin against mine, whenever she touches my lips, and whenever she accepts me, I feel peace return to my heart.
I feel a kind of euphoria that by far supersedes any feelings of guilt over my betrayal, and I find myself wanting to experience it over and over again.
"I don't remember making a promise like that… it's something you went and decided on your own."
However, that euphoria might be the same kind that one gets when taking highly addictive drugs.
That's why, as if I'm swept away by some fever, I strongly pull Kazusa into my arms and push her down on the bed.
"I want to feel you more and more."
"I want to feel your warmth. I want to feel your softness. I want to smell your scent."
"B-But… it's still 10 o'clock in the morning, you know?"
"…If we start now, we'll have so much time to make love."
"Yeah… we still have fourteen more hours left of the day."
"That sounds… like something out of a dream."
I'm doing this so I can calm down my heart. So I can continue being myself…
I'm doing this so I can free myself from the severe withdrawal from the drug called Kazusa…
I need to do this so I can rid my body from the dizzying headache and throbbing of my heart that attacked me even this morning when I boarded the train.
"Yes… After I called you yesterday, I immediately went to the hospital for a checkup…"
"Oh, come on… that means you won't be able to come in for a whole week, at least… no, it means you shouldn't come."
"I'm really sorry… I didn't want to get sick right when Ensemble is starting its big project."
"Ah～ Well, if you're sick, then there's nothing that can be done about that. You wouldn't lie about being sick… Though I wouldn't believe it if Matsuoka was the one saying it."
Even unintentionally, Hamada-san's words mercilessly pierce my heart countless times like needles.
But this time alone, I have no one else to blame. …Rather, no matter how I look at this, I'm the only one who's being terrible here.
"Well… I'll relay the message to the chiefs of both departments. I'm not sure how we'll move on from here on out, but for now, I'll let you know if anything happens."
"I'm really sorry… There's still the work I can do at home to complete, if you think that…"
"Ah, that sounds great… is what I would want to say, but I can't force someone with the flu to overwork himself. Just rest up until you get better."
"N-No… I'm not feeling that bad… my symptoms are very light."
"Oh, and by the way, avoid doing any more interviews with Touma Kazusa, okay? If you get her infected right now, there'll be hell to pay."
"For as long as you're sick, you'll only cause more problems for others if you overdo it. I forbid you from continuing as usual, okay?"
"In any case, I'll try to cover for you the best I can. Take care of yourself, then."
Once I ended the call, I kept bowing my head to a person who wasn't there, and if there was anyone around me right now, they'd point at me while laughing at what I'm doing.
Yesterday, for the first time in my life, I committed an act that was unbefitting of a proper member of society and repeated that mistake seven times over.
I pretended that I was ill… for a whole week, at that.
Moreover, I did it in such a sloppy way that my lie would immediately be revealed at the first request of a doctor's note.
But how else could I explain it…?
"I try going to the station every day, but every time I try getting on the train, I suddenly feel terrible."
I'm not a middle-schooler trying to skip school… What's happening to me?
At the sight of my own pathetic face reflected in the mirror, my expression grows even more pathetic.
I threw up in the station toilet, I rested for 30 minutes on the bench, yet my nausea and my dizziness wouldn't leave me.
It's bad enough to get in the way of my work, but the moment I head back to my apartment, it goes away as if it was all just a lie.
"What is it? I told you I was going to prepare your meal right now. Are you that hungry?"
"No, it's not about me… are you really going to skip work today too?"
"I told you, didn't I? Right now, my job is to be with you. I don't need to physically be at work."
"It's been like that since last month. Why are you worrying about it now?"
It's the moment I heard that voice, the moment I saw that face.
The moment I hugged that soft body in front of me, the moment I pushed my lips against hers.
The moment I did the exact same things I had done to her before I was leaving an hour prior, all my symptoms went away as if it was all a lie.
"I'll make it soon… so be good and wait, okay?"
In other words, with the way I am now, the longest I can go without my "drug" is less than an hour.
A world where Kazusa isn't present, and one where my superiors, my coworkers, my friends, and the person I consider the most precious to me are present… The world I used to live in…
I have begun to look at such a world as uncharted land the same way normal people would look at the depths of the ocean.
"Seriously… have you ever brushed your hair by yourself?"
"It's always my stylist, my manager, or my mom… or whoever notices it at the time who does it for me."
"Don't ruin it… this is a treasure you have."
"Not wanting to ruin it is the very reason I don't take care of it myself."
"I kind of get it, but I don't want to…"
Kazusa's magnificent long hair smoothly slides along my brush.
Just with a single grasp of the hand, it slides along my palm like water. It's like a work of art whose peculiarity is that it has no peculiarity.
If someone were to ask me what Touma Youko's greatest masterpiece was, I might decide on this hair…
"It was probably damaged because of you, considering you've shot your semen on it countless times."
"…Could you watch your choice of words?"
"It's the truth, so what of it? My hair gets pretty stiff when I try to wash it."
…Kazusa twirls her hair around her finger in boredom as her statement ruins the mood of our unreserved conversation.
"It's okay. They say that a girl's hair is tantamount to her life, but I won't die just by cutting it off."
"Aah, I seriously want to teach you how to speak proper Japanese from scratch."
"I could even sell it for your sake."
"…And if you did that, would I sell my pocket watch for your sake?"
"Only a fool calls other people idiots!"
Setting aside the dispute over who is contradicting the other for no reason…
I dig my face into Kazusa's hair, transparent as a piano wire.
"Fuuu… Haah… Damn, it smells good… not to mention how smooth it is."
"It smells just like the shampoo you bought for me, so of course you'd like how it smells."
"Aah, I just want to be like this forever."
"…That's completely up to you. I haven't said a word about not liking it."
At my inappropriate behavior, Kazusa merely twists her body around as if feeling tickled, and accepts me wholly.
And I… as if being lured by her scent, as if being enveloped by the delicate softness touching my face…
I put more and more force into my arms embracing her. I bring my lips kissing her cheeks closer and closer to her mouth…
And right before the perfect moment, we're rudely interrupted by a sound.
Kazusa picks up the cell phone from the top of the dresser, looks at the screen and frowns just a bit.
Actually, the only people who would call Kazusa in this country could be counted on just one hand.
Because of that, I can guess what the call will be about.
"I didn't show up at the studio yesterday."
After all, she was in bed with me from dawn till dusk yesterday.
After all, she was moaning, laughing, dozing off, and kissing my lips and skin.
It is said that it can take days for a pianist to recover from a single day of skipped practice.
And if that goes on for multiple days, then keeping a proper condition for the concert less than two weeks away is next to impossible…
What Kazusa just did could be considered reckless beyond any reason.
Had it been just a few days ago, I'd have lectured her.
But Kazusa was very slightly hurt by my question that conveyed that I had an unimaginable attachment to her.
"You're right here with me. All I have to do is stretch out my hand and yet…"
"And yet you're telling me to leave? You can be… really cold sometimes."
"I never told you to leave… this is your own apartment to begin with."
"Don't be smart with me, you idiot… Don't you want me to be with you…?"
"If I didn't want you to be with me, I wouldn't stretch my hand out and hold you like this."
And I accept that slight bit of unreasonableness in Kazusa.
My embrace around Kazusa's thin body has already grown strong enough to almost break it.
"You coward… why didn't you just say that from the start? Why do you always make me choose?"
"I won't let go of you again…"
"I won't ever let go of you…"
"I'll never let go of you… not today, not tomorrow, not the day after tomorrow… not ever."
With those final words, Kazusa finally relaxes her shoulders and leans against my chest as if entrusting herself to me.
Her expression is a smile with the slightest tinge of self-contempt in it.
"And you went through all the trouble to untangle my hair."
"I'll do it again as many times as I need to… whenever, and forever."
The hair I spent so much time working on was going to once again be turned messy…
After that, I turned off my cell phone too in front of Kazusa.
…I had two texts from Setsuna, but I didn't even look at them.
Another day spent from morning till night in bed.
The only time either of us put on any clothes was to greet the restaurant delivery man who came with our dinner.
Idle days like these might be something Kazusa has long since gotten used to, but they're completely unimaginable to me.
"I haven't seen the snow… not even once since I came here."
Morning, day, night. Forgetting time altogether and just going at it, with such passion that one could mistake our sleeping for us fainting. Once we wake up, we do it again.
We spend that time together even as the date changes; this lifestyle that has absolutely no value to the world at large, yet is completely irreplaceable to the two of us.
"Now that you mention it… isn't winter supposed to be a little warmer than usual this year?"
"Yet it's still as cold as always…"
Kazusa wraps around my warm body once again as if she hadn't been holding it all day.
Of course, I naturally reciprocated with an even greater force.
"Do you want to see the snow?"
"Come to think of it… it was snowing in Strasbourg."
"Of course it was… you weren't even wearing shoes."
"Back then I… no, there is no point in saying it now."
That night in Strasbourg, and those memories of five years ago…
Whenever Kazusa and I saw the snow, there was always one more person seeing that very same snow.
"If the snow won't come to Tokyo… then let's go to it."
The person who loved the snow the most among the three of us…
And the person who once hated the snow the most among the three of us, the person whose very name had the character for snow in it.
"Do you want to go somewhere up north… where it snows?"
But now, I desperately chase that name out of my mind.
I'm afraid that my body and my heart will react that same way again.
"That's right, a trip. Want to go on one, just the two of us?"
"A trip with just you and me…?"
"Won't you come and see the ground covered in snow? It's been a while since you saw the snow in Japan, right?"
I wonder who it was who said to us, "I want to see the snow" all those years ago…
Perhaps that was the first time Kazusa and I started to like seeing the snow fall down.
And that was when times equally as painful as those we enjoyed followed.
"Let's go to the travel agency tomorrow and see if they have any places where the snow is pretty."
"If we're going, we better hurry. We don't have much more than a week…"
"You don't have to be in such a rush. Until March, there are countless places in Japan with lots of snow."

"Not just snow, either. We can look at the cherry blossoms in spring, swim in the ocean in summer, and watch the fallen leaves in autumn… After all, Japan has such a contrast between its seasons that you can't find anywhere else like it."
Kazusa, who has until now looked at me with a distant smile, over time starts to look more and more lonely as she lowers her gaze.
The more passionate my words become, the more the light disappears from her expression.
"You said you hated this country, but…"
But no matter how big the difference in our body temperatures becomes, I can't stop myself from speaking.
"But Japan is really… much more beautiful than you think. I'm sure it's a country that you'll come to love."
"So… why don't you stay here? Why don't you try living here again?"
I spoke those words without any consideration of the future, without any idea of what would happen next. They were merely the words that came to my mind.
But at that moment, the feelings I put into words had no hint of lies in them. Neither did I have any doubt of my happiness if she actually did stay.
"Could you… consider it? If you do that, then…"
"I told you to stop it… Why are you…"
"Once your concert is over, you can just set up your business here instead… It's okay, you're really popular here in Japan."
"That's enough… already. Don't tell me things… that only exist in dreams."
"Your tickets sold out, you know? You haven't fulfilled the demand here by just playing one or two concerts."
"That's just a fad. I'll be completely forgotten in a year."
"As long as you're playing the piano, you can do it anywhere, right? As you are right now, that should be possible, right?"
"So come back… to Japan. Hey, Kazusa… stay with me from now on."
"I'm sorry… but I haven't even thought of such a future."
However, the joy I had expected from her at that moment was something that only I felt, something that only I felt moved by.
"Everything will be over if you say that. All the rules we've made up until now will all be for nothing, you know?"
Frankly speaking, it's nothing more than a self-satisfactory proclamation I made to clean everything up.
"It's no different from how… you've never considered a future where you abandon Japan."
But if that possibility truly does come to fruition, I can't even imagine what conclusion will be waiting for us…
I don't even have the courage to face it. It's just like my reasoning five years ago.
"…If I told you to earnestly think about it, would you actually do it?"
"It's impossible, right…? It's the same thing."
My reasoning is so awkward that even Kazusa, who has never beaten me in an argument before, can completely shatter it.
An impossible suggestion collides with the impossible suggestion made before it, causing both to break down without a sound…
"I just said something really misguided, so just forget about it."
"Just forget about it! …It's for both our sakes."
Yet… just as it was about to break down…
At the very last moment, Kazusa loosened her grip on her strict conviction.
She was the slightest bit taken by my ridiculous and utterly absurd suggestion that was supposed to be out of the question.
"I'm… going to sleep. I don't want to do it anymore today."
Abandon… everything? All for the sake of one precious thing?
Is such a path even possible?
Is that a future that even a single person could say they'd be satisfied with?
"Well, it's about noon now, so I'll be heading back."
"I'm really sorry, President… it's all because of me."
"There is nothing for you to apologize about, Miyo-chan. Everything is because of my idiotic daughter's own decisions."
"But to think that I can't even get in touch with her, on top of her not coming to practice… If only I knew where she was staying."
"…Ah, come to think of it, I never told you."
"Let's leave her be for now. I'm sure she has a lot going on… and if the weekly publications are anything to go by, I'm already considered a tyrant as it is."
"But there are only ten days left until the next concert."
"It should only take three days for her to get back in the game."
"That's only true for you, President. The mass media said that she hadn't practiced enough last time either."
"One or two failures is nothing compared to the long life she has ahead of her."
"Did you know? I once skipped a concert to chase after a guy back in the day. It was even supposed to be my first collaboration with M-Kyou."
"…I'm aware of it. I scrapped all of the articles that were written about it back then. I intended to blackmail you with them in case you refused me my holiday."
"…You have some guts, you know that?"
"But after that, you went on a dry spell for two whole years. Everyone ignored you in Japan until Europe started to recognize you again…"
"Yet despite that, I'm still getting food on the table. I can even pay your salary, so it's not that big of a deal."
"Don't think of her as on the same level as you, she's still just…"
"Everything will be fine as long as Kazusa continues to play the piano. After all, she has the talent to surpass me."
"Ah, but I can't know if she actually does continue playing the piano. For her, there is something more important to her."
"Please, don't fan my worries even further."
"…You haven't used this at all, have you? It's barely tuned."
"I've played it maybe two or three times since I graduated university."
"Jeez… People who can't properly take care of their instruments won't ever be loved by their instruments."
"…I don't think I was ever loved by the god of music in the first place."
I take a sidelong glance at Kazusa, who is teasingly fiddling with my guitar, as I prepare the afternoon tea.
…How many days have I skipped work by now? I feel like I've lost my sense of time.
"Alright… I suppose this'll do. Do you have any requests?"
"Let's see… How about a song even I know?"

"I'm asking you because I did hear you! What in the world are you saying!?"
The sound of my shouts is absorbed by the thick, piling snow, and I'm not even sure if it reached Kazusa.
In fact, I don't even know if any sound is leaving my mouth.
I feel a gust leaking out of my throat, and it feels like it's getting in the way of me being able to speak properly.
"What am I saying…? I'm saying goodbye."
Kazusa stands up and shakes off the snow from her body, and as if nothing happened, squints her eyes and gazes at the shining snow illuminated by the morning sun.
"I'm sorry for tricking you into thinking I was serious. I'm sorry for making you take part in this dangerous game."
Looking at that expression, I can't tell if she is crying or if the radiance just makes it look like she is…
"I decided from the very beginning that… that this would end today. That we would part here."
"That this place would be our last stop."
"I still don't get it at all…!"
I'm sure that my current state that's reflected in Kazusa's eyes looks utterly wretched.
"What do you mean… from the very beginning? When did you decide!?"
I'm sure that my voice reverberating in Kazusa's ears sounds pathetic.
"Didn't we promise yesterday? The day before yesterday too, and before we even went on this trip!"
Because even I think I look pathetic and wretched.
"We promised to be together no matter what. We promised to be together no matter how much time passed."
Not even trying to listen to what the other has to say. Only forcing my own opinions on her for my own convenience.
"Didn't you accept it all…? Didn't you say you were happy, that you wanted to be with me!?"
"I lied. I tricked you so you would keep loving me…"
"Then for how long has it been a lie? Was it the night before we set off? Was it when we made love for the first time in five years? Was it when we met each other again in Strasbourg!?"
"Please, Kazusa, please tell me that you're lying about that lie… Tell me that you're just trying to mess with me!"
I grab Kazusa's shoulders and shake her violently.
Kazusa doesn't resist. Instead, she looks away with her eyes still squinted.
"If you say that, then I'll get angry, but I'll immediately embrace you again. I'll punish you again just like we always do…"
Seeing the awful attitude that I have, seeing how uncool I am and how bad I am at giving up, has she truly, and finally had enough of her former lover?
"Because we even made promises about the future…"
"Yeah, it sure was fun… pretending to be married."
That was a promise we made just a few hours ago.
"We even exchanged vows… You swore to take me as your lawful wife… Haha, I feel ridiculous just thinking back at it."
Kazusa's voice is full of nostalgia, as if her memories are brought up straight from her heart, with a tone of fondness, and embarrassment.
"You couldn't possibly have believed it all yourself, could you? It was nothing more than a role-play, right?"
"Of course I believed it! Of course those vows came straight from my heart!"
"No one… not even God would acknowledge such a vow taken without a single witness but ourselves."
"But what's the issue? The sex we had after that felt better than usual. That's all it took for me to be satisfied."
"Don't draw conclusions by yourself! Don't assume I believe the same things you do…"
"Didn't it feel good for you…? It was my intention to put my entire soul into pleasing you."
"My opinion is completely different from yours. In fact, I'm doubting whether those are your true feelings to begin with…"
"Why isn't this meant to be, Kazusa…? Why won't you be with me…?"
"You've known that for these five whole years, haven't you!? Why didn't you forget about me then?"
Perhaps she was aiming for my weak point, to push me away with a single blow…
But because I didn't falter, it's now Kazusa who looks like she's in terrible pain.
"I want to embrace you now and forever! If I can do that… then I'll be able to remain myself."
Those words aren't enough to make me give up.
If it's a battle of logic, wits, or sophistry, then there is no way Kazusa can beat me.
I would never lose a battle of words.
"Yeah, that's right. I'll be able to remain the person who loves only you, who always wants to be with you…"
"How is that… supposed to be your usual self, Haruki?"
"You'd throw away everything for my sake…? You wouldn't mind going to hell with me…?"
I would never lose an argument with Kazusa…
"This… this broken, battered self of yours, this isn't the real Haruki that I know and love!"
"Like hell he'd be tricked so easily… by these obvious lies! Stop belittling my feelings!"
"He was in the audience. He finally came to listen to me play…"
"…That's not just a dream. I saw Guitar-kun sitting in the front row."
"I see… he's here. He actually came…"
"To be honest, I have no idea how this concert is going to turn out. You're behind on your practice, your sleep, your nutrition, and we're behind on promotion. We're lacking in many aspects."
"I've caused you a lot of problems. Let me apologize fully this time."
"Well, you can make up for it next time onward, by becoming a more profitable pianist…"
"I will… I'll continue playing until I fill up all the seats no matter what country I play in, because the piano is the only thing I have left now."
"Besides, if I become that popular, a certain awful promoter will no longer have a reason to obsess about Japan."
"You really don't plan on coming back to Japan? Are you going to cut yourself off completely from the country you were born in?"
"…Ah, it's going to start soon. Then I'll go back to my own seat."
"Um, Hamada-san… I'm really sorry about this whole…"
"It's fine. I'll make sure you'll make it up to me. I have enough confidence in you to trust you with that… See you later."
Hamada-san, who was sitting in the empty seat next to mine, showed consideration toward me until the very end as he left for the seats on the second floor.
He showed consideration, turned a blind eye to a lot of deplorable things, and even worked hard to make things easier for me for when I'm back to work, all for me who refused to go to work.
And being given special treatment like this… even the editing department treated me with kiddy gloves.
When I first showed my face at the office, I must've looked wretched enough for them to think that it was necessary.
"The new guy was handed such extreme tasks that he was unable to take care of them all, and ruined his health."
Even though the cause was something private, that interpretation spread throughout the office and became a topic of discussion for the editing department.
…Hamada-san's, the managing editor's, and the chief editor's managerial ability was put into question.
And I continued behaving in such an unfair and cowardly manner.
I ran away from my responsibility through lies. I tried to protect myself to a nauseating degree.
And I feel fed up with myself for not even trying to explain the truth, and in the end, I don't even have anyone I can apologize to.
The people at my workplace are acting like they're walking on eggshells around me…
And that guilt prevents me from getting any peace of mind.
The curtain rises along the resounding sound that tells us that the concert has started.
On the stage is a single grand piano waiting for its master who is playing it tonight.
My sight immediately blurs, and my heart tries to flee to a world of delusions.
But at this moment alone, I can't allow myself to run away like a coward.
I forcibly pull my heart back, and force myself to confront the reality occurring on the stage.
Because I haven't even solved the biggest problem I'm facing.
I haven't faced the punishment for my betrayal… for my deepest sin.
In the front row is a single empty seat to my left.
There's no point in asking if the seat is free, because the person who sent the ticket for this seat to this person is the pianist currently getting on stage.
The moment the girl takes a seat next to me, heavy applause breaks out in the stadium as a woman wearing a black dress appears on stage.
"I don't want to leave… of course I don't."
"In truth, I always wanted to be with you… I wanted to shut myself in a world for just the two of us."
No matter how confident I am in my ability to refute her…
"But it's all breaking down! The more you're with me, the more you'll break down, Haruki!"
I can't oppose her if I don't understand what she's saying.
"All so you can protect me, to make sure I don't break down, to make sure I don't feel sadness…"
Yes, I barely understood a thing.
The idea that I'm breaking down, that I've been making all the wrong choices up until now.
"You're working so hard, pushing yourself… ruining yourself for something so pointless!"
But have I become incapable of understanding her because I'm already broken?
Have I become incapable of understanding words of the actual, real world because I've been shutting myself in another world meant only for the two of us all this time?
"Haruki… I really do love you. That's right, I admit I was lying earlier."
"I truly felt like running away with you until last night. I planned on following you everywhere, for as long as you'd reach out your hand to me."
That her lie itself was a lie. That her teasing me was also a lie.
That the fact that she loved me was true.
"…No, of course it's still the happiest outcome for me."
I managed to force the response I wanted out of Kazusa.
I won. It doesn't amount to much, but I won.
"I didn't even decide to break up that long ago… It was actually just a short while ago."
"I wasn't even consistent with that, making up my mind and changing my mind soon after. I couldn't make any sense of it."
Why can't I give a single retort toward Kazusa…?
"I knew that I would never be able to make up my mind if I was close to you, so I tried running away…"
Even though what she's saying makes no sense.
"Yet it was the moment I saw you… smiling at me, that I finally found my resolve."
Why can't I even contradict her by saying "You're not making any sense"? Why can't I reject her reasoning and sneer at her…?
The voice I let out to interrupt Kazusa is so faint that it doesn't reach her.
I can't let her say what she's about to say. Letting her do that would be the same as admitting it.
"I realized how tiny my limited happiness was compared to you living a normal, long, and happy life."
It'll be as if I'm admitting it, yet…
The voice I muster up from my throat is still not strong enough to reach Kazusa.
The thundering applause is different from the one before the concert started. It's powerful, long, and profound.
In only ten minutes, the whole venue has become ecstatic.
"Or well, it has only been two weeks, but it feels like much more time has passed."
And between us two, unlike the enthusiasm of the crowd, there is a tense atmosphere.
"Things feel so awkward between us. I wonder why? I don't like it… it feels like we've grown distant. It scares me."
What do you mean "it's like" we've grown distant…?
We both understand it perfectly well, but it's too painful to put that truth into words.
"You know… I want you to be happy, Haruki."
For the first time in a while, I heard Kazusa's voice, and I opened my mouth.
"That's the greatest possible happiness for me… That's not a lie."
We were completely silent when we left the inn, took the taxi and arrived at the station platform, and now we're on the train as it's passing through a tunnel.
"Then be with me… My only happiness is for you to be with me."
But that train isn't heading further north. It's a line going in the opposite direction… toward Tokyo.
A train that is leading our trip to its demise.
"What am I wrong about…? I'm telling you this myself. How can you say that it's wrong?"
"The only one who would be happy from that… is myself."
"If your happiness is my happiness, then what's wrong with my happiness being your happiness…?"
Yet even though I'm pressed against a wall like this, I still don't stop fighting back.
"Think this through again, Kazusa… come with me. Be with me from now on, together…"
Nothing is decided yet. If only I can convince Kazusa before we reach the final station, I'll win.
"Stop saying things like that already… Stop going after my weak points… You know how I am when you say things like that."
"But that choice won't make anyone but me happy."
"It will make everyone around you, including the most precious person to you unhappy. It's the worst possible escape."
I tried to ignore the difference in body temperature between us.
"There is no way you could become happy by doing that. You know that, right? You know, don't you?"
"How could I know…? In my world, there is no one but you and me, Kazusa. The other 'precious person' isn't here…"
Not here, not here… at the very least, she's not here of all places…
"No, that won't do at all, Haruki. It won't do at all…"
"Why not? You'll be happy if I'm with you, and I'll be happy if you're with me. What more could you possibly want?"
"That should be obvious already… I want you to be happy in a way that's not a lie."
"How many times do I have to tell you until you understand? Right now I'm the happiest I've ever been in my entire…"
"…You've only convinced yourself that you're the happiest you've ever been in your life. It's just a pitiful delusion."
"A Haruki who doesn't wish happiness for others… A Haruki who doesn't worry about the woman he loves… is not the real Haruki I know…"
"What are you… Hey, what are you…"
Immediately, my body is overwhelmed by sweat.
A single moment is all it takes before my headache and chills assault me again.
When I betrayed "her," and when I lied to the people close to me.
"I have no one but you… How many times do I have to tell you until you understand that…?"
Just like when I withdrew from the normal world that had been my home for the first time…
It wasn't supposed to happen again.
"I want you to be happy, Haruki… In truth, I wanted to make you happy."
I'm supposed to be able to remain myself for as long as I stay in the world made for Kazusa and me.
"But I can't… no matter how hard I tried, I couldn't…"
I was supposed to get by "without breaking" for as long as I stayed in this tiny world…
"No, you've got it wrong… As long as you're with me… As long as you stay by my side…"
Yet the throbbing in my heart won't stop. It feels like my heart is about to leap out through my mouth. The goosebumps appearing on my arm begin to spread to my whole body.
"The most important treasure for me… will break if I hold it myself."
Kazusa looks at the sudden change in my body with sadness, and continues speaking as if forcing the words out of her throat.
"I'll try to treasure you, I'll try to protect you desperately, but I'm so bad at it that you'll end up collapsing before I know it…"
Even though she has cried countless times already, she does everything she can to keep the tears welling up in her eyes from spilling.
"That's why I should give you back to the person who can treasure you much better than me."
But that effort goes to waste, her voice starts shaking, and her tears fall down her cheeks…
"Back to the person who can protect you properly…"
When we exited the tunnel… we were not greeted by a white world.
The world made for us two had already disappeared, and the world where everyone else lives had come back to us.
"Why do you look so spaced-out? Did your legs give out or something?"
"…That's the same Touma we heard last time, right?"
"What's wrong with me…? I'm getting goosebumps all over. It's getting hard to breathe…"
"So she really was capable of getting a standing ovation…"
"Do you think it's because we're amateurs? Do you think we're just getting blown away by something that only sounds impressive to us?"
"Even if that's the case, her talent is still impressive… Touma is simply amazing today."
I pull a handkerchief out of my pocket and hand it over to the person sitting next to me, who can't stop crying.
"There really are things that you can't understand, but still know they're amazing…"
The two pieces Kazusa played truly sounded as if she had been possessed by God.
…Though, I suppose that's just the evaluation of an amateur, and at the very least, it was enough to amaze one.
"It was just like this during the contest five years ago too… I cried, and you couldn't cry anymore."
Setsuna's thoughts are the exact same as during the contest back then.
"I knew she would be countless times better now than back then, so I came prepared… yet Kazusa still exceeded my expectations…"
And Setsuna's thoughts right now, are the exact same as mine.
No matter how much time Kazusa spent with me, in the end, she never let me hear her play the piano.
She would always laugh and say that she would only let me hear her play during the concert, so she could amaze me. She said this with a hint of playfulness, and the slightest bit of loneliness.
But right now, I have no choice but to recognize the weight behind those words.
Because this song is all it takes to understand… that we live in completely different worlds.
Kazusa must've kept this wonderful thing hidden away, so she would be able to enter the world for us two.
Because if I ever heard this sound, I probably would have let go of my embrace around Kazusa.
I would hesitate to corrode Kazusa's talent in my dark, bleary world where the sun never shines, when she lives in a world so much broader than mine…
And yet, Kazusa is deliberately showing us her true ability right now… no, she's showing us something more than her true ability.
"You and I… simply aren't meant for each other."
She's delivering her ironic, tearful message to me. With her own strong will, she's departing from the world where the two of us had stagnated alone.
And it's also her hidden attempt to express her guilt and regret toward the woman who's sitting right next to me with tears overflowing in her eyes.
She's trying to say that there's nothing between me and herself.
Her performance is trying to convey that she's not in a position to go on romantic trysts with me, and she doesn't have the time for it either.
It's a futile attempt to conjure up an alibi.
She's presenting her own miserable solution… which she believes is the worst for everyone, but also one that would not end up hurting anyone.
"You're going home now… Back to the world where you're important to lots of people, where some get annoyed at you yet still treasure you."
"You're going back… to a world where Setsuna exists."
I wanted to lash out at her for being unfair. "Why would you bring up Setsuna's name now?" I almost pressed that question in anger.
"Weren't you the one who pulled me away from her in the first place?"
"Weren't you the one who took advantage of my wavering feelings?"
"Weren't you the one… who made me unable to live without you?"
"Setsuna… won't forgive me anymore. We can never go back to the way we once were."
Yet there was no point in saying that.
Because everything happened according to my will, and Kazusa's responsibility for what happened is long gone.
Despite that, I'm sure that Kazusa blamed everything on herself, acknowledged her sins, and is trying to accept her punishment.
"Why do you always have to be so thick headed…? If you don't tell her anything, then nothing will have happened between us."
"I can't, I can't…. pretend that nothing happened…"
"Yes, you can… because that's what you did with me."
"You pretended that there was nothing between you and Setsuna. You lied to me and said I was the only one for you."
"That was… that was not… a lie, it wasn't a lie at all…"
Or at least it wasn't supposed to be.
I'm covered in nothing but lies…
"See? You were able to lie to me. You were able to trick me regarding your feelings for Setsuna, and made love to me instead."
What she's saying is beyond cruel, yet she doesn't speak a single word of condemnation toward me, which only makes her strike more painful.
"That's why you should just do that to Setsuna… It should be easy, right? Why else would you have practiced with me?"
"I'll help you, Haruki… I'll make sure that what happened between us remains hidden."
Rather than condemning me, she takes my side. Like that, she gives me yet another wound that will never heal.
"I have faith that Setsuna will be able to save you, now that I've broken you…"
"…I'm an awful woman. Perhaps I really never should have been born."
In front of others, not in the world made for us two…
Despite that, I let out a loud sob.
"I can't protect you, Haruki. The only one who can do that is Setsuna."
"…It's not a matter of who has the stronger feelings, because I wouldn't lose to her. I'm a terrible loser, but that's the only thing I'll never yield on."
Because I finally understood that I can't bring myself to contradict Kazusa's resolve.
"Because I'm willing to do anything for you, Haruki. I could throw away everything for you."
"Despite that, no matter how much I give to anyone, I can't protect you, Haruki."
Because I finally understood that in the world made for only us two, only I remain.
"But I'm sure Setsuna will be able to protect you… without throwing away anything. She'll be able to do that without needing any more strength than she already has…"
"That's all it takes to save you, to give you peace of mind… to always keep you happy."
Because I finally understood that Kazusa is… right.
"There are things that feelings alone can't accomplish. I haven't worked hard enough up until now in my life to attain those things."
"…When I came here, I was just reminded of that."
"I'm not a person who can protect you."
"I'm a useless person incapable of doing anything but love you. I'm a weak person who can't do the slightest thing to support you."
"I'm a woman who… will never win against Setsuna."
"Haruki-kun… here you go… It's yours in the first place, though."
After wiping her own tears with the handkerchief, Setsuna noticed that the person who gave it to her was getting more emotional than herself.
I can feel Setsuna's warmth through the handkerchief. The soft feeling once again reminds me of her unyielding kindness.
"I'm fine, it's nothing… I just got a bit of dust in my eyes…"
I feel an even greater desire to shed tears at the sensation of that warmth I have no right to accept.
Because Kazusa's divine performance is still going on.
Her performance demonstrates the power of expression she had inherited from her artist of a mother, as well as the comedic acting I had enticed her to develop.
She's combining the two abilities at an exceptional level for the sole sake of my happiness that she's imagining in her mind.
She's doing this so Setsuna won't find out about our relationship…
She's performing at this legendary concert that's likely only seen once every decade, driven by that utterly ridiculous sentiment.
The second piece was more powerful than the first, and the third piece was more powerful than the second…
The applause, cheering and excitement from the audience becomes more fervent as she goes from one piece to the next.
Even though she's unable to contain her own tears, she tries to wipe the tears off my eyes, exposing her uncontrollable crying to everyone.
"We once stood on the stage… with her, didn't we?"
She could have just wiped the tears with her other hand, but even that hand was gently holding onto my hand…
"We spent time together with her. We used to be three…"
I bet she's dying to applaud herself, but she's prioritizing watching over me.
"Kazusa is amazing, amazing, so amazing… I'm so glad I got to be her friend."
Just like Kazusa said, she's trying to save me.
The boundless kindness Setsuna has is deceiving Setsuna herself, and is bringing forth my dark heart that's trying to betray her.
It makes me want to bring her to hell with me.
"Kazusa actually came back. She came back to us, didn't she?"
"If you don't tell her anything, then nothing will have happened between us."
"I'm so glad I could see her again. I'm so happy we three could gather in the same place again."
Just as Kazusa said, just as Kazusa wanted…
Don't waste Kazusa's sacrifice… that she's ruined herself.
"You're happy too, right? You're happy too… Haruki-kun?"
Today is the anniversary of our reconciliation.
I'm supposed to remove everything I've done in the past few days from my memories, and restart…
"I have no right to be treated so well by you, Setsuna. I'm just not that kind of person…"
"I'm not trying to be kind… I'm just doing what I want to do…"
"You've got it wrong! Because I've… I've…"
I shake myself free from Setsuna's hand.
I shake myself free from Setsuna's words.
"It's okay… let's stop. You don't have to say anything."
"I've spent the last few days with Kazusa… We were together all this time."
The end of the third piece signaled the first half of the concert over, and Kazusa left the stage for a ten minute break.
From the people leaving the theatre, to those remaining in their seats, there is a sense of amazement in the air, and the theatre becomes unusually noisy.
In the middle of that commotion, we sat in complete silence for a while as if the wave of excitement completely went over our heads.
"I see… so that's how it was."
Until I forced out my words in hesitation…
"That I lied to you again, that I betrayed you again, Setsuna."
"You knew that I once again… chose Kazusa over you."
After I made my resolution and told Setsuna, she tried to interrupt me.
And once I was done telling her, she was not surprised, and neither did she try to laugh it off.
Because she knew everything. She saw through every single one of my lies.
Kazusa… your effort was pointless from the start.
Setsuna knew everything. She was only pretending to not know anything.
"Haruki-kun, if you apologize, then it'll be as if you've done something wrong. It'll be as if you've done something I can't forgive."
"I did do something wrong. I did do something unworthy of forgiveness."
For Setsuna, who was always looking at us, always worrying about me…
For Setsuna, who always loved me…
"We went north, to see the snow… We promised to always be together."
At the sound of those words, Setsuna's shoulders suddenly start to shake.
That Kazusa and I rejected a reunion between the three of us… that we cast Setsuna out.
"I… loved Kazusa. No, I love her even now."
"Ever since our reunion after five years… I was thinking about Kazusa, even when I was making love to you, Setsuna."
"I've already known that for five years. I also know that those feelings will never disappear in the future."
"It might have been okay if I was just fantasizing about her… But I actually made love to Kazusa."
Setsuna's grip on my hand grows tighter.
"Before I knew it, I couldn't even bring myself to separate myself from my feelings."
Suddenly, I feel the sensation of nails piercing my skin…
But in the end, Setsuna is still Setsuna. She's unable to put any force into it, and thus doesn't cause me any real harm.
"That alone… should never be forgiven. Even you should know that, Setsuna…"
She can't bring herself to condemn me. She can't bring herself to acknowledge my sin.
On the contrary, she's accepting the situation in a way that's completely wrong by thinking that the fault lies with her.
Ever since that day at the airport, five years ago…
That's why rather than to condemn me for my sin, rather than to lament my treatment of her, she focuses on worrying about me.
Just as Kazusa worried about my life ahead over her own feelings.
"We don't have any points of contact anymore. The worlds we live in are far too different."
"That's what Kazusa is telling us right now… with her piano."
I'm sure that Kazusa wanted to tell that to Setsuna without exposing the truth.
But in the end, I even stomped on that last desire of hers, and remained truthful to Setsuna to the very last detail. In doing so, I might have done something even more despicable.
I hear Kazusa's exasperated voice telling me that.
"Don't give me the right to choose…"
She'll gladly cry over Kazusa's piano, but she protects herself to no end from the cruel truth laid before her.
"I'll… go to hell by myself. I'll accept my punishment."
"If you do that, I'll never be able to ignore you… If you suffer so much, Haruki-kun, then I'll…"
"That's enough already… There's something more important for you to do than to worry about me."
This isn't the proper reaction of a woman who just got betrayed.
"Worry about yourself a little… Do you have any idea how much I have hurt you…?"
Those naive, and direct eyes that no one can blame me for getting fed up with, for getting angry at in return.
…Those criminally gentle eyes that almost give me a misguided sense of hope.
"Hey, Haruki-kun… Did you forget about me?"
"You said that when you were making love to me, you were thinking about Kazusa, right?"
"In that case, when you were making love to Kazusa… Did you think about me even if for a little bit?"
"Why… would you ask something so pointless?"
"No matter what I answer, it won't change the fact that I betrayed you, Setsuna."
"…You're probably right. So what's your answer?"
"I'm just asking for reference. I don't expect anything to change by asking this."
Of course I can't answer that question.
…After all that has happened, I can't answer in a way that lets me cling on to Setsuna.
If my feelings were for one person alone, then I wouldn't have suffered as much as I have.
Whenever I met Setsuna, whenever I embraced Setsuna, the image of Kazusa always forced its way into my head.
It wasn't only once or twice that I heard Setsuna's gentle voice calling out to me when I was alone with Kazusa, and when I was making love to Kazusa.
That's why I closed off my heart. I broke myself.
That's why I did what I did to Setsuna…
"I forgot about you completely. I betrayed you from the depths of my heart, Setsuna…"
…Of course I can't bring myself to say that. It would be nothing else but the remark of a defeated man.
Setsuna puts her right hand tightly around her left hand, as if trying to hide her ring finger…
"You don't have to forgive me, or even understand me. I'm only saying that for my own satisfaction."
"I don't expect to be forgiven even if I apologize. I plan on living with that burden for the rest of my life."
It won't do Setsuna any good, but to me, it's nothing but a selfish decision I've chosen for myself, a punishment that will let the pain of hell remain forever.
"If you do that, Haruki-kun, you'll be crushed under your own sense of responsibility… just like that time five years ago…"
And Setsuna realizes exactly what kind of punishment I'm hinting at.
"It'd be stranger if I didn't end up that way. After all, I did the same thing I did five years ago."
My punishment began the moment I committed my sin.
That's why I can't force the burden of giving me hope upon Setsuna. I can't force the burden of giving me compassion onto her.
Setsuna should no longer be by my side.
Because not even I know how much pain awaits us in the future.
It's not okay for the best woman in the world to be with the worst man in the world.
"Because… if you stay with me any longer, Setsuna…"
"Let's listen for now… to Kazusa's piano."
Before I realized it, the surrounding illumination was gone.
The moment Kazusa in her black dress reappears on stage, she is met with an enthusiastic applause strong enough to break the walls of the building.
Robert Schumann. Piano Sonata No. 2 in G minor, Op 22.
Once Touma Kazusa is done playing all four movements, her concert in Japan will be completely over.
"I'm going back to the hotel. …This will be our farewell."
"I'll send you a ticket, so promise me you'll come."
"Stop crying already. You're not acting like an adult."
My eyes, bloodshot from crying, let out one tear after another without any sign of stopping.
I'm fully aware of how pathetic I look, but right now I'm powerless to control my emotions.
"…No matter how much you cry, I won't change my mind."
More than that, this moment alone is one in which I do not want to hold back. This moment of so much sorrow.
"Because you'll be able to live on without me… Actually, you'll be better off without me."
"B-But will… will you really be fine? Will you be okay without me?"
She's incapable of anything but playing the piano. All vital skills one needs to lead a normal life such as cooking, doing laundry and housework are completely unknown to her.
If she were to lose her pianoーif she were to lose the most precious thing to her other than me…
"It's okay, I'll go on living too. I'll manage somehow with my mother."
"I'm sure that I'll even find a new guy one day. Even without you, I'll…"
"…Of course that's a lie! I didn't want you to worry, so I forced myself to act strong, but you had to ruin it…"
But the idea that I'm worried about Kazusa's future is in itself a lie…
In reality, I just don't want to let her go, I don't want to give her over to someone else. I'm just being unreasonable and selfish.
"You don't have to act strong. You don't have to hold back. That's not what I want."
"But that's what I want. I want you to become more happy than I am. That's why I'm trying to act strong, that's why I'm holding back."
"I want you to remain strong… to live on as the Haruki that used to love me, and to remain the way you were when we first met."
"This isn't 'just one thing'! How shameless can you be!?"
"You're never accommodating of anything, but you're always moving on steadily, grasping at happiness… That's the correct way for you to live, isn't it?"
"Don't cry. We cried it out in the train, didn't we?"
"I won't cry anymore. For as long as I'm in Japan, I won't show another tear. So you shouldn't cry anymore either…"
When we cried together, we swore to not cry anymore, to not show our tears…
Even so, even so… it's just impossible.
Damn it, she's amazing. Kazusa's piano is too amazing.
She's moving further and further away from me.
Our difference in status was large enough in the first half, and we're growing even further apart in the second half.
She's telling me with the movements of her fingers that she's no longer in my league… that our paths will no longer cross.
It's frustrating, sorrowful, and lonely… It's so painful that I have no choice but to feel moved.
To be honest, I'm not sure if the reason I feel moved is because of her performance, or if it's only because of my feelings for Kazusa.
Whatever it is, I can say with certainty that her performance right now is stabbing at my heart, and forcing the tears out of my eyes one after another.
She's on a completely different level compared to five years ago… yet there's something I love in her piano that hasn't changed all this time.
At times, she would play along with my awful guitar. At times, she would play along with our unskilled cover of White Album.
And at times… she would free herself of us, and extend her wings toward the world, like she's doing now.
She's turning into someone… I can no longer reach.
"I feel like crying so bad… It wasn't like this the last time she played at all."
"I can lend you my shoulder if you want to wipe your tears."
"…Sorry, I'll borrow your shoulders for a bit."
"It's that piano that's strange… Look, there are lots of other people who are crying. Why is she so good at reaching the hearts of amateurs?"
"Are you stupid…? These are the second-floor seats, aren't they? How could you possibly notice that?"
"Because… I never fail to notice a woman crying."
"At last, it's time for the last movement."
"It is. This will be her last in Japan…"
"It'll be fine… The reactions are good enough as they are, so I'm sure another offer will come soon."
"I want to listen to her again too. Let's plan another performance in Japan next year. This time, we could even do a countrywide tour."
"That sounds nice… I'd like to hear her play again too."
"You really don't plan on coming back to Japan? Are you going to cut yourself off completely from the country you were born in?"
"But I will never give up on loving him. That's why I don't have to see him again."
"Of course I will! After all, I love him so much, you know?"
"I love the way he's so unremarkable."
"Rather than his looks, it's his weaknesses… The way he'll let himself be dragged along by someone like me like a fool, is so dear to me."
"Though I'm sure you knew everything anyway, yet you never told anyone… That's how amazing my love is."
"…Are you fed up with me? Are you fed up with me talking about my love life with my mother despite my age?"
"I suppose it's better than a mother talking about her own love life with her daughter."
"Thank you… I wanted to become a mother like that… maybe."
"Don't lose hope, and God might just arrange things in your favor."
"Curtains up in another five minutes… It's about time."
"This must be the first time you've said that."
"While I am at it then… you should know I don't regret giving birth to you."
"It looks like I've still got something to live for for quite a long time."
"I put my faith in you, God…"
"Make things right with Setsuna, okay? Though maybe it doesn't mean anything coming from the person who tore you two apart."
"Don't give up even if she finds out about me. Setsuna wouldn't hate you because of something like that."
"She's… even more stubborn than me… She's even more obsessed with a single guy than me."
"That's why I can leave you in her care… She's the only one who can save you, now that I've broken you."
"Why would you… put such a heavy burden on Setsuna?"
"Because I hate Setsuna. From this day forth, she will be my sworn enemy."
"She has everything I lack. She has the strength to do things I can't. She will steal the man I love from me."
Kazusa lowered her head as she spoke those words, but immediately afterward, she raised her head with a faint smile.
…There's no longer any trace of tears.
"Haruki… Thank you for everything up until now."
Within the bustle of the city…
"Thank you for throwing away everything for my sake. Thank you for forgetting about Setsuna, if even for a moment… Thank you for breaking yourself for my sake."
Our connection is brought down to nothing but the entwinement of our fingertips.
"But… it's all over now. You're going back to being your true self. Back to being the Haruki that belongs to Setsuna…"
If our fingertips let go of each other, then Kazusa will disappear into the city, and I'll disappear into the station.
"I'll never forget about how I got to be your wife."
We'll turn our backs on each other without turning back, and the one who looks at the other's face first will be the loser, but there won't be any punishment.
"It was only for one night, and I didn't get to do anything that would make me seem like a wife, but…"
Because if one knows the other has lost, they themself will have lost too.
"Despite that… I was unmistakably the happiest bride in the world…"
That would be our last promise, and the last thing we insist on.
Our holy ceremony, to conclude our one day as a married couple, and to get divorced immediately after.
"Let's part with a smile… Let's stop dragging each other along…"
"Everything will be solved if you just pull your hand away. You'll be able to go anywhere."
"…Don't be a bully. I wanted you to let go of me."
"I just wanted you to… reject me…"
Our hands finally separate… and our bodies start moving in different directions.
The last expression that I could see Kazusa make…
…Wasn't visible. She was desperately trying to hide her face from me.
This is perhaps the first time in my life I have heard a thunderous applause.
It isn't anything transient, but something that only grows in power as time passes, increasing its pitch and reverberating throughout the entire concert hall.
And the performer who sat by her piano in a daze stands up as if she just remembered to. She faces the audience, which only causes the applause to roar louder.
Unlike her mother, the performer doesn't show off any flashy gestures; instead, she only clumsily bows her head over and over again.
But perhaps that amateurish reaction tugged at the audience's heartstrings even more, because the applause and whistles didn't die down.
It's almost as if this is a performance that will pass into legend… Actually, I imagine that some will refer to this concert as precisely that tomorrow.
The enthusiasm in the hall doesn't lessen at all as everyone looks at her with passionate eyes, giving her all the applause they can muster.
And in the end… I lost my battle with Kazusa.
Because I find myself looking at Kazusa's expression with such intensity as she stands up on the stage.
But in the end, the two of us never settled our dispute.
Kazusa gave a short bow to the guests sitting straight ahead, the ones sitting on the sides, and even the ones sitting on the second floor.
But even at the very end, she never once glanced at the front row.
And with the passing of this last day…
Touma Kazusa vanished… from my side, and from Japan.
"Like I said, I'll take care of it tomorrow…"
"Tomorrow is no good! We have a meeting first thing in the morning on Monday, so you need to get it checked with me today."
"Huh? Hamada-san, won't you be available tomorrow…?"
"Let me take a break every once in a while. It's our monthly meeting."
"Um, I too have important business tonight…"
"Whaat? You have a lot of guts saying that to your superior when he's in so much trouble."
"…I understand. I'll return to the editing department."
"If I'm to finish it all, it'll take until about 2 AM, is that alright?"
"H-Hey, Kitahara… Sorry, forget I said anything. You can go home for today."
"Ah, well… I'll show up early on Monday and do my check, then. Don't worry about it and go home for today."
"Hamada-san, I'm grateful that you're being so thoughtful, but if you put it so bluntly…"
"No, I just got in over my head. You're already doing three people's worth of work as it is."
"I'd gladly do it anytime, but just not today… I'm sorry."
"I got it. I won't force the issue anymore… I'd rather not have you get sent off to America anyway."
"It's okay, I have no intention of going abroad right now. Besides…"
"I'm probably more liable to die under her care than here."
"Hahaha, no doubt about it. She might be good at watching over people, but the work she hands out isn't what I'd call normal."
"Well then, I'm sorry, but I should be going… I'll send you an email by tomorrow."
"Yeah, good work today. Have a nice weekend."
Even though I've managed to earn myself some time off, there's still a tiny feeling of loneliness remaining within me.
It's like a scar… The events of back then still impose a considerable effect on my daily life, even a year later.
In my second year as a working adult, during winter. I finally stopped going to the hospital, in the second month.
One year ago, I stopped having to rely on medicine anymore to treat my "mental damage as a result of overworking," as the doctors decided to interpret my symptoms as.
But even then, for half a year, certain things would cause my nerves to stop listening to me, which caused those around me considerable trouble.
Traces of that happening are still present at work, as Hamada-san and the others have stopped giving difficult jobs like before, instead only giving me assignments a new employee would get.
…It actually feels quite unfulfilling, but even this is something I brought upon myself, so I have no right to complain.
…Although I think I might have left the road to success in life.
My second year as a working adult. In other words, one year since then…
The national Touma Kazusa craze has died down. You don't see her in the newspaper nowadays, or even in the weekly magazines.
But that's not because the pianist Touma Kazusa is less active or that the public opinion of her has decreased. In fact, it's the opposite…
Her appearance in popular magazines has decreased, but recognition of her in the magazines that specialize in music has only increased.
As if planting her roots in Europe, she started an aggressive tour of musical performances where she lives. Ever since her last performance in Japan, she has truly blossomed.
Using Touma Youko's influence to her advantage, she hasn't just held individual performances, but has also played along with famous orchestras.
She has been fully recognized by the world as "the young pianist from Vienna."
…Since she's no longer known as a "Japanese celebrity," her recognition in national magazines has decreased.
It's been a year since then…
It's been a year since that last concert. A year since Kazusa disappeared before my very eyes.
A year since I broke up with Setsuna.
"Umm, this next song will be the last."
"Ahah, that was just a formality. Don't worry, I've got two encore songs prepared."
"The public relations specialist from Knights is in a band."
It was half a month ago I heard that rumor from a client…

I heard that the band's tickets for their concerts were very popular even among those that weren't aware of what was going on behind the scenes, so much that the tickets were typically sold out before noon on the day they went on sale.
"Ah, before we start the last song, I have an announcement to make."
"Thanks to the hosts here, I have another concert planned at Studio Troy… It will be on the 21st of next month, on the Spring Equinox Day, at 6 PM."
"And actually, I've been talking to the other members about some things I'd like to try out next time…"
"I'm not sure how much I should reveal yet, but… we'll probably have a new song prepared."
"Our band leader is doing his utmost to compose it right now, so I'd be happy if you could direct your cheers of encouragement to him."
"Well then, I'll be playing my last song now… Please listen to I Want To Love You."
This is actually the first time I've looked up at Setsuna from a viewer's seat.
After all, I've always been looking at her from behind as she sings, all while I played the guitar.
I pulled every string I knew and used a lot of my connections to get my hands on this platinum ticket.
But I feel like that effort was worth it. Because Setsuna really does shine when she's on stage.
…She's shining so much that she rivals even Kazusa's performance back then.
Though, of course, this performance is completely different from the performance from back then. From the audience to the mood, and above all, the amount of people watching.
Still, the audience is listening attentively as if in a trance, and they're swaying their bodies along with the slow tempo of Setsuna's voice.
It's not strong enough to leave a mark in their hearts. Rather, her voice gently envelops us, though there's also a brilliant quality to it.
More than anything… her smile is dazzling, and that's probably not just my personal opinion.
That's right, it's been a year since then…
Setsuna has now come to smile like this.
She was betrayed despite doing nothing wrong. She was one-sidedly hurt and was forced to separate from someone in the most unreasonable manner.
Just like six years ago, when she lost her smile… No, she was treated even worse this time, yet she still never broke.
She's beautiful yet strong. She's cute yet sturdy. She's turned into a good woman.
…She has no need for someone like me anymore.
In order to not be seen by Setsuna, I exit the club while the cheers are still ongoing.
…Though it's not as if anything's going to change even if she does see me.
It's long past the scheduled end of her performance, yet not a single person besides me has left the venue.
That's how popular the band is… or rather, how popular the singer is.
The sky had been on the brink of breaking down ever since I arrived at the concert hall, but in a moment's obstinance, it allowed the cold wind to freeze its tears into ice.
And now, as if to drown out the sound of Setsuna's singing, the scattering powder snow descending from the heavens grows ever more dense.
Even when I try to look for the source of that whiteness, it is completely hidden in the darkness of the night and the white snow.
Just like that day we promised never to part.
Just like that day our promise was shown to be a castle built on sand.
The first time I looked up at that girl standing on the stage.
The snow always appears at the crossroads in our lives, to remind us of all our pain, and sadness.
As I watch the snow fall down from the sky, I suddenly feel a light impact on the back of my head.
"Why would you leave in the middle of it all? I even said there was going to be an encore."
I grab my head and turn around, and I'm met with a girl still in her stage costume, raising her clenched fist at me with puffed up cheeks.
"There was only fifteen minutes left. Surely it wouldn't have hurt to wait that long, would it?"
The famous singer stands before me, out of breath.
"Actually, you should've told me if you were going to come… You haven't shown your face here once, and now you suddenly turn up out of nowhere."
In all that crowd, she had no trouble finding me standing far in the back.
"More importantly, Setsuna… What about the encore?"
"All the fans are booing at me right now, you know? You really caused me a lot of trouble."
"It's not funny! Making my customers angry is no joke! This business is all about gaining people's favor!"
"It's not my fault! It's your fault for leaving, Haruki-kun. Don't you feel the least bit sorry…?"
"I don't… know anyone as silly as you, Setsuna."
I really can't believe this woman.
She's an adorable, strong, and gentle woman… who's also incomparably foolish.
She's betrayed the expectations of all her audience for the sake of a single member among them.
But she doesn't see that action as her own; instead, she deludes herself into thinking that I made her do this.
Her unbelievable strength of will to support the one person who made her suffer… and betrayed her twice, for a whole year.
"If you keep calling me an idiot like that, I might actually turn into an idiot."
Before I know it, Setsuna's face is resting on my chest.
