"I might fall in love with you so much that I'll be unable to hate you no matter what you do to me, you know?"
But that's obvious. After all, I'm the one who pulled her toward me.
"Are you okay? Are you cold? Does it hurt anywhere? Are you… suffering?"
"It's just that I feel guilty. For falling in love with you again, Setsuna…"
Because I'm causing Setsuna trouble again. I'm giving Setsuna no choice but to protect me.
When Kazusa's final concert ended, Setsuna left my side.
But I still couldn't accept that reality, so I spent all my days in my apartment, separating myself from everyone…
It only took Setsuna a week to come back to my apartment.
She had recovered faster than the person who wronged her, and with her own power at that. After that, she put all her power into rehabilitating the perpetrator.
…She turned into an idiot who's unbelievably meddlesome and likes to look after me.
"Why did you come back to me…?"
"I came to steal you back, Haruki-kun…"
"Why do this for someone like me…?"
"Because I hate Kazusa. She's my sworn enemy."
"In a single week, I cried a year's worth of tears. That's why I had faith I could persevere for a year."
At that time, I was completely broken.
Going outside and seeing other people was painful. Just talking to people made my body shut down, so I certainly wasn't in any condition to go to work.
On top of that, when Setsuna came to visit, I felt no better. I said the most awful things to her, and rejected her with all my strength.
I will never forget… the words Setsuna spoke to me then.
"Do you want to forget me and overcome this? Do you want to overcome this with me? Those are the only two choices you have right now, Haruki-kun."
"Haruki-kun, do you know which one sounds happier to me?"
…I sobbed just as loudly as the day I parted with Kazusa, out of the sheer idiocy of it all.
"Ah, changing the subject, I have an announcement."
Half a year has passed since then…
"Thankfully, the plans for my next birthday have also been decided… It will be on the 14th this month, midnight on Valentine's Day."
"It's going to be a weekday… so how about holding it in my apartment at 8 o'clock in the evening?"
My emotional scars slowly healed, and I learned to blend into society like I used to…
"8 o'clock? The time we decided on was 6 o'clock, wasn't it? I get that you're busy, though."
"Maybe this isn't the best way to put it… but in exchange, how about you come over right now? I'll take you home tomorrow."
And next to me was this idiotic girl snuggling up to me.
"My adorable, adorable Setsuna-sama. I love you more than anyone in the world. Please stay with me until morning."
"…I'll do it if you say that."
Before I even realized it, I've begun to talk to this foolish girl who's so dear to me.
"Well, I've been trained well by the one I love the most… And by the one who loves me the second most."
"I love you more than anyone in the world."
Because I probably still love Kazusa even now. She's probably still tied for being the one I love more than anyone else in the world.
But with the way I am now, I can't live without Setsuna.
If Setsuna isn't by my side… I wouldn't know where I'd go in my life.
Setsuna's voice gently spreads throughout the city covered in snow.
As if singing a lullaby to protect me.
During a day so carefree… but also a day where our bond grows deeper.
Without apparent reason, it shows its white shape to me.
The snow will cover up all of it.
The painful days of the past, and the sins I don't want to remember.
A white world abundant only in beauty expands before our eyes, leaving us there in its wake.
But at the end of the day… Snow is all that it is.
Once it melts, all of the hidden truths and forgotten emotions it had been hiding will once again be brought into daylight for all to see.
They will penetrate the snow and the earth, and bloom into the sky like a nameless flower.
"Yes, they should be arriving at the gate soon."
"Don't use any name boards, okay? The mass media might find out. Do your best to recognize them yourself."
"Leave it to me! I remember their faces perfectly!"
"Though they've probably forgotten what you look like, Miyo-chan."
"Oh, don't dampen my spirits like that, President."
"Well, in any case, there's likely going to be crowds since it's Christmas, so do make sure to not lose sight of them."
"Yes, it certainly does seem more crowded than usual. But it's all concentrated around the departure gates. Families, couples… friends…"
"Yes… I'm sorry for bringing up the topic when it has nothing to do with you, Miyo-chan.
"Whose fault do you think it is that my life turned out this way!?"
"If anything, you should be grateful to your employer for providing you with such a convenient excuse."
"…Oh, hey! I found them! Excuse me for a moment."
"Cut it out already, Kazusa… Why do you have to insist on being so pointlessly stubborn?"
"You're the one who should cut it out! I've already told you I'll forgive you if you simply apologize. Why can't you do something as simple as that!?"
"I'll tell you precisely why I can't apologize… That's because this time, I haven't done a single thing wrong."
"That's it, I'm divorcing you! It's a Narita divorce for us!"
"Don't misuse your terms. A Narita divorce is synonymous with an instant divorce. We've been married for years now so it doesn't apply to us."
"I'll say it again, I despise how you have to find fault with everything I say, and grasp at every straw!"
"Oh, that's an absolute honor! I didn't become who I am because I wanted you to like me."
"Don't talk! Don't speak! Don't open your mouth! I never want to hear your voice again!"
"Those all mean the same thing. We're back in Japan now, so you should use proper Japanese."
"Forget about me… I don't think those two can find each other… Um, on a mental level."
"Now then, I'll be sleeping in this room… Don't you dare come in."
"I could say the same. Apologize and cry all you want about how lonely you are later, I still won't let you into my bed!"
"Like hell I'd ever do that! Not ever in my life!"
After uttering her parting remark for the umpteenth time, Kazusa vigorously shut the door and disappeared into the other room.
…I'm seriously glad I picked a suite. It would be beyond awkward if we had to stay in the same room together all night.
"…I'm sorry, Kudou-san. I know this was the absolute worst timing for all of this."
And I'm beyond sorry for all of this.
This person, or more specifically Kudou Miyoko of the Japanese branch of Touma Youko Office, showed us to our suite despite looking completely taken aback,
"Anyway, you should rest for today. I'll come pick you two up tomorrow morning."
"I'm really sorry. Pass my apologies to Youko-san as well."
"Ah, it's okay, the president doesn't seem to mind at all… She couldn't stop laughing on the other end of the line, in fact."
Well, I can deduce two things from Kudou-san's remark.
The first being that Youko-san is still doing alright.
And the second being that Kudou-san is really worried about our quarrel…
"It's surely just a pointless worry of mine, but you two don't intend on being like this for your entire stay in Japan, right!? You'll make up, right!?"
Walking away, Kudou-san kept glaring at me with a grim expression until it was no longer visible behind the closing door.
Well, it's not like I don't understand where she's coming from, and I do feel bad for her, but this matter is one I refuse to back down on.
I may be Kazusa's man and faithful employee, but that doesn't mean I have to tolerate her selfish childishness every single time.
But still… thinking back, this trip to Japan was nothing but trouble from the start.
I mean, yeah, it was my fault at first.
My business meeting back home was prolonged, causing us to miss our flight, and causing Kazusa to have to wait at the airport for five hours.
But she didn't seem to mind at the time. The problems only started after we boarded the next flight, and the transit that followed.
A certain someone began to whine that she couldn't sleep and wanted pudding on the plane. (Guess who!)
Inside a store at the transit airport, a certain someone made a scene over losing her wallet. (Guess who!)
After waking up, a certain someone watched a romance movie, but flipped out when the main characters broke up at the end despite being in love. (Guess who!)
…See what I'm talking about? I was only at fault in the beginning, but the rest is all on her.
As I murmur these complaints to myself, I turn on the shower and let the warm water pour down on me.
I can feel my stiff muscles finally start to relax after hours of doing nothing but sitting.
In the same vein, my stubborn heart also starts to relax a little.
Yes, the one who started it is to blame for everything. I'm the one who put her in that mood to begin with.
This was Kazusa's long-awaited return to Japan.
…After years of running away, we've finally returned to the place we once called home.
It's unreasonable to expect her to remain calm on such a special occasion.
And besides, the problem isn't just the fact that we've come back.
There's something waiting for us here; something that makes it even harder for the two of us to remain calm.
That's right, I should go and apologize.
When I leave the shower, I should calm myself down a little, call her, knock on her door, and bow my head…
But before I could even reflect on my actions…
"You, you… How can you stand there and take a shower so nonchalantly!? Doesn't abandoning me affect you in the slightest!?"
"I haven't abandoned you long enough to have abandoned you yet!"
"No, don't say that… It was all my fault! I'll apologize! I'll do anything! So please don't abandon me like that!"
"Try to stay angry for at least an hour. Give me time to reflect on my actions…"
"No… Let me apologize. I'm sorry, I'm sorry, Haruki."
Kazusa clings to my body while I'm still completely naked and dripping wet.
And from the still running showerhead above, warm water pours down on the both of us.
"If you stay cold like this, you'll end up catching one yourself, you know."
"It's okay. You'll keep me warm, Haruki."
Such a stupid reason to get soaked, yet Kazusa looks so beautiful, cute, and utterly helpless all the same…
In this cramped hotel bathroom, surrounded by hot water, we bring each other into a passionate and powerful embrace.
"Kitahara-saan, Kazusa-saan, it's about time you woke up."
"Hm? Ah, good morning… I'm sorry, what time is it?"
"Ehm, if I may, it's almost twelve…"
"Huh, is it so late already? I'm so sorry, I'll get ready immedi… Uaaah!?"
"S-Sorry, it's nothing… Hey, wake up already! You can't stay half asleep forever!"
"Don't worry, I've been awake for a while now…"
"But your actions make you seem half asleep! Hey, cut that out! Not so hard… Ngh!"
"Miyo-chan wouldn't mind waiting a little more."
"No, we can't do that… In fact, if we linger any longer, she'll definitely find out what we're up to."
"So what? We've finally reconciled now… And besides, you were completely engrossed in it until sunrise yourself, Haruki."
"Only because you kept pestering me to… Ah, no, Kazusa, I told you… stop that…!"
"Nope, I won't stop. Mh, mhm… Haruki, mmh… aaah…"
"So according to you, spending yet another day flirting with your husband takes priority over reuniting with your own mother…
"It's not my fault. My body has been thoroughly conditioned to wither away whenever Haruki isn't around."
Today was another eventful day, but after a brief meeting with the Japanese branch of our company (Kudou-san), I concluded all my "work" in Japan.
Although, even what I'm doing right now could be considered honorable work, as I'm having dinner with the esteemed president of our company.
Of course, neither the hostess nor our guest seem to see it that way…
"Besides, you never acted like a proper parent when I was a child to begin with. This is no less than your just deserts."
"K-Kazusa… how cold of you. You mean to say that you couldn't care less if your mother died alone in some barren corner of the world?
"You sure did. No doubt about it."
"Besides, we talked over video chat for over five hours the day before departure, didn't we?"
"How about you do your job instead, Kazusa…"
In fact, this is no more and no less than a loving family sitting around a dinner table.
These two have always found themselves separated for one reason or another,
"Well, let's set the formalities aside for now, and raise a toast."
"I'd love to hear what part of our conversation just now was 'formal' to you."
"Whenever you're around, Haruki, even the most cheerful family gathering feels like a board meeting."
"If you're going to curse anyone, you should curse yourself for choosing an inflexible control freak instead of enjoying freedom like me."
Almost as if trying to make up for the past dissonance between them, they now share a bond that binds them even stronger than when they were living together.
"Hey, by the way, is he still as stiff as ever?"
"How old do you think we are now? He's obviously as stiff as any man could possibly be, every single day."
"Okay, both of you, stop saying things that could be horribly misinterpreted!"
Though to be honest, their bond right now is so powerful that I feel slightly uncomfortable having to sit next to them.
"So what? This is my first one-on-one meeting with my daughter in so long."
The wine Youko-san ordered is a 1989 vintage Chateau Haut-Brion.
I've read about it in a feature article about wine once before. One of those bottles can easily go for at least 100,000 yen.
"Hey, do you remember, Kazusa? This is the same wine we ordered during our first visit to this restaurant."
"Of course I don't remember. You gulped the whole thing down all by yourself."
1989 also happens to be the year of my birth.
…Of course, that's probably not the reason Youko-san chose this exact wine.
"Ah, of course, you were still underage at the time. Oh how I remember seeing you cry your eyes out over your first heartbreak."
"Say another word and I'm going home. I'm not talking about the hotel, I'm going straight back to Vienna."
And it seems that the actual story surrounding this wine is one I'll never get to hear about.
"W-Well, setting the price aside, you do have permission from your doctor to drink this, right?"
"Indeed, they told me I can drink as long as I do so in moderation. I don't intend on wasting my life either."
"…Speaking of, how are you feeling lately?"
"Well, I'm doing my best. I take regular check-ups and I don't neglect my medication. I'm doing everything the doctors told me to do to the letter."
It's been three years since Youko-san was diagnosed with leukemia.
Just as Youko-san herself said back then, not even tomorrow was a certainty for her.
"At the very least, I can see myself living long enough to name my first grandchild, attend her entrance ceremony, see her reach adulthood,
"No, you'd be a lich at that point. Also, don't kill off our child before the poor thing is even born."
"…Then perhaps you should present me with a grandchild soon so I don't have to become a lich."
Whether this conversation bears any greater meaning or not, Kazusa's attitude changes immediately upon hearing it, opting now to eat without uttering a word.
In fact, she's always like this when she talks to Youko-san.
Even when talking to Youko-san over video chat, she refuses to ever touch the subject.
It's not like I don't understand her feelings, if anything, I understand them all too well…
It's just that I really need to know.
Because if the worst were to happen to Youko-san, it'd be my duty to protect Kazusa mentally.
This is the purpose I promised Youko-san I would fulfill.
"In that case… let us share a toast in honor of our new family member who is certain to be conceived any day now. You'll do your part too, won't you Kazusa?"
"I've never been against the idea once. It's only my tightfisted manager who keeps rejecting the idea."
"I just said I'd… um… think about it."
One of the reasons I'm reluctant to have a child with Kazusa… is that I don't want "the birth" to coincide with "the inevitable."
I don't want Kazusa to be forced to bear the burden of losing someone and meeting someone new at the same time.
In the end, Kazusa is all that matters to me… even if that means I have to sacrifice Youko-san's happiness.
But that can also be said about Youko-san…
Youko-san knows that I'm trying to estimate when "the inevitable" will happen.
She knows that I'm preparing myself for the moment she passes the torch to me.
Because… the two of us are close enough to be that frank with each other. We're mother and son now, after all.
"You can't be serious. Why would we hold a wedding ceremony so late?"
"Why, because you two haven't actually held a proper ceremony."
It was when dinner was over, when we had finished our drinks and our tongues were thoroughly loosened when it happened.
It was then that Youko-san finally started discussing the real reason for inviting us back to Japan.
"Nowadays plenty of people skip wedding ceremonies."
Yes, it's about Kazusa's and my wedding ceremony.
A celebratory ceremony that the two of us, having run away from Japan and betrayed everything we had, could never be allowed to hold.
"That won't do. You still haven't given your beloved mother her bouquet yet."
"You're the only mother who would pester her daughter about that."
"You know, hearing you say 'Mom, thank you for everything' all teary-eyed while reading your wedding letter is the reason I'm trying to live a long life."
"Why does your love always have to be so twisted…?"
Ever since we arrived in Vienna, we've lived our lives with our backs turned to the people we used to love.
The first sign of that snow beginning to melt was about half a year ago.
It came in the form of a visit to Vienna by Youko-san, who took the trip despite her illness.
"You two should begin to resolve yourselves… You came back to Japan knowing this was the purpose, didn't you?"
Yes, we knew. None of this is coming out of the blue.
True, Youko-san did force the issue a bit, but we were the ones who consented in the end.
The guilt from being in the same place as those we made unhappy. The shame of showing our faces once more. The memories of our horrible last farewells.
The pain associated with returning to Japan still remains strong within us.
The joy of being in the same place as those we once loved. The adoration we feel for the country we were raised in.
In the same way, these naive hopes also remain deep within us.
"The time and place are still secret for now… I'll tell you when it happens."
Without a doubt, this is an absurd plan we're going along with.
But even then, we find ourselves unable to question Youko-san's scheming, left only to gawk at her self-assured expression.
"Until that time comes, go out there and enjoy your dear Japan… How about catching up with some old friends?"
The sunlight beaming in through the massive high-rise hotel window has already lit up the room thoroughly.
Yet a sleeping beauty remains tucked within her bed amidst the abundant light.
…Though I suppose some things never change no matter what country we're in.
Of course, I'm not going to act annoyed or surprised. Kazusa's always like thisーexcept for when she's playing the piano, that is.
"Why would you wake me up so early…? Lemme sleep until lunch."
"I'm already hungry. I want lunch now."
In any case, it's been five hours since I woke up. I'm starting to get bored of looking at her sleep…
"Then call for room service or something."
"No, wake up! We're going to head out soon."
"We're going to enjoy Japan, aren't we? …Did we not promise Youko-san last night?"
I suppose it's tough to say if that can even be considered a promise, though Kazusa didn't seem to oppose the idea at the time, at least.
…But she didn't really agree to it either.
"Let's go to the lounge and discuss where we'll go over lunch, okay? Come on, let's get dressed and…"
"I'm not going. I'll be asleep all day."
"…There's seriously nothing for me to do. I've miraculously managed to wrap up all my work for the year."
"Going out is only going to exhaust me. I'd much rather have your thing… inside my mouth."
"…! That would exhaust you more than going out."
"In any case, I said I'm not going, so you should stay with me, Haruki. Let's watch some lame suspense movie rerun together."
"Don't watch it if you already know it's lame…"
Even when throwing one of her childish tantrums, Kazusa has never once suggested that I go out by myself.
"But I don't have anywhere I want to go, nor anyone I can meet."
"How about catching up with some old friends?"
I wonder if those last words by Youko-san had a specific intention behind them, or if she was simply trying to be sarcastic.
…One thing's for certain though: she didn't mean it simply as a passing remark.
You're supposed to have been forgiven.
In Vienna, half a year ago.
By a visitor we never could have imagined would come. During an impossible reunion, and the miraculous reconciliation that followed.
"Of course I do! But… I can't take the initiative."
"No matter how much she's willing to forgive me, I can't forgive myself."
"I loved her. I really did admire her."
After all, she managed to love someone like me, and yet I…
"How about you, Haruki? Can you bring yourself to meet her?"
I want Kazusa to find salvation. But I myself don't deserve it.
Really, we haven't grown at all even after three years, huh? Not me, and not Kazusa.
"I seem to remember telling you I wanted to remain inside."
"We're just going for a walk. You can tolerate that much, right?"
In the end, it took yet another 30 minutes to drag the grumbling Kazusa outside…
By the time we finished lunch and left the hotel, the faint winter sun had already made its way west.
"Just where do you think we are? This is a city of over ten million people in the heart of world-famous Tokyo!
"B-But… you know… last time I came back to Japan, plenty of people recognized me."
"Don't worry, the Touma Kazusa craze is long since over. Don't underestimate how short attention spans Japanese people have."
"Hold on, is that really something my manager should be happy about?"
"Besides, I have a plan. Anyway, accompany me for a while."
Fully awake and with a full stomach, yet still unwilling to move by herself, Kazusa decides to grab hold of my sleeve and lets herself get dragged along.
But even then, I half-forcibly drag Kazusa with me outside, into Japan.
"Look, we're here. This'll be our first tourist spot."
"Huh? But this is… just outside our hotel."
"Hey, Kazusa… Do you remember this scenery?"
"Scenery? …This is just the street in front of Onjuku Station…"
"You ran away from a journalist, and at the same time lost your wallet and your cell phone, along with everything else in your bag."
"The truth is… this number is the only one I remember. What's wrong with me?"
"From this very booth, you called me with a 100 yen coin you found…"
"Wah, wah, wah! I'm going home! I'm going home after all!"
"And with a pitiful voice, like that of an abandoned dog…"
"Of course it was. A natural reaction to hearing your pitiful voice."
"When I came for you in a panic, I found you trembling and dripping wet. I thought to myself, wow, she really does look like an abandoned dog."
"Oh that's rich, coming from the owner who abandoned me!"
"I could say the same, you bastard…! Don't try to rile me up, you bastard!"
"I'm only doing it because a certain idiot keeps falling for the same old cliched provocations."
"Only because you're the one saying them, you bastard…"
That's right, I will half-forcibly drag Kazusa with me outside, into Japan.
Because no longer will we sink into an endless cycle of self-indulgence, like we used to back then.
No matter how many punches we have to take, and no matter how hard it is, we'll live in harmony with the outside world.
I've decided to move forward with my life, even if it means I have to get hurt, whether because of myself or because of others.
"I see, this is your 'plan'… Your tastes and methods haven't changed a bit."
"I went for a similar look on purpose."
Fake glasses and a comb as a hair ornament. Then add to that a scarf and a hat.
And not least of all, a fake name.
That's what I gave to Kazusa three years ago, but it's not the only thing I gave her in this place.
The shopping mall within walking distance from the hotel.
The assortments and layouts have changed a little, but all the stores we visited together back then are still here.
"Still, thinking back now, I don't look good in glasses at all."
"Huh, you think so? I think it fits you perfectly, including your hair."
"That's what people call husband's bias. I'm sorry, but I can't take your praise seriously."
Although thoroughly deriding my opinion, Kazusa looks like she's actually happy about my questionable sense of beauty.
She looks pretty uplifted as she walks ahead of me in the shopping mall, wearing every single accessory I bought for her.
"Hey, Haruki, how about we go eat something sweet? I think they have a Rascal's in the underground mall here."
"We're back in Japan, so how about we take the occasion to grab some zenzai soup or something instead?"
"Alright, that'll be our second destination. Come on, let's hurry."
"No, wait, we don't need to eat everything in succession. There's no shortage of pudding back home in Europe."
"…You're seriously underestimating Rascal's smooth puddings. That exquisite texture is a rarity even in Europe, just so you know."
"Setting aside whether that's actually true or not… It's cold, right? We should go eat something warm."
"That's why I was kind enough to suggest that we make that our second destination! How selfish can you be?"
"I'll toss those exact words right back at you. How about you just buy the puddings and take them home as a souvenir?"
"Not happening. I want to eat them now. I'll never compromise on this. I'll eat three of them in the store, and bring twelve home with me."
"…You won't be able to eat dinner like that."
"I have another stomach for dessert! What are you even on about?"
"…Fine, I've had enough. Do whatever you want."
"Oh right, if we eat ice cream after warming ourselves up with zenzai, then…"
"Why do you insist on making me freeze!?"
She looks pretty uplifted indeed… In fact, she's getting way ahead of herself.
"Hnng… I'm finally in my element. Come on, Haruki!"
When we exited the shopping mall into the streets of Onjuku, the dynamic between the two of us was already completely reversed.
"Oh, how pathetic can you be? Did you get an upset tummy from eating that tiny amount?"
"I only feel sick because of a certain ingredient…"
In fact, I'm terrified of what results I'd get if I did a glucose urine test right now.
The same can't be said for Kazusa however. She seems completely fine despite having stuffed herself with twice the amount of sugar that I have.
"H-Hey… how about we go back to the hotel? Let's watch some lame end-of-year special variety shows together."
"Why would you watch something you already know is lame?"
But my plea falls on deaf ears. Without a care in the world about the man pressing his hands against his belly, Kazusa goes onwards on the concrete stairs.
"Just a little further. Do your best, Haruki."
"Just a little further for what… Ah."
And once at the top of the stairs, I look up to find…
"Just as massive, pretentious, and completely lacking in any trace of culture as ever."
"I see… Come to think of it, it was in this part of town."
"Hm? Do you know this place, Haruki? I seem to remember you not showing up even once."
Yes, this is where Touma Kazusa held her first concert in Japan.
And this is where she held her additional concert a month later.
"I played here twice, yet you didn't come to listen even once."
"Well, that's because… I'm sorry, it was all my fault."
Tickets for both concerts sold out immediately, and the additional concert is still regarded as a legendary performance.
But despite the weight these performances held, I never set foot in the concert hall in the end.
"Because… it's thanks to the fact that you didn't show up, that we are together right now."
There is no point in theorizing about what could've been in a potential future that never happened.
Because now, I'm together with Kazusa.
And I've managed to return to the country I once abandoned.
At this point, there is nothing else I could ask for, and I wouldn't settle for anything different either.
"By the way, mom once held a concert here too."
I even got tickets for it, but I didn't go that time either…
"Though it didn't make the rounds nearly as much as my concert."
"You can reach a conclusion about that evaluation with your mother next time, without anyone else around."
We've spent the whole day just walking around.
Not once getting on a bus or a train, only walking around the streets of Onjuku with nothing but our memories to guide us.
Just a road away from the way back to the hotel. In front of the station. Near the taxi stand.
Our feet stopped naturally, and our chatter died out.
Wry smiles surface on our faces.
Our expressions are so pained, twisted, and distant that if someone looked at us they couldn't confidently say that we're smiling.
"We acted like idiots back then… didn't we?"
"Correction: we actually were idiots. We were half-witted beyond belief."
It was never my intention to come here.
This was the one place that I wanted to avoid. This place filled with so much nostalgia and pain.
"Why are you laughing all of a sudden?"
"Because, because… even when I recall it now… Haha, hahaha…"
"You said those exact same words back then too, with a tearful voice no less… Hahaha…!"
"And weren't you laughing and crying at the same time?"
Yes, this is the place where both of us shed so many tears.
This is where we've shared so many of our first experiences.
This was where we had a serious quarrel for the first time.
This was where I struck her with my true feelings for the first time.
This was where Kazusa admitted her own true feelings for the first time.
We were both looking toward the road together, but when I turned my head… I found her gaze already firmly set on me.
No, she wasn't simply gazing at me…
"You're more used to it now than back then, right? …Because of me."
"Why are you so used to it!?"
This is where our lips touched for the first time…
Actually, that was the second time, though I'd only figured that out much later after the fact.
Those times were filled with nothing but mistakes…
But even so, that was where our relationship started. It was from then on that we were able to share our feelings with one another.
"So… let's do it one more time here."
"They were looking back then too. But you still did it."
"Don't beg for things like a child. Act your age, would you?"
"What's that supposed to mean, I'm actually still… Mmmh!? Mhn… aah…"
With the passers-by and cars still firmly within the corners of our vision…
We share a kiss passionate enough to make every one of them turn their faces away.
Right hereーat the very place where we became accomplices for the first time.
"Why do Japanese trains have to be so crowded all the time?"
"You haven't been on enough overseas trains to compare in the first place. You almost never leave the house, and whenever you do, you take a taxi."
"I make sure to bring the receipts every time, don't I? You have no right to complain as my manager."
"Company funds are not a bottomless resource… You and your family should do something about your wastefulness."
"It's okay, that's what you and Miyo-chan are for. Touma Youko Office will be in safe hands as long as you two are around."
As the conversation strays further and further away from its initial purpose, the two of us look out the train windows at the nostalgic scenery outside.
It's the 30th of December. A few days after our return to Japan, and only two days before the year ends.
As always, we spend our time together without any idea of what the future holds in store for us, even on this sudden vacation.
"Iwazu-chou, Iwazu-chou. Please mind the door when exiting."
"I know. I get it, so can you please not pull my necktie? That's seriously dangerous."
"You must remember it yourself if you know what I was referring to."
"Of course I am. I used this station all the time as a kid."
Just like the announcer said, we've arrived at Iwazu-chou.
The district Kazusa lived in until she graduated.
"Oh right, what should we get as a gift? We can't just go there empty-handed."
"I admire that you've become considerate enough to think about that, but you should've said that when we were in Onjuku.
"Haruki, you're underestimating convenience store candy. Unlike before, they sell plenty of souvenir-worthy goods now."
"You just want to buy it for yourself. Just admit it!"
I knew it from the beginning, but…
Seeing it with my own eyes leaves me speechless.
Because this house was once on the verge of turning into an abandoned ruin.
The nameplate was gone. There was a "for sale" sign at the front. The garden was overgrown.
"It really does… look like it used to."
But now, this place calls forth memories dating even further in the past.
Memories of the day I was astounded by the sheer size of the place.
Memories of the day I stepped inside, awestruck by how magnificent it was.
And lastly, memories of the day I felt feelings of admiration, respect, and sympathy for the single inhabitant of this place.
While still overwhelmed by all sorts of memories, we press the doorbell of what used to be her home.
…Even the sound of the doorbell is the same.
"Glad you made it, you two. It's been a while."
"We ate lunch together yesterday and the day before that."
"Come now, Kazusa, that was just business, a mere rite of passage, a teeny little appointment."
And the person who came to greet us is the current owner of this house.
Not that it wasn't always her home to begin with.
"You've really decided to move back here."
"I guess so. I never managed to sell it no matter how many years I waited."
It was only half a year ago that Youko-san decided to live in this house again.
It was undergoing renovations until just last month, and today is the big day she can finally show it to us.
Normally, Kudou-san and I would have been strongly opposed to a plan like this, writing it off as a "waste of money."
"I made sure not to change anything. That only made the whole thing more expensive though."
The interior design is completely identical.
I only spent a few days in this house.
But even then, this scenery is so deeply ingrained in my memories that I instantly feel a wave of nostalgia.
"In truth, Miyo-chan lives with me here too, but since today is supposed to be 'family only,' she just got up and left to her parents' house on her own."
"She didn't have to be that considerate."
"Exactly. The only thing that awaits her at her parents' house is endless nagging about when she's getting married."
"How about you show some consideration too, in both your actions and your words."
Well, back then there certainly was no mother-daughter comedy duo around.
"…Not good, it's not sweet at all."
"How strange, I'm sure I put tons of sugar in it."
"How about we try adding in some maple syrup?"
"Oh dear, now it looks like liquid candy. Well, I suppose this is tasty in its own way…"
"No, when boiling black soybeans, you need to lower the temperature a bit… The peel will come off if you heat it up too much…"
"I swear, all men are like this… They never do any cooking themselves, yet they're exemplary at complaining."
"I have more cooking experience than you two at least! So please let me help!"
This sparkly, newly renovated kitchen is being violated before my eyes.
A grossly sweet smell engulfs the whole room, and a white, almost sticky vapor spreads in the air.
Ingredients and spices lie scattered randomly on the table, and it's beyond anyone's ability to ever sort them back into their cabinets.
"Don't get in the way. New Year's osechi is something meant to be passed down from mother to daughter."
"But what is a mother meant to pass down when she hasn't inherited anything herself…?"
"To begin with, you were the one who said you wanted osechi for New Year's. You really are full of contradictions."
"I said I wanted osechi, yes, but I never said I wanted you two to make it…"
This was the inevitable result, after all.
I'm certain they'll both be sick of this when cleaning up is all that's left.
"You can just go take a nap for now. I'll wake you up when it's time for dinner."
This amount of suspense can't be good for my mental health, so I should take my leave for now. I can do all my lamenting later.
"Oh? The sweetened chestnuts for the kuri kinton are gone… Hey, Kazusa!"
"I didn't eat them all, just so you know! I made sure to leave two."
"Same here. I made sure to only eat five."
I was sure they'd at least finish preparing a meal sooner or later, but perhaps I was being too optimistic.
Going down the stairs to the basement, I open a door many times thicker than a normal one…
Beyond that door is a scenery that's completely unchanged from before.
In one of the corners of this soundproofed and all too spacious studio stands a piano belonging to Kazusa's favorite brand.
From guitars to drums to saxophones… All kinds of instruments lie piled on the floor in a heap.
Even the control room beyond the big soundproof glass looks like it's equipped with new hardware.
…Even though there's no guarantee anyone will ever use it.
This obsession of restoring this house down to the smallest details brings out a slightly bewildered smile on my lips.
Years ago, when I was still a high school student.
There was no one in this room but a lone, embittered girl all by herself.
And although that girl seemed completely unconcerned about others, she made an exception for a guy who couldn't properly play an instrument.
She brought the good-for-nothing guy who wouldn't take music seriously to this room, where she played for him, made him play, and verbally abused him…
And she stuck with him until he was ready for an actual performance.
That's why that good-for-nothing guyーwhy Iーended up relying on that strict girl, why I wanted to be spoiled by her, and why I refused to leave her side.
I came to this room countless times, played in it countless times, dozed off in it countless times, and greeted the morning in it countless times.
And then after five long years, my dream came true.
My nearly impossible dream of being on good terms with this bitter girl.
The second I heard her voice, I clumsily put the guitar back on its stand.
"Wow… I'm amazed she went as far as to restore this place."
But Kazusa pretends to not have seen that unnatural movement.
It's just a guess… but it's probably because Kazusa understands the reason why I can never play the guitar in front of her.
"Wow, she's even tuned this thing. That woman is nothing if not meticulous."
But Kazusa doesn't breathe a word about that, instead opting to stroke the keys of the piano with a hint of nostalgia.
"Well, it's all nostalgic to some degree, but this is the one place in Japan where I spent the most time."
The piano that once stood in this room now rests in Vienna, always by Kazusa's side.
Even so, Kazusa greets this new piano with the same expression she would show the original.
"Ah, by the way, Haruki, it's time for dinner soon. I only came down here to let you know that the pizza just arrived."
"…Weren't you two preparing something just earlier?"
"You poor ignorant soul. Osechi is for New Year's Day. What would be the point in eating it before New Year's?"
"You can do that tomorrow… I'll try making it properly this time."
"Alright, I'll be sleeping in the guest room."
Three people sitting around the dinner table of the Touma household, cheerfully passing the time by watching a lame variety TV show,
Just like that, these three were able to waste their time in happiness and quiet, in a way that seemed impossible just a few months prior.
But despite that, or perhaps because of that, this precious time passed by in a flash, and the needle of the table clock began to inch closer to midnight.
Inching closer to the final day of the year.
"What do you mean? You could just stay here. If you get sleepy we can all just huddle together."
"No, you two should have some time for yourselves, as mother and daughter."
"Huuh? You don't want to stay? You can prey on either of us, I wouldn't mind."
"Wow, she's actually taking it seriously. My daughter is so lame."
Even with New Year's right around the corner, the Touma comedic duo knows no bounds.
After enjoying my fill of alcohol and a good meal, I leave the living room with a sense of relief, exasperation, and the slightest hint of jealousy.
It's almost time. Time for the last day of the year. And most importantly, it's time for…
"Seriously, you two get along so well it's almost annoying… You really know how to ensnare the right kind of man."
"That's not true at all. He's stingy, loud, annoying, and all around terrible."
"It's just that… he's the only man for me."
"…Unlike what you just did, I don't think I've ever laid all my cards bare for my man to see."
"Well, you know, love is… Goodness, maybe I really have raised you improperly."
"You should make this your last one, Mom."
"Then how about we go to sleep? In the same bed."
"…You didn't even let me do that when I was a kid. Why are you trying to act like a good parent all of a sudden?"
"You've got it all wrong. This is simply me manipulatively trying to act nice so that the child I abandoned will take care of me when I grow old."
"That's right, I'm manipulative. That's why I prepared this house for you two to return to."
"So that really was… the reason you returned to this house."
"You can return whenever you want. I'm serious."
"Besides, this is a chance for you two, don't you think?"
"You know, even if my illness were to heal, it's still obvious that I'll die before you do… Then you'll inherit this house without having to pay for it."
"The only thing I can imagine is the crippling inheritance tax."
"And to solve that issue, you have a beloved husband who will earn back that money by raising sheep or something."
"Hey, just to make sure, you're not referring to anyone in specific when you say 'sheep,' right?"
"Why not? This is where you were born."
"You know already, don't you? There is a reason why the two of us were never supposed to come here in the first place…"
"There is no such reason for either of you anymore. You've both been forgiven for a long time."
"In the beginning, they wouldn't even see me. It was only after the fifth attempt that they let me into their house."
"I don't remember how many times I met them after that, but eventually their daughter helped me to convince them as well."
"That's what I should be asking you, really."
"Why would you do something like that, Mom…?"
"Well, obviously, a mother has to apologize for her daughter's mistakes."
"You shouldn't be the one to do that, Mom. I'm an adult now, aren't I?"
"No matter how old you get, you'll always remain my child. Not to mention that in your case, mental age needs to be considered as well."
"I have to say though, it was the first time in a long time, or perhaps the first time ever, that I truly felt like a parent."
"Anyway, that's how it is… In other words, there's no reason to deny my request any longer."
"That's why, Kazusa… please come back here whenever you want, okay…?"
"Even if you're only coming back to play a concert here, celebrate Obon or New Year's, or simply coming to visit some old friends. That's enough for me."
"And, and… if you ever feel the slightest bit homesick, don't hesitate to come back."
"What is it? Are you sleepy already? Then let's go to sleep together."
"B-Because! 'The' Kazusa just went on her knees, bowed… and said 'Thank you for raising me!'"
"You're the one who did something unlike you first!"
"Shut up, shut up! I'll never forget what you did for me, just so you know!"
"Me… Me neither…! I'll never forget the look of you just earlier for the rest of my life. Ahahahahaha… Aaah, ahahaha…!"
"The sun really does set early this time of year, huh…"
"…You're saying that now? The shortest day of the year in Tokyo was almost a month ago."
"Oh, we've got an expert here. In other words, the days are only getting longer and longer from now on… It's still dark though."
"Huh, I wasn't trying to belittle you or anything. Although, of course, I do think that waking up after 3 PM is unbecoming of a responsible adult."
Despite being the last commemorative day of the year, we had already lost eight precious hours of it.
Kazusa, who had proudly proclaimed that she would come over in the morning, only woke up once the sun was already well on its way west.
"You sure like getting your own way, don't you?"
When I woke up around the usual time, I saw Kazusa and Youko-san peacefully asleep in the living room, firmly in each other's embrace.
Unable to bring myself to break apart such an endearing spectacle,
…I didn't think I'd be forced to order lunch outside as well, though.
"A lot has happened. Take a hint already."
"I told you, I'm not trying to belittle you or anything."
"That's not what your attitude's implying at all."
"That's just… something I was born with."
That's right. I'm not trying to belittle her at all. I'm simply a bit jealous, that's all.
"Hey, Kazusa… never let go of what you have with your mother right now."
I want Youko-san to keep holding on to her life. I want Kazusa to keep loving her mother.
And lastly… um… if they could share with me even the slightest bit of the familial love they have for each other, I'd be really happy.
That's my wish as the newest member of their family.
"Anyway, where are we headed? Aren't we supposed to eat soba, watch the New Year's concert, listen to the temple bells, and then visit the shrine?"
"That's an alluring idea, but there's something I want to show you first."
"But the place you're heading to is…"
There is a place I simply have to visit before the day ends.
"Yeah… The place we spent three years in."
"I only spent two and a half years here, though."
"Aah, I just remembered a certain annoying class rep and now I'm pissed off. Let me kick him."
This holy ground that the both of us were thinking of ever since we came back to Japan, but could never bring ourselves to visit until now.
"But still, it feels different now that no one's here."
"Well, it's New Year's Eve, after all."
The school gates, that lead to both the high school and the nearby university campus, are not closed even on New Year's Eve.
However, the school building is still devoid of life, and paired with the warm colors of the evening sun, the building stands with an air of loneliness.
"What are you saying? This is our precious alma mater, you know?"
Kazusa raises her voice in confusion, perhaps not understanding why I'm headed in the direction I am.
"Let's visit, just for a little bit."
"It's fine, I promise. No one's here. How can you call yourself a delinquent if you're gonna get cold feet over this?"
"Wha…! And how can you call yourself a class rep when you're just doing as you please!"
In the end though, either her pride as a delinquent, or her desire to spite the class rep triumphed over her wariness.
"Uwa, you had to pick 3-E out of all places…"
The entrance leading to the shoe lockers wasn't locked either, so we were able to make it to the school hallways without any obstacle.
…I do think we're being a bit careless, but today is special.
"Still, this place hasn't changed at all either."
Just as Kazusa said earlier, the room plate read 3-E.
"This was my seat, and that one was yours…"
"Yeah, you're right… I can vaguely remember the outside view from here."
And if my memory serves right, this classroom is undoubtedly the same 3-E that we were assigned to.
"Let's see, perhaps some of your old scribbles still remain here. You know, things like music notes, or insults aimed at your teachers…"
"There might be one that says 'Kitahara is a dumbass.'"
Under the evening sun, in a classroom empty save the two of us, we bring back long forgotten memories to the light.
"Yeah, more times than I can remember. Back then I found you so unbelievably annoying that you definitely were in my top five most hated people."
"Me though… I loved you back then."
"I know that. You're a superficial bastard who falls in love based on how a girl looks, after all."
"That's why back then, I loved looking at you sleeping by the window."
"You sure enjoyed waking me up, though."
"Well obviously. By waking you up I was able to see your face… Could there be a better reward?"
"…Aah, annoying, gross! I can't stand listening to you. You've really turned into an embarrassment, haven't you?"
Although her words are relentless, Kazusa slowly inches toward me until her cheeks touch my chest.
"That's because I live with someone who keeps making me want to say embarrassing things."
Normally our conversations end with one of us busting out laughing, making us lose track of whatever we were talking about.
But this time, the quiet, scarlet, cold, dim, and melancholy evening sun preserves our embarrassing memories without letting go.
For some reason, Houjou High School has three music rooms.
Music Room 1 is the one that students in the regular program use.
In the school building on the opposite side is Music Room 3, which is reserved for students in the music program.
And lastly there is this place, Music Room 2. A classroom reserved for the best of the music program students, who use it for personal practice.
…At least on paper. Up until a few years back, it was reserved solely for a single delinquent girl.
And this is also our last destination for today…
No… Our last destination in Japan.
The moment I open the window, a somewhat powerful gust of wind enters and cools down the whole classroom.
"Yeah, it's cold. Even colder than during the school festival."
I stick my head out the window and look at the classroom to my right.
It goes without saying that the window to that classroom is tightly shut. No guitar sound can possibly be heard from it.
"Look, you're going to catch a cold. Just close the stupid thing already."
I think I'm acting strangely too.
I've come this far already, but taking the next step is turning into a real struggle.
"S-So, umm… to put it into words…"
"I'd like to… listen to you playing the piano."
But that's to be expected, I guess.
Everything needs to be done in a certain order for it to work.
As always, she grumbles about how I'm always listening to her play the piano anyway, and that her fingers are too cold to move properly…
And of course, also as always, she relents by saying "This is the last time, okay?" before quietly beginning her performance.
The solitary performance she held every day for three years, using this piano.
The piano that stood by Kazusa for those three years, and which also worsened the friction between her and her classmates.
"When did you realize the guitarist was me?"
"It's too far in the past. I can't remember."
The piano that guided my clumsy guitar to greatness. The piano that guided our amateur band to greatness.
And… the piano that after our performance, kept on playing even as Kazusa and I ever so slightly touched, but also went our separate ways.
"Did you match my melody because you knew it was me? Would you have poked your nose in if it was anyone else?"
"I just said I can't remember. It doesn't matter anyway. When it happened doesn't make a difference."
Kazusa still feels regret over the betrayal three years ago.
But there is not a hint of regret over our separation eight years ago anymore.
She has accepted everything, happy and sorrowful, that has brought her to where she is now. All she can do now is smile in recollection.
"What is it this time? I'm going out of my way to play for you, and you keep interrupting…"
I'll never let go of that smile.
On top of the piano… a tiny little box laid before Kazusa's eyes.
And inside it was a gentle, silver glint.
It is the very thing that is still missing from Kazusa's left ring finger.
"I'm sorry… I might have betrayed you just a tiny bit… I conspired with Youko-san."
"This is the ceremonial hall. This is the day."
"That's right. That is the plan for the Kitahara and Touma family banquet."
"At a school, during New Year's… I'm amazed you got permission."
"Well, I have a pretty give-and-take type relationship with Houjou University. Lots of backroom dealings, you see."
"Why, because it's a place that's special to that girl… for better and for worse."
"I didn't mean that… Why on New Year's Eve?"
"That's… well… my own form of revenge, I guess you could say."
"I wanted to retry my old strategy one more time… Just kidding, I'm just being a bit stubborn."
Though up until the very end, Youko-san never really told me what exactly she was referring to when she said she was being stubborn.
Even so, this ceremony, chosen to be held at this place and at this hour, is a product of the exquisite mix of Youko-san's love, tenacity and mischievousness.
"Did you think I'd get overwhelmed by emotions at the sight? Did you expect me to cry?"
"Like hell I'd cry, you idiot! I've always said I didn't need a ceremony!"
The words she spoke when we were snuggling in bed had a slightly different nuance in my memories though.
"And yet you set up this bizarre, forced tearjerker of a surprise… What, did you want to take pictures of me crying just so you can laugh at them later?"
"In that case, I refuse to cry even if it kills me! I'll recite my vows in the most boring, monotonous way possible!"
If anything, what's amusing is the fact she actually does plan on reciting her vows despite how angry she is.
"Youko-san and I simply did this for our own self-satisfaction. You can just begrudgingly go along with it."
In any case, I've gotten Kazusa's consent.
That's why I take out my phone and press the send button.
"Why, the family of the bride, of course. As well as her friends."
After all, they're supposed to have been waiting outside for a while.
…And while carrying the bride's ensemble, at that.
"Um, excuse me? Is she still not done?"
"Ah, I'm sorry, Kitahara-san. She actually finished changing a while ago, but…"
Kudou-san, who is in the neighboring Music Room 1, sounded somewhat troubled.
It's been well over an hour since she dragged Kazusa away to change her clothes.
"Um, Kazusa-san has been… grumbling in the hallway for a while…"
"Get a hold of yourself already, would you? I know you're dying to let him see it."
"T-That's not true! I can't think of anything worse!"
"I'll say it again, why do you have to get so insanely flustered? How old do you think you are? I feel embarrassed to be your mother."
"Oh god, I've had enough! Just go already!"
Well, I did have an idea of what she'd look like…
I knew that seeing Kazusa dressed like this would blow my socks off.
I knew I'd be at a loss for words.
"…When you heard we were holding a wedding, you knew this would happen, didn't you?"
But, how should I put it… I guess even when I'm in a state of complete astoundment, my mouth still moves.
Or rather, since she's even more panicked than I am, I feel an obligation to drive the conversation forward.
To be honest, I want to shout "Holy crap!" at the top of my lungs right now, before embracing Kazusa with all my might.
But Kazusa just looks as though she's really not ready for this.
We've been living together for three years already, and on paper, we're already married.
Yet somehow, the idea of becoming a bride in a wedding ceremony didn't even cross her mind once.
"I only wanted to become your wife. It's not like I ever wanted to be a bride…"
"I don't see the problem. Why not be a bride?"
Is there still guilt lingering deep down within her?
Up until now, Kazusa never once tried to dress up unless it was for a concert.
Although perhaps that was partially just her personality.
"You're really beautiful… It looks so good on you it's almost ridiculous."
"Are you sure you should be crying? Youko-san would gladly record and spread the tape all around."
"Our bizarre surprise seems to be a huge success…"
From now on, we will never again anguish over what we should have done, and what could have been.
We will never again disavow what we have right now.
That's why we will affirm what we have.
From this place filled with the greatest joys but also the greatest pains, we start again.
With that said, our belated wedding ceremony now commences.
"Hey, Kazusa… I swear to always be by your side."
"I've made that oath a million times already."
"Well, I guess a million times isn't that many… I do."
"Hey! Wait a second! You promised you'd say that with me as a witness!"
After taking a hot morning shower, my body finally adjusts itself to the cold winter air.
It's a bit cold, but the weather outside is nice.
From the buzzing of the washing machine to the rays of sunlight streaming through the window, everything around me signals the coming of a new day.
Or perhaps "begun" is the wrong word here, because I have yet to do anything other than relax so far, but that's what Sundays are for, right?
And now, my customary Sunday battle begins.
"It's half past ten. It's daytime already."
"You're right. It's only half past ten. It's still morning."
…That's right, a brutal battle to pinpoint where exactly morning ends and daytime begins.
"Most places will stop serving breakfast specials in 30 minutes. It's totally daytime."
"In other words, there's still 30 minutes of morning left."
"If I could actually trust you to wake up within 30 minutes, that line might've worked…"
"This is the first Sunday in ages that doesn't involve any events, shopping or strolls. I'm begging you, let me sleep a while longer…!"
My delicate princess is terrible at waking up, which incidentally makes her great at not waking up.
When she's like this, I feel like a lone traveler marching against the north wind. Ordinary means simply will not work.
Which is why I have no choice…
"Thank you, Haruki-kun. That's why I love y…"
"Right, I'll be in the kitchen making lunch. You can stay asleep as long as you want."
Of course, the only thing capable of stopping the north wind is the sun.
"No! You can't cook, Haruki-kun… That would depreciate my role as your wife."
"We're both working adults, so what's the problem? Either way, you're clearly too tired from work right now."
"You're the last person I wanna hear that from. You always leave for work before me and come home after me…"
"I normally leave everything to you, Setsuna. Let me return the favor on Sundays at least."
"But Haruki-kun, you already do the laundry and clean the house whenever I look away.
"Then wake up. I'm starving over here! If you neglect me, I swear I'll cook something myself, you hear?"
"Ohh, you're a demon! Satan himself! The CEO of the underworld!"
"My princess, may I suggest you refrain from besmirching the name of Miss Houjou High by the means of sloth?"
And so, even as she wastes the whole day away in bed, my wife makes sure to protect her role as a working housewife.
The girl formerly known as Ogiso Setsuna. Kitahara Setsuna.
Former title holder for Miss Houjou High for three consecutive years, and now the public relations idol for Knights Records.
"Come on, keep your promise and wake up."
Setsuna stretches her arms toward me from the bed like a spoiled child…
Or more accurately, like a princess; a side she would never show to anyone else.
Before I know it, her hand drags my entire body down toward her in bed.
"Now that you're down here, why don't you take a nap as well? No one will fault you for relaxing today."
"You say that, but you don't have the slightest intention of actually sleeping, do you?"
Her demeanor doesn't hint at a desire for peaceful sleep at all. There's something more aggressive and carnal in her eyes.
To be more precise, it has something to do with how her lips are going down my neck.
"You'll just feel more hungry if you do that."
"Looks like I have a delicious lunch ahead of me then. Mh, chu…"
"…! No, it's morning. This isn't the time."
"But your thing down here… is saying it's the perfect time."
To be more precise, the way her fingers go down my…
"My thing doesn't speak… Aah…! S-Setsuna… but…"
"Ah, ah… For the love of… Hey…!"
I've already stated this, but it's currently 10:30 AM.
It wouldn't be at all strange or rude for someone to come visit at this time of day…
"…Ah, come to think of it, your mom said she was coming to visit this morning."
"No, she didn't! She said she'd come at noon! Why does she always have to be so impatient?"
…And so, our argument regarding when exactly morning ends is revived, as we both hurriedly jump out of bed.
A little over a year after Ogiso Setsuna ever so slightly changed her last name.
This is the story of that winter we spent together, in this apartment.
"No, it's okay… More importantly, I'm sorry Haruki-san. My daughter is such a sleepyhead."
"Oh no, she's normally very diligent. Today's her day off, that's all…"
"That's right! Don't jump in and say things better left unsaid, Mom!"
"You too, Setsuna. Don't jump into the conversation when you don't have to…"
"That's right, at least get dressed and dry your hair first. You're so bad-mannered."
"Oh, please forgive me. You see, my parents didn't teach me how to behave."
"I'm really sorry. Her father always pampered her so she never grew out of it."
"Oh, it's nothing… I should thank you for raising her to be selfish."
"Huh? Could it be you're one of those people who enjoy being toyed with, Haruki-san?"
"No, I didn't mean it that way… Well, I suppose I wouldn't mind that either anymore."
Setsuna's mom stares at me, more out of discomfort than confusion.
But I merely respond with a vague smile, with thoughts in my mind that would probably make her even more uncomfortable.
Thank you for raising Setsuna to be so selfish, kind, normal, and strong.
For they are the ones who raised her to be so resilient… even after the many times I've hurt her in the past.
For they are the ones who helped her return to the way she was, when she broke down.
It was all thanks to her father, her mother, and her younger brother.
"Still though, to think you're moving when things are already as busy as they are."
"What do you mean, Mom? Isn't it more efficient to take care of the cleanup and moving at the same time?"
"Besides, it'll also be more efficient for our new neighbors.
"Why not stay here a bit longer, though? It should be enough for the two of you."
"I seem to remember Father getting angry at me for 'forcing his daughter to live in such a cramped space' though…"
Just as Setsuna's mother says, Setsuna and I will move out the weekend before New Year's, and move into a two-room apartment five stations away.
Anyway, that's how things stand. Setsuna's mother came over today to help us prepare for the move.
"Ah, Mom! Don't put away all the utensils. What are we supposed to eat with tomorrow?"
"Make do with paper cups and paper trays. It's better than causing a commotion on the last day because you haven't packed everything."
"There's still a whole week until then! Start with the things we won't need first. Aah, not the TV! I still wanna watch it!"
"Oh shut up already. Go ahead and take care of everything yourself then, Setsuna."
"I'll take care of everything myself, so you don't need to come over."
Those words had left my mouth the day before as if it was the most natural thing in the world… but to the Ogiso household, they were akin to heresy.
They'd retort with things like "you can't stay so formal forever" and "you're treating us like strangers" and "you said that before the wedding too."
On top of that, I think they said some rather absurd things as well, but let's not get into that…
They're not bad people, of course; I really care about them. But I can't help but laugh at how our worldviews remain so different even after all this time.
"What is it, Mom? I'm busy cleaning everything up by myself."
"Forget about that, look! This is your photo album from middle school."
"Oh, there it is! I knew I brought it over, but I couldn't find it all this time."
"You even brought your album to this tiny little apartment? No wonder it feels so cramped in here."
"…Really sorry about living in a tiny little apartment."
If I remember correctly, it was her daughter ーnot meーwho adamantly stated we should stay here until
"Oh goodness, this brings me back. Look, this is Setsuna during middle school. Look, look, Haruki-san."
"I've already seen it a thousand times."
I already know all about who her friends were, who she fell out with, and who she managed to reconcile with.
…In fact, I also uh… well… know about the soccer ace who confessed his love to her, down to his facial features.
Seriously, she didn't have to tell me about that part in such detail.
"She was so cute and obedient back then. When did she become such a stubborn girl who never listens to her parents?"
"Ah, Nagasaki! We went there on a school trip!"
"Yes, I remember very well. You had a 38 degree fever the day before the trip, right, Setsuna?"
"Exactly! Dad got mad and told me not to go on the trip."
"But you started bawling, demanding to go… Actually, come to think of it, it was around that time you started ignoring your parents' wishes."
"That's not true. My fever went down to 36 degrees the day after."
"I know you cheated with the thermometer. You didn't have it tightly under your armpit like you were supposed to, did you?"
"Come on, look at this picture. Your face is completely swollen red. It's perfect proof you were in terrible condition."
"Uwaa, I look so weird. Oh, this is so embarrassing. No, Haruki-kun, you can't look!"
"…I'm not gonna look. How about we hurry up and get this place cleaned up already?"
"Thank you so much for today, you were a huge help."
"Yes, but it was naive to think we'd manage it all in a single day. I'll come back next time."
"We'll both be at work until moving day. There won't be anyone home to open the door for you."
"Oh, is that so? But we're not even halfway done…"
"That's because we barely did anything. Seriously, why did you even come?"
"You're one to talk, when you barely did anything yourself, Setsuna."
Today went about as well as these two get along. It's almost impressive how little work got done.
It started with the album, then they went crazy about some old novels and manga, and lastly they moved on to childhood clothes Setsuna couldn't fit in anymore.
Item after item kept their hands from moving, but in return their mouths just kept going on and on.
Worst of all, they were not content with simply talking among themselves… They insisted on dragging me into their numerous "time-outs."
Even so, I didn't dare speak the truth: "Maybe it'd be faster if I did it alone."
"Still, are you sure you want to go home? Why not eat with us? Right, Haruki-kun?"
"Of course. By all means, please stay for dinner."
"Trust me, I'd love to, but I can't today."
"If you're worried about Dad and Takahiro, you can just tell them to eat out today, right? Come on, stay here a bit longer."
I can't however say "by all means" when it comes to the cruel and unusual treatment of the men in her family…
"That's not it, I have other things to take care of. I'm going to see a play tonight with Kitahara-san."
"Oh, you should've told me sooner. I would've made you a lunch box."
"I don't need that either. We have a reservation at a French restaurant after the play… Of course, I'll keep that a secret from your father and Takahiro."
The "Kitahara-san" she's talking about is of course not referring to Setsuna or me.
There is only one other person whom she'd call by the name of Kitahara.
"Anyway, that's how it is. I'll leave now."
"…No, it's nothing. Thank you very much."
"Let's see each other again in your new place. See you."
Perhaps she couldn't tell from the look on my face, or perhaps she simply let it pass out of consideration…
Regardless, my mother-in-law took her leave as if absolutely nothing was out of the ordinary.
Before I had known it, my own mother had also become entangled with the Ogiso household.
All the things I couldn't do, and all the things I couldn't bring myself to do, these people do with the lift of a finger.
She says that, but those mischievous eyes are practically laughing at me.
They're not bad people, of course; I really care about them. But I can't help but laugh at how our worldviews remain so different.
The strife and bonds I have been running away from all these years, they simply waltz into.
And they've actually managed to make it turn out all right.
They've handed me a resolution I couldn't even dream of attaining.
"Let's go back inside. It's starting to get cold."
All this is truly beyond my wildest dreams.
I never could have imagined spending a Sunday evening with my family.
Aimlessly watching TV without taking in any of the contents, all while the food and beer just keep coming our way.
Going from one pointless topic to the other, but then the other party would get mad when I'm not listening properly, so I'd spend hours trying to calm them.
Moments so lively, pointless, and completely unknown to me…
The thought of actually living these moments I could only dream about before.
This is the story of my dreamlike conclusion, where all wrongs have been righted…
No, this is not a dream, and it's certainly not a conclusion.
This is merely the continuation of a reality filled with joy.
"Listen, you better not break our promise, okay?"
"I got it. I'll make sure to be back by ten."
"Just for today, you can't go out with anyone for a drink even if they insist, okay?"
"No, I doubt anyone would ask a married man out today."
"Even if some special scoop pops up late tonight, don't go running off to cover it.
"Promise me. If you don't come back today, I'll go back home to my family."
"Uum… Fine. I promise to come back."
After our longer-than-usual parting, Setsuna kisses me lightly on the lips as she usually does.
Setsuna's being a lot more particular than she usually is today. She's also become her unreasonably spoiled self, in a way.
…But I suppose that's to be expected. And no, I'm not saying this because I'm her husband.
Setsuna only acts like this three times a year.
The first time she behaves like this is on February 14thーher birthday. That she would behave in such a spoiled manner on that occasion is only natural.
The second time is during my birthday in April.
And the third time she acts like this…
A commemorative day where married couples and lovers fall prey to the commercialist custom of indulging in presents and dates.
But for the two of us… Well, this particular day has bound us together over many years.
It's the day we once swore eternal friendship in a hot spring up north; the day we faced our greatest crisis at a seaside hotel;
Although it's a day that's exemplified by the many sins I've committed, it also serves as a very important day of remembrance, in a sense.
That's why this is the one day I absolutely cannot break a promise with Setsuna on.
I'll meet Setsuna again today, wish her Merry Christmas, and swear to her that she's the only one for me.
With that thought in my mind, I reach my workplace with reaffirmed determination.
The unshakable vow I carry in my heart is a big departure from the usual enthusiasm I have for work.
"Kitahara, I'm done here so come check it when you can."
"Ah, take care of the layout here as well, please."
"I'll take care of both those things! …However I regret to inform you that these tasks will be my last for the day."
I catch a glimpse of the editing room clock, and find that it's already nearing 8 PM.
If I'm to keep my promise with Setsuna to see her before 10 PM, I'll have to finish things up rather quickly.
"Ah, what's up with that attitude? You have a lot of cheek for a rookie!"
"It seriously irritates me when people take that attitude with me on Christmas Eve of all days."
…Is what I'd like to say, but my two seniors seem to have a lot going on during Christmas Eve…
"What's the matter, Kitahara? Planning to sneak away so you can cozy up to your gorgeous wife for Christmas?"
"Your wife is something else, isn't she? She's famous in the industry as the public relations beauty of Knights Records.
"Perhaps he's stiff in more ways than one."
"Macchan, if I sued you for that statement, I'd be swimming in cash from the reparations you'd owe me."
"…You two, if you can afford to waste time rambling on like that, why don't you just go home?
"That's precisely the thing! Come on, I need some advice from you, Kitahara…"
"Huh? But I'm just a lowly rookie, like you said."
"But you're my superior when it comes to family! I'm begging you!"
"But what worth does my opinion have…?"
"Thing is, I'm under a lot of pressure from my girlfriend right now. If I meet her now, I'm sure I'm going to be forced to make some kind of decision."
"I doubt I can be of any help. Are you sure you should even be giving me such sensitive information?"
"She's invited me to visit her family for New Year's. This is bad, right? If I go there, it'll all be set in stone, right?"
"No, I don't see the problem with visiting her family. Besides, if you're going to be in a long-term relationship,
"But I'm not even remotely ready to take that step! I want to be single at least until I'm 30, ya know…"
"…Oh dear, half-baked men like this are a dime a dozen.
"…Suzuki-san, do you have a bug planted on me or something?"
"Besides, no one starts out with self-esteem. It's something you earn by leaving your comfort zone, trying new things and giving it your best."
