There's room for one more person besides Setsuna and me.
"I want a child… A child with you, Setsuna."
Without a single worry about my hesitations.
"I don't know if I can be the best father, but I still want to give it a shot."
I don't know if I can be anything like Setsuna's father.
It's possible I'll just end up like my own father.
"I know you'll do just fine, Haruki-kun."
But for as long as Setsuna will continue to save me…
With Setsuna and the Ogiso family pulling me along, perhaps things will work out fine.
Setsuna wraps her arms around me in a tight embrace.
"I look forward to it. I'd like a boy just like you, Haruki-kun."
"Another one of me would just annoy the life out of you. I'd like a girl like you, Setsuna."
"Another one of me would just be spoiled and selfish."
"In that case… I'm fine either way."
Early in the morning, in a deserted park, a married couple holds a somewhat embarrassing ceremony.
It was a perfectly ordinary ceremony, and perfectly natural. However, the two had promised not to do it outside.
When we're done, Setsuna moves her lips to my ear, standing on her tiptoes.
And with a slight sigh, she delivers the very timely news.
It showed up positive, and when I went to the hospital, they confirmed it.
"I had my little suspicions, but the timing felt almost too convenient, so I went to make sure at the hospital…"
I slipped away from work at noon and took an examination.
"That goes doubly for you. It's as if you were reading my mind when you made that proclamation."
I tightly hug Setsuna back, making sure not to put too much pressure on her belly, of course.
I had felt so unsure for so long, but I had finally resolved myself.
But to have it all come true in a single moment feels so… strange, odd, and outlandish. Well, I guess those three things mean the same thing.
But for some reason, I feel so overwhelmed with joy…
"Soon I won't be able to call you Haruki-kun anymore. I'll have to call you 'dad' when the kids are around."
Because my family in this world is once again growing bigger. Because a new resident is going to be living with us in our new apartment.
"That's why I'll use this occasion to say it to my heart's content, okay? Haruki-kun, Haruki-kun, Haruki-kun… Congratulations, and thank you so much!"
Our somewhat embarrassing ceremony continues. In fact, it's only getting more embarrassing.
But I don't pay attention to any sense of embarrassment within me. None of that matters to me now.
Instead, I put all my energy into embracing the person I love.
The woman I will soon be calling "mom" in front of our child.
"Come on, Setsuna, don't you know we're about to leave soon? Get down here."
The moving truck had already taken off, and of course, the luggage was carried out by the entire family.
The only thing left was for the residents to leave as well.
The apartment was filled with cardboard boxes just a short while ago. And up until a week prior, the apartment was full of life.
But all that remains now is the emptiness of what used to be our home.
It's a place that we're probably not going to return to again, once we go down and get in the car heading toward our new home.
It's a place that we won't be seeing ever again after seven long years of staying here.
It's kind of pathetic to get caught up in nostalgia on the very last day, but so much has happened here…
This apartment was the background to so many events in my life. Memories that aren't limited to just Setsuna, nor to myself when I was alone.
After burning the image of the empty apartment into my eyes one last time, I slowly close the door.
All that's left is to lock the door, and once this key is returned to the realtor, that'll be the end of it…
"This package was meant for you, but it was delivered to my door by mistake."
"Thank you very much for going out of your way to give it to us."
At the very end of our final farewell, a very kind and innocent distraction jumps in.
This time, with a slight bitter smile, I make up my mind to take my final leave…
When I turn around, I see Setsuna holding up a postcard right in front of my eyes.
There's a picture of what seems to be a very primiti… uh, traditional European townscape. It all but reveals the identity of the sender.
"…She says that the Vienna performance was a massive success. Apparently she's coming back this New Year's."
"Why would she send a postcard in this day and age? …She could've just sent us an email."
"Oh, but isn't this just like Kazusa? She's always been bad with technology."
"This is nothing like Kazusa! I can't believe a couch potato like her would bother sending a picture postcard!"
She's the one who's being mean here.
She knows perfectly well where we live, yet she went out of her way to write the address number of the neighboring apartment door.
And she knowingly made sure it'd arrive today, to the apartment where she used to…
"…Okay, let's head out for real this time. I want to have something to eat by the end of the day, at least."
"Huh? Let's just eat outside! I'm sure my parents would allow that on a special day like this."
"Right, I suppose that's fine if you're tired, Setsuna. I guess I'll have to cook up a feast large enough for the whole family…"
"Hey! Don't embarrass me in front of my family! Haruki-kun, you're so mean!"
And so, the two of us… The two of us, soon to be the three of us…
…Will begin carving out our new history tomorrow, in a new place we'll call home…
Looking up, I see the same familiar sky. The same old sky I've seen for the past twenty years.
The same old sky that watches over the life I've built over the yearsーa life that has crumbled ever so slightly.
"Good morning! I'm Yanagihara Tomo from the news department. It's a pleasure to meet you!"
"Ah, are you the rumored Ms. Houjou? Everyone's calling you the rising star around here, you know?"
"No, that has nothing to do with my work here. I'm no more than a rookie around here. I'll probably make a lot of mistakes, but I hope you'll help me improve."
"Ah, you don't need to be so nervous. You're more serious than I thought you would be."
"Thank you very much. I'll do my best!"
"Haha, well, don't overdo it. Well then, I'll take you to the Managing Editor, so follow me."
"Always act humble on the outside, and when the chance comes, take the whole cake! That's my first step towards glory～♪"
"Well then, I'll be heading home for today. I'll have a new sample out first thing tomorrow."
"Ah, just a second! Hey, Iizuka-kun! Have you thought about what I told you earlier?"
"Don't play dumb. I told you about the mixer, remember?"
"Iizuka-kun, ever since they put you in charge, you've risen so far up the ranks."
"So we think we should celebrate, go out, meet some people, and keep up the good work once we're back."
"Ah, well, I am happy with how the sales have risen, but I'm only doing what's expected of me."
"Don't be like that. There'll be some new faces there."
"The girls in this one are quite cute, you know? You can pick and choose from underclassmen to high school graduates!"
"So we've gathered around five or six people. You can just see the whole thing as a friendly outing, rather than a corporate thing."
"Yeah, it doesn't get more real than this. Iizuka-kun, you're from Houjou, right? Can't you pick up some people on your end?"
"Well, if you put it that way………
!? N-No, that's not what I meant. I suck at that kind of stuff, so let me off the hook, please!"
"See ya again tomorrow. Good work today!"
"Ah, hightailed it again… Seriously, that guy is on his guard like you wouldn't believe."
"I don't get it. He was a massive playboy in his school days, and yet…"
"You can't just remove the sales course from the employee training! Especially not when the welcoming ceremony is already finished…
"Like I said, the company is short on staff this season. The other departments are demanding I send them more manpower ASAP.
"That doesn't matter, I'm just venting my bitterness. It's the sales course that's important here!"
"Last year, it took all I had to pass that course. But in my opinion, that's what made it such a worthwhile effort in the end."
"Yeah, for many people it's their only opportunity to experience the real deal. The company of course understands the value in…"
"So getting rid of it makes absolutely no sense! Please try to negotiate with the guys at the top, boss! If you don't, I'll go there myself!"
"Of course. I've gathered the opinions of all employees, including the managers."
"…And for some reason they chose you, a second-year employee, to represent them?"
"I don't mind taking up any role, that's why they chose me."
"Come to think of it, I seem to remember you wanting to move into development."
"Right now I don't mind any post. Be it development, business, working the store, or even HR. The path before me will open as long as I put in effort."
"…Seems like I've trained you to become quite the meddlesome one, in a single year, no less."
"I'm sorry, but I've been faking it a lot up until now. What you see here is the real me."
"How many times do I have to explain until you get it through your thick skull!?"
"Right back at you, Hamada-san! For once, I don't think I'm even slightly in the wrong here!"
"Don't grumble like that, Hamada-san. That's basically admitting defeat."
"Of course, doing things face-to-face is better than not, but even then there's a limit."
"But it becomes too businesslike otherwise. Magazines are written by people, so you need to convey some rawness in your reporting."
"I know, you're telling me that going out of one's way is good. I don't disagree with that. But right now I have other priorities that take precedence."
"Woah, did I just hear Macchan say something grown-up?"
"I get that I'm in my fourth year already… but right now I have to remain at the bottom."
"Alrighty then, I'll be right off to my project. I'll head home right after, so this'll be our farewell for today."
"…I'm sorry, but that's how things are. This time I really can't meet your standards, Hamada-san."
"There aren't enough hands to go around, after all. I have to make do with what I have…"
"It's fine already. I'll leave this to your judgment. Come to me for advice only if you get stuck."
"Let's keep up the good work, Macchan."
"That's not good… I have a presentation at 10 o'clock on Monday, but we're a bit lacking in material…"
"The only thing I've accomplished so far is to realize that I need to begin working on it soon."
"Well, I suppose I could cook something up if I come to work on the weekend. But if there are two of us, we could finish it today."
"God dammit! Inseparable as always, you two!"
"We have plans for dinner today so… I'm sorry."
"I bet it won't end there. You're going to stay at your boyfriend's place both today and tomorrow, aren't you?"
"I only do that sometimes… Only once every two weeks."
"In other words, on top of always forcing your junior to listen to you ramble on about your boyfriend, you're also going to refuse working on the weekends."
"Um, send me everything you've finished so far by email. I'll take the early Monday shift and get it done for you."
"I promise I'll get it done by 10 o'clock on Monday!"
"That's not what I meant… It's my fault for slacking off in the first place, and I don't wanna spoil your day when you're so happy."
"I said forget about it. I've resolved myself to work the weekend. I'll head home for today. Want to go to the station together?"
"So anyway, lemme hear about your boyfriend. It'll make for good material to taunt all the guys who have their sights on you, Ogiso-chan."
"Huh? But it's nothing but a bunch of boring stuff. We've been dating for ages already."
"I can think of five guys who'd have their worlds fall apart if they heard you say that."
Two springs ago I graduated university, and for two springs I have worked for my current company.
A friend burning with hope, in a new place to belong. A friend who never broke the oath that we swore last spring.
Like that, each friend walks their own path.
This is the story of that spring, all the way until autumn.
From the end of winter, to the beginning of the next…
Another story beginning with the melting of the snow, and ending with its fall once again.
When I open the front door, silence and darkness greet me.
Without switching on the light, I simply walk into the dark room after taking off my high-heels.
I follow the wall toward the bedroom door, then turn on the night lamp by the entrance.
"A senior at work had me all tied up. For a moment there, I was wondering if I'd ever make it home today."
Within the murky darkness of the room, no signs of life can be seen.
The only proof that he lives here is…
…The days worth of old clothes and underwear littered all over the room.
The better someone knows this guy, the more surprised they'd be at the state this place is in.
Although, any somewhat lazy person might not find anything out of the ordinary here.
"I'm sorry, this might get a bit loud."
After picking up the clothes abandoned on the floor, I put them into the washing machine and turn it on.
"Do you have anything else dirty? Are the ones you're wearing okay?"
I glance at the human-sized bulge on the bed, hidden beneath the sheets.
And then his head, the only part of him that's uncovered, gives the slightest hint of a nod.
"I see… Did you take your medicine?"
A tiny movement once again, but this time in a different direction.
"I'll make something that'll last then. I'll leave it here when it's ready, so just ding it when you feel hungry."
When I turn on the kitchen lamp, the whole place becomes ever so slightly brighter.
One by one, I line up all the ingredients from my shopping bag.
"…Oh, I said 'ding it' again, didn't I? I just can't seem to drop this habit of mine, hehe."
This is what my weekends are like.
To him… to Haruki-kun, this might just be a day like any other. Just one out of 365 others.
But to me, these moments are that of pure happiness and bliss.
It is the end of February.
When the curtains fell on Kazusa's legendary concert that day, those same curtains also fell on her final days in Japan.
That day, I left this person's side.
When he confessed everything to me, I couldn't bring myself to forgive the things he did with Kazusa, his feelings, his love for her.
For seven whole days, I ran away from the world surrounding me.
I weeped with the same regret as five years ago. I screamed at my own failure, so much worse than anything I did five years ago.
And finally, I came back to this apartment.
"I don't want to sound arrogant, but I think this stew turned out pretty well. I even had seconds, twice!"
When I once again stepped foot in this place, Haruki-kun was still running away from the world, just like I had been the day prior.
And his flight is still continuing to this day.
"…Although now my belly feels a bit heavy. I'll probably have to take some stomach medicine later."
After an interview with an occupational health physician, they determined that his condition was partly due to "stress from unjust overwork"
"Come to think of it, it's almost time for March's new music release. Tomo hasn't talked to me the past month, so I completely forgot about it."
Nowadays, he only goes outside once a week, and that's only to visit the psychiatric hospital.
…All the other days are spent here, in this apartment.
"Apparently she fulfilled her wish to work in a news department. I wonder what backhanded tricks she used this time."
During some weeks he finds himself completely unable to get out of bed, and during others he can't fall asleep at all.
"Come to think of it, Takeya-kun and Io said they wanted to visit you sometime soon."
When he can't get up, I don't force him up.
Because he never got any decent sleep since his graduation from university.
"I keep telling them there's no need to worry so much. You'll get better soon anyway, and then we'll be able to see each other every month like always."
During the weeks when he can't get any sleep, I don't say anything.
Because I know just how badly he wants to fall asleep himself.
I know just how deeply he's suffering, after being abandoned all alone in the real world.
…I know that he's desperately trying to forget about everything and just return to his dream world.
"Fuaah… I feel kinda sleepy… Perhaps I really did eat too much."
I don't have the courage, nor the right…
…To know what, or who, is waiting for him in that world.
"Setsuna, you don't have to come here anymore."
Those were the first words… that Haruki-kun said to me today.
Those are words he's desperately forcing out of himself, words that signify that he has me on his mind.
"I'll live with the person I am for the rest of my life. I've prepared myself for that."
"But that doesn't mean I can allow you to get mixed up in my stagnant life."
"Yeah yeah, let's talk about that next time."
"Stop running away and listen to me, Setsuna…"
"I'm not messing around, and I'm not running away either… I'm not running away at all…"
His trembling reaches me through his cheek and our entwined hand.
"It's just that… I want to talk about this when you're feeling better, Haruki-kun. When you can talk to me calmly. Okay?"
"And when would that be? When in the world would that be…?"
"Someday. But I promise the day will come."
"That's a lie. I'll stay like this for the rest of my life."
"In any case, there's no need to rush for an answer. We can take it slowly. Rest for today, okay?"
I want to wrap myself around him with all my might, and I want to console him with powerful words.
"Besides, you've been rushing far too much up until now, Haruki-kun. No one would blame you for taking it a bit slow for once, you know?"
"That has nothing to do with this…"
But I can't do either of those things right now.
"I didn't turn out like this because I overworked myself at the office. This has nothing to do with rushing through life."
So instead, I embrace him softly, slowly and silently.
"You should know that better than anyone, Setsuna…"
"The one who pushed you to this point was me, five years ago."
However, my body temperature isn't enough to do away with the coldness in his heart.
"…You should know that better than anyone."
"There is no forgiving what I did, and you're the last person in the world who should be forgiving me, Setsuna."
Because even now, he won't stop hurting himself. He won't stop rejecting himself.
"So you don't have to come here anymore… Just leave me be."
The reason I'm with you right now isn't because of any noble feelings on my part.
It's neither sympathy nor forgiveness that's driving me to do this…
But in the end, it wasn't my rejection of myself that put an end to his grief…
"Of course you have to stay… Without you, Setsuna, I wouldn't know what to do with myself."
It was an even greater source of grief that put a stop to it.
"If I really wanted you gone, I could've just used the door chain to lock you out. I could just chase you out even now."
The feelings of guilt he bears toward me won't ever be washed away, no matter what anyone tells him.
"Yet I did neither of those things. I never took away the apartment key from you, nor did I ever lock the door with the chain."
"Thank you, for giving me another chance."
That's why his heart only falls deeper into despair when I'm by him.
"You did my laundry, you cooked for me, you embraced me… I can finally admit this, now that I feel so fulfilled."
"It doesn't end there. When I noticed you were a little bit late, it felt as if my body was getting torn apart."
But right now, he has to rely on the very person who is nothing but poison to him.
"I was worried out of my mind that… perhaps, you had finally decided to stop coming… That you had abandoned me."
"I'm despicable. I'm such a despicable person…"
"No, it makes me happy… It makes me so happy."
I can't bring myself to leave his side. I can't bring myself to stop breaking him.
"I can't bear the thought of tormenting you, yet I can't bear the thought of a reality without you either."
I can't stop the ugliness within myself from feeling a dark sense of joy from his laments.
"I can't head in either direction. I can't decide anything. The world has no use for a man like me!"
I can't stop the patheticness within myself from feeling affection toward him, but only when he clings to me.
"Most importantly, you have no use for me, Setsuna… No, I'm nothing but a source of pain for you."
"That's not true. That's not true at all…"
"I'm sorry. I'm so sorry… Uu, uugh, uuug… Uuaah…"
Not so I can save him, but to satisfy my own desires.
"I won't ever leave you, and I promise you'll get better…!"
All I want to do… is to convince myself that the past two years weren't for nothing… when I won only because my opponent withdrew.
I let out a big yawn with my eyes on the bright sky. The clock is nearing 10 o'clock.
He cried all night, but he finally exhausted himself by early dawn, and finally fell asleep.
After a few hours of gazing at his sleeping face, I quietly slipped out of the apartment.
After all, my presence this week seems to have had a bad effect on him.
Most likely, Haruki-kun won't wake up for a day or two.
But when he does wake up, he'll probably be a good deal calmer than he was earlier.
The only thing it takes… is for me to not be around.
I was nothing but poison to him today.
I can only numb the pain for a short while, and the terrible side-effects I cause make me completely useless.
"Ah, good morning. Were you awake already?"
"No, I'm calling about the work you told me about yesterday. I'll come to the office today and do it."
"Yeah, that's how it is. I got into a big fight with my boyfriend last night so… haha."
Looking up, I see the same hollow sky. The same old sky I've been averting my eyes from for the past five years.
The same old sky that now watches over the aftermath of those dreamlike, happy days filled with so much pain.
Beyond the door of the hospital room, I'm met with a rather curt answer.
Of course, that's only because my greeting was curt as well.
A dull room decorated with nothing but empty flower pots. Though, since neither the patient nor the visitor have any interest in flowers, I don't see the problem.
Because any time spent taking care of flowers is time not spent devouring fruits. Of course, it's not the fruit itself that is valuable, but the sugar contents.
"Wait a second, this thing is frozen solid. I can't peel the skin off this thing."
"Then let me do it for you."
"Don't be ridiculous. A pianist shouldn't be getting her fingers all yellow."
In the only place for miles where Japanese is mutually understood, we can finally relax a little.
This is my hour of comfort, coming only once a day.
"What is it? Why are you staring at me?"
It's only by a little bit, but it looks like she's lost weight again.
Mom mutters those words as if she just remembered them, the frozen mandarin still in her mouth.
"You're the patient. Those words should be directed at you, not at me…"
"Where's the fun in hearing about how sick a sick person is? It's your piano that's important."
I toss a piece into my own mouth as well, and bite the crunchy chilliness which before long completely permeates my teeth.
…This freezer is way too good at freezing.
"But your massive success in Japan made you the star of the hour. You shouldn't be wasting the opportunity."
"But the first concert was a total failure. It was only during the additional concert that I managed to salvage the disaster somewhat."
"All's well that ends well. In fact, it was partially due to the mediocre first performance that the massive improvement in the second made so much noise."
"Being a pianist, I can't say that evaluation makes me happy. It's like you're telling me 'You don't know unless you try!' or something."
"Well it's true, you really don't know unless you try. If you don't like it then try being more consistent. Practice 50 or 100 hours a day if you have to."
"If you can provide me with such incredible power, then by all means, boss."
"Have you ever heard of the hyperbolic time chamber? For now I've figured out the theoretical part to make one, but I haven't started the experiments yet."
When I have these carefree conversations with my mom, it's almost as if we're back in Japan…
No, it goes even further back than our homecoming. It's as if she hasn't changed one bit.
"Indeed, a frozen mandarin must have a thin coating of ice on the surface, but the peel and contents themselves must be slightly soft…"
"I'm sorry for making you come back to Vienna… because of my selfishness."
"…I was really hoping you'd join me in my critique of these mandarins."
A week after my flight from Japan…
After finishing up the last of her business, Mom also left.
…Of course, she didn't really get to finish her business there.
She simply chased after me so she could protect me. She finally abandoned Japan for my sakeーwithout even considering her own condition.
She did it all for me, even at the cost of abandoning her modest wish of spending her last days in Japan.
"I'll do anything. I won't be fussy, I'll come to visit you every day, and I'll even do as you say… so please…"
"How many times do I have to tell you this? If you want to please me, then play your piano. Don't say 'it's going decent' at a time like this."
"Besides, I don't regret coming back here. The place I belong is wherever my beloved daughter lives. I can finally come to terms with that now…"
When I first found out about the truth, here in Vienna, my emotions were a mix of despair, unease and grief.
I understood why Mom was so obsessed with the idea of a concert in Japan. I understood why she wanted me to shine in that country.
When I managed to connect the dots, I began to hate myself.
I lost the little love I had for the idiotic daughter who trampled all over her mother's determination, all because of some childish heartbreak.
The notion that the selfishness that brought my mom back to Vienna might have… hastened the approach of 'that time'…
"R-Right! I had an exam here just earlier, at this hospital."
"So, did it turn out positive? Will I become a grandmother?"
"You were practically making me cry just moments ago. Why can't you stay serious for more than a few seconds?"
"What do you mean? This is something that would have a massive impact on your life."
"In any case, that's not what I'm talking about. Listen to me carefully."
So please, don't bring that up again.
"It was a compatibility test. For a marrow transplant."
Instead, I will put all my effort into the things I am capable of.
The one form of filial piety I am capable of.
"They said the results will come in later. Wait until then, would you?"
"If we're compatible… no, I'm sure it'll be fine. When that happens, Mom, I'll…"
Whenever I put in the effort, it usually leads me in the wrong direction. I know that much from experience…
"You've clearly spent a lot of time researching my illness, but I never knew you were considering something so idiotic."
"It means precisely what you think it means. Don't do idiotic things, you idiot!"
Even so, Mom's words were no small shock to me, as for this one instance, I genuinely believed that I was making the right decision.
"It means that it'd be more absurd not to do the test. If we're compatible, then you'll be able to…"
"Even if we're compatible, I'll never allow it."
"Stop making a scene in the hospital. They'll throw you out."
"How can I not make a scene!? You have such a great possibility right in front of you, so why would you just…"
"I would never agree to anything that would hurt you…"
It's only when I have those carefree conversations with my mom, that it feels as if nothing has changed.
"I will never allow any decision that would cause any harm to the body, talent, or the nerves of the pianist Touma Kazusa."
"What are you saying…? I'd obviously be perfectly fine…"
"I won't allow the slightest risk. It can never be allowed to happen…"
But as much as it feels like nothing has changed…
"No one has the right to take my one single hope away from me."
"Even if that's what you yourself want, I won't allow it."
As of this moment, my mom just loves me far too much.
She's envisioning me as her own successor.
She's already picturing a world where she no longer exists…
As I exit the hospital, I'm greeted by the same hollow sky.
A sky even more lost than during noon, as if reflecting the feelings of my heart. A sky at the end of a long dream.
But reality goes on even after one wakes from a dream.
A reality cruel beyond anything that preceded it. All because I've had a lifetime's worth of happiness…
"Hmm, I guess it's a tiny bit different from what I expected."
"Oh, what's this? Is Tomo out of all people experiencing new job angst?"
"How should I put it… It feels like they're taking me lightly. Makes me wonder if I'm even needed, you know."
"Uwah, I can totally relate! It feels like I'm looking at myself from a year ago."
"Well, you'll always find something different than what you expected in the beginning.
"That's true I guess. The larger the scope, the longer the learning period. I'd say that Tomo's line of work would take a year or so."
"Right now is the time to learn. If you just keep doing your best, you'll get the hang of it…
Though, I guess second-years like ourselves have no right to say that."
"I'm not talking about abstract stuff like that. There are more specific things I'm unhappy about."
"Such as the mixer just the other day.
"I couldn't be more disappointed! And to think they wanted to split the bill at such a cheap place.
"What do you mean idiotic? Connections are everything in this industry. I wonder if those guys even see us as valuable assets."
"I'll admit you're optimistic, but you're so gross I can't even bring myself to respond…"
"Hey, that's rude! Besides, wasn't today supposed to be all about encouraging me? Your treat, of course."
"What are you on about? Your salary is higher than anyone else's here. We're obviously relying on your first paycheck to foot the bill."
"Huh!? But my first paycheck was nothing special at all."
"It's okay, you have all the potential in the world, Tomo."
"For sure. I bet she'll overtake me in a single year."
"By then she'll be completely independent with 100 millions of yen in her bank account, I'm sure."
"Yeah, that's the plan, but it's a difficult journey there. Next time I get bullied by a senior newscaster out of jealousy, you two better console me, okay?"
"Oh yeah, as long as you can keep that arrogance up I'm sure you'll be fine. Alright, let's give a toast to Tomo-san's ever growing carnivorous nature!"
…But I'm still poor for now, so you two will cover the bill, won't you?"
"…Tsk, I was so close to having her."

"Damn it! This is my 19th loss in a row…

"Atara hot springs… the Izu peninsula, huh?"

"Yeah, that sounds pretty good. Izu isn't that far away."

"Nothing at all! Hot springs are great. You can just sit there and relax like an old lady… It's amazing!"

"I'm so excited. An alumni meeting of former Miss Houjou winners.

"I never had any interest in that stuff!"
"Setsuna never had any interest either, right? And yet she got chosen three years in a row. How did that happen, I wonder?"
Alright, Arata hot springs it is then! No men allowed whatsoever."
"Time to flee this cruel world and jump into a life of nothing but alcohol and sleep!"
"Even if there's a beach right in front of us, we'll swim in the hot springs!"
"What, no way. No way I'm doing that."
"We can't just swim in the bath."
"Oh, but Setsuna… will you be okay? You know…"
"A single night out should be fine. I'll set aside the time. Worst case scenario, I'll ask Takeya for a favor like I did today. Forgive me, Io."
"Huh, why are you bringing me into this?"
"Don't say that. It's because of things like this that you two just keep on…"
"But you'll really be okay, right? We can't have you getting worried and going home halfway through, you know?"
"It's okay, I'll get someone else to take care of him. …I realized, just recently."
"That unless I enjoy my own life to the fullest, I can't put a smile on his face."
"Besides, I'll only worry Haruki-kun further if I don't show him that I'm having fun."
"God, that annoying part of you is the only thing that hasn't changed over the years."
"So you two don't have to worry that much. Don't hesitate to invite me from now on."
"Yeah, this isn't just for his sake. I think it's also for my… for everyone's sake."
"I guess you're right. What's the point of life without a bit of fun? Even being together with loved ones can get draining otherwise."
I'd be fine with that. I'd be fine with just being together.
"I'm not going to sacrifice anything. I mean, I want to be happy with everyone.
"You didn't have any fun with us in the past, though."
"Even now she's totally the indoorsy type. She'd never come along unless it's about Kitahara-san or a hot spring."
"Hey, don't make fun of me… I'm trying to be serious here."
"As I was about to say, I'll of course never stop loving Haruki-kun either. I think this is something I have to do in order to remain by his side."
"I know you're being serious, but how am I supposed to react when you're going all starry eyed for your boyfriend?"
"I'm sorry, but let me get amorous at least a little bit."
Because no matter how much I struggle, I can never beat her.
Since I can't beat her, I can't use the same methods as her. I can only do what I am capable of, and do it to my utmost.
…No, my only choice is to carry through, without doing my utmost.
"In that case, Setsuna… Um, If you got an invitation to do a live concert… would you do it?"
"Yeah, perhaps. If I have the time, I guess I'd like to."
"No, I'll never quit. I love it, after all."
That's right, I'll never quit. I'm too greedy to ever quit.
"Anyway that's how things stand, so let's wrap up here and head to the after-party karaoke! Okay?"
"…I think we'll sit this one out."
Unlike her, I'm incapable of throwing everything away for his sake…
"You little… Arg… grr… Alright, this time I'll…!"
"What's up? Don't talk to me when I'm winning. You tryin' to distract me so I'll make a mistake or something?"
"I mean my life from here on out, my job, Setsuna… What am I supposed to do?"
"Never thought I'd live to see the day when you'd ask me for advice. I wish the two of us from seven years ago could be around to hear this."
"From the very first day we met you began telling me what to do. You'd lecture me for hours, days even, until I finally agreed."
"I'm such an idiot. I never knew how clueless I was."
"I always demand that everyone else is at their best, yet when it comes to myself, I just go with the flow without deciding anything.
"But it was still your choice, even if you believe you were just going with the flow."
"That's why you're here right now. There were many other paths ahead of you, but you still remain here."
"But what comfort is that, if the choice I made was the wrong one?"
"There's no value in this path if I've betrayed Setsuna, and abandoned Kazusa…"
"Yet despite that, I still can't let go of Setsuna. I'm still piling on more sins. How can that ever be forgiven?"
"Are you saying that if a person makes the wrong choice once, they don't deserve forgiveness ever? That can't be right."
"It wasn't just once… I did it over and over… at every turn…!"
"To begin with, people have the hardest time understanding themselves over anyone else.
"To sum things up, the stuff you kept telling me was right all along… More right than my own judgment, at least."
"That's precisely why I need you to tell me this time… What am I supposed to do…?"
"You've gotta decide for yourself. Don't ask me."
"…Just so you know, I'm not talking about right now. The choice you'll make is a bit further down the line."
"And when is that…? When in the world is that…?"

"…Trust that I was hesitating? That sounds weird."
"Yeah, I suppose it's a bit weird."
"When that time comes… When you've hesitated and worried enough, and when you're ready to make a choice… talk to me first, okay?"
"If it's your choice, then I won't say a word about it… is what I'll absolutely never say. I'll tell you exactly what to do like you used to with me."
"Save those words for the person who actually deserves to hear them, when you're back to your usual self."
"And once that baptism is over and done with, I'll be next.
"Thank god! We made it in time for the last train."
"Ah, my throat's all sore. I hope it'll get better by Monday, at least."
"That's only because you tried going toe-to-toe with Setsuna. Had you just let her sing by herself, we would've been done in two hours."
"But that's lame. I gotta show off the fruits of my own voice training, you know?"
"Aren't you forgetting the purpose of today's outing?"
"Oh what's the problem? I'm telling you, Setsuna will shed a lot more stress if we all have fun together."
"I sure pray so. Setsuna did look like she was having a bit of fun, I guess."
"You're the one who's being too considerate, Mizusawa-san. If only you could show that same kind of consideration to Iizuka-san as well…"
"Don't segway the conversation into something completely unrelated! I'm not taking the bait, so give it up."
"Do you hate him that much now? Haruki, I mean…"
"I don't hate him. I just can't forgive him."
"I can't even think of a scenario where I'd forgive him… Changing his mind as he pleases, hesitating as he pleases, breaking down as he pleases."
"Even if I discard my personal feelings on the matter, Kitahara-san right now is nothing but a burden on Setsuna."
"Of course, Setsuna would be livid if she heard me say that, so I'll keep this just between you and me."
"Try being a bit considerate of my mental state as well."
"So how about you, Mizusawa-san? Are you still able to forgive Kitahara-san after what he did?"
"I can't forgive him… but I want to remain his friend."
"Our friendship goes further back than Setsuna and I. I know that he's living his life in earnest, always trying to be honest."
"Besides, I can understand Touma-san's feelings a little as well. It's just that… her feelings were more powerful than I ever could have imagined."
"But the strength of those feelings was what led to this whole mess."
"Above all, Setsuna would never want to see those two punished for that."
"In any case, you can just stay the way you are. Stay by Setsuna's side and keep on supporting only her as you always have."
"Well, I guess Setsuna's completely hopeless without me anyway."
"I'm sure Takeya will continue taking Haruki's side. I think that balance is exactly what we need."
"But I really don't know yet. Whether Setsuna truly is forcing herself, or whether she actually…"
"…You might be right, but I don't know if she's reaching her limit, or if she's still able to push further."
"Even if she is at her limit, I still have to think about it. Whether I should force those two apart, or help them get back together like Setsuna wants."
"I don't know. I have an idea or two, but I still don't have any confidence in them."
"Seriously, whenever it's about men and women, your ability to decide completely evaporates."
"I see… Everything went smoothly today then. Good work."
"Yeah, alright then… huh? You mean right now?"
"…Fine, in front of the station then."
"Sorry, something just came up. I gotta go."
"Of course not, we're just going for a bite to eat."
"But you've had loads of food and drinks tonight."
"All that singing got me a little hungry again."
"And you're leaving, knowing that you'll miss the last train?"
"I could catch the first morning train if I pass the time a little."
"Isn't that what they call a date?"
"The weather outside is nice today, so I'll come back home after a little stroll."
"By the way, I'll be able to return to work soon."
"The monthly managerial meeting will be held at the end of this week, and I'm thinking of showing up then."
"Thank you for everything until now, Setsuna. I'm sorry for burdening you so much when you already had your hands full with work."
"You don't have to come every week anymore. Spend this weekend at your own place, and rest."
Spring has passed, and summer has begun, at least according to the calendar.
The mornings and evenings are still chilly, but the days are just as cheerfully warm as I remember.
"Good work, but don't push yourself too hard. Use a taxi instead if it becomes too hard on you."
He's been consulting a doctor and he's getting better, little by little.
For now, he'll be going to the library during the day once a week, allowing him to get in touch with people and society in a quiet atmosphere.
Hearing that makes me happy of course, but the greatest news is this.
"But I guess I understand why you'd want to go for a stroll today. The air feels amazing, doesn't it?"
He didn't even charge his cell phone until very recently. Even now, he never calls me nor answers any of my calls.
But even so, he's begun to talk about himself to meーand only meーagain. That's the thing I'm the happiest about.
"Ah, I'm on my way back to the office by the way. It's not like I'm texting at work or anything."
Since a long time ago, his texts have been something for me to lean on.
There were days when I'd wait impatiently for the one text a day he'd send me.
The promise was that he'd only text me once a day, yet I kept waiting for the second, and then the third…
"…But I guess it's kinda unclear whether texting while on the move from one post to another counts as slacking off at work. Hehe."
When we lost sight of each other, when I ended up rejecting him, and when our bond was so terribly damaged…
During those times, it was those single texts that would once again bind us together.
"Back on topic though. So you're thinking about going back to work, huh. That's amazing! Looks like you've gotten a lot better."
"But you don't have to be in such a rush. I've told you this before, but you should go through the steps slowly, but steadily."
"Let's discuss everything together, okay? Like the managerial meeting, your medicine, and the state of your workplace."
"With that in mind, I think I'll head over this weekend as well. There's so much to talk about now, after all."
"In fact, I'd be really glad if you didn't try to take away the one thing I'm looking forward to so much. I'll go there no matter what!"
I'm happy, of course, but I can't let myself be immersed in my own sense of satisfaction.
His text just now really seemed optimistic. I could feel the will behind what he told me.
But that's precisely why I feel so uneasy. I really hope this is just me overthinking it, but…
Going back to work all of a sudden… It's far too early to make that kind of judgment.
That's a decision he should make with a calm mind, with the advice of those around him.
"In the afternoon tomorrow, the humid weather in the west will carry over here."
"Just like in Kyushu and Shikoku, everywhere from Kinki to Kanto will be experiencing a rainy season starting this weekend."
As usual, I could feel the presence of someone in this closed off, dark room.
But unlike before, that presence was not on the bed…
"I said you didn't have to come."
But rather in the corner of the room directly opposite it.
Leaning against the wall, looking up at nothing in particular, muttering some words with even less energy than usual.
"The rain… The rain wouldn't stop, so…"
"Yup, you did the right thing. I'm glad you didn't go. I mean look at me, I'm all drenched…"
"Damn it, why does it have to rain? On such an important day…!"
Everything stands in contrast to the text he sent me yesterdayーhis tone, his voice, and his words.
The way Haruki-kun is now, the slightest trigger can send his emotions into disarray.
"Nothing we can do about the weather. Another day, perhaps."
I sit beside him, but I make sure to maintain a small distance so I don't get him wet.

"But I didn't go to the last meeting either. This makes it the second month I haven't shown up for work."
"Like I said, there's no need to rush. You always have to be so hasty, Haruki-kun."
I softly put my hand on his shoulder, guessing that this small amount of physical contact won't make him reject me.
Our level of intimacy changes by the day, so like always, I have to feel my way around to figure out what degree is okay.
"At this rate I'll be forgotten by everyone. It'll be as if I was never there from the start."
"Of course that won't happen. Everyone is waiting for you."
"How could you possibly know that? What would you know about my workplace, Setsuna…"
"Well, you know… my job is kinda similar."
"Must be nice, Setsuna… always being so busy."
"I'm just slow at my job, that's all. All I ever do is cause trouble for my co-workers."
"Must be nice being needed by everyone."
"I keep telling you, you're needed as well. They even sent you a postcard with everyone's names on it."
Beside his bed lies a piece of colored paper, sent by the editorial staff of Kaiousha.
From what I heard, the whole thing was planned by a former superior of his who now lives in America.
"That's just… how everyone felt about me two months ago, when they thought I'd get better in no time."
"No one thought that. Everyone just hopes that you'll get better someday."
That's how important he is to the company he works for.
"You can't know how anyone there is feeling right now… No, they probably don't even care anymore."
He's merely the only one who can't bring himself to believe that.
"They'll wait for you… You were good enough at your job for them to wait patiently now. I'm certain they'll wait for you."
"How would you know? People's feelings change all the time…"
"Yes, they do. After two years spent together with you, I…"

"I betrayed you, Setsuna, when I was supposed to love you forever…"

I had no choice but to believe it, when I had to sit beside you for five years as you kept thinking about Kazusa.
"It still makes no sense to me… How can you bring yourself to stay by my side, Setsuna…?"
"I told you, I'm doing this because I want to…"
"I know I told you… that I couldn't live without you, Setsuna…"

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry… I'm so sorry for making you suffer so much."
"Don't apologize… It only makes me feel more pathetic…!"
His shivering body looks more feeble than ever.
