But I can't do that right now.
Because to him, my hug is probably nothing more than the painful embrace of a vine full of thorns.
Spring has passed, and summer has begun, at least according to the calendar.
Along with the heat, this season of gloomy dimness begins.
I wake up to an all too familiar ceiling.
The ceiling of the apartment I used to visit every weekend for two years, it is not. It's the ceiling I've been looking up at since I was born, in my own room.
After turning off the alarm and opening the window, I'm greeted by the same dreary sky as yesterday.
A weekend morning, spent apart from Haruki-kun.
Yes, in the end I didn't stay at his place.
Yesterday, he was in such a terrible state that just having me around was enough to ruin him, something that only happens once every two weeks or so.
The sound of the rain and the darkness of the sky seeped into the tepidness of his room, robbing him of any courage or joy he had left.
On days like that, I never managed to restore Haruki-kun's strength, no matter how much I tried to console him, encourage him, or embrace him.
That's why I did the only thing I could to put his mind at ease a little… by disappearing from his sight.
Every weekend morning, I'm always caught in a struggle between myself and my low blood pressure, which keeps trying to hold me tied down to bed.
So that I can spend time with Haruki-kun.
Did he get any sleep after that, I wonder? Did he regain some strength, I wonder?
Did he eat properly, I wonder?
I need to make sure, because sometimes he'll even go days without drinking a single drop of water if I don't keep my eyes on him.
With my thoughts thoroughly occupied with those worries, I grab hold of my pajamas and begin to change.
I felt a strange sense of disgust at the words that had just left my mouth.
What did I mean by "I have to go"?
Whenever I leave on the weekends, I never tell them where I'm going.
And they've never bothered asking either.
"Don't need any. I'll eat over there."
There aren't enough options for that to be a question worth asking.
"…I don't know. I'll call you in any case."
"I see… Be careful not to slip in the rain, okay?"
"Yeah, I know. Okay then, see you."
This has been the unwritten rule in this household for the past two years.
Until half a year ago, they'd let it slide with a bitter smile; now, it's with a sigh.
"I need to have a talk with you, along with your mother."
"Sorry, but I'm in a hurry right now. How about tonight or tomorrow night instead?"
"No, it has to be right now. I won't allow you to leave this house until we've had a talk."
On that ever so stagnant everyday life of mine, a chilly and damp breeze flows in.
"Are you telling me to stop going? Are you telling me to abandon him!?"
"I haven't said that at all. Stop purposefully interpreting things in the most extreme way."
He told me not to go. He told me to keep my distance from him.
I always felt like those words were on the tip of his tongue these past weeks, and now he finally said it.
Further still, I'm surrounded by the chilly wind.
"Haruki-kun is family now, you know? How can you be so heartless to him just because he fell a bit ill!? You're cruel!"
"He has a family of his own. Wouldn't asking them for help be the proper thing to do?"
Dad's asserting that his family should be the one responsible for his current problem.
"In fact, wouldn't you agree that not even asking his family for their opinion is the truly heartless thing here?"
"I already explained this a hundred times… Haruki-kun isn't on good terms with his mom…"
He's telling me to leave Haruki-kun in the care of someone he hasn't talked to in years…
"Yes, I've heard that many times from you, Setsuna, but I haven't heard any of the details from Kitahara-kun himself."
"Just talking about it is painful for him… There's no way he could handle the emotional stress, given the state he's in now."
I'm the only one he'll ever tell that story to. Myself and… one other person…
No, he told her first and only told me out of convenience. About the past he had cast away.
"Perhaps Kitahara-san's symptoms have something to do with his relationship to his family. Maybe that's the cause."
"If that's the case, all the more reason to help get rid of that cause. A talk with his family could very well be a start."
"But it could also be the start of something bad, couldn't it?"
Mom's small helping hand was easily waved away by my dad's forceful reasoning.
So in the end, I'm left struggling against him alone.
"Yes, maybe what you're saying is right, Dad, but it's all just words and lacks empathy."
"I assure you it's not just words. I'm also worried about Kitahara-kun."
"That's why I'll do everything in my power… I'll meet with his family and have a talk with them."
But Dad is far too strong today.
Instead of just being confidently correct like usual, he's willing to compromise and consider my feelings as well.
…Maybe he saw no other way to handle his daughter, who's every bit as stubborn as he is.
"He might simply be in a bad way because he lost sight of his family when he was younger. Shouldn't we at least ask his mother what she thinks?"
Dad's suggestion is one I've thought about many times before.
"We can just set things straight if there was simply a misunderstanding between them.
In other words, he's just as worried about him as I am.
"A lot means a lot. For one, it means trying to support him as a family, rather than putting the entire burden on you, Setsuna."
"The rest we'll figure out after having a proper talk with them. We need to properly think about what we'll do from here on out."
Unlike me, my dad doesn't lose his way. He doesn't hesitate to put those ideas into action.
"Setsuna, we'll help you. Let's all work together on this. Now listen to me, don't get too absorbed in him."
"You're still only a second-year at your job. You should have your plate full just looking out for yourself."
What if Haruki-kun only gets worse when his family gets involved?
What if the talk doesn't go well, and the distance between our families only grows larger, regardless of what we want?
He doesn't have a shred of unease over those possibilities. "What if I'm wrong?" doesn't even enter his mind.
"Was that… everything? I'll be on my way then."
If he makes the wrong decision and Haruki-kun… and our relationship breaks apart.
"I think you're correct, Dad… but correct is all you are."
He'll probably just call it "bad luck" or say that "it wasn't meant to be."
"If people's emotions could be swayed by logic, an illness like his wouldn't exist in the first place."
"But the way you're handling it isn't doing him any good."
"Yes it is! He'll get better! I'll make Haruki-kun return to his old self no matter what!"
I couldn't possibly accept an option so slow, deliberate and high-risk.
That's why, as unfair as it is, I try to defeat him through strength in numbers.
"Right, Mom? Have a bit more trust in me."
By dragging in my mom, who albeit reservedly, has taken my side until now.
"I think that… letting Setsuna do things her own way just a little bit longer… wouldn't be a problem."
And I hit the nail on the head.
"We still don't know if talking to his parents is what Kitahara-san wants."
"It's not possible right now. Haruki-kun can't make that kind of decision yet, and I don't want to force him to either."
"However, if he's to become part of our family, we need to get this out of the way sooner or later."
"I think… just this once, I disagree with you a little, Honey."
"What do you disagree on? Aren't you worried about Setsuna?"
"Of course, Setsuna's well-being is the most important thing for me too."
"Come on, I'm perfectly fine. Dad's just a worrywart."
"But what I'm trying to say is not that… I really don't want to be saying this, but…"
I thought I hit the nail on the head…
"If perhaps, something were to happen between them, and… they break up as a result…"
That's why for a good few seconds, I didn't fully understand what Mom was trying to say.
"Then perhaps it'd be better if… we weren't on speaking terms with his family…"
It came as a complete shock.
I thought she was on my side. I thought she'd take my side over Dad's.
Yet the words my mom just uttered…
"Setsuna, listen to me. This is something worth thinking about even if Kitahara-san wasn't ill."
She interrupted my dad's proposal, just like I wanted her to.
But it wasn't at all because she thought that I was right, or that Dad was wrong.
She simply had her own reason.
I'm afraid that something bad will happen if his family interferes.
But what she's worried about is the family ties we'll be stuck with after we break up.
"You're only 24, after all. A single failed relationship wouldn't prevent you from starting again with someon…"
"I won't ever fail! I'll never find someone new! I'll become happy with him and no one else!"
My thoughts turn blank, my vision turns pitch black, and the back of my neck feels scorching hot.
"Why? Why would you say things like that now of all times, Mom!?"
The cold, sharp sting I'm feeling doesn't come from Dad's orders or warnings, but from Mom's support and advice.
"Leave me alone! Mom put you up to this anyway, didn't she?"
"What, are you gonna walk into the pouring rain without an umbrella? Come on, take this with you."
The very moment I left the house in a fit of rage, the ceaseless rain mercilessly poured down on me.
Deeming it a lost cause, I thought about going back… Only then realizing that I had left in my slippers.
I take the umbrella without looking him in the eye, and then proceed to pull out a pair of rain boots from the shoe rack.
"She's starting to wonder whether something bad happened between you and Kitahara-san.
I'm so glad our eyes aren't meeting. I'm so glad he can't see the expression on my face.
"She's beginning to wonder whether the true cause of Kitahara-san's illness is related to that…"
"…Not at all. Nothing bad happened, so it's not the cause."
"Of course… We've always been in love with each other. Past, present, and future!"
"…No point telling your little brother that. It just makes me feel uncomfortable."
"It's your fault for bringing it up."
I keep telling my family that there are no problems, so why do they insist on being so worried all the time?
"Hey, Nee-chan. Do you actually plan on marrying Kitahara-san?"
"Why do you have to say that now? First Mom, and now you, Takahiro…"
And why are they so intent on staying suspicious of everyone outside the family?
"Both of you! Until just recently, you both treated him like family, didn't you!?"
Until half a year ago, he was unquestionably a part of the family.
And that was such a joyous thing for him.
He used to tell me that when we were snuggling, with an embarrassed smile on his face.
"It's not like I hate him now or anything. But if things go on like this, Nee-chan, you'll…"
So why did things turn out like this…?
"It's okay… Haruki-kun will get better in no time. Everything will return to normal, both Haruki-kun and our family."
"But I haven't seen any change in the past four months."
"Then you were lying when you said he'd get better in no time."
"…! Why do you have to grasp at straws like that!?"
"Ah no, I'm sorry. It's just that… I feel you're getting the short end of the stick here, Nee-chan. I don't like how this is playing out."
"If you really think so, then you should stay quiet and support me. Isn't that what family is all about?"
"This is an important time for me right now. Mom and dad don't understand that at all."
Dad has demoted him from "family member" to "potential family member." Mom has started to entertain the thought of us breaking up.
"This is precisely the time I have to support him, and I need to do it slowly and carefully."
Am I the only one left still on Haruki-kun's side, I wonder?
"What is it? Was anything I said wrong?"
"I don't think it's wrong, but… Are you really okay with this, Nee-chan? The way you're describing it…"
"'I have to support him.' It sounds like you're doing it against your will."
"Up until now, you always said 'I want to support him.'"
"I've got nothing to do with this, so I can't act like I know everything, but…"
What is it that I'm beginning to lose in my speech?
"You're always super absorbed in Kitahara-san and everything, but be careful this time, okay? Don't let him drag you down."
"If you really think so, you could at least be more considerate about it! That goes for dad, mom, and you too, Takahiro!"
"No, it's okay… I realize I'm out of line here."
"I'm heading out. I won't return home today."
If so, what is it that's beginning to stain my speech?
Is it fatigue? A sense of obligation? Weakness?
I was supposed to… stop telling myself to hang in there…
"Apparently it's going to be like this the whole weekend. That's what the weather report said."
"Come to think of it, Japan should be entering its rainy season right about now."
"You still don't like talking about Japan?"
There's my mom, who still has lingering affection for Japan, and then there's me, who's abandoned even the notion of remembering Japan.
Whenever the topic of that country comes up, we lose sight of our conversation.
"If you look out the window, there's a single large tree, right?"
"When that tree loses all of its leaves, I'll be…"
"It's the beginning of summer and it's raining. That thing will only grow more leaves for a good while."
"It'll be fine until winter, at least."
Despite all that, mom keeps fighting on when she's spending time with me, continuing to play the role of "Touma Youko" as she always has.
But when mom does that, even I can clearly tell that she's fighting.
The enjoyable period at the start of every visit has been getting shorter and shorter.
She's lost weight. She's eating less. Day by day, I notice her arms and legs grow thinner.
Day by day, she gets slightly paler. Even the shine in her hair and skin have gone away.
…And above all, she's started to neglect even hiding that fact.
"You know about the safebox furthest inside the living room closet, right?"
"We do. Anyway, the key to that safe is inside the drawer of the buddhist altar."
"You came all the way to Vienna to pray to Buddha…?
Wait, we have a buddhist altar?"
"You were supposed to laugh, you know."
"It's actually in the top drawer next to my bed."
"Anyway, once you've opened the safe using that key, you'll find the key to a bank vault…"
"But the bank vault requires a PIN on top of the key. I'll tell you the code now so listen properly. Don't ever think of writing it down; memorize it."
"Just forget about it. It sounds like a pain."
"Memorize it. You'll need it when the time comes."
"I told you, I have no interest in property or entitlements. You already know that, Mom."
"Well, now's the time to start getting interested. You'll inherit Touma Youko Office someday… Or well, it'll be Touma Kazusa Office by then, I guess."
"I don't really need it. If I ever lose the ability to play the piano, I'll just drop dead by the roadside or something. I wouldn't really mind a life like that."
"You can't. You absolutely can't! Even if you end up alone, you absolutely must live a happy life."
"Money can't buy happiness. You should know that better than anyone, Mom…"
"Perhaps that's true, but no one drops dead by the roadside out of happiness. So please listen to me."
And even once the enjoyable period at the start is over, Mom remains talkative.
She's clearly tearing away at her body, her energy, in an attempt to feign indifference, but it's all too obvious.
A time unlike anything that has come before, one filled with terrible sadness for meーI'm talking with my mom, but I'm not enjoying it at all.
She's not making fun of me anymore. She's not avoiding confrontations anymore.
She's been talking more and more about her regrets, worries and memories.
It's almost as if the person I'm talking to has ceased to be Touma Youko…
"Do you want to hear about your dad?"
"But if I were to… If you were to end up all alone in this world…"
"No matter what my future holds in store, my one and only parent is Touma Youko."
I also feel somewhat guilty over being the sole descendant of Touma Youko, for that matter.
"So just stop with these what-if talks. I've said this a hundred times already, but I don't regret anything, and I don't hate or resent you at all, Mom."
"I'm sorry, Kazusa… for not being able to leave anything for you…! Haah……gh…!"
Mom's weeping breaks the silence of the hospital room, resounding amidst the pitter-patter of the rain outside.
I didn't say that out of embarrassment. I really wanted her to stop.
Because this is just too painful.
Seeing the confident and easygoing person who was my mom… slowly break apart.
Whether she's still alive or not, the very existence that is Touma Youko is already on the path to a slow death.
Touma Youko was always an arrogant goddess in my eyes. She was a selfish mother. She was an insurmountable wall of a rival.
But the person in front of me right now is just a normal person. A calm old woman trying to give guidance to the young.
This isn't the Touma Youko I, or the world, has come to desire…
"Hey, Mom. Hurry up and get discharged from this place…"
So, unable to handle this atmosphere any longer, I make an unreasonable demand of someone who's supposed to be weaker than me.
"Then I'll let you hear me playing the piano. I've gotten much better since my last concert, you know?
Because I'm still a little kid chasing her mother's shadow. It's not something I can move on from at the drop of a hat.
"What do you prefer? Beethoven? Schubert? Mozart? I'll play any request you have."
"So please, please… stop making me so sad…"
With slightly tearful eyes, Mom looks up at me and mutters…
A piece so obscure that I imagine not even classical music enthusiasts can immediately recognize it.
The composer, the period, the original name; all unknown.
Even the name Cloture was given by those who, without evidence, said that the piece originated in France.
The Germans have a completely different name for itーDie andere Seite des Glucksーand claim that their country is the true origin.
And I'm familiar with both names.
"It's the first piece I ever played here in Europe… It's the piece I've played more than any other in my lifetime."
Because it's the song my mom knows better than any other… and more than anything…
It's a piano concertoーa performance that requires an accompanying orchestra.
In other words, I'd have to either hold a concert of my own, or hire an orchestra…
It's not a piece I can play by myself. It's something that requires the help of many others.
"…That's how it is. So can I count on you to join, Setsuna?"
"Jeez, this is our once-a-month girls' night out. Try focusing on having fun with us instead of letting your mind wander off."
"N-No, I'm fine. Sorry, let me hear what you said one more time."
When Tomo started talking to me, the hand of the clock was pointing exactly at 9 PM.
"Like I said, it's about the live performance! They're doing a live performance in October for the 10 year anniversary of Troy."
Today is our usual once-a-month girls' night out.
Takeya-kun should be with him in my stead right about now. In other words, it's the day I can finally enjoy myself without having to worry about anything.
"Right, it's an all-night showing of all the regulars. It'll start Saturday night and will continue until everyone's performed.
"How should I put it… Seems like they're pretty loose with time, huh."
"Haha, that's just like Troy. Everyone gets along so well there. They don't seem to have any rivalries at all."
"It'll begin at 6 PM on the first Saturday of October. You'll come, right?"
"Hmm, I don't think I can handle the entire night. I guess I'll just check out the performers that I know. I really hope they come early on."
"No, you won't be checking it out… You'll be the one performing, Setsuna."
Our outings like these are supposed to be breathers from everyday stress, yet now, it's beginning to weigh heavily on me.
"I said 'all the regulars,' right? So obviously Routes will perform. In other words, our beloved songstress SETSUNA will perform too!"
"Ah, that sounds great. I haven't heard Setsuna sing in so long. I look forward to hearing it."
"Eh? B-But… I'm just a backup singer."
"The only person who thinks that way is you, Setsuna.
In fact, the members have all asked me to convince you to come."
On top of that, Tomo is bringing up something way heavier than usual…
"Routes is really popular so they might appear last. It's entirely possible you'll have to stay the entire night."
"Ah… In that case, I'll have to call it off. I can't go."
"It's on the weekend, so what's the problem? I'll convince your parents to let you go."
"…The weekend is an even worse time for me. Tomo, you know that, right?"
"But it's just a single day, and it's the anniversary of Troy. They've helped you out more than once in the past."
"But I'll have to rehearse, right? I'll be forced to take countless days off, right?"
"Just one or two days should be enough. You can rehearse the rest during karaoke."
The way Tomo is in high spirits like always… Today, it feels painful somehow.
"Oh, right! You can even invite Kitahara-san if you want. He might actually get a bit better if he sees you sing."
"No way! There's no way I could allow Haruki-kun to be in a crowded place."
Yes, this girl never changes, ever staying at her own pace.
I'm aware of that. I'm fully aware of that, but…
"You don't have to be so angry, Setsuna. She just didn't know about that."
"I-I'm not angry… I just wanted her to understand. I just wanted her to understand Haruki-kun."
"W-Well, you know how I am. Sometimes I get too pushy and people get annoyed with me."
Why won't she change for my sake…?
Whose fault is it that I'm feeling this way?
"Still, you should enjoy yourself, Setsuna. Have enough fun for both you and Kitahara-san."
"Exactly! You said it yourself. Don't you remember?"
"That unless I enjoy my own life to the fullest, I can't put a smile on his face."
"You can't stay this way… You'll both go under if you continue like this…"
Thinking back at those words, they lack so much understanding and delicacy that it almost feels like someone else said them.
"I understand that you want to take on all his suffering, but he's not gonna get better just because you suffer yourself, Setsuna.
"There's a time and place for being so easygoing!"
The person who said those words… I doubt I could be friends with them…
"You wouldn't understand, Tomo! No one could possibly understand!"
"That's enough. Let's call it a day."
"It's okay, you can go to Haruki's place. I noticed you were looking anxiously at the clock anyway."
The rainy season ended, and the true summer arrived.
The sky soaring high above, deep in blue. The raging sun so powerful, as if its true strength has finally been unveiled to us.
The gloomy dimness of my own world refuses to be chased away.
"And here I was wondering why you guys called me back so early. Who would've thought it was for something like this."
"Yeah, I'm sorry. She's just too much for me to handle alone."
"I… I… made Setsuna angry again…! Uaaaaah…"
"You said exactly what you had to. You wouldn't be Yanagihara Tomo if you hadn't."
"Yes, really. For once, Setsuna is the one in the wrong. I know you did the right thing."
"But… What's the point of being right if Setsuna won't listen to me? Uuuaah… hah… uuu…"
"She'll realize in time, so please… I said this before, but… don't ever stop being Setsuna's ally."
"…You guys better make this your treat, got it? Least you could do for making me drink this lousy booze."
"I see, so that's how it was…"
"Well, so what's actually going on with Haruki's condition?"
"Nothing's changed. Sometimes he sleeps through entire days, but it's not like he's any less asleep when he's awake."
"Though I suppose he doesn't seem to be about to do anything stupid on impulse either, so I guess things are stable for now."
"I imagine that for Setsuna, Haruki not changing is the very thing that is putting pressure on her."
"Perhaps she's beginning to think that she's not of any help to him; that perhaps she's just getting in his way."
"But wasn't she the one who told us? That things like these take time, so we have to look at the big picture."
"She was probably still hoping for some results. Anything that would show that Haruki has gotten at least a little bit better."
"And that hope slowly, slowly turned into despair, and it began to wear away at her heart…"
"Not good signs at all. That's obviously true for Haruki, but it goes doubly so for Setsuna."
"I hate to admit it, but I don't have the answer to that right now. There's a limit to what the two of us can do for them."
"Maybe they'll have to sort it out among themselves in the end. Haruki, Setsuna, and…"
"Even if Haruki gets better as a result, it'll be the end of those two."
"Perhaps… that'll be the right time to cross that bridge."
"Perhaps some people aren't destined to be together, incompatible even, no matter how much they love each other."
"Aaah, and here I was all cheery over my bonus paycheck, but now the mood is completely spoiled. Whaddya think? Want another round of drinks?"
"Before we get to that… we'll have to take care of this chick."
"Well… I suppose someone has to get her home safely."
"You're saying I get to take her home?"
"Then how about we call it a day and you carry her back? Or would you rather we all left together, the three of us, and send her home first?"
"Oh, unusual for you to answer so quickly."
"Physical labor is obviously the man's job."
"Those are some ancient values you've got there. Besides, you've got many times the horsepower I do."
"How rude… Besides, we can't go for another round of drinks if we separate here."
"Wow, you've gotten a lot better at hanging out."
"Does that mean we'll have a 'grown-up hang out' later?"
"Stop being stupid and help Tomo already. I'll handle the bill."
Heey, Tomo, how about at least walking to the taxi?"
"…It's about time you grew up as well."
"Thank you for your call. This is the Japanese branch of Touma Youko Office PLC."
"I sincerely apologize, but company operations are currently under a temporary hiatus."
"If you have urgent business, please contact the European branch of Touma Youko Office. The number to them is…"
"Just how long is Miyoko's vacation, exactly…?"
The call might have only lasted for a few seconds, but just imagining the fee for international calls to Japan makes my head hurt.
This is the tenth time since I first called her, and I've been greeted by the answering machine the entire month.
…Not to say that wasn't obvious after the third call.
It's been a month since Mom managed to bring herself to ask for that song…
Day in and day out, I've been searching for any orchestra willing to play that piece with me.
In fact, it's probably because I'm the one doing the searching that I'm struggling to find anyone.
At first, I used the time between my lessons to check the phone book for all orchestras from A to Z. After the third orchestra I tried to negotiate with…
If anything, it's only tarnished the reputation of Touma Youko Office further, because my negotiation skills are next to none.
How can everyone else carry conversations so smoothly without even seeing the person on the other line? That's a concept completely foreign to me.
After that, I resorted to emails.
It took me three days to get the computer running. Getting an email address and functioning internet took another three.
After nearly ten days worth of effort, the resulting message was sent to every single orchestra in the phone book, whose email addresses I found on the web.
About the pay, about the scheduling, about the venue…
Apparently, the traditional Japanese custom of "we'll cross that bridge when we get there" doesn't work on westerners.
After seeing me run around like a headless chicken for nearly half a month, the headquarters of our European branch just couldn't bear to watch any longer.
"Yeah, and about what I needed. Ah, yes, right… Did you find them?"
Unfortunately though… Emma Bergen was more akin to a mere assistant to my mom back in the day. She didn't have the discretion nor knowledge that Miyoko had.
That's why the negotiations are still struggling. Currently, the number of orchestras who've even come to the negotiating table are…
"Yes, yes… Thank you. Call me if anything new comes up."
This was a bitter pill to swallow.
I've allowed myself to completely misunderstand my value as a pianist, all thanks to that concert in Japan.
The name of the promising pianist "Touma Kazusa" doesn't mean anything here. It hasn't caught on at all.
The label of "Touma Youko's daughter" doesn't get me anywhere either.
People in this part of the world don't care for marketing slogans like that when it comes to music. It's a complete meritocracy.
At my wits' absolute end, I finally decided to dirty my hands through my forbidden last resort.
It's the means I hated most of all.
"That's right, the chief editor at Ensemble… I'm sure I had his business card."
I could sign a contract with a Japanese orchestra through the Japanese branch, invite them to Vienna, and hold an all-Japanese concert…
"…! What am I even saying? That's Kaiousha, isn't it…?"
I felt so cornered that I found no other choice but to rely on something that would probably end in failure… No, it would definitely end in failure.
But whatever the means, I must play Cloture for my mom.
Because there's no telling if this might be…
Just as I was getting lost in my thoughts, a pop-up appeared on my computer screen reading "new mail."
Checking the address, I noticed it was from the very first orchestra I sent a request to, but never got any response from.
But any hope I had as I opened the mail was quickly gone when I read its contents.
The writing was polite, but you could immediately tell it was a refusal.
Yes, and underneath the polite refusal…
There was a letter of introduction to a different orchestra.
Mom froze in place the moment she heard the name of that orchestra.
"I'll do it. That's what you want, right?"
"Yeah but, this is Franz we're talking about… You hate his guts."
A French conductor working out of Paris.
He's in his mid 30s. Even amongst the fierce competition that is typical of France, his skills are well attested to.
Any orchestra he commands always fills every seat at their concerts, and he's booked solid until next year.
His status and fame is international. A man of his stature should have no time for some upstart asian pianist like Touma Kazusa.
"I said I'll do it, so I will… But I still insist on the "Don't ever touch me" clause at the top of the contract."
…And he was once my mom's illicit lover.
And he also happens to be a bastard who tried to make advances on me in the past.
The only potential setback in our contract is this one issue.
"Well, you probably don't have to worry about that. That man turns into a different person when he's performing."
"…I can trust you on this, right?"
"Yes, no doubt about it. Besides, he could never lay his hands on you this time. After all, the one who set this whole thing up is probably…"
"No, forget it. More importantly, when's the concert?"
"That's the only time their schedule is open. Apparently they had a big spat with a sponsor from New York and they had to cancel."
The very fact that the Franz Dubre Orchestra could even find an opening within the year is a miracle in and of itself.
That's what Emma told me after three minutes of silence on the phone.
"Very well, I'll make sure to survive until then. Come hell or high water."
"…Yeah, you go ahead and do that. I'll show you the best concerto you've ever heard."
At any rate, there's only two months left.
I'll have to somehow master Cloture before then.
I'll make sure that my efforts will reach her.
I'll make it in time, no matter what…
"Thank you… old man. Sorry if I end up passing on before you do."
Summer continues, and the heat grows only more powerful.
So powerful that one could forget all about how blue the sky is, or how high it soars above us.
Sweat pouring out just by standing outside during the day, and discomfort no matter how many times I turn over in bed during the night.
Is that truly the only thing it has deprived me of?
"…What's the matter? Why would you cover your body head to toe in this scorching heat? You'll get a heatstroke like this."
"Don't you 'good morning' me! What time do you think it is? What about work?"
"Aah… Sorry, I forgot to tell you. I asked for sick leave yesterday night, so I'm off work today."
"Yeah, it started yesterday night. It's pretty heavy this month…"
"Oh, then you should've told us yesterday too. Now the breakfast's gone all cold."
"I'm sorry… but I don't need any today. You don't have to make lunch for me either."
"It's really bad… I don't have any appetite at all right now."
"I'm okay. I just have to make it through the day…"
"…Are you sure it's just your menstruation?"
"I am… but you really don't have to say it out loud."
"Give me a day and I'll be fine. I'll go to work tomorrow too, so just leave me alone for today."
"If you say so, I guess I'll believe you for today…"
"That's how it is, so good night."
"But if you feel there's anything wrong with your body… No, if you feel even the slightest bit unusual, you'll tell me right away, okay?"
There's no way I could tell her…
"Now then, good night. Mommy will be heading out today, but…"
"Off you go then. I'll be fine. I can handle this much."
If I ever did, she'd probably tell Dad.
And then Dad would get pointlessly worried about me.
"…Fine, but be a good girl, okay? Don't think about going to 'that place' again with the excuse that you suddenly got better. Not today of all days."
Then he'd never let me visit "that place" again.
After I've made sure Mom's gone downstairs, I finally crawl out of the blanket covering me.
My pajamas are so drenched in sweat it feels gross. How strange… Doesn't our air conditioner work?
Mom will notice when she does the laundry. I'll have to make sure to wash them myself when she's out.
Sweat was disgustingly pouring out of my entire body all night, non-stop.
Even now in the morning, it still hasn't stopped.
…In fact, it didn't even start last night. I've been like this every night the past few days.
I raise my body to get out of bed, only to immediately slump back.
I feel dizzy, my vision is blurry, and worst of all, I have no energy.
I always managed to get out of bed despite that until yesterday. I'd get dressed in the morning like always, and then head out for work.
…Though my performance at work was less than impressive.
What I told Mom about having the day off was of course a makeshift lie. The truth was that I simply couldn't get up.
What's going on? What's happening to me…?
No, this is plain and simple heat fatigue. I'll be back to normal after a good day's rest.
Because tomorrow is Friday. I just have to work one more day and it'll be the weekend… That's why… I'll be fine.
I'll be able to see him again then. I just have to hang in there one more day, and I'll get to see Haruki-kun again. He must be waiting for me.
That's the reason I can hang on…
"The train on Line 1 toward Onjuku will depart shortly. Please stay within the white lines."
The weekend I was so eagerly waiting for arrived… half a day later than usual.
Normally I'd head straight for his apartment after work on Friday. But right now, I'm heading there at 11 o'clock on Saturday.
Unsurprisingly, my family didn't allow me to visit him on Fridayーnot after having spent the entirety of Thursday bedridden.
So left without a choice, I spent the night resting at home.
I felt a lot better this morning thanks to that. My headache and sweating are all gone, but most importantly of all, I got a decent night's sleep.
So there's nothing to worry about anymore.
I almost forgot… I should do some groceries before I go to his apartment.
A week's worth of food, daily necessities… Oh, didn't he run out of laundry detergent last time?
Then when I've arrived at his place, I'll have to make something we can eat together. Then there's the laundry, cleaning and finally, dinner.
When all that's over with, I'd like to… chat with him, if possible.
About all the things I've done this week, and about how he's been the past week.
Speak, listen, and understand each other…
"The train on Line 1 is departing. The doors are closing. Please be careful."
Yeah, the day will go something like that.
Then we'll be able to spend much more time together.
It'll mark the start of a period so full of joy, that we'll forget all about work and the scorching heat of summer.
Just thinking about it makes my heart leap.
I thought my heart was going to leap, yet…
My breath feels heavy. My sweating won't stop.
How strange… I felt fine this morning.
I had so much energy that I was easily able to shake Mom off when she tried to stop me by the doorstep.
I thought the unceasing sweat pouring out of me as I walked toward the station was simply the result of the terrible heat outside.
I thought it'd all go away once I reached the shade of the station… or once I got on the train with its many air conditioners.
But right now, I can't even board the train that I'll be getting off a single station later.
I tried to stand up when the train came, but my entire body became overwhelmed with this gross, numbing sensation.
As my entire body was chained to the bench, it was only in my thoughts that I kept frantically yelling "move, move!"
Huh, what's going on? Did I misunderstand something?
My unceasing sweat, my heavy breath, my fear of crowds, my inability to board the train…
My body trying to reject the destination I'm heading to?
The unthinkable that flashed through my mind summoned a wave of nausea.
Because there's just no way that could possibly be. This is what I've wanted this entire week. Being with Haruki-kun is my happiness.
Seeing his sleeping face, engraving the few words he mutters in my heart, gazing at his ever so slightly changing expressions.
But is all of that… just my own ego talking?
Haruki-kun always looks so pained when I'm around him.
His sleeping face is always full of anguish, his words only hurt himself, and his expressions are only that of sadness.
And I'm sitting beside him every time, gazing at his despair.
I get it now… How could he possibly get better when he's visited by the angel of death every week?
Is that why God is trying to distance me from him? Because that's the best way to keep his heart at ease? Have I become nothing but a burden to him…?
Is that how He's protecting him?
This is all wrong… Thinking about it that way is nothing but an ugly excuse.
It's a stupid justification for the fact that my body isn't as strong as my feelings.
Besides, what will I do once I get there…?
Even if I stay by his side, he won't whisper words of love to me. He won't embrace me. That place isn't where I belong…
What is unconditional love, I wonder…
Maybe you're the only one who knows after all…
Beyond the front door is the same silence as always.
The only sound is that of my own rather loud voice.
"Ah, the air conditioner feels so good! I never want to go outside again."
However, the somewhat chilly air filling the room slowly reveals the dweller inside.
"It's so darn hot outside. I just can't stand it."
Today, that dweller is sitting in front of the computer on the dining table.
I take a glance at his face and see it's somewhat pale, but not completely white. It could be much worse.
Yeah, he might be feeling pretty well today.
"What do you want for lunch? It's a bit late, so is it okay if I make some Somen noodles? Or would you rather have something more filling?"
"I won't be as motivated if you're fine either way. Well, whatever. Let's go with a light lunch and a filling dinner then, okay?
"Oh, right! Since we already have pork, let's add it to the noodles cold… Yeah, that sounds great!"
"Ah, but then that means we'll have meat for both lunch and dinner. Perhaps I should make something different for dinner then."
"What do you think, Haruki-kun? Do you want…"
Aah, I'm sorry, I couldn't make it yesterday. I had to work overtime the whole week so… No, what I meant to say was… work was just piling up a little."
"No, that's not what I'm asking about…"
"It'll be done right away. I'm sorry, but can you wait for a bit?"
I messed up… I wasn't supposed to show off how busy I am, because that'll just alienate him.
I can't allow myself to get carried away, no matter how excited I am.
"I ate a bit too much for breakfast this morning. Sorry, but could you finish the rest, Haruki-kun?"
"I'm not sure if I can eat all of this…"
"You can leave some of it. The leftovers can go in the soup we'll have for dinner. Ahaha…"
"No, I'll eat it. But I feel like I'll gain weight if I eat that much, since I barely move as it is."
"Now that you mention it! Wanna go for a walk after lunch as exercise? We don't have to go further than the nearby park."
"A walk, huh… Yeah, I don't mind."
"Ah, but… You'll probably get a heat stroke if you suddenly go outside in this weather. Sorry, I take back what I said."
What a simple mistake. What am I even talking about, going outside…?
"Yes, I'm managing to wake up properly in the mornings now, so maybe my sleep pattern is stabilizing."
"I see, I see… Then you're close to returning to work now!"
The words Haruki-kun spoke to me were amazing news.
The results of last week's medical diagnosis were unexpectedly good, and the physician even reduced his amount of medication.
"Well, there've been many ups and downs until now, so I don't know if I can return to work that easily."
"No, I know you'll manage this time! Everything will return to how it used to be…!"
I'm so glad… I'm so glad he's getting better so soon.
Haruki-kun will get better soon. Everyone will be freed from the burdens and the anguish.
"Hey, Setsuna? Want to come over here and talk?"
"Hm, I'm okay. I'm not done vacuuming yet."
"You've been working nonstop since you came here. Take a break for once."
"I got to hear the most amazing news today, so I simply can't relax without working."
Working so hard that I barely have time to think about anything else is better for me right now.
"Hey, what should we do for summer break?"
"A trip would of course still be too early for you, but you can still go outside a little in your current state, right?"
Once the laundry and the cleaning was done, I started cleaning the bathroom. Then I prepared dinner while Haruki-kun was taking a bath.
"We could go to the library you always visit. Then we could go for a tiny bit of shopping… go watch a movie…"
And then, it was finally nighttime.
"But we'll still have to avoid big crowds, though. Actually, what kind of shopping district doesn't have big crowds? Hahahaha."
…Somehow, we've made it through the day without incident.
"Even so I still look forward to it. We haven't gotten to spend a whole week together since university, on the summer break of our fourth year."
Today was fun, and so joyous.
"Although, even in university you'd keep finding reasons to not be with me, be it your graduation thesis, or your part-time job!"
He showed signs of improvement. He talked to me far more than usual. He ate all of the food I made for him.
"You were so stubborn. At times I'd even begin to wonder if you were still trying to avoid me or something… haha."
And as a natural result, I also found myself talking more, getting more excited.
"Besides, the summer before that was… Oh right, we weren't supposed to talk about that anymore! Sorry."
It's only natural for things to end up this way. Today has after all been full of happiness…
There was real force in that voice, perhaps even the same kind of force I hadn't heard from him in half a year.
"Setsuna… I know it's too late, but I want to thank you again. Thank you so much for all the time you've spent taking care of me."
Even the words that followed after that had that same strength, kindness and softness to them.
"O-Oh jeez, what's the matter? There's no need to be so formal, I only did what's natural… being your girlfriend and all."
That hope makes my heart pound even harder.
"It wasn't natural… It wasn't natural at all. Because I betrayed you, Setsuna. I betrayed and ran away from you, and then I broke down at the very end…"
"Did you now…? I seem to have completely forgotten."
"Despite that you devoted yourself to me, Setsuna."
"That was the only choice I had, because I…"
Can I finally say it now? Will he accept it if I do?
"If you weren't there for me, Setsuna… I would've ran away from everything, and in the end there'd be nowhere left to run away to.
"I'm going to be indebted to you for the rest of my life. I'm really sorry."
My efforts have finally been rewarded…
I did it, I did it, I did it!
"It's okay… That will all resolve itself in time. Our future together still has such a long road ahead of it, after all."
My heartbeat is soaring. My body feels warm. My breath is heavy…
With this, I no longer… I no longer have to…
"So please, Setsuna… calm down and listen to my request."
"Go home now. You don't have to come tomorrow, or during the summer break either."
A bolt out of the blue, befitting the current season.
"I'm sorry that these cruel words are all that I can offer you."
"I'm sorry… I'm so sorry, Setsuna… Forgive me for being so weak…!"
What's going on? What is this?
Why? But why? Why, why, why?
"Forgive me, forgive me…! Uua… uu… aah…!"
What is this? Haruki-kun hasn't gotten better even in the slightest…
"The truth is, I wanted to send you home the moment you arrived here."
Wasn't he supposed to have fully recovered? Weren't my efforts supposed to have been finally rewarded?
"But I kept quiet about it until now. I'm sorry for being such a spineless coward."
Now that he's gotten better, he's just going to cast me aside?
No, it's all wrong… I know better than anyone that he isn't that kind of person.
Could it be that… he's abandoning me because I'm terrible enough to make those kinds of assumptions of him?
"Why? Why would you…? What is it about me you don't like!?"
Is that why it won't work out? Will my feelings never reach him?
"What's wrong with me? I'll fix it… I'll change for you… So please don't say things like that…!"
My heartbeat is soaring. My body feels warm. My breath is heavy…
My body has gone numb and it refuses to move. My throat feels so terribly dry, yet the desire to vomit overwhelms me.
And right after… Haruki-kun softly touches my forehead.
"That you were beginning to break down too, Setsuna…"
It's not just my forehead he's touching, but the pouring sweat as well…
Haruki-kun turns off the faucet I left running, then bends down to pick up the broken pieces of the plate I dropped on the floor.
"It's getting harder for you to wake up in the mornings, isn't it?
"That's because… you know, I got low blood pressure."
But I remain unable to help him do any of that, only standing there, staring at where his eyes used to be before he bent down.
"Sometimes you notice that you can't stop sweating, and it suddenly hurts to breathe, doesn't it?"
"Only because it's summer. It's really hot outside…"
"Your feet stop moving. You find yourself unable to move forward."
I thought I drove it away, but the desire to vomit is now stronger than ever.
"And in order to hide that fact, you force yourself to keep your spirits up. You force yourself to act cheerful."
"And as you are playing the role of your usual self, you fail to realize that you're nothing like your usual self."
"Setsuna, you always took on the opposite demeanor as me. You'd act strong and cheerful when I was feeling down, and you'd tread carefully when I was cheerful."
"Thinking back now, I've come to realize that your demeanor was something you forced upon yourself in desperation, to put my heart at ease."
My shallow plan born out of desperation could never have worked on someone as clever as him.
Today, I got caught up in the idea that he was getting better, so I took my own spirits to an exaggerated height.
There's no way he wouldn't notice…
"I realized that maybe, you were throwing all your energy into deceiving yourself today, Setsuna. That you felt so cornered that you had no other choice…"
"No, that's not true… You're just misunderstanding things…"
"I'm confident that I know your current self better than you do yourself, Setsuna."
"Why!? Haruki-kun, what could you possibly know about me…!?"
"How couldn't I know…? How could I possibly not notice the state you're in right now, Setsuna…?"
At that moment, I understood what Haruki-kun was trying to tell me better than he did himself.
"Because right now, Setsuna… you're just like I was half a year ago."
And everything I knew he would say, he engraved in my mind word for word.
"Worse still, I got nothing less than I deserved, but you've done nothing wrong, Setsuna. You only got dragged into this because of me."
Along with words that are hurting himselfーwords that I never wanted to hear.
He was finally feeling better. He was finally nearing his recovery, yet…
I ended up making a mess of it all. This is all my fault.
"So just go home, Setsuna… and take proper care of yourself."
Does… Does it mean then, that…
Regardless if I'm by his side or far apart… I'll remain nothing but a burden to him?
"You can still make it in time. If you go right now, you can avoid turning out like me."
"B-But, but… What'll happen to you then, Haruki-kun…?"
"I'll be… fine. I told you I'm getting better, didn't I?"
"But you're crying right now! You're breaking apart because of me again!"
"It's only for a little bit… I'll recover after a good rest."
"That won't do… Even the doctor said so! He said the recovery period is the most dangerous of all."
"The doctor also said this… 'The time one's starting to get sick is the most important time to pay attention.'"
"Hey, Setsuna… I'm begging you, listen to me."
His tearful voice stirs up my own tears, and an overwhelming desire to cling to him, crying and screaming, overtakes me.
"If you go about this the wrong way now, you'll never be able to undo it."
But I can't cry nor scream. Neither can I cling to him.
I'd break him if I did. Just as I thought, I'd be nothing but a burden to him, an angel of death.
"I'll say it as many times as it takes, Setsuna."
Mustering up whatever courage remains in his broken self, Haruki-kun… cuts me away from him.
He's choosing to enter hell by himself, so that he won't have to bring me down with him.
"And don't come back here for a while."
Without hesitation, he's choosing to protect me without any regard for the fact that he's fallen apart.
Even though he was prepared to bring Kazusa down to hell with him.
"…You're asking me what went wrong? Hm, I don't even feel like telling you."
"If I had to say, I suppose it's the whole thing."
"You're completely useless… I heard you were the peerless up and coming pianist, young and full of promise, but this is so far from what I expected."
"Did you think you'd have it easy here in Paris because you succeeded back home? You think we're that easy to please?"
"You probably just invited a bunch of relatives to your faux-piano concert, and then got the wrong idea when they gave you massive applause."
"I've had enough! It's pointless to continue any further."
"Now I finally understand why Youko never allowed you to play concerto."
"I've never seen a pianist this self-absorbed. Our orchestra has no need for you."
I collapsed straight on the bed the moment I got out of the shower, too mentally and physically exhausted to even wipe down my body.
I lie down on it with my head facing down, not even caring about the water dripping down from my hair and skin to my sheets.
"I'll quit for sure! But first I have to beat the shit out of him."
With a great concert ahead, one I was looking so forward to, that was the impression I had of the first rehearsal.
It's been a week since I arrived in Paris…
Delay after delay on their part forced me to practice by myself until yesterday.
I left my mom in Vienna full of determination that I was going to succeed in Paris, but that hope was slashed before I even got the chance to play.
During those days, when there wasn't even a point to me being in Paris, the only thing that went up was my level of stress.
And today, when my long awaited meeting with the orchestra finally arrived…
Yet the three hour long rehearsal was made up of only me and the violinists.
What I got to hear was not the performance of an orchestra, but a storm of verbal abuse from the creepy conductor Franz or whatever his name was.
I didn't make a single mistake. In fact, it's not even a piece that requires that much skill.
But he still refused to give me a single thumbs up.
Thanks to that, we never made it to the end of the piece. Hell, we didn't even make it past the first measure.
And to make matters even worse…
"Emma-san? It's Kazusa speaking… How has Mom been since then?"
Mom hasn't been feeling well the past three days.
"I see… and no visitors allowed like before?"
I asked Emma-san to give Mom a visit every now and then in my place, but apparently no one's been allowed in since she got worse.
"What did the doctor say? …Yes, yes, I see."
There's nothing concrete about what is happening yet, but we do know that her condition is deteriorating, and that she's not been eating well.
The only good news, or any news at all, was the message one of the nurses passed on to Emma-san.
"…Thank you. I'll call you tomorrow then."
"Don't come back to Vienna until the concert is over, no matter what."
"Make sure you make Cloture a success."
"A normal success won't do either. You'll have to deliver a performance so legendary it will send all European media into a craze."
Traces of my mom's strength still remained in those sentences.
But I still would've liked to talk to her.
It doesn't matter how weak my mom looks. Even if I'll feel like crying at the sight of the state she's in, I won't complain.
I want to talk to you, Mom…
"What the hell is up with that bastard!? He's not even seeing me as a human being, let alone a woman!"
"I told you, didn't I? That man turns into a different person when he's performing."
"He ignored thirty other people for a full three hours! Everyone was in the back playing cards…"
"Oh that's a normal sight for his orchestra. He only picks on the newcomers."
"I'm amazed anyone's willing to follow his lead…"
"He's a genius when it comes to conducting, after all. I mean, I discovered his talent myself."
"Genius or not, his personality is rotten. I've never had my piano performance dissed like that in my entire life."
"I sometimes say things like 'this is kinda boring' too, don't I?"
"This is completely different from your dry criticism, Mom. He's stubborn, unrelenting and condescending. He nitpicks everything from my personality to my life…"
"Oh, I can just imagine the scene… I wish I was there to see it."
"I'll end up hating the piano at this rate…"
"Huh? Does that mean you enjoy playing the piano? I always thought you only kept at it to get 'his' attention…"
For some reason, living in the Paris Integral Hotel suite reminds me of spending time with my mom.
I see… half a year ago in that country, the place my mom and I stayed in was also like this…
The performance that disgusting conductor called a "faux-concert."
Come to think of it, my motivation right now isn't all that different from then.
Is salvaging a small bit of hope from misery the only thing I am capable of? Misery born of the world's rejection of me.
Let's say… the upcoming concert becomes a success. Will that save Mom?
Will my performance give her the hope she needs to live a long life?
Or will my performance make her let go, no longer having any lingering regrets left…
Can I say for certain that Cloture isn't the requiem Mom is waiting for?
Should I play it with all my might despite that? Should I do away with her lingering regrets? Should I give her everything I can give her?
…As if. Even thinking about it is nothing but arrogance.
Because if things continue at this rate, I can't imagine the concert going even slightly well.
But what am I supposed to do about that…? I can't even complain to her outside of my own thoughts anymore.
Because the strong, light-hearted and all-accepting mom I know… now only exists in my own thoughts.
The real mom has changed. She cries all the time, and she reminisces about the past like an old woman… She's turned weak, like a regular person.
Will she ever return to her old self, I wonder…
Whenever I told old man Fluegel about mom, our views on her always clashed.
"The Youko you know, Kazusa, and the Youko I know are very different people."
"The Youko I knew was full of ambition, jealousy and strife. She was inexperienced, immature, rough and young enough to put you to shame, Kazusa."
"It was that personality thatーafter growing in both age and experienceーturned into the whimsical Youko we know today."
"So if you ask me, the Youko you take for granted is one that has already changed."
I realized something when he told me that. Even the mom I've taken for granted is really two different people.
The first Touma Youko was someone who truly didn't care about me when I was a child.
Someone who was completely uninterested in anything other than how much I excelled in playing the piano, almost like a recruiter.
And the second Touma Youko is someone who until recently, was the whimsical mother I loved so dearly.
"Change, growth and maturity. Don't ever mistake aging for decline."
"For human beings are bound to change."
"You're simply the one who's changing too little, Kazusa…"
Crap, I was dozing off for a second there.
I'll catch a cold if I fall asleep like this… That might actually get the contract terminated.
Through my blurry vision, I catch a glimpse of the ceiling I've grown accustomed to the past few days.
The conversation I had with that teacher permeates my thoughts.
People are bound to change, huh.
Then I should play the piano, so that I can guide Mom into becoming the type of old woman I want her to be.
Just like how I played the piano to get away from him, and return him to her.
That's the best choice, right? I don't have any other choice, right…?
"Touma… hey… sorry to bother you, but I need you to wake up for a bit."
Ah, that was… the first time and he and I…
He told me it was love at first sight.
He said that he was captivated by the sight of me fast asleep in the classroom.
Why would he wait five years to say that…? What an idiot.
"This is the first time you've spoken to me on your own, isn't it?"
And that was the first time we ever talked to each other properly.
Despite the scorching heat, I went to school for no other reason than the unreliable intel that he might be there.
…What kind of moronic girl was I?
Doesn't that mean I've been in love ever since that time?
"Hey, Touma-san… don't you think we could be really good friends?"
"Not at all. And what makes you think we would?"
"I have no idea what you're talking about."
But she already knew by then.
She saw through my feelings before she even got to know me.
She was so sharp that it made me uncomfortable. She was so dangerous that it made me want to cry.
That's why I was able to accept her. We developed a type of relationship even more difficult than one-sided feelingsーfriendship.
I'm sorry for pulling in such a huge audience, okay?"
"Whenever you act all arrogant like that, it just leaves me speechless… Come on, let's go, Kitahara!"
"Yeah! Don't make fun of me if I mess up the solo, you two!"
And then we became three. We became irreplaceable friends.
Doing so would only invite pain and sadness. I knew that full well…
I knew someone had to lose, and I knew the winner couldn't get away without their share of pain either.
But I still couldn't resist that sweet allure. I just wanted friends… I was the same as her…
That's not something I want to hear from my best friend's boyfriend!"
"Weren't you the one who left me first!? Weren't you the one who went to a place beyond my reach first!?"
"Always keeping me at arm's length, but never letting me reach you. Wasn't that torture your idea!?"
Yes, I knew it would end up that way…
I backed away, but then I forced myself upon him. I broke the three of us. I made a mess of our irreplaceable friendship.
"Hey, Kitahara… I… really loved you, you know."
"I loved you so much, so when you were taken by Setsuna, it was so painful for me…"
"There, I said it… Setsuna, I'm so sorry. But this is fine, right…? Because he can only hear my voice… Because I'll never meet him again…"
That's how I tore it apart.
I hurt the person I loved. I hurt the person who was my friend. Then I ran away by myself…
If only I could've avoided the pain by doing so… Staying over here, forgetting about them…
If only… after five whole years, I could've just forgotten about him.
People are bound to change… That's only natural, right? Then why am I…
"…It's not good to be picky with your food."
"I don't want any cabbage either, or onions. Actually, don't put in any vegetables."
"…That would defeat the purpose of a stew. This dish exists to make people eat vegetables."
Why can't I live like my mom…? Why can't I live like a normal person?
Why am I able to fill five years worth of emptiness in a single day, by just sitting around the same dinner table?
"Do you swear it? Do you swear to make me your wife, Haruki?"
"And until death do us part, I swear right here to dedicate myself to you…"
I kept on longing for him, and even though I knew that I shouldn't, what wasn't meant to be still came true…
That's why the final result was…
…Tell me, are you really going to see what lies ahead? Do you dare to look?
Am I stupid…? What's wrong with being happy in my dreams, at least?
What's wrong with rolling the credits right there…?
"Let's part with a smile… Let's stop dragging each other along…"
"Everything will be solved if you just pull your hand away. You'll be able to go anywhere."
"…Don't be a bully. I wanted you to let go of me."
"I just wanted you to… reject me…"
I saw it through to the very end… when I really didn't want to.
It was as if my life was flashing before my eyes.
The few hundred days of my life when our lives overlapped.
But to me, those days were like an eternity. They might as well have been half my life.
I thought I finally managed to stop thinking about it… I desperately tried to keep it out of my mind until now…
We live in different worlds now. Even our hearts, and our homes are completely separate now.
He belongs to her now, yet…
I look at my phone contacts, and his number is of course no longer there. I had even erased him from the phone's memory.
…That means I'm living in reality right now. I'm not in Japan, I'm not back where I was half a year ago, or five years ago.
It's been six years since our first meeting, five years since our break up, and half a year since our second break up.
How do you expect me to change in half a year, when I couldn't even change in five…?
Summer is over. Chilly breezes in the morning and evening herald the arrival of the new season.
But fall hasn't started yet. The glaring sunlight at noon rejects the coming of the new season.
But even during these days of alternating heat and cold, the city slowly loses its warmth day by day.
Even the warmth I've held within me since winter, day by day, it goes away.
"Oh. You could at least answer me if you're actually in there."
"Of course I'm in here. Did you think I jumped out the window or something?"
"Don't be like that. No one's forcing you to stay in that room, you know."
I've said those ugly words enough times this month to get sick of it.
"Your share of dinner is in the fridge. Mom said you should eat it if you feel hungry.
Oh, and I just watched the news and…"
"I don't need it. Leave me alone."
"How long you plannin' on shutting yourself in…? Everyone's worried about you, Nee-chan."
I've been shut away ever since that day last month… Within the cage of my family's kindness.
My health just never got any better, so I couldn't leave the house even once during the summer break.
Once the summer break was over I did return to work, but this time I'm trying not to overdo it, and I'm avoiding working overtime as well.
My superior accepted it without me even having to explain much.
…Maybe that's just how terrible of a state I was in, and he was simply waiting for me to bring it up.
"You're fine as in you took your medicine? Or you're fine as in you don't need any medicine?"
"I'm even going to work like usual. I'm perfectly fine."
"But you're like a car without gasoline during the weekends, just like now."
Ah, whatever. I'm going to sleep, so just go already."
"I'm going to sleep because you said everyone's worried about my health. Make up your mind."
The truth is, my current state isn't really that big of a deal at all.
My sudden illness has softened quite a bit since summer break.
Mornings are still a bit of a struggle, but I can get up in time nevertheless.
I'm no longer sweating for no reason, and I can get on the train normally. Neither is it having any noticeable effect on my work.
So there's no problem anymore. Everything's back to normal.
…But those words don't work on my family.
Dad began to oppose my weekend outings.
He said my old symptoms would reappear if I returned to my old habits.
He said that since stress is the cause, the lack of any current stress has led me to mistakenly believe that I'm cured now.
Dad believes that the cause of my stress lies in the weekends.
As for Takahiro, he has become really considerate, almost uncomfortably so.
He was always a kind little brother to me, but nowadays he's practically walking on eggshells around me.
He has stopped talking back to me. And our usual fights, big and small, have ceased entirely.
…As a result, we no longer reconcile like we used to. All of our conversations just kind of end awkwardly now.
But the worst reaction is my mom's…
She doesn't reprimand me for my actions, nor does she show any more consideration than she has to; she merely watches from slightly afar.
I woke up late at night one day feeling thirsty, so I went downstairs for a drink.
I became apprehensive about going downstairs after that happened, so I barely even leave my room during the weekends…
That's why I can't even go to Minami-Suetsugu anymore, even though it's only one station away.
I left my room making purposely loud footsteps, and when I reached the living room for the first time today, no one was there.
Opening the fridge, I see dinner wrapped in plastic film on the middle shelf. One portion for one person, just like Takahiro said.
But I disregard that and instead reach for my barley tea bottle, still useful even in September.
I sit down by the table and blow at the barley tea in my cup.
The cold tea permeates my throat to my stomach, causing me a tiny bit of pain.
When I wearily look up at the ceiling, I get the strange feeling that the empty room is quietly laughing at my expense.
And with that, I'm confronted with the reality that I'm deceiving myself.
The reality that my family's behavior is nothing but an excuse.
The reality that my feet aren't moving because I don't want them to. I'm confronted with the fact that I'm the only one responsible for my own fear…
Summer break is over, and so is summer.
Yet ever since I was turned away from Haruki-kun's apartment that day, I haven't taken a single step forward.
I haven't done so not because of anyone else, but of my own free will.
I've been taking advantage of my family's objections, and have willingly shut myself in the cage… no, the protective sanctuary of my home.
The idea of closing the distance between us again, when we've now fallen so far apart is suffocating me.
If I attempt to force things right now, he might only shun me. And I might only shun him in return.
I might hurt him more deeply than I already have. I might get hurt myself once again.
But if I allow us to fall apart like this, he might forget about me and leave me behind. I might forget about him and leave him behind.
He might end up getting even more crushed than he already is right now. But he also might feel a sense of peace by separating from me.
I might be unable to bear the sense of loss if I let go of him. I might be able to bear it, and it'll mark the start of my new life.
I love him, and I'm also a burden to him. Both of these things are undoubtedly true.
Then, does that mean that he loves me? Is he a burden to me?
Can I blindly follow his lead like "she" could…?
…Is a jealous woman like me even a good match for him?
Would the things I'm worried about not even be a small hindrance for her?
Not a matter of what she could do for him, but a matter of what she wanted to do for him. Can I even stand a chance against someone like that?
"Touma Kazusa, taking on the world again."
"Touma Kazusa, the famous pianist who was a sensation in Japan last winter, will finally resume her activities in Europe in earnest."
"Her first performance will be done in cooperation with the Franz Dupre Orchestra."
"The live broadcast of this concert will be delivered to you exclusively here on CS East Asia!"
"Guess who I just saw on the news…"
"Thank you for your call. This is the Japanese branch of Touma Youko Office PLC."
"I sincerely apologize, but company operations are currently under a temporary hiatus."
"If you have urgent business, please contact the European branch of Touma Youko Office. The number to them is…"
I haven't been able to reach her in three months. Did the Japanese branch close or something?
With only a week left until the concert, I've still been unable to talk to Mom.
But it's not like my voice can reach anyone right now…
The moment I lie down on the bed, an unpleasant sense of fatigue soaks through my body.
My rehearsals with the orchestra only get more and more demanding by the day. I barely have any time to sleep anymore.
…The rehearsals which include me, the conductor, and the strings.
The brass crew were still playing cards in the back, while the woodwinds, slightly more modern, were playing online games on their smartphones instead.
But no one warns them, and no one gets angry.
That goes without saying. This is our fifth full rehearsal, but the time they've spent playing in total is less than an hour.
In truth, no one could complain if they got angry instead and left the project.
…No, I guess I'm the one holding it back.
It's not a difficult piece no matter how you spin it. As far as the sheet music is concerned, I haven't made a single mistake.
But this piece is the one my mom played more than any other, always met with thunderous applause in every corner of the globe.
That means there's an important nuance missing in the sheet music.
But that stupid conductor won't tell me what that is. All he does is force repetitions, and he won't let me continue until I've got it perfectly down.
Is he trying to tell me to "listen to my own blood?"
There's only one full rehearsal left.
This is usually the time one would start considering cancellation if things are going this badly.
But this concert isn't going to be canceled, nor is anyone going to lose out because of it.
Because just yesterday, our concert got itself a sponsor.
It's not some local music shop or magazine either, but the same Japanese electronics company that made the smartphone the woodwinds are playing their games on.
Yes, just like the conductor said, this concert has been degraded to nothing more than a faux-concert. "Touma Kazusa-chan's cute little marketing gig."
The moment that piece of news reached his ears, his attitude fully altered course.
Not in the direction of being nicer to me, mind you, nor did he go any easier on me during rehearsals…
"This is amazing! As expected of the Japanese people!"
"To think there are companies willing to throw a fortune down the drain for a mediocre pianist like you…
"I've heard the Japanese are as serious and grave as the Germans, but I can't say I've ever seen a German this generous with money."
"Oh this is just great, please do take all the time in the world."
"After all, even if the concert gets delayed, your excellent sponsor will take the fall for precious little you."
…The only change in his attitude was that he found new and creative ways to verbally abuse me.
Seriously… I know it's only this one time, but why do I have to deal with this guy…?
